intro.heading: The specification, the mark scheme and the past paper
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where a tutor's knowledge of the paper matters most, because the content is almost entirely public and almost entirely teachable, and yet the marks keep going missing. A Year 11 student in Arabian Ranches who can factorise, solve simultaneous equations and use the sine rule should not be sitting on a 5. Usually they are, and usually the reason is not mathematical. It is that nobody has shown them how the mark scheme distributes marks, or made them work a past paper in a way that teaches rather than confirms.

Start with the specification, because two students in the same classroom on this belt can be entered for different things. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, with Core and Extended routes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1, with Foundation and Higher tiers. Cambridge Additional Mathematics is 0606 and Pearson's Further Pure is 4PM1, both taken alongside the main course by students heading for A Level Mathematics. The papers, the tiering and the calculator rules differ between them, and the rules have been revised recently, so the awarding body's own page for your child's series is the only place to confirm them.

Then the mark scheme. IGCSE mathematics mark schemes award method marks and accuracy marks separately, and they are generous in a way that students never exploit because nobody has told them it exists. A method mark survives an arithmetic slip. A follow-through mark pays for correct work built on an earlier wrong answer. Both require the working to be visible and legible on the page. A student who does three lines in their head and writes the answer has thrown away every method mark in the question, and the loss is invisible until a mock comes back.

Then the past paper, which almost every family in this community already has and almost nobody uses properly. Working a paper means sitting it in one go, at the right time of day, without notes, then marking it against the published mark scheme line by line and classifying every lost mark. Doing the questions over several evenings with the mark scheme open is not working a paper; it is reading a paper. The first produces a diagnosis. The second produces a feeling of progress, which is worse than nothing because it is mistaken for the first.

On delivery, the honest position. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; sending tutors to houses is a service we operate only in India. Mathematics teaching here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen or writing surface so the working is visible both ways. For this subject that is not a compromise: the whole lesson is working, step by step, and a shared annotated page is a better record of it than a kitchen table, because the student keeps the file afterwards and the marks that were missed stay marked.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two written papers of equal weight, entered at Foundation or Higher tier, with Higher carrying the top grades. Content covers number, algebra, sequences and functions, geometry and trigonometry, mensuration, vectors and transformation geometry, and statistics and probability. Examined in May or June and again in November, so a retake sits months rather than a year away.
programmes.countryNote: Used by a minority of Dubai schools and occasionally for maths while the sciences sit with Cambridge in the same school. That split is the practical reason to work from the syllabus code rather than the subject name: a tutor planning from 0580 past papers for a 4MA1 candidate will be working on the right mathematics in the wrong format.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: An extra qualification taken alongside Extended Mathematics by students heading for A Level Mathematics. Content reaches into calculus, trigonometric identities, functions, logarithms, series and vectors, so it covers material most students meet for the first time in the sixth form. Assessed by written papers with no coursework component.
programmes.countryNote: Offered by a number of schools near Arabian Ranches as a bridge into A Level, and it is a genuinely different subject rather than more of 0580. A student comfortably scoring well in Extended Mathematics can still struggle here, and the two need separate plans even when the same tutor covers both.

Entry conditions are set by each school and are usually subject-specific: a high grade in IGCSE Mathematics, and for Further Mathematics often a requirement at the top of the range or evidence from Additional Mathematics. The algebraic fluency assumed on day one is considerable.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools near Arabian Ranches continue to A Level, and their published maths conditions are the real reason a single June grade matters. dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranch.subjectsIntro: An IGCSE mathematics grade is decided topic by topic, and the topics are not equally expensive. The list below is the content map with the honest note attached to each area: what the paper asks for, and what students on this belt most often lose there. Tiering determines which of these appear at all.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds and surds depending on tier. Reverse percentages and upper and lower bounds produce more lost marks than their weighting suggests, because both look routine and both have a step most students skip. Cheap marks, quickly recovered, and usually the first thing worth drilling.

subjects.name: Algebra and graphs
subjects.description: Manipulation, expansion, factorising, rearranging, simultaneous and quadratic equations, inequalities and graph sketching. This is the load-bearing wall of the whole subject: weakness here reappears in trigonometry, mensuration and statistics. Six to eight weeks of short frequent practice moves it, and nothing moves it faster.

subjects.name: Sequences and functions
subjects.levels: Extended and Higher, with basics at Core
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic nth terms, function notation, composite and inverse functions at the higher tiers. Students lose marks by describing a pattern instead of producing a general rule, which is the same error that costs them in investigations. Notation marks are available and routinely dropped for untidy work.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, lengths, parallel and perpendicular lines and the equation of a straight line. Reliable marks for a student who learns the four formulas properly, and a surprising source of loss when a negative reciprocal is rushed. Quick to secure and worth doing before the harder topics.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle rules, polygons, congruence, similarity and circle theorems at the higher tiers. Marks here depend on naming the reason, not just the angle: a correct value with no stated theorem loses the explanation mark. One of the clearest cases where knowing the mark scheme is worth more than knowing more geometry.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs, sectors and compound solids. The usual losses are units, unconverted dimensions and premature rounding inside a multi-step calculation. All three are discipline rather than understanding, which makes them among the cheapest marks on the paper to win back in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, Pythagoras, bearings, and the sine and cosine rules plus three-dimensional work at the higher tiers. Bearings questions are the reliable trap because they test reading rather than trigonometry. Three-dimensional questions need a drawn diagram, and students who refuse to draw one lose the method marks.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.levels: Extended and Higher, with basics at Core
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry proofs, and the four transformations with full descriptions. Transformation questions award marks for the complete description, so a rotation without a centre or a direction scores partially. Vector proofs need the route written in vectors rather than reasoned verbally.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and conditional probability at the higher tiers. Tree diagrams carry method marks for the structure itself, so drawing the tree earns marks before any arithmetic happens. Students who calculate without drawing lose those marks and never know it.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Averages, grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, and box plots. Histograms with unequal class widths are the standard high-tier trap because frequency density has to be computed rather than read. Interpretation questions want a comparison in context, not a restatement of the numbers.

sections.heading: Which maths specification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the first question and most families cannot answer it, which is reasonable because nothing in school communication makes it prominent. The entry carries a syllabus code and a tier, and those two facts determine which papers are sat, which topics can appear, what the maximum attainable grade is, and whether a calculator is permitted in each component. A tutor who does not have them is guessing, and in mathematics the guess is usually close enough to feel right and wrong enough to cost marks.

Four specifications cover nearly every student on this belt. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 runs Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 sit alongside the main course for students heading to A Level. The content overlaps substantially; the papers, the question styles, the formula provision and the calculator rules do not, and the calculator rules in particular have been revised in recent syllabus editions.

What to do about it takes one email. Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code, the tier, the paper numbers and the administrative zone for mathematics, and ask whether a calculator is permitted in each paper for your child's series. Then confirm the papers on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com for that exact series rather than relying on a revision site, because an old edition of a specification is the most common reason a student practises the wrong thing diligently for a term.

sections.heading: The topic map, and where students on this belt actually lose marks
paragraphs: Mathematics marks do not go missing evenly. A handful of topics account for a disproportionate share of lost marks in every cohort, and they are not the topics families worry about. Parents worry about circle theorems and trigonometry. The marks tend to go on reverse percentages, upper and lower bounds, histograms with unequal class widths, and the stated reason in a geometry answer. None of those is conceptually hard. All of them have one step that is routinely skipped.

The pattern is worth naming because it changes what a session should do. Hard topics are lost because they were not understood, and the repair is teaching. Easy topics are lost because of a missing habit, and the repair is a rule plus repetition: always write the reason, always convert units first, always draw the tree, never round until the last line. Habit repairs are fast, they are cumulative across the paper, and they are almost never what a tutor is asked to work on.

The table below sorts the content map by what it costs rather than by where it sits in the syllabus. Use it with a marked script in hand: find the rows your child lost marks on, and notice whether they cluster in the understanding column or the habit column. A student whose losses are nearly all habits can move a grade in six weeks. A student whose losses are spread across the understanding column is a two-term project and should be told so honestly in November rather than in April.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme notation, and the marks nobody is taught to collect
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics mark schemes are published documents written in a compact notation, and almost no student has ever read one. That is a strange situation, because the notation describes exactly how the marks are awarded and therefore exactly what a good answer looks like on paper. A student who understands it writes differently within a week: more working, clearer lines, the reason stated, the answer left exact until the end.

The important distinction is between method and accuracy. A method mark is awarded for a correct approach even where the arithmetic goes wrong afterwards, which means an answer that is wrong can still score most of the available marks, provided the method is visible. An accuracy mark is awarded for the correct value. Follow-through marks pay for correct subsequent work built on an earlier error. None of this helps a student who writes only the final answer, because an invisible method cannot be credited.

This is where an online lesson with a shared writing surface earns its place. The whole exercise is about what lands on the page, so a lesson in which both sides are writing on the same visible page, and in which the tutor annotates where a mark was available and not taken, teaches the habit faster than a conversation about it would. The student also keeps the annotated file afterwards, which means the correction survives the session instead of evaporating with it. Three weeks of that is usually enough to change how a script looks, and a script that looks different scores differently even before anything new has been learned.

sections.heading: Calculator discipline, and the papers worked by hand
paragraphs: Calculator rules in IGCSE mathematics differ between the awarding bodies, between routes, and between syllabus editions, and they were revised in recent editions, so the only reliable source is the awarding body's page for your child's exact series. That caveat matters more than it sounds, because a family practising from papers of the wrong edition can spend a term preparing with a calculator for a component that does not allow one, or the reverse.

Once the rules are confirmed, the two kinds of paper need genuinely different preparation. A paper worked by hand rewards mental arithmetic, fraction fluency, surd manipulation where the tier includes it, and a willingness to leave answers exact rather than converting to decimals early. A calculator paper rewards something quite different: knowing the machine, storing intermediate values instead of rewriting rounded ones, and checking a result by a second method rather than trusting the display.

Most of the lost marks in calculator papers on this belt are rounding marks, and they come from the same habit. A student computes an intermediate value, writes it down to two decimal places, then types that rounded number back in for the next step. The final answer then misses the required accuracy and the accuracy mark goes, while the method marks survive. The fix is a rule rather than a lesson: keep everything in the calculator memory, round only on the final line, and state the answer to the accuracy the question demands.

sections.heading: How to work a past paper so that it teaches
paragraphs: Every family in Arabian Ranches already has access to past papers, and most of them use them in the way that produces the least learning. The usual pattern is to attempt questions across several evenings, with notes nearby and the mark scheme open when a question stalls. That produces a pleasant sense of coverage and almost no diagnostic information, because the conditions have nothing in common with the conditions of the real paper.

Working a paper properly has four parts and the first is the hardest. Sit it in one go, timed, without notes, at roughly the time of day the real paper is sat. Mark it afterwards against the published mark scheme, strictly, line by line, giving no credit the scheme would not give. Classify every lost mark into one of five categories: never taught, taught but not understood, understood but mis-executed, ran out of time, or answered a different question. Then act on the proportions rather than on the total.

The proportions are the whole point. A script losing most of its marks to mis-execution and timing needs drills and timed sections, not more teaching. A script with blanks in two topics needs those two topics taught, and nothing else. A script losing marks evenly across every category is telling you the content is not secure, and that is a two-term conversation. Four papers worked this way across a term tells a family more than a year of weekly lessons without one, and it costs nothing but the student's own Saturday mornings.

sections.heading: Algebra is the rest of the subject in disguise
paragraphs: If one area has to be prioritised, it is algebraic fluency, because almost every other topic eventually asks for it. Trigonometry needs rearranging. Mensuration needs substitution and solving. Statistics needs manipulation inside a formula. Coordinate geometry is algebra with a diagram attached. A student who is slow and uncertain at manipulation is paying that tax in every topic on the paper, which is why their marks look spread out when the cause is concentrated.

The practical consequence is a different sequencing of work from the one most plans use. The intuitive plan works through the syllabus in order and tries to shore up each topic as it arrives. The effective plan spends the first few weeks on manipulation until it is quick and automatic, then returns to the topics, most of which improve without being taught again. Families find this counter-intuitive because it looks like time spent away from the problem, and it is the shortest route to the problem.

It is also why Year 10 is the right year to do it. Fluency is built by repetition over months and cannot be assembled in a fortnight, so a student who arrives in Year 11 with weak manipulation is carrying a cost that cannot be fully removed before June. It can be reduced, materially, by six to eight weeks of short daily practice. It cannot be eliminated, and anyone promising otherwise in March is selling something. The honest version of that conversation names the gap, states what six weeks will and will not recover, and leaves the family to decide whether the remaining marks are worth the hours.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor costs around Arabian Ranches, and what the money buys
paragraphs: It helps to ask what a given rate is actually buying in this subject, because the answer differs sharply by band. At the bottom, EdFlik lists online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That money buys somebody who can do the mathematics and talk a student through a question. It does not buy mark-scheme knowledge, and in a subject where a third of the recoverable marks are mark-scheme habits, that is a significant part of the job left undone.

In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's examiner-led rate is AED 650. What the step up from AED 65 to AED 200 buys in mathematics specifically is somebody who has marked papers: who can look at a script and say which marks were available and not taken, which is a different skill from being able to solve the question. In-home delivery is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent providers, and that premium pays for travel rather than for mark-scheme experience.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 at the budget end for one weekly hour, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more where an exam-year specialist is involved. Market packages run roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Set against the lead times earlier on this page, a sensible purchase in mathematics is often smaller than families expect: a past-paper marking block of four sessions plus a daily ten-minute drill moves more marks than twelve hours of topic teaching. Every figure here belongs to the provider named, on the date its own page carried it; IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page and the first lesson is free.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics, and the bridge into A Level
paragraphs: Students heading for A Level Mathematics are often entered for Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 alongside the main course, and families regularly treat it as extra practice for the same subject. It is not. The content reaches into calculus, trigonometric identities, functions, logarithms and series, which most students meet for the first time in the sixth form. A student scoring well on Extended Mathematics can genuinely struggle here, and the struggle says nothing about their main grade.

The useful way to think about it is as the first term of A Level brought forward. That reframing changes the teaching: more emphasis on exact answers, on manipulating expressions rather than evaluating them, and on multi-step problems where the method has to be chosen rather than recognised. It also changes the timetable, because a student carrying both courses needs the additional one planned separately rather than folded into the same weekly hour.

On the decision itself, the honest position is that it suits a student who already finds Extended or Higher mathematics comfortable, and loads a student who does not. It is also worth checking what the receiving sixth form actually requires: some schools near Arabian Ranches use it as evidence for Further Mathematics entry, others do not reference it at all. Ask the question in Year 10 rather than after the entries are made, and treat tutoring as support for the choice rather than as a reason to make it. Tutoring is not required for any entry decision, and nobody should imply that it is.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and getting started from Arabian Ranches
paragraphs: Before any booking, two checks. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website or e-services system. Ask to see it in the tutor's own name with its expiry. Then ask whether they teach at your child's school, because the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

On materials and honesty, the rule in mathematics is simpler than in coursework subjects but still worth stating. Specifications, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites for the appropriate series, and that is where a family should get them; a tutor may point you to the right page and should not be circulating copies. No tutor should promise a grade in this or any subject, and a mathematics tutor in particular should be able to say plainly which lost marks are recoverable in the time available and which are not.

Getting started takes four things: the syllabus code, the tier, the last marked script, and the evening window that genuinely exists once the bus has reached the community. The trial lesson is free and the condition is stated: one session, before any payment, with no card details taken beforehand and written feedback afterwards. Mathematics fills first in the evening slots across this belt, so if the hour you want is not available we say so and offer a different evening or a short wait rather than filling it with somebody approximate.

process.title: Get the code, the tier and the calculator rules
process.description: Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code, the tier, the paper numbers and whether a calculator is permitted in each paper for your child's series. Then confirm on the awarding body's own page. An old syllabus edition is the commonest reason a student practises the wrong format diligently for a whole term.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: A marked paper or school assessment shows whether the lost marks are understanding or habit, and those have completely different lead times. Six weeks fixes a habit. Two terms fixes insecure content. Nobody can tell the two apart from a description of how your child feels about maths.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson on a real question
process.description: One lesson at no charge, booked before any payment and with no card details taken first. It runs on an actual question from the script, with the mark scheme open, so you can see whether the teacher can name the marks that were available and missed. Written feedback follows the session.

process.title: Fix the practice, not just the lesson
process.description: Every lead time in this subject assumes ten to fifteen minutes of drill most days plus one timed paper a fortnight. Write that into the plan in hours. Weekly lessons without practice in between produce about a third of the progress, and no rate per hour changes that arithmetic.

process.title: Review on a marked paper, not on a feeling
process.description: After four or five sessions, sit a full paper under timed conditions and mark it strictly. The script either shows movement in the categories you targeted or it does not. At that point we continue, change teacher, or stop, and the decision is made on evidence rather than on impressions.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the specification, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ in papers, tiering, formula provision and calculator rules, and the rules have been revised recently. We ask for the code and the tier before matching a teacher, and we point you to the awarding body's page for the exact series rather than to a revision site.

whyPoints.title: Mark-scheme notation taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Method marks, accuracy marks, independent marks and follow-through are published in every mark scheme and read by almost no student. Teaching the notation changes how a student writes within a week, and it is the fastest source of recoverable marks available in this subject at any tier.

whyPoints.title: Habit repairs separated from understanding repairs
whyPoints.description: Reverse percentages and frequency density are understanding problems. Units, rounding, stated reasons and visible working are habits. The two have different lead times and different prices, and telling a family which they are buying is the difference between a six-week plan and a wasted term.

whyPoints.title: Past papers worked properly, or not counted
whyPoints.description: One timed sitting, no notes, strict marking against the published scheme, every lost mark classified. Four papers worked that way across a term tell a family more than a year of weekly lessons without one, and the only cost is the student's own Saturday morning.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what cannot be recovered
whyPoints.description: Algebraic fluency is built over months and cannot be assembled in a fortnight, so a Year 11 student with weak manipulation in March can be improved materially and not completely. We say so. Nobody here promises a grade, and no part of any assessed submission is produced for a student.

faqs.question: Which maths specification is my child sitting, 0580 or 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Only the school can tell you, and the exams officer can do it in one reply. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended routes; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers. Ask for the code, the tier, the paper numbers and whether a calculator is permitted in each paper for your child's series, then confirm the papers on the awarding body's own page. It matters because the question styles, the formula provision and the calculator rules differ, and a tutor planning from the wrong specification will be teaching the right mathematics in the wrong format.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended in Cambridge Mathematics 0580?
faqs.answer: They are two routes through the same subject with different content coverage and different grade ceilings. Extended examines additional topics that Core does not, and the top grades are available only on the Extended route. The school decides which route to enter a candidate for, usually on the strength of Year 10 performance, which makes Year 10 the year in which the ceiling is effectively set. Ask which route your child is on and by when it could still be changed; the honest answer is normally the entry deadline for the series, and after that it is fixed.

faqs.question: What does M1 mean on an IGCSE maths mark scheme?
faqs.answer: M1 is a method mark: one mark awarded for using a correct method, whether or not the arithmetic that follows is right. It is the single most useful thing a student can understand about how maths is marked, because it means a wrong final answer can still collect most of the available marks provided the method is written down and legible. A1 is an accuracy mark for the correct value, B1 is an independent mark for a correct statement on its own, and FT means later work is credited even though an earlier answer was wrong.

faqs.question: The answers are correct but the score is low. Where are those marks going?
faqs.answer: Usually accuracy or presentation rather than mathematics. The commonest causes are rounding an intermediate value and feeding the rounded number back into the next step, giving an answer to the wrong degree of accuracy, omitting units, or spoiling a correct answer by continuing past it where the scheme demands the correct answer only. In geometry it is often a correct angle with no theorem named, which loses the explanation mark. All of these are habits, they are cumulative across the paper, and they come back in two or three weeks of strict marking.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics cost students here the most marks?
faqs.answer: Not the ones families worry about. Reverse percentages, upper and lower bounds, histograms with unequal class widths, mensuration with mixed units, and stated reasons in circle theorem questions account for a disproportionate share of lost marks in most cohorts. None is conceptually difficult; each has a single step that gets skipped. The hard topics, trigonometry in three dimensions and vector proofs, lose fewer marks overall because fewer questions depend on them. Work from a marked script rather than from reputation when deciding what to target.

faqs.question: How should a Year 11 student actually work a past paper?
faqs.answer: In one timed sitting, without notes, at roughly the time of day the real paper is sat. Then mark it afterwards against the published mark scheme, strictly, line by line, awarding nothing the scheme would not award. Then classify every lost mark: never taught, taught but not understood, understood but mis-executed, ran out of time, or answered a different question. Act on the proportions between those categories rather than on the total. Attempting questions across several evenings with the mark scheme open is reading a paper, not working one, and it produces almost no diagnostic information.

faqs.question: Is my child allowed a calculator in every IGCSE maths paper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board, the route and the series, and the rules have been revised in recent syllabus editions, so the awarding body's page for your child's exact series is the only reliable source. The practical consequence is worth taking seriously: a family practising from the wrong edition can spend a term preparing with a calculator for a component that does not permit one. Ask the exams officer for the paper numbers and the calculator position in writing, then check it against cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com for that series.

faqs.question: How much algebra does the rest of the IGCSE maths course depend on?
faqs.answer: Nearly all of it. Trigonometry needs rearranging, mensuration needs substitution and solving, statistics needs manipulation inside a formula, and coordinate geometry is algebra with a diagram. A student who is slow or uncertain at manipulation pays that cost in every topic, which is why their lost marks look scattered when the cause is concentrated. The effective sequence is therefore counter-intuitive: spend the first weeks on manipulation until it is automatic, then return to the topics, many of which improve without being taught again.

faqs.question: Should my child take Additional Mathematics alongside IGCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: It suits a student who already finds Extended or Higher mathematics comfortable and loads one who does not. Cambridge 0606 and Pearson 4PM1 reach into calculus, trigonometric identities, functions, logarithms and series, which is sixth-form material brought forward rather than extra practice on the main course. Check what the receiving sixth form actually requires, because some schools near Arabian Ranches use it as evidence for Further Mathematics entry and others do not reference it. Ask during Year 10, before entries are made, and treat tutoring as support for the choice rather than a reason to make it.

faqs.question: What grade does my child need in IGCSE maths for A Level Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Each school sets and publishes its own condition, and it is usually subject-specific rather than a single overall threshold, with Further Mathematics typically carrying a higher requirement than Mathematics. So the answer lives in your child's prospective sixth form's entry criteria rather than in any general rule. The useful move is to read those criteria during Year 10, when a condition is still a target, instead of in August, when it is simply an outcome. Then work backwards from the condition rather than from a vague wish for a better grade.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an IGCSE maths grade take to move?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is wrong. Habit problems, which means units, rounding, stated reasons and invisible working, come back in two or three weeks of strict marking and are cumulative across the whole paper. A single misunderstood topic such as frequency density is usually one or two sessions. Weak algebraic manipulation is six to eight weeks of short daily practice and cannot be compressed. A specification still largely unlearned is a two-term project. Only a marked script distinguishes between them, which is why we ask for one before quoting any number.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published range runs from roughly AED 33 to 65 at the homework-help end, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's examiner-led rate is AED 650. In maths specifically, the step from the bottom band to the middle buys somebody who has marked papers and can diagnose a script, which is a different skill from being able to solve the questions.

faqs.question: Is one longer session a week better than two short ones for maths?
faqs.answer: For fluency work, two short sessions beat one long one, because manipulation and arithmetic accuracy are built by frequent repetition rather than by extended exposure. For past-paper work the opposite holds: a full Extended or Higher paper plus marking does not fit inside sixty minutes, so a ninety-minute weekend slot is the sensible shape. Most plans on this belt end up mixed: one short weekday session on technique, and a longer weekend slot every fortnight for a timed paper and its marking.

faqs.question: Can maths be taught properly over video when the working has to be shown?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this subject it has a specific advantage. Lessons run with a shared writing surface, so both sides are working on the same visible page and the tutor can annotate exactly where a method mark was available and not taken. The student keeps that annotated file afterwards, which means the correction survives the lesson rather than disappearing with the paper it was written on. For a subject where the whole argument is about what lands on the page, a shared and saved page is more useful than a kitchen table.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach maths privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time listed on MoHRE's own service page. Teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may apply. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see it in the tutor's own name, and ask separately whether they teach at your child's school, which the code of conduct prohibits.

faqs.question: Our slot is 19:30 on a Tuesday. Is maths usually available then?
faqs.answer: Later evening slots are generally the easiest to fill, because nobody has to drive to them, so 19:30 is a better request than 16:30 even though it feels like the harder one. Mathematics is the most requested subject on this belt and the earlier weekday slots go first, particularly between November and March. If the exact hour is not available we say so and offer a different evening or a short wait rather than putting a generalist in the slot. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: The cheapest grade is the one bought before the entry code is fixed
paragraphs: Every conversation about what an IGCSE maths tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 should cost skips the question that decides the answer. Which tier is the child entered for, and under which board. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits candidates into Core and Extended. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3, and the award cannot exceed a grade C. Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4 and the range runs from A* to E. Pearson's Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, splits into Foundation, reporting grades 5 to 1, and Higher, reporting 9 to 4 with an allowed 3.

This changes the economics of tutoring completely. Thirty hours bought for a Core candidate who is already comfortably achieving a C buys nothing at all, because the ceiling is already reached. Four hours bought in Year 9, which establishes that the same child should be entered for Extended, changes what every subsequent hour is capable of producing. Families in this community routinely do the first and almost never do the second, which is the largest single waste of money in IGCSE maths.

The second thing that moves the price is the board, and specifically the calculator rule. In Cambridge 0580 the Extended pair is Paper 2, two hours and 100 marks without a calculator, and Paper 4, two hours and 100 marks with one. In Pearson 4MA1 both papers are two hours and 100 marks and a calculator is permitted in both. A tutor who drills calculator methods for a child sitting a non-calculator Cambridge paper is being paid to make that child slower. Buying by syllabus code rather than by subject name costs nothing and removes the risk entirely.

Arabian Ranches 2 pays a particular version of the market premium. It is a villa community off Sheikh Zayed Bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street with no secondary school inside the gates, so every Year 10 and Year 11 is bussed out to Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Nad Al Sheba, Al Barsha South or the Sustainable City. Published in-home rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to 500 an hour because somebody is driving into Dubailand in evening traffic; qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to 300. For a family in Camelia or Azalea, at the back of the community, that difference is the largest it gets.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranch.subjectsIntro: An IGCSE maths budget is spent on components and topics, not on the subject as a whole. The entries below are the units a session actually gets built from, ordered by how reliably paid hours convert into marks.

subjects.name: Non-calculator paper technique
subjects.description: Exact values, surd manipulation, index laws, fraction arithmetic and standard form at speed. Half the Cambridge grade sits on a paper where none of this can be checked with a device. It is also the most diagnosable weakness in the subject: one marked paper shows it immediately, and eight to twelve hours of drilling shifts it.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, algebraic fractions, rearranging and completing the square. Not a topic so much as the machinery every other topic runs on. A student who is slow here loses marks everywhere and appears to have gaps in six different places at once, which is why generalist tutors chase symptoms for a term.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem setup
subjects.description: Both Pearson papers permit a calculator, so arithmetic is rarely the barrier. Marks go instead on reading a wordy question, defining what is being solved for and choosing the right route. This responds to practice on whole past papers rather than topic exercises, and it is quick to improve once identified.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, three-dimensional problems and bearings. Reliably the largest single topic loss in this catchment after algebra. Students usually know the formulae and lose marks on diagram interpretation, so the fix is drawing practice rather than more formula recall.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, Venn diagrams and set notation. Cheap to fix and frequently ignored because it appears late in the scheme of work. Three or four hours here often returns more marks per dirham than the same time spent on a harder topic the student is already half-competent at.

subjects.name: Graphs, functions and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching, intersections, gradients, transformations of functions and reading solutions from a graph. On Cambridge Paper 4 and Pearson Paper 2 this is calculator territory, and fluency with a graphic display calculator converts directly into saved time elsewhere in the paper.

subjects.name: Calculus and identities
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, stationary points and trigonometric identities, taught at pace and assuming fluency. This is where 0606 students fall behind and where specialist teaching is genuinely necessary rather than merely helpful. Fifteen to twenty-five hours is a realistic figure rather than an upsell.

subjects.name: Graphics calculator investigation
subjects.description: An investigative component with its own demands: exploring a situation with technology, noticing structure and communicating the finding. Students who are strong on routine questions often score poorly here, and no amount of 0580 past-paper work prepares them, because 0580 does not contain anything like it.

subjects.name: Tier and entry review
subjects.description: Not a topic but the highest-return piece of work available. Reading a marked paper against the tier the child is entered for, and saying plainly whether the entry matches the performance. Four hours here in Year 9 is worth more than thirty in Year 11, because it decides what every later hour can achieve.

subjects.description: Whole papers under exam conditions, marked immediately, with error categories counted each time. The only component where progress can be measured honestly week to week, and the work that should dominate spending in the final eight weeks rather than new teaching.

sections.heading: What the entry code commits you to, and what it costs to find out late
paragraphs: An exam entry is a contract about the maximum grade available. In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, a Core candidate sits Paper 1 and Paper 3 and cannot be awarded above a grade C. An Extended candidate sits Paper 2 and Paper 4 and the award range runs A* to E. Pearson's 4MA1 divides into Foundation, reporting 5 to 1, and Higher, reporting 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. Nothing a tutor does changes which of those applies; only the school's exams officer can.

The money consequence is blunt. A Core candidate already achieving a secure C has reached the ceiling, and every hour bought after that point purchases confidence rather than grades. Families in Arabian Ranches 2 buy those hours regularly, usually because nobody told them the entry was capped. The conversation that prevents it takes ten minutes with the school and costs nothing.

In the other direction, a student entered for Extended who is not coping with the Extended paper pair is in a more expensive position. Dropping to Core protects a grade but caps it at C, which may close off the sixth-form subject the family is aiming at. Staying on Extended means thirty hours of catch-up rather than ten. This is the decision a four-hour diagnostic block exists to inform, and it has to happen before the entry deadline rather than after the mocks.

Dates matter here because they sit months ahead of the papers. UAE candidates sit a June series and a November series, and Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable shows the shape: the papers run from late October to 19 November 2026, results reach students in January, and the entry closes early in the autumn term before most centres have run a single mock. For a Cambridge June sitting the gap is wider still, with entries closing in the spring, roughly four months out, on a date your centre prints on the statement of entry. An October tier conversation is timely for either. An April one is a conversation about resits.

sections.heading: Price it monthly, because that is how the household actually pays
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how the market quotes and monthly totals are how families decide. Published monthly estimates for a single weekly hour in Dubai are AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, according to Bestimate's 2026 rate work. Packages exist too: published examples in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Reading those monthly bands against a school year is more useful than comparing hourly figures. A sensible IGCSE maths plan is light from Year 10 term two, slightly heavier in Year 11 term one when mocks produce real data, and intense only for the final six to eight weeks. Spread that way, the total across two years sits well below what a panicked February costs, because the February version buys specialist-band intensity for two months to compress work that nine months would have absorbed comfortably.

The hourly ladder, for reference and with sources named: budget online and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home visits run AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500; specialists reach AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; and premium named tutors run to AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

One piece of context worth having while you plan. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. It means the larger education line in a Ranches 2 household budget is stable this year, which makes planning the tutoring line against a term rather than a crisis realistic.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson: the same maths, a different purchase
paragraphs: Parents often assume IGCSE maths is one thing and that a good maths tutor covers it. The content does overlap heavily. What differs is the assessment, and assessment is what the final eight weeks of tutoring are spent on. Getting this wrong is not a small inefficiency; it is paying for preparation aimed at papers your child will not sit.

The sharpest difference is the calculator. Cambridge Extended candidates sit Paper 2 for two hours with no calculator, which puts half the grade on handwritten arithmetic, surds, exact values and standard form. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, which removes arithmetic as a barrier and shifts the losses onto problem setup and multi-step reasoning. A revision plan built for one board is close to useless for the other in the weeks that matter.

Paper length and mark totals differ too. Cambridge Core sits two papers of ninety minutes and 80 marks; Cambridge Extended sits two of two hours and 100 marks; Pearson sits two of two hours and 100 marks at both tiers. Pacing practice has to match the real paper, because a student trained to a ninety-minute rhythm runs out of concentration in a two-hour paper and a student trained to two hours leaves marks on the table in a shorter one.

Grade scales complete the picture and matter for sixth-form applications. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G; Pearson International GCSE reports 9 to 1. A school asking for a grade 6 in maths for A Level entry and a school asking for a B are asking for broadly comparable things, but the comparison has to be made deliberately rather than assumed, and the published requirement for the specific school is the only safe reference.

sections.heading: Where the hours go, and which topics actually repay them
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths budget disappears into a small number of topics, and knowing which ones changes how a term is bought. Algebraic manipulation is first, and it is not really a topic. Expanding, factorising, handling algebraic fractions and completing the square are the machinery every other question runs on. A student who is slow here appears to have gaps in six places at once, which is why a generalist tutor chases symptoms for a term while the cause sits untouched.

Trigonometry is second and is usually misdiagnosed. Students know the sine and cosine rules; they lose marks reading a diagram, placing a bearing or seeing the right triangle inside a three-dimensional shape. The fix is drawing and annotating practice rather than formula recall, which is a different kind of session and a shorter one.

Then there is the cheap end of the list, which families skip because it feels unserious. Probability, set notation and Venn diagrams are late in most schemes of work, lightly taught and worth real marks. Three or four hours there often returns more per dirham than the same time spent on a hard topic the student is already half-competent at. Buying marks where they are cheapest is not a compromise; it is how a capped budget produces a grade.

The non-calculator paper deserves its own line for Cambridge candidates. Half the Extended grade sits on Paper 2, where exact values, surds, index laws and fraction arithmetic cannot be checked with a device. It is the single most diagnosable weakness in the subject - one marked paper reveals it - and eight to twelve hours of short, frequent drilling shifts it reliably. Short and frequent beats long and occasional here, which also makes it the easiest work to fit around a Dubailand school run.

sections.heading: Group hours against one-to-one: the arithmetic of a shared lesson
paragraphs: Small-group tuition is quoted per student and looks like an obvious saving. It is a real saving in one specific situation and a false economy in every other. The condition is simple: the students must be on the same board, at the same tier, with substantially the same weaknesses. Two Year 11s both sitting Cambridge Extended who both lose marks on surds and algebraic fractions can work together productively, and the per-student rate genuinely falls.

Change any one of those variables and the economics invert. A Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same hour are sitting different papers with different calculator rules, so the tutor alternates and each student receives roughly half a lesson at a shared price. A Pearson student and a Cambridge student need different past papers. Two siblings two years apart are not a group at all; they are two half-lessons sold as one.

There is a quieter cost too. In a group, nobody's marked script gets read closely. The most valuable single activity in IGCSE maths tutoring is sitting with one student while they rewrite a solution properly, and that is a one-to-one activity by definition. Families who move to a group to save money sometimes find the sessions become content revision - comfortable, pleasant and unmeasurable.

The sensible pattern for a Ranches 2 family on a tight budget is not a group; it is fewer one-to-one hours used better. One hour a week with a tutor matched to the exact code, built on a marked script, with the student doing timed practice independently between sessions, beats two group hours a week at a similar total cost. If the budget only supports a group, insist that tier and board match before the first session rather than discovering the mismatch in week four.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics 0606 and the premium nobody mentions
paragraphs: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is the most expensive line in a Ranches 2 maths budget, and it is usually unplanned. Schools enter able Year 11 students for it alongside 0580 Extended, sometimes with extra timetabled lessons and sometimes without. Where the teaching time is not there, the family ends up buying it, because a half-prepared second maths entry is worse than no second entry at all.

The reason it costs more is scarcity. The number of tutors in the Dubailand villa belt who have taught 0606 to exam is small, and they are generally already teaching it in schools. This is the clearest case in this whole subject for widening the pool beyond driving distance: the code either has a specialist or it does not, and geography has nothing to do with which.

The content is the other reason. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early and the course assumes algebraic fluency that most Year 11 students are still building. Fifteen to twenty-five hours is a realistic estimate rather than a sales figure, and it should start the moment the entry is confirmed rather than after the first poor assessment. Students who took 0606 tend to land more comfortably in A Level Mathematics and in Diploma Analysis and Approaches, so the spend has a return - but only if the preparation is real.

The honest advice some families need is to decline the entry. If a Year 11 is already stretched by 0580 Extended, three sciences and the mandatory UAE subject load, adding a second maths qualification that will be half-prepared helps nobody. That conversation belongs with the school before the entry deadline, and for a Cambridge June sitting that deadline falls in the spring term, roughly four months ahead of the papers themselves, which is long before the point at which the strain actually becomes obvious.

sections.heading: What a November resit really costs, and when to decide
paragraphs: A resit is a second entry plus a short block of teaching, and it is cheaper than a repeated year by a very wide margin. The timing of the decision is what determines the cost. Pearson's rhythm makes the window visible: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. That is roughly nine weeks between a disappointing grade and the next set of papers.

Nine weeks is enough for a targeted second attempt and not enough for a rebuild. The work that fits is narrow: identify which paper lost the marks, which topics inside it, and drill those under time. The work that does not fit is reteaching a two-year course. Families who try the second version spend specialist-band money for two months and arrive at the papers tired, which is why deciding in advance is worth so much.

Deciding in advance means budgeting for the resit in spring, not in August. If a Year 11 is borderline in February, set aside the entry fee and a short block of hours then, and treat it as insurance you hope not to use. Entry fees for private candidates are set by the examination centre rather than by the board, so ask your centre for its current schedule rather than relying on a figure from a page like this one.

Cambridge offers a comparable second chance on a different clock. There is a June series and a November series, and no February or March option for a UAE candidate, because Cambridge runs that sitting in India only. The decision you are really making is therefore June-then-November or November-then-June, and the entry for whichever comes second closes months ahead of it: spring for a June sitting, early autumn for a November one. Note how far ahead that puts the deadline. A family waiting for August results before deciding about a November entry is already working against the clock, so ask the exams officer for the current date as soon as the first sitting is over.

sections.heading: What not to buy, and what to ask before you pay
paragraphs: Four purchases waste money reliably in this community. Hours bought for a capped entry that is already achieved. A generalist tutor who has not taught the code and prepares the wrong paper pair. A travel premium paid by default because a search returned the word nearby. And intensity bought in the final six weeks to replace regularity that nine months would have provided more cheaply.

A fifth, less obvious, is buying maths when the problem is not maths. A student whose marks fall while effort rises usually has a pacing, sleep or workload problem rather than a knowledge gap, and it shows up as unfinished papers rather than wrong answers. Thirty hours of content teaching will not move that. One honest diagnostic hour will identify it, and the fix is often a conversation with the school rather than a purchase.

Before paying anybody, ask four questions. Which syllabus code and tier have you taught to exam. Which paper in that code forbids a calculator. What will the first four sessions cover, based on the marked script I have sent you. And what would count as progress by session four. A tutor who answers all four concretely is worth the mid band; one who cannot answer the second is not worth the budget band.

Our own position, stated plainly: one free trial lesson per student, booked before any payment and with no card details taken at that point. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all. Every AED figure on this page belongs to the publisher named beside it and describes the market, not our price list. And no tutor can promise a grade, so treat any number offered in place of a plan with scepticism.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor in Arabian Ranches 2 cost per month rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates for a single weekly hour in Dubai are AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, from Bestimate's 2026 rate work. Packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student the middle band is the sensible default. faqs.question: Can my child get an A in maths if they are entered for Cambridge Core tier?
faqs.answer: No. A Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Core entry cannot be awarded above a grade C, regardless of how well the candidate performs. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4 and the range runs A* to E. If your child is working above a C, the fix is an entry change through the school's exams officer, not more lessons. That conversation has to happen before the entry deadline, which sits months ahead of the papers.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths paper does not allow a calculator?
faqs.answer: In Cambridge 0580, Paper 1 at Core and Paper 2 at Extended forbid a calculator; Paper 3 and Paper 4 permit one. Each pair splits the grade in half, so for a Cambridge Extended candidate half the award rests on handwritten arithmetic, surds, exact values and standard form. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers at both tiers. Any tutor quoting for this subject should be able to state this rule without being asked, because the revision plan depends entirely on it.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for maths help in Year 9, before IGCSE starts?
faqs.answer: It is the best value purchase available, and almost nobody makes it. A four-hour block in Year 9 or early Year 10 can establish whether the child should be entered for Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, and that decision sets the grade ceiling for the whole qualification. At published mid-band rates that block is roughly AED 600 to 1,200. Thirty hours in Year 11 spent working against a capped entry costs far more and cannot change the ceiling at all.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson maths need different tutoring in the final weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where a board mismatch becomes expensive. Cambridge Extended candidates need protected non-calculator drilling because Paper 2 forbids technology and carries half the grade. Pearson 4MA1 candidates have a calculator in both papers, so their losses sit in reading wordy questions and choosing a route. Past-paper sets are not interchangeable either. Content overlaps heavily across the two boards; assessment does not, and the final eight weeks are almost entirely about assessment.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the most marks back per hour paid?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation first, because it is the machinery every other topic runs on and a slow student appears to have gaps in six places at once. Then non-calculator technique for Cambridge candidates, which is half the Extended grade. Then the cheap end that families skip: probability, set notation and Venn diagrams are lightly taught, late in most schemes of work and worth real marks. Three or four hours there often beats the same time on a hard topic the student half-knows already.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and it genuinely saves money in one situation: the students share a board, a tier and substantially the same weaknesses. Change any of those and the hour splits. A Core candidate and an Extended candidate sit different papers with different calculator rules, so each receives half a lesson at a shared price. Two siblings two years apart are not a group. On a tight budget, fewer well-matched one-to-one hours usually beat more group hours at the same total.

faqs.question: Why is Additional Mathematics 0606 more expensive to support than 0580?
faqs.answer: Scarcity and content. Few tutors in the Dubailand villa belt have taught 0606 to exam, and those who have are usually teaching it in schools, so the local pool is thin and the rate reflects it. The course also front-loads calculus and trigonometric identities while assuming algebraic fluency most Year 11 students are still building. Fifteen to twenty-five hours is a realistic figure. If the school entered your child without extra teaching time, you are buying that time.

faqs.question: Should we decline an Additional Mathematics entry to save money and time?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a fair question to put to the school. A Year 11 already carrying 0580 Extended, three sciences and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons may not have room for a second maths qualification that will be half-prepared. A poorly prepared 0606 helps no sixth-form application. Have the conversation before the entry deadline rather than after the first assessment, because the deadline sits months ahead of the exam period.

faqs.question: What does a November maths resit actually cost us?
faqs.answer: A second entry fee plus a short targeted block of teaching, which is far cheaper than a repeated year. Entry fees for private candidates are set by the examination centre rather than the board, so ask your centre for its current schedule. The timing is the real cost driver: Pearson June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and the November 2026 series ran from late October to 19 November, leaving roughly nine weeks. Budget for it in spring, decide in August.

faqs.question: How far ahead do we have to commit to an exam entry?
faqs.answer: Further than most families expect. UAE candidates sit June and November, and both deadlines land long before the papers. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January, as the November 2025 series did on 22 January 2026; the entry for that sitting closes early in the autumn term. A Cambridge June entry closes in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, on a date your centre states rather than one we would publish here. Pearson also releases provisional timetables ahead of each series, so get the dates from your school's exams officer rather than from any third-party page, including this one.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home maths tutor more expensive here than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because the rate includes a drive into Dubailand in evening traffic. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts ordinary in-home sessions at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. From the back clusters of Arabian Ranches 2 the premium sits at its highest, because the journey is longest. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so no travel line appears in a figure we quote you.

faqs.question: My child works hard at maths and the grade will not move. Should we buy more hours?
faqs.answer: Probably not, at least not yet. Falling or static marks alongside rising effort usually point at pacing, workload or sleep rather than knowledge, and the evidence sits on the script: answered well for two thirds, then abandoned. More content teaching does not fix that and is demoralising, because the student spends the hour being taught what they already know. One diagnostic hour identifies which problem you have, and the fix is sometimes a conversation with the school rather than a purchase.

faqs.question: What should I ask a maths tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Four things. Which syllabus code and tier have you taught to exam. Which paper in that code forbids a calculator. What will the first four sessions cover, given the marked script I sent you. And what would count as progress by session four. Concrete answers to all four justify the mid band of the market. An inability to answer the second question means the tutor has not taught the syllabus, whatever their mathematics background looks like.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education count IGCSE maths towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Maths counts as one of the subjects in the British-track equivalency requirement, which is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Tutoring helps with grades and does not perform the process. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry of Education directly before relying on any summary.

intro.heading: Three syllabuses, one phrase on the invoice
paragraphs: The useful comparison in IGCSE mathematics is not between neighbourhoods. It is between the three qualifications Dubai schools actually enter students for. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is the default at most British-curriculum campuses in the Dubailand belt. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a separate syllabus, not a variant, with a graphics calculator built into the course and an investigation flavour to some of its questions. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiers rather than Core and Extended and sits papers in its own house style.

Two children living on the same street in Arabian Ranches 3 can be entered for different ones, because they attend different campuses. That is the whole answer to the question families here actually ask, which is whether the community matters. It does not. The campus matters, because the campus is the examination centre and it decides the board, the syllabus and the tier. The postcode decides how long the child spends on a bus.

A tutor matched on the wrong code wastes a term in a way that is invisible until a mock. The content overlaps enough that lessons feel productive. The question styles differ enough that the practice transfers poorly, so a student arrives at the paper having rehearsed the wrong shape of question. The fix costs one email to the school's exams officer: board, syllabus code, tier, and the Cambridge administrative zone if the entry is with Cambridge.

On delivery, plainly, since the search phrase invites the question. No tutor is sent to an address in Arabian Ranches 3, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai at all; the in-home service exists only in India. Mathematics here is taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, on a shared whiteboard the student writes on while the tutor watches. For mathematics that is a real advantage rather than a concession: the error is almost always in the method, and the method is visible line by line as it happens instead of arriving as a finished page.

What follows is the comparison done properly, because the research behind this project found exactly one syllabus code mentioned across an entire cluster of competitor pages for this area. The three syllabuses are set out side by side. The tiers appear with their grade ceilings and with the deadline at which a ceiling stops being negotiable, which is the day the centre submits its final entries, months ahead of the first paper of the June or November series. The additional mathematics qualifications some campuses offer alongside the main entry are named, because they change what a student can do at sixteen and nobody mentions them. There is a topic-by-topic account of where marks actually leave an IGCSE mathematics script, which turns out to be seven categories, six of them mechanical. There is a structured version of the gap between IGCSE Extended and Diploma mathematics, which is the reason a strong Year 11 can receive a mediocre first DP1 report. And the cost section starts at the cheapest adequate rung rather than at the most impressive one, because for most requests in this belt the cheapest adequate rung is the correct answer.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranch.programmesIntro: Mathematics decisions in a Dubai British-curriculum school are taken at four points, and three of them are taken before anyone thinks of hiring a tutor. These are the four, with what each one settles and what it leaves open.

programmes.name: Choosing the mathematics route, Year 9
programmes.description: The point at which a school's option process sets the mathematics route, sometimes including whether a student is on a track toward Core or Extended and whether Additional Mathematics will be available later. Nothing external is sat, so the only evidence a parent has is the school's internal assessment. A diagnostic on a real paper at this stage is cheap and is the moment at which a trajectory can still be changed without any administrative consequence.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai campuses in the Dubailand belt run different option blocks, so children from the same community can emerge from Year 9 on different mathematics routes. Families here often compare notes and conclude something is wrong when the real difference is simply that two schools structure the year differently.

programmes.name: The two-year IGCSE mathematics course
programmes.description: Two years of content with one administrative moment that matters: the tier submitted with the centre's final entries. Content is front-loaded into Year 10 and the harder material lands in Year 11, which is why a student can be comfortable for twelve months and then meet trouble in a spring mock. The honest diagnosis separates a late-taught topic from a genuine weakness, and only a marked script does that.
programmes.countryNote: Across the Dubailand campuses this is the most commonly entered mathematics qualification, and the one most tutoring in the belt is aimed at. Where a school runs Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 instead, the preparation changes materially, so the code is worth confirming rather than assuming.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics alongside the main entry
programmes.description: An extra Cambridge qualification taken by strong Extended students, usually in Year 11 and usually in addition to 0580 rather than instead of it. It introduces calculus, further algebra and more trigonometry, which is precisely the material the Diploma assumes from its first term. Students who sit it arrive in DP1 with the biggest single gap already closed, and students who do not are not disadvantaged permanently.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school offers it, and availability varies between campuses in the same belt. For a family whose child is heading toward Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level it is worth asking whether the school runs it, because the alternative is closing the same gap during DP1 when there is less time to spare.

programmes.name: The step into Diploma or A Level mathematics
programmes.description: The first term after IGCSE is where the gap shows. Diploma mathematics assumes radians, composite functions, exact-value work without a calculator and, in Analysis and Approaches, differentiation almost immediately. A Level makes comparable assumptions. A student with a strong Extended grade and no calculus exposure is not weak; they are missing specific prerequisites that can be named and taught.
programmes.countryNote: From Arabian Ranches 3 both post-16 routes are available but at different campuses, which means the decision carries a commute as well as a curriculum. The mathematics requirement is usually the binding constraint on that choice, so it is worth checking the receiving school's entry grade in Year 11 rather than after results.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-arabian-ranch.subjectsIntro: An IGCSE mathematics page should name the topic areas rather than list unrelated subjects. These are the areas the syllabuses cover, written with the error that actually recurs in each rather than with a content summary a parent could read on the school's own page.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Standard form, surds at the higher tiers, bounds, and the percentage work that catches most students out. Reverse percentage and compound change are routinely confused, and a plausible wrong answer attracts no method credit. Writing the multiplier before touching the numbers removes most of this category.

subjects.name: Algebra and graphs
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The single largest source of lost marks. Sign errors in expanding and factorising propagate into every later line of a multi-step question, so one slip costs a whole answer rather than a mark. Short daily sets on signs alone are duller and more effective than another topic sheet.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Gradients, parallel and perpendicular lines, midpoints and the equation of a straight line. Marks leave when a student finds a gradient correctly and then writes the equation in a form the question did not ask for, which is a reading problem rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Geometry and angle reasoning
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Circle theorems and angle chains, where the mark is often for naming the reason rather than for the number. Students give a correct angle and omit the justification, which is the cheapest category on the whole syllabus to fix because the mathematics is already right.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors. Losses cluster around units and around rounding applied mid-calculation, both of which carry separately allocated accuracy marks. Keeping full precision to the final line removes the second category entirely.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Right-angled work plus the sine and cosine rules at the higher tiers. The characteristic failure is choosing the wrong rule at the start and losing the entire question from one decision. A two-question routine applied before any calculation fixes it in a session or two.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and describing transformations fully. Marks are allocated to the completeness of the description, so a student who names a rotation without the centre or the direction has done the mathematics and not collected the credit for it.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Tree and Venn diagrams, conditional reasoning at the higher tiers. The recurring error is a tree whose branches do not sum correctly, which matters because later parts depend on the diagram and the loss compounds through the question rather than stopping at one mark.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths. The histogram is the standing trap: frequency density has to be calculated rather than assumed, and a correct-looking chart built on frequency alone collects almost nothing.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics content
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0606, where the school offers it
subjects.description: Calculus, further algebra, logarithms and more trigonometry, taken alongside the main entry by strong Extended students. It is the closest thing available to a bridge into Diploma or A Level mathematics, and the students who sit it meet DP1 differentiation as revision rather than as new material.
