sections.heading: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 compared
paragraphs: Start with the comparison nobody publishes. Across the whole area cluster researched for this project, exactly one syllabus code appeared on any competitor page. That is a strange omission, because the code is the single most useful fact about a mathematics entry and the schools supply it on request.

Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is the default across most Dubai British-curriculum campuses. It is tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade at C and Extended opening the full range. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a different syllabus with its own tiering, built around a graphics calculator and carrying a stronger investigation flavour in parts of its assessment. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiers and sets questions in Pearson's own style, which is recognisably not Cambridge's even where the mathematics is identical.

Because Cambridge and Pearson both revise their assessment arrangements between series, the honest instruction on paper counts, durations and calculator permissions is to read the current syllabus or specification for the series your child is actually entered for, on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com. This page links those rather than restating details that can change, which is a discipline most tutoring sites in this market do not keep: several still display arrangements that have since been superseded.

What does not change between series is the consequence for preparation. A student who revises from the other board's past papers has practised the wrong house style and will meet unfamiliar phrasing under time pressure. A 0607 student who has drilled non-calculator arithmetic has spent weeks on something their paper does not reward. Matching the code is not pedantry; it is the difference between practice that transfers and practice that does not.

sections.heading: Tiers and grade ceilings, and the day the ceiling stops moving
paragraphs: A tier is a ceiling, and a ceiling is the one thing in an IGCSE year that no amount of tutoring can lift. A Cambridge Core entry caps the available grade at C. That is sufficient for some post-16 routes and closes others, particularly A Level mathematics and either Diploma mathematics course at Higher Level. Pearson's Foundation tier works the same way with its own range. Parents routinely learn about the ceiling from a sixth-form entry requirement rather than from a school report.

The decision belongs to the school on the subject teacher's recommendation, and it is submitted with the centre's final entries. That submission date is therefore the practical deadline for the whole conversation. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit those two; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and again in November. In both cases entries close months before the first paper, so a tier discussion held in the spring term of a June series is a discussion after the board has already been told the answer. The exams officer holds the exact date for the series your child is entered for.

What makes the conversation productive before that date is evidence rather than opinion. A marked higher-tier paper showing which questions the student can already attempt is a different kind of argument from a parent's impression of their capability. Teachers recommend tiers partly on risk: a student entered too high and sitting unfamiliar questions can score worse than the same student entered appropriately. That is a reasonable concern and a marked script is the right answer to it.

After the deadline, the honest advice is to stop asking about the tier and spend the hour on marks within it. Both positions are defensible; mixing them up, which is common, costs a term of attention on something that is no longer movable.

sections.heading: The extra mathematics qualifications some campuses offer
paragraphs: A quieter comparison, and one that matters more than the tier for a student heading toward Higher Level mathematics. Some Dubai campuses offer an additional mathematics qualification in Year 11, taken alongside the main entry by students already secure on the higher tier. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is the common one; Pearson centres may offer Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 to a similar purpose.

What these add is the material the Diploma assumes and the main IGCSE syllabuses largely do not: calculus, further algebra, logarithms and more trigonometry. A student who has sat one of them meets differentiation in DP1 as revision. A student who has not meets it as new content in the same term as everything else, which is the single most common reason a strong IGCSE mathematician gets a disappointing first Diploma report. The gap is not a reflection of ability; it is a curriculum seam.

Availability varies between campuses in the same belt, which is one of the few places where comparing communities produces a real difference, and even then it is the campus rather than the community doing the work. The question to ask the school is simply whether it offers an additional mathematics qualification, who is eligible, and when the decision is made. If it does not, the same ground can be covered in a short bridging block after the series, which is what most families end up doing.

Nothing about this is required. A student can reach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level without an additional qualification and do well. The point of naming it is that the alternative, closing the gap during DP1, costs more attention at a busier time, and knowing that in Year 10 is worth more than discovering it in Year 12.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE mathematics marks are actually lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: This is the shortest useful list on the page. After one marked paper, almost every lost mark falls into one of seven categories, and six of the seven are mechanical rather than conceptual. That matters for a family deciding whether an hour a week is worth buying, because mechanical losses respond to practice on a scale of weeks.

Algebra is the largest single source, and specifically signs. An error expanding or factorising propagates into every subsequent line, so a single slip costs a whole question rather than a mark. The remedy is unglamorous: short daily sets on signs alone until the slip stops appearing, which is more effective than another full topic sheet. Percentage work produces the second largest category, with reverse percentage and compound change confused often enough that writing the multiplier before touching any numbers is worth drilling as a reflex.

Then there are the categories where the mathematics is already correct and the credit is not collected. Angle reasoning questions award marks for naming the reason, and students give the number and move on. Transformation questions award marks for the completeness of the description, so a rotation named without its centre and direction loses marks the student had earned. Graph sketches award marks for intercepts, asymptotes and turning points, which go unlabelled. These are the cheapest fixes available anywhere on the syllabus.

The last two are about process. Method not shown, because mark schemes award method marks for the working rather than the answer, which is the habit of students who have always been right. And rounding and units: rounding applied mid-calculation propagates error, and omitted units lose separately allocated accuracy marks. Holding full precision to the final line and writing the unit as part of the answer removes both.

sections.heading: The campus decides the syllabus, not the postcode
paragraphs: Here is the comparison this page exists to resolve. Families in the Dubailand belt compare communities as though the tutoring answer changed between them. It does not. The entry deadline is the same, the mark schemes are the same, the papers are the same, and the errors are lost in the same seven places. What differs between Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon, Town Square and Motor City is how long a child sits in a vehicle, which affects what hour a session can start and nothing else.

What does differ, genuinely and importantly, is the campus. The campus is the examination centre. It chooses the board, enters the syllabus code, sets the tier, decides whether an additional mathematics qualification is available, runs the mock calendar and sets the internal coursework deadlines. Two children in the same phase of Arabian Ranches 3 attending different campuses need different plans, and two children in different communities attending the same campus need the same plan.

That reframes the useful question. Rather than asking who is the best mathematics tutor near Arabian Ranches 3, ask the school's exams officer for four facts: board, syllabus code, tier and, where the entry is with Cambridge, the administrative zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states in its own guidance that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

With those four facts a parent can compare tutors on something real: has this person taught this code, at this tier, for how many cohorts, and can they mark a paper against its scheme. Without them, the comparison reduces to distance, which is the only input on the list with no measurable effect on a mark.

sections.heading: The gap between IGCSE Extended and Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: One competitor page in the research for this project has a single subheading about the IGCSE-to-IB gap. Nobody has a structured, subject-by-subject version, which is odd because it explains the most common bad surprise in the Dubai academic year: a student with a strong Extended grade receiving a mediocre first Diploma mathematics report.

The gap is specific and nameable. Radians: IGCSE works in degrees throughout and the Diploma treats radians as the default unit almost immediately. Exact values and surds without a calculator: Analysis and Approaches sits a paper with no calculator permitted, and a student who has worked with a device on the desk for two years has no fluency in that register. Composite and inverse function notation, which is more an obstacle of language than of mathematics but trips students for weeks. And calculus, which is absent from the main IGCSE syllabuses and assumed from the first term of DP1 unless the student sat an additional qualification.

None of those is a weakness. They are prerequisites that the curriculum seam leaves unaddressed, and they are teachable in a short, specific block rather than through a term of general support. Four to six sessions across a summer, aimed at radians, non-calculator work, function notation and a first pass at differentiation, changes the first Diploma report more reliably than the same hours spent in October when everything else is also competing for attention.

For Applications and Interpretation the emphasis shifts. The calculus gap is smaller and the statistics gap is larger, because that course expects distributions, correlation and written interpretation at a depth the IGCSE statistics topics do not approach. The bridging work is the same idea pointed at different content, which is one more reason to know which Diploma route the student is heading for before the bridging block is planned.

sections.heading: What IGCSE mathematics tuition costs, cheapest rung first
paragraphs: Most pages in this market start at the premium end because that is where the margin is. Start at the bottom instead, because for a large share of IGCSE mathematics requests the cheapest adequate rung is the right one and buying above it is simply waste.

The lowest rung is a group class at a tuition centre, priced per course rather than per hour, and it suits a student roughly at the group's pace who works better with other people in the room. Above that sits budget online one-to-one at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is a sound purchase for Year 9 and Year 10 consolidation and a poor one for Extended-tier method marks. The rung that matches most Year 11 needs is a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. For a standard Extended entry, that is usually where the ladder should stop.

Above it the money starts buying things an IGCSE student may not need. In-home one-to-one including travel is published at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500; the premium is justified for a young child who will not work without an adult beside them and not for a Year 11 whose problem is unshown method. IB and IGCSE specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270, which earns its rate for a bridging block into Diploma mathematics or a Further Pure entry. A premium tier advertises examiner experience at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650, and there is nothing a standard IGCSE mathematics entry specifically requires at that level.

Monthly, Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, with packaged pricing in the market at about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Each figure here is another provider's published number or a published rate survey, cited so you can check it rather than take it on faith. IB Gram publishes no price list on these pages; the free first lesson exists so the figure arrives with a named tutor attached.

sections.heading: Past papers, the boards' own materials, and booking from Arabian Ranches 3
paragraphs: Past papers are the most productive hour an IGCSE mathematics student can spend and they have to be sourced properly. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material. IB Gram does not host them, email them or supply them as downloads; they come from the school's own subscription or the board's official channels. A provider offering a folder of papers is handing you a copyright problem, and where any material is unreleased it becomes a malpractice exposure for the student.

Used properly a paper generates information rather than a score. The student works questions live on the shared board while the tutor stops at the point the method goes wrong, which is rarely the line where the answer went wrong. Working by topic until a topic is secure, then moving to mixed papers, produces honest signals; attempting the same paper four times produces a rising score and no learning. The test of whether topic work has landed is a question on that topic inside a mixed paper, answered unaided, a week or more later.

Booking is short. Tell us the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the hour your child is genuinely free; we propose one tutor with the code they teach stated and their permit position; the first lesson runs free with no card details taken and is spent on a real paper. You keep the marked script and the written notes whether you continue or not. If the match is wrong, saying so after the first lesson is the expected outcome. Where the best fit is an India-based tutor, that is said plainly ahead of payment, and the slot remains on Gulf Standard Time.

On data: an enquiry collects the child's name, school, year group, syllabus and tier, because the matching does not work without them. We need neither a report card nor a photograph in order to propose a tutor, a deletion request is honoured, and the privacy notice linked from this page sets out how long anything is kept under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection.

process.title: Get four facts from the exams officer
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and, for a Cambridge entry, the administrative zone. Those four turn an impossible comparison of tutors into a straightforward one, and they decide which past papers are worth your child's evening. A single email produces all four.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a predicted grade
process.description: A script shows which of the seven error categories is costing marks. A predicted grade records a teacher's estimate of an outcome. Only one of those can be planned against, which is why the free first lesson is spent producing a marked script rather than discussing one.

process.title: One tutor proposed, with the code named
process.description: You receive a single match with the syllabus they have taught, the tier, their permit position and whether they are UAE-based. Where coverage in your slot is thin you are told at this stage. No shortlist, because a shortlist returns the assessment to the parent who cannot make it.

process.title: Flag the tier while it is still movable
process.description: If the marked paper suggests the tier is wrong, you hear that in writing early enough to take it to the subject teacher before final entries are submitted. The decision belongs to the school; the evidence is what makes the conversation useful rather than awkward.

process.title: Topic work, then timed papers, then stop
process.description: Topics until two are secure, then mixed timed papers, with a halfway review against a paper the student has not practised. When the work is done the booking ends, and if a bridging block into Diploma mathematics is what is actually needed, we say so rather than extending the current one.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is between syllabuses, not neighbourhoods
whyPoints.description: Exactly one syllabus code appeared across the whole area cluster researched for this project. Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are separate qualifications, and matching a tutor to the code is the difference between practice that transfers and practice that does not.

whyPoints.title: The tier is flagged while it can still change
whyPoints.description: A Core entry caps the grade at C and the tier is fixed once the centre submits final entries, which happens months ahead of the first paper of the June or November series. Your exams officer holds that date. A marked paper in the autumn is the only thing that makes the tier conversation productive rather than awkward.

whyPoints.title: Paper details point at the board, not at us
whyPoints.description: Paper counts, durations and calculator permissions are revised between series, so this page links the current Cambridge syllabus and Pearson specification rather than restating arrangements that can change. Several pages in this market still display superseded details.

whyPoints.title: The Diploma gap is named topic by topic
whyPoints.description: Radians, exact values without a calculator, composite function notation and calculus. One competitor page has a single subheading about this transition; nobody publishes a structured version, and it is the commonest cause of a disappointing first Diploma report.

whyPoints.title: The cheapest adequate rung is recommended
whyPoints.description: For a standard Extended entry the right band is a qualified subject tutor at the published AED 150 to 300, not the premium tier at AED 500 to 650 and above. A page that recommends its own most expensive option for every request is selling rather than advising.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE mathematics syllabus my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for four things: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and, where the entry is with Cambridge, the administrative zone. The code will be something like 0580, 0607 or 4MA1, and it decides which past papers are useful and which are a waste of an evening. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0607 harder than 0580?
faqs.answer: It is a different syllabus rather than a harder one. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is built around a graphics calculator and carries an investigation flavour in parts of its assessment, where 0580 is a more conventional structured syllabus. Students on 0607 lose marks to device fluency rather than to the mathematics, which is a different problem needing different practice. Both are tiered, so both carry a grade ceiling at the lower tier. For the current paper arrangements of either, read the syllabus for the series on cambridgeinternational.org.

faqs.question: Does Pearson 4MA1 cover the same content as Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps substantially and the assessment does not. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers where Cambridge uses Core and Extended, and Pearson sets questions in its own recognisable house style. The practical consequence is that a student revising from Cambridge past papers for a Pearson entry has rehearsed the wrong phrasing and will meet unfamiliar question shapes under time pressure. Confirm the code with the school and read the current specification on qualifications.pearson.com for the series your child is sitting.

faqs.question: What is the highest grade available on a Cambridge Core entry?
faqs.answer: C. The Core tier covers the shared content of the syllabus and caps the available grade there, while Extended opens the full A* to E range. That ceiling is sufficient for some post-16 routes and closes others, notably A Level mathematics and either Diploma mathematics course at Higher Level. Parents often discover it from a sixth-form entry requirement rather than from a school report. The tier is set by the school on the subject teacher's recommendation and is fixed once final entries are submitted to the board.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose marks when her answers are correct?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the marks were not allocated to the answer. Mark schemes award method marks for the working, so a correct final figure with nothing between it and the question collects a fraction of what was available. Angle reasoning questions award marks for naming the theorem rather than for the number. Transformation questions award marks for a complete description, so a rotation without its centre and direction loses credit already earned. Graph questions award marks for intercepts and asymptotes, which go unlabelled. All of those are habits, not knowledge gaps.

faqs.question: Which calculator should my son be using for IGCSE mathematics?
faqs.answer: The model the school uses, which the mathematics department will name. It matters more than parents expect: for Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 a graphics calculator is integral to the course rather than an aid to it, so fluency with the specific device is part of the preparation. For other syllabuses the calculator permissions are set in the current syllabus for the series entered, and Cambridge and Pearson revise those arrangements between series, so read the board's own document rather than any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE Extended to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Specific rather than vague, which is the good news. Four things close it: radians, which IGCSE never uses and the Diploma treats as default; exact values and surds without a calculator, because Analysis and Approaches sits a non-calculator paper; composite and inverse function notation, which is a language obstacle more than a mathematical one; and calculus, absent from the main IGCSE syllabuses and assumed from the first term of DP1. Four to six sessions across a summer, aimed at exactly those, changes the first Diploma report more than the same hours spent in October.

faqs.question: Would a mathematics tutor living in Arabian Ranches 2 teach anything different?
faqs.answer: No. The tutor's address has no bearing on the syllabus, the tier, the papers or the mark scheme, and children in Arabian Ranches 2, Mudon, Town Square and Arabian Ranches 3 attend overlapping campuses and sit the same entries. What proximity changes is journey time, and because lessons run over live video there is no journey to change. What actually differs between tutors is which syllabus code they have taught and how many cohorts of it they have taken through a series, and that is the thing to ask about.

faqs.question: Can my child take Additional Mathematics alongside the main IGCSE entry?
faqs.answer: If the campus offers it. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is taken by secure Extended students, usually in Year 11 and in addition to the main entry rather than instead of it, and Pearson centres may offer Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 to similar effect. Both introduce calculus, further algebra and more trigonometry, which is the material the Diploma assumes from day one. Availability varies between campuses in the same belt, so ask the school whether it runs one, who is eligible and when the decision is made.

faqs.question: How many mathematics sessions a week does a Year 11 in Dubai actually need?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, plus the student's own practice between them. A single well-used hour with a marked paper behind it does more than two unfocused ones, because the limiting factor is usually what the student does in the six days between sessions rather than the session itself. Two a week earns its place in the final eight weeks before a series, when timed papers need running alongside topic work. Three is almost always a sign that the diagnosis was never done properly in the first place.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting mathematics support in Year 10 rather than Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper in every sense. The tier is still open, the entry deadline is a year away, the content being taught is current rather than historical, and a habit built then carries through the second year without further spend. Year 11 support is reactive by design: the hardest material is landing, the mock has usually already happened, and the tier may already be fixed. Most families call after the first Year 11 mock, which is roughly four months after the result it reports was decided.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE mathematics tutoring cost around Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3?
faqs.answer: The band that matches most Year 11 needs is a qualified subject tutor working online, published at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Below that, budget online tuition runs AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which suits consolidation rather than Extended-tier technique. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Those are other providers' published figures, cited so you can check them, and the geography makes no difference to any of them.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor if the school has a strong KHDA inspection rating?
faqs.answer: The two questions are answered with different evidence. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the outcome describes the institution: leadership, teaching across the school, provision for different groups. A strongly rated school can still have a Year 11 losing fifteen marks a paper to unshown method, and a lower-rated school can teach mathematics very well. The band helps you choose a campus. A marked past paper tells you what your own child needs, and nothing else does.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover mathematics and a science in the same week?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and it is one of the more sensible pairings. Mathematics and physics in particular share technique: unit discipline, rearranging formulae, graph interpretation and the habit of showing method. A single tutor covering both keeps that teaching consistent and gives the household one slot to protect instead of two. Three separate sciences plus mathematics is a different matter and is usually two people. We say which it should be at the match stage rather than agreeing to whatever is asked for.

faqs.question: What happens if no IGCSE mathematics tutor is free at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: You are told at the match stage rather than left waiting. Mathematics is the best-staffed subject in this set on UAE evening hours, so a straightforward Extended or Higher-tier request is usually filled within a few days. The slots that get tight are the final weeks before a series and the 16:30 to 17:00 window that every family in the belt wants. If the person who fits is in India rather than the UAE, that is on the table before any money is, and the lesson keeps its Gulf Standard Time slot.

Send us the four facts and the hour your child is genuinely free. intro.heading: The right day matters more than the right hour
paragraphs: Most tutoring schedules are built around a convenient time. For IGCSE mathematics that is a mistake, because the subject has a weekly rhythm set by the school: homework is assigned on a particular day, due on another, and returned marked some days later. A session's value depends enormously on where in that cycle it falls, and almost nobody asks.

A session the evening before the deadline works on live material. The student has attempted the questions, has met their own confusion, and a tutor can intervene while it matters. A session two days after the work was returned marked works on history: the questions are closed, the student has moved on, and the hour becomes a review of something nobody is invested in. The teaching is the same. The effect is not.

On Bluewaters Island this is more than an optimisation. The island is a compact residential community off JBR joined to the mainland by one road bridge, with no school on it. Every child commutes inland to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, The Greens, Jumeirah Park or Emirates Hills, and arrives home late enough that the week holds perhaps one genuinely usable weekday evening. If there is only one slot available, it had better be on the right day.

So this page starts with the homework cycle, then covers what maths work survives a tired six o'clock session and what does not, then the board and tier questions that determine what material the hours go into. The order is deliberate: a family with the right day and a slightly wrong revision emphasis will outperform one with a perfect plan on the wrong evening.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. There is a specific consequence for this page: because nobody travels, a session can be thirty minutes and can move to a different day when the school changes its homework pattern. An in-home arrangement cannot do either, since no tutor crosses the bridge in evening traffic for half an hour.

One calendar outranks the school's homework cycle, and it is the board's. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, so the day-of-week argument on this page operates inside a window that ends on a fixed date rather than a flexible one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable runs to 19 November 2026. Everything on this page was reviewed in October 2026. Where a timetable decides anything for you, open the board's own live PDF rather than any restatement of it, this one included.

One clarification before the detail. None of this assumes a struggling student. The homework-cycle argument applies just as strongly to a capable one, because the marks a capable IGCSE mathematician loses are overwhelmingly method marks and notational slips rather than gaps in understanding, and those are visible only in work they have actually attempted. A session on the wrong day will teach them topics they already know; a session on the right day will show them the four marks a week they are handing back.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bluewaters-is.programmesIntro: Three mathematics qualifications appear in Bluewaters households at this stage, and they are frequently confused. The difference between a tier and a separate syllabus is the one that causes most trouble.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Tiered Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. Core covers number, algebra, geometry, mensuration, basic trigonometry, statistics and probability. Extended adds functions, harder algebraic manipulation, the sine and cosine rules, vectors and transformations. Each tier is assessed by two written papers at the end of the course.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. The zone governs study leave planning, so ask the exams officer for it alongside the syllabus code.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher, graded 9-1, assessed by two written papers per tier. Higher tier content includes algebraic fractions, functions and their inverses, vectors and advanced trigonometry. Foundation tier carries a grade ceiling in line with Pearson's published tier arrangements for the qualification.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables a year ahead and revises them, so plan against the live official PDF. The results calendar matters locally twice a year: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate qualification rather than a tier, taken alongside 0580 Extended by a small strong cohort. Content covers functions, the quadratic discriminant, non-linear simultaneous equations, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, differentiation, integration and kinematics. It is the closest thing to A Level Mathematics available at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one subject on this page that does not suit a short tired slot. It is abstract and demanding, needs a fresh student and a proper run at a topic, and belongs on a weekend morning. Local specialist supply is also thin, because the cohort in any one Dubai community is small.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bluewaters-is.subjectsIntro: Maths topics grouped by whether they suit a short weekday slot or need a weekend morning. This is the scheduling information that decides whether a plan survives, and no provider publishes it.

subjects.name: Method marks and visible working
subjects.description: The largest avoidable loss in the qualification, because the mark scheme awards reasoning separately from the answer. Pure habit formation, which means it suits thirty minutes twice a week far better than an hour once, and it pays on both papers.

subjects.name: Bounds and estimation
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds produce more lost marks per question than any other number topic, usually because students round rather than bound. Mechanical, learnable in one session, and perfectly suited to a short tired slot.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Changing the subject where it appears twice, and simplifying algebraic fractions. Drills well in short bursts. The losses are almost always unwritten steps rather than misunderstanding, which is why this pairs naturally with method-mark work.

subjects.name: Quadratics
subjects.description: Factorising, completing the square and the formula. The recurring loss is using the formula where the question wanted completed square form for a minimum point, leaving the second part unanswerable. Needs a moderately alert student but fits a weekday slot.

subjects.name: Circle theorems
subjects.description: High-frequency and high-return, because the marks are for naming the theorem rather than reaching the angle. Short, self-contained questions that work well late in the day, and a reliable source of recovered marks.

subjects.name: Non-right-angled trigonometry
subjects.description: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area, including the ambiguous case where two answers exist. Needs more alertness than circle theorems because rule selection is a judgement, so better earlier in the evening.

subjects.name: Histograms and frequency density
subjects.description: Frequency density is the most misunderstood quantity in the qualification, and plotting raw frequency against unequal class widths loses the entire question. Conceptual to fix, then mechanical, so one alert session then short practice.

subjects.name: Conditional probability
subjects.description: Tree and Venn diagrams without replacement, where students reuse the first denominator on the second branch. Needs concentration to establish and then drills well, so introduce it fresh and practise it tired.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic is straightforward; describing a transformation fully is not. A rotation needs the angle, direction and centre, and two of three scores partially. Checklist-type work that suits a short slot.

subjects.name: Full timed papers
subjects.description: Needs an uninterrupted block and real concentration, plus time to mark against the published mark scheme in the same session. This belongs on a weekend morning and never in a weekday evening after a bridge crossing.

sections.heading: Find the maths homework cycle, then pick the day
paragraphs: Ask your child two questions: which day is maths homework set, and which day is it due. Then ask when marked work usually comes back. Those three answers determine where in the week a session is worth most, and they take one conversation to establish. Schools differ, and some set maths twice weekly, which changes the answer again.

The pre-deadline evening is the strongest placement. The student has attempted the questions and met their own confusion, which means the session starts from a real difficulty rather than from a tutor's guess about what might be difficult. It also means the work goes in improved rather than being corrected after the fact, and the student sees the connection between the session and their own mark.

The post-return placement is the second-best and serves a different purpose. For a student making consistent errors they cannot see, the marked script is better material than live homework, because the pattern is visible across several questions. A student losing method marks throughout, or mishandling bounds every time, needs the diagnosis rather than the rescue.

The worst placement, and the most common, is a session two or three days after work was returned and before the next is set. Nothing is live, nothing is urgent, and the hour becomes generic practice. That is also precisely the slot families are offered when they ask for availability rather than asking which day would be best, and it is the main reason weekly maths tutoring so often feels like it is not doing much.

sections.heading: The honesty line inside the homework cycle
paragraphs: Placing a session before a deadline raises a question that deserves a direct answer, because it is where well-meaning tutoring most easily goes wrong. A tutor working on homework due tomorrow must be teaching the method, not completing the assignment.

The distinction is practical rather than philosophical. If the student has attempted the questions and is stuck on question seven, teaching the technique that question seven requires and then having the student do it is teaching. Working through question seven while the student copies is not, and the fact that the student watched does not change what the teacher's mark will be measuring.

This is why we ask that the student attempts the work before the session rather than bringing it untouched. An untouched sheet invites the tutor to lead, and a student who watches a solution appear learns substantially less than one who has already failed at it and then sees why. It also means the session can be short, because the diagnosis is already done by the student's own attempt.

Where school-set work is formally assessed rather than practice, the line tightens further. A tutor teaches the skills, explains what the criteria reward, questions the approach, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any part of it. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material, and we work from papers the school or student already holds legitimately.

sections.heading: Maths at six o'clock: what survives a tired slot
paragraphs: A Bluewaters secondary student arriving home between half past four and half past five has limited cognitive capacity for a session at six, and pretending otherwise is how good plans fail. The useful response is not to abandon the weekday slot but to put the right maths in it.

Habit work survives tiredness well, and in IGCSE mathematics habit work is where most of the recoverable marks sit. Writing the method step, converting units as a separate line, labelling the axes, writing the denominators on a probability tree before multiplying, stating the theorem used in a circle question: all of these are mechanical, all are worth marks on both papers, and none requires insight. A tired student can establish a habit perfectly well.

Conceptual work does not survive tiredness. Introducing frequency density, establishing why the ambiguous case of the sine rule exists, or working out how to approach an unfamiliar structured question all need a student who can hold several things in mind at once. Introduce those fresh and practise them tired, which is the opposite of how most schedules are built.

Additional Mathematics 0606 is the clear exception to any weekday placement. It is abstract and demanding, the cohort taking it is strong enough that the work is genuinely difficult, and a tired session achieves very little. Put it on a weekend morning or accept that it will go slowly. Full timed papers belong there too, because they need an uninterrupted block plus time to mark in the same session.

sections.heading: Why a local tutor cannot offer the day or the length
paragraphs: Everything above depends on two freedoms: choosing the day from the homework cycle, and choosing a length the student can actually use. An in-home arrangement on Bluewaters Island struggles with both, for reasons that are about geography rather than willingness.

On length, the arithmetic is simple. A tutor coming from the Al Barsha campus ring at five faces Sheikh Zayed Road, the Marina approach, one bridge and then visitor parking in a residential tower, which is thirty to forty-five minutes each way. Nobody makes that journey for a thirty-minute lesson, so in-home arrangements are locked to hour blocks whether or not a tired fifteen-year-old can use sixty minutes. The published Dubai travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour, visible in the gap between the in-home band of AED 180-350 and the online band of AED 150-300, is that journey priced in.

On the day, the constraint is scheduling. A tutor filling an evening with three island families has a route, and moving one family to a different day breaks it. So when a school changes its homework pattern in January, which happens, the family that needs to move from Tuesday to Wednesday finds they cannot, and the session stays on the wrong day for the rest of the year.

IB Gram does not offer UAE home visits, so this is not a comparison between two things we sell; it is why we only sell one here. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present, an independent local tutor across the Marina or JBR can genuinely be the better choice, and the hour-block constraint matters far less at that age.

sections.heading: Syllabus code and tier, because the hours need the right material
paragraphs: Once the day is right, the content needs to be right, and that starts with one email to the exams officer asking for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series. In a school entering candidates with both boards the answer differs by subject, which is why a report card can show 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades without any error.

Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher on the 9-1 scale. Both assess by two written papers per tier, but content emphasis differs: Cambridge Extended weights functions, transformations and vectors, while Pearson Higher gives more attention to algebraic fractions and inverse and composite functions. A student revising from the wrong board's past papers is practising for an exam nobody is sitting.

The tier answer carries the hard consequence. A Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform, and if a sixth-form entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, the tier has settled the outcome before revision begins. The decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and close to closed by the second term of Year 11, because Extended content never taught would have to be learned alongside revising everything else.

Also establish whether 0606 Additional Mathematics is in play, because it is a separate qualification rather than a tier and it is routinely confused with one. It suits a student comfortably at the top of 0580 Extended and is the best preparation for A Level Mathematics available at sixteen. For a student working hard for a B on Extended, the same hours are better spent securing that grade.

sections.heading: The mock term, when the cycle itself changes
paragraphs: Mock season breaks the homework cycle, and a plan built on it has to be rebuilt rather than continued. Homework gives way to revision tasks, school days lengthen with revision sessions so arrival moves later, and the material becomes past papers rather than exercises. The pre-deadline logic stops applying because there are no deadlines of the same kind.

What replaces it is the mock script. Ask the school for component marks rather than the grade, because the grade blends three unrelated problems. Clusters of blank or abandoned questions mean content gaps needing teaching in dependency order. Attempted questions marked low across the paper mean method marks and command-term misreads, which is the fastest thing to fix and where most recoverable marks sit. A script strong at the start and thin at the end is a pacing problem.

The weekend morning becomes the most valuable block in the week at this point, because timed papers are now the highest-return activity and they need an uninterrupted run plus marking in the same session. The weekday slot is better spent on the two or three topics the script identified rather than on broad revision, which feels productive and improves very little.

And if arrival has moved later, move the slot rather than accepting late starts. Three weeks of a session beginning twenty minutes late, followed by a quiet stop, is how most tutoring arrangements end, and they end in the term they were bought for.

sections.heading: What it costs at this session length
paragraphs: Because this page recommends shorter sessions, the cost figures need stating at that length rather than per nominal hour. The Dubai market bands, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table, are as follows.

Start with the band this page rules out. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs AED 180-350 an hour and rises to AED 500 at specialist levels, and none of it is available in thirty-minute units, because the travel is the cost. Online, the figures read as follows. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified IGCSE subject tutors at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. Halve each of those for a thirty-minute session and the half-hour at the qualified band costs roughly what a single in-home hour does at the bottom of its range.

Converted to the patterns here: a thirty-minute weekday session across a twelve-week term is six hours, or AED 900 to AED 1,800 at the qualified band. Two thirty-minute sessions a week is twelve hours, or AED 1,800 to AED 3,600. Adding a weekend morning block for papers and 0606 takes the term towards twenty hours. For most IGCSE mathematics work the qualified band is the right one, and the specialist band is worth paying mainly for 0606 and for a late tier move.

One piece of context matters for the term arithmetic above. The other half of a Dubai education budget is school fees, and for 2026-27 that half is not moving: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A term of twice-weekly half-hours is therefore being added to a known figure rather than to a moving one, which is the right condition for committing to a full twelve weeks on a fixed weekday instead of buying hours ad hoc when a test appears. None of the rates set out here are IB Gram prices; they are what other Dubai providers publish. This page carries no price list, and the first session is a free trial.

sections.heading: Permits, verification and starting
paragraphs: Individual tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system, and u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Dubai private schools themselves are overseen by KHDA, which inspects annually and publishes ratings from Outstanding to Very Weak. Those reports are free and public. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence for training institutes with physical premises, and has no UAE office.

To start, send four things: the syllabus code, the tier, which day maths homework is set and due, and a recent marked paper. The first two determine the material, the third determines the day, and the marked script determines whether the work is habit formation, a specific content gap or pacing. That combination makes the first session useful rather than exploratory.

Then take the free trial lesson, run at the day, time and length we intend the weekly session to be, so you find out whether it works before committing. No card is held, nothing renews, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots are a normal request and the slot is held. What we will not do, on the island or anywhere in the UAE, is send a tutor to your address; that service runs in India only.

process.title: Ask which day maths is set and due
process.description: Two questions to your child, plus when marked work comes back. Those three answers decide where in the week a session is worth most, and they are the ones nobody asks for. Some schools set maths twice weekly, which changes the answer again.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and tier
process.description: One email to the exams officer: board, syllabus code, tier, series, and the Cambridge administrative zone. Cambridge 0580 Core is capped at grade C and Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher on 9-1, so the answer changes both the material and what grade is reachable.

process.title: Send a recent marked paper
process.description: It shows whether the losses are method marks, a specific topic or running out of time. Those three need different work and different session lengths, and a report card only confirms that something is wrong, which you already knew before searching.

process.title: Trial at the real day, time and length
process.description: We run the free trial on the day and at the length we intend the weekly session to be, so you find out whether a Bluewaters evening slot actually works before committing. A short written note follows, no card is held and nothing renews.

process.title: Rebuild when the cycle changes
process.description: Mock season replaces homework with revision and lengthens the school day, so the pre-deadline logic stops applying and arrival moves later. We rebuild from the mock script and move the slot rather than letting late starts erode a session that was working.

whyPoints.title: The day is chosen, not inherited
whyPoints.description: A session the evening before maths homework is due works on live material the student has already struggled with. One placed two days after marked work returns works on a closed assignment nobody is invested in. Same teaching, very different effect, and nobody else asks the question.

whyPoints.title: Thirty minutes genuinely offered
whyPoints.description: Habit work such as method marks, bounds and unit conversion suits thirty minutes twice a week better than an hour once, because the repetition interval matters more than the block. In-home arrangements cannot offer that length, since no tutor crosses a bridge for half an hour.

whyPoints.title: Tired work and fresh work separated
whyPoints.description: Habit formation survives a six o'clock slot after a long commute. Introducing frequency density or the ambiguous case does not, and Additional Mathematics 0606 certainly does not. We introduce concepts fresh and practise them tired, which is the reverse of how most schedules are built.

whyPoints.title: The homework honesty line stated
whyPoints.description: The student attempts the work before the session, and the tutor teaches the method rather than completing the questions. An untouched sheet invites the tutor to lead and teaches the student less, so we ask for the attempt first as a matter of method, not just of principle.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different exams with different tiers, grading and content emphasis. We ask for the code before matching anybody, because revising from the wrong board's past papers costs a term rather than a session.

whyPoints.title: The slot can move when the school changes
whyPoints.description: Schools alter homework patterns, and mock season changes everything. Online, moving a session from Tuesday to Wednesday is trivial. An in-home tutor with an evening route across the bridge cannot do it, so the session stays on the wrong day for the rest of the year.

faqs.question: Does it really matter which day the maths session falls on?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, and it is the cheapest improvement available. A session the evening before maths homework is due works on live questions the student has already attempted and got stuck on, so the intervention lands in real confusion and before the work is submitted. A session two days after marked work returns works on a closed assignment nobody is invested in, and becomes generic practice. Ask your child which day maths is set, which day it is due, and when marked work comes back, then place the session accordingly.

faqs.question: Is thirty minutes of maths tutoring actually useful?
faqs.answer: For a great deal of IGCSE maths work, yes, and often more useful than an hour. Habit work is where most recoverable marks sit: writing the method step, converting units as a separate line, labelling axes, writing denominators on a probability tree before multiplying, naming the theorem in a circle question. All of that is mechanical and benefits from short frequent repetition rather than long blocks, so thirty minutes twice a week beats sixty once. The exceptions are first teaching of a concept, full timed papers and Additional Mathematics 0606.

faqs.question: What maths work can a tired fifteen-year-old actually do at six?
faqs.answer: Habit and mechanical work, which fortunately is where the marks are. Method-mark discipline, bounds, unit conversion, circle theorem practice, transformation checklists and probability tree layout all survive a tired slot because they need persistence rather than insight. What does not survive is first teaching of frequency density or the ambiguous case of the sine rule, where a student has to hold several ideas at once. Introduce those fresh at the weekend and practise them tired on a weekday, which is the opposite of how most schedules are built.

faqs.question: Will the tutor just do my son's homework with him?
faqs.answer: No, and we ask for the work to be attempted before the session partly to prevent that. If he has tried the questions and is stuck on question seven, teaching the technique that question seven needs and then having him do it is teaching. Working through it while he watches is not, whatever it feels like, because the teacher's mark will measure what he can do alone. An untouched sheet also invites the tutor to lead, and a student who watches a solution appear learns substantially less than one who failed first.

faqs.question: Why can an online tutor offer half an hour when a local one cannot?
faqs.answer: Because the journey has to justify the trip. A tutor coming from the Al Barsha campus ring at five faces Sheikh Zayed Road, the Marina approach, one bridge and visitor parking, which is thirty to forty-five minutes each way, and nobody makes that for a thirty-minute lesson. So in-home arrangements are locked to hour blocks whether or not a tired student can use sixty minutes. The published travel premium of AED 50-150 an hour, visible between the in-home and online bands, is that journey priced into the rate.

faqs.question: Our school changed its homework days in January. Can the session move?
faqs.answer: Online, easily, and that flexibility is worth more than it sounds. Schools do alter homework patterns mid-year, and a session that was placed perfectly in September can end up on the worst day of the week by February. An in-home tutor filling an evening with three island families has a route, and moving one family breaks it, so in practice the session stays where it is. Tell us when the pattern changes and we move the slot, which takes one message rather than a renegotiation.

faqs.question: Which syllabus is our daughter sitting, 0580 or 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Email the exams officer and ask for the board, syllabus code, tier and series in writing, plus which Cambridge administrative zone the school sits in. In a school entering candidates with both boards, mathematics can be on one and the sciences on another, which is why a report card can show 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades with nothing wrong. It matters because content emphasis and question phrasing differ, so revising from the wrong board's past papers is practice for an exam nobody is sitting.

faqs.question: Can our son move up from Core to Extended in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Rarely after the first term, and the ceiling is why it matters. Cambridge 0580 Core is capped at grade C, so a student at the very top of the tier cannot be awarded a B, and if his sixth-form requirement is a B or a grade 6 the tier has already settled it. A move in the second term of Year 11 means learning Extended content he never met alongside revising everything else. If it is being considered, ask the school for a timed Extended paper and decide from the script rather than from classwork.

faqs.question: Should Additional Mathematics 0606 go in the weekday slot?
faqs.answer: No. It is the clearest exception on this page. 0606 is a separate qualification rather than a tier, covering functions, the discriminant, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, differentiation, integration and kinematics, and it is abstract enough that a tired weekday session achieves very little. Put it on a weekend morning. It also suits only a student comfortably at the top of 0580 Extended; for one working hard for a B, the same hours are better spent securing that grade instead.

faqs.question: What changes in the mock term?
faqs.answer: The cycle itself. Homework gives way to revision tasks, so the pre-deadline logic stops applying, and school days lengthen with revision sessions so arrival moves later. Rebuild from the mock script instead: ask for component marks rather than the grade, because blank questions mean content gaps, low marks on attempted questions mean method marks and command-term misreads, and a script that thins at the end means pacing. The weekend morning becomes the most valuable block, because timed papers are now the highest-return activity available.

faqs.question: What does a short weekly maths session cost across a term?
faqs.answer: A thirty-minute weekly session across a twelve-week Dubai term is six hours, which at the market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online of roughly AED 150-300 an hour is AED 900 to AED 1,800. Two thirty-minute sessions a week is twelve hours, or AED 1,800 to AED 3,600. Specialists sit higher at AED 200-450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and for most IGCSE mathematics work the qualified band is the right one. Figures read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table.

faqs.question: Which single habit recovers the most maths marks?
faqs.answer: Writing the method. The mark scheme awards visible reasoning separately from the final answer, so a student who rearranges an equation in their head and writes only the result forfeits marks they genuinely earned, on every paper and in every tier on both boards. It is a habit rather than a knowledge problem, which means short frequent practice establishes it in two or three weeks, and it is the first thing we work on for most students because the return per minute is higher than any topic revision.

faqs.question: Do you send a maths tutor to our apartment on Bluewaters?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. On this page that matters for two specific reasons: because nobody travels, a session can be thirty minutes, and it can move to a different day when the school changes its homework pattern. Independent home tutors do work across the Marina and JBR at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, and for a younger child who needs an adult physically present they can be the better choice.

faqs.question: Which exam sittings will a Dubai IGCSE maths candidate have?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise, so ask which zone applies.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. A MoHRE private tuition work permit is required, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system. u.ae states that tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so distrust any amount quoted.

intro.heading: Count the weeks to the paper before you buy a single hour
paragraphs: There is a question that should come before any discussion of a tutor, a rate or a topic list: which series is your child entered for, and how many weeks away is it? UAE candidates sit two Cambridge series a year, June and November, and two Pearson International GCSE series, May/June and November. The February and March series that circulates online is offered to India only and does not apply to a student in Bur Dubai. Families who book maths tuition without establishing the series routinely buy the wrong shape of help: a two-year programme when eleven weeks remain, or crisis revision when there was a whole year to use properly.

The second date that controls everything is the entry deadline, and almost nobody outside a school exams office thinks about it. Entries close months before the papers are sat. Your child's school makes the entry, and it is the entry that fixes the board, the syllabus code and - critically - the tier. Once Foundation tier has been entered with Pearson, or Core with Cambridge, the grade ceiling is set and no amount of tutoring lifts it. A tutor brought in during the spring term of Year 11 to rescue a grade that the tier does not permit is being asked to do something arithmetically impossible.

So the honest sequence for a Bur Dubai family is: find the syllabus code on the exam entry slip or ask the maths department, confirm the series, confirm the tier, then count the weeks. That gives you a number, and the number tells you what to buy. Twelve weeks out, the right purchase is a tight programme of past-paper work on the three or four topics that carry the most marks. Fifteen months out, it is a weekly hour that builds algebraic fluency slowly and makes the tier decision from a position of strength rather than panic.

There is a third date most families never hear about, and it is a genuine second chance. A student who sits June and is disappointed can enter the November series in the same calendar year and get a fresh result before university applications harden. The Pearson International GCSE November final timetable has run from late October to 19 November, with results reaching students in January - November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. That window is a real strategic option and it changes what a summer of tutoring is for.

One practical note on how we work. IB Gram is an online platform, and for families anywhere in the UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For maths against a deadline this is an advantage rather than a concession - a shared screen with a past paper, a worked solution and the mark scheme's own wording side by side does more in an hour than a tutor working from a textbook across a dining table, and the hour does not move because Khalid Bin Al Waleed Road is blocked.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bur-dubai.programmesIntro: Four routes a Bur Dubai student might be on. The syllabus code matters more than the subject name, because the papers, the calculator rules and the grade scale differ between them.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The most common route in Dubai. Two tiers: Core, assessed by a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of 1 hour 30 minutes each, and Extended, assessed by a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of 2 hours each. Each paper carries 50 per cent. The non-calculator component is the change most families have not adjusted to, and it rewards arithmetic and algebraic fluency that a calculator previously hid.
programmes.countryNote: Sat in the June and November series by UAE centres. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your school's exams officer knows the zone; ask rather than assume.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A
programmes.description: Two papers of 2 hours, 100 marks each, 50 per cent each, with a calculator permitted in both. Tiered: Foundation covers grades 5 to 1, Higher covers 9 to 4 with an allowed grade 3. Because both papers allow a calculator, the failure mode differs from Cambridge - students lose marks on method and on reading the question rather than on arithmetic, and the tutoring emphasis shifts accordingly.
programmes.countryNote: Available in May/June and November each year. The November final timetable has run from late October to 19 November, with results to students in January. June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: A different syllabus from 0580, not a variant of it. It assumes a graphics calculator throughout and includes an investigation-style component, which makes it a closer fit for students heading into IB Mathematics. Students and parents frequently confuse it with 0580 when searching for past papers, and working through the wrong code is one of the more wasteful mistakes available in a short run-in.
programmes.countryNote: Offered by a minority of Dubai schools, usually IB continuum schools running IGCSE in Years 10 and 11. If your child's school teaches 0607, graphics-calculator technique is a legitimate tutoring topic in its own right and worth two or three sessions on its own.

programmes.name: Spec B and Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Pearson Specification B (4MB1) and Cambridge Additional Mathematics (0606) are the harder options, usually taken by students intending A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. Spec B runs two papers of unequal length and a different style of question; 0606 is sat alongside 0580 rather than instead of it and introduces calculus. Both reward algebraic confidence over topic coverage.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Bur Dubai school offers Additional Mathematics alongside 0580, taking it is the single best preparation available for Diploma Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. It is also the subject most often dropped under timetable pressure, and that decision is worth thinking about in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: Topic by topic, this is where IGCSE maths marks actually go in the final weeks, and roughly how long each is worth spending on when the clock is short.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, solving. It appears in questions that are nominally about something else, so weakness here taxes the whole paper. On the Cambridge non-calculator paper it is unforgiving. If a student is shaky on fractions in algebra, that is the first eight hours of any short programme, whatever the topic list says.

subjects.name: Number and surds
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, ratio, percentages including reverse percentage, and surds at Extended level. Bounds questions are routinely dropped because students round early. On a non-calculator paper this section is pure technique and is the cheapest set of marks to recover in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Linear and quadratic graphs
subjects.description: Sketching, intersections, gradient, and solving graphically. Students who can solve a quadratic algebraically often cannot read the roots off a sketch, and examiners ask both. Accurate plotting with a sharp pencil and a sensible scale is worth real marks and takes one session to fix.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, then sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, and bearings. Bearings questions lose marks on diagram-drawing rather than on trigonometry. Three-dimensional trigonometry is the discriminating question at the top of the paper and is skipped by most mid-range candidates.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, then similar areas and volumes with their squared and cubed scale factors. The scale-factor questions are a classic trap: students apply a linear factor to an area. Worth a dedicated session because it recurs every series.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms with unequal class widths. The histogram question is where marks go: frequency density is either understood or guessed. Cumulative frequency reading errors are a close second.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs, and the four transformations with full descriptions. Describing a transformation fully - naming it and giving every parameter, centre, scale factor, mirror line - is a mark-scheme requirement students routinely half-satisfy. Fixable in a single session.

subjects.name: Functions and sequences
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, and nth-term rules including quadratic sequences. Composite function order is reversed by a large share of candidates. Quadratic sequences have a reliable method that is rarely taught explicitly and is worth teaching.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Not a topic, but worth timetabling. Fraction mode, memory, stored answers, degree versus radian, and the discipline of writing an unrounded intermediate value. Premature rounding costs accuracy marks on nearly every long question, and no amount of topic revision catches it.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Long multiplication and division, fraction arithmetic, surd simplification and index laws done cleanly by hand. The Cambridge non-calculator paper carries 50 per cent of the grade, and students who have always had a calculator need deliberate practice rather than reassurance. Ten minutes a day for six weeks does it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bur-dubai.regionsTitle: Bur Dubai and the districts around it
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bur-dubai.regionsIntro: Bur Dubai sits on the south bank of the creek inside the oldest and densest part of the city. What varies between these neighbourhoods is not the syllabus but the hour at which a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: Flats, short school runs and a heavy early-evening street. Students here are overwhelmingly in British or Indian curriculum schools, which makes IGCSE maths the single most-requested subject in the district.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Immediately west of Bur Dubai with its own school cluster. Many families walk or make a five-minute drive, so the 4pm slot is genuinely available here - rarer than it sounds in old Dubai, and worth claiming at the start of term.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense apartment living a few minutes inland. Shared study space and one laptop between siblings is the normal condition, not the exception, and staggered session times matter more than the tutor's postcode.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Sitting inside the school belt itself, with several large schools walking distance away. Short commutes mean the earliest slots are usable, which is the one real scheduling advantage in this part of Dubai.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Across the creek near the airport, with the closest concentrated IB provision to Bur Dubai. Students here more often sit 0607 than 0580, which changes the past papers a tutor should be using.

regions.name: Deira
regions.note: The north bank. Crossing the creek at five o'clock is unpredictable, which is why Deira students with a Bur Dubai school and Bur Dubai students with a Deira tutor both end up preferring a fixed online hour.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: A large British and Indian school belt further out towards Sharjah. Longer commutes push useful session times past six, and the Sharjah-side traffic makes any travel-dependent arrangement fragile in the exam term.

regions.name: Al Jaffiliya and Satwa
regions.note: Between Bur Dubai and Jumeirah, mixed housing, short runs to the Al Mankhool and Jumeirah school clusters. Families here often have children on two different boards, which is a timetable problem as much as a teaching one.

schoolClusters.city: Bur Dubai, Al Mankhool and Oud Metha

sections.heading: The IGCSE maths year counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Everything in an IGCSE maths plan follows from one date, and the date is not the exam. It is the entry deadline. Entries are made by your child's school months before the papers are sat, and the entry fixes the board, the syllabus code and the tier. After that point the grade ceiling is decided. This is why the useful conversation with a school happens in the autumn term of Year 11 rather than in the spring, and why a tutor engaged in February is working inside constraints nobody discussed with the family.

Work backwards from there and the year has a shape. Entries close. Mocks follow, usually using a real past paper, which makes a mock script the most valuable diagnostic document a family will get all year. Then a long revision run, then the series itself, then results. For Pearson International GCSE, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day; the November series final timetable has run from late October to 19 November, with results reaching students in January - November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. For Cambridge, UAE centres sit June and November, and the February/March series offered to India does not apply.

The zone point deserves its own sentence because it catches people out. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A parent printing a timetable found online rather than taking the school's own copy is taking a real risk for no reason. Ask the exams officer.

The table below is the planning document. Fill in your own dates from the school and the official board timetable, because provisional timetables get revised and a restated date on a web page ages badly. The milestones themselves do not change.
