sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision with a grade ceiling on it
paragraphs: Both major boards tier IGCSE mathematics, and the tier is the single most consequential academic decision in the two years. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation, covering grades 5 to 1, and Higher, covering 9 to 4 with an allowed grade 3. A student entered on the lower tier cannot be awarded a grade above that tier's ceiling however well they perform on the day. There is no appeal against arithmetic.

Schools make this decision for sound reasons. A student placed on a tier they cannot cope with can come out with nothing at all, and a secure grade on the lower tier is sometimes genuinely the better outcome. The problem is not the decision; it is that families frequently do not know it has been made. Ask explicitly, in writing, which tier your child is entered for and what the ceiling is. Then ask what evidence the decision rested on, and when it could be reviewed.

The practical consequence for tutoring is severe. If the goal is a grade 7 and the entry is Foundation, the tutoring cannot deliver it and anybody who implies otherwise is selling you something. If the entry is still open, tutoring aimed at the specific gap the department is worried about - usually algebra - can change the decision, and that is worth far more than generic revision. This is the argument for starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11: in Year 10 the tier is still a question, and in the spring of Year 11 it rarely is.

One more detail that matters for Pearson candidates. Because both 4MA1 papers permit a calculator, a Foundation candidate's marks are usually lost on method and question-reading rather than on arithmetic, while a Cambridge Core candidate faces a non-calculator paper worth half the grade. Two students on nominally equivalent lower tiers need quite different tutoring, and a tutor who does not ask for the syllabus code will not know which one they have.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1: the same mathematics, different papers
paragraphs: A Bur Dubai family with children at two different schools may well be dealing with both of these at once, and the assumption that they are interchangeable costs time. The mathematics overlaps heavily. The examination does not, and tutoring that ignores the difference produces a student who is well taught and under-prepared.

The headline difference is the calculator. Cambridge 0580 now sets one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper, each worth 50 per cent of the grade. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. That single fact redistributes where marks go. A Cambridge candidate must be able to handle fractions, surds, indices and long arithmetic cleanly by hand under time pressure, and this is the area in which students who have grown up with a calculator are weakest. A Pearson candidate faces longer papers - two hours each, 100 marks each - where the risk is losing method marks and misreading multi-part questions.

Paper length changes revision too. Two two-hour papers demand stamina that two ninety-minute papers do not, and a Pearson Higher candidate who has only ever worked in forty-minute homework blocks will fade in the last twenty marks. That is a training problem with a mechanical solution: build up to full-length timed papers from the start of the run-in rather than attempting one in the final fortnight and concluding the student cannot do it.

Then there is the grade scale, which confuses Dubai parents more than anything else on a report. Pearson International GCSE reports 9 to 1. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G on some syllabuses and 9 to 1 on others depending on the school's choice. A parent comparing a sibling's 7 with another's B is not comparing like with like. Ask the school which scale each child is on, and get the tier alongside it.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks out: what each block of weeks has to achieve
paragraphs: A twelve-week run-in is the most common situation a Bur Dubai family actually presents with, and it is workable if nobody pretends it is a two-year programme compressed. Twelve weeks cannot cover the syllabus. It can convert a student who knows most of the content into one who converts that knowledge into marks, which is usually where the missing grade is hiding.

Weeks twelve to ten are diagnostic and nothing else. One full past paper, under timed conditions, marked against the real mark scheme rather than generously. The output is not a grade; it is a list of where marks were lost, sorted by how many. Almost always three or four topics account for the bulk of it, and those are the only topics the programme should touch. Resist the urge to start with the topic the student dislikes most - start with the one costing the most marks, which is rarely the same thing.

Weeks nine to five are repair plus consolidation. Teach the identified topics properly, then immediately set questions from past papers on those topics so the student sees them in exam form rather than in textbook form. A second timed paper in week seven checks whether the repair took. If it did not, change the approach rather than adding hours - a topic that has not landed twice will not land on the third identical attempt.

Weeks four to one are technique and nothing new. Full papers under timed conditions, marked hard, with a focus on the mechanical mark-losers: premature rounding, unlabelled transformations, incomplete descriptions, working not shown, questions abandoned instead of attempted for method marks. Introducing new content in the final fortnight reliably destabilises a student who was nearly ready, and we will say no to it.

sections.heading: The November series as a second attempt, and when it is the right call
paragraphs: This is the part of the calendar nobody explains to Dubai families. A student disappointed by a June result does not have to wait a year. Both major boards run a November series, and a student can enter it in the same calendar year. Pearson International GCSE November has had a final timetable running from late October to 19 November, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs November as the resit route for UAE centres.

Whether to take it is a genuine decision with arguments on both sides. In favour: a fresh result before sixth-form or university applications harden, a short and highly focused period of work with a clear target, and a student who now knows exactly what the paper feels like. Against: results in January can sit awkwardly against application timelines, the student is simultaneously starting a new course, and a resit with no change in approach tends to reproduce the original grade rather than improve on it.

That last point is the one worth dwelling on. The most common resit failure is repetition - more of the same revision, the same topics, the same technique - and it is predictable. If you are going to use November, the work has to start from evidence: the June script if the school can obtain it, or at minimum a fresh timed paper diagnosed properly in the first fortnight after results. Then the question of whether a tier change is possible, which is a conversation with the school and not with a tutor.

Two practical points. The entry deadline for November sits well before the series, so the decision has to be made quickly after August results - it is not a thing to think about in October. And private-candidate entry, where a student is no longer at the school that entered them, is a separate route with its own centre arrangements. Your school's exams office or an approved examination centre handles that; we teach the mathematics and we do not administer entries.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition costs around Bur Dubai, counted by the month
paragraphs: Most families think in hourly rates and then budget monthly, which is where the surprises come from. So take it monthly. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put the budget end at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-market at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year work at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the numbers that actually hit a household budget.

Converted back to the hour, the market splits into clear bands. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end, which buys homework supervision rather than examination coaching. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate puts IGCSE, IB and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits, which include the tutor's travel, are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors.

The calendar changes what you should be willing to pay. Fifteen months out, a mid-market weekly hour at the lower end of these bands is sensible and the compounding effect of consistent algebra practice is worth more than tutor prestige. Twelve weeks out, you are buying mark-scheme judgement and past-paper diagnosis, and the specialist band earns its premium because an experienced examiner-trained teacher reads a script faster and more accurately than a generalist. Two weeks out, almost nothing in the market is worth a premium, because the work left is technique the student has to practise themselves.

These are market figures, taken from each provider's own published rates as read in October 2026, and none of them are IB Gram prices - we do not publish a rate card on a landing page and we would rather you got a quote against your actual requirement. We also hold no office or centre in the UAE, and we are not accredited, approved or licensed by KHDA, Cambridge International or Pearson. Anyone in this market claiming such approval should be asked to show the permit number.

sections.heading: An in-home maths tutor in Bur Dubai against one-to-one online, with a deadline running
paragraphs: Parents in Bur Dubai look for a home tutor for reasons that make sense. A tutor in the room can be supervised, a younger child does not have to be left, and in a flat it is easier to keep an eye on whether the hour is being used. Those arguments are real and we are not going to dismiss them.

Our position, stated before you pay rather than after: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai family is one-to-one over live video. We say it on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits, and that is a trust failure a family discovers only after paying.

With a deadline running, the online format has concrete advantages rather than merely acceptable ones. A past paper, the student's own attempt and the official mark scheme can sit on one shared screen, annotated together in the tutor's own hand, and saved for the student to revisit before the next timed paper. That is close to impossible across a table with three sheets of paper. The hour also holds: it does not shift because Sheikh Zayed Road is stopped at 5.30pm, and in a twelve-week programme a session lost to traffic is eight per cent of the plan gone.

The supply argument is the strongest one. A Cambridge 0607 graphics-calculator specialist, or a teacher who has marked 4MA1 Higher and can read a script for method marks at speed, is not necessarily living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mankhool. Insisting on physical proximity narrows the pool to whoever is near, and for a specific syllabus code in a specific tier that is a real cost. The market data above also shows what the travel premium buys: in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the difference above the online band is paying for a drive.

sections.heading: KHDA, the school report and what an inspection band does not tell you about maths
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and which inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students and Indian at 26 per cent. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

Bur Dubai parents read inspection bands closely, and they are worth reading. What they do not tell you is anything specific about the maths department your child is in. A band is a judgement on a whole school across many measures. It does not say whether the Year 11 maths teaching is strong, whether the tier decisions are made generously or conservatively, or whether mock papers are marked to the real scheme. Those are the questions that affect an IGCSE maths grade, and the answers come from other parents in the same year group and from the head of mathematics.

There is also a timetable layer. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and a minimum advised lesson length of 25 minutes. Those hours are real and they sit in the same week as nine or ten IGCSE subjects. A Year 11 student who is struggling across several subjects may be struggling with load rather than with mathematics.

Finally, on equivalency, because it drives subject choices in Year 10. For the UAE Ministry of Education's British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case on the Ministry's own channel - we describe the process and do not perform or guarantee it.

sections.heading: Permits, private candidates and the things we will not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and a Bur Dubai parent is entitled to ask about it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published anywhere official, so no amount should be quoted to you.

One related rule worth knowing. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. If someone offers you your child's own maths teacher privately, that is an arrangement neither of them should be making.

On examination materials, we are deliberately narrow. We do not publish, reproduce or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or syllabus documents as downloads. We reference them, we cite the official source, and we link out, because reproducing them is somebody else's copyright. Where a student needs past papers, the school or the board's own site is the right route, and your child's teacher can usually provide them directly.

And on IB Gram itself, three plain statements. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson. We hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor headcount, because we cannot attach a sample size, a date and a method to any of them, and a statistic without those three things is decoration. Every AED figure on this page carries the provider who published it and the month we read it.

process.title: Find the syllabus code and the series
process.description: Before anything else, get the exam entry details: board, syllabus code, tier and series. It is on the entry slip or a one-line question to the maths department. Without it, a tutor is guessing between 0580, 0607, 4MA1 and 4MB1, and those four need different papers and different technique.

process.title: Count the weeks, then choose the shape
process.description: The number of weeks to the paper decides what to buy. Fifteen months means a weekly hour building algebraic fluency. Twelve weeks means a diagnosed run-in on three or four topics. Three weeks means technique and timed papers only. We will tell you which of those you are in.

process.title: A free trial, starting with a real paper
process.description: One session at no cost with the tutor you would continue with, spent on a past-paper question set from the correct syllabus and marked against the real scheme. You get a written note of where marks were actually lost, whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Fix the hour against the Bur Dubai afternoon
process.description: Pick a slot that survives the real school run rather than an optimistic one. Oud Metha and Al Mankhool households can often hold a 4pm start; Al Nahda and Deira-side families are usually better after six. The hour is in Gulf Standard Time and does not move for traffic.

process.title: Measure against timed papers, not opinions
process.description: Every two to three weeks, a full paper under timed conditions, marked hard. That is the only honest measure of whether the tutoring is working. We report the mark and the error pattern, and if it is not moving we change the tutor or the approach rather than adding hours.

process.title: Decide about November deliberately
process.description: If June does not go to plan, the November decision has to be made quickly after August results because the entry deadline sits well before the series. We will help you think it through from the evidence, and the entry itself is handled by the school or an approved examination centre.

whyPoints.title: We start from the entry, not the topic list
whyPoints.description: The first questions are the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series. Those four facts determine whether a target grade is even available and which past papers are the right ones. A tutor who does not ask them is working blind, and in a short run-in that is expensive.

whyPoints.title: Honest about grade ceilings
whyPoints.description: If the entry is Foundation tier and the goal is a 7, we say so rather than selling hours against an impossible target. Where the tier decision is still open we aim the work at the specific gap the department is worried about, because changing the entry is worth more than any amount of revision.

whyPoints.title: Past papers and mark schemes, not a tutor's own worksheets
whyPoints.description: Marks are awarded against a published scheme, and the fastest route to more of them is working inside that scheme's language. We work from the official papers through the school or the board's own site, and we do not host or redistribute them ourselves.

whyPoints.title: Clear about where the tutor sits
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video and we state it before payment. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE. Two providers in this market route UAE parents to overseas numbers without disclosing delivery, and we would rather lose the booking than copy that.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: The AED ranges on this page each name the provider who published them and the month they were read. We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor count, because we cannot attach a sample size and a method, and an unsourced number across thousands of pages is a liability rather than a selling point.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to stop
whyPoints.description: A twelve-week run-in ends. Technique practice in the final fortnight is the student's work, not a tutor's, and we will say so rather than booking hours nobody is measuring. If the timed-paper marks have plateaued, that is information, not a reason to buy more.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths exam series will my child in Bur Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge runs June as the main series with November as the resit route, and Pearson International GCSE is available in May/June and November each year. The February and March series that appears in online searches is offered to India only and does not apply to a student in Dubai. Your child's school makes the entry and the exams office can confirm the series in one email. Ask for it in writing, because the series determines the entire shape of any tutoring plan.

faqs.question: What is the entry deadline for IGCSE maths and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Entries are made by the school months before the papers are sat, and the entry fixes the board, the syllabus code and the tier. That last item is the reason it matters: once a lower tier is entered, the grade ceiling is set and tutoring cannot lift it. Ask the exams office, in writing, which tier your child is entered for and what the ceiling is. If the decision is still open, tutoring aimed at the department's specific concern - almost always algebra - can change it, and that is worth more than generic revision.

faqs.question: Can my child retake IGCSE maths in November if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both major boards run a November series and a student can enter it in the same calendar year. Pearson International GCSE November has had a final timetable running from late October to 19 November, with results reaching students in January - November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. The decision has to be made quickly after August results because the November entry deadline sits well before the series. A resit with no change in approach tends to reproduce the original grade, so start from the June script or a fresh diagnosed paper.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0607 just a harder version of 0580?
faqs.answer: They are separate syllabuses, not tiers of one. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 sets one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper, each worth 50 per cent. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 assumes a graphics calculator throughout and includes an investigation-style component, which makes it a closer fit for students heading into IB Mathematics. Working through 0580 past papers for a 0607 candidate is a common and expensive mistake. Confirm the code on the entry slip before buying any tutoring or downloading any papers.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge non-calculator paper really carry half the maths grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge 0580 sets a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, each contributing 50 per cent of the grade, at both Core and Extended. For students who have had a calculator available throughout their schooling this is the single biggest adjustment, and it is not a knowledge problem - it is fraction arithmetic, index laws, surd simplification and long division done cleanly by hand under time pressure. Ten minutes of deliberate hand arithmetic a day for six weeks does more for that paper than any amount of topic revision.

faqs.question: How long before the exam should we start IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what you want it to do. If the goal is to influence the tier decision, the work has to happen in Year 10, because by the spring of Year 11 the entry is usually made. If the goal is to convert existing knowledge into marks, twelve weeks is enough and is the most common situation we see. Under four weeks, the useful work is technique and timed papers, which is largely the student's own practice. We will tell you honestly which of those three you are in.

faqs.question: Why do Pearson 4MA1 and Cambridge 0580 need different tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because the papers differ even where the mathematics overlaps. Pearson 4MA1 sets two papers of two hours and 100 marks each with a calculator permitted in both, so marks tend to go on method, question-reading and stamina. Cambridge 0580 sets a non-calculator paper worth half the grade, so marks go on hand arithmetic and algebraic manipulation. The grade scales also differ. A tutor who has not asked for the syllabus code does not know which of these two students they have, and the revision diet should not be the same.

faqs.question: How much should a Bur Dubai family budget each month for IGCSE maths help?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai rate table estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Market packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those were read in October 2026 and are the market, not our prices. When you get a quote, ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, and what happens if you stop after one.

faqs.question: Do you send a maths tutor to our home in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai family is one-to-one over live video, and we state it before you pay. With an exam date fixed, the online format is genuinely better: the past paper, the student's attempt and the official mark scheme sit on one shared screen, get annotated together and can be revisited. The hour also holds regardless of traffic, which matters when one lost session is eight per cent of a twelve-week plan.

faqs.question: Why is my child good at maths but still getting a low IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Usually because knowing mathematics and converting it into marks are different skills. The commonest mechanical losses are premature rounding, working not shown so no method marks are available, transformations described incompletely, questions abandoned rather than attempted for partial credit, and misreading multi-part questions under time pressure. None of those are content problems and none of them are fixed by re-teaching topics. A full paper marked hard against the real scheme will show you which of them is costing your child the grade, usually within one session.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics carry the most marks in the final weeks?
faqs.answer: The honest answer is: whichever ones your child is losing marks on, which is why a diagnostic paper comes first. The recurring high-cost areas, though, are algebraic manipulation - because it taxes questions that are nominally about other topics - then trigonometry including bearings, similar areas and volumes with their squared and cubed scale factors, histograms with unequal class widths, and bounds. Those five appear every series and are routinely half-answered. Three or four topics usually account for the bulk of lost marks, and those are the only ones a short run-in should touch.

faqs.question: Is there a private-candidate route for IGCSE maths from Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an approved examination centre rather than through us. Private-candidate entry is a separate route from a school entry and carries its own arrangements, deadlines and centre requirements, and it is the route a student uses when they are no longer enrolled at the school that would have entered them. We teach the mathematics and we do not administer entries or act as a centre. Start with your current school's exams office, or contact an approved Cambridge or Pearson centre in Dubai directly to confirm what they accept and by when.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics calculator for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Only for Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, which assumes one throughout. Cambridge 0580 sets one paper where no calculator is permitted at all and one where a scientific calculator is used. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers and does not require a graphics model. Buying the wrong calculator is a common and avoidable expense, and learning an unfamiliar model in the final weeks is worse than using a familiar one well. Confirm the requirement with the maths department before buying anything.

faqs.question: For equivalency, how many IGCSE passes does a Dubai student actually need?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure; the sourced number is five. Verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel - we describe the process and neither perform nor guarantee it.

faqs.question: What should we ask for after the maths mock, rather than just the grade?
faqs.answer: Ask for the script. The marked paper is the most valuable diagnostic document a family will get all year, because mocks usually use a real past paper and the losses on it are the losses that will recur in June. A grade tells you where the student stands; the script tells you why. With it, a first tutoring session can produce a ranked list of the topics costing the most marks instead of spending an hour establishing what the school already knew in December.

faqs.question: Does our maths tutor need a UAE permit, and can we check it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask any prospective tutor directly whether they hold one. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no official fine schedule is published.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingHeading: Get the four facts, then pick the plan
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-bur-dubai.closingBody: Board, syllabus code, tier, series. Those four facts cost one email to your child's school and they determine everything else: which past papers are the right ones, whether the target grade is even available, and how many weeks you are actually working with. Once you have them, book the free trial lesson. One hour, no cost, with the tutor you would continue with, spent on a real past-paper question from the correct syllabus and marked against the official scheme. You get a written note of where the marks went, whether or not you book anything further. All lessons for Bur Dubai families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Counting the weeks before you count the topics
paragraphs: Nearly every family who looks for an IGCSE maths tutor in Business Bay is doing so at a specific point in a specific year, and the point in the year changes the right answer completely. A Year 10 in the autumn term has eighteen months and can rebuild anything, including a tier decision. A Year 11 in January has one mock window and a few months, and should be spending them on marks rather than on understanding. A student holding a disappointing result in August is making a resit decision, which is a different conversation again.

So this page is organised as a calendar rather than as a syllabus tour. It sets out what each term of the IGCSE maths course has to achieve, what a focused eight-week block can realistically change, how the mock window should be used, and when entering the next series beats waiting for the one after. The mathematics content is here too, but it sits inside the timeline, because a list of topics without a deadline attached is what most tutoring pages in this market offer and it helps nobody decide anything.

Two facts anchor the whole calendar. First, a UAE candidate sits the June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Second, and this one costs families real money, the Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only. A revision plan built around a February or March exam window is built on the wrong country's calendar, and if a provider quotes you a March deadline for a Dubai candidate, that tells you something about the provider.

Business Bay's role in this is logistical. The district has no school inside its boundary, so every Year 11 here commutes out, mostly towards Sobha Hartland, Al Safa, Al Quoz or Al Jaddaf. A 3.15pm finish plus a canal crossing produces a 4.10pm to 4.30pm arrival home, which sets the earliest hour a session can usefully start. We schedule from 4.30pm. In the eight weeks before a series, when the calendar is tightest, the difference between a slot that works and one that does not is the difference between eight sessions and four.

One thing stated plainly before anything else. IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE and we operate no centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. In the final weeks before a maths paper this is practically useful rather than a compromise, because a session can be moved by a day at short notice without anybody's drive across Al Khail Road having to be rearranged.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-business-bay.programmesIntro: Three stages matter to a Business Bay maths candidate, and the useful question at each is what the calendar still allows. These are the stages with their decision windows rather than their content lists.

programmes.name: Year 10, the year with options
programmes.description: The year in which everything is still negotiable, including tier. Content is being taught for the first time and gaps are small enough to close without displacing the current scheme of work. A Year 10 who is struggling with algebra has eighteen months, which is enough to reach Higher or Extended tier comfortably. This is the cheapest and most effective point to buy tutoring, and it is the point at which almost nobody does.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the tier entry decision is usually made during Year 10 or very early Year 11, within the board's deadlines, on the basis of internal assessment. A Business Bay family that raises a tier concern in the autumn of Year 10 is having a different and much more productive conversation than one that raises it in the spring of Year 11.

programmes.name: Year 11, the year of marks
programmes.description: Content teaching finishes and the work becomes about converting knowledge into marks: timing, working, method lines, calculator discipline. A Year 11 autumn term is still long enough to repair a topic; a Year 11 spring term generally is not, and the right plan becomes paper technique on the topics that carry the most marks. The mock window around the turn of the year is the most useful piece of information the whole year produces.
programmes.countryNote: Business Bay's commute means Year 11 evenings are shorter than they look. A student arriving home at 4.30pm after a day at school in Al Quoz or Al Barsha has perhaps three usable hours before fatigue, and those hours are already contested by eight other subjects. Volume is not available; selection is.

programmes.name: The resit window
programmes.description: A grade can be improved by entering the next available series, and for a UAE candidate that means the November series after a June result or the June series after a November one. The decision should be made from component marks rather than from the overall grade, because a paper that fell four marks short is a different proposition from one that fell twenty. Entry is made through the school as the examination centre.
programmes.countryNote: Looking backwards at a published pattern makes the shape clear: Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. A November entry therefore produces a grade in the following January, which is in time for most sixth-form confirmations but not all. Check with the receiving school before relying on it.

programmes.name: Year 9 and Lower Secondary Checkpoint
programmes.description: The year before the IGCSE course starts, and the year in which the tier conversation can be won rather than argued. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests give an external datapoint before the school's tier decision, and a Year 9 scoring in the lower bands has a full year to change the picture. A year is genuinely enough; a term in Year 11 is not.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. For a Business Bay family the October window is the useful one, because it produces evidence before the tier decision rather than after it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-business-bay.subjectsIntro: The topic strands of IGCSE Mathematics, ordered by how much they typically cost a Higher or Extended tier candidate in Dubai. The calendar matters here too: the strands at the top of this list are the ones worth attacking when there are eight weeks left.

subjects.name: Algebra and manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Rearranging, factorising, simultaneous and quadratic equations, algebraic fractions. The largest single source of lost Higher tier marks and the strand every other strand depends on. Students who cannot factorise fluently lose marks in geometry, in graphs and in the calculus-adjacent questions, which is why algebra repairs pay back twice.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic, reciprocal and exponential graphs, transformations, gradients and areas under curves. Marks go missing on the written justification rather than the sketch: a student who draws the correct transformation and does not state the mapping loses the explanation marks entirely.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Compound interest, reverse percentages, bounds and standard form. Reverse percentage questions are the most reliably failed item on any Higher paper, because students apply the forward operation. This strand is pure technique and responds within two or three sessions, which makes it the best value in a short block.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and Pythagoras
subjects.description: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangles, the sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems. The common loss is in the three-dimensional questions, where the student cannot identify the correct triangle inside the solid and so solves a different problem correctly.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area, volume, similar shapes, circle theorems and angle reasoning. Circle theorems are a memorisation task with a reasoning requirement attached: naming the theorem used earns the mark, and students who see the answer without naming the rule lose it. Similar-shape scale factors for area and volume are the second predictable loss.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, and conditional probability on tree diagrams. Histograms with unequal class widths are the standout failure: frequency density is a definition students half-remember and then guess at under time pressure.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations. The proof-style vector questions appear late in Higher papers and are frequently left blank by students who could do them, because they have never practised the layout of a vector argument.

subjects.name: Non-calculator technique
subjects.levels: Where the specification sets a calculator-free paper
subjects.description: Fraction arithmetic, surds, index laws and mental estimation done by hand. Students who have revised entirely with a calculator are unprepared for the paper that does not allow one, and the deficit is in arithmetic confidence rather than in mathematics. It is fixable in weeks but only if it is identified.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Using the device as a mathematical tool rather than as an arithmetic one: statistical functions, bracket discipline, memory, and recognising when a displayed answer is implausible. Students lose marks to premature rounding inside multi-step calculations more often than to any conceptual error.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Offered by some Dubai schools to strong Extended candidates and the best available preparation for IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. It assumes complete fluency in the main specification, so a student still consolidating the core content should not take it on in a short timeframe.

subjects.name: Past-paper discipline
subjects.description: Working whole papers to time, marking them against the published scheme, and recording where marks went by question type rather than by topic. This is a trainable habit and it is what the final weeks before a series should consist of, rather than further content teaching.

subjects.name: Formula recall and provided formulae
subjects.description: Which formulae are printed on the paper and which must be recalled differs between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel and between tiers. Students regularly memorise provided formulae and fail to memorise required ones. Confirm the current list against the specification your child actually sits, through the school.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can actually change
paragraphs: The most common question a Business Bay parent asks in the spring of Year 11 is whether it is too late. It is a good question and it has a specific answer: eight weeks can move marks substantially and cannot rebuild content substantially. Knowing which of those two a student needs is the entire value of the first session.

Marks that move in eight weeks are the procedural ones. Reverse percentages, histogram frequency density, circle-theorem naming, area and volume scale factors for similar shapes, premature rounding inside multi-step calculations, and the habit of writing a method line before a numeric answer. Each is a discrete technique, each is worth marks on almost every paper, and each is learnable in two or three sittings. A student losing marks across that list is losing a grade boundary's worth of marks to things that are not mathematics.

What does not move in eight weeks is a missing year of algebra. If a student cannot factorise reliably, cannot rearrange a formula with the subject appearing twice, and cannot handle algebraic fractions, then every topic above sits on sand and the honest plan is different: pick the strands that do not depend on heavy algebra, secure them completely, and accept the ceiling that follows. That is a worse answer than a parent wants and it is a better plan than pretending.

The way to tell the difference is to look at a marked paper rather than at a grade. Procedural losses are scattered across the paper in ones and twos and sit beside correct method. Content losses cluster: whole questions blank or abandoned after the first line. Any tutor should be able to tell you which pattern your child shows within one session, and if a provider proposes a package before seeing marked work, that is a sales process rather than a diagnosis.

sections.heading: The mock window is data, not a dress rehearsal
paragraphs: Dubai schools run mock examinations roughly a term before the series, and most families treat them as a performance to be survived. They are better understood as the only large, free, properly timed dataset a Year 11 will produce before the real papers. The grade from a mock is the least interesting thing it generates.

What matters is the distribution of lost marks. Ask the school for the marked paper, not just the mark, and then sort the losses into three piles: questions not attempted, questions attempted and wrong, and questions right in method but wrong in final answer. The three piles mean entirely different things. Unattempted questions at the end of a paper indicate a timing problem. Attempted and wrong indicates content. Right method with a wrong answer indicates rounding, calculator discipline or arithmetic, which is the fastest of the three to fix.

A fourth check is worth two minutes. Look at whether the losses are concentrated in the second half of each paper. If they are, the student is running out of time rather than out of knowledge, and the intervention is question-order strategy and pacing rather than any topic at all. This single observation redirects a substantial number of revision plans in the right direction, and it requires no tutor to make.

Mocks also tell you whether the tier entry was right, which is an uncomfortable but valuable use of them. A Higher or Extended tier student scoring in the bottom band of a mock may be better served by the grade that a different tier can reliably deliver, where the school and the board deadlines still allow a change. That decision belongs to the school, but a parent armed with a mock analysis is in a much better position to have the conversation.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are not the same course
paragraphs: A Business Bay student may be sitting Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A 4MA1, or another specification entirely, and the tier names differ between them. Cambridge divides into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel into Foundation and Higher. The content overlaps heavily and the paper structures, formula provision and question styles do not.

This matters for revision rather than for teaching. A student entered for 4MA1 Higher who revises with Cambridge 0580 Extended past papers is practising a related subject. The topics are mostly shared, the phrasing is not, and the distribution of question types across the papers is different enough to leave a student surprised on the day. In a final eight-week block, where every paper worked is one of only six or eight the student will complete, using the wrong board's papers is a significant waste.

The first action for any parent reading this is therefore administrative rather than mathematical. Email the school and ask, in writing, for the exact specification code and the tier your child is entered for in mathematics. Both pieces of information take one reply to obtain and both are needed before a single past paper is downloaded. Many families in this corridor discover at this point that they had assumed the wrong board, often because an older sibling sat a different one.

The second action is to establish which formulae are printed on the paper and which must be recalled, because this differs by specification and by tier. Students routinely memorise formulae that are provided and fail to memorise ones that are not. Confirm the current list against the specification document the school holds, since boards revise them and no tutoring page, this one included, should be the source of record for that detail.

sections.heading: The year in sequence, term by term
paragraphs: Laid out as a sequence, an IGCSE mathematics course has four decision points and most families engage with only the last one. The first is tier, decided in Year 10 or early Year 11. The second is the mock window, which generates the data. The third is the final eight weeks, which convert knowledge into marks. The fourth is the resit decision after results.

Working forward: in Year 10, content is being met for the first time and the useful intervention is weekly consolidation that stops gaps forming. In the autumn of Year 11, content teaching completes and there is still time to repair a genuine topic weakness. In the spring, repair becomes expensive and the work shifts to paper technique, timing and the procedural marks. After the series, the component marks decide whether a resit is a four-mark problem or a twenty-mark one.

Cambridge adds one administrative item to this sequence that is worth more than it looks. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A revision calendar built from a timetable found online rather than confirmed with your own examinations officer carries a real and avoidable risk.

Dates that are already past can be stated because they are checkable, and they illustrate the shape better than any projection. Pearson's November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is exactly why the table below names milestones and tells you to read the live document rather than restating a date that can be revised.

sections.heading: When a resit beats another month of revision
paragraphs: After results, the decision is not simply whether to resit but which papers and when, and it should be made from component marks rather than from the overall grade. A UAE candidate has two series a year, so the choice is between the next one and the one after, and the gap between them is substantial in planning terms.

Where a student fell a handful of marks short on one paper and performed as expected on the other, a resit of the weaker component in the next available series is a narrow, well-defined piece of work with a high chance of changing the grade. Where the shortfall was spread evenly and large, a resit without a change in approach tends to reproduce the result, and the honest conversation covers whether the tier was right and whether the timeline was ever realistic.

Timing against the receiving school matters more than families expect. Looking at a published pattern: Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry therefore produces a grade in the following January, which is in time for many sixth-form confirmations and not all of them. Ask the receiving school, in writing, what date it needs the grade by, before committing to a series. That one email has saved families from choosing the wrong window.

A resit also has an opportunity cost that nobody mentions. The weeks spent preparing for a November mathematics paper are weeks a DP1 or Year 12 student is not spending on their new course, which carries its own consequences. For a borderline case the better answer is sometimes to accept the grade and protect the sixth-form start, and a tutor who will say that is more useful than one who will sell the resit block.

sections.heading: What a block of maths tuition costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Because this page is organised by the calendar, the useful cost figure is not the hourly rate but the total for a block. An eight-week block at two sessions a week is sixteen sessions, so a published hourly rate multiplies out quickly and a family can work out the whole commitment before speaking to anybody. The figures below are each provider's own published rates, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

At the budget end of online tutoring, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Sixteen sessions at those rates is roughly AED 530 to AED 1,040. For a qualified subject tutor online, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, which puts sixteen sessions at around AED 2,400 and upwards. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialist work at AED 200 to 450 or more per hour, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium named-tutor end. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Multiplying a block out changes how the in-home premium reads. Sixteen in-home hours at the Bestimate band against sixteen online hours at the qualified-tutor band is a difference of several hundred to a couple of thousand dirhams, and the difference is travel. It does not buy a better match to Cambridge 0580 Extended or to Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher. A family in Business Bay deciding between formats in the final two months before a series is really deciding how much of its budget to spend on a drive across Al Khail Road.

IB Gram does not publish a UAE rate card on these pages and does not present market rates as ours. The free trial lesson exists so that a family can see the teaching before discussing money, and the consultation exists so that the number of sessions is set from marked papers rather than from a package size. For context on the wider budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the weeks that quietly disappear
paragraphs: A revision calendar built on paper assumes every week is usable, and in Dubai several are not. Ramadan shortens school days and reorganises evenings around iftar. The winter and spring breaks remove two to three weeks each year. A family travelling in the long summer loses momentum that takes three or four weeks to rebuild in September. None of this is an obstacle; all of it is predictable, and predictable things can be planned around.

For a Year 11 whose series falls after Ramadan, the practical move is to agree an alternative session pattern before the month begins rather than improvising weekly. Early-afternoon sessions and post-iftar sessions both work, and committing to one in advance preserves continuity through what is otherwise the single largest gap in the revision year. Families who leave it to chance typically lose three or four weeks at the point in the calendar where weeks are most expensive.

School breaks are a different calculation. A break is the only time a student has whole days available, which makes it the best window for whole-paper practice under timed conditions and the worst window for new content. Two timed papers across a one-week break, properly marked, are worth more than six rushed weeknight sessions in term time, and they cost less.

Travel is the one families underestimate. A Business Bay student spending four weeks abroad in the summer before Year 11 returns having lost arithmetic fluency and calculator familiarity rather than conceptual understanding, which is why the first September sessions should be fluency work rather than a new topic. Online delivery means the sessions themselves can continue through travel where the family wants them to, which is a genuine scheduling advantage rather than a selling point.
bullets: Agree the Ramadan session pattern before the month starts, not during it
Breaks are the right window for timed whole papers, the wrong one for new content
Four weeks abroad costs fluency, not understanding; plan September accordingly

sections.heading: Equivalency, the permit and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Mathematics is one of the five subjects that matter for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, which is worth knowing while there is still time to act on it. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one ranking tutoring site in this market publishes six subjects, which is wrong.

We do not publish an IB points threshold for equivalency, because no figure could be read on an official Ministry source, and a number a parent acts on has to be right. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation for anybody; we describe the requirement and point you to the official channel. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

On the permit: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

And on what we will not claim: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, licence, approval or partnership, and operates no office, branch or centre in the United Arab Emirates. We do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status, do not publish satisfaction percentages or average-score claims, and do not distribute board specifications, past papers or mark schemes. Your child's school has legitimate access to all of those documents, which is where a revision plan should start.

sections.heading: Getting started with a deadline already in view
paragraphs: When there is a date on the calendar, the first conversation should be short and the first session should produce something usable. Bring three things: the specification code and tier confirmed by the school, the two most recent marked mathematics papers rather than the grades, and the date of the series your child is entered for. With those, a diagnosis is possible in the trial lesson and a block can be planned the same week.

Coverage is reliable for IGCSE mathematics at both boards and both tiers, which is the single most-requested subject in this market, so a match is usually available within a few working days. What fills first is the hour rather than the subject. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is contested by the whole emirate; for a Business Bay student arriving home around 4.30pm, the slots that stay open longest are 4.30pm itself, anything after 7.30pm, and weekend mornings. In a final eight-week block, taking an open slot immediately is worth more than waiting three weeks for a preferred one.

If no specialist is free at the hour you need, you will be told at the enquiry rather than matched to the nearest available person. Where a UAE-based tutor for a specific specification and tier is not available, the match may be a specialist teaching into the Gulf timezone from elsewhere, and that is stated before the trial lesson rather than discovered afterwards.

A last piece of advice that costs nothing. Do not add four subjects at once in the final term. A Year 11 carrying nine courses and a thirty-minute commute can absorb one or two tutored subjects at a session each, and the usual consequence of a four-subject plan is attendance that collapses in week five followed by the conclusion that tutoring does not work. Start with mathematics if mathematics is the widest gap, measure at six weeks against marked papers, and add only if the calendar genuinely has room.

process.title: Confirm the specification and tier in writing
process.description: Email the school for the exact mathematics specification code and the tier your child is entered for. It takes one reply and it determines which past papers are worth working. A surprising number of Business Bay families discover at this step that they had assumed the wrong board, often from an older sibling's experience.

process.title: Send marked papers, not grades
process.description: The two most recent marked mathematics papers are worth more than any report. They show whether losses are scattered beside correct method, which is procedural and fast to fix, or clustered in abandoned questions, which is content and takes a term. Grades cannot distinguish the two.

process.title: Agree the deadline and count backwards
process.description: A short consultation on Gulf Standard Time to establish which series your child sits, where the mock window falls, and how many usable weeks remain after breaks and travel. The plan is then written backwards from that date rather than forwards from today.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a ranked list
process.description: The trial is taught and ends with a written list of marks lost by question type, ranked. That list is the plan. No card is required to take the trial, and the list is useful to you whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Run the block with timed papers from week four
process.description: Two sessions a week, strands first and whole papers from week four onwards, each marked against the published scheme with losses coded by type rather than by topic. The student finishes with an exam-day checklist they have actually rehearsed.

process.title: Review at six weeks, and stop when it is done
process.description: At six weeks we compare marked papers against the baseline and decide whether to continue, narrow the focus or finish. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and the end of a defined block is a natural place to do it. We will not propose a renewal that the marks do not justify.

whyPoints.title: Planned from a date, not from a syllabus
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts with the series your child is entered for and counts backwards through breaks, Ramadan and the mock window to the usable weeks that actually remain. A revision schedule that assumes fifty-two usable weeks a year is the most common reason a term's work underdelivers.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the specification, not to maths
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher share most of their content and little of their phrasing. In a short block where a student will complete six or eight papers in total, working the wrong board's papers is a waste nobody can afford.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from marked papers
whyPoints.description: The first session reads two marked papers and sorts the losses into unattempted, attempted-and-wrong, and right-method-wrong-answer. Those three categories point at timing, content and procedure respectively, and they need entirely different work.

whyPoints.title: Procedural marks treated as marks
whyPoints.description: Reverse percentages, frequency density, circle-theorem naming, scale factors for area and volume, premature rounding and the missing method line. Each is worth marks on almost every paper and each is learnable in two or three sittings, which is why they come first in a short block.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what eight weeks cannot do
whyPoints.description: A missing year of algebra is not recoverable in two months, and we will say so rather than sell a block that cannot deliver. In that situation the better plan is to secure the strands that do not depend on heavy algebra and be realistic about the ceiling.

whyPoints.title: Figures sourced, limits stated
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here belongs to the provider that published it, with the month it was read. No in-home visits in the UAE, no UAE office, no claim of regulator or board approval, no board documents distributed, and no statistic without n, date and method.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the maths paper. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong, and one session with two marked papers will tell you. Eight weeks moves procedural marks reliably: reverse percentages, frequency density on histograms, naming circle theorems, area and volume scale factors, rounding discipline and writing a method line. Those are worth a grade boundary's worth of marks on most Higher tier papers and each is learnable in two or three sittings. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild a missing year of algebra. If the losses are whole abandoned questions rather than scattered slips, the honest plan is narrower and the ceiling is lower.

faqs.question: What should we do with my child's mock maths paper?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the marked paper rather than the grade, then sort the lost marks into three piles: questions not attempted, questions attempted and wrong, and questions with correct method and a wrong final answer. Unattempted questions late in the paper mean a pacing problem. Attempted and wrong means a content gap. Correct method with a wrong answer means rounding, calculator discipline or arithmetic, which is the fastest of the three to repair. That sorting takes twenty minutes, needs no tutor, and redirects most revision plans correctly.

faqs.question: Which maths specification is my child actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Email the school's examinations officer and ask for the exact code in writing. In Dubai it is most often Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A 4MA1, and the tier names differ: Core and Extended for Cambridge, Foundation and Higher for Pearson Edexcel. The content overlaps heavily but the phrasing and the distribution of question types do not. In a final block where a student will complete only six or eight full papers, working the wrong board's papers wastes a meaningful share of the available practice.

faqs.question: Can my child revise maths with past papers from the other board?
faqs.answer: For topic practice, sometimes; for timed whole papers, no. The mathematics overlaps substantially between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, so a question on similar shapes is useful whichever board wrote it. But the paper structures, the balance of question types and the phrasing differ enough that a student who has only ever worked the other board's complete papers will be surprised on the day by what the paper asks for and how much of it there is. Use the correct board's papers for anything timed.

faqs.question: Which maths formulae does my child have to memorise?
faqs.answer: That differs by specification and by tier, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. Some formulae are printed on the paper and others must be recalled, and students routinely memorise the provided ones while neglecting the required ones. Ask the school for the specification document and read the formula provision section, or ask the mathematics teacher directly for the recall list. No tutoring website, including this one, should be your source of record for that detail, because boards revise it and a wrong list costs marks on the day.

faqs.question: Why do reverse percentage questions catch everyone out?
faqs.answer: Because students apply the forward operation. Asked what a price was before a twenty per cent increase, a student subtracts twenty per cent from the new figure instead of dividing by 1.2. The error is procedural rather than conceptual, it appears on almost every Higher or Extended tier paper, and it takes about two sessions to make the correct approach automatic. It is a good example of why the first weeks of a short block should target technique rather than understanding: the marks are already within reach and are being discarded.

faqs.question: What is frequency density and why does my child keep losing those marks?
faqs.answer: Frequency density is frequency divided by class width, and it is what the vertical axis of a histogram with unequal class intervals shows. Students half-remember the definition and then guess under time pressure, usually plotting frequency directly. The question type recurs reliably, carries several marks, and is entirely learnable in one or two sittings. It belongs on the short list of procedural repairs worth doing first in an eight-week block, alongside reverse percentages and the area and volume scale factors for similar shapes.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Dubai maths candidate sit?
faqs.answer: The June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. One warning that matters: the Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only, so any revision plan built around a February or March exam window is built on the wrong country's calendar. Read the exact dates from the board's live timetable, since provisional timetables are revised before they become final.

faqs.question: Our examinations officer mentioned a zone. What is that about?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Practically, your child's revision calendar should be built from the timetable your own school's examinations officer confirms rather than from a version found online. It takes one email and it removes a genuine risk at no cost.

faqs.question: Should my child resit the maths paper in November or wait?
faqs.answer: Decide from the component marks rather than the overall grade. A shortfall of a few marks on one paper is a narrow, well-defined piece of work with a good chance of moving the grade in the next series. A large shortfall spread evenly across both papers usually reproduces itself unless something changes about the tier or the approach. Also count the opportunity cost: the weeks spent preparing a November paper are weeks the new sixth-form course also needs. Sometimes protecting the Year 12 start is the better decision.

faqs.question: Will a November resit grade arrive in time for sixth form?
faqs.answer: Often, but check rather than assume. Looking at a published pattern, Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November entry produces a grade in the following January. That is in time for many sixth-form confirmations and not for all of them. Ask the receiving school in writing what date it needs the grade by, before committing to a series. That single email has saved families from entering the wrong window and then discovering the timing does not work.

faqs.question: How much does a two-month block of IGCSE maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Multiply the published hourly rate by sixteen sessions and the commitment becomes clear before you speak to anybody. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, so sixteen sessions is roughly AED 530 to 1,040. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, which puts sixteen sessions at AED 2,400 upwards. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places specialist work at AED 200 to 450 or more per hour. Those are each provider's own published figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Does paying for in-home maths tuition in Business Bay buy a better tutor?
faqs.answer: It buys travel. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once the drive is priced in. Across a sixteen-session block that difference is several hundred to a couple of thousand dirhams, and what it covers is the journey to your tower, the parking and the lift. It does not improve the match to Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher, which is the thing that actually moves marks.

faqs.question: How do we keep maths revision going through the Ramadan weeks?
faqs.answer: Agree the alternative pattern before the month begins rather than deciding week by week. School days shorten and evenings reorganise around iftar, so the usual 5pm slot stops working for most Business Bay families. Early-afternoon sessions and post-iftar sessions both work well; what fails is improvisation, which typically costs three or four weeks at the point in the revision year when weeks are most expensive. For a Year 11 whose series falls after Ramadan, that gap is the single largest avoidable loss in the calendar.

faqs.question: Is a school break a good time for extra maths sessions?
faqs.answer: It is the best time for timed whole papers and the worst time for new content. A break is the only period when a student has whole uninterrupted days, which is exactly what a full paper under examination conditions requires and exactly what a weeknight after a canal commute cannot provide. Two properly marked timed papers across a one-week break are worth more than six rushed term-time sessions and cost less. New topics taught during a break tend not to survive the return, because nothing reinforces them for a fortnight.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor in the final term of Year 11?
faqs.answer: One or two. A Year 11 carrying nine courses and a thirty-minute commute each way can absorb one or two tutored subjects at a session each, and the usual outcome of a four-subject plan is attendance that collapses around week five, followed by the conclusion that tutoring did not work. Start with the subject where the gap is widest, measure at six weeks against marked papers rather than impressions, and add a second only if the calendar genuinely has room. Selection beats volume when the weeks are fixed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our building in Business Bay for the last few weeks?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates and has no office, branch or tuition centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In a final block this is a practical advantage: a session can be moved by a day at short notice around a mock or a school commitment, without anybody's drive across Al Khail Road in the evening peak having to be rearranged first.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-business-bay.closingHeading: Start by counting the weeks you actually have
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-business-bay.closingBody: Before buying anything, do three free things. Email the school for the exact specification code and tier. Ask for the two most recent marked mathematics papers, not the grades. Then count the weeks to the series your child is entered for, subtracting the breaks, the Ramadan weeks and any travel. What remains is the real calendar, and it is usually shorter than the one in a parent's head. Bring those three things to a short consultation on Gulf Standard Time and we will tell you whether the losses are procedural, in which case eight weeks is genuinely enough, or structural, in which case the plan is different and we will say so. The trial lesson is free, no card is needed, and it ends with a ranked list of the marks being lost.
