sections.heading: 0580 and 0606 together: comparing the load
paragraphs: Cambridge Additional Mathematics is taken alongside 0580 by students heading towards A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, and the decision is usually presented as a question of ambition. It is better treated as a comparison of load against return. The course covers calculus, functions, series and trigonometric identities at a level approaching AS, which is real content on top of an already full Year 11 timetable.

For a student fluent in algebraic manipulation the return is substantial: most of the step up at sixteen has already been met once, and the first term of A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis becomes recognisable rather than alarming. For a student who finds 0580 Extended genuinely hard, the same course adds load that makes every other subject harder without reaching a grade that justifies it.

The test is current performance rather than interest, and it is assessable from one marked 0580 paper plus twenty minutes of non-calculator work. A student who rearranges fluently will find 0606 demanding and doable. A student who hesitates at every sign change will not, and the honest recommendation in that case is to secure 0580 Extended properly, which is a better use of the same hours.

Where 0606 is taken, the early difficulty is almost never the mathematics. It is notation: writing a derivative correctly, using function notation consistently, setting out an integration with its limits. Those conventions are assessed in practice and rarely taught explicitly, which is why six sessions on notation plus composite differentiation resolves most early 0606 enquiries from this belt.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE mathematics leads at sixteen
paragraphs: The third comparison is the one with the longest reach and it is usually made last. A Level Mathematics, IB Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and IB Mathematics Applications and Interpretation all accept IGCSE leavers and all expect different things from them. Knowing which destination is intended changes what a Year 11 block should prioritise.

A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis both assume algebraic fluency and both include assessment without a calculator in part. For a student heading that way, the Year 11 priority is manipulation rather than topic coverage, and 0606 is the most direct preparation available. IB Applications assumes comfort with technology and with writing about what a result means, so the priority shifts towards calculator procedure and contextual interpretation.

Students not continuing mathematics have a different and entirely legitimate priority: securing the grade their post-16 course requires with the least disruption to everything else. For them a tier conversation and a mechanical-marks block is usually the whole plan, and spending Year 11 on Additional Mathematics would be a waste of hours that other subjects need.

The table compares the destinations on what they expect, which is information most Year 10 families do not have when they make the option and tier decisions. It should be read alongside the admissions pages of the specific universities under consideration, because degree prerequisites are set by course and are the one input that overrides preference.

One caution about reading it. The expectations listed are about preparation rather than about formal entry requirements, which are set by the receiving school or sixth form and vary between them. A school may accept a particular grade and still find that a student arrives under-prepared for the course, which is the gap this table is describing. Ask the receiving school what grade it requires, and then ask separately what it expects students to be able to do on arrival; the two answers are rarely the same.

paragraphs: The formats a DAMAC Hills family can actually buy differ in what they can reach, and the rates differ too. The published figures in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises online tuition from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors.

In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with local packages advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

All of those are provider-published figures read in October 2026, and none is IB Gram's price list. The reason for printing them is that three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a DAMAC Hills family transacts in. A parent should be able to see where a quote sits before agreeing to it.

The comparison that matters more than the rate is what each format can reach. A group class at a centre cannot be matched to a tier. sections.heading: The two series, and what results day decides
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate plans around June with November as the resit route and should discard any schedule referencing a February window.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct version of the timetable for that zone is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. Ask the school which zone its centre sits in rather than relying on a timetable found by searching.

On the Pearson side the shape is the same with different labels: Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and that is the trap, because a provisional version downloaded in September and saved to a phone is what families are still revising from in April, so the live official timetable is the only one worth building a plan on. What the published record tells you is how long the wait after each series actually runs. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is around two months between the last paper and the grade. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, a shorter wait that lands in the middle of the summer holiday.

Results day then settles the post-16 comparison in practice rather than in theory. Where a mathematics grade blocks a named requirement and the loss was specific, a November resit in that subject alone is reasonable. Where mathematics is not being continued, a resit competes with the first term of a demanding new course and usually costs more than it returns. That decision should be made against a stated requirement rather than against disappointment.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and what is not claimed
paragraphs: A DAMAC Hills address puts your child's school under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and KHDA is the body whose inspection reports and published requirements sit behind everything the school tells you about mathematics sets and tier entries. The reason to know which authority applies is that families move within the country and assume the rules travel with them. They do not. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The powers differ as well as the postcode: in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so a mathematics syllabus decision a Dubai school makes for itself is an approval question elsewhere.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Year 11 student the effect is that the examined subjects are not the whole timetable, so a revision plan drawn from the entry sheet assumes hours that are already committed.

The permit is the second layer, and it attaches to the tutor rather than to the school. Any individual teaching IGCSE mathematics privately in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. The eligibility list is wide, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category is the one worth pausing on in mathematics specifically, because a capable sixteen-year-old genuinely can drill a Core-tier student through transformations, and is still required to hold the permit in order to be paid for it. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

IB Gram holds no Cambridge, Pearson, International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and timetables are linked at source rather than reproduced. No grade is promised, no rating is published, and no statistic appears without a sample size, a date and a method.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 make the maths harder?
faqs.answer: Neither is harder in any meaningful sense, and the grade on a certificate does not record which paper structure produced it. What differs is the shape of the questions, the tiering vocabulary, the formula provision and how much scaffolding the questions give. Those differences are enough to justify matching a tutor to the actual code, because teaching correct mathematics against an unfamiliar question shape produces marks lost for reasons that look like carelessness in a mock report.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE maths tutor come to DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors do, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted. IB Gram does not: all UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For mathematics the shared screen is also the better surface, since the tutor reads the working line by line as it appears rather than a finished page across a table.

faqs.question: My child is on Core. Can that be changed?
faqs.answer: Only before the entry deadline, and only with evidence. Core caps the grades available however well the student performs in the series. The evidence a department can act on is performance against the Extended content list, showing which topics are absent rather than weak, plus twenty minutes of timed non-calculator manipulation. Take both to a Year 10 parents' evening and ask three questions: which tier, what grade does it cap, and when do entries close.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth the extra load in Year 11?
faqs.answer: For a student fluent in algebraic manipulation heading towards A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, yes: it covers calculus, functions, series and trigonometric identities at a level approaching AS and removes most of the step at sixteen. For a student who finds 0580 Extended genuinely hard, it adds load that makes every other subject harder without reaching a grade that justifies it. Judge it on current fluency rather than on interest.

faqs.question: Does IB Applications need the same IGCSE preparation as IB Analysis?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the comparison most Year 10 families have not made. Analysis assumes fluent algebra and includes assessment without a calculator, so manipulation drill and possibly 0606 are the right Year 11 preparation. Applications assumes comfort with technology and with writing about what a result means, so calculator procedure and contextual interpretation matter more. Preparing generically for 'IB maths' under-serves whichever route the student actually takes.

faqs.question: Is DAMAC Hills at any disadvantage for maths tutors?
faqs.answer: No. Mathematics has the deepest tutor pool of any subject, and once lessons are delivered online every community in this belt draws on the same one. What differs is the clock: secondary students here travel out to Al Barsha, Jumeirah or the Ranches and arrive home after five, so the earliest workable slot is around 5.30pm and two shorter sessions beat one long one. The community affects scheduling and nothing else.

faqs.question: Why does the formula provision matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it decides what has to be memorised, and it differs between boards, between tiers and sometimes between syllabus versions. A student who believes a formula will be given and finds it is not loses the question entirely. The current specification states what is provided, and it is published free and revised between cohorts. A tutor working from a memory of the paper's old format is the most common avoidable waste of a student's weeks.

faqs.question: Which single topic should a Year 11 student fix first?
faqs.answer: Histograms with unequal class intervals, where frequency density has to be calculated rather than read. It appears with little variation across years on both boards, it has a fixed procedure, and a large share of candidates plot frequency instead. One session usually fixes it permanently. Close behind are without-replacement tree diagrams and quartiles from a cumulative frequency curve, both mechanical and both routinely skipped in revision.

faqs.question: Can a tuition centre group class work for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: For content coverage at a fixed pace, sometimes. For anything specific to one student it cannot, because the class is set before the student arrives, so it cannot be matched to the board or the tier and cannot spend a session on one marked script. For a student losing marks to a nameable mechanical habit, one-to-one matching reaches the problem and a group class does not, whatever the relative cost.

faqs.question: Should practice papers from both boards be used?
faqs.answer: No. Use five recent years of the board the student actually sits, with that board's own mark schemes. Mixing boards means meeting question shapes that will not appear, and more importantly means marking against schemes that reward slightly different things. The archive for either board is large enough that there is no need to borrow, and the time spent on the wrong board's papers is time taken from the right one's.

faqs.question: How do I compare two tutors who both sound confident?
faqs.answer: Ask both which code and tier your child is entered for, then show both the same marked script and ask what went wrong. A code-matched specialist names specific withheld marks: method not written, accuracy lost to early rounding, a circle theorem used without being named. A generalist describes the student instead, usually in terms of confidence or effort. The two answers separate within ten minutes and the hourly rate does not predict which you get.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the university-student end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, to AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour sessions are AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more by tier.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit, and does February exist?
faqs.answer: June, with November as the resit route. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series and offers the February/March series to India only, so a UAE candidate should discard any revision schedule referencing a February window. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with separate timetables, and states that using the correct zone version is essential.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week for a student home after five?
faqs.answer: Two sixty-minute sessions rather than one ninety-minute session, with ten minutes of written drill on the days between. Concentration rather than teaching time is the limit after a commute, and mathematics fluency decays within days, so frequency matters more than session length. The most resilient pattern in this community is one weekday evening plus a weekend morning, with the longer weekend slot used for whole papers.

intro.heading: What families in DAMAC Hills 2 pay for IGCSE maths, and what they get
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote US dollars, which is not a currency any family in DAMAC Hills 2 pays school fees in. One ranking agency's own frequently-asked-questions section asks how much tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. So the ordinary experience of shopping for an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai is to be quoted a number on a phone call with nothing to compare it against.

Here is the published market instead. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. Qualified online subject tutors run AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate research giving the specialist band as AED 200-450 plus. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home visiting is AED 180-500 an hour including travel. Every one of those figures was read from the publishing provider's own page in October 2026.

Monthly is the number a household actually feels. Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour visits.

None of those are IB Gram prices. We do not publish a rate card on these pages, because the honest number depends on the board, the tier, the year group and the weeks remaining, and a figure that ignores those is a marketing device rather than a quote. What we will do is tell you what the market charges, say what each band genuinely buys, and then be specific about where DAMAC Hills 2 families most often spend money that produces nothing.

That last part is the useful half of this page. Maths is the subject families worry about most, which means it is the subject they buy most impulsively — fastest available tutor, lowest advertised rate, whichever evening slot is free. Each of those decisions has a predictable failure mode, and each one is avoidable with a question asked before the first invoice rather than after the third.

Lessons for DAMAC Hills 2 are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. That is relevant to the cost conversation, because from the Al Qudra corridor the in-home premium is substantially a driving charge, and a driving charge is the one part of a tutoring invoice that teaches nobody anything.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: IGCSE maths is one subject with several distinct cost centres inside it. These are the components and adjacent courses DAMAC Hills 2 families buy help with, and what each is genuinely worth paying for.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The commonest entry in Dubai UK-curriculum schools. Core caps below the top grades; Extended covers the full syllabus. Paying for Extended-level tutoring while entered for Core is a straightforward waste, and so is the reverse, so confirm the tier before agreeing a rate.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: A different specification with its own tiering and paper structure. Past papers are not interchangeable with Cambridge. A term of the wrong board's practice is the second most common wasted spend we see, and it is invisible until the real paper arrives.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: The foundation layer, and where most Year 11 students who name a different problem actually need the work. Expanding, factorising, rational expressions, rearranging formulae. Cheap to fix in Year 9, expensive in Year 11, and the single highest-return topic in the subject.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Fractions, indices, surds, standard form and mental estimation under time pressure. Students with calculator habits lose marks steadily rather than dramatically. A short, specific block closes it, which makes it good value compared with general revision.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.description: Unstructured questions where nothing indicates which technique applies. This is pattern recognition, built only by working many real questions with feedback, and it is the main thing a specialist delivers that a generalist cannot.

subjects.name: Showing method
subjects.description: Method marks are available throughout and are forfeited daily by students who can reach a right answer in their head. Changing this habit is a behaviour change rather than a knowledge gain, takes a few weeks, and is possibly the cheapest grade movement available.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Circle theorems, bearings, three-dimensional trigonometry and the sine and cosine rules. Students often know the rules and cannot see which applies to an unfamiliar diagram, which again is recognition practice rather than content teaching.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, tree diagrams and conditional probability. Unequal-interval histograms are a reliably examined topic that students reliably get wrong, and it can be taught properly in a single session.

subjects.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: A bridging course for students heading to A Level or Higher Level Diploma maths. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early, and residual algebraic weakness is exposed immediately. Worth paying for only if the post-16 route needs it.

subjects.name: Post-16 bridging
subjects.description: A short block on the algebra, functions and trigonometry that A Level or IB Analysis and Approaches assumes and IGCSE does not fully build. Taken in the summer it is inexpensive; taken in November of Year 12 it is a rescue at rescue prices.

sections.heading: The four ways DAMAC Hills 2 families waste money on maths tutoring
paragraphs: These are not hypothetical. They are the four patterns we see most often when a family comes to us after a year of paying somebody else, and each one has a question that would have prevented it.

First: a budget generalist handed an exam-year student. At AED 33-65 an hour a capable graduate can genuinely help a Year 8 with homework. Put the same person in front of a Year 11 sitting Extended tier and they will teach plausible mathematics that is not the specification, pleasantly, for a term, with no change in paper performance. It felt cheap, which is what makes it the most expensive mistake available. The preventing question: which specification do you teach, and at which tier?

Second: the wrong board. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 set different papers with different tiering. A term of the wrong board's past papers trains the wrong instincts about what a question wants, and it is invisible until the real paper arrives. The preventing question is one email to the school office asking for the code.

Third: paying the travel premium for proximity when proximity was not the problem. In-home visits are published at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from the Al Qudra corridor a real share of that is driving. For a younger child who needs physical presence that is money well spent. For a Year 11 working through past papers, it buys a car journey. Fourth: buying five subjects in February of Year 11 when two could move and three could not — which is how a family spends the specialist exam-year rate across a load that dilutes every session.

paragraphs: Sorting the market by price rather than by prestige makes the decision clearer, because it shows what each step up actually adds. The bottom band buys attention and company. The middle buys specification knowledge. The top buys scarcity, and sometimes a credential you cannot verify.

Working up: budget online tutoring from AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65. Tuition-centre group classes typically AED 60-150 per student per hour. Premium named tutors AED 500-650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Two cautions on the top end. A premium rate is not evidence of a premium outcome, and claimed examiner status should be treated as a claim until it is evidenced — examiner status also gives nobody access to marking, boundaries or paper content, whatever is implied. sections.heading: Cost per grade rather than cost per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for this decision, because the same hourly rate produces wildly different results depending on when it is spent and on what. A family comparing AED 150 against AED 270 is answering a less important question than a family comparing eight sessions in Year 10 against thirty in Year 11.

Consider the arithmetic over the two examined years. A weekly mid-band session through Year 10 at the published AED 600-1,200 monthly range runs to roughly AED 6,000-12,000 across the school year, and arrives in Year 11 with foundations secure and a tier decision taken deliberately. A family that skips Year 10 and buys a Year 11 specialist intensive at the published AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, usually across more than one subject, frequently spends as much in five months and starts from a worse position.

The cheapest intervention of all is the one almost nobody buys: a short fixed-scope block in Year 9 on algebraic fluency and non-calculator work. Six to ten sessions in the mid band, perhaps AED 1,500-3,000 in total at published rates, addressing the exact layer that Year 11 students most often turn out to need. It feels unnecessary because nothing is examined yet, which is precisely why it is cheap.

sections.heading: The tier decision changes the value of every dirham
paragraphs: No amount of tutoring moves a student above the ceiling of the tier they are entered for, which makes tier the first thing to establish and the thing most parents are never told clearly. Cambridge offers 0580 Mathematics in Core and Extended versions; Pearson runs 4MA1 at Foundation and Higher. Core and Foundation cover a reduced syllabus and cap below the top grades.

Spending in the wrong direction is easy here. A family paying specialist rates for a child entered on Core, aiming at a grade the Core paper cannot award, is buying something that cannot be delivered. A family paying budget rates for a child on Extended who needs the full syllabus covered is buying something too thin to work. Neither mistake is visible on an invoice.

The tier decision is usually taken by the department during Year 10 on the basis of class performance, and is often reversible for a while. That window is where tutoring has its maximum financial leverage, because moving tier opens grades that no amount of later practice can reach. Once entries are confirmed by the centre, months before the papers, the question is closed.

So the sequence that spends money well is: establish the tier, check it against the post-16 route the child actually wants, change it in Year 10 if there is a mismatch, and only then buy teaching. Reversing that order is how families spend a year of fees inside a ceiling they did not know existed.

sections.heading: Why we charge nothing for the thing that tells you most
paragraphs: The free trial lesson is not a sales device and it is not taught by a different person from the one who would continue. The specialist proposed for your child teaches a full session, and you and the student judge it afterwards. If the explanation style does not land, nothing has been spent and we propose somebody else.

The reason it is free is straightforward: in maths, explanation style matters more than in any other subject, and no amount of written description predicts it. A tutor with the right specification knowledge and the wrong pace for your child will produce a term of pleasant sessions and no movement. One hour tells you what a brochure cannot, and charging for that hour would mean families commit on worse information.

The diagnostic sits before the trial. The student works through real questions from the correct board at the correct tier while a specialist watches. That is where the genuine gap appears, and in maths it is almost always underneath the named topic: a student who says trigonometry is the problem usually needs algebraic rearrangement, and a student who says statistics is the problem usually needs to read the question more slowly.

Being specific about the free part matters because the word free gets misused in this market. The trial is one full lesson, with the proposed tutor, with no card required and no obligation to continue. If any condition attaches to an offer you are given elsewhere, it should be stated on the same screen as the word free, and frequently it is not.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are paying permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This belongs in a cost discussion because it is a risk you are paying for without being told. Private tuition in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service is Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for via its smart app, website or e-services with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit costs nothing and takes two working days, there is no legitimate price reason for a tutor not to hold one. Eligibility is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify amounts, so ignore any figure circulating informally.

The permit also carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes the same restriction for Abu Dhabi school staff. A provider offering your child's own classroom teacher privately is telling you something about itself.

For completeness: an individual needs the MoHRE permit, and an organisation running tutoring from premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership and claims none, and has no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: What a maths grade is worth downstream
paragraphs: Spending decisions make more sense with the downstream consequences in view, and for maths they are unusually concrete.

The immediate one is post-16 access. Most UAE British-curriculum schools split after Year 11 into A Levels or the IB Diploma, and maths-heavy courses at both — A Level Mathematics, IB Analysis and Approaches, particularly at Higher Level — expect a strong Extended-tier or high-grade result. A capped tier or a weak grade closes those doors quietly, and the closing happens before anybody discusses university.

The second is equivalency. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student needs five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, which catches families out because both are mandatory in Dubai schools. Maths is almost always one of the five a plan depends on.

The third is simply time. A student who arrives in Year 12 with shaky algebra will spend the first term of an A Level or Diploma maths course repairing it, usually with paid help, at exactly the moment the new course is accelerating. That is a cost incurred later for a saving made earlier, and it is the clearest argument for buying in Year 9 or Year 10 rather than Year 11.

sections.heading: What we will not sell you
paragraphs: No guarantee of a grade, a tier change or an improvement. The variables are not under a tutor's control, and in a market where several ranking pages do offer guarantees, declining to is information rather than modesty.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which in practice means no statistics at all. No average grade achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction score, and no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish figures like 4.9 from several hundred reviews, sometimes two conflicting versions on the same page, and none of them states how the number was produced. A figure like that is decoration priced as evidence.

No awarding-body material as downloads. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and we cite and link them rather than hosting them. No description of our tutors as examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can demonstrate. And no home visits anywhere in the UAE, at any price, because there is no UAE visiting service to buy.

What we will sell you is the smallest thing that solves the problem. If a fixed-scope block of eight sessions on algebraic manipulation is what the diagnostic shows, that is what we propose, and we will say so even when a weekly arrangement running to the series would be worth more to us. A fixed-scope block ends on the date the scope says it ends, and the review at that point is an honest one rather than a renewal conversation dressed as a review.

whyPoints.description: No promised grade, no improvement percentage, no self-generated rating, no claimed regulator approval, no hosted past papers and no UAE home visits. What you get is a diagnostic verdict that sometimes says the time available is not enough.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths tutor cost for a DAMAC Hills 2 family?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai spread, read in October 2026, runs from AED 33-65 an hour at the budget end (Tutopiya AED 33-52, EdFlik AED 45-65), through AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor (Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150), to AED 200-450 and above for a specialist (TutorChase AED 270, Bestimate AED 200-450+), with BartyED at AED 650 premium. In-home visits are AED 180-500 including travel. Those belong to the providers named, not to us. We quote after a diagnostic, because board, tier and year group change the answer.

faqs.question: What should we budget per month for maths help in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai research puts specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month for one weekly hour, with mid-tier at AED 600-1,200 and budget at AED 240-600. In practice Year 11 families often buy two or three sessions a week in the final term, which multiplies the monthly figure. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits. The cheaper route is to buy the same total earlier, across Year 10, rather than compressed into five months.

faqs.question: Is a cheap maths tutor ever good value for an exam-year student?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and this is the commonest expensive mistake in this market. At AED 33-65 an hour a capable graduate can genuinely help a Year 8 with homework and keep them company through it. Handed a Year 11 entered for Extended or Higher tier, the same person will teach plausible mathematics that is not the specification, agreeably, for a term, and the paper performance will not move. The low hourly rate makes the total feel small, which is exactly why it goes unexamined until results day.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium buy anything for IGCSE maths out here?
faqs.answer: It buys physical presence, which is genuinely worth money for a younger or less self-managing student — someone to take a phone off the table and notice attention going before you do. For a Year 11 working through correct-board past papers, it buys a drive down Al Qudra Road. In-home rates are published at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from this corridor a real share of that is the journey. The thing that moves a maths grade is whether the tutor knows the specification, and that is uncorrelated with how close they live.

faqs.question: When is maths tutoring cheapest to buy?
faqs.answer: Year 9, which is when almost nobody buys it. A fixed-scope block of six to ten sessions on algebraic fluency and non-calculator work costs perhaps AED 1,500-3,000 at published mid-band rates and addresses the exact layer that struggling Year 11 students usually turn out to need. It feels unnecessary because nothing is examined yet. Year 10 is the next best, at roughly AED 6,000-12,000 across the year for a weekly mid-band session, and it arrives in Year 11 with foundations secure and the tier chosen deliberately.

faqs.question: Can tutoring move my child above their tier's grade ceiling?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge 0580 Core and Pearson 4MA1 Foundation cover a reduced syllabus and cap below the top grades, so no amount of teaching inside that entry produces an uncapped grade. This is why tier is the first thing to establish and why paying specialist rates inside a capped tier is money spent on something undeliverable. The decision is usually taken by the department during Year 10 and is often reversible for a while, which is where tutoring has its maximum financial leverage. Once the centre confirms entries, the question is closed.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to have practised the wrong exam board?
faqs.answer: A term, usually, and it is invisible until the real paper arrives. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different specifications with different tiering and paper structures, and past papers are not interchangeable. A tutor drilling the wrong board teaches correct mathematics while training the wrong instincts about what a question is asking for. The preventing step is free: one email to the school office asking for the board and syllabus code of each subject, because Dubai schools routinely use both across different departments.

faqs.question: Would a Dubailand tuition-centre group class be better value for us?
faqs.answer: Per head, yes; per outcome, it depends entirely on the student. Dubai centre listings put group classes at roughly AED 60-150 per student per hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified one-to-one tutor. A group works when a student's gap is the same as the group's gap and they will speak up. It works poorly when the gap is specific, because the pace is set by the middle of the room and nobody diagnoses an individual. For a DAMAC Hills 2 family there is also the drive out and back for every session.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week should we actually pay for?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two only in an exam term with a diagnosed reason. Maths rewards consistency and reflection between sessions more than volume: a student given three hours a week often does less independent practice, because the tutoring replaces it rather than directing it. Where we do recommend two or three, it is for a specific window with a defined endpoint rather than as a standing arrangement. More sessions is the easiest thing for any provider to sell and frequently the least effective thing to buy.

faqs.question: Why is the trial lesson free, and what is the catch?
faqs.answer: There is no card required and no obligation to continue, and the lesson is taught by the specialist who would actually carry on rather than by a salesperson. It is free because in maths explanation style decides whether the money works, and nothing written down predicts that — a tutor with the right specification knowledge and the wrong pace produces a pleasant term and no movement. Charging for the hour would mean families commit on worse information. If you are offered something free elsewhere, check whether its conditions appear on the same screen.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate mean a better maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The published Dubai top end is AED 500-650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650, and a premium rate reflects scarcity and reputation rather than demonstrated outcomes. Treat claimed examiner status as a claim until it is evidenced, and note that examiner status gives nobody access to marking, boundaries or paper content whatever is implied. We do not describe our own tutors as examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can demonstrate to you. Specification knowledge plus the right explanation pace is what you are buying.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the best return on tutoring spend?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation first, because almost everything else sits on it and most Year 11 students who name a different problem need this one. Then showing method, which is a habit change worth real marks and costs a few weeks. Then non-calculator fluency, and then the reliably examined topics students reliably get wrong — unequal-interval histograms, circle theorems, three-dimensional trigonometry. Each of those is a fixed-scope block with a visible endpoint, which makes them far better value than open-ended general revision.

faqs.question: Do we have to keep paying once the gap is closed?
faqs.answer: No, and we will tell you when it is. A fixed-scope block ends when the agreed topic list is covered, with a review and a deliberate stop rather than an automatic rollover into open-ended tutoring. An arrangement that continues by default is the quietest way a family overspends on tutoring, and it is easy for any provider to let happen. If you want to continue weekly after a block, that is a decision to make rather than a drift to notice six months later.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a UAE permit, and does it cost us anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs the tutor nothing, which means there is no price reason for anyone to lack one. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligibility covers school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see it. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.

faqs.question: Why does maths matter for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Because it is almost always one of the five subjects a plan depends on. For the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, even though both are mandatory in Dubai private schools. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae; IB Gram does not process or guarantee equivalency and nobody should imply tutoring is required for it.

intro.heading: Four comparisons to make before you book anything
paragraphs: Deira families searching for IGCSE mathematics help almost always start from a grade: a 5 that needs to be a 7, a C that needs to be a B, a mock that went badly. That is the right motivation and the wrong starting point, because before a grade can be moved somebody has to establish what is actually available to move. Four comparisons decide that, and most parents have never been shown any of them.

The first is the specification. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics carries the code 0580, with a 9 to 1 graded version also in circulation, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A carries 4MA1. The content overlaps heavily. The paper structure, the question style and the tiering language do not, and a student drilling the wrong board's past papers is rehearsing a question type they will not meet. The second is the tier: Core or Extended in Cambridge, Foundation or Higher in Pearson, with different content and a different grade ceiling in each.

The third is whether a fourth mathematics paper is involved. A number of Dubai schools enter stronger students for Cambridge Additional Mathematics or Pearson Further Pure Mathematics alongside the main qualification, which is a different syllabus requiring different teaching, and families frequently discover that only when the second set of homework appears. The fourth is what comes next: A Level Mathematics and IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches make different demands of an IGCSE base, and a student heading for one is best served by slightly different preparation than a student heading for the other.

Run those four comparisons and the tutoring brief usually writes itself. What does not change across any of them is the delivery question. IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video on a shared whiteboard, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics that is a positive rather than a compromise: both people write on the board, the student's own working is preserved rather than erased, and the board is saved so the next session opens where the last one stopped.

The local context is worth a line. Deira is dense apartment housing north of the Creek with both Metro lines running through it, and most secondary students travel out to schools in Al Qusais, Al Mamzar, Bur Dubai or across the water towards Al Garhoud. Arrival home is late and variable, and a quiet room at 5pm is not guaranteed, which is why sessions here are set from arrival rather than dismissal and why weekend mornings carry more of the sustained work than they would in a villa suburb.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-deira.subjectsIntro: The topic list is common to both specifications, with differences in emphasis and question style rather than coverage. Below is each area with how the two boards treat it and where marks go.

subjects.name: Number and the four operations in context
subjects.description: Ratio, percentages, compound interest, standard form and bounds. Both boards examine it heavily at the lower tiers and keep it present at the top. The commonest loss is reverse percentage and compound growth questions, where students apply the forward operation and the mark scheme credits nothing.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: All tiers, heaviest at Extended and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. This is the base the rest of the subject rests on and the single highest-leverage repair in either specification. Pearson's longer questions chain more steps, so weak manipulation shows up more sharply on 4MA1 Higher than on 0580 Extended.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Quadratics by factorising, formula and completing the square, plus simultaneous linear and non-linear pairs. Method marks dominate, so showing a clear line of working matters as much as the answer in both boards' mark schemes.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching, interpreting, reading solutions from graphs and transforming curves. Both specifications ask for graph interpretation in context, and students who treat a graph as a picture rather than as information lose marks across several questions on the same paper.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: All tiers, deeper at Extended and Higher
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, Pythagoras, trigonometric ratios and the sine and cosine rules. Diagram discipline carries real marks: students who do not annotate the given figure lose them systematically in both boards' longer multi-step problems.

subjects.name: Mensuration and three-dimensional work
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, and similar shapes with area and volume scale factors. The scale factor questions are reliably the most-missed topic in the whole syllabus in both specifications, and they are learnable in two sessions.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, tree diagrams and conditional probability at the top tiers. Histograms with unequal class widths are where marks concentrate, because frequency density is a step students skip.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and geometric reasoning with vector paths. Conceptually awkward and often taught late in the course, so it is still unfamiliar when mocks arrive, which is why it appears disproportionately in post-mock repair work.

subjects.name: Calculus, in the additional qualifications
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration with applications to gradients, stationary points, rates and areas. Present only in Additional Mathematics and Further Pure, and taught on a different timetable from the main course, which is why a student taking both needs a plan rather than goodwill.

subjects.name: Problem solving across topics
subjects.description: Multi-step questions that combine two or three topic areas without saying so. These separate grades more than any single topic, and they are practised only by sitting full papers to time rather than by working through topic exercises.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1
paragraphs: This is the comparison that changes what a tutor should be doing, and the one almost no family has been given. Both qualifications cover IGCSE mathematics to a similar depth and both are accepted on the same basis for progression, so the choice is not about quality. It is about structure, and structure determines revision.

The differences that matter in practice. Cambridge codes the subject 0580, with a 9 to 1 graded variant also in circulation, and tiers it into Core and Extended; Pearson codes it 4MA1 and tiers it into Foundation and Higher. Each tier in each board sits two papers. Pearson's questions tend to be fewer and longer, which rewards stamina and penalises a student who runs out of time halfway down a multi-part problem; Cambridge spreads marks across more items, which rewards pace and penalises careless short answers. Calculators are permitted throughout in both, which is worth knowing because it distinguishes IGCSE sharply from what comes next.

The practical consequence is simple and often ignored. Past papers must match the specification exactly. A student on 4MA1 Higher who has worked through 0580 Extended papers has practised a different distribution of question lengths, and will find the real paper unfamiliar in a way that has nothing to do with the mathematics. Ask the school for the exact code on the entry form, write it on one sheet, and give it to any tutor before the first session.

The calendars differ too. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates and allocates centres to one of six administrative zones, warning that the correct zone timetable must be used. Pearson runs May/June and November, and its November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only, so no UAE revision plan should reference it.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, Foundation against Higher
paragraphs: The tier is the most consequential thing about a student's mathematics entry and the thing parents are least often told explicitly. It sets both the content to be taught and the highest grade available, which means a tutoring plan built without knowing the tier can be targeting material the student will never be examined on.

The lower tiers cover a defined subset of the syllabus and cap the grade. The upper tiers cover that subset plus additional content — more demanding algebra, functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, vectors, and conditional probability — and leave the full grade range available. Question style differs as well as content: lower-tier questions carry more scaffolding and fewer unstructured multi-step problems, while upper-tier papers assume a student can combine two or three topics without being told to.

Schools allocate tiers on Year 9 and Year 10 attainment, and the realistic window to change one is early in Year 10 rather than the term before the papers. That makes the tier conversation a Year 10 action with a deadline, not a Year 11 complaint. Ask the school in writing which tier your child is on in mathematics, what evidence that rests on, and what the deadline is for changing it. If a change is both possible and worth pursuing, the tutoring brief becomes precise: close the gap on the upper-tier-only topics before the school's decision date.

One caution on ambition. Moving a student to the upper tier who is not ready converts a comfortable middle grade into a poor one, because upper-tier papers give fewer easy marks. The decision should rest on whether the student can handle unstructured multi-step problems, not on whether the family would prefer a higher ceiling.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually sit, topic by topic
paragraphs: Revision time should follow the marks, and in IGCSE mathematics it usually follows the textbook chapter order instead. Comparing topics by how much they typically contribute, and by how often students lose marks in them, produces a very different priority list from the one a student would construct alone.

Algebraic manipulation is the heaviest contributor at the upper tiers in both specifications, not because it is examined as a topic in its own right but because it is the machinery every other topic uses. A student weak in rearranging and factorising loses marks in equations, functions, trigonometry and mensuration, and will experience that as four separate problems. Repairing it is the single most efficient intervention available in the subject.

Then there are the reliably-missed topics, which are missed in the same way every year. Similar shapes with area and volume scale factors: students apply the length scale factor to an area. Histograms with unequal class widths: students read frequency off the vertical axis instead of computing frequency density. Reverse percentages and compound growth: students run the forward calculation. Vectors: students attempt the geometry without drawing the path. All four are narrow, teachable, and worth a session each.

The last category is problem solving across topics, which contributes more to the gap between grades at the top of either tier than any individual topic does. It cannot be practised through topic exercises, only through complete papers sat to time on the correct specification, which is why the weekend paper session exists as a separate format rather than being folded into weekday work.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure: the fourth paper
paragraphs: A number of Dubai schools, with the Al Qusais cluster the most common near Deira, enter capable Year 11 students for Cambridge Additional Mathematics or Pearson Further Pure Mathematics alongside the main qualification. Families frequently discover this only when a second set of mathematics homework appears, and almost nobody explains what the comparison involves.

These are separate qualifications, not extensions of the upper tier. They cover differentiation and integration, trigonometric identities, functions, series and coordinate geometry at a level closer to the beginning of A Level than to the end of IGCSE. That is the whole argument for taking one: a student heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches arrives with calculus already met, and the first term of post-16 study is noticeably easier.

The argument against is workload. A fourth mathematics paper in Year 11 sits alongside eight or nine other subjects, mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons, and the main mathematics entry. For a student who is comfortable it is a good use of the time; for a student who is managing, it is the thing that makes everything else slip. A strong grade in the main qualification and no fourth paper is a better outcome than two mediocre results, and that comparison should be made honestly in the autumn of Year 11 rather than in the spring.

For tutoring, the key point is that a tutor comfortable with 0580 Extended is not automatically comfortable with 0606. The calculus content is different teaching, and a tutor should be asked directly which of the two qualifications they have taught. In practice, a student taking both is often better served by one session on the additional qualification and school provision for the main one, since the additional syllabus is where the genuinely new material sits.

sections.heading: Comparing what comes next: A Level Mathematics against IB Maths AA
paragraphs: A Deira family choosing post-16 provision is usually choosing between A Levels at a school in Al Qusais or Bur Dubai and the IB Diploma across the Creek in Al Garhoud or Dubai Festival City. Both routes make demands of an IGCSE mathematics base, and the demands are not identical, so a student with a known destination can be prepared slightly differently.

A Level Mathematics assumes fluent algebra and introduces calculus, trigonometric identities and proof over two years in one subject, with examinations at the end. IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches covers comparable ground alongside five other Diploma subjects, adds an internally assessed exploration worth a fifth of the grade, and at Standard Level sits one paper without a calculator. That last point is the sharpest contrast with IGCSE, where calculators are permitted throughout, and it catches students who have never had to work without one.

The implications for IGCSE preparation are small but real. A student heading for either route benefits most from algebraic fluency, which is the shared prerequisite. A student heading for IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches additionally benefits from deliberate non-calculator practice in Year 11 — exact trigonometric values, surds, index laws, mental manipulation — because that is the specific habit the Diploma will demand and IGCSE will not have built. A student heading for A Levels benefits from Additional Mathematics if the school offers it, since the calculus overlap is direct.

None of this changes the tutoring format, and that is the point this page keeps returning to. Whichever side of each comparison a family lands on, the requirement is a tutor matched to the current specification who can also see the destination, and the fastest route to that person is a pool rather than a radius.

sections.heading: Comparing self-study, a group class and one-to-one
paragraphs: Before comparing providers, compare whether a provider is needed. IGCSE mathematics is unusually well served by free material, and a disciplined student with the right past papers can do a great deal without paying anybody. The honest comparison is therefore between three things, and the right answer is often a mixture.

Self-study works for content revision and for timing practice, provided two conditions hold: the papers are from the correct specification and tier, and the student marks against the official mark scheme rather than checking answers. Most Dubai schools make papers and schemes available on their learning platform, and most students use neither properly. Where self-study reliably fails is in diagnosing a habit: a student who loses method marks cannot see that in their own work, because the thing missing is invisible to the person who omitted it.

A group class, concentrated near Deira in the Al Qusais and Al Nahda centres, adds structure and pace at well below one-to-one rates, and for a student whose problem is not working consistently rather than not understanding, that structure is the thing they are missing. What it cannot do is work on one student's specific error pattern, because the class is moving at the group's speed.

One-to-one earns its premium on exactly that: diagnosis and the fix. An hour spent reading a marked script and naming the one behaviour costing marks is worth several hours of re-teaching. The sensible layering, then, is school provision and self-study for content, a group class if structure is missing, and one-to-one sessions used sparingly for diagnosis and for marked timed papers. A family who does this spends less than one buying three weekly sessions and usually gets more.

sections.heading: Comparing cost against what it changes
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates, read in October 2026 and attributed, give the bands. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, online and generally generalist. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table in the same range. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the named or examiner-level end. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted to AED 500.

The comparison worth making is not between the bands but between each band and the specific job. A budget-band hour buys supervised practice, which is genuinely useful for a Year 9 or Year 10 student who is not working consistently. A qualified-band hour buys content teaching, which is what a student with a real topic gap needs. A specialist-band hour buys diagnosis against a mark scheme and a judgement on tier readiness, which is what a Year 11 student stuck below a boundary needs. Buying the wrong band for the job is the commonest way money is wasted in this subject, and it happens in both directions.

Two specific cautions for mathematics. First, the in-home premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour buys proximity in a subject where a shared digital whiteboard is a better working surface than paper, so the premium purchases a worse environment as well as a smaller pool. Advertised monthly packages make the gap visible: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Second, the premium band above AED 500 is almost never necessary at IGCSE; it exists for scarce post-16 specialisms.

These are market figures rather than IB Gram's prices. We quote after a free trial lesson, before any payment, against a written plan with a total, because a two-topic repair block and a year of Year 10 work are different purchases.
