faqs.question: Which maths comparisons actually matter for a Discovery Gardens family?
faqs.answer: Four. Which board and syllabus code your child sits, Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1. Which tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. Whether the entry includes a paper without a calculator. And whether revision is marked paper work or unmarked topic coverage. All four are answerable from documents the school already holds. The comparison that does not matter is which community you live in, because Discovery Gardens and Al Furjan draw on exactly the same pool of tutors.

faqs.question: What changes between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 in practice?
faqs.answer: The number of papers, calculator provision across them, the formula support given in the exam room, how mark schemes credit method, the tier names, and the grade boundaries, which are published separately. So comparing a raw mark against the wrong board's boundaries is meaningless and practising the wrong board's papers teaches correct mathematics with unfamiliar conventions. Several schools in this corridor enter a different board for mathematics than for the sciences, so the entry list is the only reliable source.

faqs.question: My child is on Higher tier. Is that the top?
faqs.answer: In Pearson terms yes, and the Cambridge equivalent is called Extended, which is a frequent source of confusion between parents comparing notes. Both reach grade 9. The ones that cap the grade are Core at Cambridge and Foundation at Pearson, and both sound milder than they are. Ask the exams officer for the tier in writing alongside the board and code, and check it against your child's target grade before planning any revision at all.

faqs.question: When is it right to accept the lower tier?
faqs.answer: When algebraic fluency itself is missing across a year of marked work. A student pushed to the upper tier on ambition can score below what they would have achieved on the lower paper, because the questions assume fluency they do not have and time pressure compounds it. If the losses are method and reading rather than fluency, the student is stronger than the mark suggests and the upper tier is right. Three marked papers distinguish the two cases.

faqs.question: Does the non-calculator paper really need two years of preparation?
faqs.answer: It needs two years of maintenance, which is different from two years of preparation. Manual arithmetic, fractions, surds and paper-based algebra erode quietly through calculator-assisted homework, and the loss is invisible until a paper takes the calculator away. Ten minutes of manual work inside every weekly session holds it at almost no marginal cost. Rebuilding it in the final six weeks is possible and expensive, because fluency responds to frequency and there is none left by then.

faqs.question: Why does unmarked past-paper practice not work?
faqs.answer: Because it produces reassurance rather than information. Working through a paper with answers beside it builds recognition of question types and nothing else, which is why heavy past-paper use often coincides with a plateau. The version that works is timed, one sitting, no notes, then marked strictly against the real scheme with method and accuracy separated, then every loss categorised by cause. The categorisation is the step that converts a score into a plan.

faqs.question: What is an error log and how long does it take?
faqs.answer: Three columns per paper: which paper, what type of loss, and one sentence on what to do differently. About five minutes per paper. After four papers the pattern is undeniable and revision stops being a matter of opinion about which topics feel weak. It is the cheapest habit available in IGCSE mathematics and almost no student does it unprompted, because students see the question they got wrong rather than the behaviour that caused it.

faqs.question: Do Al Furjan families really have better tutoring options than we do?
faqs.answer: No. Neither community has a resident population of mathematics specialists, both are reached on the same drive from where Dubai's tutors live and work, and visiting tutors quote them in the same band. What the villa side has is a room with a door, which matters for hosting a visitor and is irrelevant once lessons are online. Travel actually runs slightly in your favour, because Discovery Gardens is compact and pickup is quicker than Al Furjan's long bus loops.

faqs.question: Is a centre class near Ibn Battuta worth it for Year 11 maths?
faqs.answer: For structure, pace and momentum, yes, and it prices well below one-to-one. For a diagnosed problem, no, because content is set in advance and delivered to the middle of the room: a student losing method marks will sit through a syllabus review that never mentions showing working. Many families here get the best result from both, a centre course for breadth plus one weekly one-to-one session on the thing that is not moving, which costs less than one-to-one across several subjects.

faqs.question: Which calculator model should my child practise on?
faqs.answer: The one the school requires, and it is worth asking in the first week of any tutoring arrangement. Statistical and table functions differ between models in ways that cost time under exam pressure and invite misread outputs, so a student who has learned a different model's menus is slower and more error-prone. Equally important is the habit of recording what was entered and what came back, because a bare number shows no method and the method carries most of a multi-step question.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking, or is a summer bridge enough?
faqs.answer: If post-16 mathematics is likely, the qualification is stronger, because Cambridge 0606 and Pearson 4PM1 bring calculus, logarithms, series and trigonometric identities a year early and examine them. That matters particularly here, since families in this corridor usually change schools at 16 and would otherwise meet a new school, a new teaching style and calculus in one term. Where the school does not offer it, four to six summer sessions on the same content does most of the useful work.

faqs.question: Which maths topics get skipped and then examined?
faqs.answer: Vectors, set notation and histograms with unequal class widths. All three are short and mark-dense, all three appear reliably, and all three get left out of revision because they look unfamiliar rather than because they are hard. Frequency density is skipped in class about as often as it is examined. For a student in the final term these are usually the fastest marks available, which is why a tutor should work from the marked mock rather than a syllabus checklist.

faqs.question: What time do maths sessions run for students in this community?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:00 or 17:30. Discovery Gardens students travel out of the community for school and are home from about 15:50 on the nearest Dubai Investments Park routes or 16:30 from the Al Barsha corridor, with Year 11 revision clinics pushing it later. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, seven days a week. In an apartment the protected hour matters more than the exact time, and that is a household agreement made once at the start.

faqs.question: Does online maths tuition work from a shared living room?
faqs.answer: It is among the easiest subjects to deliver well that way, because a session is shared written working rather than discussion: the student writes, the tutor sees it, and both annotate the same page. What it needs is a desk, over-ear headphones with a microphone and the marked work to hand. The harder half is interruption, which equipment does not solve: a session treated as a timetabled lesson by the household runs properly, and one treated as homework does not.

faqs.question: Can a tutor sit with my child during a timed school assessment?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor teaches method, questions reasoning, demonstrates technique and marks the student's own work against the board's conventions, with the feedback written down. A tutor does not complete set work, supply answers for submission, or support a student during an assessed task. It is also worth knowing that a tutor should not be distributing downloaded board papers and mark schemes, which are not theirs to give, and for unreleased material that is a malpractice exposure for the student.

faqs.question: Which of the four comparisons should we settle first?
faqs.answer: The board and the code, because every other decision depends on it and it takes one email to the exams officer. Then the tier, while Year 10 is still running and the entry window is open. Then the calculator question, which sets a habit rather than a plan. The revision method comes last only because it needs a marked paper to work from, and it is the comparison that then shapes every session for the rest of the course.

intro.heading: A long commute, a short evening, and a subject that needs a desk
paragraphs: Downtown Dubai is one of the densest residential districts in the city and one of the emptiest of schools. There is no large campus inside the Burj Khalifa district or along the Boulevard, so secondary-age children travel out: east across the creek extension to Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf, south-east to Meydan and Nad Al Sheba, west into Al Quoz and Al Safa, or further to Festival City and the coast. Those are not five-minute journeys. A Downtown student commonly spends between forty minutes and an hour and a half a day in a vehicle.

That has two consequences, and most tutoring advice ignores both. The first is that the evening is short. A child leaving home before seven and arriving back after five has a limited number of usable hours, and mathematics is the subject that suffers, because it cannot be half-done and cannot be skim-read. It needs a desk, a clear head and a full attempt at a question that will not accept a partial answer.

The second consequence is more useful. A Downtown student has a substantial, predictable, otherwise wasted block of time every single day, and some mathematics can genuinely be done in it. Not method work and not timed sections, which need a surface and silence. But formula recall, times tables and squares, standard-form conversions, angle facts, unit conversions, and the vocabulary of transformations are all memory work, and memory work survives a moving vehicle perfectly well.

So this page splits the subject in two. One list of things to practise in transit, built to be done without writing. One list of things that require the hour at the desk, which is what a tutoring session should be spent on. Separating them is worth more to a Downtown family than any amount of general advice about study habits, because it converts an hour of commuting a day into something, and it stops the desk hour being spent on work that did not need a desk.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the question, the working and the mark scheme on a shared surface both people can write on. For a household in a Downtown tower, where a visiting tutor negotiates approach roads, visitor parking and a security desk before reaching a lift, the removal of that overhead is not a small thing. What the format mainly buys, though, is a tutor matched to your child's syllabus code and tier.

Two things this page does not do. It does not claim that IB Gram is approved or accredited by Cambridge, Pearson or any UAE regulator, because it is not. And it does not promise a grade, because no honest provider can. What it contains instead is the split between commute work and desk work, the content difference between the two tiers, the three pieces of examination administration that cost grades silently, and the published Dubai market rates with their sources attached so that any quote you receive can be checked against them.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-downtown-duba.programmesIntro: Four things decide what an IGCSE mathematics tutor should do, and three are printed on your child's school documents.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Tiered Core or Extended. Core is capped at the middle grades; Extended reaches the top and carries functions, transformations, vectors, harder algebra and the non-right-angled trigonometry rules that Core does not touch. Cambridge has revised the paper structure for this syllabus, including a non-calculator component, so the live syllabus document is the authority on which papers your child's cohort sits.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June series with November as the resit route; the February and March series is offered to India only. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two written papers of equal weight, two hours each, with a calculator permitted throughout, tiered Foundation or Higher. The question-style distribution differs from Cambridge enough that a student switching boards misjudges pacing on their first full paper. Foundation caps at the middle grades and Higher reaches the top, exactly as Core and Extended do.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in a May or June window and a November window, and the published record is checkable: the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Where Your Child Is in the Two-Year Sequence
programmes.description: The variable most families cannot answer and the one that determines whether a weak topic is a worry or a non-event. Schools teach the syllabus in their own order, so a Year 10 student who has not met vectors has not fallen behind; a Year 11 student in the second term who has not met them has. Knowing the scheme of work turns anxiety into a checklist.
programmes.countryNote: Downtown families feed campuses across several districts and the schemes of work differ between them, so there is no single Dubai order. Ask the mathematics department for the Year 10 and Year 11 scheme of work; it is a routine request and it is the single most useful document for planning tutoring.

programmes.name: What the Mathematics Grade Opens
programmes.description: The IGCSE mathematics grade is the most commonly specified sixth-form entry requirement in Dubai for both A Level and the IB Diploma, and the higher post-16 mathematics routes assume Extended or Higher tier content as their floor. It also feeds Ministry of Education equivalency for students who later apply to UAE universities.
programmes.countryNote: The published British-track equivalency rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. IB Gram does not perform equivalency; verify current rules with the Ministry.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-downtown-duba.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics splits into work that can be practised anywhere and work that needs a desk. Each entry below says which it is, which is the organising idea of this page.

subjects.name: Times tables, squares, cubes and roots
subjects.description: Pure recall, and therefore commute work. A student who hesitates over seven times eight is spending attention on arithmetic that should be free, and that attention is needed elsewhere in a question. Ten minutes a day in a vehicle settles this permanently and costs nothing.

subjects.name: Formula recall
subjects.description: Both boards provide some formulae in the examination and not all of them, and which is which is on the live specification. The ones not provided are commute work: areas and volumes of standard shapes, the quadratic formula, the trigonometric ratios, and the circle results. Knowing which list applies is the first thing to establish.

subjects.name: Standard form and unit conversion
subjects.description: Largely commute work once the rule is understood. Converting between units of area and volume is the recurring loss, because students scale by the wrong power. Said aloud a few dozen times it becomes automatic, and it then stops costing marks in mensuration questions it has nothing to do with.

subjects.name: Angle facts and circle theorems
subjects.description: The statements themselves are recall and travel well; applying them to an unfamiliar diagram is desk work. A useful division is to learn the theorems aloud in transit and then spend the session on the diagrams, which is where students actually lose the marks.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Desk work, unambiguously, and the foundation the rest of the subject stands on. A student who rearranges hesitantly will spend their trigonometry lesson doing algebra badly. It is also the slowest thing on the course to repair, which is why it belongs in Year 10 rather than in a late block.

subjects.name: Quadratics
subjects.description: Desk work. Factorising, completing the square, the formula and solving graphically. Sign errors inside the formula and giving one root where two were asked for are the standing losses. Completing the square is often learned as a ritual and breaks as soon as the leading coefficient is not one.

subjects.name: Functions and graph transformations
subjects.description: Desk work and higher-tier only, which makes it the clearest content marker of the tier boundary. A student moved up a tier mid-course has usually never met function notation or transformation rules, so this needs teaching from first principles rather than revision.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Mixed. The ratios and the rules are recall; choosing between them for a given triangle is desk work. Students lose marks by applying right-angled methods to a non-right-angled triangle, and by leaving the calculator in degrees or radians wrongly for an entire question.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Desk work. Tree diagrams, conditional probability, cumulative frequency and histograms with unequal class widths. The histogram is the standing higher-tier trap: frequency density has to be calculated and students plot frequency, losing a whole question rather than part of one.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: The formulae are commute work; the scale factors are desk work. Lengths scale by k, areas by k squared and volumes by k cubed, and higher-tier questions are designed to punish the wrong power. Able students lose marks here more often than weak ones, because they answer quickly.

subjects.name: Showing working
subjects.description: Not a topic but the largest recoverable loss on any mathematics paper, and pure desk work because it is a writing habit. Method marks exist and are awarded for the intervening steps. Students praised for mental speed forfeit them most often, and the fix is one instruction repeated until it sticks.

subjects.name: Exam pacing
subjects.description: Desk work requiring a clock. Over-answering the accessible early questions and abandoning the last page is a recurring pattern on both boards, invisible in untimed homework, and therefore undiscovered until a mock. Three or four timed sessions with the time per question recorded fixes it in most students.

sections.heading: What the Downtown school run actually costs a maths student
paragraphs: Here is the commute written out as a table, because it is the organising fact of a Downtown week. Children leave a district with almost no schools in it and travel to campuses in four or five directions, and the journey lengths differ enough to change what an evening can contain. Find the row that matches your child and the rest of the plan follows from the last column.

The pattern is consistent. The creek corridor towards Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf is the shortest run and leaves the most usable evening. Al Quoz and the coastal direction are moderate but unpredictable, because cross-traffic at pickup varies day to day. Meydan, Nad Al Sheba and Festival City are the longest regular journeys, and students on those routes are home late enough that a serious mathematics session has to start after six or move to a weekend.

What the table also shows is the size of the transit block, and this is the part worth acting on rather than lamenting. Forty minutes to an hour and a half a day, five days a week, is a substantial quantity of time that currently produces nothing. It cannot produce method work, because that needs a surface and silence. It can produce recall, and recall is a real component of an IGCSE mathematics grade rather than a consolation prize.

The specific items are listed in the next section, but the principle is simple enough to state here. Anything a student could say aloud and check without writing belongs in the car. Anything requiring a written line of working belongs at the desk. Families who separate the two find that the desk hour gets noticeably more productive, because it stops being partly spent on things that did not need a desk.

sections.heading: What can be practised in a car, and what cannot
paragraphs: This is the division that makes a Downtown week work, and it is more specific than it first sounds. The test is whether the item can be said aloud and checked without a written line. If it can, it belongs in transit. If it requires a line of working, a diagram or a calculator, it belongs at a desk and should be the content of a paid session.

The transit list is genuinely useful rather than token. The formulae the examination does not provide, which is the first thing to establish from the live specification. Times tables, squares to twenty and the common cubes and roots. Standard-form conversions. Unit conversions, particularly the area and volume ones that students scale by the wrong power. Angle facts and circle theorem statements. The names and defining features of the four transformations. Metric prefixes. The vocabulary of probability. All of that is recall, and all of it currently costs marks for want of fluency.

The desk list is everything else and it is where a session belongs. Algebraic manipulation, which is a reflex built through writing. Quadratics in all their forms. Choosing between the trigonometric rules for a given triangle. Any diagram-based question, including the circle theorem applications that follow from the statements learned in the car. Histograms with unequal class widths. Scale factors for area and volume. Showing working, which is a writing habit. And timed sections, which require a clock and a surface.

A practical caution about the transit list. It works when it is short and verbal and fails when it is ambitious. A list of four items said aloud for ten minutes gets done; a printed sheet of twenty questions in a moving vehicle does not, and insisting on it produces a child who associates the car with being tested. The useful version is small, spoken, and refreshed each week from what the session revealed.

sections.heading: Ask for the scheme of work, then stop worrying about half of it
paragraphs: One free request changes the whole tone of IGCSE mathematics for a family, and almost nobody makes it. Ask the mathematics department for the Year 10 and Year 11 scheme of work. It is a routine document, departments have it, and it lists what will be taught in which term. With it in hand, a weak topic becomes a scheduling fact rather than an alarm.

The reason this matters is that schools teach the syllabus in their own order, and there is no single Dubai sequence. A Year 10 student who cannot do vectors has almost certainly not been taught vectors, which is not a problem. A Year 11 student in the second term who cannot do vectors has been taught them and has not retained them, which is a different situation needing a different response. Without the scheme of work, both look identical to a parent and both produce the same worry.

The document also makes the tier conversation concrete. The higher-tier-only topics, functions and graph transformations, vectors, the sine and cosine rules, unequal-width histograms and the area and volume scale factors, will appear somewhere in the sequence, and their position tells you when the school expects a student to be coping with higher-tier demand. A family wanting an Extended or Higher entry can see exactly which term the evidence has to be produced in.

And it makes a tutoring plan checkable rather than open-ended. With the sequence in front of you, a plan can say which topics are already taught and weak, which are coming, and which are not relevant yet. That turns a request for help into a list, and a list has an end. Without it, a mathematics arrangement tends to run on general grounds, which is how a sensible decision becomes a two-year commitment.

sections.heading: What the formula list gives you, and what it does not
paragraphs: Both main boards provide some formulae in the examination and not all of them, and which list applies is on the live specification for your child's syllabus. That single fact should shape revision and almost never does, because students memorise everything or nothing rather than finding out which half matters.

Establishing it takes one look at the specification and it changes two things. First, it tells you what is genuinely worth committing to memory, which becomes the transit list described earlier. Second, it tells you what can be looked up, which means those items should be practised for speed of retrieval rather than recall. Hunting for a provided formula under time pressure costs minutes, and minutes lost on the final page are marks.

A related point about the calculator applies to Pearson candidates in particular, who have a calculator in both papers, and to Cambridge candidates under the revised structure, which includes a non-calculator component. What is given and what is calculable are different questions, and a student who assumes the device will carry them through a non-calculator paper is in trouble for reasons that have nothing to do with understanding.

None of this is sophisticated and all of it is routinely skipped. Open the current specification, find the formula list, mark which items your child must know from memory, and put those on the transit list. The rest become retrieval practice. Twenty minutes of administration, once, and it removes a whole category of lost marks for the remainder of the course.

sections.heading: What an hour costs in Downtown Dubai, and what the commute does to its value
paragraphs: Here is the published market, every figure credited to the provider that published it and read in October 2026, none of it IB Gram's price list. Budget online and university-student tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the premium end.

In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, travel included, with monthly in-home packages published at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. For a Downtown tower the travel component of an in-home rate is larger than in most districts, because the approach roads off Sheikh Zayed Road, the limited or valet-only visitor parking and the security registration are all before the lift.

The commute changes the value of the hour as well as its price, and this is the Downtown-specific point. A student arriving home at six after an hour in traffic is not at their best, which means the hour bought at 18:00 is worth less per dirham than the same hour on a weekend morning. Families who shift one of their two weekly sessions to a Saturday morning consistently report it as the more productive of the two, and it costs exactly the same.

Which produces a simple spending shape for this district. One weekday desk hour, timed late enough to be realistic. One weekend morning session where sustained work is possible. A transit list that costs nothing and uses time already spent. And no in-home premium, because in a tower in this district the premium is buying the right to negotiate a security desk. sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects and the arithmetic of the week
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. One of KHDA's requirements has a direct bearing on whether a Year 11 student has time to practise mathematics, and it is rarely connected to tutoring in anything a family reads.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA setting the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes are required by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs strictly prohibited.

Add those lessons to nine or ten IGCSE subjects, and then add a Downtown commute of up to an hour and a half a day, and the independent study time the mathematics syllabus assumes largely does not exist. When a parent in this district says their child has no time for past papers, it is usually the literal truth. That is the reason this page is organised around reclaiming transit time rather than around adding evening hours that are not there.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none of those relationships. The reason to set out the framework is that it explains the shape of the constraint. Any provider promising to add three hours of mathematics to this week has not looked at the week, and a plan that depends on hours which do not exist will fail regardless of the teaching quality.

sections.heading: The entry deadline, the tier and the zone timetable
paragraphs: Three pieces of examination administration decide more than most teaching does, and all three can be settled with an email to the school. They belong on a page about a crowded week precisely because they cost nothing in time and can cost a grade if ignored.

The first is the tier. Both boards tier mathematics, Cambridge as Core and Extended and Pearson as Foundation and Higher, and the tier caps the achievable grade because the questions that reach the top grades do not appear on the lower paper. The tier is fixed at the final entry deadline, which sits months before the exam, and schools form the decision on internal evidence at the end of Year 10 or early in Year 11. After the entry closes, nothing changes it.

The second is the entry deadline itself, which is administered by the school's exams officer against the board's published date. Knowing when it falls tells a family when the tier conversation has to happen, and the answer is always earlier than feels natural. If you want a higher-tier entry, the classwork evidence supporting it has to exist before the decision is made, which means the work producing that evidence happens the term before.

The third is specific to Cambridge and costs candidates whole examinations. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre sits in, then use that version only. One email, and a category of disaster that no tutoring repairs is removed.

sections.heading: Booking, and the shape we will recommend
paragraphs: Send the board, the tier, and a marked piece of work if you have one. A marked script shows whether marks went to method, content, a calculator habit or time, and those four need different interventions and different numbers of sessions. If you can also send the scheme of work from the mathematics department, the plan that comes back will be a checklist rather than a general offer.

The first session is free and is a timed section from a real paper rather than an introduction, with the student attempting while the tutor watches where the method breaks. Afterwards you receive a short written note splitting the lost marks, naming the earliest genuine gap, estimating the sessions the remaining window needs, and listing the recall items to practise in transit. That last part costs nothing and is the Downtown-specific half of the plan.

On timing, we will usually recommend the shape described earlier: one weekday desk hour timed late enough to be realistic for your child's journey, and one weekend morning session where sustained work is actually possible. Families in this district consistently find the weekend session the more productive of the two at the same price, and it is the easiest change to make. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there.

Two limits before you commit. Weekend morning slots are in demand across the city and go early in the second term, so arranging one in term one matters. And if no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai and no office, centre or branch in the UAE; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Four specifications, two tiers, and a decision that closes doors two years out
paragraphs: Start with the code, because in mathematics more than any other subject it changes the revision plan completely. Cambridge runs Mathematics 0580 and the 9-1 graded variant 0980, each split into Core and Extended tiers sitting different papers. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, with Foundation and Higher tiers, and Specification B, 4MB1, which is a separate qualification with its own content and style. A tutor who assumes one of these is teaching the wrong course.

The most practical difference is the calculator. Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its equally weighted papers. A student drilled in mental and written arithmetic for a paper that allows a calculator has spent weeks on a skill that earns nothing, and a student who has never practised without one will meet Cambridge Paper 1 unprepared. This is a five-minute question with a term-sized consequence.

In this cluster the answer varies by school. Dubai International Academic City is a university free zone, and its own secondary, Dubai English Speaking College, runs the British route. The other schools families here use - in Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Garhoud - make their own board choices, sometimes differently for mathematics than for the sciences. Ask the examinations officer for the entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option, in writing.

The second decision is tiering, and it is the one with the longest shadow. Cambridge Core caps the achievable grade at C or grade 5; Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5. Both are perfectly sufficient for Ministry of Education equivalency, which asks for no less than E or grade 3 across five accredited subjects. Neither is sufficient for a sixth form requiring grade 6 for A Level Mathematics or for the IB Diploma's Analysis and Approaches. The cap is invisible in Year 10 and decisive in Year 12.

The good news is that the gap between Core and Extended is a named list of topics rather than a general standard, which makes it schedulable. A targeted block through the first term of Year 10, working specifically on the Extended-only content, is often enough to move a borderline student. The table further down this page sets out what those topics are, because no competitor page in this market does.

IB Gram delivers this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE, where home visits are an India-only service. For mathematics the practical gain is that the tutor can be somebody who teaches 4MA1 Higher or 0580 Extended routinely rather than whoever lives near Dragon Mart and remembers GCSE maths from another country.
bullets: Cambridge 0580 and 0980 split into Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher
Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants; 4MA1 allows a calculator throughout
Core and Foundation cap the grade at C or 5; Extended and Higher run the full range
MoE equivalency needs five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, which Core reaches comfortably
A sixth form asking for grade 6 in mathematics has excluded a Core candidate before the paper is sat
Lessons are one-to-one and online; no tutor travels to a UAE address

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-academi.programmesIntro: Three points in the mathematics route where families in this cluster ask for help, and what the work actually is at each.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 mathematics, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Nothing is externally examined, so weakness is invisible until the IGCSE course begins. The specific gaps that cause trouble later are negative-number work, fraction arithmetic without a calculator, rearranging formulae, and the ability to factorise without stopping to think. None of these is advanced and all of them are assumed from the first week of Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: The Year 9 conversation matters more here than parents expect, because it is where the school forms a view on tier. Ask at the Year 9 parents' evening which tier they intend to enter your child for in mathematics and what evidence would change that view. In this cluster, where several schools sit within a few kilometres, the same student can be assessed differently at two of them.

programmes.name: Year 10, the building year
programmes.description: Content is taught and nothing is urgent, which makes this the cheapest place to fix a problem and the best place to argue for a tier change with evidence. Past-paper work can begin at the intended tier rather than being saved for Year 11, and a topic genuinely missing from Key Stage 3 can be rebuilt without competing against revision.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Academic City, Silicon Oasis and Mirdif who start mathematics tutoring in the first term of Year 10 typically buy fewer total hours across the two years than those who start after the Year 11 mocks. The arithmetic is simple: building is cheaper than repairing, and repairing under deadline pressure is the most expensive version of all.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the series
programmes.description: Content finishes and the work becomes technique: working shown, rounding controlled, timing per mark, and the long final questions attempted rather than abandoned. In mathematics this reliably recovers marks because so much of the loss is habit. It cannot replace a topic that was never taught, and a tutor should say which of the two you are buying.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. Mock results in Dubai schools usually arrive in the second term, which leaves a defined run to the June papers and makes the marked mock script the most useful document in the process.

programmes.name: IGCSE into A Level or the Diploma
programmes.description: The step up is steeper in mathematics than in anything else, because A Level Mathematics and the IB Diploma's Analysis and Approaches both assume the Extended or Higher content is automatic rather than achievable. A student who reached grade 6 by leaning on a calculator finds the first term of Year 12 genuinely difficult, since new content arrives faster than old content can be repaired.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster the route splits visibly: Dubai English Speaking College continues to A Level inside Academic City, while families wanting the Diploma move towards Silicon Oasis, Mirdif or Nad Al Sheba. Either way, six to eight bridging sessions in the summer after Year 11 on indices, surds, algebraic fractions and function notation is the best-value mathematics tutoring available.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-academi.subjectsIntro: Mathematics tutoring is topic work. These are the areas families in this cluster raise, with the specific demand each one makes.

subjects.name: Number and arithmetic without a calculator
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form and estimation worked by hand. Essential for Cambridge variants with a non-calculator paper and irrelevant for Pearson 4MA1, which is exactly why establishing the specification first saves weeks of misdirected practice.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying algebraic fractions and rearranging formulae with the unknown appearing twice. This is the foundation that every later topic stands on, and a student who does it slowly cannot do the rest of the paper in the time available.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic equations, inequalities on a number line, and simultaneous equations solved algebraically. Extended adds quadratic simultaneous equations and the quadratic formula applied to awkward coefficients, where sign errors cost most of the lost marks.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, graph sketching and transformations. Extended-only territory in Cambridge and a reliable source of marks for students who understand transformations rather than memorising a list of rules.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry at Core; the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional trigonometry at Extended. Marks go on failing to draw the triangle, on using the wrong rule, and on calculators left in the wrong angle mode.

subjects.name: Geometry, circle theorems and similarity
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, congruence, similarity and, at Extended, circle theorems. Circle theorem questions require the theorem to be named as part of the reasoning, and students who state the answer without the justification lose the reasoning marks every time.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry and the four transformations. Extended questions combine vectors with ratio along a line, which rewards drawing the diagram and labelling it before any calculation is attempted.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, and tree diagrams. Extended adds conditional probability. Histogram questions involving frequency density are among the most reliably mishandled on the paper.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Area, surface area, volume, arcs and sectors, speed, density and pressure. Marks disappear on unit conversion, particularly between cubic centimetres and litres, and on rounding applied before the final step of a multi-stage calculation.

subjects.name: Calculus foundations at Extended and Higher
subjects.description: Gradient functions, differentiation of polynomials, and turning points where the specification includes them. Worth attention beyond the examination because it is the direct bridge into A Level Mathematics and the Diploma courses.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MB1 Specification B content
subjects.description: A separate qualification with its own content and examination style, taken by a minority of schools. Worth confirming explicitly on the entry list, because a tutor prepared for 4MA1 will not be prepared for this and the difference is not cosmetic.

subjects.name: Bridging content for A Level and the IB Diploma
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, basic differentiation and the trigonometric identities both routes assume from the first week. Six to eight sessions over the summer, and the cheapest genuinely useful mathematics tutoring a family in this cluster buys.

sections.heading: Which mathematics qualification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This sounds like a trivial question and it is the one that most often goes unanswered until a tutor asks it. Four specifications are in common use across Dubai schools, and they differ in grading scale, calculator rules, tier names and examination style. Two of them share almost all their content and differ in how it is assessed; one of them, Pearson Specification B, is a genuinely different qualification.

The grading scale alone causes confusion. Cambridge 0580 reports on A* to G while 0980 reports 9-1, and parents comparing a cousin's results across the two scales reach conclusions that do not hold. Pearson 4MA1 reports 9-1. When a school changes variant between cohorts, older siblings' results stop being a useful benchmark, and nobody announces the change.

The practical test is to get the entry list in writing from the examinations officer and read it with the table below. If the list says 0580 Extended, non-calculator practice belongs in the plan. If it says 4MA1 Higher, it does not, and the hours go into the long multi-step problems at the end of each paper instead. If it says 4MB1, say so to any tutor before booking, because preparation for Specification A does not transfer.

One more reason the code matters in this district specifically. Students in this cluster change schools within Dubai more often than in older, more settled neighbourhoods, and a transfer in Year 10 can mean a change of specification mid-course. That produces a particular kind of gap - content covered under one specification and never under the other - which is invisible on a report and obvious in a marked paper.

sections.heading: The topics the higher tier adds, named
paragraphs: The gap between Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher, is routinely described to parents as a difference in standard. It is better understood as a list. The higher tier covers everything the lower tier does and then adds a defined set of topics, and most of the distance between a borderline student and the higher tier sits inside that added set rather than across the whole subject.

That matters because a list is schedulable and a standard is not. A term of targeted work through Year 10 on function notation, circle theorems, vector geometry with ratio, histograms with unequal intervals and the harder trigonometry covers most of the added ground. Delivered alongside the school's teaching rather than instead of it, it produces marked evidence at the higher tier, which is what a school needs in order to revisit a decision.

The table below is generic across the common specifications, because the exact division varies by code and revision. Confirm it against the syllabus for your child's specification on the board's own site rather than relying on any summary, including this one. What does not vary is the principle: ask the school which topics your child is not being taught because of the tier they are in.

The reason to do this in Year 10 is that it stops being possible later. By the second term of Year 11 the tier is fixed in most schools, the content is nearly complete, and the only remaining lever is technique. Technique is worth real marks and it cannot lift a ceiling that was set eighteen months earlier.

table.caption: CONTENT THE HIGHER TIER ADDS, TYPICAL ACROSS SPECIFICATIONS
rows: Algebraic fractions, harder quadratics, rearranging with the unknown twice
Function notation, composite and inverse functions
Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, three-dimensional problems
Circle theorems, similar area and volume ratios
Vector geometry with ratio along a line
Histograms with unequal intervals, cumulative frequency, conditional probability

sections.heading: Where IGCSE mathematics marks actually go
paragraphs: Mark two timed papers properly and the same short list appears almost every time. Working not shown, so a correct answer scores one mark out of three. Rounding applied at an intermediate step, so later accuracy marks fall away. The last long question left blank because it looked unfamiliar. Units omitted or converted wrongly. A calculator left in the wrong angle mode. A circle theorem used without being named.

None of these is a failure of understanding and all of them are expensive. That is why technique work moves a mathematics grade faster than content revision in the final months: habits change in weeks, where understanding takes terms. A student losing eight marks a paper to method can usually recover most of them in six to eight sessions of deliberate practice.

The method for finding your own child's list is simple and almost nobody does it. Have one timed paper marked question by question against the published mark scheme, with the reason for each lost mark written down in the student's own words. Most students have three or four recurring reasons. That list is the lesson plan, and it becomes an error log checked for recurrence every session.

The topic-level gaps are usually narrower than they feel too. Across this cluster the recurring weak areas are algebraic fractions, circle theorems, histograms involving frequency density, and the ratio-and-vector questions that combine two ideas. Those are nameable and schedulable, which is a very different proposition from a general sense that mathematics is not going well.
bullets: Working omitted turns a correct answer into one mark out of three
Early rounding destroys accuracy marks for the rest of the question
Final long questions abandoned rather than attempted for partial credit
Unit conversion errors, especially cubic centimetres to litres
Circle theorems applied without being named in the reasoning

sections.heading: What the mathematics grade closes, and when
paragraphs: A mathematics grade is unusual in how much else it determines. It gates A Level Mathematics and the IB Diploma's Analysis and Approaches, and through those it gates engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics degrees. It also gates entry to some sixth forms entirely, independently of the subject the student wants to study. Few families in this cluster see that chain until Year 12.

The equivalency picture is separate and much more relaxed. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Core tier reaches that comfortably. Equivalency is almost never the reason to buy mathematics tutoring.

So the planning question is not the floor but the ceiling. Find out, in Year 10, what grade the sixth forms your child might attend require for mathematics, and whether Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is on the table at any of them. Then work backwards. The table below sets out the typical chain, and the specific requirements should be read on each school's and university's own admissions page.

For families in this cluster, the local route split makes this concrete. Dubai English Speaking College inside Academic City continues to A Level on site; the Diploma schools are in Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa and Nad Al Sheba. Each sets its own entry grades. Asking two of them in Year 10 rather than one in Year 11 is the whole of the planning work required.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper, and calculator discipline on the others
paragraphs: Where a specification includes a non-calculator component, it is a different examination requiring different preparation, and it is where a certain kind of strong student quietly loses marks. Fraction arithmetic, percentage work, standard form, surd manipulation and estimation all have to be fluent by hand. A student who has used a calculator since Year 7 can understand every topic on the paper and still run out of time on it.

The preparation is specific and slightly tedious: short, frequent hand-calculation drills rather than long problem-solving sessions. Ten minutes at the start of each session, every session, for a term. It is the least glamorous thing a tutor does and it shows up directly in a mark.

On calculator papers the discipline runs the other way. The common errors are angle mode, premature rounding of a stored value, and using the calculator to reach a numerical answer on a question that wanted algebraic reasoning and awarded marks for it. Storing intermediate values rather than rewriting rounded ones is a two-minute habit that protects accuracy marks through an entire paper.

And for Pearson 4MA1 candidates, where a calculator is permitted in both papers, the hours that would have gone into hand arithmetic belong somewhere else: the extended multi-step problems at the end of each paper, which carry substantial marks and which students leave blank far more often than they attempt partially. Partial attempts score. Blank space does not, and that single sentence is worth more marks across a paper than most topic revision.

sections.heading: The June series, the November series, and the resit question
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any page advising a Dubai family to prepare for a February mathematics paper is giving them a date for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November.

The useful reference points are sourced. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any date you plan around should come from the live official timetable rather than from a summary.

One Cambridge detail that belongs in every mathematics plan: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Establish the zone before reading any dates yourself.

For the resit decision, ask the school for the component breakdown rather than working from the grade. In mathematics a grade built on one collapsed paper is a strong resit case with roughly five months to work on a named problem; a uniformly weak profile across both papers usually is not, because the same preparation repeated produces the same result. Note also that November results reaching students in late January land after most sixth-form courses have begun.

sections.heading: What mathematics tutoring costs here, and what the bands actually contain
paragraphs: Every figure in this section was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram rate. The market splits into bands and the useful thing is not the numbers but what each band contains. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That band contains competent help with Key Stage 3 and Core-tier content, and rarely contains anybody who teaches Higher tier to grade 8.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is where most useful IGCSE mathematics tutoring in Dubai actually happens. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180 to 500.

Monthly, which is how families budget: published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

For context on fees generally: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For our own rates, the free trial lesson comes first and the figure is quoted against your child's actual specification and tier rather than against a table.

sections.heading: Finding a tutor who teaches the specification, and checking the permit
paragraphs: The matching question here is narrow. You are not looking for a maths tutor but for somebody who teaches 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher routinely enough to know which question types appear where and what the mark scheme credits. In this part of Dubai the number of such people within driving distance of Academic City is small, which is the practical argument for taking travel out of the equation.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, so no tutor can price it into a rate, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you. Ask to see the permit.

One arrangement to decline rather than seek: the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An offer of your child's own mathematics teacher, privately, is a problem for the teacher before it is a benefit to you.

We also state what we are not. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the permit issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not publish star ratings we cannot evidence with countable reviews.

process.title: Get the entry list from the school
process.description: Subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option, in writing from the examinations officer. For mathematics this single document decides whether non-calculator drilling belongs in the plan, which topics the tier includes, and whether a tutor prepared for Specification A is any use at all.

process.title: One timed paper, marked properly
process.description: At the intended tier, against the published mark scheme, with the reason for every lost mark written down. That produces three or four recurring reasons rather than a general impression, and those reasons become the plan for the first six sessions.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written note
process.description: A real lesson on real mathematics with the student working and the tutor diagnosing. Afterwards a plain summary: the method habits found, the topic gaps, and what the available weeks would target. Say no and nothing further is owed.

process.title: Weekly sessions with an error log
process.description: One session a week, two in the run-up to a series, with the student keeping the error log and the tutor checking it for recurrence each session. Short written reviews every few weeks on what has moved. If the match is wrong we reassign rather than defend it.

whyPoints.title: The code before the lesson plan
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0980, Pearson 4MA1 and Pearson 4MB1 are four different preparations. We ask for the entry list before matching, which prevents a term of non-calculator drilling for a candidate sitting two calculator papers.

whyPoints.title: The higher tier as a topic list, not a standard
whyPoints.description: Function notation, circle theorems, vector ratio, histograms with unequal intervals, the sine and cosine rules. Naming what the tier adds makes a tier push schedulable in Year 10, which is the only point at which it is still possible.

whyPoints.title: Method marks treated as a subject
whyPoints.description: Working shown, rounding controlled, units checked, angle mode verified, final long questions attempted. Most IGCSE mathematics mark loss is habit, and habits move in weeks where understanding takes terms.

whyPoints.title: The chain from this grade to the next decision
whyPoints.description: A mathematics grade gates A Level Mathematics, the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches and much of engineering through them. Equivalency needs only E or grade 3. Knowing which number matters in Year 10 is worth more than any amount of Year 11 effort.

whyPoints.title: The calendar UAE candidates sit
whyPoints.description: Cambridge June and November, Pearson May/June and November, and the February and March series offered to India only. We also name the Cambridge zone timetable issue, which has caused candidates to miss papers and appears on almost no tutoring page.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider who published it and the month it was read. Where we cannot staff a specification well, you hear it at the enquiry stage with a realistic wait, rather than meeting a generalist at specialist rates in session three.

faqs.question: Can I get an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your address, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. For mathematics specifically the online route solves a real problem in this district: the small number of tutors living within driving distance of Academic City are unlikely to teach your child's exact specification, and 0580 Extended, 4MA1 Higher and 4MB1 are not interchangeable preparations. Matching online lets us pick on the code and tier instead of on the postcode.

faqs.question: Which maths specification is my child entered for, and how do I find out?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer for the entry list in writing: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option. Four specifications are common in Dubai schools. Cambridge 0580 grades A* to G and often includes a non-calculator paper; Cambridge 0980 covers the same content graded 9 to 1; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers; Pearson 4MB1 is a separate qualification whose preparation does not transfer from 4MA1. The class teacher may not know; the examinations officer will.

faqs.question: Does my child need non-calculator practice for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Only if the specification includes a non-calculator component, which common Cambridge 0580 variants do and Pearson 4MA1 does not. This is why confirming the code first matters: a student drilled in hand arithmetic for two calculator papers has spent weeks on a skill worth nothing, and a student who has never practised without one will run out of time on Cambridge Paper 1 despite understanding every topic. Ten minutes of hand calculation at the start of each session, for a term, is the right dose where it applies.

faqs.question: What exactly does Extended tier cover that Core does not?
faqs.answer: A defined list rather than a vaguely higher standard. Typically: algebraic fractions and harder quadratics, function notation with composite and inverse functions, the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional trigonometry, circle theorems and similar area and volume ratios, vector geometry involving ratio along a line, and histograms with unequal intervals plus conditional probability. Confirm the exact division against the syllabus for your child's code on the board's own site. The point is that a list can be scheduled, and most of a borderline student's gap sits inside it.

faqs.question: Can we still change my son from Core to Extended tier?
faqs.answer: In Year 10, often yes, with evidence. The work is specific rather than general: a targeted block on the topics Extended adds, run alongside the school's teaching, with timed questions at Extended tier producing marked papers you can take to the school. By the second term of Year 11 most schools have fixed entries and the content is nearly complete, which leaves technique as the only remaining lever. Technique is worth real marks and cannot lift a ceiling set eighteen months earlier.

faqs.question: What grade does my daughter need in maths for A Level or the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Read each sixth form's published requirement, because they differ. The pattern is that A Level Mathematics and the IB Diploma's Analysis and Approaches usually ask for grade 6 or above, with the Higher Level version depending on fluency as much as on the grade. Note that Ministry of Education equivalency asks for far less - five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3 - so equivalency is not the number to plan around. Ask two sixth forms in Year 10 rather than one in Year 11.

faqs.question: My son understands the maths but loses marks in papers. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always method rather than comprehension. The recurring habits are working omitted so a correct answer scores one mark out of three, rounding applied at an intermediate step so later accuracy marks fall, the final long question left blank rather than attempted for partial credit, unit conversion errors, and a calculator left in the wrong angle mode. One timed paper marked question by question against the published mark scheme will name his three or four reasons, and those are weeks of work rather than terms.

faqs.question: Why does my child leave the last question on each paper blank?
faqs.answer: Usually because it looks unlike anything practised and the time has gone. Both causes are fixable. Partial attempts score in mathematics: setting up the right equation, drawing the right diagram or stating the right rule earns marks even when the answer never arrives, and students routinely do not believe this until a tutor shows them a mark scheme. The timing fix is a minutes-per-mark habit practised on half papers under strict time, which usually leaves ten minutes that previously disappeared.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE maths tutoring cost in eastern Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026, attributed to the providers publishing them: budget and university-student online tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more; in-home one-to-one with travel at AED 180 to 500. The budget band is usable for Core-tier content and rarely contains anybody teaching Higher tier to grade 8.

faqs.question: Is Silicon Oasis or Academic City better placed for maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Silicon Oasis marginally, because schools sit inside the district and a 4.45pm session is realistic, where from Academic City 5pm is the practical floor. But that is logistics rather than substance. Neither neighbourhood contains a usable local choice of tutors who teach a named international mathematics specification at Higher or Extended tier, and nor does Mirdif or International City. Once lessons are online all four draw from the same pool, which is larger than any of them had on its own.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Year 11 maths need?
faqs.answer: One a week through most of the year, moving to two in the run-up to the series or when a specific topic needs rebuilding. From International City, where weekday starts slip towards six, one weekday evening plus a weekend morning works better than two evenings - and the weekend slot is where a full paper can actually be sat to time, which cannot be done properly at seven at night. Two sessions a week for a full year is rarely necessary and often a sign the plan is unfocused.

faqs.question: My child moved schools in Year 10 and changed boards. What should we check?
faqs.answer: Two things. First, the content gap: a change of specification mid-course can leave topics covered under one and never under the other, which is invisible on a report and obvious in a marked paper. Second, the tier, because tier names and ceilings differ between boards and a Foundation entry at the new school may not match the expectation set at the old one. Ask both schools for the entry details and have one timed paper marked at the new specification to find the gap.

faqs.question: Should we resit maths in November after a disappointing June result?
faqs.answer: Decide on the component breakdown rather than the grade, and request it from the school as soon as results arrive. A grade built on one collapsed paper with the other solid is a strong case: the problem is named and roughly five months is ample. A uniformly weak profile usually is not, because repeating the same preparation tends to reproduce the result. Check timing too - November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, after most sixth-form courses had started.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a UAE permit to teach maths privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it.

faqs.question: Will you give us past papers for the specification?
faqs.answer: We cite and link the official sources on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than distributing copies, because that material belongs to the boards. The official site is also the only place certain to hold the current version rather than a syllabus two revisions out of date, which matters in mathematics where content is periodically moved between tiers. Schools hold past papers and will usually release them to candidates, and the subject teacher is the quickest route to the right tier and variant.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-creek-h.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IGCSE mathematics for families around Dubai Creek Harbour: specialists matched to one specification and one tier, who work from that board's own past papers and mark to its published scheme.

intro.heading: Five questions before you hire anyone
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai Creek Harbour asking whether anyone nearby actually knows this syllabus is asking a fair question, and the answer depends entirely on which syllabus is meant. IGCSE mathematics is not one qualification. Cambridge runs Mathematics 0580, divided into Core and Extended, and Additional Mathematics 0606 as a separate award. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher, and Specification B, 4MB1, which is a different paper structure again. Four codes, three tier systems, and no interchangeability between the past-paper sets.

So the five questions are these. Which board? Which code? Which tier? Is 0606 or an equivalent additional award also being taken? And which series is the entry for, June or November? A tutor who cannot answer those after three lessons is teaching mathematics competently in the general direction of your child's examination. That is the specific failure this market produces, and it is invisible until the mock, when marks come back lower than the student's understanding deserves and everyone concludes more hours are needed.

Geography makes it worse here rather than better. Dubai Creek Harbour contains no private school, so its secondary pupils travel out every morning: across the Ras Al Khor crossing to Dubai Festival City, down Al Khail Road into Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba, or over the Creek to Al Jaddaf. Those schools do not share one board. A family selecting a tutor by proximity is therefore selecting from a pool that happens to live near a bridge, not from a pool that has taught their child's code.

IB Gram removes travel from both sides of the arrangement. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai Creek Harbour or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service that exists only in India. That is stated plainly because a family weighing a visiting tutor against an online specialist should know which one they are reading about, and because the trade is a real one with a cost table attached further down this page.

On the calendar, one correction worth making early. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any provider quoting a Dubai family a March maths window has the wrong country, and a family that planned revision towards it would lose a term. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers and are set by the school's own exam office.

What follows is specific to mathematics and specific to this neighbourhood: the two boards compared code by code, what each tier ceiling actually means for a grade, the topics where marks reliably disappear, why Additional Mathematics 0606 matters more than its reputation suggests, what the Dubai market charges, and how a session fits around a Creek Harbour school run.
