dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-creek-h.programmesIntro: Creek Harbour families need IGCSE maths support at three distinct points, and the useful work differs sharply between them. These are the routes we cover.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The two-year Cambridge award, entered at Core or Extended. Core is capped below the top grades; Extended carries the full range. Assessment is by written papers at the end of the course with no coursework component. Number, algebra, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics make up the content, with Extended adding depth in each.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable per zone, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is why two Creek Harbour pupils at different schools can sit the same maths paper at different local times. We plan revision from the school's own issued timetable and check paper durations against the current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge revises them.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Specification A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher and assessed by two written papers of two hours each, 100 marks apiece, with a calculator permitted. Specification B, 4MB1, is a different structure and is entered by a smaller number of schools. Foundation tier carries a grade ceiling, so tier choice is a grade decision taken a year before the exam.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so we work from the live official PDF rather than restating a date that may be revised.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate award taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for post-16 mathematics. It introduces functions, quadratics in depth, binomial expansion, differentiation, integration, advanced trigonometry and vectors a year early. There is no Core tier; the whole award sits at Extended level.
programmes.countryNote: Around Dubai Creek Harbour, 0606 is where the local tutor pool thins out fastest. It is taken by a minority of students, so the number of tutors within driving distance of Ras Al Khor who have taught it to completion is small. It is also the single strongest bridge into A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, which makes a thin local pool an expensive constraint rather than a minor one.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-creek-h.subjectsIntro: Within IGCSE mathematics the requests cluster in predictable places. These are the topic areas Creek Harbour families ask about most, and what each one actually requires.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, algebraic fractions, changing the subject of a formula and solving simultaneous equations including one non-linear. This is the largest single source of lost marks at the top tiers, and almost all of it is sign error inside a correct method rather than a misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Sketching quadratics, cubics, reciprocals and exponentials, reading solutions from intersections, and in 0606 composite and inverse functions with domain and range. Marks go to students who label axes and intercepts; sketches without labels are treated as decoration by the scheme.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled triangles, sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings, and three-dimensional problems at the higher tiers. The reliable failure is the ambiguous case of the sine rule, closely followed by a calculator left in the wrong angle mode for a whole question.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, and circle theorems. Scale factors are the discriminator: students who square and cube them correctly gain marks that students who apply the linear factor throughout cannot recover.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths, tree diagrams and conditional probability. Histograms with unequal widths are a standing trap, and tree diagrams are where a drawn diagram earns marks the same reasoning in prose would not.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentage
subjects.description: Standard form, bounds and limits of accuracy, compound interest, reverse percentages and proportional division. Reverse percentage is the single most commonly failed Foundation and Core question type, and bounds questions reward a student who writes the interval before calculating.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry proofs, and the four transformations with full descriptions. A transformation question requires the complete description, so a rotation without a centre and direction earns part marks at best.

subjects.name: Calculus in 0606
subjects.description: Differentiation of polynomials, products, quotients and trigonometric functions, stationary points, rates of change, and integration including definite integrals and areas. This is the content that makes 0606 the bridge into post-16 mathematics and the reason specialist availability matters.

subjects.name: Paper technique and timing
subjects.description: Minute-per-mark allocation, writing method so that method marks are claimable, and the final-five-minutes checking habit. For most students at a mid grade, technique work moves marks faster than any additional topic coverage does.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1, specification by specification
paragraphs: These two codes dominate IGCSE mathematics in Dubai, and a family can reach Year 11 without being told which one applies. It is on the statement of entry and the school exam office will confirm it in one email. Doing so before buying tuition is the highest-value five minutes available in this whole process, because the past-paper sets are not interchangeable and the tier systems are not equivalent.

Pearson Specification A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher and assessed through two written papers of two hours each, 100 marks apiece, with a calculator permitted. Specification B, 4MB1, exists and has a different structure; a smaller number of schools enter it. Cambridge 0580 divides into Core and Extended rather than Foundation and Higher, entered as a shorter paper plus a longer structured paper at each tier, with no coursework. Cambridge has revised paper durations and calculator arrangements across syllabus versions, so the current syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org is the only safe reference for those details, and we check it per cohort rather than relying on memory.

The scheduling difference matters as much as the content one. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone, and it states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson publishes one international timetable, provisional first and then final. A Creek Harbour revision plan built from a timetable found through a general search rather than issued by the school is built on the wrong document.

sections.heading: What a tier choice actually costs, and when it is made
paragraphs: Tier is the most consequential decision in IGCSE mathematics and it is frequently made quietly. Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation both carry a grade ceiling: a student entered at the lower tier cannot be awarded the top grades regardless of how well they perform. Extended and Higher carry the full range but include harder content and a steeper paper. Schools usually decide on the basis of Year 10 performance, and a parent who does not ask will often learn the decision after it has been made.

The reason to ask early is that the decision is reversible for a while and then is not. A student sitting mid-range marks in Year 10 may be placed at the lower tier for safety, which protects a pass and closes the top grades. If post-16 plans include A Level Mathematics, Physics, Economics or an IB Higher Level science, the ceiling matters, because those courses assume the Extended or Higher content. Closing that door at fifteen to secure a safer grade at sixteen is a trade worth making deliberately rather than by default.

Where tuition genuinely changes the picture is in the window between the provisional tier decision and the final entry. A student who is borderline and gets focused work on the specific Extended topics that scared the department can move the decision. A student who gets generalised extra maths usually does not, because the department is watching particular evidence: algebraic fluency, confidence with the harder geometry, and performance on the longer structured paper under timed conditions.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Parents in Creek Harbour usually report that the topics got harder. The mark schemes usually report something else. A large share of lost marks at both tiers are not knowledge failures at all. They are sign errors inside correct methods, unclaimed method marks, scale factors applied linearly to areas and volumes, calculators left in the wrong angle mode, and the last three questions on the long paper left unattempted because minutes were spent unevenly.

Take reverse percentage, the most reliably failed question type at Core and Foundation. The student knows what a percentage is. The question gives a price after a discount and asks for the price before. The student multiplies instead of dividing. It is a one-line error that recurs across every paper and costs marks every time, and it is fixed in roughly twenty minutes of deliberate practice. Similar shaped errors sit in area and volume scale factors, where the linear factor is applied to a volume, and in histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency is read instead of frequency density.

At Extended and Higher, the dominant loss is unclaimed method. A student reaches a correct answer in three lines where the scheme awards marks across five, then loses two marks on a question they fully understood. In the reverse case, a student makes an arithmetic slip early and writes so little working that no method mark can be rescued from a wrong answer. Both are solved by the same instruction: write the line you were about to do in your head. It takes a fortnight of enforced habit and is worth more than a month of new content.

This is why the first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. One timed paper on the exact code and tier, marked against the published scheme question by question, and the topic list is then written by the marking. A list produced that way shortens each week. A list copied from the syllabus contents page stays the same length until the exam.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics 0606: the bridge most families find out about late
paragraphs: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is taken by a minority of IGCSE students and it is the single most useful qualification for anyone heading into post-16 mathematics. It introduces differentiation, integration, binomial expansion, composite and inverse functions, and advanced trigonometric identities a full year before A Level or the IB Diploma would. A student arriving in Year 12 having done 0606 meets almost nothing genuinely new in the first term. A student arriving from 0580 Extended alone meets several things at once.

There is no Core tier in 0606, so there is no safer version to fall back on, and schools often teach it in less curriculum time than the content warrants, sometimes as an additional option outside the main timetable. The result is a cohort of capable students covering calculus quickly, with the department moving on before fluency has settled. That is exactly the shape of problem one-to-one work solves well, because the gap is narrow and specific rather than broad.

The availability problem is the reason this section exists on a Creek Harbour page specifically. Within a practical driving radius of Ras Al Khor, the number of tutors who have taught 0606 through to a June series is small. It is not a reflection on Dubai's teaching market; it is arithmetic about a minority subject in one district. Nationally the pool is considerably larger, and online delivery is what makes it reachable. Where we cannot match a 0606 specialist in the window a family needs, we say so and give a realistic wait rather than placing a general maths tutor against it.

For families still choosing options, the practical advice is simple. If post-16 plans point towards A Level Mathematics, Physics, Engineering or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, 0606 is worth the extra load. If they do not, the same hours spent raising an Extended grade are better spent.

sections.heading: Fitting a maths session into the Creek Harbour evening
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject most sensitive to session timing, because it is the one that collapses fastest when a student is tired. Reading a history source at 19:00 after a long commute is possible. Holding four steps of an algebraic rearrangement in working memory at the same hour frequently is not. So for maths specifically, an earlier shorter session beats a later longer one, and a weekend morning beats both.

The arithmetic of a Creek Harbour evening runs roughly like this. A secondary pupil at a Dubai Festival City school is generally home by 16:00 if the Ras Al Khor crossing behaves, making 16:45 the first realistic slot. A pupil commuting to Sobha Hartland is better at 17:00, and one travelling to Nad Al Sheba or Downtown at 17:15 or later. A co-curricular day pushes all of those back by an hour or shifts the session to the weekend entirely. Choose the slot for the worst normal weekday rather than the best, because the fixture nobody mentioned is what kills a weekly arrangement in week three.

Two practical consequences follow. First, sixty focused minutes at 17:00 is worth more for maths than ninety minutes at 18:30, and we will say so rather than sell the longer session. Second, families able to offer a weekend morning have materially more choice of tutor, because the weekday window from 17:00 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time is the busiest hour in the UAE tutoring day. For a scarce specification such as 0606 that often decides whether the match is exact or approximate.

Where two children in one household need maths at different levels, running both sessions back to back on one evening keeps the rest of the week clear and keeps a parent supervising once rather than four times. It is a small logistical point that makes a term-long arrangement survivable.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the coursework line
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, with thirty-seven per cent of pupils on UK curricula, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. None of that is an endorsement of any tutor. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and no claim on this page depends on one.

Tutoring is regulated separately, by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here and none should be quoted to you.

There is a related boundary worth naming. A Creek Harbour parent may be tempted to pay their child's own maths teacher for private lessons. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The person who teaches the class and sets its assessments should not be separately paid by one family in it.

On materials, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works. We reference and link them from the boards' own sites; we do not reproduce or supply them as downloads. In lessons we show a student how to find the official source themselves, which is a skill worth more than any file we could hand over.

sections.heading: Getting matched, and what happens if the specialist is not free
paragraphs: Send five things: board, specification code, tier, whether 0606 is also being taken, and the series the entry is for. Add two evening windows that genuinely survive a normal week after the school run. We match a specification specialist, run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, and give you a plan afterwards. One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, no card details required to book it.

Then the honest part. Specialists concentrate unevenly, and the thinnest coverage is for 0606 and for Pearson Specification B, in the weeks immediately before a series when demand is highest. If nobody with the right specification has a slot in your window, we will tell you, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest genuine alternative: a different time slot, a shorter weekly commitment with a specialist whose availability is limited, or paper-technique work while the subject slot is pending. What we will not do is place a general maths tutor and describe the match as exact.

Review happens at the school's next assessment rather than on a fixed schedule. If marks have not moved where the plan predicted, the plan changes or the tutor does, and replacement inside the same week is possible precisely because the match was never bounded by driving distance from Ras Al Khor. That is the practical benefit of online delivery that nobody advertises, and it matters most in the final term.

Two limits to state plainly. Nobody can promise a grade and this page does not. And nothing here implies that tutoring is needed for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university entry or for school progression; on the British track the published equivalency rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. Verify your own case with the Ministry.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE maths tutor come to our apartment in Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: Some Dubai agencies do send visiting tutors, at published in-home rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers. IB Gram is not one of them. We deliver one-to-one tuition for UAE families online over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to any UAE address; home visiting is an India-only service. The trade for a Creek Harbour family is usually favourable, because it replaces a pool bounded by a drive from Ras Al Khor with one that has actually taught your child's specification.

faqs.question: Which maths specification code will my child's Dubai school have entered them for?
faqs.answer: It will be one of four in common use: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics at Core or Extended, Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics, Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Specification A at Foundation or Higher, or Pearson 4MB1 Specification B. The code appears on the statement of entry and the school exam office will confirm it by email. Ask before buying any tuition. The past-paper sets are not interchangeable, and a term of preparation aimed at the adjacent code looks fine until the mock, when marks come back below what the student's understanding deserves.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Core and Extended in Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: Content and ceiling. Core covers a narrower syllabus and is capped below the top grades, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded them however well they perform. Extended includes algebraic fractions, vectors, circle theorems and harder trigonometry, and carries the full grade range. The decision is normally made by the school on Year 10 evidence. If post-16 plans involve A Level Mathematics, Physics, Economics or an IB Higher Level science, the ceiling matters, so it is worth asking the department which tier they are planning well before entries close.

faqs.question: Is Pearson Foundation tier a safer choice than Higher for a borderline student?
faqs.answer: It is safer for securing a pass and it closes the top grades, which is a real trade rather than a free one. Foundation reduces the algebra and geometry demand, which suits a student who is losing marks through insecurity rather than through gaps. Higher keeps the full range open but presents a steeper paper where written method becomes essential. For a genuinely borderline student, the useful window is between the provisional decision and the final entry, and focused work on the specific Higher topics the department doubts can move the decision when general extra maths will not.

faqs.question: Why does Additional Mathematics 0606 matter if my child is already taking 0580?
faqs.answer: Because it introduces differentiation, integration, binomial expansion, composite and inverse functions and advanced trigonometric identities a year before A Level or the IB Diploma would. A student who has done 0606 meets almost nothing new in the first term of a post-16 maths course. A student arriving from 0580 Extended alone meets several things at once. It has no lower tier, and schools often teach it in less curriculum time than the content warrants, which is why one-to-one support on it is a narrow, specific job rather than a broad one.

faqs.question: Why is it hard to find a 0606 tutor close to Ras Al Khor?
faqs.answer: It is arithmetic rather than a reflection on Dubai's teaching market. Additional Mathematics is taken by a minority of IGCSE students, so the number of tutors in any single district who have taught it through to a June series is small. Nationally the pool is considerably larger, and that is what online delivery reaches. Where we cannot match a 0606 specialist inside the window a family needs, we say so and give a realistic wait rather than placing a general maths tutor against a calculus syllabus and describing the match as exact.

faqs.question: Which maths topics cause Creek Harbour students the most lost marks?
faqs.answer: At Core and Foundation, reverse percentage leads by a distance: the question gives a price after a discount and asks for the price before, and the student multiplies instead of dividing. Close behind are area and volume scale factors applied linearly instead of squared and cubed, and histograms with unequal class widths read as frequency rather than frequency density. At Extended and Higher, the dominant loss is unclaimed method, where a correct answer in three lines forfeits marks a five-line scheme would have awarded on a question the student fully understood.

faqs.question: How much should a Creek Harbour family budget each month for IGCSE maths help?
faqs.answer: Using published market estimates rather than an hourly figure alone, Bestimate's monthly bands for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to other providers, not to IB Gram. Our own quote follows the free trial lesson, because it depends on code, tier and series proximity.

faqs.question: Is AED 50 an hour enough for Core or Foundation maths support?
faqs.answer: For a narrow purpose, often yes. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik, which generally means a tutor who sat the subject recently. For unblocking Core or Foundation homework that can be genuinely sufficient, and paying more would be waste. For Extended algebra, 0606 calculus or paper technique marked against a published scheme, it usually is not, and the limit is specificity rather than ability. Match the tier of tutor to the job rather than to the budget alone.

faqs.question: What time should a maths session start if my child commutes to Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: Around 17:00 on a normal weekday. Secondary schools in the Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City corridor finish in the mid-afternoon and the run back to Creek Harbour puts the student on southbound Al Khail Road at the school-run hour. Mathematics is the subject most sensitive to fatigue, because holding several steps of a rearrangement in working memory is harder than reading a text at the same hour. Sixty focused minutes at 17:00 is worth more than ninety at 18:30, and a weekend morning is worth more than either.

faqs.question: Can my child retake IGCSE maths in November rather than losing a year?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series, and UAE candidates may sit either. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The November route is the standard retake path. Two practical points: the entry must be made through the school's exam office shortly after the June results, and results arrive in the new year rather than in August, which matters where a sixth-form or university conversation depends on them. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Should we be planning for a February or March maths exam in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. This matters because several pages written for Gulf parents quote a February or March window with an Indian entry deadline, and a family acting on it would plan a term of revision towards an exam their school cannot enter them for. Treat a provider quoting that window to you as a reason to check everything else they have said.

faqs.question: Does my child's Cambridge maths exam start at a different time from a friend's?
faqs.answer: It can, and it depends on the school's administrative zone rather than its district. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, and it states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is why two Creek Harbour pupils at different schools can sit the same maths paper at different local times. Print the timetable the school issues, give the tutor the same copy, and do not work from one found through a general search.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by Cambridge or by KHDA to teach IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; it regulates and inspects schools, and an inspection rating is a judgement about a school rather than about any tutor. A KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff. Treat any provider implying regulator endorsement as a reason to examine their other claims carefully.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers and mark schemes for my child to work through?
faqs.answer: We work from them in lessons and we link the official source, but we do not reproduce or supply them as downloads. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works, and redistributing them is not something a legitimate provider should offer. What we do instead is show the student how to find the official material on the board's own site, which is a more useful skill: a student who can locate a current syllabus can also check a claim a tutor has made.

intro.heading: Price IGCSE maths by the month, then ask how many months
paragraphs: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives monthly estimates for one weekly hour, and they are more useful than any hourly figure: roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist. Those are the numbers that land on a household budget. An hourly rate of AED 150 sounds moderate until it is a two-year commitment, and a rate of AED 400 sounds alarming until it is four sessions in total.

So the question that decides the bill is duration, and duration is decided by what is actually wrong. A Year 10 student who missed a unit on trigonometry needs two or three sessions and is done. A Year 11 student who cannot reliably rearrange a formula has a problem that started in Year 8 and will take two terms, because algebraic fluency is built by repetition rather than by explanation. Both students look identical on a report that says grade 5.

The second thing that decides the bill is the tier. On Cambridge 0580 a student is entered for Core or Extended; on Pearson 4MA1 for Foundation or Higher. The lower route in each case does not reach the top grades. A family spending at the exam-year specialist rate in the spring of Year 11 on a Core or Foundation entry is paying the highest band in the market for a grade ceiling that was fixed months earlier by somebody else. That is the single most expensive misunderstanding in this subject.

The rate bands themselves, for completeness and with their sources. Budget online tuition runs AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. A qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 across the market, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. All published by those providers and read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Dubai Festival City the delivery is live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For mathematics that is not a compromise: the working appears on a shared screen at the same size for both people, a wrong line can be annotated as it happens, and a marked past paper can be walked through question by question with both pairs of eyes on the same marks.

What follows is the detail that makes a monthly figure meaningful. Which board sets what. What the tier actually caps. The nine topics that cost most marks in this subject and what each costs to fix. What the 9 to 1 scale means and where the boundaries bite. And when in Years 9, 10 and 11 the money does the most work, which is earlier and smaller than almost anybody spends it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-festiva.programmesIntro: IGCSE mathematics sits in the middle of a longer sequence, and where a family spends in that sequence changes the total more than any discount. These are the three stages that matter.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 mathematics, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Number, algebra, ratio, geometry and statistics with no external examination at the end. Nothing is at stake in grade terms, which is precisely why it is the cheapest place to buy. Fluency with indices, fractions, negative numbers and rearranging formulae is established here or it is not established at all.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Festival City families routinely spend nothing in Year 9 and a great deal in Year 11. A term of budget-band support at AED 45 to 65 an hour aimed at one named Year 9 weakness prevents an exam-year specialist booking at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month two years later. The comparison is not close and nobody markets it.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years to externally marked papers, with two papers sat per tier in both Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1. Cambridge splits into Core and Extended routes, Pearson into Foundation and Higher tiers. The entry decision taken during Year 10 sets the range of grades available in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the money goes, and where it should be spent on fewer months with a clearer target. Mathematics also underpins the quantitative parts of IGCSE physics and chemistry, so fixing it first often lifts two other subjects without anybody being paid to teach them. That sequencing argument is worth more than any hourly saving.

programmes.name: A Level, IB Diploma or BTEC after Year 11
programmes.description: Sixth-form mathematics routes have specific IGCSE grade requirements, and so do the sciences and economics that depend on mathematical fluency. A grade short of the requirement means either a November resit, with entry fees and a term of preparation, or a change of plan.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School runs the IB continuum into the Diploma and other schools near Dubai Festival City lead into A Level, so the consequence of an IGCSE maths grade varies by destination. Ask the school what grade the intended route needs before deciding how many months of tuition to buy, not after results arrive in August.

programmes.description: Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade.
programmes.countryNote: Mathematics is almost always one of the five, which makes it the subject where an equivalency problem is least likely but most consequential. At least one page ranking for UAE tutoring queries states that six subjects are required; it is five. Verify on moe.gov.ae, and note that IB Gram does not perform equivalency and cannot affect it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-festiva.subjectsIntro: This is IGCSE mathematics broken into the topics families actually buy tuition for, with what the topic costs in marks and roughly what it costs to fix. Use it to decide which two or three to pay for rather than booking the subject as a whole.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying, and rearranging formulae. The single highest-value topic in the subject, because it appears in every paper and underpins physics and chemistry calculations too. Weakness here is structural and takes repetition rather than explanation, so budget terms not sessions.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and indices
subjects.description: Adding, subtracting and simplifying algebraic fractions, fractional and negative indices. A classic Extended-tier discriminator: students either handle these fluently or avoid every question containing one. Four to six focused sessions usually closes it because the procedures are finite.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry at all tiers, with the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional problems at the higher tiers. Marks are lost by picking the wrong rule rather than by arithmetic, which makes it a diagnosis-and-drill topic with a short fix.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic and reciprocal graphs, gradients, intercepts and transformations. Students sketch plausible curves without the features that carry the marks: intercepts, turning points and asymptotes. A technique fix rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms, tree diagrams and conditional probability. Usually the best-value topic to buy, because the methods are procedural and a short block produces visible movement on a mock paper.

subjects.name: Ratio, proportion and percentages
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Direct and inverse proportion, compound interest, reverse percentages. Reverse percentages are the commonest single error in the whole subject at every tier, and they are taught properly in under an hour, which makes them nearly free marks.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, similar shapes and circle theorems at the higher tiers. Similar shapes with area and volume scale factors is the topic students most often think they understand and most often get wrong under time pressure.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry and the four transformations. Compact topic with a predictable question style, so a single targeted session plus marked practice tends to be sufficient rather than a term.

subjects.name: Number without a calculator
subjects.levels: Where the syllabus sets a non-calculator component
subjects.description: Exact fractions, surds, standard form and arithmetic done cleanly on paper. Check with the school whether your child's entry includes a non-calculator paper, because if it does this becomes a separate drilling job from everything else on this list.

subjects.name: Exam technique and timing
subjects.description: Reading the command word, showing enough working for method marks, and not spending twelve minutes on a four-mark question. Technique responds faster than content and is the correct purchase for the last eight weeks before a series.

sections.heading: The monthly numbers, and what duration does to them
paragraphs: Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are the figures to plan against: roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist. Alongside those, the packages actually seen in this market are about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Same contact time in those two packages, roughly double the price for the second.

Multiply by months and the picture changes shape. Two terms of mid-band weekly tuition is around six months, so AED 3,600 to 7,200 on those estimates. A four to six session topic block at the same band is a fraction of one month. An eight-week final intensive is two months. Those three plans differ by an order of magnitude, and which one a family needs is determined entirely by the diagnosis rather than by how worried anybody is.

This is why the first useful conversation is not about price. It is about whether the problem is a missed unit, a technique habit, or structural fluency. A missed unit is two sessions. A technique habit is a block. Structural fluency is two terms, and buying two sessions for it wastes both. Nobody can tell which of the three you have from a report grade, which is the whole argument for a diagnostic before a booking.

One more thing the monthly view exposes. A family that commits to weekly tuition in September and never reviews it will spend nine or ten months regardless of whether the subject stabilised in November. Reviewing at the mock window and cutting where the evidence says to cut is the single largest saving available in this subject, and it requires nothing except asking the question.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE mathematics in Dubai and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge International's mathematics syllabus carries the code 0580 and splits candidates into Core and Extended routes, each sitting two papers. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE mathematics is 4MA1 and splits into Foundation and Higher tiers, each sitting two papers of two hours with a calculator permitted throughout. Cambridge has also introduced a non-calculator component on the current syllabus, so confirm with the school which papers your child's entry involves.

The content overlap is large and the assessment experience is not. Command-word phrasing differs. The distribution of marks between topics differs. The way a question is scaffolded differs, and scaffolding is exactly what a student relies on when they are uncertain. A tutor who has taught one board for years will teach a competent term of the other and the student will meet an unfamiliar paper in the mock, which is both expensive and avoidable.

Grading is the other thing to check. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on an A* to G scale and others on a 9 to 1 scale, depending on the variant a school enters, while Pearson's International GCSE mathematics reports 9 to 1. That matters when a sixth-form requirement is expressed as a grade 6 or a grade B, because the two are not identical and a family comparing them without checking can misjudge how far from the requirement their child actually is.

The fix is one message. Ask the school for the syllabus code and the tier, in writing, for mathematics specifically rather than for the subjects as a group. Many Dubai schools enter some subjects with Cambridge and others with Pearson, so an answer about the school is not an answer about the subject. Quote that code when you request a tutor, and ask the tutor to tell you how the two boards differ before you book.

sections.heading: The tier decides the ceiling, and Year 10 is the window
paragraphs: Core on Cambridge 0580 and Foundation on Pearson 4MA1 do not reach the top grades. That is the most financially significant sentence on this page. A student entered for the lower tier can work extremely hard, be tutored expensively, and still finish below a grade threshold a sixth-form course requires, because the papers they sat do not contain the marks needed to cross it.

The entry decision is made by the school, usually during Year 10, on the basis of classwork and internal assessment. It is a prediction about which papers the student will perform best on, and it is often correct. It is also sometimes a reaction to one weak term, or to a student who was absent during the unit that the decision rested on. Those cases are reviewable, and the review has to happen while the entry can still be changed.

So the sequencing of tuition money follows directly. If there is any ambition towards a sixth-form course with a specific mathematics requirement, the diagnostic belongs in Year 10, aimed at establishing whether the ceiling is set by ability or by a gap from Key Stage 3. That is a small, cheap, early purchase. Spending the exam-year specialist band in the spring of Year 11 on a lower-tier entry is the opposite: the largest spend at the moment it can do least.

A practical note on evidence. Schools respond to specifics rather than to parental conviction. A written assessment showing that a student handles Extended-level algebraic fractions and indices once the Year 8 index rules are secure is a conversation; a request to move tiers because the parent believes the child is capable is not. The useful tutoring purchase in Year 10 is often the assessment itself rather than a term of lessons.

sections.heading: The topics that cost the most marks, and what each costs to fix
paragraphs: Not every weakness is equally expensive to repair, and knowing the difference is how a family buys three topic blocks instead of two terms. Reverse percentages, for instance, are the commonest single error in this subject at every tier and can be taught properly in under an hour. Similar shapes with area and volume scale factors are a close second and take two sessions. Both are nearly free marks sitting unclaimed.

At the other end, algebraic fluency is not a topic at all but a capability, and it is the one thing that genuinely requires months. Expanding, factorising, simplifying and rearranging appear in every paper and underpin the calculation marks in IGCSE physics and chemistry too. A student without it will appear to have weaknesses in trigonometry, graphs, mensuration and probability, when in fact they have one weakness showing up in five places.

That is the diagnostic insight worth paying for. Take two marked papers, classify every lost mark, and look for whether the errors cluster by topic or by capability. Clustered by topic means buy blocks. Spread evenly across topics with algebra visible inside each one means buy terms. Most families never do this and buy an average of the two plans, which costs more than the right plan and achieves less.

The table below is the version to work from, and the final column is written as honestly as we can make it. Several rows say that a cheap fix is available, which is not a commercially useful thing for a tutoring page to say. It is, however, the correct thing, and a parent who closes three cheap topics before deciding whether to buy a term will usually find the term is shorter than it would have been.

sections.heading: What the grade scales mean and where boundaries bite
paragraphs: A grade is a boundary, not a continuum, and that changes how tuition money should be aimed. A student two marks below a boundary and a student eighteen marks below it look similar on a report and need entirely different plans. The first needs the cheap topics closed and the timing fixed, which is a matter of weeks. The second needs the capability work, which is a matter of terms.

The scales themselves are worth confirming. Pearson's International GCSE mathematics reports on a 9 to 1 scale. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on A* to G and others on 9 to 1 depending on the variant a school enters. When a sixth-form entry requirement is expressed as a grade 6, or as a B, check which scale your child's certificate will use before assuming the two map onto each other neatly. The school's exams officer can confirm it in a line.

Grade boundaries themselves move between series, because they are set after the papers are marked according to how the cohort performed. That is why no honest page publishes a mark total for a grade, and why anybody who tells you a fixed number is required is guessing. What is stable is the relative value of the cheap fixes: reverse percentages and similar shapes carry marks in every series regardless of where the boundary lands.

The practical method for a Dubai Festival City family is to ask the school, after mocks, roughly how far from the target grade the student sat. Schools can answer that from internal marks even without published boundaries. A gap of a few marks is a short, cheap, technique-led plan. A larger gap is a longer one, and knowing which you are in before committing six months of mid-band tuition is worth the conversation.

sections.heading: One-to-one or a small group for maths specifically
paragraphs: Mathematics divides more cleanly than most subjects on this question. Procedural topics taught to a group of two to four students work well, because everybody needs the same method demonstrated and then everybody practises it. Cumulative frequency, reverse percentages, circle theorems: these are group-friendly, and the cost per student falls accordingly without the teaching getting worse.

Capability work does not divide. A student whose algebraic fluency is weak needs their own errors caught as they happen, repeatedly, which cannot be done while three other students are working at a different pace. Buying the group version of this is the commonest false economy in IGCSE mathematics, because it looks like tuition, costs less, and produces no change in the marked papers.

A hybrid is usually the cheapest effective plan. Put the procedural topics into a group or into supervised self-study with the school's past papers, and spend the one-to-one money on the capability. Families around Mirdif and Al Badia who split the spend this way consistently report paying less across Years 10 and 11 than those who choose one model and apply it to everything.

Tuition centres sit outside this comparison and should be judged separately. A centre with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, up to six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That compliance position is checkable, which is a genuine advantage over an individual advertising on a community board.

sections.heading: When in Years 9, 10 and 11 the money works hardest
paragraphs: Earlier and smaller, almost always. Year 9 has no external stakes, which makes it the cheapest year in which to fix fluency, and the budget band at AED 45 to 65 an hour is perfectly adequate for repetitive marked practice. Nobody sells Year 9 tuition hard because there is no deadline to point at, and that is precisely why it is underbought relative to how well it works.

Year 10 autumn is when tier decisions start forming, so a diagnostic assessment belongs there. Year 10 spring is for the one structural subject, if there is one, taken slowly. Year 11 autumn is the mock window, which produces the best free diagnostic data in the whole sequence: a marked mock paper tells you more than any paid assessment, and reading it properly costs nothing.

Year 11 spring is for technique, and technique only. Marked timed papers, command words, working-out conventions, question selection and timing. This genuinely moves marks because exam technique responds faster than knowledge does. What it cannot do is build algebraic fluency from scratch, and a family buying the exam-year specialist band in March to do that is buying the most expensive version of the least likely outcome.

Set against the series, the shape is simple. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series in the UAE, and the February and March series is India-only, so no Dubai candidate sits it. Pearson International GCSE runs May and June and November, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. That January date is what makes November a viable resit route, and it is why a small reserve for entry fees belongs in the budget from the start.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Festival City, and what we will not sell
paragraphs: Send the board code, the tier, and the last two marked papers. The marked papers are the valuable item, because every lost mark can be classified before a dirham is committed and the classification is what determines whether you need blocks or terms. Add the hour your child is genuinely at a desk on a school night, allowing for the bus from Al Mizhar or the queue out of Festival City.

We match a tutor to that board and tier and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost. Afterwards you receive a written note setting out the clustered errors, the topics worth a block, whether the underlying issue is capability rather than content, and a recommended plan with a duration attached. If the plan is three topic blocks rather than two terms, take the three blocks.

The honest limits. Lessons are online: IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, which is a service we offer only in India, and there is no UAE office, centre or branch. We hold no regulator or board approval and claim none, so nobody here is KHDA approved or Cambridge accredited. We do not supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because reproducing them is not ours to do; we reference them and link to the official source.

One further limit about outcomes. Nobody can promise a grade, and this page deliberately contains no prediction. What the first month should produce is specific: your child knowing which tier and which papers they are sitting, a written list of the topics costing marks, and one measurable improvement in timing or working-out conventions. If a provider opens with a predicted grade instead of a diagnosis, that is information about the provider.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tuition cost per month around Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour give roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist. Packages seen in this market run about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All read in October 2026 and belonging to those providers. The figure that matters most, though, is how many months you need.

faqs.question: How many months of maths tuition will my Year 11 child actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which of three problems you have. A missed unit is two or three sessions. One hard topic is a four to six session block. Structural algebraic weakness, which means expanding, factorising and rearranging are not automatic, takes two terms because fluency is built by repetition. A report grade cannot tell you which of the three it is. Two marked papers with every lost mark classified can, and that costs nothing.

faqs.question: Does the Core or Foundation tier really cap my child's maths grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. Core on Cambridge 0580 and Foundation on Pearson 4MA1 do not reach the top grades, because the papers sat do not contain the marks required to cross those boundaries. The entry is decided by the school, usually during Year 10, and the realistic review window is Year 10 and the very start of Year 11. Spending at the specialist band in the spring of Year 11 on a lower-tier entry buys the highest rate in the market for a ceiling fixed months earlier.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the fastest improvement for the money?
faqs.answer: Reverse percentages first, because they are the commonest single error in the subject at every tier and can be taught properly in under an hour. Then similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, which take about two sessions. Then graph sketches, where students draw a plausible curve and omit the intercepts, turning points and asymptotes that carry the marks. Closing those three before committing to a longer plan often shortens the longer plan considerably.

faqs.question: Is my child on Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, and how do I find out?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the mathematics syllabus code and the tier in writing, for that subject specifically. Many Dubai schools enter some subjects with Cambridge and others with Pearson, so an answer about the school as a whole is not an answer about mathematics. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher with two two-hour papers. Quote the code when you request a tutor, because it determines whether the match is right.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in maths when they understood the work?
faqs.answer: Usually four habits rather than missing knowledge. Working compressed so tightly that method marks cannot be awarded. Answering less than the question asked, for instance finding two solutions to a trigonometric equation when the interval contains four. Sketching graphs without the features that carry the marks. And spending twelve minutes on a four-mark question and then running out of time. All four are technique, all four respond to marked timed practice, and none responds to further explanation.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to homes in Nad Al Hamar or Mirdif for maths?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Across the market, in-home one-to-one maths is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour because travel is inside the figure, and in these communities a visiting tutor arrives in the evening window by default, which is the weaker of the two daily slots for mathematics. Our lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time with working shared on screen.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class as good as one-to-one for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For procedural topics, yes, and it costs less per student. Cumulative frequency, circle theorems, reverse percentages: everybody needs the same method demonstrated and then everybody practises, so a group of two to four works well. For capability work it does not, because a student with weak algebraic fluency needs their own errors caught as they happen. The cheapest effective plan is usually a hybrid: group or self-study for procedure, one-to-one for fluency.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE maths exams held for a Dubai candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series in the UAE. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no Dubai student sits it, and any page quoting a February entry deadline to a UAE parent has imported another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so take the actual dates from your school's exams officer.

faqs.question: Can my child resit IGCSE maths in November, and when do results come?
faqs.answer: Yes, the November series is the standard resit route in the UAE for both boards. Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is early enough to matter for sixth-form conversations, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Entry fees are set by the examination centre rather than by a tutor, so ask the school and hold a reserve for them before committing the whole budget to lessons.

faqs.question: What grading scale will my child's maths certificate use?
faqs.answer: Pearson's International GCSE mathematics reports on a 9 to 1 scale. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on A* to G and others on 9 to 1 depending on the variant a school enters, so confirm which applies to your child's entry. This matters when a sixth-form requirement is expressed as a grade 6 or a grade B, because the two scales do not map onto each other neatly and families comparing them casually can misjudge the size of the gap.

faqs.question: Should we start maths tuition in Year 9 if there are no exams yet?
faqs.answer: It is the best value in the whole sequence and almost nobody does it. Year 9 has no external stakes, so fluency with indices, fractions, negative numbers and rearranging formulae can be built at the budget band of AED 45 to 65 an hour through repetitive marked practice. The same gap addressed in Year 11 costs the exam-year specialist band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month and succeeds less often. There is no deadline in Year 9, which is why nobody sells it.

faqs.question: Will fixing maths help my child's physics and chemistry grades?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, and it is the best argument for sequencing. The calculation marks in IGCSE physics and chemistry depend on rearranging formulae, handling indices and standard form, and manipulating units, all of which are mathematics rather than science. A student with weak algebraic fluency shows apparent weaknesses in several subjects that are really one weakness appearing in several places. Fixing it first can lift two other grades with nobody being paid to teach them.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE maths tutor working in Dubai Festival City need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Because the permit is free, ask directly and expect a straight answer.

faqs.question: What should the first month of maths tuition actually show?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is a grade. Your child should know which tier and which papers they are sitting. You should hold a written list of the topics costing marks, with an indication of whether the pattern is topic weakness or capability weakness. And one element of technique should visibly improve, most often the amount of working shown or the time spent per question. Grade movement takes longer, and a provider opening with a predicted grade has told you how it sells.

intro.heading: Three comparison questions, and the evidence each one needs
paragraphs: Families in Dubai Harbour contact us about IGCSE mathematics for three reasons and they are all comparisons. The first is the tier: the school has placed a child at Core or at Foundation and the family believes the higher tier is within reach. The second is arrival: a student has moved into a British-curriculum school mid-course from a different system and nobody can say how far behind they are, or in what. The third is the next step: what grade does A Level Mathematics, or Analysis and Approaches, or a particular sixth form actually require.

Each has a specific evidence requirement and none of them is answered by a report card. The tier question needs a full higher-tier paper sat under timed conditions, marked strictly, because that is the only document a school can act on and the only one that distinguishes a capable student from an optimistic parent. The arrival question needs a mixed diagnostic across the whole syllabus, because what a student is missing depends entirely on what their previous system emphasised and a transcript will not show it. The next-step question needs the receiving provider's own stated requirement, in writing.

The reason this matters is that the tier sets a ceiling before any revision begins. Cambridge Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Pearson applies the same logic through Foundation and Higher. A capable student placed at the lower tier on thin evidence has lost the top of the grade range, and the decision stops being live once final entries are filed.

Dubai Harbour shapes the practicalities. The district is new, built around a cruise terminal and marina berths, approached through a single corridor off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street shared with Emaar Beachfront and the Palm Jumeirah approach. It contains no school and no tuition centre. Children travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, leaving before 07:00 and returning after 15:30, which puts a mathematics session at 17:00 or later on a weekday. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows sets out how to build a tier case the school can act on, maps the gap for students arriving from the Middle Years Programme and from other national curricula, compares what each post-16 route expects of an IGCSE mathematics grade, explains when Additional Mathematics is a sensible addition, and says honestly where a group class is better value than we are. Confirm the board, code and tier with your exams officer before acting on any of it.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-harbour.subjectsIntro: These are the mathematics strands that decide a tier decision and a transition diagnosis, with the evidence each one produces. The strands are narrow because a tier case has to be specific.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying, including algebraic fractions at the higher tier. The single best predictor of whether a student can hold the Extended tier, and the strand a school looks at first when a tier case is made to it.

subjects.name: Simultaneous and quadratic equations
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic solving, with completing the square and the formula at the higher tier. Sign errors during rearrangement dominate the losses, and the thirty-second habit of substituting a solution back recovers whole questions.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, reciprocals, exponentials and transformations. A sketch drawn without intercepts or asymptotes marked makes the subsequent question unanswerable from the student's own diagram, which is a drawing habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and Pythagoras
subjects.description: Right-angled work and, at the higher tier, the sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Almost every lost mark traces to a diagram drawn from a misread rather than to the trigonometry itself.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measure
subjects.description: Area, surface area, volume, density, speed and pressure. Unit conversion is the entire difficulty, particularly between cubic centimetres and litres, and it is the strand where students arriving from other curricula most often have a genuine gap.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Standard form, reverse percentages, compound interest and ratio division. Reverse percentages are the most reliably failed topic at this level, because students apply the percentage forwards without noticing the question asked otherwise.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms. Histograms with unequal class widths cause disproportionate loss because frequency density is routinely treated as frequency.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and describing a transformation completely. The marks are in completeness: naming the type without the centre, scale factor or vector collects part of the available credit at best, which is a checklist problem.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, further trigonometry, series and logarithms, taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Analysis and Approaches. It assumes complete 0580 algebraic fluency from the first lesson and punishes a student who lacks it.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel 4MA1
subjects.description: The Edexcel alternative, tiered on the same principle with its own question phrasing and formula provision. Students arriving from a school that used the other board need their practice material changed with them, which is frequently overlooked.

sections.heading: Building a tier case the school can act on
paragraphs: Schools place students at a tier on the evidence they have, which is usually classwork, internal assessments and a teacher's judgement about reliability under pressure. A parent who believes the higher tier is within reach is arguing against that evidence with an opinion, and the conversation goes nowhere because nothing new has been put on the table. The way to change the outcome is to produce a document the school can use.

That document is a full higher-tier paper, sat under genuine timed conditions without help, marked strictly against the official mark scheme with method marks applied properly rather than generously. A score comfortably above the previous series' lower boundary on the higher tier is an argument. A score just below it is also useful, because it shows exactly which strands are short and gives the school a reason to review in six weeks rather than to say no. What does not work is a practice paper completed over two evenings with a calculator and a textbook open.

Timing matters as much as the evidence. In Year 10 the decision is live and a school can reasonably reconsider. Once final entries are filed, the tier is fixed for that series and the conversation is over, which is why a family who suspects a misplacement should be producing the paper early in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11. Four to six sessions is usually enough to produce the document, which makes it one of the cheapest interventions available in the whole qualification.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-course from another curriculum
paragraphs: Dubai Harbour filled recently and with families from many different school systems, so mid-course arrivals are more common here than in long-established communities. A student joining a British-curriculum school in Year 10 or Year 11 from the Middle Years Programme, from an American high school, from a national curriculum or from a different British school may be ahead, behind, or both at once depending on the strand. A transcript will not tell you which, and nor will the first half-term's classwork.

The gaps are predictable by origin rather than random. A student from the Middle Years Programme usually has investigation and modelling habits and lacks procedural speed under timing. A student from an American programme is often comfortable with graphing technology and applied contexts and short on manipulation done by hand. A student from a national curriculum with heavy procedural drilling may be ahead on algebra and behind on the data handling, probability and problem-solving strands that IGCSE emphasises.

The efficient response is one diagnostic session across every strand, producing a map rather than a verdict, followed by a catch-up block ordered to intersect with what the school is teaching next. Starting from the beginning wastes the student's strongest strands and starting from the school's current topic leaves the gap in place. The map is what makes the difference, and it takes one session to produce rather than a term to infer.

One further point that applies to every origin. A student who has moved countries mid-course is managing a new school, a new social group and often a new language of instruction at the same time, and a diagnostic that reads a weak first half-term as a mathematics gap will mislead everybody. Sit the diagnostic after a few weeks of settling rather than in the first fortnight, and treat anything produced in week one as provisional.

sections.heading: What the next step actually expects of this grade
paragraphs: The third comparison question is the one families leave latest and it is the easiest to answer, because the answer is published. Post-16 providers state their own entry requirements: a sixth form will say what IGCSE mathematics grade it requires for A Level Mathematics, and an IB school will say what it expects for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Those statements are specific, they differ between providers, and they are revised. Reading them is an afternoon's work and it reframes the whole tutoring question.

It reframes it because the target changes what is worth doing. A student needing a grade for a course that requires a strong Extended pass should be working on the strands that course depends on, which for Analysis and Approaches means algebraic manipulation above all. A student whose target route does not require mathematics beyond a pass should be securing the pass efficiently and spending the recovered hours on the subjects that do matter to their application. Both are rational and they look completely different in a weekly plan.

The practical step is a written list: each post-16 destination the family is considering, with its current stated mathematics requirement and the source it was read from. Compile it in Year 10 while subject and tier decisions are still open. Ask the schools directly rather than relying on general impressions, and treat anything more than a year old as out of date. This is the single most useful piece of homework a parent can do, and no tutor can do it for you because the requirements belong to the receiving institution.

sections.heading: MYP mathematics against IGCSE mathematics
paragraphs: This comparison matters in this district because several schools serving it switch between the two at the end of Year 9, and because families compare across towers. The two assess genuinely different things. Middle Years Programme mathematics is marked against four criteria out of eight each, covering knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, with grades converted by the school's own boundary table. IGCSE mathematics is a tiered external written examination with published syllabus codes.

What each builds follows from that. MYP builds generalisation, justification and the ability to write about mathematics, which is excellent preparation for the IB exploration and for university work and poor preparation for a timed written paper. IGCSE builds procedural speed, mark-scheme literacy and examination stamina, which is excellent preparation for a timed written paper and leaves the writing and investigation skills to be acquired later.

A student switching at the end of Year 9 therefore meets a real transition, and the first term of Year 10 is where it shows. Criterion marking rewarded a justified approach developed over time; the new papers reward a correct answer produced quickly with method visible. Six to eight sessions on timed procedural work and mark-scheme reading in that term prevents the disappointing first set of Year 10 assessments that otherwise convinces a student they have become worse at mathematics.

Worth adding that the switch is a school decision rather than a family one in almost every case here, so the useful question is not which route is better but what the student will need in the first term of the new one. That is answerable, cheap and almost never planned for, because the switch is presented administratively rather than academically.

sections.heading: When Additional Mathematics is worth adding
paragraphs: Additional Mathematics 0606 is proposed to stronger sets in Year 10 and accepted by families on the reasonable assumption that more mathematics is better. It is a separate Cambridge qualification sat alongside 0580, covering calculus, further trigonometry, series and logarithms, and it assumes complete fluency in everything 0580 Extended contains from its first lesson. For a student who has that fluency it makes the first term of A Level Mathematics or Analysis and Approaches considerably less punishing.

For a student who does not, it is the commonest overreach in this cluster. Learning new content on an unstable foundation, under the same examination pressure, in the same series, produces two mediocre grades where one strong grade was available. The test is unsentimental: can the student complete 0580 Extended algebraic manipulation quickly and accurately, without a calculator, today? Not with effort, not eventually. If the answer is no, the answer to 0606 is not yet.

The decision should also be checked against the destination. Some sixth forms note 0606 favourably for Further Mathematics entry; many do not require it at all, and a student who takes it unnecessarily has spent two years of lesson time that could have gone to a subject their application needed. Ask the post-16 providers directly in Year 10, before timetables are built, and make the decision against what they say rather than against the general impression that an extra qualification cannot hurt.

There is a scheduling consequence too. Where 0606 is taken, it should not share a session with 0580: the content overlaps enough that a tired student blurs the two, and the papers reward different things. Two shorter slots in the week work better than one long one, which from this district usually means a weekday evening and a weekend morning.

sections.heading: Where a group class is better value than we are
paragraphs: This is worth saying plainly because almost nobody selling tutoring says it. In Year 9 and much of Year 10, where the need is content exposure and consolidation rather than diagnosis, a small group at a centre is good value and the shared pace is not a disadvantage. The student hears the material, works problems alongside others, and the cost per hour is lower. If that is the need, buying one-to-one is buying precision that nothing is using.

The calculation inverts in two situations. The first is a tier case, which requires a student to sit a full paper under genuine conditions and have the marking audited line by line. No group format produces that document. The second is Year 11, where the marks a particular student is losing are individual: unshown method, a misread rounding instruction, a unit conversion, a question abandoned after a wrong part. A class pitched at a group cannot see which of those applies.

There is also a logistics cost specific to this district. A centre class means a second journey after a school run that already takes ninety minutes of the day, along a single approach corridor, at the hour the whole cluster is moving. For a family in Dubai Harbour that is the real price of the lower hourly rate, and it is worth calculating before committing to a term of it. Our sessions run over live video and we provide no home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison is between those two arrangements.
