sections.heading: The four habits that decide the grade inside any tier
paragraphs: Once the tier is settled, the grade inside it is decided largely by four habits, and they are the same at Core and Extended. Method not shown, which forfeits method marks and, on a structured question, the follow-through credit that would have carried a student past one arithmetic slip. Rounding and accuracy instructions printed in the question and then ignored, which is a mark declined rather than a mark lost. Unit conversion in compound measure and volume work. And a question abandoned after an early part went wrong.

All four are mechanical and all four are invisible to a student who has never been shown them. They persist into Year 11 because they look like presentation rather than mathematics, so neither classroom teaching nor extra practice addresses them. A student losing twenty-six marks to these four and four marks to genuinely unknown content should spend a fortnight on the habits, which is the opposite of what usually gets bought.

Identifying the mix takes one marked script and ten minutes, which is why we ask for the script rather than the grade before quoting anything. It also changes the honest answer about what tutoring can achieve: a habit-led deficit in Year 11 is recoverable in weeks, and a content-led one with three missing strands is not recoverable in the same term. Both produce identical report cards and need completely different conversations.

The fifth item, which is not a habit but belongs here, is the unattempted question. Count the marks left blank on the last page of a mock script before concluding anything about content: a paper with eight blank marks at the end was not a test of what the student knew, and the repair is a timing rule rather than any teaching at all.

sections.heading: Booking from a Dubai Harbour address
paragraphs: Tell us which of the three questions you are asking: tier, transition, or next step. Send the board, syllabus code and current tier from the entry confirmation or the school's own statement, the most recent marked assessment, and the hours that genuinely exist after a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30. If the question is the tier, say so at the outset, because the first block is then a bounded piece of work with a document as its output rather than an open weekly arrangement.

We match a tutor to that syllabus at that tier and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing either a gap map, a tier assessment or a habit breakdown depending on the question you arrived with. You keep the document whether or not you continue, and it is useful to any tutor you engage instead, including one the school recommends.

The limits. Extended-tier specialists at popular spring evening hours are sometimes unavailable for a given week and we will say so rather than substituting someone who teaches the other board. We cannot promise a grade. We will tell you when a group class would serve your purpose better than we would. And we will not argue a tier case the evidence does not support, because a student placed above their reliable level loses more than a student placed one tier below their ceiling.

whyPoints.description: Post-16 providers publish their own mathematics entry requirements and revise them. We help interpret what one means in practice and tell you to read the current statement from the receiving school itself.

whyPoints.title: Honest about group classes
whyPoints.description: For Year 9 and early Year 10 content coverage a small group is better value than one-to-one. We say so, because a family who buys precision nothing is using concludes the spending was wasted and does not return when it is needed.

whyPoints.title: The four habits named and costed
whyPoints.description: Unshown method, ignored rounding instructions, unit conversion and abandoned structured questions decide the grade inside any tier. They repair in a fortnight, and we will tell you when that is the whole job rather than selling a term.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code and the tier
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 at Core or Extended, 0606, or Edexcel 4MA1 at Foundation or Higher. We match on what the entry confirmation says, because a tutor working from the wrong board's question style trains the wrong reading habits.

faqs.question: How do I persuade our school to move our child to the higher tier?
faqs.answer: With a document rather than an opinion. Have the student sit a full higher-tier paper under genuine timed conditions, with no help, and mark it strictly against the official scheme with method marks applied properly rather than generously. A score comfortably above the previous series' lower boundary on that tier is an argument a school can act on; a score just below it still names the short strands and gives a reason to review in six weeks. Produce it early in Year 10, because the decision closes at final entries.

faqs.question: What is the ceiling on the Cambridge Core tier?
faqs.answer: A grade C. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above that however well they perform, while Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Pearson applies the same principle through Foundation and Higher tiers. This is why the tier decision outweighs any individual topic: it sets the ceiling before revision begins. If your child is already entered at the lower tier for this series, the productive target is the top of that tier.

faqs.question: Our child joined in Year 10 from a different system. How far behind are they?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the strand, and a transcript will not tell you. Students from the Middle Years Programme usually arrive with investigation habits and without procedural speed. Students from an American programme are often comfortable with graphing technology and short on manipulation by hand. Students from a heavily procedural national curriculum may be ahead on algebra and behind on data handling and problem solving. One diagnostic session across every strand produces a map, which is what efficient catch-up needs.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths grade does A Level Mathematics need?
faqs.answer: Whatever the sixth form you are applying to says it needs, which they publish and revise. Requirements differ between providers and between A Level Mathematics and Further Mathematics, and an IB school will state its own expectation for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level separately. Compile a written list in Year 10 of each destination with its current stated requirement and where you read it. Ask the schools directly, and treat anything more than a year old as out of date.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking?
faqs.answer: Only where 0580 Extended algebraic manipulation is already quick and accurate without a calculator, today, rather than achievable with effort. 0606 front-loads calculus, further trigonometry, series and logarithms and assumes that fluency from its first lesson, so a student still consolidating algebra collects two mediocre grades instead of one strong one. Check too whether your target sixth forms actually require it; many note it favourably and few demand it, and the lesson time has an alternative use.

faqs.question: What changed when our school switched from MYP to IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: What is being measured. Criterion marking rewarded a justified approach generalised and explained over an extended task; the new papers reward a correct answer produced quickly with method visible under strict timing. A student who keeps producing thorough, reflective work meets a paper that does not reward it and concludes they have got worse at mathematics. Six to eight sessions on timed procedural work and mark-scheme reading in the first term of Year 10 prevents that.

faqs.question: Would a group class at a centre be enough for our Year 10?
faqs.answer: For content coverage and consolidation, often yes, and we will say so. The need at that stage is exposure rather than diagnosis, the shared pace is not a disadvantage and the cost per hour is lower. The real price from this district is a second journey after a school run that already takes ninety minutes, along a single approach corridor at the hour the cluster is moving. Calculate that before committing to a term, because it is the part families underestimate.

faqs.question: Why does our child lose marks when their answers are right?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded for visible working, and follow-through credit on a structured question depends on the examiner seeing the route. A student who does the algebra mentally and writes one line is penalised for competence: one slip in part (a) then costs four later parts rather than one mark. Installing the habit takes two or three sessions of enforcement and is the cheapest grade movement in the qualification, which is why we look for it in the script first.

faqs.question: Which topic should a borderline Extended student work on first?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation, without exception. It is the strand everything else rests on, it is the first thing a school looks at when a tier case is made, and a student who manipulates slowly rather than inaccurately still loses marks because they run out of time on later questions. After that, reverse percentages and histograms with unequal class widths, both of which are reliably failed, rarely revisited and fixable in a session each, which makes them unusually good value.

faqs.question: Can a tier change still happen in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Only before final entries are filed, and only with the school's agreement. After the entry deadline the tier is fixed for that series and the conversation is finished. If you suspect a misplacement, the evidence paper belongs in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11. Where the entry is already filed, the productive plan is to secure the top of the entered tier, which on a transcript is worth more than a bare pass on the higher one.

faqs.question: How long does catch-up take for a mid-course arrival?
faqs.answer: It depends on the gap map rather than on how long they have been away. A student missing the statistics and problem-solving strands needs a focused block of six to eight sessions on those strands and nothing else. A student missing algebraic manipulation needs longer, because everything rests on it. A student who is simply on the other board needs their practice material changed immediately and very little else. The map takes one session; the estimate follows from it.

faqs.question: Should we revise from the school's board or whichever papers we can find?
faqs.answer: The school's board, confirmed in writing by the exams officer. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 ask comparable mathematics in different house styles with different formula provision, so practising the wrong archive trains a student to decode the wrong question format. The time lost decoding in the examination comes out of thinking time before it comes out of marks. Cambridge resources are more abundant online, which is exactly why this error is common in this cluster.

faqs.question: What does the first session produce if we are asking about the tier?
faqs.answer: A timed paper and the beginning of a document. The student sits a full higher-tier paper under genuine conditions, the tutor marks it strictly against the official scheme and audits the student's own marking, and the output is a written analysis naming which strands are short and by how much. Four to six sessions complete the block. The point of the work is the document the school can act on, not the teaching, and we are explicit about that.

faqs.question: What hour works for maths sessions from this district?
faqs.answer: 17:00 at the earliest on a weekday, 17:30 if the school run from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh is unreliable, with longer diagnostic or paper-sitting work on a weekend morning. A full timed paper needs a continuous block that does not exist on a weekday evening here. Mathematics also degrades faster with fatigue than any other subject, and a tired student's arithmetic slips are routinely diagnosed as conceptual gaps by whoever was not watching the working.

intro.heading: Why the neighbourhood matters less than the syllabus code
paragraphs: Search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Hills Estate and the results try to sell you proximity. Proximity is the least useful variable in this decision. Two households a four-minute drive apart, one in Dubai Hills Estate and one in Arabian Ranches, routinely have children sitting different mathematics qualifications: one on Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended, the other on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A 4MA1 Higher, and a third child nearby on Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 because their school routes students towards the IB Diploma. Those are three different papers, three different grading scales and three different sets of examiner habits.

That is the comparison this page is built on, and it runs through every section: what differs between these communities, what differs between the syllabuses their schools use, and why the practical answer ends up the same in each case. The answer is a specialist matched to the code on the front of the paper, delivered online so that the pool of specialists is not limited to whoever lives within a short drive of your villa and has Tuesday evening free.

The second thing that differs by community is time, not content. Dubai Hills Estate sits between Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Street, so its buses run to Al Quoz, Al Barsha South and Meydan. Arabian Ranches has its own primary school on site but sends secondary students further. Arabian Ranches 3, Town Square and Mudon have the longest runs of this group, and a Year 11 student getting home at 16:20 has a different evening from one home at 15:40. A tutor who has to drive loses part of the window to the road. A tutor on video does not, and the slot holds at the same time every week regardless of which of these communities you live in.

The third difference is what families worry about. In Dubai Hills Estate the common question is tier: a Year 10 student placed on Core who wants a grade above a C, or a Year 11 student on Higher losing marks they clearly understand. In the Ranches, with a longer-established cohort, the question is more often the step from IGCSE into the Diploma or A Level. In Motor City and Sports City, where the apartment population turns over faster, the question is mid-year transfer: a student arriving from a CBSE or American school into Year 10 of a British curriculum, three months behind on a syllabus nobody has mapped for them.

All four of those problems have the same shape. Identify the exact qualification, identify the tier, identify which papers carry which marks, then work the published past papers against the published mark scheme until the gap between what the student knows and what the student scores closes. What follows sets out the syllabus differences, the real entry and results dates from Cambridge and Pearson, the Dubai market rates in dirhams with sources, and the five-subject rule that the UAE Ministry of Education actually applies when a certificate is submitted for equivalency.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: The two years before an IGCSE course starts are where tier placement is effectively decided, because schools set groups on Year 9 performance. Work at this stage is fluency: fractions, negatives, index laws, rearranging formulae and straight-line graphs. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which some schools use as an external marker before setting groups.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches families often meet this stage without realising it is a decision point. A Year 9 student who is comfortable but slow usually gets placed on the lower tier, which caps the grade available two years later. A term of fluency work in Year 9 is cheaper and less stressful than a tier appeal in Year 11, and it is the most under-used intervention in this market.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: A two-year course sat at the end of Year 11, tiered in every version. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher; Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics splits into Core and Extended and adds an investigation component that suits IB-bound students. The tier caps the grade, so it is the single most consequential administrative fact about your child's mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Schools used by Dubai Hills Estate families run different combinations of these. Repton Al Barsha, Kings' School Al Barsha, GEMS Metropole Motor City and Dubai Heights Academy are all British-curriculum routes, and the board and specification are a school-level choice that can change between cohorts. Ask the department which code is on this year's entry rather than assuming last year's applies.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma, the two exits
programmes.description: An IGCSE mathematics grade is a gatekeeper twice over: schools set minimum grades for A Level Mathematics and for IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, commonly a 7 or an A, and the content gap is real in both directions. A* and 9 students still meet calculus, proof and vectors as new material in the first term after IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Around Dubai Hills Estate both exits are available within a short bus ride, which is unusual. GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai run IB Diploma routes; Repton Al Barsha and Kings' School Al Barsha run A Level routes. A Year 11 student choosing between them should look at the mathematics requirement for each before the option form, not after.

programmes.name: Mid-year transfer into a British-curriculum Year 10 or 11
programmes.description: Students joining from CBSE, American, French or MoE curricula meet the same mathematics in a different order and with different assessment conventions. The gap is rarely ability; it is coverage and command terms. A mapping exercise against the syllabus content list identifies exactly which sections have not been taught, which is faster than general revision.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-hills-e.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics divides into content strands and into paper skills, and a first lesson usually finds the problem in one rather than both. These are the areas students around Dubai Hills Estate most often need.

subjects.name: Number and index laws
subjects.description: Standard form, surds at the higher tier, upper and lower bounds, percentage change in reverse, and compound interest. Bounds questions are the clearest tier marker: lower-tier students usually have never met them, and they appear reliably on higher-tier papers.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations including one linear and one quadratic. This strand is the strongest predictor of whether a student will cope with A Level or IB Mathematics, and it is where higher-tier marks are most often thrown away.

subjects.name: Quadratics and the function toolkit
subjects.description: Solving by factorising, formula and completing the square, plus turning points, roots and sketching. Students who only know the formula lose the questions that ask for a minimum value or a vertex, because those need the completed-square form.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle rules, similarity, congruence and the circle theorems at the higher tier. Marks here depend on naming the reason, not just the number: an unjustified angle in a 'give reasons' question scores part of the available credit at best.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras at both tiers, then the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional problems at the higher tier. Three-dimensional trigonometry is the single most avoided topic in Year 11 revision in our experience.

subjects.name: Graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Straight lines, gradients, parallel and perpendicular lines, quadratic and reciprocal curves, and gradient of a chord or tangent at the higher tier. Sketches lose marks for missing intercepts and asymptotes in exactly the same way they do at IB level.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths, and tree and Venn diagram probability. Histograms with unequal widths are the most reliable source of lost marks at the higher tier, because frequency density is rarely taught twice.

subjects.name: Ratio, proportion and rates
subjects.description: Direct and inverse proportion, best-value comparison, compound measures and exponential growth and decay. These are the questions dressed as real-life contexts, where students lose marks by answering the arithmetic and ignoring the units asked for.

subjects.name: The investigation component
subjects.description: 0607 includes an investigation paper, which is unusual at this level and valuable for students heading to the IB, because it rehearses the kind of extended reasoning the Diploma exploration demands. Schools that run 0607 are usually IB continuum schools and choose it deliberately.

subjects.name: Paper technique and command terms
subjects.description: Show that, work out, explain, give a reason, hence. Each instruction has a mark-scheme consequence, and a student who writes the answer to a 'show that' question without the intermediate lines loses the method marks. This is taught separately from content and usually changes a grade boundary faster.

sections.heading: Dubai Hills Estate against Arabian Ranches, Motor City and Town Square
paragraphs: Start with the comparison, because it decides the schedule. Four communities within fifteen minutes of each other produce four different evenings for a Year 11 mathematics student, and the differences are entirely about distance to school and household shape rather than about anything academic.

Dubai Hills Estate families mostly bus into the Al Quoz and Al Barsha South school belt, with returns clustered around 15:40 to 15:55. Arabian Ranches has a primary school inside the community, so younger siblings are home early while secondary students travel further; the net effect is often more than one pick-up in the same afternoon. Motor City and Sports City are apartment-heavy, with some students walking to school and others on long runs, so two children in the same building can need slots two hours apart. Town Square, Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3 sit furthest out with the longest bus journeys of the group.

The academic picture varies too, in a way that follows the housing rather than the geography. Established villa communities have settled cohorts, so the questions are sequential: tier placement in Year 10, then the A Level or Diploma choice in Year 11. Faster-turning rental areas generate mid-year transfers, where the issue is coverage rather than ability, and a student may be three chapters behind through no fault of their own.

What does not vary is the remedy. In each case the work is to establish the exact syllabus code, the tier, the papers and their weightings, then close the measurable gap with past papers marked against the published scheme. Because that work is identical across all four communities, the only thing that should change by address is the time the lesson starts. Online delivery is what lets the specialist stay the same while the clock moves.

sections.heading: Which mathematics qualification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question that should be asked before any tutor is hired, and it is answered on the front of a past paper or on the school's entry information rather than by guesswork. Across the schools Dubai Hills Estate families use, at least three distinct mathematics qualifications are in circulation, and they are not interchangeable.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the most widely sat. It is tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped below the top grades and Extended reaching A*. Cambridge revised the specification, and the paper structure differs between the older and the current version, including how calculator and non-calculator assessment is split. Check which syllabus year your child is entered for on the Cambridge syllabus page for their examination series, because past papers from the wrong version drill the wrong paper shape.

Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is the quieter one and worth knowing about. It is also tiered, and it adds an investigation component, which is why IB continuum schools often prefer it: the extended reasoning rehearses what the Diploma exploration later demands. A student on 0607 who is given 0580 past papers by a tutor who did not check will practise a paper they are not sitting.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, is tiered into Foundation and Higher, with two papers of two hours at each tier and a 9 to 1 grade scale. Specification B, 4MB1, is a different structure again. A grade 9 and an A* are not the same statement about a student, and a tutor should be able to explain which they are aiming at without looking it up.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the last moment it can be changed
paragraphs: Tier is the most consequential administrative fact in IGCSE mathematics and the least discussed. Core and Foundation entries cap the grade available. A student entered on Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, which means a Year 10 placement made on a single set of Year 9 results can quietly decide what a sixth-form application looks like two years later.

Schools place students for defensible reasons. A student who would be swamped by the higher tier scores better on the lower one, and a safe grade on Core is worth more than a scattered one on Extended. The problem is that placement is often treated as settled when it is still movable, and parents in Dubai Hills Estate frequently discover the cap in Year 11 when the sixth-form entry requirement is published.

The practical test is whether the student can handle the content that only appears at the higher tier. For Cambridge Extended and Pearson Higher that means bounds, surds at the appropriate level, the sine and cosine rules, circle theorems with reasons, histograms with unequal class widths, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations with a quadratic. A student who can be taught those six to eight areas to a reliable standard across two terms is a candidate for a tier conversation. A student who is still insecure with negatives and index laws is not, and saying so early is kinder than agreeing with the ambition and failing in June.

Timing matters because entries are made months before the examination. A UAE candidate sits either the June series or the November series, and the entry for a June sitting closes in the spring term, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, on a date your centre prints on the statement of entry. Pearson's November 2026 timetable makes the same gap concrete at the other end of the year: the papers run from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry for them closed early in the autumn term. The gap between entry and exam is the point: by the time revision feels urgent, the tier has already been submitted. Ask the department in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, with evidence from marked higher-tier papers rather than a general sense that your child could do better.

sections.heading: The IGCSE exam calendar with real dates, and why zones matter in Dubai
paragraphs: No competitor page we examined for these queries names an examination series, an entry deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because these dates are published, they are the dates that constrain everything, and they are the reason a January decision is worth more than an April one.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Those Checkpoint months are not IGCSE sittings, and the February sitting quoted on a surprising number of tutoring sites is one Cambridge offers in India only, so a Dubai family planning against it is planning against an exam their child cannot enter. The distance between entry and examination is still the useful fact: a June entry closes in the spring, roughly four months out, and the November series then sits as the resit route with its own entry closing early in the autumn. Read your own series on cambridgeinternational.org rather than borrowing another series' dates.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

The zone point is specific to being in Dubai and almost nobody mentions it. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A family in Dubai Hills Estate downloading a timetable found through a search engine may well be reading a different zone's version. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that document.

sections.heading: Where a grade 6 becomes a grade 7, and where it does not
paragraphs: Most families hiring an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Hills Estate are asking for one or two grades, not a transformation, and the work that delivers that is narrower than general revision. Across the students we see, the same handful of areas separate a 6 from a 7 or an A, and the pattern is consistent enough to plan against.

The first is algebraic fractions and the harder simultaneous equations, where one linear and one quadratic equation are solved together. These appear reliably on higher-tier papers, carry several marks each, and are routinely skipped in revision because they look unpleasant. The second is histograms with unequal class widths, which require frequency density and are taught once, early, and then never revisited. The third is circle theorems where the question asks for reasons: the angle is often right and the justification missing, which costs the communication marks.

The fourth is three-dimensional trigonometry, which students avoid because it needs a diagram drawn before any calculation starts. The fifth is not content at all. It is method recording: writing down enough intermediate working that the method marks survive an arithmetic slip at the end. Students at this level frequently lose two or three marks a paper to answers presented without the lines that earned them.

The useful consequence is that a seven or eight week block aimed at those five areas is a realistic and measurable plan, which a general promise to improve at maths is not. We mark two recent papers in the first lesson, count the losses by category, and name the three areas worth the time. Anything that is not costing marks comes off the list, including topics the student finds uncomfortable but is not actually being examined on heavily.

IB Gram delivers that online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated on every UAE page on this site, and it is stated here rather than buried because the alternative is letting a family discover it after a phone call.

The case for it is the comparison itself. Hiring within driving distance of Dubai Hills Estate means choosing among mathematics teachers who live nearby and have that evening free. Online, the same family chooses a Cambridge 0607 specialist, or a Pearson 4MA1 Higher specialist, or someone who has taught the revised 0580 paper structure from the year it changed. For a narrow requirement, specialism beats proximity, and the narrower the requirement the bigger the gap. The honest trade-offs are real too: a video lesson needs a quiet corner and a charged laptop, younger students need a parent within earshot for the first few sessions, and a tutor on screen cannot take a phone away.

On the legal position, which the competitor set covers in a single heading at best: an individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two working day completion time through the MoHRE app, website or e-services. sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: what the UAE actually requires at equivalency
paragraphs: Families on a British curriculum around Dubai Hills Estate eventually meet Ministry of Education equivalency, usually when a UAE university application is being prepared, and the published rule is narrower than the rumour. For the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details are routinely reported wrongly. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which changes the arithmetic of a Year 11 option choice. And the number is five: one page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six subjects, which is not what the published clarification says. Getting the count right is a small thing that changes real decisions, because a family planning a sixth subject purely for equivalency may not need it.

For completeness, the American track is assessed differently: English proficiency via a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics via at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB there is no points threshold we have been able to read on an official source, so this page publishes none. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority directly, and treat any specific IB figure found elsewhere as unverified until you have seen it on the Ministry's own page.

Alongside all of this, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects occupy real timetable space in a Year 11 week, and a revision plan that ignores them is a plan the student cannot keep. Equivalency itself is a process completed with the Ministry; no tutoring service performs it, influences it or is required for it.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's school in Dubai Hills Estate use for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: The school decides, and it can differ between year groups and between subjects in the same school. The fastest way to find out is the front page of a recent past paper or assessment, which carries the board name and the syllabus code, or the entry information the examinations officer issues. Around Dubai Hills Estate all three of Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are in circulation. Ask before booking any tutoring, because practising the wrong board's papers drills a paper structure your child will not sit.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 harder than Pearson Edexcel 4MA1?
faqs.answer: They are differently shaped rather than ranked. The content overlaps heavily, but the paper structures, timings and grade scales differ: Cambridge reports A* to G with the available range capped by tier, while Pearson reports 9 to 1 with the same kind of cap. Cambridge has also revised 0580, so the paper split differs between syllabus versions. What matters for a student is familiarity with the examiner's conventions on their own specification. A tutor who has taught the specific code will see the recurring question styles that a general maths tutor will not.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and 0607 International Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Both are tiered Cambridge IGCSE mathematics qualifications, but 0607 includes an investigation component and is often chosen by IB continuum schools because the extended reasoning rehearses what the Diploma exploration later requires. The content emphasis differs as well, with 0607 leaning more on graphical and technology-supported work. A student on 0607 needs 0607 past papers; being given 0580 material is one of the more common tutoring mismatches around schools in the Al Barsha corridor, and it is avoidable by checking the code once.

faqs.question: My son is on the Core tier and wants a top grade. Can the tier be changed?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the window closes earlier than families expect because entries are submitted months before the examination. A UAE candidate sits June or November, and a June entry closes in the spring term, roughly four months before the first paper, on a date the centre states rather than one we would publish here; Pearson's November 2026 papers, by comparison, ran from late October to 19 November 2026 on an entry that closed early in the autumn. Raise it in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, with marked higher-tier papers as evidence. The content test is whether bounds, circle theorems with reasons, histograms with unequal class widths and algebraic fractions can be taught to a reliable standard in the time left.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE maths exams actually sat by students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Results dates differ by board and series: Pearson sent June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable for your series, since provisional versions are revised.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE maths tutoring cost more in Dubai Hills Estate than in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Online, no, because there is no travel in the price. In-home tutoring does vary by community, and that is the whole in-home premium: a tutor reaching Dubai Hills Estate from Al Barsha at 16:15 loses twenty to thirty minutes each way, while reaching Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square at the same hour can cost closer to fifty. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors, against AED 200 to 450 and above for online specialists. The teaching is identical; the driving is not.

faqs.question: Do you travel to homes in Arabian Ranches or Motor City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own working on camera and written notes afterwards. The gain is the pool you choose from: instead of the mathematics teachers who live near Motor City and have Tuesday free, you choose someone who teaches your child's exact specification and tier, and the lesson starts the moment the student sits down.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is more efficient and Year 11 is more common. Starting in Year 10 means fluency and algebra can be fixed while they are still cheap to fix, and it means a tier conversation can happen with two terms of evidence behind it rather than a rushed appeal. Starting in Year 11 works, but the available work narrows to the areas that measurably cost marks, and the exploration of alternatives is gone. The least useful timing is the term of the examination, when only paper technique and method recording can still move.

faqs.question: For a Dubai Hills family, how many IGCSE passes does the UAE equivalency route actually require?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE searches states six subjects, which the published clarification does not support. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority, because equivalency is their process rather than a school's or a tutor's.

faqs.question: Can my daughter sit different subjects with different exam boards?
faqs.answer: Many schools do exactly that, choosing Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson Edexcel for others, and a student can also sit a subject as a private candidate at an approved centre. The practical consequences are administrative: two sets of timetables, two results release dates, and two sets of entry deadlines to keep track of. For tutoring it means confirming the board subject by subject rather than assuming the school uses one throughout. Ask the examinations officer for the entry list, which shows the board and code against each subject.

faqs.question: What does modular mean with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Modular structures let components be sat in different series rather than all at the end, which some Pearson qualifications allow and others do not. Whether it applies to your child depends on the specification the school has entered them for, so check the specification document on qualifications.pearson.com rather than relying on a general answer. Where a modular route is available it changes revision planning substantially, because an earlier component needs to be examination-ready while the rest of the course is still being taught. The examinations officer can confirm which structure is in use.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge timetable zone matter for a school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable you read may not be the one your centre is using. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A parent in Dubai Hills Estate who downloads a timetable from a search result can easily be reading another zone's document. Ask your examinations officer which zone the centre is in and plan from that version only.

faqs.question: Will a grade 7 in IGCSE maths be enough for IB Maths Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: It usually meets the school's entry requirement, and it is not the same as being ready. IGCSE mathematics stops short of the calculus, proof and vector work that Analysis and Approaches opens with, so even strong IGCSE students meet genuinely new material in the first term of DP1. The students who cope are the ones whose algebraic manipulation is automatic rather than merely correct. A bridging block in the summer between Year 11 and DP1, aimed at differentiation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities, is the most useful few hours available at that point.

intro.heading: Three maths qualifications, two tiers, and one entry form that settles it
paragraphs: Maths is the subject Dubai Internet City families ask about first, and it is the subject where the wrong assumption costs the most. The assumption is that IGCSE maths is one thing. It is not. Schools in this cluster enter candidates for at least three different qualifications, and the differences are not cosmetic — they change the papers sat, the topics examined, whether a calculator is permitted and how the marks are awarded.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the most common. Two written papers, tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capping at grade C or 5 and Extended running the full range. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is the one most parents have never heard of and some schools in this belt use, often as the pre-IB route; it includes an investigation paper and assumes a graphic display calculator rather than a scientific one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, tiers into Foundation and Higher and has its own formula-sheet conventions and its own way of phrasing questions.

A tutor who has taught 0580 for a decade and is handed a 0607 candidate will be competent at the mathematics and wrong about the preparation. The investigation paper has no analogue in 0580. Conversely, a 0607 specialist put in front of a 4MA1 Higher candidate will not have drilled the particular phrasing Pearson favours. Mathematics does not change; the examination of it does, and the last eight weeks before a paper are all about the examination.

Then there is the thing almost no family is taught, which is how a maths paper is actually marked. A mark scheme awards method marks and accuracy marks separately, and it allows follow-through credit in defined circumstances. A student who understands that will write differently — more steps, clearly labelled, with the method visible even when the arithmetic has gone wrong. A student who does not will produce an elegant three-line answer with a slip in it and score zero on a question they could do. That is not a knowledge gap. It is a presentation habit, and it is worth a grade on its own in many scripts.

A practical note before the detail. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Maths for a family in Dubai Internet City is taught one-to-one over live video on a shared whiteboard, which suits this subject well — every line of working is preserved, a photographed attempt can be annotated live, and the match is made on the syllabus code rather than on who happens to live within reach of the Al Sufouh tram at six in the evening. For a tiered subject with three competing specifications in one school cluster, that is not a small distinction.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and standard form
subjects.description: The lowest-risk marks on the paper and the ones most often thrown away. Percentage change in reverse, compound interest over a non-integer period, and standard form arithmetic without a calculator are the three places capable candidates drop easy marks through haste rather than ignorance.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying algebraic fractions. Extended and Higher candidates lose most here through sign errors carried into later parts, which is precisely the situation follow-through credit exists for — provided the method is visible on the page.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous systems
subjects.description: Quadratics by factorising, by formula and by completing the square, plus simultaneous equations with one linear and one non-linear. Candidates who memorise one method and meet a question that blocks it stall, so the fix is fluency across all three routes.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching, reading, and transforming curves. This is the single most reliable discriminator between a grade 7 and a grade 9 script. Students who can describe a transformation but not perform it in the correct order lose the composite-transformation marks every time.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, parallel and perpendicular lines, and the equation of a line from varied starting information. Short, well-paid questions that reward a candidate who writes the general form down first instead of trying to see the answer.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and Pythagoras
subjects.description: Right-angled work at Core, then sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems at Extended. Three-dimensional trigonometry is where marks vanish, almost always because no diagram was drawn before the calculation began.

subjects.name: Mensuration and circle work
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, and similar shapes with area and volume scale factors. The scale-factor questions are heavily examined and routinely answered with a linear factor where a squared or cubed one is needed.

subjects.name: Vectors and matrices
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic, magnitude, and geometric proof using vectors. Vector proof asks a candidate to argue rather than calculate, which is unfamiliar at this level and therefore trainable in a small number of sessions.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths, and averages from grouped data. Histogram frequency density is the classic lost mark: candidates plot frequency and lose every subsequent mark on the question.

subjects.name: The investigation paper (0607 only)
subjects.description: Unique to Cambridge International Mathematics. The candidate explores a situation, finds a pattern, generalises it and comments on it. It rewards persistence and clear communication rather than recall, and it cannot be prepared for from a 0580 revision guide.

sections.heading: Finding out which IGCSE maths your child is sitting
paragraphs: This takes one message to the exams officer and it should happen before any tutor is hired. The statement of entry names the qualification and the tier, and that pair determines the whole preparation. Families in this cluster are more likely than most to be caught out, because the IB-pathway schools nearby commonly choose Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 rather than the more familiar 0580.

The differences are substantial enough to matter. 0580 and 4MA1 are two-paper qualifications with no investigative component. 0607 includes an investigation paper and assumes a graphic display calculator throughout, which changes both the content emphasis and the equipment a student needs to be fluent with. A candidate who arrives at that paper having revised from 0580 material is meeting the format for the first time in the exam hall.

Tier is the second half of the answer and carries the grade ceiling. Cambridge Core caps at grade C or 5. Cambridge Extended and Pearson Higher run the full range. The tier is usually fixed during Year 10 and becomes difficult to change once the final entry deadline passes, which is months before the paper rather than weeks.

There is a third question worth adding while you have the officer's attention: whether the school is also entering your child for Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, which some schools in this belt run alongside 0580 for strong candidates. It is a separate qualification with its own preparation, and it frequently goes unmentioned at home until a paper appears on the timetable.
The table below is the ten-minute version. Take it to the exams officer, get the answers, and every subsequent decision about tutoring becomes straightforward rather than speculative.

sections.heading: How a maths paper is actually marked, and why it changes how you write
paragraphs: Very few students in this cluster have ever been shown a real mark scheme, and it is the single most useful hour a tutor can spend. A maths mark scheme does not award marks for correct answers alone. It separates method marks, awarded for a valid approach regardless of arithmetic, from accuracy marks, awarded for the correct value. It also permits follow-through credit, where a candidate who makes one error and then handles the rest of the question correctly still earns the later marks.

The consequence is concrete and immediate. A student who writes three lines and reaches a wrong answer scores nothing. A student who writes eight lines showing the same approach and reaches the same wrong answer, because of one slip in line four, earns the method marks and often the follow-through accuracy marks as well. On a 100-mark paper that distinction routinely moves a grade, and it has nothing whatsoever to do with how much maths the student knows.

This is why strong mental mathematicians often underperform at IGCSE. They have been rewarded all their lives for getting there quickly, and the examination rewards getting there visibly. Changing that habit is uncomfortable for about three weeks and then it holds, and it is the most reliable return available in this subject.

Pearson 4MA1 rewards this behaviour particularly strongly, which is worth knowing if that is the specification on the entry form. The table sets out the mark types and what a candidate has to do to earn each one, which is the version a Year 11 can actually act on.

sections.heading: The seven ways marks leave an IGCSE maths script
paragraphs: After enough marked papers the list stops being mysterious. Almost nothing on it is content the student has never met, which is why a diagnosis based on scores alone is so misleading: two candidates on 58 per cent can need entirely different interventions.

In rough order of how much they cost: method not written down, so a slip takes the whole question. Premature rounding, which quietly loses accuracy marks on otherwise perfect work. Misread form, where a question asks for an exact answer or a fraction and receives a rounded decimal. Scale factors applied linearly to areas or volumes. Histogram frequency plotted instead of frequency density. No diagram drawn for a three-dimensional trigonometry or bearings question. And uneven timing, which leaves the last page blank.

The useful move is to count them. Mark two full papers, classify every single lost mark into one of those seven categories, and then look at the totals. A student losing 19 marks to timing and rounding and 5 to content does not need more content taught, and treating every low score as a knowledge problem is the most expensive mistake families in this market make, partly because it feels like diligence.

Once the counts exist, the next six weeks write themselves. The largest category gets attacked first, the error log is updated after every marked paper, and when a category stops appearing it stops getting hours. That is a plan built on evidence rather than on a syllabus checklist.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: The tier decision is made during Year 10, usually by the school with the family consulted, and it is more consequential than any amount of revision that follows. Cambridge Core caps at grade C or 5. Extended runs to A* or 9. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher work the same way. Once the final entry deadline passes, changing becomes an administrative problem rather than a choice.

Both errors are common and both are costly. Entering a struggling candidate for Extended in hope produces a low Extended grade rather than a high Core one, and it also means two years of lessons pitched above the student's reach, which does real damage to confidence. Entering a capable candidate for Core removes the grades a competitive sixth form wants to see, and no amount of effort in Year 11 can lift a capped result.

The decision should rest on evidence. Sit a past paper at each tier under timed conditions and mark both against the official scheme. The pattern is usually unambiguous: a candidate comfortably above the Core ceiling on the Core paper and scoring in the middle bands on the Extended one belongs on Extended, and a candidate struggling on Core does not improve by being moved up.

There is also a forward question. Extended or Higher at grade 7 and above is what most sixth forms in this cluster want before admitting a student to A Level Mathematics, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or any engineering-facing route. If that is the destination, the tier conversation is really a Year 12 conversation held two years early.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and whether it is worth it
paragraphs: Most cost discussions in this market start with the cheapest option. Start instead with the most expensive line and ask what the extra money is actually purchasing, because that is the question a family in Internet City is really weighing. The in-home band in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's rate table, with independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. A qualified tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150.

So the premium for a visit is real but moderate at the bottom of the band and substantial at the top. What it buys is a person in the room. That is worth paying for if your child genuinely will not engage with a screen — some will not, and it is better to know that than to argue with it. What it does not buy is a better mathematician, and it comes with two costs that are easy to miss. The tutor's travel time has to be recovered from somewhere, usually from the hourly rate and from the slots they are willing to offer. And the pool shrinks to whoever lives nearby.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages circulating in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. At the budget end of the market, EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, typically university-student tutors; TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the top.

None of those are IB Gram's prices — they are market figures attributed to the providers who published them, so you can check each one. For a specific quote in your child's tier and specification, the route is the free trial lesson and the conversation after it.

sections.heading: Why a screen works for a subject done with a pen
paragraphs: The intuition runs the other way, so it is worth being specific. Maths is the subject where online teaching loses least and gains most, because the artefact that matters is the working, and a shared digital whiteboard preserves it. Three weeks later the student can scroll back to the line where they first went wrong on a quadratic, and so can the tutor.

Marking works better too. A student photographs a handwritten attempt, the image goes on the shared board, and the tutor annotates it live, marking method and accuracy separately exactly as a mark scheme would. That is a far more useful exercise than handing a page back with a score on it, and it is awkward to do well across a dining table.

Graph work is the third gain. Dragging a coefficient and watching a parabola move, while the tutor explains which transformation is happening and in what order, explains composite transformations better than any static diagram. For a 0607 candidate with a graphic display calculator, the screen can be shared directly, which means inefficient keystroke habits become visible and fixable in minutes.

The honest limit is attention. A student who will not sit with a screen, or who has nowhere quiet in a shared tower apartment, does better with someone present. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so if that is your child, a local in-home tutor is the right recommendation and it will be given rather than argued around.

sections.heading: Counting backwards to the maths paper
paragraphs: No competitor page in this cluster publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the decisions a parent can still influence are all clustered early. By the time revision feels urgent, the tier is fixed and the entry is made. The useful question is not what to do in May; it is what should already have been done by each point before it.

The fixed points for UAE candidates are the Cambridge June series and November series, and the Pearson May/June and November windows. The Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only and is not available to candidates sitting in Dubai, which matters because a large amount of online revision material is written around it. Cambridge publishes a separate timetable for each of six administrative zones and is explicit that using the wrong one is the candidate's risk, so the correct window comes from your school's exams officer.

Dates already past can be stated with confidence because they are checkable. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. For the series ahead, read the live official timetable rather than a restated version, because provisional timetables get revised.

The November series is also the resit route, which is worth understanding before results arrive rather than after. A candidate who misses a target grade in June can re-sit in November, and the decision about whether that is sensible depends on how far short they fell and on what the sixth form actually requires.
