sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths has to get your child to next
paragraphs: A maths grade at 16 is a gateway rather than an endpoint, and in this school cluster the gates are unusually varied, because sixth forms within a few kilometres of Internet City offer A Level, the IB Diploma, or both. What the grade needs to be depends on which door the student intends to walk through.

A Level Mathematics typically wants a grade 7 or above at Extended or Higher tier, and A Level Further Mathematics wants more. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma is the equivalent ask, and students arriving there from IGCSE Extended usually find the algebra fluent and the calculus and proof entirely new, which is a content gap and a manageable one. Applications and Interpretation is more forgiving on algebra and less forgiving on interpretation.

Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, taken alongside 0580 by strong candidates in some schools here, is a genuinely useful bridge: it introduces calculus and more demanding algebra a year early and makes the first term of either post-16 route noticeably easier. It is not a replacement for 0580 and it is not necessary, but for a student certain about a maths-facing route it earns its hours.

The planning point is simple and almost always acted on too late. Work backwards from the intended sixth-form course to the tier decision in Year 10, not forwards from results in August. A family that does this has options; a family that does not finds out in results week that one has closed.

sections.heading: Academic honesty and materials in a maths context
paragraphs: Maths at IGCSE has less coursework exposure than the essay subjects, but two honesty questions still arise and both deserve a plain answer. The first concerns the small number of specifications that retain coursework or an investigative component, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 among them. The second concerns materials.

On assessed work the boundary is firm. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, model the method on a different problem, explain the criteria, and give feedback on what the student has already produced. A tutor may not write it, redraft it to completion, or supply text or results for submission. For an investigation this matters more than for a written paper, because the work is produced out of sight and the student is the one who carries the consequence if it is not their own.

On materials, the boards hold copyright in syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables. A tutor should work from the official source on the board's own site, or through the school's access, and should not be distributing reproduced packs to families. Any tutor offering you a bundle of board material is telling you something about how they operate generally.

The practical version of all this is reassuring rather than restrictive. The most valuable thing a maths tutor does is mark a student's own attempt against the real scheme and explain each decision. That is both entirely legitimate and considerably more useful than a worked solution handed over.
bullets: A tutor teaches the skill, models it elsewhere, and marks the student's own attempt
No investigative or coursework text is written or supplied for submission
Official papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked, never redistributed
Marking a student's own script against the real scheme is the highest-value activity available

sections.heading: Starting, and the honest version of availability
paragraphs: Three facts make the first conversation useful: the qualification code, the tier, and the most recent marked paper with its real score and the script if possible. The script matters more than the score, because a mark of 58 tells you nothing about whether the problem is content, method presentation, rounding or the clock.

The trial lesson is free and should begin with a question from the correct specification rather than with a discussion of goals. Watching a Year 11 attempt a real question for ten minutes is more diagnostic than half an hour of conversation, and it tells you whether the two of them can work together, which no amount of credentials will.

On availability, the honest position. For 0580 and 4MA1 at either tier, a specialist on Gulf Standard Time is usually available within a few days. For 0607 with the investigation paper as the target, in a crowded evening slot, in the weeks before the June series, there may be a wait, or the only available specialist may be working from outside the UAE on the same time zone. Which of those applies is said before booking rather than discovered afterwards. No competitor page found in this market states a coverage limit at all.

And sometimes the right answer is less. Four sessions on histograms and transformations, a re-test, and a stop. That recommendation will be made where it fits, because a platform unable to suggest buying less than it sells is not giving advice.

process.title: Get the code and the tier
process.description: One message to the exams officer returns the qualification and the tier. In this cluster that is a genuinely consequential question, because the IB-pathway schools nearby often run Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 rather than the 0580 most tutors assume.

process.title: Send the script, not just the score
process.description: The last marked paper with the working visible is worth more than a percentage. It shows whether the marks went to content gaps, invisible method, premature rounding or the clock, and those four lead to four different programmes.

process.title: Diagnostic question in the free trial
process.description: The first session opens with a real question from the correct specification, attempted live. The tutor watches where the hesitation falls and gives you a written read of what it showed, including whether tutoring is the right purchase at all.

process.title: Match on the specification
process.description: A tutor is proposed for the exact qualification and tier, with their background stated. Where no 0607 investigation specialist is free in your slot, that is said before a booking is taken rather than filled with the nearest available substitute.

process.title: Weekly work, marked like a paper
process.description: Set work comes back marked with method and accuracy separated, the way a real scheme marks it, including credit the student assumed was lost. Every marked piece updates the error log, and the log drives what the next session contains.

process.title: Finish and say so
process.description: When the category that was costing marks stops appearing in the log, that strand ends. For some students the whole engagement is four sessions on two topics, and that gets recommended rather than extended into a standing booking.

whyPoints.title: The code question asked first
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are three qualifications, and this school cluster uses all three. Matching on the specification before anything else prevents the commonest and most expensive error in this market.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes taught, not just used
whyPoints.description: Students are shown how M marks, A marks and follow-through credit actually work, and then taught to write so they earn them. For a strong mental mathematician this single change is often worth a grade, and it costs about three weeks of discomfort.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis by cause, not by score
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is classified — method invisible, premature rounding, wrong form, linear scale factor, no diagram, timing — and the counts decide the plan. Two students on the same percentage usually need entirely different work.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED figures here are attributed to the providers who published them and framed as market rates rather than ours. Most pages competing for this search either publish nothing or quote in dollars, which is no use to a family paying in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Online, with the reason given
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For maths the format is a real advantage — working preserved, scripts annotated live, graphs manipulated on screen — and the argument rests on that rather than on availability.

whyPoints.title: Willing to recommend less
whyPoints.description: Where a student needs two topics repaired and nothing else, the recommendation is two topics and a stop. The error log makes that call evidence-based rather than a judgement, which is what makes it possible to say out loud.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0607 really different enough from 0580 to need a different tutor?
faqs.answer: Different enough to matter in the last two months, yes. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 includes an investigation paper that has no equivalent in 0580, assumes a graphic display calculator rather than a scientific one, and places heavier weight on function work. The underlying mathematics overlaps substantially, so a good 0580 teacher will handle the content. What they may not have is experience of preparing a candidate for an investigative component, which is the part your child will find least familiar. Several IB-pathway schools near Al Sufouh use 0607, so check the entry rather than assuming.

faqs.question: What are M marks and A marks, and why does my child keep scoring zero on questions they can do?
faqs.answer: Because the marks are awarded for visible method as well as for the right answer. M marks reward a valid approach regardless of arithmetic; A marks reward the correct value; follow-through credit rewards correct later work built on an earlier slip. A student who writes three lines and makes one error scores nothing. The same student writing eight labelled lines earns the method marks and often the follow-through marks too. Strong mental mathematicians suffer most from this, because speed has always been rewarded and the examination rewards visibility instead.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics do Year 11 candidates in this part of Dubai lose most on?
faqs.answer: Functions and transformations first, which is the reliable discriminator between a grade 7 and a grade 9 script, particularly composite transformations performed in the wrong order. Then histograms with unequal class widths, where candidates plot frequency instead of frequency density and lose every subsequent mark. Then similar shapes, where a linear scale factor gets applied to an area or a volume. Then three-dimensional trigonometry and bearings, almost always because no diagram was drawn first. Vector proof comes next, because arguing rather than calculating is unfamiliar at this level.

faqs.question: How do we decide between Core and Extended tier for maths?
faqs.answer: On two marked papers, not on optimism. Sit a Core paper and an Extended paper under timed conditions and mark both against the official scheme. A candidate comfortably above the Core ceiling on Core and landing in the middle bands on Extended belongs on Extended. A candidate struggling on Core does not improve by being moved up; they get a low Extended grade and two years of lessons pitched out of reach. Remember the ceiling: Core caps at grade C or 5, and most sixth forms in this cluster want a 7 at Extended before A Level Mathematics.

faqs.question: Does premature rounding really cost marks on a calculator paper?
faqs.answer: Regularly, and it is one of the cheapest errors to eliminate. Mark schemes award accuracy marks for a correctly rounded final answer, and they expect intermediate values to be carried at full accuracy. A candidate who rounds a trigonometric value to three figures in the middle of a multi-step problem can arrive at a final answer that falls outside the accepted range, losing the accuracy mark on work that was entirely correct. The habit to train is simple: store intermediate values in the calculator, round once, at the end, and only to the accuracy the question asks for.

faqs.question: Why is there no maths tutor who can come to our building in Internet City?
faqs.answer: Because IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service. Maths here is taught one-to-one over live video on a shared whiteboard, which for this subject is a genuine advantage: every line of working is preserved and can be revisited weeks later, a photographed handwritten attempt can be annotated live the way a marker would, and graphs can be manipulated on screen while the tutor explains. It also means the match is made on the specification and tier rather than on whoever happens to live within a short drive.

faqs.question: What does a qualified IGCSE maths tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Read it from the top down. Independent home tutors in Dubai ask AED 200 to 500, and Bestimate's rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with travel priced into the hour. A qualified tutor working online sits lower, at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and A Level work runs AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270. Budget online tuition is published from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. Those are market figures, attributed, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Is a visiting tutor worth the extra money for maths specifically?
faqs.answer: It buys a person in the room, which matters a great deal for some students and not at all for others. What it does not buy is better mathematics, and it carries two hidden costs: the tutor's travel has to be recovered from the hourly rate and from the slots they will offer, and the pool shrinks to whoever lives nearby. For a subject where the working is the lesson, a shared whiteboard that saves every line is arguably the better tool. If your child genuinely will not engage with a screen, pay the premium — that is a real reason.

faqs.question: My child finishes school at three and is useless by five. When can sessions actually happen?
faqs.answer: Later than most in-home tutors want to work, which is one of the practical arguments for the online format in this belt. A Year 11 finishing at 15:00 on Al Sufouh Road often is not settled at a desk until 16:15 once the school run clears, and attention is poor between then and dinner. The most-requested weekday slot from Internet City and Knowledge Park is 19:30, after parents working on the nearby campuses are home. Because nobody is travelling, that slot can be held week after week rather than lost to a family who live closer to the tutor.

faqs.question: When are the maths papers, and is there a February sitting we should plan around?
faqs.answer: There is no February or March sitting available to candidates in Dubai. Cambridge offers its February/March series to India only; UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong version, so take the window from your school's exams officer rather than from a revision site written for another country.

faqs.question: Can my child re-sit maths in November if June does not go well?
faqs.answer: Yes — November is the resit route for Cambridge, and Pearson also runs a November series. Whether it is the right move depends on two things: how far short the grade fell, and what the sixth form actually requires. A candidate one grade below a 7 with a clear technique-based loss pattern is a strong resit case, because that gap is recoverable in a focused block. A candidate several grades short with broad content gaps may be better advised to take a different route. Decide on the marked script, not on the headline grade.

faqs.question: What grade does my child need for A Level Maths or Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Most sixth forms in this cluster want a grade 7 or above at Extended or Higher tier for A Level Mathematics, with more for Further Mathematics, and the equivalent ask applies for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma. Requirements vary by school, so confirm with the specific sixth form rather than relying on a general rule. The planning consequence is the point: that requirement makes the Year 10 tier decision a sixth-form decision taken two years early, and families who work backwards from the destination keep their options open.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking alongside 0580?
faqs.answer: For a student certain about a maths-facing route, it earns its hours. 0606 introduces calculus and more demanding algebraic work a year early, which makes the first term of A Level Mathematics or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level noticeably less of a shock. It is not a replacement for 0580 and it is not required by anyone. For a student still deciding, or already stretched across nine subjects, it is an avoidable extra load. The honest test is whether the student finds Extended 0580 comfortable rather than survivable.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give us worked solutions and past paper packs to work through?
faqs.answer: A tutor will point you to the official source and work from it, and will mark your child's own attempts, but will not hand over reproduced packs. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the exam boards' copyright and should be accessed through the board's own site or through your school. More importantly, a worked solution handed over teaches considerably less than the same question marked line by line against the real scheme, with each method and accuracy decision explained. That marking is the thing worth paying for.

faqs.question: One session a week or two, for a candidate heading into the mocks?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, at 60 or 90 minutes, with set work marked properly in between. A single weekly session that consolidates what the school has just taught achieves more than two sessions covering the same ground twice over. Two a week makes sense in two situations: a Year 11 with a substantial algebraic debt to clear before the mocks, and a candidate running separate strands for content and paper technique in the final term. Starting at two as a precaution usually produces a tired student and a plan nobody follows past week five.

faqs.question: If the specialist we need is not free at our time, will somebody tell us?
faqs.answer: Before you book, yes. For Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 at either tier, a specialist on Gulf Standard Time is usually available within a few days. For Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 with the investigation paper as the target, in a crowded evening slot, in the weeks before the June series, there may be a wait, or the only available specialist may be working from outside the UAE on the same time zone. Which applies is stated in advance. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-interne.closingHeading: One message to the exams officer, then a plan
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-interne.closingBody: Before you hire anybody, send one message to your child's exams officer and ask two things: which maths qualification is on the entry, and which tier. With 0580, 0607 or 4MA1 and the tier in hand, plus the last marked script, a sensible eight-week plan takes a quarter of an hour to build and rests on evidence rather than guesswork. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the working saved on a shared board so that nothing is lost between weeks. The first lesson is free, it starts with a real question from the right specification, and if the answer turns out to be four sessions on two topics, that is what you will be told.

intro.heading: The money is not wasted on the rate, it is wasted on the aim
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, mixing industrial and commercial plots with residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, served by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and its own Metro station towards Expo City. A British-curriculum school and two IB schools sit inside the district, and most secondary students travel out to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan or Dubai South.

Families here ask about cost earlier in the conversation than families in central districts, and they are right to. In a corridor where the school run already consumes several hours a week, tutoring has to justify itself in both money and time. So this page leads with the arithmetic rather than burying it, and the arithmetic has a clear conclusion: the hourly rate is rarely where the waste happens.

The waste happens in four places. Buying general weekly mathematics support when the marked script showed one specific failure. Continuing after the problem is solved because nobody set a review point. Paying a premium rate for revision of content the student already knows. And paying for practice built from the wrong board's past papers, which is the quietest and most complete waste of all because everybody involved is working hard.

Avoiding all four costs nothing. Read the marked script, name the failure, confirm whether your child sits Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, ask any prospective tutor how many sessions the fix should take and what will show it is done, and set a review point before the first session rather than after the tenth. That is the whole method, and it reliably turns a vague monthly cost into a finite, comparable block.

It is worth being concrete about how short most fixes are, because that is what changes a budget conversation. Method marks lost to unshown working is roughly four sessions. Premature rounding is two. A calculator left in the wrong angular mode is one or two. Histograms with unequal class widths, and conditional probability without replacement, are about three each. At mid-market rates those are costs in the low hundreds to low thousands of dirhams, with an observable test of whether the money worked.

The expensive exception is worth naming in the same breath. A genuine algebraic fluency gap is not a block at all; it is a term of short regular work, because fluency is built by repetition over time rather than fixed by explanation. A family told that honestly can decide whether to commit. A family not told it discovers the same thing after four sessions have produced nothing, and usually blames the tutor.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE mathematics tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. In this corridor the in-home option also carries the highest travel premium in the market, which the tables below set out with sources.

programmes.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger cohorts as a bridge to A Level or Higher Level IB, introducing calculus and more formal function work. A student comfortable in 0580 Extended who struggles here usually has a speed and fluency gap, which responds to short regular practice rather than to re-teaching.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-investm.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is best organised by the failure that shows up in marked work, because that is what a block of sessions can be aimed at and costed against.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. Fluency here determines performance everywhere else, and a genuine fluency gap is the one problem on this page that costs a term rather than a block, which is why identifying it early matters financially.

subjects.name: Equations and simultaneous systems
subjects.description: Quadratics by factorising, formula and completing the square, plus simultaneous equations including one non-linear at the higher tiers. Marks go missing when a solution set is found and never checked against the original condition.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients, intercepts and interpretation. Lost marks usually come from sketches that are qualitatively right but missing the labelled features the question named, which is a reading failure rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Geometry and mensuration
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle properties, similarity, and area and volume of composite solids. Reasons are marked as well as answers, so an unstated angle fact forfeits the explanation mark even where the number is right.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangles, bearings and three-dimensional problems. The recurring failure is a calculator left in the wrong angular mode, which is a one to two session fix and is almost never diagnosed because each instance looks like carelessness.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and scatter graphs. Histograms are reliably the worst-answered topic here because frequency density gets treated as optional, and three sessions usually closes it.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and set notation at the higher tiers. Errors cluster around failure to adjust for non-replacement, and around products left unsimplified where a value was asked for.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude and geometric reasoning. Marks are available for the reasoning chain rather than the final vector, so answers given without intermediate statements score below their apparent worth.

subjects.name: Number in context and precision
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form and bounds. Premature rounding is the dominant error, producing answers just outside the accepted range on work that was correct throughout, and it is a two-session fix with a rule.

subjects.name: Method presentation and timing
subjects.description: Showing working so method marks are collected, and holding a per-question time budget. Together these account for more lost marks across a paper than any single topic, and both are trainable in four sessions without new content.

sections.heading: The four ways the money gets wasted
paragraphs: These are the failure modes, in rough order of how much they cost. None of them involves a bad tutor, which is why they are so persistent: in every case somebody is working hard and the money is still going nowhere.

First, buying general support with no diagnosis. A weekly mathematics session aimed at the subject rather than at a component will spend most of its time on material the student already knows, because that is what fills a syllabus. This is the single largest source of waste in this market, and the fix is one marked script read before anything is booked.

Second, continuing after the problem is solved. Without a stated completion test, a block becomes a standing arrangement, and a standing arrangement gets reviewed when the invoice becomes uncomfortable rather than when the work is done. Third, paying a specialist premium for content revision, which is paying AED 270 an hour for supervision that a budget-band tutor could provide equally well, because the task is practice rather than diagnosis.

Fourth, and the quietest: practice built from the wrong board's past papers. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 differ in paper structure, mark allocation and tier vocabulary, departments choose independently, and the content overlap is large enough that nobody notices until a paper feels unfamiliar. This waste is total rather than partial, and it costs one email to prevent.

A fifth failure deserves mention because it is specific to households under time pressure: booking three subjects at once because all three feel urgent. Three simultaneous plans with no sequencing produce three shallow efforts and no completed fix, at three times the cost. One component, verified on a timed paper, then the next, is both cheaper and faster.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Edexcel 4MA1
paragraphs: Across the researched competitor pages for this market, exactly one syllabus code appeared in an entire seven-page cluster. That silence is the reason the board mismatch persists: families are never told the distinction matters, so they never check it, and the error is invisible from inside a session because the content overlaps heavily.

What differs is the examination rather than the mathematics. Paper structure, the number and length of papers, mark allocation conventions and topic weighting all vary. Tier vocabulary differs outright, with Cambridge setting Core and Extended while Edexcel Mathematics sets Foundation and Higher, which creates a specific hazard: a parent translating between those terms on a phone call can agree to the wrong entry without anyone noticing.

Check per subject rather than per school, because departments choose independently and a single student can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics alongside Edexcel Chemistry in the same year. The code is printed on the school's assessment paperwork and the subject teacher will confirm it in a line. Then state it to the tutor in writing and ask which series their practice papers come from.

On dates: Cambridge runs June and November for a candidate sitting in Dubai, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Edexcel runs May and June and November. Both publish provisional timetables ahead of a series and revise them, so plan from the official live document rather than from any restated date.

One further check costs nothing and catches the problem early. Ask the tutor to tell you, in writing, which code and which series each practice paper came from. A tutor with an organised set answers immediately; one who is improvising cannot, and improvised practice in Year 11 is the quietest way for a term and a budget to disappear together.

sections.heading: The tier decision as a financial decision
paragraphs: The tier entry is usually discussed in academic terms and it is also a money decision, because the two tiers need different amounts of work and because a capped entry closes a route that is expensive or impossible to reopen later.

On the work side, a secure grade within the capped tier needs fewer hours than a competitive grade at the fuller tier, since the extension topics absorb most of the tutoring time. A family choosing the capped tier for a student who genuinely belongs there is buying a cheaper and more certain outcome, and there is nothing wrong with that.

On the route side, the cost runs the other way. A Core or Foundation mathematics entry does not position a student for A Level Mathematics or for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, whatever grade is achieved inside the cap. Reopening that route later means a resit or a different post-16 plan, both of which cost considerably more than the extension work would have. In this corridor the risk is higher because families move schools as the area fills, and post-16 provision varies between the established Jebel Ali schools and the newer ones near Dubai South.

Decide with a timed paper from the harder tier, taken now, with no notes and marked honestly. Mid-range or above and the decision is made. Near the bottom of the range and there is a genuine question about whether a block closes the gap in the weeks available, which is exactly the question a costed block answers. Ask the subject teacher for the confirmation deadline and work backwards from it.

sections.heading: Why in-home costs more out here than it looks
paragraphs: In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel built into the rate, according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. In Dubai Investments Park that headline gap understates the real difference for three reasons.

First, the travel component is doing more work here. DIP sits in the southern corridor off two motorways, and a tutor coming from a central district is making a long journey at the busiest hour. Rates quoted for central areas are not a reliable guide to what will be quoted for an address here, and some providers apply a surcharge outside a stated radius.

Second, the pool shrinks. The willingness to make that drive is a filter applied before any question of subject expertise, so a family insisting on in-home delivery is selecting from a short list that gets shorter for every specific requirement added. Paying more for a smaller choice is the opposite of what a premium is supposed to buy.

Third, reliability costs money indirectly. A session that depends on a vehicle arriving through afternoon traffic is a session that starts late or gets cancelled, and in a household already short of hours each lost session is both a sunk cost and a gap in the plan. An online session has no journey of its own, so it starts when it is booked and can be moved when the school run goes wrong.

sections.heading: What to verify before paying anyone
paragraphs: Comparing tutoring providers on warmth is unreliable, because warmth is the easiest thing to produce. These five items are checkable, and a provider who answers all five plainly is telling you something real about how they operate.

One: a published rate, or at minimum a clear statement of how the price is set, in dirhams rather than a currency you do not transact in. Two: a stated position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years, and whose absence exposes the tutor to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion.

Three: a free trial with any condition stated on the same screen, such as its length, eligibility or whether a commitment follows. Four: a tutor who can name the board, the syllabus code and the entered tier, and who can estimate a block length from a marked script. Five: no claimed approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because an independent tutoring platform holds none and IB Gram holds none either. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises and says nothing about an individual tutor.

There is a sixth item which is not about the provider at all: your own review point. Agree, before the first session, what will be looked at and when. A school assessment or mock is the right trigger. Without that, the most likely outcome is not a bad tutor but an unreviewed arrangement, which is how a reasonable hourly rate becomes an unreasonable annual total.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Send five things: the board and code, the tier, the school, the last two marked mathematics papers, and the session length your household can sustain on a weekday. The free trial lesson comes before any payment and produces the two numbers that make the decision financial rather than vague: which failure you have, and how many sessions it should take.

Ask for the completion test in the same conversation. If a provider cannot say what will show that the block worked, the block has no end, and a block with no end is the most expensive thing in this market. We would rather tell you that a problem is four sessions than sell a term, partly because it is true and partly because a family that gets a true answer comes back for the next component.

What will not be claimed. No grade promise, because nobody can honestly make one, and no claim that a particular grade is achievable with a particular number of sessions. No suggestion that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval, no UAE office or centre, and no satisfaction statistics, because a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration.

Two final notes. Enquiry forms collect information about a child, so we ask only for what the plan needs, state why, and keep a privacy link on every page; we do not ask for a photograph and you can ask for the record to be deleted. And we do not publish or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright. We cite it, link to it, and work from what your school legitimately provides.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring actually cost in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: The market, attributed and dated October 2026: budget online provision from AED 33 to 65 per hour, a qualified subject tutor online roughly AED 150 to 300, specialists AED 200 to 450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, and in-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 table. Advertised monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Ours is set after the free trial, because the honest price depends on how many sessions the diagnosis actually requires.

faqs.question: Why does our tutoring spend never seem to change the grade?
faqs.answer: Usually because nothing was aimed. A weekly session pointed at the subject rather than at a component spends most of its time on material the student already knows, since that is what fills a syllabus. The other three causes are continuing after the problem was solved, paying a specialist rate for routine practice, and practising from the wrong board's past papers. None involves a bad tutor, which is exactly why all four are so common.

faqs.question: Can we pay for in-home maths lessons at our DIP address instead?
faqs.answer: Not through us. We teach IGCSE mathematics one-to-one into DIP homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. In this corridor in-home delivery also carries the steepest travel premium in the market, since a tutor from a central district is making a long journey at the busiest hour of the day.

faqs.question: How many sessions should a specific problem take?
faqs.answer: Most are shorter than families expect. Method marks lost to unshown working is about four sessions; premature rounding two; angular mode in trigonometry one or two; histograms three; conditional probability three; timing four. A genuine algebraic fluency gap is the exception and needs a term of short regular work, because fluency is built by repetition rather than fixed by explanation. Ask any provider for the estimate and for what will show the block is finished.

faqs.question: What is a completion test and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: It is an observable sign that the work is done, as opposed to a date on which the block happens to end. Examples: the student predicts their own mark before it is given, the error stops appearing in the log, the back page of a timed paper is no longer blank, or speed measurably improves on timed sets. A block with an end date drifts into a standing arrangement; a block with a test ends, and you can say with confidence that the money achieved something.

faqs.question: Is a budget tutor at AED 50 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right task. Practice supervision, company while working through question sets and keeping a student on task are all genuinely useful and do not require someone who knows the mark scheme. What a budget rate will not reliably buy is diagnosis: reading two marked papers and identifying that the loss is method marks rather than content. Match the rate to the task and you will spend less overall than a family who buys one rate for everything.

faqs.question: How do I check which board my child sits?
faqs.answer: The code is printed on the school's assessment paperwork, and the subject teacher will confirm it in one line. Check per subject rather than per school, because departments choose independently and a student can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics alongside an Edexcel science in the same year. Then state the code to the tutor in writing and ask which series their practice papers come from. This single email prevents the most complete form of waste available in this market.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home premium worse in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three reasons beyond the headline rate. The travel component is doing more work, since DIP sits in the southern corridor off two motorways and a tutor from a central district is driving a long way at peak hour, with surcharges possible outside a stated radius. The pool shrinks to those willing to make that drive, so you pay more for less choice. And sessions that depend on traffic start late or get cancelled, which is sunk cost plus a gap in the plan.

faqs.question: Should we fix the tier entry or the grade?
faqs.answer: Settle the tier first, because it caps what any amount of tutoring can produce. Take a timed paper from the harder tier now, with no notes, and mark it honestly: mid-range or above and the decision is made. Remember the financial asymmetry too. The capped tier needs fewer hours for a secure grade, but it removes the A Level Mathematics and Higher Level Analysis routes, and reopening those later costs far more than the extension work would have.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use a tuition centre?
faqs.answer: Per hour, often yes. Per outcome, it depends entirely on what is wrong. A group class teaching a fixed syllabus cannot stop for your child's specific error, which is usually the whole problem, and from DIP you should add two car journeys per session as a real cost in time whether or not it appears on an invoice. If a marked script points at histograms and unshown working, three one-to-one sessions will get further than a term of class work.

faqs.question: What do we do if we can only afford a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Spend them well rather than spreading them. Use one on diagnosis, from the marked script, then put the remainder into the single highest-yield failure, which for most students is method marks lost to unshown working. That is marks on work your child already gets right, which is the cheapest possible source of improvement. Avoid dividing a small budget across three subjects, because three shallow plans produce less than one completed block.

faqs.question: Do you charge more closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: We do not raise rates as a series approaches, and it is a fair question to ask any provider, because peak-season pricing is a real practice in this market and it arrives at the point when switching is hardest. What does change near a series is availability: early-evening slots are genuinely contested because much of Dubai's Year 11 cohort wants the same hour, which is an argument for agreeing the pattern before mock results rather than after.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle Mathematics and Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is more economical, because 0606 Additional Mathematics extends the algebra and functions work in 0580 Extended and the same tutor can hold both. The thing to check is that they have taught 0606 specifically, since it introduces calculus and formal function work a general IGCSE tutor may not have covered. A student fluent in Extended who struggles in 0606 generally has a speed gap, which responds to short regular practice.

faqs.question: What is the single cheapest thing we can do this week?
faqs.answer: Two emails and twenty minutes, all free. Email each relevant subject teacher to confirm the board, code and tier. Then sit with the last marked paper, ignore the grade, and look for which pattern appears: correct answers with low marks, long answers with one mark, losses concentrated in one region, or a rushed final page. Those point to blocks of four, three to four, three to five and four sessions respectively, which means you will know roughly what you need before anyone quotes you.

intro.heading: Four different maths courses, one subject name
paragraphs: The honest answer to the question behind this search is that plenty of people in Dubai can teach mathematics, and rather fewer can teach the specific course your child is entered for. Around the Marina and the schools that serve it, a Year 11 student might be sitting Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1, or 0580 alongside Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 as a stretch option. The subject on the report card says maths in all four cases. The papers, the calculator rules, the available grades and the content lists do not match.

That distinction is not academic pedantry. A student on 0580 Extended sits a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of different lengths and mark totals. A student on 4MA1 Higher sits two papers of the same length with a calculator allowed throughout. A student on 0607 is expected to own and use a graphic display calculator, which changes how a whole family of questions is approached. A tutor who has spent years on one of those courses and is handed a student on another will be competent but imprecise, and imprecision in maths exam technique is exactly where marks go.

So the first useful thing a parent can do is get the codes. Email the examinations officer at your child's school and ask for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for mathematics. The reply takes a day and it changes every subsequent decision. It tells you which past papers to practise on, which formula sheet will be in front of your child in the hall, which grades are available on that tier, and which of the two annual series the school intends to enter.

The second useful thing is to test a prospective tutor rather than read their profile. Three or four specific questions, set out further down this page, will tell you within ten minutes whether somebody knows your child's course or knows mathematics in general. The questions are not trick ones. They are the sort of thing a teacher who marks the paper answers instantly and a well-meaning generalist has to hedge.

On delivery, we are direct about it because the search phrase implies otherwise. IB Gram does not send a maths tutor to a Marina address, and does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE. Lessons are one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The reason that works in your favour is simple: a child on 0607 with a graphic display calculator question does not need somebody nearby, they need somebody who teaches 0607, and dropping the travel radius is what makes that person reachable at 5pm on a Tuesday.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.programmesIntro: Mathematics at 14 to 16 in the schools serving this part of Dubai arrives in three shapes, plus one stretch option. Knowing which one your child is on tells you what the final two years contain and what the jump into Year 12 will look like.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The most widely entered maths course in British-curriculum schools in Dubai. Candidates are entered for either Core or Extended papers, and the current syllabus pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper at each tier. The grade range available differs by tier, which is the single most consequential fact about the entry. Confirm the paper combination for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org, since the structure was revised in recent syllabus versions.
programmes.countryNote: Around the Marina this is the default for schools running IGCSE at 16 before A Level. Where a school also offers the IB Diploma from Year 12, departments sometimes enter their stronger set for 0580 Extended plus Additional Mathematics 0606, because the calculus in 0606 is the best available bridge into Diploma Higher Level maths.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics (Specification A)
programmes.description: Tiered as Foundation and Higher, with two papers at each tier and a calculator permitted throughout. The grade scale is numeric. Pearson examines International GCSE in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so work from the live PDF.
programmes.countryNote: Several Marina-serving schools enter Pearson for mathematics while using Cambridge for the sciences, which is how a child ends up practising on the wrong board's papers for a term. If the code on the entry begins with a 4 and a letter pair, the past papers you want are on qualifications.pearson.com, not on the Cambridge site.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: A distinct course, not a variant of 0580, written with a graphic display calculator assumed throughout and with an emphasis on modelling and investigation rather than hand manipulation. It is chosen most often by schools whose sixth form is the IB Diploma, because the calculator culture and the style of question map onto Diploma mathematics more closely. Paper structure differs from 0580; check the current syllabus for your child's series.
programmes.countryNote: In the Marina cluster this course turns up in the IB-continuum schools in the Meadows and Emirates Hills rather than in the A Level schools. Tutors who have only taught 0580 often underestimate how different the questions feel, and a student moved between the two mid-course needs the difference taught explicitly rather than discovered in a mock.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: An extra qualification taken by a minority of strong candidates. It introduces differentiation, integration, trigonometric identities, logarithms and the factor theorem a year earlier than the main course, and it is examined on two papers with no tiering. It is demanding and it is optional, so it should be entered on evidence rather than ambition.
programmes.countryNote: For a Marina student heading into A Level Mathematics or Diploma Higher Level maths, this is the single most useful preparation available at 16, because the first term of Year 12 assumes exactly the calculus 0606 covers. For a student already stretched by Extended 0580, adding it is usually a mistake.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is examined as a set of strands, and marks leak from specific places inside them rather than from the subject in general. Below is each strand, what the Extended or Higher tier adds to it, and the failure that recurs most often in marked papers.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Standard form, surds, upper and lower bounds, percentage reverse problems and compound interest. The recurring loss is bounds: students round at an intermediate step and then cannot justify the final accuracy. Reverse percentage questions are the other reliable trap, because the instinct is to subtract rather than divide.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Factorising quadratics with a leading coefficient, algebraic fractions, rearranging formulae with the subject appearing twice, and simultaneous equations where one is non-linear. Nearly all lost marks here are method marks surrendered by working mentally and writing only the answer.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, transformations of curves, and reading gradients and intercepts from a sketch. Students who can solve equations algebraically frequently cannot describe what the solution means on the graph, which is where the explanation marks sit.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradient, midpoint, distance, and the equation of a straight line in more than one form. Parallel and perpendicular conditions are examined often and confused often. The questions are short and reliably winnable, which makes them the fastest place to recover a few marks before a series.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area and volume of compound solids, arcs and sectors, similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, and circle theorems. The scale-factor questions are the biggest single source of avoidable error, because students apply a length factor to an area or a volume.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled triangles, the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings, and three-dimensional problems. At Extended tier the graphs of sine and cosine and the solving of trigonometric equations in a given interval appear, and the second solution in the interval is the mark most often missed.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and the geometry of a vector proof. Transformation questions ask for a full description, and a description missing the centre of rotation or the invariant line scores partially. Vector proofs reward writing the route rather than stating the conclusion.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, conditional probability and the difference between with and without replacement. The reliable error is a tree diagram drawn without adjusting the second set of branches, and the second reliable error is adding where multiplication was needed.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency, box plots, averages from grouped data, and histograms with unequal class widths. Frequency density is the single most commonly dropped idea in the whole statistics strand, and it is also one of the quickest to fix in a session.

subjects.name: Problem-solving and multi-step questions
subjects.description: The longer questions that combine two or three strands and carry the top marks. Progress here depends less on content and more on a habit: writing down what is known, naming what is wanted, and choosing a route before calculating. It is coachable and it is rarely coached.

sections.heading: Which maths course is your child actually entered for?
paragraphs: Start here, because everything else depends on it. Ask the examinations officer at your child's school for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for mathematics, and you will get back something like '0580, Extended' or '4MA1, Higher'. That one line determines which past papers are the right ones, which formula list your child will have in the hall, how many papers they sit, whether a calculator is permitted throughout, and which grades are even available to them.

The table below compares the four courses commonly found in schools serving this part of Dubai. Treat the paper details as indicative and confirm them against the current syllabus for your child's series, because Cambridge has revised the 0580 paper structure in recent versions and a page restating an old structure would be worse than no page at all. The syllabus documents are free and public on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, which is where they should be read rather than from a summary.

What the comparison shows is that these are genuinely different examinations. The calculator rule alone changes how a student should practise: a course with a non-calculator paper demands arithmetic fluency that a course with a calculator throughout does not, and a student who has spent two years on one and is moved to the other will feel the difference in the first mock. Tiering changes the ceiling. And 0607 changes the style of question rather than only the content, which is the hardest difference for a tutor to fake.

sections.heading: The tier decision and the grade it caps
paragraphs: Tiering is the part of IGCSE mathematics that surprises families arriving from systems without it. In Cambridge 0580 a candidate is entered for Core or Extended; in Pearson 4MA1 for Foundation or Higher. Each tier has its own papers and its own range of available grades. A Core or Foundation entry does not merely make the exam easier, it removes the top grades from the table entirely, and the decision is taken by the school department, typically during Year 11 and typically on mock evidence.

The important nuance is that the higher tier is not always the right answer. A student entered for Extended who can access only the first two thirds of the paper may finish with a lower grade than the same student would have achieved on Core, where the questions sit inside their range and the time pressure is different. A department recommending Core is often reading the evidence accurately, and arguing them out of it on principle can cost a grade rather than win one.

Where tutoring genuinely shifts this is in the window before the decision, which means Year 10 and the autumn of Year 11. A gap in algebraic manipulation or in fractions is a foundational gap, it is fixable, and fixing it before the mock changes the evidence the department is reading. After entries close, the useful work changes shape entirely: it becomes maximising the grade inside the chosen tier, which is mostly paper technique, timing and the method marks that are given away by working mentally.

There is a practical question to ask at the first Year 11 parents' evening, and it is not 'can she be moved up'. It is: what specifically would need to improve for you to reconsider the tier, and by when. A maths department will answer that precisely, because they have the mark breakdown in front of them. The answer becomes the topic list for the next ten sessions.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1 for the same student
paragraphs: Families moving school mid-course, or comparing two schools before choosing, often want to know whether one board is harder. The useful answer is that they differ in shape rather than in difficulty, and the shape is what a tutor has to teach to. The comparison below sets out the practical differences a student feels in the exam hall.

The grading scale is the most visible difference. Pearson 4MA1 reports numerically and Cambridge 0580 reports in letters, which matters when a UAE school, a UK sixth form or the Ministry of Education equivalency process later reads the certificate. The Ministry's British-track requirement is expressed as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, so both scales are catered for. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel before relying on it for an application.

The second difference is calculator culture. A course with a dedicated non-calculator paper demands fluency in arithmetic and in surd and fraction manipulation that a calculator-throughout course does not reward in the same way. A student who transfers from 4MA1 to 0580 part-way through Year 11 frequently loses marks not on content but on arithmetic they have been allowed to outsource for two years. That is a teachable gap, and it needs to be identified rather than assumed.

The third is question style in the longer items. Both boards set multi-step problems at the top of the paper, but the phrasing conventions and the way working is credited differ enough that practising on the wrong board's papers produces false confidence. If there is one thing to get right before buying any tutoring, it is that the papers in front of your child carry the same code as the one on their entry.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that reveal whether a tutor knows your syllabus
paragraphs: A tutor's profile will tell you they teach IGCSE mathematics. It will not tell you whether they teach yours. These questions do, and they take about ten minutes on a trial call. They are not designed to catch anyone out; a teacher who marks the paper answers them without pausing, and that fluency is the thing you are buying.

Ask which tier the student should be entered for and why, given the last mock percentage. A tutor who knows the course will ask for the mark breakdown by question rather than the overall percentage, because the breakdown is what the decision rests on. Ask what the formula list provides and what has to be memorised; the answer is specific to the board and the code, and a vague answer here is informative. Ask where frequency density usually goes wrong, or what a full description of a rotation must contain. Then ask which paper carries the longer multi-step questions on your child's tier.

Finally, ask what the first three sessions would cover and why. The answer you want names strands and references the mock. The answer that should worry you is a promise to go through the syllabus from the beginning, because that is both the slowest route and the one that ignores the evidence already sitting in the mark breakdown. A tutor who begins by asking to see the marked paper has already told you most of what you need to know.

One more check belongs on the list, and it is about legality rather than competence. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount you see quoted. Asking the question is reasonable and a permitted tutor will not mind it.
bullets: Which tier, and what in the mark breakdown makes you say that?
What does the formula list give us, and what has to be learned?
Where do students on this code usually lose marks in statistics?
What would the first three sessions cover, and why those?
Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit?

sections.heading: The six places Extended and Higher maths marks actually go
paragraphs: Marked papers are repetitive. Across a Year 11 cohort the same handful of errors accounts for a large share of the gap between a predicted grade and an achieved one, and none of them is about intelligence. They are habits, and habits respond quickly to one-to-one attention because they can be named, demonstrated and then checked in the next piece of work.

The first is working mentally and writing only the answer, which forfeits method marks even when the answer is right and loses everything when it is wrong. The second is rounding at an intermediate step, which makes the final accuracy indefensible and is fatal in bounds questions. The third is scale factors: applying a length factor to an area or a volume in similar-shape problems. The fourth is frequency density, where a histogram with unequal class widths is treated as a bar chart. The fifth is trigonometric equations in an interval, where the second solution is simply not looked for. The sixth is the incomplete transformation description, missing a centre or an invariant line.

Every one of those is diagnosable from a marked paper in a few minutes, which is why the first session should be spent on your child's own script rather than on a generic diagnostic test. It is also why progress should be judged against the next marked paper rather than against how the sessions felt. A session that feels productive and does not change the error log has not worked, and that is worth knowing in week three rather than in week twelve.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs around the Marina, starting from the bottom
paragraphs: Begin at the cheapest end, because that is where most families begin and where the most money is wasted. EdFlik advertises tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. At that level you are generally buying a university student or a group class, and for a Year 9 child who needs homework supervision that can be perfectly sensible. For Extended or Higher tier mathematics in Year 11 it rarely is, because the skill you need is knowing which method marks the mark scheme awards, and that comes from marking papers rather than from having passed the exam.

The next band up is where most Year 11 maths support actually sits. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour, TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted higher again at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, with home tutors reaching AED 500, and BartyED quotes AED 650 at the named-examiner end. Those are each provider's own published figures recorded in October 2026; they are not IB Gram prices and they will move.

The spread between the bottom and the top of that range is roughly fifteenfold, which tells you that the rate on its own is almost useless as a quality signal. Two questions make it useful. Has this person taught this syllabus code at this tier, and can they say where marks go on it? And what does the rate include, specifically: marking of timed papers, a written session note, a replacement if the match fails? Those inclusions are worth more than twenty or thirty dirhams of hourly difference.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on these pages and none of the figures above is ours. The sensible route is a free trial lesson and then an honest conversation about how many sessions the situation needs, which for a well-diagnosed problem is often six to ten rather than a standing weekly commitment for a year. Ask whether any quote you receive includes VAT, since the published market figures are not consistent on that and the difference compounds across two academic years.

sections.heading: Why a tutor's postcode stopped being the useful filter
paragraphs: Searching for somebody nearby made sense when the lesson required a journey. A tutor driving from Mirdif to a Marina tower for a 5pm Tuesday slot either arrives late, prices the journey into the hour, or declines. So families filtered by distance, and accepted whichever maths tutor the filter returned. For a course split across two boards, two or three tiers and four syllabus codes, that filter is the reason so many children end up with a tutor who is good at maths and imprecise about their exam.

Drop the journey and the filter changes from distance to specification. The pool becomes everybody who teaches 0580 Extended and is free at 5pm on a Tuesday, rather than everybody free at 5pm within twenty minutes of your building. For 0607 or for Additional Mathematics 0606 that difference is stark, because those courses are taught in relatively few schools in the emirate and the local pool for them may be nobody at all.

It also changes the shape of what you can buy. A session with no drive attached can be thirty or forty-five minutes, which suits the week before a mock far better than a ninety-minute block does. Three short contacts in a week is a format a visiting tutor cannot offer economically and an online one can. For maths specifically, where the gain often comes from frequent short correction rather than long exposition, that is a real advantage rather than a consolation.

To restate the delivery position plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and will not send a tutor to a Marina address. Lessons are one to one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, and the in-home rates quoted earlier are market figures published by other providers, not an offer. Home visiting is a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: The jump from IGCSE maths into Year 12, and how to pay for it early
paragraphs: The most expensive maths problem a Marina family encounters is not IGCSE. It is the first term of Year 12, when a student who achieved a strong IGCSE grade meets A Level Mathematics or Diploma Analysis and Approaches and discovers that the algebraic fluency assumed on day one is higher than the fluency their IGCSE required. New content arrives weekly from that point, so there is no quiet period in which to catch up, and families end up buying significantly more support in Year 12 than they would have needed in the summer before it.

What closes the gap is narrower than a full course. It is algebraic manipulation at speed and without error, confident work with indices and surds, functions and their transformations, and, for a student who did not take 0606, an introduction to differentiation so the idea is familiar before it is examined. For a Diploma-bound student add graphic display calculator fluency, because Diploma mathematics assumes it and a student arriving from 0580 may never have used one in anger.

A short block across July and August does this. It is cheap relative to the Year 12 support it prevents, it has no competing deadlines, and it can be run fortnightly rather than weekly without losing its effect. Families who travel through the summer, which in this cluster is most of them, can keep it running across time zones because the lesson follows the laptop. The alternative is discovering the gap in an October test and buying remediation at the worst possible moment of the two-year course.

The route choice matters too and it should be made with the maths in view. A student heading for a quantitative degree needs the harder of the available routes rather than the one that protects the grade, because university prerequisites are read from the course title and not only from the mark. That is a conversation to have in Year 11, with the school, before the Year 12 options form is signed.

process.description: One full session at no cost, spent on a question your child recently got wrong rather than on introductions. The tutor finds out whether the loss was content, method, arithmetic or reading of the question, and you get that in writing. Those four causes need four different responses.

process.description: Three or four strands, drawn from the marked paper, with a stated review point. If six sessions is the honest answer rather than a year of weekly hours, that is what we will say. A plan with an end point is easier to judge than a subscription.

process.title: Re-cut the list after every mock
process.description: The error log and the next marked paper decide what changes. Strands that have stabilised come off the list; new ones go on. Where maths has become reliable, the sessions should stop or move to another subject rather than continue from habit.
