faqs.question: How do I know whether a maths tutor really knows my child's IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions on the trial call. Which tier would you enter this student for, and what in the mark breakdown makes you say that? What does the formula list provide and what has to be memorised on this code? Where do students on this specification usually lose marks in statistics? What would the first three sessions cover and why those? A teacher who marks the paper answers all four without pausing and asks to see the marked script. A generalist hedges, and offers to work through the syllabus from the beginning, which is both the slowest route and the one that ignores the evidence you already have.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 harder than Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: They differ in shape rather than in difficulty. Cambridge reports letter grades and tiers as Core and Extended; Pearson reports numeric grades and tiers as Foundation and Higher. The current Cambridge syllabus includes a non-calculator paper, while 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout, which changes how a student should practise. The longer multi-step questions follow different phrasing conventions on each board. The practical consequence is that a student must practise on papers carrying the same code as their entry, and a student transferring between boards mid-course usually needs arithmetic fluency rebuilt rather than content retaught.

faqs.question: What is Cambridge 0607 and why has nobody mentioned it to us?
faqs.answer: IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is a separate Cambridge course, not a variant of 0580. It assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and leans towards modelling and investigation rather than hand manipulation, which is why IB-continuum schools choose it: the style maps onto Diploma mathematics more closely than 0580 does. Around the Marina it appears in the schools whose sixth form is the IB Diploma rather than A Level. If your child is on 0607, a tutor who has only taught 0580 will be competent and slightly off-target, and the difference shows up in the calculator-led questions first.

faqs.question: Should my son take Additional Mathematics 0606 alongside 0580?
faqs.answer: Only on evidence. 0606 introduces differentiation, integration, logarithms and trigonometric identities a year early, and it is the best available preparation for A Level Mathematics or Diploma Higher Level, because the first term of Year 12 assumes exactly that content. For a student already stretched by Extended 0580 it adds a second demanding examination to the same series and usually costs marks in both. The useful test is whether 0580 Extended currently feels comfortable rather than survivable. Ask the department whether they would put him forward; they have the mark breakdown and they will answer directly.

faqs.question: My daughter is on Foundation tier. How much can tutoring change that?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on when you ask. The tier is set by the school department, usually in Year 11 and usually on mock evidence, and once entries close it is fixed. Before the decision, a foundational gap in algebraic manipulation or fractions is fixable, and fixing it changes the evidence the department reads. After entries close, the work changes to maximising the grade inside the chosen tier through technique and timing. Ask the department exactly what would need to improve for them to reconsider, and by when; that answer becomes the topic list for the next ten sessions.

faqs.question: Where do Extended tier students lose the most maths marks?
faqs.answer: Six places account for most of it. Working mentally and writing only the answer, which forfeits method marks. Rounding at an intermediate step, which makes the final accuracy indefensible and is fatal in bounds questions. Applying a length scale factor to an area or volume in similar-shape problems. Treating a histogram with unequal class widths as a bar chart, which is the frequency density error. Failing to look for the second solution to a trigonometric equation within the given interval. And an incomplete transformation description that omits a centre of rotation or an invariant line. All six are habits, and habits respond fast to one-to-one correction.

faqs.question: Can a maths tutor work with my child over video as well as in the room?
faqs.answer: For mathematics specifically, yes, and in one respect better. The tutor needs to watch the working appear line by line rather than read a finished answer, and a live shared whiteboard does that as well as sitting at the same table. It also leaves a saved record of every worked example your child can return to before a mock, which a paper notebook rarely delivers in a usable state. IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visiting is a service we run only in India, so nobody is sent to a Marina address.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay an hour for IGCSE maths help in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates span roughly fifteenfold. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is the university-student and group end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those figures are each provider's own, recorded in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price. Judge a quote on whether the person has taught your syllabus code at your tier, and on what the rate includes.

faqs.question: Is a cheap maths tutor a false economy for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Often, and for a specific reason. At the bottom of the market you are usually buying somebody who passed the exam rather than somebody who marks it, and the skill a Year 11 student needs is knowing which method marks the mark scheme awards and how the longer questions are credited. For a Year 9 child needing homework supervision the cheaper end is perfectly reasonable. For Extended or Higher tier in the final year it generally is not, because the sessions will cover content the student has already met rather than the technique that is costing them marks.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Year 11 student need?
faqs.answer: One is the right starting point for most students, with the hour aimed at a three or four strand list drawn from a marked paper. Two can be justified where the gap is large and the household can protect two slots. Beyond that the homework attached to each session stops being done, and the tutoring becomes a substitute for independent practice rather than a prompt for it. The lever that actually moves marks is specificity rather than volume: a shorter list, revisited, beats general revision. Re-cut the list after each mock instead of adding hours.

faqs.question: We are moving from a UK school mid-GCSE. Does the maths content match?
faqs.answer: Not exactly. A domestic GCSE specification and an international one share most content but not all of it, and the paper conventions differ. A child arriving in Year 11 may have been taught topics in a different order, or may not yet have met something the new specification examined in Year 10. The first hour of tutoring is best spent mapping what has and has not been covered against the specification your child will actually sit, rather than starting revision on an assumption. That mapping is unglamorous and it regularly saves several weeks later in the year.

faqs.question: Will my child's maths grade be enough for UAE Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: The Ministry's British-track requirement is expressed as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Both the letter and the numeric scales are therefore catered for. This is a description, not an application: equivalency is handled by the Ministry and not by any tutoring provider, and you should verify the current requirement on its own channel before relying on it.

faqs.question: Can we do maths sessions during the summer while we are travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the summer is the best window in the year for anything foundational, because no school deadlines compete for attention. A student who needs algebraic fluency rebuilt can realistically do it across July and August at a fortnightly cadence. Because the lesson follows the laptop rather than an address, a family moving between Dubai and another time zone can keep the slot by agreeing a time that works in both. The one thing summer does not suit is timed paper technique, which fades without the pressure of assessment and is better placed closer to the series.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer before Year 12 maths starts?
faqs.answer: Close the fluency gap rather than preview the course. A Level Mathematics and Diploma Analysis and Approaches both assume algebraic manipulation at a speed and accuracy that IGCSE does not require, and new content arrives weekly from the first week of term, so there is no quiet period in which to catch up. Target indices and surds, algebraic fractions, functions and transformations, and for a student who did not take 0606 an introduction to differentiation. For a Diploma-bound student, add graphic display calculator fluency. A short fortnightly block does it and is far cheaper than Year 12 remediation.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE maths tutor start for a Marina address?
faqs.answer: For 0580 or 4MA1 at either tier, usually within a few days, because those are the two most widely taught courses in the emirate and the evening slots are reasonably well covered. For 0607 International Mathematics or Additional Mathematics 0606 the pool of genuine specialists is smaller and the best available slot may be a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening. We say which situation applies before anything is booked, rather than filling the hour with a tutor who has not taught the code. Sending the syllabus code with your first message is what makes a fast match possible.

intro.heading: Two boards, four tier combinations, and the paper your child will actually sit
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics in Dubai is not a single qualification. The two boards used most widely here are Cambridge International, whose Mathematics syllabus is 0580 and which tiers into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel, whose International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1 and which tiers into Foundation and Higher. A family asking for a maths tutor is asking about one of four combinations, and they are not interchangeable in the examination room.

The content overlaps heavily, which is why the distinction gets waved away. The papers do not overlap. The number of papers differs, the time allocation differs, which paper permits a calculator differs, and the amount of formula support provided in the examination differs. A tutor who has spent three years on one board's past papers and is handed a candidate from the other will teach the mathematics competently and work from the wrong mark scheme, and the cost shows up in the final third of the paper where the marks are tightest.

Finding out takes a day. Email the school's examinations officer and ask for the board, syllabus code and tier for mathematics, or look at the front of any past paper your child has been given: the code is printed there. Then ask a prospective tutor which board and tier they teach and when they last taught it. A specialist answers with a number. A generalist says the content is much the same, which is true and is not an answer.

Dubai Media City makes the geography side of this question easy to resolve, because there is no local answer to find. It is a free zone of offices and studios in Al Sufouh between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, with residential towers and no school inside it. Children travel out to Al Barsha, Emirates Hills, The Greens or along the coast. The nearest tuition centres are inland. Nothing in that geography helps you match a syllabus code.

What does help is widening the pool. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm on school nights. For mathematics the medium is close to free: the work is a shared screen with a solution built line by line, and a past paper annotated live, which is how mathematics gets taught at a table anyway.

One more framing point before the detail. Most IGCSE mathematics marks are lost procedurally rather than through ignorance, and the repair is a habit rather than a syllabus. Unwritten working, misread command words, abandoned multi-step questions and a slow calculator all cost marks a student has already earned the knowledge for. That is good news, because habits change inside a term.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-media-c.subjectsIntro: These are the topic areas IGCSE mathematics requests from this corridor actually concern, with what each is examined on and where the marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, percentage change, ratio and proportion. Bounds questions are a reliable source of lost marks because students round at the wrong point or use the wrong bound for a division. The fix is a drilled procedure rather than a conceptual explanation.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Extended and Higher carry considerably more
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations including non-linear pairs. This is the single best predictor of whether the rest of the paper is accessible, and the area where students from lower tiers are slow rather than ignorant. Slowness costs marks by consuming time elsewhere in the paper.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and sequences
subjects.levels: All tiers; harder forms at Extended and Higher
subjects.description: Quadratics by factorising, formula and completing the square, inequalities on a number line and in regions, and nth-term work for linear, quadratic and geometric sequences. Students lose marks by giving one root where two exist and by not checking which root the context allows.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, reciprocal and exponential graphs, gradients and areas under graphs, transformations and inverse functions at the higher tiers. The usual loss is sketching from memory rather than from the function's features, which fails as soon as asymptotes or intercepts have to be justified.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, circle theorems, similarity and congruence. Circle theorems are reliably examined and reliably half-remembered: a student who can state the theorem still loses marks for not naming it as the reason in a geometric argument, which the mark scheme explicitly wants.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Right-angled at all tiers; the rest at Extended and Higher
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Students handle right-angled work confidently from earlier years and then lose marks on non-right-angled triangles and on multiple solutions within a given range, which is technique rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations with full descriptions. Marks go missing in the descriptions: a student performs a rotation correctly and then omits the centre or the direction, and the mark scheme requires both. This is cheap to fix with a checklist.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.levels: All tiers; tree and conditional work higher up
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and set notation, with conditional probability at the higher tiers. The common error is multiplying along the wrong branch or forgetting to account for events without replacement, both of which show up immediately in marked practice.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and scatter graphs. Histograms with unequal class widths are a dependable mark-loser because frequency density is skipped. Interpretation questions want a comparison in context rather than a restatement of a figure.

subjects.name: Problem-solving across topics
subjects.description: The multi-step questions at the end of the paper, which combine two or three topics and carry the most marks. Students abandon them early. Practising the first two lines of such questions, repeatedly, recovers more marks than any amount of additional topic revision, because the marks are front-loaded into setting the problem up.

subjects.name: Calculator and non-calculator technique
subjects.levels: Depends on the paper and the board
subjects.description: Which paper permits a calculator differs between boards and tiers, and so does the formula support provided. A student who has only ever practised with a calculator will lose marks on exact-value and surd work, and one who never uses it efficiently will run out of time. Both are mechanical problems with quick fixes.

sections.heading: Pin down the board and the tier before you shortlist anybody
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Media City is only useful once two facts are fixed: the board and the tier. Until then you are buying mathematics in the abstract. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 set different papers, use different tier names with different ceilings, differ on which paper allows a calculator, and differ on how much formula support appears in the examination.

Parents reasonably assume the school has communicated this. In practice it is usually in a letter from the previous year, and families with children at different schools, or in different subjects at the same school, end up with a mixed picture. The quickest route is an email to the examinations officer asking for the board, syllabus code and tier for mathematics. The second quickest is the front page of a past paper, where the code is printed.

Once you have it, the question to a prospective tutor becomes short and diagnostic. Which board do you teach this on, which tier, and when did you last teach it. A specialist answers with the code and the tier. A generalist tells you the content is largely the same across boards, which is true of the mathematics and false of the paper, and that distinction is exactly what you are paying for in Year 11.

Geography contributes nothing to this. Media City has no school in it, the nearest centres are inland in Al Barsha, and whether a tutor lives in Al Sufouh has no bearing on which mark scheme they know. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For mathematics that is a shared screen with the working built line by line, which loses nothing.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1
paragraphs: Both are respected, widely used in Dubai, and lead to the same sixth forms. The differences are structural and they matter in the room. The table below sets out the shape of each so you can see what a board-specific tutor is actually bringing, beyond knowing the topics.

The most consequential differences are tiering and formula support. Cambridge tiers 0580 into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade available; Pearson tiers 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher. The amount of formula support provided in the examination differs between boards, so a student trained to expect a formula sheet and sitting a paper without one loses marks in the first ten minutes through no fault of their understanding. Confirm the current arrangements for your child's syllabus version with the school, because these details are revised between versions.

There is also a difference in flavour that experienced teachers notice and students feel. Pearson papers tend to signpost multi-step questions slightly more explicitly; Cambridge Extended papers more often leave the student to decide which tool applies. Neither is harder in aggregate. They reward marginally different exam behaviour, and a tutor who has marked one board's papers for years has internalised that behaviour and can teach it.

Practically, this means the first four sessions with a board-matched tutor look different from the first four with a generalist. A matched tutor will put a real paper from the right specification in front of the student in session one and mark it against the right scheme. A generalist will teach topics, which is pleasant, slower, and less likely to change a grade in a single term.

sections.heading: The tier ceiling, and the evidence that should decide it
paragraphs: Tier is the most consequential decision in a British-curriculum Year 10 and it is frequently made on a single Year 9 assessment. The lower tiers cover less content and cap the grade; the higher tiers cover the full syllabus and leave the top grades available. Schools make the call to protect students from a paper they cannot access, which is legitimate, and the decision is reviewable if a parent brings evidence rather than an opinion.

The evidence that settles it is two papers from the same series, one at each tier, both sat under time. If the student is comfortable on the lower tier and falls apart in the second half of the higher one, the school is right. If they score moderately on both, the gap is a small number of specific topics, which is what a term of weekly work exists to close. This takes one weekend to find out and is more persuasive than any conversation about potential.

What the ceiling costs later is the part families underestimate. A Level Mathematics and both IB mathematics courses assume the higher-tier algebra, trigonometry and function content from the first week. A student arriving from Core or Foundation carries an algebra debt into Year 12, where the course does not pause to let them repay it. Closing that gap in Year 11, with the content fresh and the pressure lower, takes a short block; closing it in Year 12 takes a year and feels much worse.

The table sets out the shape of the decision. Exact content and grade arrangements depend on the syllabus version your child's centre has entered, so confirm the detail with the school rather than with this page.

sections.heading: Method marks: the single largest avoidable loss
paragraphs: Mark a set of IGCSE mathematics papers and the same losses appear regardless of tier or board. The largest is unwritten working. A student reaches a correct answer by a route the examiner cannot see, and the method marks are gone, which on a long question can be most of the marks available. The second largest is a misread command word, usually a student treating show that as the same instruction as find.

Show that is worth understanding properly because it is a gift and students treat it as a threat. The answer is already given, so the marks are entirely in the derivation, which means there is no ambiguity about what to write: every step, in order, to the stated result. Students who skip to the conclusion score nothing on a question they could have fully answered. The same logic applies to prove, justify and explain, each of which asks for a different quantity of words.

After those, the pattern is abandonment. Long multi-step questions at the end of the paper carry the most marks and are given up fastest, usually within two lines. But the marks are front-loaded into setting up the problem: writing the equation, labelling the diagram, stating the rule. A student who attempts the first two lines of every long question, even without finishing, collects a surprising number of marks that currently go uncollected.

None of this requires learning new mathematics, which is why it is the right place for a term of tutoring to start. A student who writes out method, reads command words deliberately and attempts the opening of every long question has recovered marks they already had the knowledge to earn. That shows up in a marked paper within four or five weeks, which is the honest test of whether the tutoring is working.

sections.heading: What a weekly maths hour costs here, and what a car would add
paragraphs: The published market gives a clear picture. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted from AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

For a single IGCSE mathematics subject, the qualified band is where most of the value sits. The premium band buys a reputation rather than a different mark scheme, and for a Year 11 student whose problem is unwritten working and abandoned long questions, a mid-tier tutor marking a real paper weekly does the job. The specialist band earns its keep where a grade sits on a hard sixth-form threshold, or where a student is attempting the higher tier from a weak base and needs the honest assessment as much as the teaching.

In-home visits are published between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour with travel included, and Bestimate's in-home band is AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For weekly paper practice, eight shorter contacts beat four long ones, and the four-visit package costs roughly double. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Those are other providers' published figures rather than IB Gram prices. What you can verify before paying is short and worth insisting on: the rate, whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether travel is inside the number, the cancellation terms and the remedy if the match is wrong. Three of the six strongest-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no rate at all, which is the reason a sourced table belongs on this page.

sections.heading: June, November and the arithmetic of a resit
paragraphs: Two dates govern the plan: the papers and the entry. The second is handled by the school months in advance and rarely announced, which is why a tier objection raised in March is usually too late to act on.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a Dubai candidate. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states in its exams officers' guide that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning from.

The resit arithmetic is worth doing early. If a June grade misses a sixth-form threshold, November is the recovery route, with results arriving in the new year. That means the decision window is August and September, when the student is also starting Year 12 or a new course. A November entry decided in August is a calm, six-week block; the same decision taken in October is a scramble, and every specialist is already booked. Plan the resit before you know whether you need it.

sections.heading: The algebra debt, and what IGCSE mathematics is really for
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics is a qualification and it is also a foundation, and the two purposes pull in different directions in the spring of Year 11. A student who crams procedures can pass well and still arrive in Year 12 unable to manipulate an expression at speed, which is the thing both A Level Mathematics and IB mathematics assume from the first week.

That debt has a predictable shape. It presents as slowness and small errors rather than as not knowing a topic. The student can factorise; they take four times as long as the course expects and make a sign error one time in three. In Year 12 that is fatal, not because the new content is hard but because the new content is built on top of the old at speed. By the second term they conclude they are bad at mathematics, which is the expensive part and also wrong.

The cheap intervention is in Year 10 and the summer before Year 12. Six to ten sessions spent purely on manipulation fluency, practised to speed rather than to understanding, closes most of it. Nobody buys this, because it does not feel urgent and there is no examination attached. The families who do are the ones whose children find Year 12 mathematics manageable, and the connection is rarely drawn because the intervention happened two years earlier.

If your child is heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, that is the single most useful thing to ask a tutor to do with the last term of Year 11 after the papers are done. It is also the least glamorous, which is why this page is the only place you will read it.

sections.heading: When the right tutor is not available
paragraphs: Mathematics is the easiest IGCSE subject to match in this corridor, with one exception: a weekday evening slot between 6pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time, in the spring, on a specific board and tier. That combination is the hardest booking in the UAE market, because every family in Al Sufouh and the Marina has worked out the same thing about the school run.

If no suitable specialist is free in the slot you want, you are told so, with the earliest realistic alternative, rather than matched to a tutor on the wrong board. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a request, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before you book. Two providers ranking for Dubai searches route parents to numbers in another country without disclosing it, which is a trust problem rather than an operational one.

There are two workarounds worth knowing. A weekend double frees the contested weekday evening entirely and suits households with heavy activity schedules, and for mathematics it works better than for essay subjects because the work is self-contained. The other is booking in September for the slot you will need in February, which sounds excessive and is simply how this market behaves.

If a match turns out wrong after the first paid session, you are matched again. No tutor can guarantee a grade in IGCSE mathematics, and anyone offering one is describing their marketing. The testable promises are narrower and more useful: a diagnosis from your child's own paper, a weekly hour that holds, marking against the real scheme, and a re-match if the fit is wrong.

Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 and tiers into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1 and tiers into Foundation and Higher. Once you have those three facts you can match a tutor to the specification rather than to the words maths tutor.

faqs.question: Do the two boards really differ enough to matter for maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: In Year 11, yes. The mathematics overlaps heavily, so any competent teacher covers the content. What differs is the paper structure, the tier names and ceilings, the calculator rules by component, how much formula support appears in the examination, and how explicitly long questions are staged. A tutor who has marked one board's papers for years has internalised that behaviour and teaches it; a generalist teaches topics, which is slower and less likely to move a grade in one term.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core maths. What does that cap?
faqs.answer: The Core and Foundation tiers cover a reduced subset of the syllabus and cap the grade available, which changes what counts as a good outcome and removes the point of revising material the paper cannot reward. The bigger cost is later: both A Level Mathematics and IB mathematics assume the higher-tier algebra, trigonometry and function content from the first week. If a sixth-form mathematics course is the plan, the tier conversation needs to happen in Year 10, with evidence.

faqs.question: How do I argue for a tier change with the school?
faqs.answer: With papers rather than opinions. Have your child sit one lower-tier and one higher-tier paper from the same series, both under time, over a single weekend. If they are comfortable on the lower tier and fall apart in the second half of the higher one, the school is right. If they score moderately on both, the gap is a handful of specific topics, which is exactly what a term of weekly work closes. Entries go in months ahead, so raise it early.

faqs.question: What is the single biggest reason IGCSE maths marks are lost?
faqs.answer: Working that is never written down. Marks are awarded for method as well as the answer, so a student who gets there by a route the examiner cannot see loses most of the marks on a long question even with a correct final figure. It is the largest avoidable loss at every tier and on both boards, and it is a habit rather than a topic, which means it changes within four or five marked papers rather than within a term of teaching.

faqs.question: What does a show that question actually want?
faqs.answer: Every step of the derivation, in order, ending at the result you have been given. Because the answer is printed in the question, all the marks are in the working, which makes it one of the most generous question types in the paper and one of the most commonly thrown away. Students read show that as a harder version of find and skip to the conclusion, scoring nothing on a question they could have answered fully. Prove, justify and explain each ask for different amounts of written reasoning.

faqs.question: Why does my child give up on the last questions on the paper?
faqs.answer: Because they look longer than they are, and because nobody has taught them that the marks are front-loaded. The multi-step questions at the end carry the most marks, and a large share of those marks are awarded for setting the problem up: writing the equation, labelling the diagram, naming the rule. A student who attempts the first two lines of every long question, even without finishing any of them, collects marks that are currently going uncollected week after week.

faqs.question: Should we practise with or without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Both, separately, and in the proportion your child's papers require. Which component permits a calculator differs by board and tier, so check the specification. A student who has only ever worked with a calculator loses marks on exact-value and surd questions, while one who never uses it efficiently runs out of time on the applied paper. Both are mechanical problems. Practising one paper by hand and one against the clock each fortnight fixes most of it.

faqs.question: Which maths topics most reliably lose marks at the higher tier?
faqs.answer: Upper and lower bounds, where students round at the wrong point; circle theorems, where the theorem is used but not named as the reason; histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density is skipped; transformations, where a correct rotation is described without the centre or direction; and non-right-angled trigonometry with multiple solutions in range. All five are procedural and all five respond to a checklist rather than to reteaching the concept.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting maths tutoring in Year 10 rather than Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest and most effective option available. Year 10 support builds manipulation speed before it becomes a constraint, allows a tier decision to be argued with evidence, and leaves room to treat past papers as practice rather than as a verdict. A student who starts in the spring of Year 11 has eight or nine usable weeks, which reliably improves technique and does not rebuild two years of algebra. Both are worth buying; they are different purchases.

faqs.question: How much should a weekly IGCSE maths hour cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Qualified subject tutors working online are published from AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, which is where most IGCSE mathematics work belongs. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and the premium band reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond. Monthly, Bestimate puts a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are published market figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Does an in-home maths tutor teach better than an online one?
faqs.answer: For mathematics specifically, there is very little in it, and the price difference is real. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor, and the premium is the drive rather than the teaching. The lesson itself is a shared screen with the working built line by line and a past paper annotated live, which is what happens at a kitchen table anyway. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai.

faqs.question: At what point in the year should a November maths resit be planned?
faqs.answer: In August, before results confirm whether you need one. November is the recovery series for both boards, with Pearson results reaching students in the new year, and the preparation is short and surgical because the previous attempt usually points at two or three topics plus a timing problem. A resit planned in August is a calm six-week block. The same decision taken in October is a scramble, and by then every specialist in the subject is already booked.

faqs.question: Can one tutor prepare my child for both IGCSE maths and the sixth form?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is worth asking directly, because the last term of Year 11 after the papers is the best window for it. Ask whether they also teach A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, and whether they would spend that term on manipulation fluency rather than new content. Six to ten sessions at that point prevents the slowness that makes Year 12 mathematics feel impossible, and almost nobody buys it because there is no examination attached to it.

faqs.question: What should I expect to see after four sessions?
faqs.answer: A timed paper, marked against the official scheme, comparable with the one from the first session. Specifically, you should see method written out where it previously was not, show-that questions attempted in full, and the opening of every long question attempted rather than skipped. If none of that has changed after four sessions, the honest reading is that the match or the diagnosis was wrong rather than that more hours are needed, and a re-match is the right response.

intro.heading: Two syllabuses, four tiers, and one of them has a grade ceiling
paragraphs: Before any tutoring question, a Production City family needs two pieces of information: which board their child is entered with, and which tier. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, and Core is capped at grade C. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher on a 9-1 scale. A student on the lower tier of either cannot reach the top grades however hard they work, and a surprising number of families discover this in Year 11.

Dubai Production City, which residents call IMPZ, has no secondary campus inside its boundary. Students travel to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha and Jebel Ali, and the schools they attend do not all use the same board. In a school entering candidates with both, the board can differ by subject, so a report card carrying 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades is not an error. It is two boards.

That matters more in mathematics than anywhere else, because the syllabuses diverge in content emphasis and the papers are structured differently. Revising from Cambridge past papers for a Pearson entry wastes a term. Practising the Extended content when the student is entered for Core wastes energy on material that will not appear. Both happen regularly, and both are avoidable with one email to the exams officer.

So this page is written at syllabus level. What each paper contains, where the mark schemes catch students topic by topic, what a tier decision actually costs, and what a serious past-paper programme looks like as opposed to simply doing more papers. These are things a parent can verify, which is more than can be said for most claims in this market.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. For mathematics the online format has a particular benefit: a shared digital whiteboard keeps every worked solution, so a student revising in the spring is reading their own tutor's working rather than reconstructing it from a notebook.

Everything here was reviewed in October 2026. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson runs May/June and November. Where a timetable is involved, read the board's own live PDF rather than any restatement, including this one.

One habit is worth stating before the detail begins, because it underlies most of what follows. In mathematics, marks are awarded for visible reasoning as well as for the right answer, and the mark scheme lists those method marks separately. A student who does the algebra mentally and writes only the result is giving away marks they had already earned, on every paper, in every tier, on both boards. Fixing that one habit usually recovers more than any topic revision, and it is where we start.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-product.programmesIntro: Three mathematics qualifications appear in this cluster at this stage, and they are frequently confused with one another. The distinction between a tier and a separate syllabus is the one that causes the most trouble.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Tiered Core and Extended. Core covers number, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry at a basic level, statistics and probability, with a grade ceiling of C. Extended adds functions, harder algebraic manipulation, more demanding trigonometry including the sine and cosine rules, vectors and transformations. Each tier is assessed by two written papers sat at the end of the course.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your Production City child's exams officer for the zone in writing before planning any revision schedule around published dates.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher, graded 9-1, assessed by two written papers per tier. Higher tier content includes algebraic fractions, functions and their inverses, calculus at an introductory level in some specifications, vectors and advanced trigonometry. Foundation tier has a grade ceiling in line with Pearson's published tier arrangements for the qualification.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables for sessions a year ahead and revises them, so plan against the live official PDF. Results dates matter for Dubai resit decisions: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate qualification rather than a tier, taken alongside 0580 Extended by a small and strong cohort. Content includes functions, the quadratic discriminant, simultaneous equations with non-linear terms, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, differentiation, integration and kinematics. It is the closest thing to A Level Mathematics available at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: The cohort sitting 0606 in any single Dubai community is small, which is why genuinely experienced 0606 tutors are scarce locally and why the subject is one of the clearest cases for online matching. A student taking it is usually heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics and benefits enormously from the head start.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-product.subjectsIntro: Topic by topic, where IGCSE mathematics marks actually disappear. These notes are drawn from marking student scripts rather than from a syllabus summary, and they apply across both boards unless stated.

subjects.name: Number: bounds and estimation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds produce more lost marks per question than any other number topic. Students round rather than bound, or take the upper bound of a denominator when calculating a maximum. The correction is mechanical and takes one session, and it reappears on both papers.

subjects.name: Algebra: manipulation and rearrangement
subjects.description: Changing the subject of a formula where the subject appears twice, and simplifying algebraic fractions. Marks go missing because students work in their heads and write only the result, forfeiting method marks the mark scheme awards separately from the answer.

subjects.name: Algebra: quadratics
subjects.description: Factorising, completing the square and the quadratic formula. The recurring loss is a student using the formula where the question clearly wanted completed square form for a minimum point, then having no way to answer the second part of the question at all.

subjects.name: Trigonometry: non-right-angled
subjects.description: Sine rule, cosine rule and area of a triangle. Two failures dominate: choosing the wrong rule because the given information was not labelled on a sketch, and the ambiguous case of the sine rule where two answers exist and only one is given.

subjects.name: Geometry: circle theorems
subjects.description: High-frequency and high-return. The marks are for naming the theorem used, not merely for the correct angle, so a student who reaches the right number without writing angle in the same segment loses reasoning marks that were available for free.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similarity
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Area and volume scale factors are the standard trap: students apply the length scale factor to a volume. Writing the ratio as a cube before substituting prevents it entirely, and it appears in some form on most papers.

subjects.name: Statistics: cumulative frequency and histograms
subjects.description: Frequency density is the single most misunderstood quantity in the qualification. Students plot frequency against unequal class widths and lose every mark on the question. Reading a median or interquartile range off a cumulative frequency curve needs the plot at the upper class boundary.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic is straightforward; describing a transformation fully is not. A rotation needs the angle, the direction and the centre, and an answer giving two of the three scores partially. Enlargement needs the scale factor and the centre.

subjects.name: Probability: tree and Venn diagrams
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Conditional probability without replacement is where the grade is decided at the top of the tier. Students reuse the original denominator on the second branch. Drawing the tree with denominators written in before any multiplication removes the error.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, compared properly
paragraphs: The two syllabuses running in Dubai British-curriculum schools are not interchangeable, and the differences go beyond the grading scale. Cambridge 0580 tiers into Core and Extended with Core capped at grade C. Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics A tiers into Foundation and Higher and reports on the 9-1 scale. Both assess by two written papers per tier, and both allow a calculator in line with their own published arrangements, which the school confirms.

Content emphasis differs in ways that change revision priorities. Cambridge Extended places weight on functions, transformations and vectors; Pearson Higher gives more attention to algebraic fractions, inverse and composite functions, and in some entry patterns introductory calculus. A student moving between schools mid-course, which happens often in this cluster, can meet a topic they have never been taught and miss one they have already mastered.

Grading creates confusion on a Dubai report card. A student holding 9-1 grades in two subjects and A*-G grades in three is not inconsistent; they are entered with two boards, which schools running both do routinely. Nobody volunteers this, so it is worth asking directly and getting the answer in writing.

The operational consequence is simple and strict. Revise with past papers from the board of entry only. A Cambridge paper is excellent practice for a Cambridge candidate and a misleading use of an afternoon for a Pearson one, because question phrasing, mark allocation patterns and the balance of topics all differ. The exams officer can confirm the entry in a single line, and that line should precede any revision plan a family pays for.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and what a ceiling actually costs
paragraphs: Cambridge 0580 Core is capped at grade C. That is the single most consequential fact in IGCSE mathematics and it is often explained to families late, vaguely, or not at all. A student on Core who works hard and performs at the very top of the tier still cannot be awarded a B, and if their sixth-form entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, the tier has already decided the outcome.

The decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and narrows every term afterwards. By the second term of Year 11 a move up is close to impossible, because Extended content the student never met has to be learned alongside revision of everything else. So the decision should be made early and on evidence: a timed paper from each tier, marked properly, with the scripts on the table.

There is a real case for the lower tier and we will make it when it applies. A student who is genuinely insecure on number and basic algebra will score more marks, more reliably, on Core than they will on Extended, and a secure C is worth more than a scattered E. The error is not choosing the lower tier; it is choosing it without knowing about the ceiling, or choosing the higher tier out of anxiety when the foundations are not there.

What usually makes the higher tier viable is not advanced work at all. It is fractions, negative numbers, index laws and rearrangement. Close those four and a student who looked incapable of Extended frequently turns out to have been missing Year 8 rather than Year 11, which is both the good news and the reason the decision needs evidence rather than impressions.

sections.heading: Where the mark schemes actually catch students
paragraphs: Marking student scripts rather than reading syllabus summaries produces a short, repetitive list. The same errors appear across both boards and both tiers, and most of them are notational or procedural rather than conceptual, which is why they are worth attacking first: they are quick to fix and they recur on every paper.

Method marks are the largest single loss. The mark scheme awards visible reasoning separately from the final answer, so a student who rearranges an equation mentally and writes only the result forfeits marks they genuinely earned. In a two-paper qualification, establishing the habit of writing the step is worth more than most topic revision, and it takes two or three sessions of deliberate practice to establish.

Then come the specific traps. Frequency density, where students plot raw frequency against unequal class widths and lose the whole question. Volume scale factors, where the length ratio is applied instead of its cube. The ambiguous case of the sine rule, where two answers exist and one is given. Circle theorems, where the reasoning mark requires naming the theorem rather than merely reaching the angle. Conditional probability without replacement, where the first denominator is reused on the second branch.

None of these is hard to teach. All of them are invisible in classwork, because a student doing an exercise on circle theorems knows which theorem the exercise is about. They only surface in a mixed paper under timing, which is exactly why past-paper work has to be timed and mixed rather than topic-by-topic all the way to the exam.
bullets: Method marks: write the step, or forfeit marks already earned mentally
Frequency density: plot density, never raw frequency, against unequal widths
Scale factors: cube the length ratio before substituting for a volume
Sine rule: check for the ambiguous case and give both solutions where asked
Circle theorems: name the theorem, because the reasoning mark is for the name
Conditional probability: write the denominators on the tree before multiplying

sections.heading: A past-paper programme that is more than doing papers
paragraphs: Most students do past papers, mark them against the answers, note the score and move on. That produces a plateau after three or four papers, which families then read as a ceiling on ability. It is not. It is a marking problem.

Marking against the published mark scheme rather than an answer key is the difference. A mark scheme shows which marks a specific script earned and which it missed: this line earned the method mark, this one did not, this answer needed the unit to score. That is diagnostic information. A score out of eighty is not. A student who finds that two thirds of their lost marks are method marks has a completely different problem from one whose losses cluster in statistics.

Sequence matters as well. Topic questions first, while the content is fresh from the school lesson. Then mixed sections under timing, because mixing is what reveals the traps that topic practice hides. Then full papers, late in the process, when the student can actually finish one. A full paper attempted in October mostly teaches a Year 11 student that they cannot yet sit a full paper.

We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. We work from papers your child or their school legitimately holds and reference the official source. Any provider offering a downloadable library of mark schemes is distributing material they do not own.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics 0606, and who should take it
paragraphs: Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics is a separate qualification rather than a tier of 0580, and it is routinely confused with one. It is taken alongside 0580 Extended by a small, strong cohort, usually in Year 11, and it covers functions, the quadratic discriminant, non-linear simultaneous equations, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, differentiation, integration and kinematics.

It is the best preparation available at sixteen for A Level Mathematics, and for a student heading towards engineering, physics, economics or mathematics itself, that head start is substantial. Students who have met differentiation at IGCSE arrive in Year 12 able to concentrate on the new abstraction rather than on the mechanics. Those who have not spend the first term catching up.

It is not for everybody, and the honest filter is 0580 Extended performance. A student who is comfortably scoring at the top of Extended will manage 0606 and benefit from it. A student who is working hard for a B on Extended will usually do better putting that time into securing the Extended grade, because 0606 is genuinely demanding and a poor grade in it helps nobody.

The practical difficulty in this cluster is supply. The 0606 cohort in any single Dubai community is small, so the number of local tutors who have actually taught it is small too, and the number free on a weekday evening in IMPZ is smaller again. It is one of the clearest cases in the whole subject for matching on expertise rather than geography.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Start with what the market actually charges, because almost nobody in this search publishes it. Three of the six main competitor pages in our research give no price at all and two quote US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below were read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 Dubai rate table, and they describe the market rather than our prices.

Budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online run roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200-450, with TutorChase quoting AED 270, and premium or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650 or more. In-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180-350, rising to AED 500 at specialist levels.

For IGCSE mathematics specifically, the band a family needs is narrower than the range suggests. A Core or Foundation student who needs procedural practice and somebody to check their working is well served at the lower end, and paying specialist rates for that is money wasted. A Higher or Extended student working on bounds, functions, the ambiguous case and conditional probability under timing needs mark-scheme fluency, which sits in the middle band rather than the premium one.

Context is useful. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. We publish no price list on these pages; we start with a free trial lesson and a conversation about which band the actual problem sits in.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the coursework boundary
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspections published on a six-band scale. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Individual tutors need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system. u.ae states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

Mathematics carries little assessed coursework at IGCSE, but the honesty boundary still applies to school-set tasks and investigations. A tutor teaches the skills, explains what the criteria reward, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete the work. We also do not reproduce board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes.

IB Gram is not KHDA approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence for training institutes with premises, and has no UAE office. Ask any provider calling itself approved which permit it means; the precise answer is informative.

The code and tier come from the exams officer in one email. The marked paper is worth more than a report card, because it shows whether the losses are method marks, specific topics or timing, and those three need different work.

Then take the free trial lesson, which is a real teaching hour on this week's sticking point rather than a consultation. You get a short written note afterwards on what the tutor found, in topic and mark-scheme terms. No card is held, nothing renews, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge.

On availability we give dates. Mainstream 0580 and 4MA1 matches are usually two to three days. 0606 Additional Mathematics is thinner and can run to a week or more, because the cohort is small and so is the pool of tutors who have taught it. If the specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book rather than afterwards.

Production City sessions usually land at 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time or later on weekdays, with weekend mornings better for full timed papers. process.title: Get the syllabus code and tier in writing
process.description: One email to the exams officer: board, syllabus code, tier and series for mathematics. Cambridge 0580 Core is capped at grade C and Pearson 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher on a 9-1 scale, so the answer changes both the revision material and what grade is achievable at all.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a grade
process.description: A marked script shows whether the losses are method marks, particular topics or running out of time. Those three need different plans and different numbers of hours. A report card shows only that something is wrong, which is the one thing you already knew before searching.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then decide
process.description: A real teaching hour on this week's sticking point, followed by a short written note on what the tutor found in topic and mark-scheme terms. No card held, nothing renews. If the match is wrong, say so and we rematch once at no charge.

process.title: Fix the habit before the content
process.description: In the first sessions we establish the habit of writing the method step, because the mark scheme awards visible reasoning separately from the answer. For most students this single change recovers more marks than any topic revision, and it applies to both papers in both tiers.

process.title: Move to mixed timed papers
process.description: Topic practice hides the traps, because a student doing circle theorem exercises knows the topic. Mixed questions under timing is what exposes frequency density, scale factors and the ambiguous case, and that is when the error log becomes genuinely useful.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different exams with different tiers, different grading and different content emphasis. We ask for the code before matching anybody, because a student revising from the wrong board's past papers is practising for an exam nobody is sitting.

whyPoints.title: The tier ceiling explained early
whyPoints.description: Core on 0580 is capped at grade C. Families are frequently told this late or not at all, and by the second term of Year 11 a move up is close to impossible. We make the decision on timed scripts from both tiers, and we will recommend the lower tier when the evidence supports it.

whyPoints.title: Marked against mark schemes
whyPoints.description: Work is marked point by point against the published mark scheme, not an answer key, so a student sees which marks their own script earned. A score out of eighty tells a family nothing diagnostic; a breakdown showing two thirds of losses are method marks tells them exactly what to do.

whyPoints.title: 0606 taught by people who have taught it
whyPoints.description: Additional Mathematics is a separate qualification with a small cohort, so local supply is thin and generalists often take it on. We match on actual 0606 experience and tell you honestly when the wait is a week, rather than filling the slot with somebody learning it alongside your child.

whyPoints.title: Honest about which band you need
whyPoints.description: A Core student needing procedural drill does not need a specialist at AED 200-450 an hour, and we say so. Budget tutors advertise from AED 45. Paying premium rates for practice that a cheaper tutor could supervise competently is the most common overspend in this market.

whyPoints.title: A saved archive of worked solutions
whyPoints.description: Online delivery keeps a shared whiteboard record of every solution, which matters in a cumulative subject. Spring revision starts from the student's own October working rather than from a textbook and a vague memory of how the method went.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge Core really capped at grade C?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended, and Core carries a grade ceiling of C. A student on Core who performs at the very top of the tier still cannot be awarded a B. If their sixth-form entry requirement is a B or a grade 6, the tier has effectively decided the outcome before any revision begins. This is the single most consequential fact in the subject and it is often explained to families late, vaguely or not at all, so ask the exams officer which tier your child is entered for.

faqs.question: Can my son still move from Core up to Extended in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Technically sometimes, practically rarely after the first term. Extended content he has never met would have to be learned alongside revision of everything else, which is a very hard year. The decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and narrows every term afterwards. If a move is being considered, ask the school for a timed Extended paper, have it marked properly, and decide from the script. What usually makes Extended viable is not advanced work but fractions, negative numbers, index laws and rearrangement.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits 0580 or 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Email the exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series, in writing. In a Dubai school entering candidates with both boards, mathematics can be on one and the sciences on another, which is why a report card can show 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades without anything being wrong. Nobody volunteers this information. It matters because question phrasing, mark allocation and topic balance all differ, so revising from the wrong board's past papers is a wasted term rather than a wasted afternoon.

faqs.question: What is the most common avoidable loss in IGCSE maths papers?
faqs.answer: Unwritten method. The mark scheme awards visible reasoning separately from the final answer, so a student who rearranges an equation in their head and writes only the result forfeits marks they genuinely earned. It is a habit rather than a knowledge problem, which means it can be established in two or three sessions of deliberate practice, and across two written papers it recovers more marks for most students than any single topic revision would. We attack it before content in almost every case.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose every mark on histogram questions?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly frequency density. Where class widths are unequal, the vertical axis must be frequency density, calculated as frequency divided by class width, not raw frequency. A student who plots frequency loses the entire question rather than part of it, which is why it looks catastrophic on a script. It is a ten-minute fix conceptually and then needs three or four questions of practice to become automatic. Reading a median or interquartile range from a cumulative frequency curve has a companion rule: plot at the upper class boundary.

faqs.question: What is the ambiguous case of the sine rule and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: When the sine rule is used to find an angle, there are often two valid answers in the range, because sine takes the same value at an angle and at its supplement. Students find one, write it down and lose the second mark. Whether both are required depends on the question and on any diagram given, which is exactly the judgement the mark scheme is testing. The habit to build is to check whether the obtuse solution is geometrically possible before committing, and to state both when the question allows them.

faqs.question: Is 0606 worth adding for a Production City student heading to A Level?
faqs.answer: Only if they are comfortably scoring at the top of 0580 Extended. 0606 is a separate qualification rather than a tier, covering functions, the discriminant, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, differentiation, integration and kinematics, and it is the strongest preparation for A Level Mathematics available at sixteen. For a student working hard for a B on Extended, the same hours are better spent securing that grade. Local tutoring supply for 0606 is genuinely thin because the cohort in any one Dubai community is small, so match on experience rather than proximity.

faqs.question: How should past papers actually be used?
faqs.answer: Marked against the published mark scheme rather than an answer key, under timing, and in the right order. Topic questions first while the school content is fresh, then mixed sections under time pressure, then full papers late in the process. Mixing is what exposes the traps that topic practice hides, because a student doing circle theorem exercises already knows the topic. Keep a categorised error log: a student who learns that two thirds of their losses are method marks has a completely different problem from one whose losses sit in statistics.

faqs.question: Will you send us Cambridge or Pearson past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Board past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are copyright material and we neither reproduce nor distribute them. We reference the official source, link to it, and work from papers your child or their school legitimately holds. Your child's mathematics teacher can supply past papers through the proper channel, and that is the route to use. Any provider offering a downloadable library of mark schemes is distributing material it does not own, which is worth noticing for what else it might be casual about.

faqs.question: Does my child need a different calculator for each board?
faqs.answer: Check with the school rather than assuming, because both boards publish their own permitted-calculator arrangements and schools apply them. What matters more in practice is fluency with whichever model your child actually uses: the difference between a student who can compute a standard deviation and a trigonometric value in degrees and radians without hesitation, and one who hunts through menus mid-paper, is minutes rather than marks in principle but marks in reality. We check device fluency explicitly in the first sessions, because it is invisible in classwork.

faqs.question: What does weekly maths tuition cost in Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market band for a qualified subject tutor online is roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45, with EdFlik at AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which is genuinely enough for Core or Foundation drill. Specialists sit at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Those figures were read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table and describe the market rather than our price list, which is why we start with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Do you send a maths tutor to our building in IMPZ?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For mathematics the online format has a specific advantage: the shared whiteboard keeps every worked solution, so spring revision starts from the student's own tutor's working rather than a half-remembered notebook page. Independent home tutors do work in this area at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, and for a younger child who needs a hand kept on the page they can genuinely be the better choice.

faqs.question: When can sessions start for a Year 11 student commuting out of Production City?
faqs.answer: Realistically from 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time on weekdays. With no secondary campus inside Dubai Production City, students bus to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Jebel Ali and are typically home between four and half past, needing food and a break before anything demanding. Dubai South and Emaar South families often need six o'clock or later. Weekend mornings are better for full timed papers, which need sustained concentration that a weekday evening after a long bus day rarely supports.

faqs.question: Which exam sittings are open to a Dubai IGCSE maths candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your exams officer which zone applies.

faqs.question: Are private maths tutors in Dubai required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. A MoHRE private tuition work permit is required, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system. u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so distrust any amount quoted to you.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-silicon.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 at both tiers for families around Dubai Silicon Oasis. For a week-by-week plan the useful tutor is one who asks how many weeks are left and what the last marked paper showed, before proposing any topic at all.

intro.heading: Turning the weeks you have left into a maths plan
paragraphs: Count the weeks before you count the money. A family arriving in the spring term with eight weeks until the June series has a different problem from one arriving in September with thirty, and the same tutor at the same rate will produce completely different outcomes in the two cases. Not because effort differs, but because mathematics divides into gaps that close in days and gaps that close in months, and eight weeks only contains the first kind.

The gaps that close quickly are procedural. Reverse percentages, which are the commonest single error in the subject at every tier and can be taught properly in under an hour. Similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, about two sessions. Cumulative frequency and histograms, two or three. Circle theorems, two. Balancing the use of the calculator against exact working, one. Each is a finite set of steps that a student either has or does not, and a short block installs it.

The gap that does not close quickly is algebraic fluency. Expanding, factorising, simplifying and rearranging appear in every paper and underpin the calculation marks in IGCSE physics and chemistry too. A student without it looks weak in trigonometry, in graphs, in mensuration and in probability, because the same deficiency surfaces in each of them wearing different clothes. Fluency is built by doing things several hundred times, and eight weeks does not contain several hundred times alongside eight other subjects.

So an honest eight-week plan names what it excludes. It picks the procedural gaps, fixes the technique faults, revises the topics that were never properly revised, and tells the student explicitly that the algebra work is not in scope for this window. Plans that quietly include an impossible goal produce a sense of failure rather than progress, and they are the plans that end with a family concluding tutoring does not work.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis and the surrounding communities, maths lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For a week-by-week schedule that matters practically: a session can move when a mock week shifts, the same working appears at the same size for both people, and a marked past paper can be walked through question by question with both pairs of eyes on the same marks.

The rest of this page is the schedule itself. Eight weeks topic by topic. The longer version for a term. The classification exercise that tells you which plan you need. The two series a UAE candidate sits. And the tier question, which is the one calendar fact that can quietly cap everything else.

One further note before the schedules. A plan with an honest exclusion list usually outperforms an ambitious one, because the student can see progress against the actual target rather than failing against an impossible one. Families who are told in week one that the algebra work is a Year 10 job, and that these eight weeks are about technique and two named topics, tend to finish the eight weeks having done exactly that. Families given a plan that promises everything tend to finish having done very little.
