dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-silicon.subjectsIntro: This grid is sorted by repair speed, because that is the only question an eight-week plan can answer. The top of the list is what a short window can genuinely close; the bottom needed a term that has already passed.

subjects.name: Reverse percentages
subjects.description: The commonest single error in the subject at every tier, and teachable properly in under an hour. Appears in every series, costs marks reliably, and nobody drills it deliberately. The first thing any eight-week plan should contain.

subjects.name: Similar shapes, area and volume scale factors
subjects.description: The topic students most often believe they understand and most often get wrong under time pressure, because the squared and cubed relationships are counter-intuitive. One explanation plus marked practice, about two sessions, and it holds.

subjects.name: Cumulative frequency and histograms
subjects.description: Procedural: reading a curve, locating quartiles, handling unequal class widths with frequency density. Two or three sessions of marked practice produces reliable marks, and it is one of the most predictable question types on either board's papers.

subjects.name: Circle theorems
subjects.description: A finite list of results with a recognisable question style, so the repair is memorisation plus pattern practice rather than conceptual work. Two sessions, and the reasoning marks for naming the theorem used are the part students most often forget to claim.

subjects.name: Trigonometry rule selection
subjects.description: Marks are lost by choosing the wrong rule rather than by arithmetic. A diagnosis of which situations trigger the sine rule, the cosine rule or basic right-angled work, then drilling, takes two or three sessions and holds across both papers.

subjects.name: Graph features that carry marks
subjects.description: Students sketch plausible curves and omit the intercepts, turning points and asymptotes that the mark scheme actually rewards. A technique fix rather than a content one, about two sessions, and it transfers to every graph question on the paper.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and indices
subjects.description: A classic higher-tier discriminator. Students either handle them fluently or avoid every question containing one. Four to six sessions because the procedures are finite, which places this at the edge of what an eight-week plan can absorb.

subjects.name: Timing and working conventions
subjects.description: Showing enough working for method marks, reading the command word, and not spending twelve minutes on a four-mark question. Pure technique, responds within two or three weeks of marked timed practice, and worth marks in every single paper.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying and rearranging. Not a topic but a capability, built by repetition over terms. The one item on this list that an eight-week plan cannot deliver, and the one most families are implicitly asking for when they call in March.

subjects.name: Problem-solving and multi-step questions
subjects.description: Questions that require assembling two or three techniques without being told which. Depends on fluency underneath, so it improves as a by-product of a term's work rather than as a target for a short block. Honest planning leaves it out of an eight-week window.

sections.heading: The eight-week schedule, week by week
paragraphs: Week one is diagnosis and nothing else. Take the most recent marked paper, classify every lost mark, and choose the two procedural topics that cost the most. Resist the urge to start teaching in week one: a plan built on instinct rather than evidence spends weeks three and four discovering that the real problem was elsewhere, and in an eight-week window there is no room for that.

Weeks two and three install the technique. Command word reading, working layout so that method marks can be awarded, and timing. These move faster than anything else on the list and they apply to every question on both papers, which is why they come before topic work rather than after it. A student who starts showing working properly in week two carries that benefit through every subsequent week.

Weeks four and six take the two procedural topics, with week five as a full timed paper between them. The timed paper is not a test, it is mid-plan evidence: if the technique work has landed, the error tally will show fewer timing and working losses even where topic marks are unchanged. If it has not landed, that is worth knowing at the halfway point rather than at the end.

Week seven is a second full paper under exam conditions and week eight is deliberately light, spent on the error tally rather than on new material. Students who revise at maximum intensity into the papers arrive depleted, and the marginal topic learned in the final days is worth less than the alertness it costs. The schedule below is the version to print and keep visible.

sections.heading: The classification exercise that chooses your plan
paragraphs: Before deciding between eight weeks, a term and two terms, do this with the last marked paper. Go through every lost mark and sort it into five categories: did not know the topic, knew it but the algebra collapsed, ran out of time, misread what the question asked, or knew it and wrote an answer that did not earn the marks. Then count the five. It takes under an hour and requires no mathematics from the parent.

The pattern tells you the plan. Losses concentrated in did-not-know means content revision, which is cheap and can often be supervised rather than taught. Losses concentrated in ran-out-of-time or misread means technique, which is the eight-week plan and moves fast. Losses concentrated in did-not-earn-the-marks means working layout, which is the quickest fix of all and frequently worth a grade boundary on its own.

Losses concentrated in the second category, where the student knew what to do and the algebra fell apart, is the finding that changes the plan. That is capability rather than content, it appears across every topic, and it needs terms rather than weeks. A family that identifies this in week one of an eight-week plan should rebuild the plan around what is achievable and start the fluency work anyway, accepting that its benefit lands later.

The reason this exercise matters so much is that all five patterns look identical on a report. A grade 5 in mathematics tells you nothing about which of the five it is, and neither does a parent's impression of how hard the student is trying. The marked paper does, it is free, it is already in the house, and almost nobody reads it this way.

sections.heading: The term version, and where fluency starts to move
paragraphs: A term is twelve to fourteen weeks, and the difference from eight is not more topics. It is repetition. Fluency in algebraic manipulation forms when a student performs the same operations often enough that they stop requiring conscious thought, and that threshold sits somewhere above a hundred repetitions for most students rather than above ten. A term contains that; eight weeks alongside eight other subjects does not.

The structure that works puts five minutes of algebraic drill at the start of every single session, regardless of what the session is about. Expanding, factorising, rearranging, indices, fractions. Not as a warm-up in the pleasant sense but as deliberate installation, marked, with errors classified as sign, index, fraction or method. The topic work then proceeds as in the eight-week plan, and the drill runs underneath it the whole way.

The second thing a term allows is a proper mid-point review. At week six or seven, a full timed paper gives a comparison against the week-one baseline, and the error tally should show the proportion of algebra-caused losses falling even if the topic losses are unchanged. If that proportion is not falling, the drill is not being done between sessions and the conversation to have is about homework rather than about teaching.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist, all read in October 2026. A term at the middle band is therefore a meaningful but bounded sum, and a family should be able to say at the start what the term is supposed to change and check at the end whether it did.

sections.heading: Anchor the plan to the mock, not to the examination
paragraphs: Schools along this corridor run mocks at different points, and the mock date rather than the examination date is the right anchor for a plan. A mock is marked, it is free, and it produces the evidence that the following block should be built on. A plan that aims at the June papers and ignores the mock throws away the only full-length diagnostic the student will get before the real thing.

Practically, that means two plans rather than one. The first runs up to the mock and is aimed at arriving ready for it, because a mock taken seriously produces better evidence than one treated as a rehearsal. The second runs from the mock to the series and is built entirely from the mock's error tally. Families who structure it this way describe the spring term as calmer, because the second plan is evidence-led rather than anxiety-led.

There is also a predicted-grade consequence. Sixth-form and foundation applications are generally made on predictions formed from classwork, internal assessments and mock papers, so a student who performs better in the mock gets a better prediction and a better set of options regardless of what June produces. Almost no family buys tuition for the mock, and the cost is identical to buying it later.

Ask the school for the mock dates in September. This costs nothing, takes one message, and it is the single most useful scheduling fact in the year. Everything in this page's schedules can then be positioned against a real date rather than an assumed one, which is the difference between a plan and a hope.

sections.heading: Which series, and when results arrive
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no student at a Dubai school sits it, and any plan built on a February entry deadline has imported another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. Take your dates from the school's exams officer or the board's live timetable, never from a tutoring page.

On results, Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those backward-looking dates are the ones worth knowing, because they tell you the shape of the year rather than a figure that will change.

The planning consequence is straightforward. A June candidate who falls short has a November route whose results arrive in January, early enough for most sixth-form and foundation conversations. Preparation for it is an eight to ten week block rather than a repeat of the year, since the content has been met. Hold the entry-fee reserve from the start, because entry fees go to the examination centre and not to a tutor.

sections.heading: The tier can cap everything the plan achieves
paragraphs: A schedule is only worth as much as the ceiling above it. On Cambridge 0580 a student is entered for Core or Extended, and on Pearson 4MA1 for Foundation or Higher. The lower route in each case does not reach the top grades, because the papers sat do not contain the marks required to cross those boundaries. An eight-week plan executed perfectly on a Core entry cannot produce a grade the entry does not allow.

The entry is decided by the school, usually during Year 10, from classwork and internal assessment. It is often correct. It is sometimes a reaction to one weak term or to absence during the unit the decision rested on, and those cases are reviewable, with the school, while there is still time. If a sixth-form course requires a grade above the current ceiling, this is the conversation to have before buying any schedule at all.

Schools respond to evidence rather than to conviction. A written assessment showing that a student handles Extended-level algebraic fractions and indices once an earlier gap is secure is something a head of department can act on; a parental belief that the child is capable is not. In Year 10 the useful purchase is therefore often the assessment itself rather than a term of lessons.

For a family already in Year 11 on a lower-tier entry, the honest plan changes shape. The target becomes securing the top of the range the entry allows, which is a real and worthwhile goal, and the sixth-form conversation becomes about alternative routes or a November entry at the other tier if the school supports it. That is less satisfying than pretending the ceiling is movable, and it is the version that helps.

sections.heading: Group or one-to-one, week by week
paragraphs: The schedules above divide differently between formats. Procedural weeks work perfectly well in a small group of two to four students, because everybody needs the same method demonstrated and then everybody practises it. Reverse percentages, cumulative frequency and circle theorems are group-friendly, and the cost per student falls without the teaching getting worse.

The classification week and the fluency drill do not divide. Classifying one student's marked paper is specific to that student, and catching algebraic errors as they happen requires attention that cannot be split three ways while others work at a different pace. Buying the group version of fluency work is the commonest false economy in IGCSE mathematics: it looks like tuition, costs less and changes nothing on the marked papers.

So the cheapest effective plan for many families along this corridor is a hybrid. One-to-one for week one and for the drill that runs underneath everything, group or supervised self-study with the school's past papers for the procedural practice. Families who split it this way consistently spend less across Years 10 and 11 than those who pick one format and apply it to everything.

Tuition centres sit outside this comparison and should be judged separately. A centre with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, up to six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That compliance position is checkable, which is a real advantage over an individual advertising on a community board.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks until the maths exam. What can a tutor realistically fix?
faqs.answer: Technique and two procedural topics. Working layout so method marks can be awarded, command-word reading and timing all move within two or three weeks and apply to every question on both papers. Then two finite topics chosen from the last marked paper, typically reverse percentages, similar shapes, cumulative frequency or circle theorems. What eight weeks cannot deliver is algebraic fluency, because that is built by repetition over terms, and an honest plan says so at the start.

faqs.question: How do we work out whether our Silicon Oasis child needs eight weeks or two terms?
faqs.answer: Classify the last marked paper. Sort every lost mark into five causes: did not know the topic, knew it but the algebra collapsed, ran out of time, misread the question, or knew it and wrote working too compressed to earn the marks. Count them. Losses concentrated in timing, misreading or working mean an eight-week plan. Losses concentrated in algebraic collapse mean two terms. All five look identical on a report, which is why the paper is the only reliable source.

faqs.question: Which maths topics are worth fixing first in a short window?
faqs.answer: Reverse percentages, because they are the commonest single error in the subject at every tier and can be taught properly in under an hour. Then similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, about two sessions, because the squared and cubed relationships are counter-intuitive and students believe they understand them. Then graph features, since students sketch plausible curves and omit the intercepts, turning points and asymptotes that the mark scheme actually rewards.

faqs.question: Should the plan be built around the mock or around the June papers?
faqs.answer: The mock, in effect two plans. The first runs up to the mock and aims at arriving ready for it, because a mock taken seriously produces better evidence than one treated as a rehearsal. The second is built entirely from the mock's error tally. Mocks also feed the predicted grades that sixth-form applications are generally made on, so performing better in the mock changes the options available regardless of what June eventually produces.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to Cedre Villas or Silicon Gardens for maths?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For a week-by-week schedule the online format has a practical advantage: sessions can be moved when a mock week shifts, the same working appears at the same size for both people, and a marked past paper can be walked through question by question with both pairs of eyes on the same marks rather than one person reading upside down.

faqs.question: Can my child's Core or Foundation tier still be changed?
faqs.answer: Realistically only in Year 10 and the very start of Year 11, and the decision belongs to the school. Core on Cambridge 0580 and Foundation on Pearson 4MA1 do not reach the top grades, because the papers sat do not contain the marks needed to cross those boundaries. Schools act on a written assessment showing the student handles higher-tier content, not on parental conviction, so in Year 10 the useful purchase is often the assessment itself.

faqs.question: What does a term of IGCSE maths tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour, read in October 2026, are roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist. A term at the middle band is therefore a meaningful but bounded sum. Our own terms follow the free trial lesson and the classification exercise, because the plan length depends entirely on what the marked paper shows.

faqs.question: Why is five minutes of algebra drill in every session so important?
faqs.answer: Because fluency forms through repetition rather than explanation. Expanding, factorising, rearranging, indices and fractions need to be performed often enough that they stop requiring conscious thought, and that threshold sits in the hundreds of repetitions for most students. A term plan that includes marked drill at the start of every session moves this; one that teaches algebra as a topic in week three and moves on does not, however well it is taught.

faqs.question: Which series does a Dubai Silicon Oasis maths candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series or the November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no Dubai student sits it, and any plan built on a February entry deadline has imported another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so take the actual timetable from the exams officer.

faqs.question: If June goes badly, how long does a November maths plan take?
faqs.answer: Eight to ten weeks, because the content has already been met and the work is the specific topics that failed plus the technique that cost marks. Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is early enough for most sixth-form and foundation conversations, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Entry fees go to the examination centre rather than to a tutor, so hold a reserve from the start of the year.

faqs.question: Is group tuition suitable for a week-by-week maths plan?
faqs.answer: For some weeks, yes. The procedural weeks work well in a group of two to four, because everybody needs the same method demonstrated and then everybody practises, and the cost per student falls without the teaching getting worse. The classification week and the algebraic drill do not divide, because catching one student's errors as they happen cannot be split three ways. A hybrid is usually the cheapest plan that actually changes the marked papers.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when the answer is right?
faqs.answer: Compressed working. A multi-step calculation written in two lines cannot be awarded method marks, because the method is not visible to the examiner. Students do this to save time and lose more than they save. Teaching a standard layout of formula, substitution, then answer with units takes about one session and pays back across both papers for the rest of the course. It is the fastest single fix available in the subject.

faqs.question: Will fixing maths help my child's physics and chemistry?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is the strongest argument for sequencing. The calculation marks in IGCSE physics and chemistry depend on rearranging formulae, handling indices and standard form, and manipulating units, all of which are mathematics doing science work. A student with weak algebraic fluency shows apparent weaknesses in several subjects that are really one weakness appearing in several places, so fixing it first can lift two other grades at no extra cost.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working in Dubai Silicon Oasis need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Since it is free, ask directly.

faqs.question: How will we know whether the eight-week plan worked?
faqs.answer: By comparing the week-five and week-seven timed papers rather than by impression. The error tally should show fewer losses caused by timing, misreading and compressed working, and the two chosen topics should no longer be costing marks. Those are checkable outcomes. A grade prediction is not, and no honest provider will give you one, so judge the plan on the tally and on whether your child arrives at the papers rested.

intro.heading: The comparison worth making, and the one families make instead
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai South comparing maths tutors usually compare locations. The Al Furjan listings look busier; Jebel Ali has longer-established provision; Dubai Investments Park has the schools. It is a reasonable instinct and in this case it answers the wrong question, because the variable that actually changes an IGCSE maths grade is not where the tutor lives. It is whether the tutor is working from the right syllabus and the right tier.

Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are separate qualifications. Cambridge runs Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings and, on the Extended route, sets Papers 2 and 4. Pearson runs Foundation and Higher tiering with two equally weighted calculator papers. The content overlaps heavily. The question styles, the tiering logic and the way a paper is structured do not. A tutor setting Cambridge past papers for a Pearson candidate is teaching the right mathematics in the wrong format for a whole term, and the student will discover it in the examination hall.

The second comparison families skip is the tier. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade available however well a candidate performs. That decision is usually made by the school in Year 10 on the strength of class performance, and it is reversible with evidence — a timed higher-tier paper marked against the official scheme — but only while there is time to produce the evidence. By the spring of Year 11 the ceiling is a fact rather than a choice, and the honest conversation becomes whether the November series with a revised entry is a better route than pushing at it in June.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with working written on a shared digital surface that persists from week to week. For mathematics that persistence earns its keep: an algebraic slip that appears in week three and again in week nine is visible on the record rather than remembered differently by two people.

One factual note before the comparisons begin. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the ratings, which are the best public document about any school in this cluster. KHDA does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Ask to see it, then ask which syllabus code they have taught. dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: Dubai South students meet IGCSE mathematics after Key Stage 3, or take Middle Years mathematics instead to the same age. Both lead onward to A Level or IB Diploma mathematics, and both leave characteristic gaps.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 mathematics
programmes.description: The three years in which algebraic fluency is either built or not. Nothing is externally examined, so a weakness in index laws, fractions, negative numbers or rearrangement passes unnoticed until the first IGCSE mock. By then two years of easy fix time have gone and the student is also meeting new content. Most Year 11 maths crises trace back to a Year 8 gap.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai South the Key Stage 3 years are also when the school settles which board a cohort will take and whether Additional Mathematics is offered. That varies between the Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park schools, and it is worth asking in Year 9 rather than discovering in Year 10 that a route was never available.

programmes.name: International GCSE mathematics
programmes.description: Two years, externally examined, with a tier decision that caps the achievable grade. Cambridge 0580 Extended sets Papers 2 and 4, both calculator-permitted; Pearson 4MA1 sets two equally weighted calculator papers. Grading runs 9 to 1 on Pearson and on reformed Cambridge subjects, with A*-G still in use on some. The formula list is supplied and most candidates never read it beforehand.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South candidates sit the June series with November as the resit route. Entry is made by the school as the examination centre, months before the papers. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable, so confirm the zone with the school.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: An extra Cambridge syllabus some schools offer alongside 0580, covering calculus, trigonometry and vectors beyond the main course. It is not a replacement and the overlap is smaller than students expect, so it needs its own slot in a revision timetable. For a student heading towards A Level mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches it is a genuine head start on hand algebra.
programmes.countryNote: Availability varies sharply between schools in this cluster, and the British-curriculum schools around Jebel Ali and Al Furjan are where most Additional Mathematics candidates in this corner of Dubai come from. A family whose school does not offer it is not disadvantaged, but will need a summer block before Diploma or A Level maths instead.

programmes.name: Middle Years mathematics
programmes.description: The IB route for the same age band, marked against four criteria from A to D on a 0-8 scale and converted to a 1-7 grade. Criterion C rewards communication and criterion D rewards application in real contexts, so a student can hold a strong grade while procedural fluency lags. There is usually no public examination, which changes the whole rhythm of the two years.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Dubai South run Middle Years mathematics rather than IGCSE, so two children of the same age in neighbouring villas face different assessment entirely. Families moving between the systems mid-secondary need the gap mapped in writing across a holiday, because the content overlaps while the assessment format does not.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The components and topics an IGCSE maths candidate in Dubai South actually needs work on, broken out by where marks go rather than listed as one subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Paper 2
subjects.description: The shorter Extended paper of structured short-answer questions, calculator-permitted. Marks leak on questions that say show your working, where a correct answer alone earns less than the available total, and on the accumulation of single-mark slips in arithmetic that a candidate would never make unhurried.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Paper 4
subjects.description: The longer Extended paper of multi-part structured questions building towards harder final parts. Transformations, bearings, vectors and the compound probability questions at the end are where the spread sits. Candidates who ration time badly lose the final question entirely, which is often the most accessible of the hard ones.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MA1 Papers 1 and 2
subjects.description: Two equally weighted calculator papers with a heavier emphasis on multi-step contextual problems than Cambridge uses. A student transferring mid-course stumbles on phrasing rather than content: the mathematics is familiar and the wrapper is not, and that is a four-session adjustment rather than a term.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, index laws, surds and algebraic fractions. Not a topic so much as the substrate everything else rests on. A student weak here appears weak in simultaneous equations, in functions and in the quadratic work, and treating those three separately wastes the term.

subjects.name: Ratio, proportion and percentage change
subjects.description: Reliably examined, reliably under-practised, and the single most common place a Higher or Extended candidate loses easy marks. Reverse percentage, compound interest and direct and inverse proportion all respond quickly to drill, which makes this a good early target in a short block.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: The sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, and three-dimensional work. Bearings questions fail on the diagram rather than the trigonometry: candidates who do not draw and label north lines reliably get the angle wrong. A deliberate habit of sketching first recovers marks across the whole topic.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and the geometric reasoning questions that ask for a route in terms of two given vectors. Transformations require the full description — type, centre, scale factor, direction — and an incomplete description scores part marks at best. Both are learnable procedures rather than insights.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and Venn notation. The errors are structural: unlabelled branches, failing to adjust for without replacement, and reading a Venn region incorrectly. Candidates who draw the diagram fully before calculating almost always outperform those who try to reason it out.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching quadratics and reciprocals, reading gradients and intersections, and the inverse and composite function work. Marks go on sketches with no intercepts marked and on reading a graph to insufficient precision. Graph questions are among the most reliably available marks on either board's papers.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Surface areas and volumes of compound solids, arc and sector work, and the area and volume scale factors for similar shapes. The scale-factor rules are short, examined often and forgotten reliably, which makes them a high-yield topic for a compressed revision block late in the course.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, further trigonometry, vectors and logarithms beyond 0580, taken alongside the main entry. It needs its own revision slot rather than being folded into maths, and it rewards a student intending A Level mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches with a real head start on hand algebra.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: Pearson's extension syllabus, the counterpart to Cambridge 0606, covering calculus, series and coordinate geometry beyond 4MA1. Offered by fewer schools in this cluster. Students who take it generally need less bridging work before A Level or Diploma mathematics than those who do not.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1: what actually differs
paragraphs: The comparison that decides whether a term of tutoring is useful. Both boards examine essentially the same mathematics at this level, so a tutor working from the wrong one will still be teaching true things. What they will not be doing is preparing the student for the paper they will sit, because the structures differ in ways that matter under time pressure.

Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier sets Paper 2, a shorter structured paper, and Paper 4, a longer paper of multi-part questions building to harder final parts. Both are calculator-permitted. Pearson 4MA1 sets two papers of equal weight, both calculator-permitted, with a noticeably heavier emphasis on multi-step contextual problems where the mathematics has to be extracted from a described situation before it can be done. A Cambridge-trained candidate meeting Pearson phrasing for the first time in an examination loses time on reading rather than on calculation.

Tiering differs too. Cambridge runs Core and Extended as separate syllabus content with different grade ceilings. Pearson runs Foundation and Higher with the Higher tier needed for the top grades. Cambridge supplies a formula list; so does Pearson, and both are routinely met for the first time in the hall. The table sets the differences out so a parent can check them against a child's timetable in a couple of minutes, which is the first action worth taking before any tutoring is booked.

One scheduling difference is worth noting alongside the papers. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Neither board offers a February or March series to UAE candidates; that one is for India only, and planning a revision block towards it wastes a term.

sections.heading: The tier ceiling, and the evidence that reopens it
paragraphs: A Core entry in Cambridge or a Foundation entry in Pearson caps the grade available. That is the single most consequential thing that happens to an IGCSE maths candidate and it usually happens quietly, in Year 10, on the strength of a term's class performance. A student capable of more who is entered at the lower tier cannot reach the top grades however hard the revision, and the revision will feel futile in a way nobody can quite explain.

Over-entry is a real risk in the other direction. A student placed on Extended who cannot handle multi-step algebra will sit papers designed for somebody else and may finish below where a confident Core performance would have landed them. So the decision is genuinely two-sided, and it should rest on evidence from timed papers at both tiers rather than on an impression formed in a classroom.

Producing that evidence is a specific, achievable task and the reason Year 10 tutoring is worth more than Year 11 tutoring per hour. A full higher-tier paper, sat under timed conditions and marked against the official scheme, is a document a subject lead can act on. An assertion that the child is capable is not. Families in this cluster who come to us in Year 10 get that conversation; families who come in the spring of Year 11 get a plan that works within a ceiling already set.

If the ceiling is discovered late, there is one question left worth asking. The November series exists as a resit route with a fresh entry, which means a student who hits a Core ceiling in June can be entered at Extended for November with an autumn term of properly aimed preparation behind them. That is often a better outcome than pushing at a ceiling in June, and the decision has to be made in the days after August results rather than the weeks.

sections.heading: What the next school along offers that yours might not
paragraphs: This is the comparison between neighbourhoods that is actually worth making, and it has nothing to do with tutor supply. Schools in this corner of Dubai differ in which board they enter, whether they offer Additional Mathematics, and whether they set early-entry options. Those differences are real, they affect what a student can reach, and most parents discover them when a neighbour mentions something their own school never offered.

Additional Mathematics is the clearest case. Cambridge 0606 is offered by some schools in the Jebel Ali and Al Furjan arc and not by others in the same few kilometres. A student who takes it meets calculus and further trigonometry a year earlier than their peers, which is a real advantage going into A Level mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches. A student whose school does not offer it is not disadvantaged permanently, but will need a summer bridging block that the other student does not.

The second difference is mock timing. Mock windows in the Dubai Investments Park cluster and in the Dubailand corridor differ by several weeks, which matters because the mock is the fixed point a revision block should be built around. A plan copied from a neighbour whose school mocks a month earlier is aimed at the wrong date. The third is tiering practice: some schools enter broadly at the higher tier and let performance sort itself out, others are conservative, and that institutional habit affects your child's ceiling more than their own ability does.

None of this is an argument for changing school. It is an argument for asking three specific questions of your own school rather than comparing buildings: which board, is the extension syllabus available, and when is the mock. Those three answers determine the shape of a maths plan more than any other information a parent can gather, and all three are available for the cost of one email.

sections.heading: Where Extended and Higher candidates lose marks
paragraphs: The losses are consistent across both boards and they are mostly technique rather than knowledge. The largest single one is algebraic manipulation: a candidate who hesitates over index laws, surds or algebraic fractions will appear weak in simultaneous equations, in functions and in the quadratic work, and treating those three as separate topics wastes most of a term. Fixing the substrate fixes all three at once.

The second is ratio, proportion and percentage change, which is examined reliably on both boards and practised far less than its mark value justifies. Reverse percentage questions in particular catch strong candidates, because the instinct to divide rather than multiply is hard to unlearn without drill. The third is the diagram subjects: bearings, vectors and transformations all fail on the drawing rather than the mathematics. A bearings question attempted without a labelled north line usually produces the wrong angle from correct trigonometry.

The fourth is time allocation on the long paper. Cambridge Paper 4 and Pearson's papers both build towards harder final parts, and candidates who ration badly lose the last question entirely. That last question is frequently more accessible than the one before it, so the loss is not of the hardest marks but of available ones. Measuring pacing requires a timed paper rather than untimed homework, which is why a diagnostic timed section belongs in the first fortnight of any block.

The fifth is the formula list. Both boards supply one, both are available before the examination, and most candidates meet theirs for the first time in the hall. Reading it in advance and annotating which formulas are there and which are not takes twenty minutes and prevents the specific failure of deriving something that was printed on page two.

sections.heading: IGCSE maths against Middle Years maths, for families with both
paragraphs: Households in this cluster regularly contain one child on IGCSE and another on the Middle Years Programme, sometimes in schools a few minutes apart. The two systems look similar from outside and reward opposite things, which makes comparing the two children's progress actively misleading. Worth understanding once rather than puzzled over repeatedly.

IGCSE mathematics is externally examined at the end of two years, and the grade is produced by performance on papers. Middle Years mathematics is marked against four criteria from A to D on a 0-8 scale, converted to a 1-7 grade, and there is usually no public examination. Criterion C rewards communicating mathematics and criterion D rewards applying it in real-life contexts, so a Middle Years student can hold a strong grade with presentation and investigation strength while procedural fluency lags behind.

That difference has a practical consequence at sixteen. An IGCSE Extended candidate arrives at A Level or Diploma mathematics with two years of timed paper practice and sometimes shaky conceptual depth. A Middle Years student arrives with good mathematical communication and often no experience of a timed paper at all. Both gaps are real and they are different gaps, which is why a transition block has to be written for the system the student came from rather than for the course they are entering.

For a parent the useful translation is this: a Middle Years 6 and an IGCSE grade 6 are not the same statement about a child. Comparing siblings across the two systems tells you nothing reliable. What does transfer is a specific diagnosis from a specific piece of work, which is the only comparison worth making between two children in the same house.

sections.heading: What comes after IGCSE maths, and how the choice is made
paragraphs: At sixteen a Dubai South student with an IGCSE maths grade faces a route decision: A Level mathematics, IB Diploma mathematics in one of two routes, or a programme where mathematics is not compulsory. The decision is usually framed around which the student prefers, and it should be framed around what the degree they want requires, because some requirements are specified by name and cannot be substituted later.

IB Diploma mathematics is compulsory within the Diploma and comes in two routes. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebra, calculus and proof with a non-calculator Paper 1, and some engineering, physics, mathematics and economics programmes specify it by name. Applications and Interpretation is built on statistics, modelling and finance with a calculator throughout, and is accepted widely but not universally. A Level mathematics is a single qualification with Further Mathematics available alongside it.

The IGCSE grade and tier feed directly into this. A Core or Foundation candidate may not satisfy the entry requirement for a sixth form's higher mathematics option, which is a second reason the tier decision matters beyond the grade itself. An Extended candidate with Additional Mathematics behind them has the widest set of options available at sixteen, and that is usually a decision made in Year 9 by a school rather than by a family.

There is also a UAE-specific process worth knowing about. Ministry of Education equivalency recognises a school-leaving certificate for use in the UAE, and for the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. The IB threshold is not published in any source this page can verify, so none is stated here. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency and tutoring is not required for it.

sections.heading: Comparing provider models on price, with sources
paragraphs: Since this page is built on comparison, the money deserves a comparison of models rather than a single band. The published figures in Dubai split cleanly by model, and the model explains the price better than quality does. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33-52 an hour on Tutopiya and AED 45-65 on EdFlik, usually delivered by university students or non-specialists. Agencies with qualified subject tutors publish higher: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

In-home provision sits apart. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour. UK-based agencies serving the Gulf publish higher again: TutorChase quotes AED 270. Premium named-tutor services reach AED 650 on BartyED. Monthly packages give the clearest view of the model difference: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours.

What that comparison shows is that the price ladder tracks delivery model and travel, not teaching quality in any measurable sense. A budget online hour and a specialist online hour cost very different amounts and the difference is who is teaching. An online specialist hour and an in-home specialist hour cost different amounts and the difference is largely the car. A parent choosing between models should be clear which of those two differences they are paying for.

Every figure above belongs to the provider named and is published by them. These are market bands rather than an IB Gram price list, and three of the most visible competitors in this market publish no price at all while two quote in US dollars, which no Dubai household transacts in. Our own commercial conversation starts with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis rather than with a rate card.

sections.heading: Online and in-home maths tuition in Dubai South, compared honestly
paragraphs: For IGCSE mathematics specifically the two formats are closer than they are for a niche Diploma subject, because 0580 and 4MA1 specialists are reasonably plentiful. A Dubai South family hiring in-home for core maths has a workable local pool. The same family hiring in-home for Additional Mathematics 0606 at short notice does not, and will end up with somebody who has not taught the extension syllabus.

Where online genuinely wins in mathematics is the record. Working written on a shared digital surface persists, so the algebra from week three is still there in week nine when the same slip reappears. That is not a convenience; it is what makes a technique fault diagnosable. Loose paper passed across a table does not survive the term, and a tutor relying on memory will treat a recurring error as a one-off.

Where in-home wins is a younger child who will not settle at a screen, and a parent's ability to observe from the next room without being in it. Both are real and both matter less for a Year 11 candidate working through marked past papers, where the material is two documents best read side by side. Scheduling favours online too: a visiting tutor fits one session an evening, so a household with two secondary children is choosing between them.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so there is nothing to soften in this comparison. The question for a Dubai South family is whether presence outweighs specialist matching, record-keeping and scheduling flexibility. For a seven-year-old it often does. For an IGCSE maths candidate eight weeks from a paper it usually does not, and the table sets out why in terms you can test against your own week.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and the tier
process.description: 0580 or 4MA1, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, plus whether Additional Mathematics is also being taken. Those facts set which past papers appear in session one. A request that says only maths costs a fortnight of the wrong practice, which a Year 11 plan cannot absorb.

process.title: Send the most recent marked paper
process.description: A mock or class paper with the marks on it distinguishes between five things that look identical from a grade: algebraic weakness, pacing, diagram habits, formula-list ignorance and command-word errors. Each needs different work. Also ask the school which paper and mark scheme were used, since an adapted mock changes the diagnosis.

process.title: Ask the school three questions
process.description: Which board and code, is Additional Mathematics available, and when is the mock window. Those three answers shape a maths plan more than anything else a parent can gather, and all three come back from one email. The Cambridge timetable zone is a useful fourth.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One full session at no charge and no card, taught by the person who would take the block. The output is a written diagnosis naming the technique faults in priority order and a proposal for the first four sessions. If the match is wrong we rematch rather than asking you to continue with it.

process.title: In Year 10, build towards a timed higher-tier paper
process.description: If the tier looks conservative, the goal of the term is a full higher-tier paper sat under conditions and marked against the official scheme. That is the document a subject lead can act on. An assertion of capability is not, and the window for producing evidence closes with the entry deadline.

process.title: Check at every fortnight boundary
process.description: Each fortnight ends with a timed section marked against the official scheme, which is the evidence a repair held. If it did not, the fortnight repeats instead of advancing. That decision is made by the checkpoint rather than by impression, which is the point of placing them in advance.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are separate syllabuses with different paper structures and different question styles. Matching on the code means correct past papers from session one. The commonest avoidable waste in IGCSE maths tutoring is a term of technically correct teaching aimed at the wrong paper format.

whyPoints.title: The neighbourhood comparison is replaced with a useful one
whyPoints.description: Dubai South, Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park draw on the same tutor pool once delivery is online. What genuinely differs between them is school maths provision: board, extension syllabus availability and mock timing. Those three questions are worth asking; tutor geography is not.

whyPoints.title: Tier evidence a school will actually act on
whyPoints.description: A full timed higher-tier paper marked against the official scheme is a document. A classroom impression is not. For a student placed conservatively in Year 10, producing that evidence is worth more than any amount of later revision, because the ceiling is set before revision begins.

whyPoints.title: Working that survives the term
whyPoints.description: Sessions are written on a shared digital surface that persists, so the same algebraic slip appearing in week three and week nine is visible on the record. That is what turns a vague sense that a student is careless into a specific, fixable fault, and loose paper cannot do it.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus does my child's school in Dubai South use?
faqs.answer: It varies between schools in this cluster and the only reliable source is your child's own timetable or report, where the code appears. 0580 is Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics and 4MA1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A. Cambridge also offers Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson offers Further Pure 4PM1 as extension syllabuses, taken alongside the main entry. There is no safe generalisation by neighbourhood: the British-curriculum schools around Al Furjan and Jebel Ali use both boards between them. Checking the code takes under a minute and determines which past papers are useful.

faqs.question: Should a Dubai South parent worry if the school uses 4MA1 rather than 0580?
faqs.answer: No. Neither board is harder in a way that shows up in grades; they are differently structured. Cambridge Extended sets a shorter structured paper and a longer multi-part one, both calculator-permitted. Pearson sets two equally weighted calculator papers with a heavier emphasis on multi-step contextual problems, where the mathematics has to be extracted from a described situation before it can be done. A candidate trained on one and examined on the other loses time on reading rather than calculation, which is why a tutor must work from the correct board from the first session.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Foundation to Higher tier in maths?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the lever is a document rather than a conversation. Schools reconsider an entry when a student sits a full higher-tier paper under timed conditions and the marked script supports the move. Class performance alone rarely shifts it. The practical route is a term of weekly work in Year 10 ending in that timed paper, then taking the script to the subject lead before the entry deadline passes. The decision matters because a lower-tier entry caps the achievable grade however well a candidate performs on the day.

faqs.question: Does Additional Mathematics 0606 matter for a Dubai South student?
faqs.answer: It matters most for what comes next. 0606 covers calculus, further trigonometry, vectors and logarithms beyond 0580, so a student who takes it arrives at A Level mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches having already met differentiation rather than meeting it in Year 12 alongside everything else. Availability differs between schools a few kilometres apart in this cluster, and the Jebel Ali and Al Furjan arc is where most candidates come from. If your school does not offer it, a summer bridging block closes the gap instead.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on questions they can do?
faqs.answer: Usually one of five specific habits. Not showing working where a question says to, so a correct answer earns less than the available marks. Rounding early, so a correct method yields a rejected answer. Attempting bearings or vectors without drawing and labelling a diagram. Misallocating time so the final question of a long paper is lost. And deriving a formula that was printed on the supplied list. All five are technique rather than knowledge, all five are visible on a marked script, and all five respond to about four sessions of targeted work.

faqs.question: What should a Year 10 maths plan in Dubai South aim at?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency first, and a timed higher-tier paper by the end of the term. Index laws, surds, algebraic fractions and rearrangement are the substrate under simultaneous equations, functions and quadratics, so fixing them treats three apparent weaknesses at once. The timed paper matters for a second reason: it is the evidence that reopens a tier decision while the entry deadline is still ahead. By the spring of Year 11 the ceiling is fixed and the same hours buy less, which is why Year 10 tutoring is the better value.

faqs.question: How does the supplied formula list change revision?
faqs.answer: It changes what needs memorising, and almost nobody uses it properly. Both Cambridge and Pearson supply a formula list in the examination, and most candidates meet theirs for the first time in the hall. Reading it weeks in advance and annotating which formulas are provided and which are not takes about twenty minutes, and it prevents two specific failures: spending examination time deriving something printed on page two, and assuming something is provided when it is not. It is the cheapest single revision action available.

faqs.question: My two children are on IGCSE and MYP maths. Can I compare them?
faqs.answer: Not usefully. IGCSE mathematics is externally examined and the grade reflects performance on papers. Middle Years mathematics is marked against four criteria from A to D on a 0-8 scale, with criterion C rewarding mathematical communication and criterion D rewarding application in real contexts, then converted to a 1-7 grade. A Middle Years 6 and an IGCSE grade 6 are different statements about a child. What does transfer between two children is a specific diagnosis from a specific marked piece of work, which is the only comparison worth making in one household.

faqs.question: Does a Core maths entry close off A Level or IB maths?
faqs.answer: It can, and that is a second reason the tier decision matters beyond the grade. Sixth forms set their own entry requirements for higher mathematics options, and a Core or Foundation grade may not satisfy them even when the grade itself looks respectable. The practical step is to get the sixth-form entry requirement in writing before accepting a tier, because it converts an abstract conversation about ceilings into a concrete one about a route the student may want. Ask in Year 10, not after results.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published bands split by provider model. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33-52 on Tutopiya and AED 45-65 on EdFlik. Agencies with qualified subject tutors publish higher, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. These are market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram prices; our own conversation starts with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a Dubai South address?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with working written on a shared digital surface that is saved from week to week. For mathematics that record is a real advantage, because a recurring algebraic slip becomes visible rather than remembered. Independent in-home tutors do operate in this part of Dubai if physical presence is the priority for your household.

faqs.question: When is it worth entering a November maths resit?
faqs.answer: When a June grade sits below what a sixth-form place or an equivalency requirement needs, and when the decision is made in the days after August results rather than in October. The entry goes through the school as the examination centre months before the November papers, and the autumn term is long enough for a properly aimed block if the decision is early. Preparation should start from the June script rather than from a blank revision plan, because the script says which topics and techniques cost the grade in the first place.

faqs.question: Should a tutor cover the topic the class is on this week?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and this surprises parents. Following the class turns a tutor into a second teacher of content the school is already delivering, and it means the gaps underneath never get touched. A better use of the hour is the substrate: the algebra, ratio and diagram habits that are quietly costing marks across every topic. The exception is the fortnight before a school assessment, where alignment is genuinely useful. Otherwise the session should be aimed by the marked script rather than by the timetable.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does an IGCSE candidate in Dubai South need?
faqs.answer: One a week through Year 10 and most of Year 11, rising to two for an eight-week repair block after a mock and three or four short ones in the final fortnight. The limit is how much independent practice a student finishes between sessions, not how much teaching they can sit through. Two long sessions a week in the final fortnight work less well than four short ones, because concentration rather than available time is what runs out at that stage of the year.

faqs.question: What time can maths sessions start in Dubai South on a school night?
faqs.answer: About 16:30 for most households here, since school runs ending in Dubai Investments Park put families home between 16:00 and 16:30. Green Community families can manage 16:00 because the school is minutes away, while Dubai Production City households driving to Motor City or Sports City are closer to 17:30. Mathematics immediately after a commute produces less than mathematics at 18:00 after a break and a meal, so the slot worth booking is the one your child can concentrate in rather than the earliest one free.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both IGCSE maths and Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and often the same specialist should, because the extension syllabus builds on the core one and a single tutor can see where a weakness in 0580 algebra is limiting 0606 calculus. What should not happen is folding both into one weekly hour. The overlap is smaller than students assume and calculus needs its own practice, so the sensible arrangement is two separate slots with the same tutor rather than one hour split in half and neither subject getting enough time.

intro.heading: Why a capable student scores in the middle
paragraphs: The most common maths enquiry from Dubai Sports City describes the same student. They follow the lesson. They finish the exercise. They explain the method back correctly when asked. Then the paper comes back at a grade nobody expected, and the family concludes the subject is suddenly too hard. Almost always it is not. The gap is between doing mathematics and writing mathematics in the form the mark scheme pays for.

At IGCSE that distinction is worth a great deal. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 both award method marks separately from answer marks, which means a correct final answer with nothing written down can score less than a wrong answer with full working. Students who have learned to compute mentally or on a calculator, and who were praised for speed in earlier years, arrive at Year 10 with a habit that systematically costs them marks they have earned.

The second large category is accuracy discipline. An intermediate value rounded early and carried forward produces a final answer outside the accepted range, and the accuracy mark goes even though the method was right. A unit omitted costs its own mark. A probability given as a decimal when the question asked for a fraction can cost one. None of these is difficult; all of them are invisible to a student who has never read a mark scheme.

The third is topic selection within the paper. Extended papers contain questions nearly every candidate can attempt and questions most will not finish, and a student who works strictly front to back can run out of time before reaching marks they could have taken. That is a strategy problem, solved by sitting whole papers to time rather than by learning more mathematics.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For mathematics specifically the shared screen is an advantage rather than a compromise: the tutor reads the working as it is written, in the right orientation, and stops the student at the line where the method broke rather than after the answer.

Matching to the code also matters more in maths than families expect. 0580 and 4MA1 cover similar ground and ask for it differently, the tiering structures are not identical, and the formula provision differs. A tutor who has taught one and not the other will teach correct mathematics against unfamiliar question shapes, and in a mock report that reads as the student's problem.

What follows is the subject itself: the topic weighting as it behaves on real papers, what Core entry caps and what the Extended content adds, why algebra is effectively the whole course, the statistics marks almost nobody drills, and how many sessions a block realistically needs depending on where the student is starting from.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubai-sports-.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is one subject with a handful of distinct demands. Each entry below names what the topic asks for on a real paper and where the mark scheme refuses to pay.

subjects.name: Algebra and algebraic fractions
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, solving linear and quadratic equations, simultaneous equations and simplifying algebraic fractions. Extended adds harder factorising and manipulation. Nothing else in the paper is independent of this, which is why a weakness here reads as a weakness everywhere.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, sketching and transformations, and reading solutions from graphs. Marks are lost to notation rather than to understanding, particularly in composite functions written in the wrong order.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional problems. The three-dimensional questions are routinely skipped, which hands over marks that are often more accessible than the ones students chase instead.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, similarity and circle theorems. Circle theorems reward naming the theorem used; answers that reach the right angle without a reason lose the explanation mark.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds and limits of accuracy. Bounds questions are a reliable source of lost marks because students compute with rounded values instead of with the upper and lower limits the question defines.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Averages from tables and grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and box plots. Histogram frequency density is the single most commonly dropped technique on the paper, and it takes one session.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and conditional probability at Extended. Tree diagrams are high-yield and mechanical; the errors are almost always in not reducing the denominator for without-replacement cases.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry and describing transformations fully. Descriptions lose marks for incompleteness — a rotation without a centre, an enlargement without a scale factor and centre — rather than for being wrong.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, equations of straight lines, parallel and perpendicular conditions. Reliable marks, usually answered well, and worth securing early because they are a predictable component of every paper.

subjects.name: Calculus (0606 only)
subjects.description: Differentiation including the chain, product and quotient rules, stationary points, and integration with applications. Notation discipline is assessed in practice as well as in principle, and students arriving straight from 0580 are usually unaware of that.

sections.heading: What the 0580 and 4MA1 papers ask for
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Sports City should be able to tell you, before teaching anything, which paper the student is sitting and what that paper rewards. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 both examine the subject across written papers at the end of the course, both award method and accuracy marks separately, and both publish a content list that doubles as the only revision checklist a student needs. IB Gram teaches this live online, one to one; no tutor visits a UAE address, and home visiting runs only in India.

The structural difference families should establish is the tier. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended with different papers and a different grade range available. Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher. The school makes the entry, usually during Year 10, and after the entry deadline it is fixed for that series. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however the revision goes.

The content difference between tiers is narrower than parents expect and the demand difference is wider. Extended adds topics — harder algebraic manipulation, functions, vectors, conditional probability — but it also asks the shared topics in less scaffolded ways. A question that gives a formula at Core may expect it to be recalled and rearranged at Extended, and that is where a student with shaky algebra loses ground even on familiar material.

Formula provision is the last thing to check and the easiest to get wrong. What is given on the paper, what has to be recalled, and what is given only at one tier all come from the current specification, which the board publishes and revises between cohorts. Teaching from a memory of how the paper used to look is a real failure mode, and it is why a code-matched tutor matters more than a generically strong mathematician.

sections.heading: Topic by topic: where the Extended marks actually live
paragraphs: Revision is usually organised by the order of the textbook, which bears little relation to where the marks are. A more useful organisation is by how reliably each topic appears, how accessible its marks are, and how often students drop them. Done that way, the picture is consistent across cohorts in Dubai and gives a clear order of work for an eight-week block.

The highest-yield group is the one students assume they have already secured: number and accuracy, coordinate geometry, and basic statistics. These appear every series, the questions vary little, and the marks are lost to carelessness rather than to difficulty. Securing them properly is quick and makes the rest of the paper feel calmer, which has an effect of its own on a nervous candidate.

The middle group is algebra and trigonometry, which carry the largest share of demand and the widest mark spread. This is where a block spends most of its time, and where improvement is slowest but most durable. The low group is not low in value but low in accessibility: vectors, conditional probability and the harder function work, which are worth attempting only once the first two groups are secure.

It is written so a parent can hold it against a marked paper and see immediately which group their child is losing marks in, because the group decides the block. A student dropping marks in the first group needs weeks of care; one dropping marks only in the third is close to the top of the paper already.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the ceiling and the real difference
paragraphs: The tier decision is the one with the longest shadow, and it is usually made without the family in the room. Where a Cambridge syllabus is tiered, Core and Extended sit on different papers and Core caps the grades available. The entry is made by the school, generally in Year 10, from attainment to that date, and it holds for the series once entries close.

Pushing every student up a tier is not the answer. A candidate on Extended who cannot handle the algebraic demand loses more marks on harder papers than the raised ceiling gains them, and sitting a paper they cannot attempt does real damage in the final weeks. The decision is a genuine judgement, and it deserves evidence: the student's Year 10 mark profile, and specifically their performance on algebra under non-calculator conditions.

Where the gap is closable, the move is a targeted block in the first half of Year 11 followed by a conversation with the department. Where it is not, the honest recommendation is Core with a clear plan for mathematics at 16, which may mean a different post-16 route rather than a lesser one. Pretending otherwise sets a student up for a series they cannot sit well.

sections.heading: Algebra is effectively the whole subject
paragraphs: If a single sentence had to carry this page, it would be that IGCSE mathematics is algebra wearing different hats. Trigonometry is algebra with triangles. Mensuration is algebra with shapes. Statistics is algebra with tables. A student who cannot rearrange a formula reliably will fail to finish questions in six different topics, and from the outside that looks like six separate weaknesses.

This is why an honest diagnostic starts with manipulation under non-calculator conditions, whatever the paper's calculator rules happen to be. Rearrangement, expanding brackets with negative terms, factorising, solving quadratics, simplifying fractions. Twenty minutes of that tells a tutor more than a term of classroom observation, and it is the single assessment a parent can meaningfully interpret themselves: either the student does it fluently or they do not.

Rebuilding fluency is slow and it does not respond to long sessions. Little and often works: ten minutes of written drill four times a week beats an hour once. That is also why a rebuild is a term or two of work rather than an eight-week block, and why it is cheapest to do in Year 10 or earlier rather than in the months before the series.

The payoff is disproportionate, because every topic sitting on top of algebra becomes accessible at once. Families often report that a student who spent a term on manipulation suddenly improved in physics and chemistry as well, which is not a coincidence: both subjects assume rearrangement and both penalise its absence in exactly the same way.

sections.heading: The statistics and probability marks nobody drills
paragraphs: There is a cluster of techniques on the IGCSE maths paper that are mechanical, reliably examined, and routinely dropped. Histograms with unequal class intervals, where frequency density has to be calculated rather than read. Cumulative frequency and the quartiles taken from it. Tree diagrams for without-replacement problems, where the denominator changes on the second branch. Averages from grouped data using midpoints.

None of these requires insight. Each has a fixed procedure, each appears with little variation across years, and each takes a single session to install properly. Together they are worth a meaningful number of marks on every paper. Students drop them because revision time goes to the topics that feel hard, and these do not feel hard — they feel done, until the paper asks for frequency density and the class widths are not equal.

The diagnosis is easy to make at home. Find a histogram question with unequal intervals in a past paper and ask the student to do it. If they plot frequency instead of frequency density, that is a mark loss that will repeat in every series until someone fixes it. The same test works for without-replacement tree diagrams: ask whether the second branch denominator changes, and listen to how confidently the answer comes.

This cluster is the best argument for the topic-and-scheme drill format. Pull every histogram question from five years, do them consecutively, mark them against the official scheme, and the pattern becomes obvious to the student rather than being asserted by the tutor. Twenty minutes of that is worth more than an hour of explanation, and it is the kind of work a shared screen handles well.

sections.heading: How many sessions, by where the student is starting
paragraphs: The question every family asks is how many sessions it will take, and the honest answer depends on the starting point rather than on the target. A student who understands the content and loses marks mechanically needs a short block. A student with absent algebra needs a term. Treating those as the same request is how both get the wrong plan.

The published rates in this market sit behind whatever that block costs. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 once travel is counted. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with local packages advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Every one of those is a provider-published figure read in October 2026; none is IB Gram's price list, and the figures appear here because most pages ranking for this search publish none at all.

Read against the starting point, the arithmetic argues for acting early. A four-session block in Year 10 on written-method discipline costs a fraction of a two-term rebuild in Year 11 and prevents some of the need for it. The most expensive version of this is the one families fall into most often: an unmeasured weekly hour across two years, at mid-band rates, with no stated target and no review.
