sections.heading: 0606 and the step at sixteen
paragraphs: Cambridge Additional Mathematics sits alongside 0580 for students heading towards A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, and it is the best available preparation for the jump at 16. It covers calculus, functions, series and trigonometric identities at a level close to AS, which means a student arriving in Year 12 having passed it has already met most of the first term's content once.

It is also where a comfortable 0580 Extended student and a struggling one separate visibly. The content is new, but the thing that trips students is notation: writing a derivative correctly, using function notation consistently, setting out an integration with its limits. These conventions are assessed in practice, they are rarely taught explicitly, and a student who has only ever written mathematics informally finds marks disappearing for reasons nobody has explained.

The other common difficulty is the chain rule and its companions. Differentiating a composite function requires identifying the inner and outer functions before anything else, and students who skip that identification get the right shape of answer with the wrong factor. Six sessions on notation plus composite differentiation resolves most early 0606 enquiries from this part of Dubai.

For families weighing whether to take it at all, the test is current algebraic performance rather than enthusiasm. A student fluent in manipulation will find 0606 demanding and doable. A student who is not will add a subject that makes the rest of the timetable harder without reaching the grade that would justify it. That judgement can be made from one marked 0580 paper and twenty minutes of non-calculator algebra.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and what is not claimed
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Year 11 student the practical effect is that the examined subjects are not the whole timetable, so revision plans built from the entry sheet overstate the hours available.

Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified.

IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval or accreditation and claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. No grade, mark or admission outcome is promised. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are referenced and linked to their official sources rather than reproduced, because reproducing board material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, worse.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and a marked paper
process.description: 'Cambridge 0580 Extended, Year 11, last mock 5' is answerable. 'Needs maths help' is not. The code is on the subject information sheet and every past paper, and the marked paper shows whether the losses are mechanical or content-based, which decides the whole plan.

process.title: Twenty minutes of non-calculator algebra
process.description: The trial session includes a short manipulation assessment, because algebraic fluency predicts performance across six topics at once. It is the one diagnostic a parent can interpret without help: either the rearranging happens fluently or it does not, and everything else follows from that.

process.title: Order the work by accessibility
process.description: High-accessibility marks first — number, coordinate geometry, histograms, tree diagrams — then algebra and trigonometry, then the Extended-only topics last. Securing easy marks early changes how a nervous candidate approaches the paper, which is worth more than it sounds.

process.title: Weekly written work, self-marked
process.description: Questions are set from five years of past papers and marked by the student against the official scheme during the session, with every withheld mark named. Errors are logged by category so a repeated habit becomes visible rather than being re-explained each week.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target from session one is measured in writing. In mathematics that comparison is clean: the same paper type, the same time limit, the same scheme. If nothing has moved, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes, and making that call at week four saves a month.

whyPoints.title: Code and tier matched before teaching
whyPoints.description: 0580 Extended, 0580 Core, 4MA1 Higher and 0606 are four different preparations. Formula provision, scaffolding and question shape differ, and a tutor working from a memory of how the paper used to look will teach correct mathematics against an unfamiliar paper.

whyPoints.title: Algebra treated as the whole subject
whyPoints.description: Six apparently separate weaknesses are usually one weakness in manipulation. Diagnosing with twenty minutes of non-calculator algebra, then rebuilding with short frequent drills rather than long sessions, is slower than topic teaching and the only thing that changes a student's ceiling.

whyPoints.title: The dropped mechanical marks taken first
whyPoints.description: Histogram frequency density, without-replacement tree diagrams, quartiles from cumulative frequency, grouped-data midpoints. Each is a fixed procedure, each appears nearly every series, and each takes one session. Revision time goes elsewhere because these feel done rather than hard.

whyPoints.title: Students mark their own work
whyPoints.description: The student marks against the official scheme while the tutor asks why each mark was awarded or withheld. That teaches the examiner's logic and transfers to papers nobody has marked. Being marked silently by an adult teaches the score, which is why heavily marked students often plateau.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation held in time
whyPoints.description: Core entry caps the grade however the revision goes, and the entry is usually made in Year 10 without much discussion. A diagnostic against the Extended content list shows whether the gap is weeks or years, which is the only thing that makes that conversation productive.

whyPoints.title: Delivery, rates and limits all stated
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live, one-to-one and online in Gulf Standard Time; no tutor is sent to a UAE address and home visiting runs only in India. Every AED figure names its source and date, no accreditation is claimed, and no grade is promised at any price.

faqs.question: Why does my child get the right answer in IGCSE maths and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded separately from answer marks. A correct final answer with nothing written down can score less than a wrong answer with full working, since the method marks were never available. Add early rounding, which loses the accuracy mark on a carried value, and omitted units, which cost their own mark. Count how many of the lost marks on your child's last paper are mechanical rather than knowledge-based; for most Year 11 students in this belt the mechanical count is the larger one.

faqs.question: Which maths code is my child entered for, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Look at the top of a past paper or at the school's subject information sheet. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Additional Mathematics is 0606; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. It matters because formula provision, the amount of scaffolding in questions and the tiering structure differ between them. A tutor matched to the right code teaches against the paper the student will actually sit rather than one with similar content.

faqs.question: Is a Core entry in 0580 worth challenging?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence, and only before entries close. Core caps the grades available however well the student performs, so if they intend to continue mathematics at 16 the ceiling matters. The useful evidence is a diagnostic against the Extended content list plus twenty minutes of non-calculator algebra, which shows whether the gap is weeks of work or years of foundations. Take that to the department before the entry deadline; afterwards the tier is fixed for the series.

faqs.question: What single topic gives back the most marks fastest?
faqs.answer: Histograms with unequal class intervals, where frequency density has to be calculated rather than read off. It appears with little variation across years, it has a fixed procedure, and a large share of candidates plot frequency instead. One session usually fixes it permanently. Close behind are without-replacement tree diagrams, where the second branch denominator changes, and quartiles taken from a cumulative frequency curve. All three are mechanical and all three are routinely skipped in revision.

faqs.question: How do I test my child's algebra myself?
faqs.answer: Give them twenty minutes of non-calculator work: rearrange three formulae for a different variable, expand two brackets with negative terms, factorise two quadratics, and simplify one algebraic fraction. Watch rather than mark. Fluent students do it with little hesitation; students who pause at every sign change are the ones whose difficulties in trigonometry, mensuration and statistics all trace back here. It is the one diagnostic a parent can interpret without any specialist knowledge.

faqs.question: Does little and often really work better for maths than long sessions?
faqs.answer: For manipulation, yes. Ten minutes of written drill four times a week builds fluency better than a single hour, because what is being trained is recall speed and accuracy rather than understanding. Long sessions suit different work: whole papers to time, or a topic worked through five years of past questions in one sitting. A block that mixes both — short drills between sessions, longer paper work inside them — covers each purpose properly.

faqs.question: My child runs out of time on the Extended papers. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: Whole papers sat to time, with question order treated as a decision rather than a default. Extended papers contain questions almost everyone can attempt and questions most will not finish, so working strictly front to back costs reachable marks at the end. Six sessions of timed papers, marked immediately, with an explicit rule about how long to spend before moving on, is the standard fix. More teaching does not address it at all.

faqs.question: Should a Sports City student take 0606 Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: If they are heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, it is the best available preparation: calculus, functions, series and trigonometric identities at a level close to AS. If 0580 Extended is already hard, it adds load without a clear return. The honest test is current algebraic fluency rather than interest, and that can be judged from one marked 0580 paper plus a short non-calculator assessment. Early 0606 difficulty is usually notation and the chain rule rather than content.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an IGCSE maths block usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the starting point rather than the target. Content secure with mechanical losses: four to six sessions. Content secure but running out of time: about six sessions of timed papers. One or two genuinely absent topics: around eight sessions of topic drill. Algebra not fluent: one to two terms of short frequent work, which is the only version that changes the ceiling. Anyone quoting a session count before seeing a marked paper is guessing.

faqs.question: Can online lessons really teach written mathematics properly?
faqs.answer: For mathematics the shared screen is arguably better than a table. The tutor reads the working as it is written, the right way up, and can stop the student at the line where the method broke rather than after the final answer. Sessions can be reviewed when the same error recurs a fortnight later. What a screen cannot do is supervise unaided practice, which is why short written drills between sessions are set rather than hoped for.

faqs.question: Do circle theorem questions need the theorem written down?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Many circle theorem questions carry a mark for the reason as well as for the angle, so reaching the correct value without naming the theorem used loses part of the credit. The fix is procedural: write the theorem name beside the working every time, even when the answer feels obvious. Students resist it because it feels slow, and it is one of the cheapest mark recoveries available in the geometry section of either board's paper.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tuition cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the university-student end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, to AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour sessions are AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more by tier.

faqs.question: Will improving maths help my child's physics and chemistry?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is not a coincidence. Both subjects assume fluent rearrangement and both penalise its absence the same way: a student who cannot make a quantity the subject of a formula will stall partway through calculations in all three subjects. Families who spend a term on manipulation often report improvement in science marks they were not targeting. It is the strongest argument for treating algebra as the foundation block rather than as one topic among many.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start maths tutoring in the spring of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the plan has to change. At that range the work is triage: secure the high-accessibility marks, drill the mechanical procedures, sit whole papers to time, and make explicit decisions about content that will not be revisited. What does not work is starting at the beginning of the content list and hoping to arrive at the end before the series. Expect visible movement on technique and little change on genuinely absent foundations.

intro.heading: Paying for IGCSE maths in Dubailand: what the money should buy
paragraphs: Mathematics is the best-supplied tutoring subject in Dubai, which cuts both ways for a family in Arabian Ranches or Motor City. Choice is wide and rates are competitive, and the abundance makes it easy to buy a great deal of teaching that does not touch the thing costing marks. The published hourly spread runs from AED 45 at the bottom to AED 650 at the top, and a parent with no map of what sits in between is choosing more or less at random.

The first thing worth paying for is information, and it is free. Email the school's examinations officer and ask for the syllabus code and the tier. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different specifications. Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C; Pearson tiers into Foundation and Higher on a 9 to 1 scale. Material built for one is partly useful for the other and the revision plans are not interchangeable. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole competing area-page cluster researched for this project, which tells you how rarely anyone asks.

The second thing worth paying for is a diagnosis. Maths marks go missing in a small number of identifiable places: unshown method, mishandled algebraic fractions and indices, trigonometry with the wrong solution range, probability and tree-diagram structure, and timing on the longer multi-step questions. Each of those is a block of work with a beginning and an end. Priced as a block of six or eight sessions, it is a defined purchase. Priced as a monthly retainer with no endpoint, it becomes an indefinite subscription, and that is the shape most tutoring spend takes in this belt.

The third thing worth paying for is the right band for the stage. A university student at AED 50 an hour drilling times tables and index laws with a Year 8 in Mudon is sound value. The same person preparing a Year 11 for an Extended paper eight weeks out is not, because the work at that point is board-specific technique. Bestimate's monthly Dubai estimates frame the choice: AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support.

IB Gram's part in this is stated plainly. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so no part of the fee is paying for a car crossing Al Qudra Road. Home visits are a service we operate only in India; nobody is sent to a Dubailand address. The trial lesson is a full session, free, and requires no card, and it is used as a diagnostic rather than an introduction. A parent should finish it knowing which topic block is costing the marks and roughly how many sessions closing it would take. Everything below is the detail needed to interrogate any quote, this one included.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: Maths tuition is best bought by topic block, because each block has an identifiable failure and a finite amount of work attached. These are the blocks Dubailand students most often need, and what each one typically takes.

subjects.name: Indices, surds and standard form
subjects.description: Negative and fractional indices are the foundation most later topics rest on, and a gap here resurfaces in algebra, graphs and growth problems. Short to fix and expensive to ignore: usually three or four sessions of drilled practice rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and fractions
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying algebraic fractions and rearranging formulae. This is where Extended papers separate candidates, and where the marks lost are procedural rather than conceptual. Responds to volume of short timed practice.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous systems
subjects.description: Including quadratics by factorising, formula and completing the square at the higher tiers. Students lose marks by abandoning a method halfway rather than by choosing the wrong one, which is a confidence problem with a technical fix.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients and interpreting graphs in context. The recurring loss is a sketch without the intercepts and asymptotes the markscheme wants. Four to six sessions typically moves this block substantially.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and Pythagoras
subjects.description: Right-angled work at every tier, with sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional problems at the higher tiers. Marks go missing on solution ranges and on diagrams that are never drawn. A self-contained block of roughly five sessions.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Area, volume, arcs, sectors and the area and volume scale factors for similar figures. The scale-factor questions are reliably among the worst answered on the paper and among the quickest to fix, which makes this unusually good value as a block.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.description: Conditional probability and structured tree work. Students who understand the ideas still lose marks by not drawing the diagram, because the diagram is where the method marks live. Two or three sessions is often enough.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.levels: All tiers, heavier at higher tiers
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals. Histograms with unequal class widths are a standard trap and an easy block to close. Interpretation sentences are where the final marks sit.

subjects.name: Paper technique and timing
subjects.description: Question triage, method-mark discipline, and knowing when to abandon a question and return to it. This is not a topic and cannot be revised; it is drilled on timed papers of the correct board, and it is the block that most often moves a grade in the final weeks.

sections.heading: 0580 or 4MA1: the free question that changes what you are buying
paragraphs: Before any money changes hands, establish the code. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics is 4MA1, and they are not interchangeable. The paper structures differ, the tiering works differently, the grading scales differ, and Pearson offers a modular route in some subjects that Cambridge does not offer at all. A tutor who begins planning without the code is planning for an average student rather than yours.

Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended, with the tier decided at entry by the school. Core papers lead to grades C to G and Extended papers to A* to E. Pearson 4MA1 uses a 9 to 1 scale with Foundation and Higher tiers. The practical effect is that the word Higher means something different on each board, and a parent comparing two tutors' claims about experience with higher-tier maths may be comparing experience of two different papers.

Getting this wrong has a measurable cost. A term of weekly sessions at the mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour aimed at the wrong specification is a real sum spent on partially relevant practice. The preventive measure is one email, and it should ask three things: which board, which syllabus code, which tier. Ask also whether the entry is final, because that answer determines whether a tier conversation is still possible.

sections.heading: The tier decision is the most expensive thing on this page
paragraphs: A Cambridge Core entry in mathematics cannot produce a grade above C. Once entries are submitted, no quantity of tuition changes that. A family paying AED 600 to 1,200 a month against a ceiling that already sits below the grade they need is buying nothing, and it is the single largest waste of money this market produces. It is also entirely preventable.

The tier is chosen by the school, usually on internal assessment evidence, and the principle behind it is sound: a student should sit the paper where they can demonstrate what they know. The difficulty is timing. The decision is often made in Year 10 on a limited sample of work, and entries close months before the papers. A family who notices in the spring of Year 11 that the ceiling is wrong has missed the window.

This is where a short diagnostic is the best-value purchase available. Three to five sessions against the actual specification produces a written assessment of whether the higher tier is realistically reachable and what closing the gap would take in weeks. That document is more persuasive in a conversation with a head of department than a parent's conviction, and sometimes it says the opposite: an honest Core entry with a strong grade beats an Extended entry producing an E, and the money is then better spent elsewhere.

For Pearson candidates there is an additional lever. Where a subject permits the modular route, units can be sat across more than one series with the better result carried forward, which converts one high-stakes paper into two lower-stakes ones. Whether a particular centre enters modularly is a question for the examinations officer, because it is a centre decision rather than a published default.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks go, and which hours actually recover them
paragraphs: Maths is the easiest subject to diagnose because the losses are visible on marked paper. A tutor who has seen one past paper with the mark breakdown can usually name the problem before the first session, and a tutor who has not seen one is offering general revision because it is the only plan available without evidence. General revision is also the most expensive product in this market, because it bills by the month and converts slowly.

The pattern repeats across both boards. Method not shown, which forfeits the marks a markscheme awards for intermediate steps. Algebraic fractions and index laws, which underpin later topics and resurface everywhere. Trigonometric solution ranges, where a correct calculation produces an incomplete answer. Probability questions attempted without a tree diagram, which is where the method marks live. Histograms with unequal class widths, a standard and reliably mishandled item. And timing on the longer multi-step questions, which is not a topic and cannot be revised, only drilled.

Each of those is a block with a finite amount of work attached, which is why block pricing is more honest than monthly pricing for maths specifically. Scale-factor questions on similar shapes, for instance, are among the worst answered on a typical paper and among the quickest to close, often inside two or three sessions. A family that spends AED 1,000 on exactly that block gets more movement than one that spends AED 4,000 on general coverage across a term.

The honest caveat is that some gaps are not blocks. A student who never secured negative and fractional indices in Year 8 has a foundation problem that touches every later topic, and that is a term of work rather than a fortnight. A good diagnostic says which of the two situations applies, and says it before invoicing for a year.

sections.heading: Why the budget band is more defensible in maths than anywhere else
paragraphs: Mathematics is the one subject where the cheapest band genuinely competes, and a page that pretended otherwise would be selling rather than informing. Below Year 10, a large share of what a student needs is drilled practice with immediate correction: index laws, fraction arithmetic, expanding brackets, solving linear equations. That work does not require a specialist who has read the 0580 markscheme. It requires patience, accuracy and frequency.

So the budget band of AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, is reasonable value for Years 7 to 9 in this belt. At roughly AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's estimate for a weekly session, it is also the band that keeps the stage affordable for the years when consistency matters more than expertise.

The band stops being defensible at a specific point: when the work becomes board-specific. Extended-tier technique, question triage, method-mark discipline and the particular phrasing habits of 0580 or 4MA1 all require somebody who has worked with the specification and its markschemes. At that point the qualified band of AED 150 to 300, or the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and upward, is not a luxury. Twenty hours at AED 60 will not produce what six hours at AED 270 produces, because the cheaper tutor cannot see what the markscheme is paying for.

A practical rule for a Dubailand family: pay the budget band for fluency, the mid band for consolidation while content is being taught, and the specialist band for the examination year. Spending in the wrong direction at either end is the commonest overspend in this market, and no provider in it publishes the distinction.

sections.heading: Budgeting by block instead of by month
paragraphs: Monthly pricing suits providers and open-ended plans. Block pricing suits families and finite problems. For mathematics the block is the natural unit, because the subject decomposes cleanly into topics with identifiable failures, and a parent can see what has been bought at the end of each one.

A worked approach. Start with a diagnostic: three to five sessions at the mid band, producing a written gap list ranked by mark weight. Then buy the highest-weight block, six to eight sessions, and reassess against the same question types. Then decide whether a second block is warranted or whether the money is better spent on a different subject entirely. That cycle costs less over a year than twelve months of weekly sessions and produces a record of what changed.

Compare that against the retainer shape most families end up in. At AED 600 to 1,200 a month on the mid band, a nine-month Year 10 commitment in one subject is a substantial sum, and in many cases two or three blocks placed deliberately would have achieved the same thing for less. The retainer wins only where the student needs steady consolidation across all topics as they are taught, which is a legitimate case and should be chosen rather than defaulted into.

On in-home comparison, the arithmetic is stark in this belt. Market packages run roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Four contacts against eight, at twice the price, with the difference being the journey along Al Qudra Road. IB Gram does not sell UAE home visits at all; the service exists only in India. These figures are published market rates from the providers and sources named, not our price list.

sections.heading: The November resit, and what it costs to use it well
paragraphs: A resit is a cost decision as much as an academic one, and the calendar determines whether the money is well spent. The word November returned no hits across every fetchable competitor page researched for this project, which means most families in this belt are making the decision without the basic facts.

Here they are. Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE page quoting a spring window is handing parents a date they cannot use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Backward-looking anchors can be checked: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The cost consequence is the January gap. A student retaking in November learns the outcome roughly nine weeks later, in January, which is after many sixth-form conversations have begun. Paying for an intensive run between August and November is therefore a bet placed before the information arrives, and a family should price it as such rather than assume the resit resolves the question in time. Where a grade is needed for a specific post-16 route, talk to the school about conditional arrangements before committing to the tuition.

One Cambridge administrative point that costs nothing to check and can cost a paper. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre sits in.

sections.heading: What no amount of money fixes
paragraphs: A page about cost should end with the limits, because the alternative is implying that spend and outcome are the same variable. They are not, and the places where money stops working are specific.

No tutor can promise a grade. Not at AED 50 an hour and not at AED 650. Grades depend on the work done between sessions, on what a particular series asks and on where boundaries fall, and nobody selling tuition controls any of those. We publish no grade promise, no improvement promise and no refund tied to an outcome. We also publish no satisfaction or results figure, because a statistic without the number of students, the date and the method is not evidence, and most of the figures displayed in this market carry none of the three.

Money cannot reopen a closed entry. If the tier caps the grade, additional hours achieve nothing and an honest provider says so rather than invoicing. Money cannot substitute for practice either: mathematics improves through the student doing problems, and a tutor who does the problems while the student watches is producing a comfortable hour and no learning. And money cannot buy board material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are their copyright; a provider offering a download library has a problem a parent would be inheriting.

Nor is tutoring required for anything regulatory. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited International GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. That requirement is a matter of record and checking it on moe.gov.ae costs nothing. Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, expedites or guarantees, and no page should suggest that paying for tuition affects a regulatory process.

faqs.question: What is the fee for an IGCSE maths tutor in the Dubailand area?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai spread runs from AED 45 to AED 650 an hour. Budget online provision is AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Specialist provision is AED 200 to 450 and upward, TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel. None of these are IB Gram prices; they are cited so you can judge a quote.

faqs.question: Is it better to buy maths sessions monthly or in a block?
faqs.answer: For a specific gap, a block. Mathematics decomposes into topics with identifiable failures, so six to eight sessions aimed at algebraic fractions or trigonometry solution ranges has a start, an end and a measurable result. A monthly retainer at AED 600 to 1,200 running for nine months is harder to attribute progress to and usually costs more over a year. The retainer is the right choice only where the student needs steady consolidation across all topics as they are taught, which is a real case but should be chosen deliberately.

faqs.question: Does a cheap maths tutor work for a Year 8 in Mudon?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and this is the one subject where the budget band genuinely competes. A large share of what a Year 8 needs is drilled practice with immediate correction: index laws, fraction arithmetic, expanding brackets, solving linear equations. That needs patience and frequency rather than markscheme expertise. At AED 45 to 150 an hour, or roughly AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's estimate, it is defensible value. The band stops working when the task becomes board-specific technique in Year 11.

faqs.question: How much does the wrong tier cost a Dubailand family?
faqs.answer: Potentially everything spent on the subject. A Cambridge Core entry in mathematics cannot exceed grade C, and once entries are submitted no quantity of tuition changes that. A household paying AED 600 to 1,200 a month against a ceiling below the grade they need has bought nothing of use. The prevention is cheap: three to five diagnostic sessions producing a written assessment of whether the higher tier is reachable, taken to the school before entries close. After that date, the money is better redirected to another subject.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the fastest return on tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Three stand out. Scale factors for area and volume on similar shapes, reliably among the worst answered items on a paper and often closed in two or three sessions. Histograms with unequal class widths, a standard trap with a standard remedy. And probability questions where the student understands the ideas but never draws the tree diagram, which is where the method marks sit. Method communication generally is the fastest change of all, because it is a habit rather than a knowledge gap and usually shifts within three or four sessions.

faqs.question: Why do home visits to Town Square cost more than to Motor City?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is longer and less predictable. Dubailand runs south-east along Al Ain Road and Al Qudra Road, so a tutor visiting the far communities attaches up to eighty minutes of travel to a sixty-minute lesson. They either quote the top of the AED 180 to 500 in-home band or broaden their subject range to fill a diary with nearby families. Either way the parent pays more and chooses from less. Online delivery removes the travel component entirely, which is why the comparison is with the AED 150 to 300 band instead.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions before we see the grade move?
faqs.answer: Method usually changes before grades do, which is the honest answer. Habit-level failures such as unshown working often shift within three or four sessions, visible immediately in marked work. Self-contained topic blocks take six to eight. A foundational gap in indices and algebraic fractions carried from Year 8 is a term or more, because it touches every later topic. Grades follow once enough of the measured losses are closed, and anyone quoting a timeline before seeing a marked paper is guessing rather than estimating.

faqs.question: Should we pay for both maths and science support in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually not simultaneously at the specialist band, which is where budgets break. A better pattern is a diagnostic across both, then a concentrated block in whichever subject is losing the most marks, holding the remaining budget for the examination run in the subject that matters most to the post-16 plan. Spreading an identical sum thinly across two subjects for nine months is the default shape and rarely the most productive one. Note too that equivalency on the British track requires five subjects, not six.

faqs.question: Can online maths lessons really replace sitting beside a tutor?
faqs.answer: For International GCSE mathematics, in most cases yes. A shared screen with the student's own working annotated live does more for method communication than watching somebody write on paper, and the session leaves a record rather than evaporating. Timed paper practice works identically. The honest exceptions are young children and students with significant attention difficulties, where physical presence does real work. For a Year 10 or 11 student in this belt the limiting factor is the tutor's familiarity with 0580 or 4MA1, not the medium.

faqs.question: What does the tutor's UAE permit add to the cost?
faqs.answer: Nothing. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts are published. A licensing line item in a quote is charging for something free.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth paying for?
faqs.answer: It depends on the timing more than the teaching. Cambridge runs June and November series in the UAE, and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. The February and March series is India-only. The catch is the gap: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a resit candidate waits roughly nine weeks and learns the outcome in January, after many sixth-form conversations begin. Paying for an August-to-November intensive is therefore a bet placed before the information arrives, and worth discussing with the school first.

faqs.question: Do you charge more for Extended than for Core tier maths?
faqs.answer: The market does, broadly, because Extended-tier work needs somebody familiar with the specification and its markschemes rather than a generalist, and that sits in the AED 150 to 300 or AED 200 to 450 bands rather than the budget one. What matters more than the rate difference is whether the tier is right in the first place. We publish no rate card on these pages because the honest figure depends on subject, level and frequency, and a number quoted before anybody has met the student is marketing rather than information.

faqs.question: Will you provide worked solutions to past papers?
faqs.answer: Not reproduced from the boards. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from material the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent questions with full worked solutions in the same style. That gives the same practice without using somebody else's copyright, and in mathematics it is straightforward to produce.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to prepare for the June maths paper?
faqs.answer: Spend on diagnosis rather than coverage. One marked past paper, three to five diagnostic sessions, then a single block aimed at the highest-weight failure, then timed papers of the correct board with the method-mark discipline drilled explicitly. That sequence typically costs a fraction of a nine-month retainer and produces a visible change in marked work. The expensive route is general revision across the whole syllabus billed monthly, which converts slowly because most of the hours address content the student already has.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis before the hours
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: An IGCSE maths tutor in Dubailand should start by asking for the syllabus code, the tier and a marked paper, and should finish the first session able to name which block is costing the marks. That sequence is what converts money into grades. Everything else in this market, including the comfortable monthly retainer, is a slower version of it. Book a free trial lesson with a specialist in 0580 or 4MA1 as applicable, treat it as a diagnostic, and buy a defined block rather than an open-ended arrangement. No card is required and nobody is sent to your address.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-emaar-beachfr.tutorsIntro: The mathematics tutors below teach a specific syllabus rather than a school subject: Cambridge 0580 at Core or Extended, Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics, or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 at Foundation or Higher. Each teaches from the question style their students will actually face.

intro.heading: Two boards, two tiers, one subject name on the report card
paragraphs: The phrase "IGCSE maths" covers at least four different examinations. Cambridge 0580 at Core tier is a pair of papers with a grade ceiling of C. Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier is a different pair reaching A*. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 tiers the same way as Foundation and Higher, with its own paper style and its own formula provision. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics is a separate qualification taken alongside. A tutor who hears "IGCSE maths" and starts teaching has not yet learned which of those four your child sits.

This is the comparison that matters, and almost nobody makes it. Parents in this cluster are instead invited to compare locations: would a family on Emaar Beachfront do better with a tutor from Dubai Marina, from JBR, from the Palm? The honest answer is that those neighbourhoods differ on commute and session timing and not at all on who can teach Extended-tier mathematics. The same pool serves all of them, the same schools absorb their children, and the same evening traffic window constrains everybody.

The second genuine comparison is between question types. A Year 11 student scoring in the fifties on an Extended paper is not uniformly weak. The marks are leaking from specific places: unshown method on multi-part questions, rounding instructions printed in the question and ignored, unit conversion in compound measure and volume work, the structured question where part (a) goes wrong and takes four further parts with it. Those are four separate repairs with four different timescales, and a marked script identifies all of them in ten minutes.

Emaar Beachfront's own geography is worth stating plainly because it changes what is practical rather than what is possible. One road link onto the peninsula. No school and no tuition centre inside it. Basement parking a visitor cannot use without a resident escort. Children leaving before 07:00 for Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah and returning after 15:30. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India.

What follows compares the two boards paper by paper, sets out where Year 11 marks actually go, puts the five nearby neighbourhoods side by side on the things that genuinely differ, publishes the AED rates this market charges with each figure attributed, and explains the 0606 decision for students heading towards A Level Maths or Diploma Analysis and Approaches. Confirm the board, code and tier with your school's exams officer before acting on any of it; that single email settles more than any amount of comparison shopping.

A note on what this page will not do. It will not tell you that mathematics is hard, that confidence matters, or that every child learns differently. Those statements are true and they are not actionable. What is actionable is a board, a code, a tier, a question type and an hour of the day, and a plan you can check at the fortnight. If a tutor cannot give you those five things after reading one marked script, the sessions that follow will be general revision sold at a specialist rate.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-emaar-beachfr.programmesIntro: A maths tutor is buying a different thing in each of three school years, and the price of waiting rises steeply. These are the positions families in this cluster book from.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the course starts
programmes.description: The year the tier is effectively decided. Algebraic manipulation, fraction work, rearranging formulae and reading a graph either become automatic now or they become a Year 11 problem. Where a school uses Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint, those tests run in March, May and October and give an external reference before anything is committed.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving the Beachfront and Harbour towers teach MYP mathematics to Year 9 before moving to IGCSE, which means a change of assessment model rather than a continuation. Ask which it is before planning two years of support.

programmes.name: Year 10, content coverage
programmes.description: The syllabus is delivered across this year and part of the next. Tutoring closes topics as the school teaches them, which is the cheapest route to a grade in the whole qualification. It is also when the tier decision is taken, usually on evidence the school already holds rather than on a dedicated test.
programmes.countryNote: This is the point at which a capable student placed provisionally at Core can still be moved, and the window closes when final entries are filed. Ask the school what evidence the decision rests on.

programmes.name: Year 11, technique and timing
programmes.description: Content finishes and the work becomes method discipline, timing and paper strategy. The mock script is the document of the year, because it separates marks lost to absent content from marks lost to the four habits that cost most, and those need different work and different session counts.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June or November and Pearson in May/June or November. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and should not appear in a Dubai revision plan.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-emaar-beachfr.subjectsIntro: These are the mathematics strands most often responsible for a Year 11 grade in this cluster, with the error that characterises each. The strand names are deliberately narrower than chapter headings, because that is the level at which a repair is planned.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying. The foundation everything else rests on, and the single best predictor of an Extended grade. Students who manipulate slowly rather than inaccurately still lose marks, because they run out of time on later questions.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.description: Linear, simultaneous, quadratic and, at Extended, algebraic fractions. Marks go on sign errors during rearrangement and on solutions not checked against the original equation, which is a thirty-second habit that recovers whole questions.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, reciprocals, exponentials and transformations. The usual loss is a sketch drawn without intercepts or asymptotes marked, after which the question about the graph cannot be answered from the student's own diagram.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and Pythagoras
subjects.description: Right-angled work, the sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems at Extended. Almost every lost mark traces to a diagram drawn carelessly or to an angle placed in the wrong triangle before any calculation begins.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measure
subjects.description: Area, surface area, volume, density, speed and pressure. The dominant error is unit conversion, particularly between cubic centimetres and litres or between kilometres per hour and metres per second, and it is wholly mechanical to fix.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms. Histograms with unequal class widths cause disproportionate loss because frequency density is routinely treated as frequency.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and describing a transformation fully. The marks are in completeness: a description naming the type of transformation but omitting the centre, scale factor or vector collects part of the available credit at best.

subjects.name: Number and ratio
subjects.description: Standard form, percentages, reverse percentages, compound interest and ratio division. Reverse percentage questions are the most reliably failed topic at this level because students apply the percentage forwards without noticing the question asked otherwise.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics, Cambridge 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, further trigonometry, series and logarithms, taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Maths or Diploma Analysis and Approaches. It assumes complete 0580 algebraic fluency and punishes a student who has not got it.

subjects.name: Edexcel 4MA1 question style
subjects.description: Not a topic but a skill in its own right. Edexcel phrases problems differently from Cambridge and provides formulae differently, so a student practising the wrong board's papers spends exam time decoding the question before attempting the mathematics.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1
paragraphs: Both qualifications certify international GCSE mathematics and universities treat them as equivalent. For a student preparing for one of them, they are not interchangeable. The tier names differ, the paper pairs differ, the formula support differs, and the question phrasing differs enough that a student practising the wrong board loses time in the exam decoding what is being asked. Six months of revision from the wrong board's past papers is a common and entirely avoidable loss in this cluster.

Cambridge tiers 0580 into Core and Extended. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above a C. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Cambridge has revised which of its papers permit a calculator, so confirm that detail with the school for your child's cohort rather than assuming it from an older resource. Pearson tiers 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher, with two written papers per tier.

The resit route differs in timing rather than in principle. A Cambridge candidate who underperforms in June looks to November. A Pearson candidate has the same option, with November results reaching students in January: the November 2025 series results landed on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. For a student whose post-16 place depends on a grade, a January result changes what can be negotiated with a sixth form and when, which is a conversation to have before the summer series rather than after it.

sections.heading: Where a Year 11 actually loses marks in maths
paragraphs: Read enough marked Extended papers and the same four losses appear regardless of the student. Unshown method is the largest: a correct answer with no intermediate line collects a fraction of the marks allocated, and on a multi-part question it forfeits follow-through credit entirely, so one arithmetic slip in part (a) takes four later parts with it. Students who do algebra mentally are penalised precisely because they are competent, which is why this habit survives into Year 11 unchallenged.

Second, rounding and accuracy instructions. A question that says to three significant figures is awarding a mark for that, and a student who writes the full decimal expansion has declined it. Third, units, concentrated in volume, area, density, speed and pressure work, where converting between cubic centimetres and litres or between kilometres per hour and metres per second is the whole difficulty. Fourth, the structured question abandoned after a wrong part, when the mark scheme would have carried the method forward.

None of these is a knowledge failure and all of them are mechanical. A student losing twenty-six marks to these four habits and four marks to genuinely unknown content should spend a fortnight on the habits, not a term on the content. That is the opposite of what usually gets sold, because habits look like technique and technique feels like something a school should have covered. The script tells you which it is, which is why we ask for the script rather than the grade before matching anyone.

sections.heading: Does the neighbourhood change the answer? A straight comparison
paragraphs: Families moving into this part of New Dubai are told the neighbourhoods are broadly similar for schooling, and for tutoring that is almost true in a way nobody explains. What genuinely differs between Emaar Beachfront, Dubai Harbour, Dubai Marina, JBR and Palm Jumeirah is the commute, the predictability of the afternoon, and therefore the earliest hour at which a maths session can run without the student being too tired to be accurate. Those are real differences and they matter, because tired students make arithmetic errors that get misdiagnosed as misunderstanding.

What does not differ is the depth of the local specialist pool. All five addresses draw on the same tutors, feed the same school cluster in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Jumeirah, and compete for the same few people who teach Extended-tier mathematics and are free twice a week at a fixed hour in April. A family who moves the search from the Beachfront to the Marina gets a longer list of names and the same shortage at the top of it. This is not a claim about online tutoring being superior; it is an observation about who exists.

The practical conclusion is to stop comparing addresses and start comparing hours. Work out honestly when your child can concentrate, allowing for a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30, then find a tutor matched to the right board and tier who is free then. Online delivery is what makes that ordering possible, because it removes travel from the equation entirely. We do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison below is between our online sessions and what the local in-home market charges and delivers.

That premium buys presence, and on this peninsula it also buys risk. Across a twenty-session Year 11 block, the sessions that do not happen are the real cost, and they arrive in April when there is no room to make them up. The premium does not buy a better-qualified mathematician: the same person teaching online charges less.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics 0606 and the route after Year 11
paragraphs: 0606 is a separate Cambridge qualification sat alongside 0580 by students intending to take A Level Mathematics or Diploma Analysis and Approaches. It front-loads calculus, further trigonometry, series and logarithms, and it assumes complete fluency in everything 0580 Extended covers. For a student who already has that fluency it is genuinely useful preparation and makes the first term of post-16 mathematics considerably less punishing.

For a student who does not, it is the commonest overreach in this cluster. Taking 0606 while still consolidating algebraic manipulation means learning new content on an unstable foundation, under the same exam pressure, in the same series. The usual outcome is two mediocre grades where one strong grade was available. The test to apply is simple and unsentimental: can the student complete 0580 Extended algebraic manipulation quickly and accurately, without a calculator, today? If not, the answer is not yet.

The decision also depends on what comes next, and that is worth researching rather than assuming. Post-16 mathematics entry requirements are published by each school and each university programme, and they change. Some A Level and Diploma Higher Level routes expect a strong Extended grade; some will note 0606 favourably without requiring it. Read the current requirement from the school or institution itself in Year 10, before timetables are built, and make the 0606 decision against that rather than against the general impression that more mathematics is better.

One scheduling point specific to this cluster. Where a student does take 0606 alongside 0580, the two subjects should not share a session. The content overlaps enough that a tired student blurs them, and the papers reward different things: 0580 rewards accuracy under time pressure while 0606 rewards sustained technique. Two shorter slots in the week work better than one long one, and on this peninsula that usually means a weekday evening and a weekend morning rather than two weekday evenings.

sections.heading: Calculators, mental arithmetic and the paper that takes the calculator away
paragraphs: Where a board sets a paper without a calculator, that paper is a different examination from the one with it. Algebraic manipulation, fraction arithmetic, exact values and standard form have nowhere to hide, and a student who has been getting by on the calculator discovers it in a single sitting. Because Cambridge has revised its calculator arrangements for 0580, the first thing to confirm with the school is which of your child's papers permit one. Planning a fluency block for a paper that does not exist wastes a month; skipping one for a paper that does costs a grade.

Where calculators are permitted throughout, as in Edexcel 4MA1, the risk inverts. Students become fast at operations and slow at deciding, and the lost marks move to question interpretation: reading what is actually being asked, choosing a method, and checking whether the answer is plausible. A student who gets an answer of 4,800 metres per second for a cyclist has made an arithmetic error their calculator cannot detect and their own judgement should have.

Both problems respond to the same discipline, applied in opposite directions. For the non-calculator risk, drill fluency with a time target per question until the standard is speed rather than eventual success. For the calculator-permitted risk, require an estimate written down before any calculation and a plausibility check written after. Both are short interventions with measurable results, and both are easier to enforce in a session where the tutor can watch the working appear line by line.

sections.heading: What the first month should produce
paragraphs: A maths block should be falsifiable. In the first session the tutor reads the marked script and produces a list: marks lost by question type and by habit, with an estimate against each and a judgement about which are worth chasing before the next paper. That list is the plan, and you should be able to read it. If a tutor cannot produce one after seeing a script, the sessions that follow will be general revision at a specialist price.

By the end of week two the student should be showing method without being reminded, because that is the first and cheapest habit to install. By week four the same question types that were failing should be answered correctly without prompting, on questions the student has not seen before. By week six the student should be sitting a whole paper under timing, marking it strictly against the official scheme, and predicting their own total within a few marks. That prediction accuracy is the real measure; a student who can predict their mark has internalised the mark scheme.

If those checkpoints are not appearing, the diagnosis was wrong or the work is not happening between sessions, and both are worth saying out loud in week three rather than week eight. We would rather change the tutor or change the plan early than defend either. And official papers and mark schemes come from your child's school or the board: we reference and explain them in sessions and do not redistribute board material, because that is not ours to hand out.

process.title: Confirm board, code and tier
process.description: Email the exams officer and ask for the board, syllabus code and tier in writing. 0580 Extended and 4MA1 Higher need different past papers and different formula familiarity. That single email prevents the most expensive mistake available in an IGCSE year, which is six months of practice from the wrong archive.

process.title: Send the marked mock script
process.description: The script separates marks lost to absent content from marks lost to method, rounding, units and abandoned questions. Those four habits usually account for most of the gap, and they repair in a fortnight. A reported percentage cannot distinguish between them, and guessing wastes the fortnight.

process.title: Choose the hour honestly
process.description: 17:30 from this peninsula on a weekday, earlier only if the school run is genuinely reliable. Mathematics is the subject most damaged by fatigue, because a tired student's arithmetic slips look like conceptual gaps and get treated as such. Weekend mornings are the strongest slots we schedule here.

process.title: Free trial, then a written plan
process.description: One trial lesson per student, no card required. It ends with marks sorted by question type and habit, an estimate against each, and a judgement about what to chase first. You keep that document whether or not you continue, and it is useful to any tutor you hire.

process.title: Measure at the fortnight
process.description: Method shown unprompted, then unfamiliar questions of the same type answered correctly, then a timed paper self-marked with the prediction within a few marks. If a checkpoint does not appear, we change the plan or the tutor rather than extending the block and hoping.

faqs.question: Is a maths tutor in Dubai Marina any better placed than one for Emaar Beachfront?
faqs.answer: Better placed to travel, not better placed to teach. The Marina has a denser resident population and a more established freelance market, so the list of names is longer. The list still thins to very few at Extended tier, free twice a week at a fixed hour in April, because the constraint is how many adults teach that tier in Dubai at all. Since our lessons run over live video and we do not offer home visits in the UAE, the address stops being a variable in the shortlist entirely.

faqs.question: Which board's past papers should my Year 11 be working from?
faqs.answer: Only the board they are entered with, confirmed in writing by the exams officer. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 ask comparable mathematics in different house styles with different formula provision, so practising the wrong archive trains a student to decode the wrong question format. Time lost decoding in the exam comes out of thinking time before it comes out of marks. Families in this cluster regularly find out in April; one email in September settles it permanently.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on questions they got right?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded for visible working and follow-through credit on a structured question depends on the examiner being able to see the route. A student who does the algebra mentally and writes a single line is penalised for competence: one slip in part (a) then costs four later parts instead of one mark. Installing the habit of showing method takes two or three sessions of enforcement and is the cheapest grade movement available in the whole qualification.

faqs.question: What is the ceiling if my child stays on the Core tier?
faqs.answer: A grade C on Cambridge 0580, however well they perform, because Core candidates sit a different pair of papers set to that ceiling. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Edexcel applies the same logic through Foundation and Higher. If you believe your child is capable of the higher tier, the conversation belongs in Year 10 while the decision is still open, and it should be evidence-led: offer a full higher-tier paper sat under timed conditions.

faqs.question: How much should a Beachfront family expect to pay per hour?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits with travel included are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. Budget online provision runs from AED 33 to 65. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours; our figure is agreed after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium buy a better mathematician?
faqs.answer: No. It buys presence and it buys travel. The same tutor teaching online charges less, because the hour is no longer costing them two and a quarter. On a peninsula with one road link and escorted basement parking, the premium also buys the risk that a session does not happen, and across a twenty-session Year 11 block the sessions that go missing are the real cost. They tend to go missing in April, when there is no room to replace them.

faqs.question: Should my child add Additional Mathematics 0606?
faqs.answer: Only if 0580 Extended algebraic manipulation is already quick and accurate without a calculator. 0606 front-loads calculus, further trigonometry, series and logarithms and assumes that fluency from the first lesson, so a student still consolidating algebra ends up learning new content on an unstable foundation and collects two mediocre grades where one strong grade was available. For a student heading to A Level Maths or Analysis and Approaches with the fluency in place, it is genuinely useful.

faqs.question: How do we handle the paper that does not allow a calculator?
faqs.answer: First confirm which of your child's papers that is, because Cambridge has revised its 0580 calculator arrangements and an older resource may mislead you. Where such a paper applies, the preparation is a separate fluency block: index laws, fraction arithmetic, exact values and standard form, drilled with a time target per question until speed rather than eventual success is the standard. It runs alongside topic work for a few weeks and produces visible movement because the skill is mechanical.

faqs.question: Which maths topic is most reliably failed at this level?
faqs.answer: Reverse percentages, followed by histograms with unequal class widths. Both fail for the same reason: the student applies a familiar procedure forwards when the question asked for it backwards, or treats frequency density as frequency. Neither is conceptually hard and both are rarely revisited once taught, so they survive into Year 11 untouched. A single session on each usually fixes them permanently, which makes them unusually good value for a student hunting marks.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in the spring of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Not for one or two subjects, if the work is habit-led rather than content-led. A student losing most of their marks to method, rounding, units and abandoned structured questions can recover a great deal in eight weeks. A student missing three topics outright cannot, and anyone promising otherwise is selling hours. The marked mock script tells you which situation you are in, which is why we ask for it before quoting a session count rather than after.

faqs.question: Can sessions move if the school run is late?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is most of the argument for the format. A video slot can shift by thirty minutes with a message and nobody loses an evening. An in-home visit across the causeway at 17:00 either happens or is cancelled, and a cancellation in April costs a week of a plan that has no spare weeks. Over a twenty-session block that flexibility is worth more than any single session, because continuity rather than intensity is what moves a maths grade.

faqs.question: What should we see after four weeks of maths sessions?
faqs.answer: Method shown without being reminded by the end of week two. By week four, the question types that were failing answered correctly on unfamiliar examples without prompting. By week six, a whole paper sat under timing, self-marked strictly against the official scheme, with the student's predicted total within a few marks of the real one. If those checkpoints are not appearing, the diagnosis was wrong or the work between sessions is not happening, and both are worth raising immediately.

faqs.question: Do you provide the past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who does. Board material is copyrighted, and redistributing unreleased material creates an exposure for the student rather than for the site hosting it. We reference and explain papers and schemes in sessions and link the official source. Most schools will release recent papers and mark schemes on request, because that is what they are for. Ask the subject teacher first; the exams officer can confirm which series are available.

faqs.question: How quickly can a 0580 Extended tutor start from this peninsula?
faqs.answer: For a Core-tier or Year 10 slot, usually within a few days, because the only variable is matching an hour. For an Extended-tier specialist at a popular twice-weekly evening time in the spring, it takes longer, and occasionally there is nobody free that week. We will say so and offer a different hour or a short block rather than substituting someone who teaches the other board. The trial lesson is the first fixed point, with the weekly slot agreed straight after it.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, one shortened evening, and maths wants the biggest share
paragraphs: A Year 11 IGCSE candidate is usually entered for eight to ten subjects. Each sets homework, each has a mock, each expects revision, and every one of them wants a share of the same evening. For a student travelling out of Emaar South to school and back, that evening has already lost ninety minutes to the road. The question a maths tutor in this community is really being asked is not how to teach mathematics. It is which maths is worth the hours that exist.

Emaar South has no school inside it. Children travel to Dubai Investments Park, to Al Furjan and Jebel Ali, or east along the Dubailand corridor, arriving home anywhere between 16:00 and 17:30 depending on destination and whether the journey was by bus or car. Deduct arrival, changing and eating, and a Year 11 student typically has four to four and a half usable hours on a weekday, against a workload designed on the assumption of a shorter journey.

Maths has a reasonable claim on a large share of that, because it is the subject that repays targeted work most reliably: the faults are specific, visible on a marked script, and improvable inside a term. But the claim has to be earned topic by topic rather than asserted. Reverse percentage questions are examined reliably and take two sessions to fix. Reading more of the textbook takes the same hours and moves nothing. The difference between those two uses of a Tuesday is most of what this page is about.

The other thing a crowded timetable changes is the tier conversation. A Core entry in Cambridge or a Foundation entry in Pearson caps the grade available, the decision is usually made by a school in Year 10, and reopening it requires a timed higher-tier paper marked against the official scheme. Producing that evidence takes a term of deliberate work, and a family who only starts thinking about it in Year 11 has usually missed the window while being very busy.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor is dispatched to an Emaar South address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with working written on a shared digital surface that persists from week to week. In a crowded year that record matters: the same algebraic slip appearing in October and again in February is visible rather than re-diagnosed from scratch.

One factual note. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series; Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. KHDA oversees Dubai's private schools and does not accredit tutors; IB Gram holds no KHDA approval or partnership and runs no UAE centre.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The maths topics competing for an Emaar South student's scarce hours, each annotated by how reliably it is examined and how long it takes to repair.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, index laws, surds and algebraic fractions. Not a topic but the substrate under simultaneous equations, functions and quadratics, so repairing it treats three apparent weaknesses at once. The highest-leverage claim on the hours and the first thing a plan should fund.

subjects.name: Ratio, proportion and percentage change
subjects.description: Reverse percentage, compound interest, direct and inverse proportion. Examined reliably on both boards, practised far below its mark value, and repairable in roughly two sessions because the methods are procedural. The best return per hour available in the subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Paper 4
subjects.description: The longer Extended paper of multi-part questions building to harder final parts, where transformations, bearings, vectors and compound probability sit. Candidates who ration time badly lose the final question entirely, and it is often the most accessible of the hard ones, which makes pacing work unusually cheap.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Paper 2
subjects.description: Structured short-answer questions, calculator-permitted. Losses accumulate as single marks on arithmetic slips a candidate would never make unhurried, and on questions saying show your working where an answer alone appears. Both are checking habits rather than knowledge gaps.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MA1 Papers 1 and 2
subjects.description: Two equally weighted calculator papers with a heavier emphasis on multi-step contextual problems. A student arriving from Cambridge mid-course stumbles on phrasing rather than content, which is a four-session adjustment rather than a term of work.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, triangle area, and three-dimensional work. Bearings questions fail on the diagram rather than the trigonometry: candidates who do not draw and label north lines get the angle wrong from correct working. Sketching first is a habit, not a skill.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, route questions in terms of two given vectors, and full transformation descriptions. A transformation described without its centre, scale factor or direction scores part marks at best. Learnable procedures that repay a short block.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and Venn notation. The errors are structural: unlabelled branches, no adjustment for without replacement, a Venn region misread. Candidates who draw the diagram fully before calculating almost always outperform those reasoning it out.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching quadratics and reciprocals, reading gradients and intersections, inverse and composite functions. Marks go on sketches with no intercepts marked and on reading a graph imprecisely. Reliably available marks and good value for a tired evening slot.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Compound solids, arc and sector work, and the area and volume scale factors for similar shapes. The scale-factor rules are short, examined often and forgotten reliably, which makes them high-yield for a compressed block late in the course.

subjects.name: The supplied formula list
subjects.description: Both boards provide one and most candidates meet theirs in the examination hall. Twenty minutes spent reading and annotating which formulas are supplied and which are not prevents a candidate deriving something printed on page two. The cheapest single action in the subject.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, further trigonometry, vectors and logarithms beyond 0580, overlapping less with the main syllabus than students expect. It needs its own slot in the timetable, which in a crowded Year 11 means it competes with the main maths entry rather than extending it.
