sections.heading: Online one-to-one maths from Green Community, limits included
paragraphs: Mathematics transfers to video unusually well because the work is a shared writing surface. The tutor writes a line, the student writes the next, both see the same page, and the whole session is reviewable afterwards. For marking a script together it is better than a single paper copy across a table, since both people can annotate the same mark line at the same moment.

The scheduling gain is real and specific to this subject. A 4.30pm session catches a student who can still rearrange an equation accurately. A 6.15pm session, after a tutor has crossed the city, catches one who makes sign and transposition errors. Parents frequently read those errors as weak mathematics, buy content help, and are puzzled when nothing changes.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and this page says so near the top rather than leaving it to be discovered after a booking, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

The honest limits: a student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better in person; a weak connection shortens the hour whatever the invoice says; and a shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines the lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. If one of those applies, hire locally and ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first lesson.

sections.heading: Permits, equivalency and how to start
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so no amount should be quoted to you. Never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

On equivalency, mathematics matters more than most subjects because it is nearly always one of the counted five. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One page ranking in this market states the figure as six, which is not what the published rule says.

What we do not claim: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation or partnership, publish no self-asserted rating, promise no grade or improvement figure, and quote no statistic without its source and date.

To start, send the syllabus code, the route or tier, the year group and a photograph of the most recent marked paper. The paper carries the code on its front cover if you do not have it to hand. A specialist on that specification then teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online built on that paper, ending in a written note of which topics and which question shapes are costing marks. The note is yours whether or not you continue, and if nobody suitable is free at your hour we say so and offer alternatives.

faqs.question: Why has revision not improved my child's IGCSE maths mark?
faqs.answer: Usually because revision is organised by chapter and the paper is organised by question shape. A paper asks about bounds by giving a measurement to the nearest unit and wanting a maximum area; it asks about vectors by wanting a one-line geometric reason after the computation. Rereading the chapter prepares for neither. What moves the mark is attempting the shapes under timing and having them marked against the official scheme by someone who is not the student, which produces a diagnosis rather than a score.

faqs.question: What are bounds questions and why do they cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: A quantity is given to a stated accuracy - 12 centimetres to the nearest centimetre - and the question wants a maximum or minimum of something derived from it. Two errors recur. The student uses the stated value rather than the bound. Or they identify both bounds correctly and pair them wrongly, taking two maxima when a minimum density needed the maximum mass and the minimum volume. It is a reasoning error about which bound belongs where, and three focused sessions normally removes it.

faqs.question: Does the Core route actually remove topics, or just cap the grade?
faqs.answer: Both, and the topic consequence is the one families overlook. A Cambridge Core candidate is not examined on graph transformations, vector proof, the harder trigonometry or Extended-level algebraic fractions, which is a materially smaller body of work. That makes the route decision concrete: for a student who cannot access Extended questions, Core concentrates the available weeks on bounds, ratio, mensuration and percentage work the Core papers ask about repeatedly. For a student losing marks to habits, it removes content they could have learned.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose vector marks when the working is right?
faqs.answer: Because the mark is usually for the reason rather than the computation. A question asks for a column vector and then asks what that tells you about two lines or three points. The expected answer is one sentence: the vectors are multiples of one another and therefore parallel, or three points are collinear because two vectors between them share a point and a direction. Students compute correctly and write nothing. It is the most consistently omitted single sentence in the Extended papers, and it is trained in two sessions.

faqs.question: Which maths topics should a Year 11 in this catchment prioritise?
faqs.answer: The ten calculations that recur across almost every series, because they cut across chapters and therefore escape chapter-based revision: reverse percentage, repeated percentage change, ratio in context, bounds in a compound measure, unit conversion in two and three dimensions, rearranging where the subject appears twice, quadratics by factorising and by formula, sine and cosine rules with a diagram drawn first, probability along and across tree branches, and reading a cumulative frequency estimate with an interpretation sentence attached.

faqs.question: Should past papers be done whole or by topic?
faqs.answer: By topic first, whole later. A whole paper gives you a total, and a total hides the cause. Ten questions on one topic drawn from several series, sat under timing and marked externally, tells you whether the method is secure and the arithmetic is not, whether a particular sub-type is the only failure, or whether the question is simply being misread. Whole papers belong in the last few weeks, once the topic lists are clean, to test stamina and timing rather than to diagnose.

faqs.question: Why is self-marking a problem for maths practice?
faqs.answer: Because the student knows what they intended to write and reads their own shorthand generously. A missing method line, an unexplained value taken from the calculator, a bound used where the stated value belonged: all pass unnoticed, because the intention was right. An examiner-literate reader marks what is on the page, and seeing two marks withheld for the same reason three times is what changes the behaviour. Self-study plus periodic external marking is a genuinely economical arrangement that very few families use.

faqs.question: My child cancels algebraic fractions and gets them wrong. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly cancelling before combining. Faced with two fractions to add, the student spots a common factor between one numerator and the other denominator and cancels it, producing a tidy answer that is wrong. The premature cancellation feels like efficiency, which is why it persists. The rule is combine first, then factorise, then cancel, and it needs enforcing rather than explaining: the student writes the combined single fraction every time before any simplification is allowed.

faqs.question: How do we find an Additional Mathematics 0606 tutor near Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Locally, with real difficulty. Cambridge 0606 and Pearson's Further Pure 4PM1 have the thinnest specialist supply of any code in this catchment, because few students take them and fewer tutors cover the calculus, logarithm and trigonometric identity content properly. A radius search from Green Community, Dubai Investments Park or Dubai South commonly returns nobody usable. Online those codes are coverable, though matching takes two to three days rather than one, and we state the expected wait at the enquiry.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge Paper 2 or Paper 4 the one to practise?
faqs.answer: Both, separately, because they reward different behaviour. Paper 2 is a shorter paper that rewards speed and automatic method on self-contained items. Paper 4 rewards sustained multi-part work, carrying a partial result forward when one part does not resolve cleanly, and holding accuracy as the arithmetic gets messier. A student who practises only one produces a lopsided result. On Pearson 4MA1 the two papers carry equal weight, which removes the distinction and replaces it with a demand for even accuracy throughout.

faqs.question: Does maths count towards the five subjects UAE equivalency requires?
faqs.answer: In practice it almost always does, which is another reason to take the route decision seriously. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One page ranking in this market states the figure as six subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Verify through the Ministry.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix one maths topic?
faqs.answer: Usually four to six for a single topic, and the number varies with what kind of failure it is. Reverse percentage and bounds take three or four because the error is about reasoning rather than arithmetic. Unit conversion in two and three dimensions takes about two, because it is a single rule. Rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice takes three. What matters more than the count is that the block has a defined end point, so the pressure that makes a habit change actually stick is present.

faqs.question: Can online lessons really work for a visual subject like geometry?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arguably better than sitting alongside, because the shared writing surface means the tutor can draw the diagram the student skipped and the student can redraw it immediately on the same page. Trigonometry beyond right angles fails most often because no diagram was drawn, so a format that makes drawing the default is useful rather than a compromise. The whole session is also reviewable afterwards, which a sheet of paper on a dining table is not.

faqs.question: Will our maths slot survive Ramadan in Green Community?
faqs.answer: It will move and it should not pause. School hours shorten during Ramadan and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot typically becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. For mathematics, protect the frequency over the length: fluency decays faster than content knowledge, and two shorter sessions a week hold more than one long one while a student is fasting. Because nobody is travelling to your address, the change is a shared-diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation of a commute.

intro.heading: The same tutoring costs a third as much in October of Year 10 as in March of Year 11
paragraphs: Almost every maths enquiry we receive from this part of Deira arrives in the spring of Year 11. That is the most expensive moment to start and the one with the least room for the work to pay off. The same student, with the same gap, supported for one session a week from October of Year 10, needs fewer sessions in total, keeps the higher tier available, and arrives at the examination needing technique practice rather than content rescue. Nothing about that is controversial and almost nobody does it.

The reason is structural rather than negligent. Year 10 produces no alarming documents. Reports say satisfactory, the topics look familiar from Year 9, and there is no examination on the horizon to make anything urgent. The gaps that will matter are forming quietly: index laws, negative numbers, rearranging a formula with the unknown on both sides, proportional reasoning. They are cheap to fix in Year 10 and they are the exact gaps that cap a grade eighteen months later.

So this page is a calendar rather than a syllabus. It maps Year 10 month by month and Year 11 month by month, names what each school report should trigger, and says honestly what remains achievable at each point. It also deals with what happens after results, because the resit decision is the one families consistently make under time pressure with the least information.

Hor Al Anz is a dense apartment district in Deira, next to Abu Hail and Al Muteena, inland from Al Mamzar, with the Green Line of the Metro running through it. Students here travel to schools across Al Qusais, Al Nahda, Al Mamzar and over the Creek, mostly by bus or Metro, which gives a more predictable afternoon than New Dubai traffic without making it early. The practical consequence for a weekly maths slot is that 17:00 to 17:30 is the honest earliest start for most of this district.

There is also a particular local pattern worth naming. A substantial number of students here moved into a British-curriculum school from CBSE or ICSE, and they arrive with stronger procedural arithmetic than average and less practice at the worded, multi-step questions IGCSE papers are built from. That is a technique gap wearing the costume of a content gap, and it is closed in a term once somebody names it rather than re-teaching a syllabus the student largely has.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the camera on the page so the tutor watches the working appear rather than hearing about it afterwards.

sections.heading: Year 10 month by month: the year almost nobody tutors
paragraphs: Year 10 generates no urgency and that is its whole problem. The topics look like harder versions of Year 9, the reports are reassuring, and the examination is eighteen months away. Meanwhile the gaps that will cap a grade are forming, and they are not exotic: index laws applied inconsistently, negatives dropped when expanding, an inability to rearrange a formula when the unknown appears twice, and proportional reasoning that works on simple numbers and fails on awkward ones.

Those four take weeks to repair in Year 10 and months in Year 11, because by then they are load-bearing. Every new topic in the second year assumes them, so a student with a rearrangement weakness meets it again in trigonometry, in algebraic fractions, in simultaneous equations and in every physics calculation they attempt. The compounding is what makes late intervention expensive, not the difficulty of the material.

The table sets out what the year typically contains and what support should be doing at each stage. The pattern worth noticing is that the recommended work is rarely the topic being taught that month. A tutor shadowing the school's scheme of work in Year 10 is usually doing the less valuable thing; the valuable thing is maintaining the foundations underneath while the school builds on top of them.

One decision closes during this year and it is the important one. The department will form a view on tier, and the view hardens as sets settle. If the family intends Extended or Higher tier, the question to ask is specific: what would need to improve for that entry to be considered? The answer is a work plan with a real deadline, and acting on it in Year 10 is dramatically cheaper than living with a capped grade afterwards.

sections.heading: Year 11 month by month: from the first mock to the series
paragraphs: Year 11 is the year families do act, and the useful thing is to act on evidence rather than on anxiety. The year has a clear shape: content finishes, a mock series produces the only genuinely diagnostic document of the two years, a second mock sometimes follows, and then the real papers. Everything worth doing in the second half of the year follows from a marked mock paper, not from a mock grade.

The distinction matters. A grade tells you the total. A marked script tells you whether the marks went to instruction-reading, abandoned method, a genuine content gap, arithmetic slips or questions never reached, and those five point to five different plans with five different costs. Our first request after any mock is the script, and the categorising takes twenty minutes. Families who do that in January are in a different position by March from those who waited.

The second feature of Year 11 is that the time is finite in a way it never was before, so allocation becomes the main skill. At sixteen weeks out, content repair is still sensible. At eight weeks, content has to be rationed to two topics with the rest going to whole papers under time. At four weeks, adding new content displaces revision of material the student half-knows, which is where the recoverable marks actually are. Students resist that last rule and it is the one that most reliably protects a grade.

The table maps the year with what each stage should produce. Note the final row: the last fortnight is not a revision period in the usual sense. It is a protection period, and the work in it is pacing, the order of attack for each paper, and eliminating errors the tally says keep recurring.

sections.heading: What to do with each report you receive
paragraphs: School reports are usually read for reassurance and then filed, which wastes them. Each one is a decision point, and the decisions are different. An early Year 10 report is about placement: is the set and tier trajectory what the family wants, and if not, what specifically would change it? That question has a factual answer and it is the most useful thing a parent can extract at that stage.

A mid-Year 10 report is about gaps. The useful question is not how is my child doing but which specific topics or skills has the department identified as weak, in their own words. Teachers answer that precisely when asked precisely. Vague questions get reassuring answers that feel better and change nothing, which is the most common failure mode of a parents' evening.

A Year 11 mock report is about allocation. The grade indicates a position and the script indicates where the marks went. Ask for the script or for a copy, and ask which questions the department considers recoverable. That conversation converts a disappointing number into a work plan with two named topics, and it costs nothing.

A final Year 11 report is about expectations and the resit question. If the predicted grade is below what a post-16 route requires, that is the moment to find out what the receiving school or institution will accept and by when, in writing. Doing it in June rather than in late August is the difference between a decision and a scramble, because the November entry closes within weeks of summer results arriving.

sections.heading: Topic order, and which gaps compound
paragraphs: Not all maths gaps are equal and the difference is whether later topics depend on them. A weakness in, say, probability is contained: it costs the marks on probability questions and nothing else. A weakness in rearranging formulae is load-bearing: it costs marks in trigonometry, in algebraic fractions, in simultaneous equations, in every physics calculation and in most chemistry ones. Fixing a contained gap is worth its own marks. Fixing a load-bearing gap is worth several topics at once.

The load-bearing list is short and stable. Index laws. Handling negatives through expansion and factorisation. Rearranging a formula where the unknown appears more than once. Fractions as ratios and as operators. Converting between forms, including standard form and percentage change. A student fluent in those five finds the second year of the course mostly a matter of new vocabulary, and a student who is not finds it a sequence of unrelated difficulties.

This is why a tutor who simply follows the school's current topic can be doing the less useful work. If the class is on circle theorems and the student cannot rearrange reliably, the circle theorems will be learned as procedures and forgotten, and the rearrangement weakness will reappear a month later in another costume. The honest sequence is to repair the load-bearing skill while supporting the current topic lightly, which takes a little longer to feel productive and produces a different result.

One practical note for this district. Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE are frequently strong on exactly these load-bearing skills and weak on the worded, multi-step presentation IGCSE uses. For them the diagnosis inverts: the foundations are sound and the technique needs building, and a tutor who starts by re-teaching algebra is wasting their time and your money. This is why the first session is diagnostic rather than instructional.

sections.heading: The codes, the tier and the series
paragraphs: Four maths syllabuses are in common use in Dubai schools and they are not interchangeable for revision. Cambridge 0580 sits two papers with one taken without a calculator, so non-calculator fluency and exact form carry real weight. Cambridge 0607 is the graphic-display-calculator syllabus with an investigation element. Pearson 4MA1 sits two equally weighted papers with a calculator throughout, which shifts the risk to rounding and interpretation. Pearson 4MB1 is more compressed and more algebraic with a much smaller past-paper bank.

The tier sits alongside the code. Cambridge entries are Core or Extended and Pearson entries are Foundation or Higher, and the lower tier in each is capped below the top grades. Both facts live on the examination entry rather than in anybody's memory, and one email to the examinations officer asking for the code and tier removes the largest source of wasted revision time in this subject. A student practising the wrong board's papers is working hard in a dialect nobody will speak in the hall.

On the series: Cambridge IGCSE runs in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Those are the windows available to a UAE candidate. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, which deserves emphasis in a district where many families have direct experience of the Indian system and might reasonably assume otherwise. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson's published pattern gives a sense of the surrounding calendar: its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official document rather than any restatement is what a family should plan from.

sections.heading: After results: resit, retake or move on
paragraphs: The post-results decision is the one families make with the least information and the most pressure. Summer results arrive late in August, the November entry closes within weeks, and the script has usually not been seen. The result is a decision taken on disappointment rather than on evidence, and it goes wrong in both directions: students resit a paper they would not improve on, and students accept a grade they could comfortably have lifted.

The evidence that makes this decision properly is the script. If marks were lost to technique, instruction-reading and pacing, a short focused block before November is likely to move the grade, because those recover quickly. If they were lost across the whole paper to genuine content gaps, a November resit eleven weeks later is optimistic, and the honest advice may be to take a different route or to accept the grade and move on.

The second input is what the receiving institution will accept. A school offering a sixth-form place, a university considering an application, or the Ministry equivalency process each have their own requirements and deadlines, and a resit that lands after the deadline it was meant to satisfy has cost a term for nothing. Ask them in writing in June or July, before results, so the answer is in hand when it is needed.

sections.heading: A Deira evening, and the session that holds through a term
paragraphs: Students in this district travel mostly by school bus or on the Green Line. Those attending the Al Qusais, Al Nahda or Abu Hail cluster are generally home between 15:30 and 16:30; those crossing the Creek arrive later. After food and a change of clothes, the slot that survives a full term is 17:00 to 17:30 at the earliest, and later for the longer journeys. Booking earlier in optimism produces reschedules by the third week, and in a dated Year 11 plan a rescheduled session is a lost week rather than a lost hour.

Study conditions in an apartment deserve five minutes of setup rather than being left to chance. A hard surface rather than a sofa, squared paper and a ruler, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, and headphones so a busy household is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page, because the whole diagnostic value of a maths session is watching the working appear and catching a sign error as it happens rather than after it has propagated through three lines.

Where siblings share a room, which is common here, staggered evenings work and a shared session does not. Two students at different points in the course in one hour means one is supervised while the other is taught. If a budget covers one child, making that choice deliberately and using a marking clinic for the other is better than halving the value for both.

Ramadan shifts the pattern for several weeks and Dubai schools adjust their hours. The arrangement that works is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work set between them, agreed before the month begins. For a Year 11 student those weeks frequently sit close to a mock series, which is precisely why planning the shift beats improvising through it.

sections.heading: Permits, limits and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit, which is worth knowing in a district where informal home tuition is widely advertised. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified. Asking a tutor about their permit is an ordinary question, and irritation in response is informative. We would also advise against any arrangement involving your child's own schoolteacher, which the permit's code of conduct and reported regulatory rules both point away from.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will claim one. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE, we do not enter candidates for examinations, and we do not perform Ministry equivalency. A tutoring operation with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we hold none because we have no premises.

On materials and figures: we reference and link official syllabus, specimen and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, and we do not supply board-owned papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions. Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 500; those come from provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table and are the market rather than our price list. We publish no success rates or satisfaction scores.

In this district both Cambridge and Pearson centres are in use, sometimes for different subjects in the same year group, and the code decides which past papers are worth the student's time.

A short written note follows naming the two priority items and whether they are load-bearing or contained gaps, and the note is yours whether you book or not.

If the pattern has moved we continue; if not we change the approach or the tutor. If the problem is solved we say so and stop rather than renewing by default.

For a Year 9 or early Year 10 enquiry the honest recommendation is often one session a week for a term and then a review, which is less than most providers would sell.

whyPoints.title: Load-bearing gaps prioritised over contained ones
whyPoints.description: Index laws, negatives, rearrangement, fractions and form conversion cost marks across several topics and in physics and chemistry too. Fixing those is worth more than fixing the topic the class happens to be on, which is why we do not simply shadow the scheme of work.

whyPoints.title: Reports turned into decisions
whyPoints.description: Each report has one useful question attached to it, and we tell you which. Early Year 10 is about tier trajectory, mid Year 10 about named gaps, the mock about allocation, the final report about what the next institution will accept. Specific questions get specific answers.

whyPoints.title: The resit decision made on evidence, in spring
whyPoints.description: Summer results arrive late in August and the November entry closes within weeks. We tell families to ask the examinations officer in spring when the entry closes and how a script copy is obtained, which turns an August scramble into a decision with evidence behind it.

whyPoints.description: An eight-week block containing a holiday week and a school activity week is six weeks of teaching. We count that at the planning stage and adjust the session number, which is a small administrative habit that keeps the rest of the plan honest.

whyPoints.description: No board or regulator approval, no UAE premises, no home visits in the Emirates, no candidate entries and no equivalency service. Where a regulator appears on this page it is explained and linked rather than used as a credential.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting maths tutoring in Year 10 if nothing looks wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the best-value decision available in this subject. Year 10 produces no alarming documents, which is exactly why the gaps that cap a grade form there unnoticed: index laws applied inconsistently, negatives dropped when expanding, rearrangement that fails when the unknown appears twice. Those take weeks to repair in Year 10 and months in Year 11, because by then every new topic depends on them. One session a week for a term, aimed at assumed skills rather than at this week's lesson, is normally the whole intervention.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE maths tutor come to our flat in Hor Al Anz instead?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Maths sessions here are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the camera angled at the page so the tutor watches the working appear and catches a sign error as it happens. In this district that also means you select from everyone who has taught your child's syllabus code rather than from those willing to travel to Abu Hail on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: What should we do with a disappointing Year 11 mock result?
faqs.answer: Ask for the marked script rather than acting on the grade. The script shows whether marks went to instruction-reading, abandoned method, a genuine content gap, arithmetic slips or questions never reached, and those five point to five different plans with five different costs. Categorise every lost mark, name two priority topics in writing, and subtract the school and public holidays before agreeing how many sessions a block really contains. A family that does this in January is in a different position by March from one that waited.

faqs.question: Which maths gaps matter most in IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The load-bearing ones, because later topics depend on them. Index laws, handling negatives through expansion and factorisation, rearranging a formula where the unknown appears more than once, fractions as both ratios and operators, and converting between forms including standard form and percentage change. A weakness in any of those reappears in trigonometry, algebraic fractions, simultaneous equations and every physics calculation. A weakness in something contained, like probability, costs only its own marks and is much cheaper to leave until later.

faqs.question: Our child came from CBSE and the algebra is fine but the grades are not. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the gap is technique rather than content. IGCSE wraps the mathematics in worded, multi-step scenarios and expects the student to extract what is needed, credits method shown even when the final answer is wrong, and specifies rounding or exact form in ways that are marked literally. A student trained to produce correct answers efficiently loses marks they had earned. That is closed in a term of focused work, and re-teaching algebra the student already has is the common and wasteful alternative.

faqs.question: How do we find out which tier our child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer, because the entry is the only reliable source. Cambridge mathematics is entered at Core or Extended and Pearson at Foundation or Higher, and the lower tier in each is capped below the top grades. The tier also changes what revision should contain, since a Core student working through Extended material is doing unnecessary work and an Extended student revising only Core material is under-prepared. Ask for the syllabus code in the same email, because both facts live on the entry together.

faqs.question: What would need to change for a higher tier entry?
faqs.answer: Ask the department that exact question, because the answer is specific and it is a work plan. Departments decide tier from set performance across Year 10, and they can usually name what they would need to see: consistency on a particular class of question, performance on the supplementary content, or a result in a specific assessment. Acting on that in Year 10 while sets are still fluid is dramatically cheaper than living with a capped grade, and by the spring of Year 11 the entry is lodged and the question has changed.

faqs.question: When should we think about a November resit?
faqs.answer: In spring, before results exist. Summer results arrive late in August and the November entry closes within weeks, which puts the decision under pressure before anyone has seen a script. Ask the examinations officer in the spring when the entry closes and how a script copy can be obtained, and ask the receiving school or institution in writing what grade they will accept and by when. Then the August conversation is a decision with evidence behind it rather than a scramble driven by disappointment.

faqs.question: Would a resit actually improve the grade?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on where the marks went, which is why the script matters. Marks lost to technique, instruction-reading and pacing recover quickly, and a focused block of eight to ten weeks before November can move a grade meaningfully. Marks lost across the whole paper to genuine content gaps are a different proposition, and eleven weeks is optimistic for rebuilding three years of algebra. We will say which situation the evidence supports, including when the honest answer is to accept the grade and change route.

faqs.question: Can a local group class do the job more cheaply?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, often yes. A group class is a reasonable and affordable way to work through material a student is simply behind on, and this district has plenty of them. What a group cannot do is read one student's script against a mark scheme and identify that the losses are coming from rounding instructions and abandoned method. The best value for many families here is group content coverage plus periodic one-to-one marking, which costs less than weekly private teaching and targets better than extra group hours.

faqs.question: Why does our child lose marks when the method was right?
faqs.answer: Usually an instruction. An answer given to two decimal places when three significant figures were asked for, a length supplied where an area was wanted, units omitted, or an exact form requested and a decimal provided. These are reading errors rather than mathematical ones and they are the cheapest marks in the paper to recover. The second common cause is working that was never written down, because method marks are available on multi-step questions even when the final value is wrong and a student who writes only answers forfeits them.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 block need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the weeks remaining and what the script says, and the honest number is usually smaller than families fear if the work is correctly targeted. Sixteen weeks out, one session a week is generally enough. Eight weeks out, two a week with content rationed to two topics. Four weeks out, weekly sessions on pacing and error elimination with nothing new introduced. Always subtract the school and public holidays before agreeing a number, because an eight-week block containing two holiday weeks is six weeks of teaching.

faqs.question: What does maths tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300, and an in-home visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the fee. Monthly figures run about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject. Those come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table rather than from us. We quote after the free trial lesson, once we know what the work actually is.

faqs.question: Should our child take Additional Mathematics alongside the main grade?
faqs.answer: Only once the main grade is secure. Cambridge 0606 brings calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities forward by a year, which removes most of the shock of A Level Mathematics or higher level IB maths later. Taken while the main grade is still uncertain, it competes for exactly the revision time that grade needed, and the usual outcome is two mediocre results instead of one strong one. A tutor should tell you plainly when the right advice is to drop it, and the decision belongs early in Year 11 rather than in the spring.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-international.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE mathematics across Cambridge 0580 and 0980 at Core and Extended tier and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 at Foundation and Higher, for students travelling out of International City to schools across eastern Dubai.

intro.heading: Mathematics in a week with an hour of travel in it
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject most affected by a long commute, and not for the reason families expect. It is not that the student is too tired to understand - it is that mathematics improves through repetition rather than through explanation, and repetition needs small regular slots rather than one long one. A student who travels out of International City to Silicon Oasis or Al Qusais has fewer of those small slots than a student who walks to school.

So the planning question is not 'when can we fit a lesson' but 'where do twenty minutes of practice go on three evenings a week'. That is the hour that moves a mathematics grade. The weekly session is where the practice gets marked, the errors get named and the next set gets chosen, and it is worth far more when it sits on top of practice than when it stands alone.

This matters because of what mathematics marks are actually lost to. Working omitted, so a correct answer scores one mark out of three. Rounding applied at an intermediate step, so every later accuracy mark falls. Units missed or converted wrongly. A calculator left in the wrong angle mode. The final long question left blank rather than attempted for partial credit. Every one of those is a habit, and habits change through doing rather than through being told.

The second practical matter is the specification, which takes five minutes to confirm and prevents a term of waste. Cambridge runs Mathematics 0580 and the 9-1 graded 0980, each split into Core and Extended. Pearson runs 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers, and 4MB1 as a separate qualification. Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants; 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. Drilling hand arithmetic for the wrong specification is weeks spent on nothing.

Students in these clusters also change schools within Dubai more often than in more settled districts, which means a mid-course change of board is a live possibility. That leaves content covered under one specification and never under the other - invisible on a report, obvious in a marked paper, and worth looking for deliberately rather than discovering in May.

One more thing worth settling early is the tier, because it may be the real constraint rather than the teaching. Cambridge Core caps the achievable grade at C or grade 5 and Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5, while Extended and Higher run the full range. A student entered for Core who needs grade 6 for A Level Mathematics cannot reach it however disciplined the practice, so the entry list is worth reading before any lesson plan is written.

IB Gram delivers this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are an India-only service for us. For a household on this timetable the practical gain is simple: an online session starts when the laptop opens, rather than when a second person has also finished crossing the city at half past six.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-international.subjectsIntro: The topics to drill, ordered by what they are worth across a paper rather than by syllabus order, because when time is short that is the only sensible order.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying algebraic fractions and rearranging with the unknown appearing twice. Appears inside questions throughout both papers rather than in one section, which makes it the highest-value drilling target in the subject.

subjects.name: Number and arithmetic by hand
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form and estimation worked without a calculator. Essential for Cambridge variants with a non-calculator paper, and entirely irrelevant for Pearson 4MA1 - which is why the specification check comes first.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic equations, inequalities on a number line, simultaneous equations solved algebraically, with quadratic simultaneous equations at Extended. Sign errors account for most of the lost marks and respond directly to short daily practice.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry at Core; the sine and cosine rules, triangle area and three-dimensional problems at Extended. Marks go on not drawing the triangle, choosing the wrong rule, and leaving the calculator in the wrong angle mode.

subjects.name: Geometry, circle theorems and similarity
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, congruence and similarity, with circle theorems at Extended. Circle theorem questions require the theorem to be named as part of the reasoning, and an unnamed correct answer loses the reasoning marks every time.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Area, surface area, volume, arcs and sectors, speed, density and pressure. Lost marks concentrate on unit conversion, especially cubic centimetres to litres, and on rounding applied before the final step of a multi-stage calculation.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and tree diagrams, with conditional probability at Extended. Frequency-density questions are among the most reliably mishandled on the whole paper.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, graph sketching and transformations. Extended-only territory in Cambridge, and a reliable source of marks for students who understand transformations rather than memorising a list.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry with ratio along a line, and the four transformations. Extended questions combine vectors with ratio, which rewards drawing and labelling the diagram before calculating anything.

subjects.name: Calculus foundations
subjects.description: Gradient functions, differentiation of polynomials and turning points where the specification includes them. Worth attention beyond the examination, because it is the direct bridge into A Level Mathematics and the Diploma courses.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MB1 Specification B content
subjects.description: A separate qualification with its own content and examination style, taken by a minority of schools. Confirm it explicitly on the entry list, because preparation for Specification A does not transfer and the difference is not cosmetic.

subjects.name: Bridging for Year 12
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, basic differentiation and trigonometric identities, all assumed from the first week of A Level or Diploma mathematics. Six to eight summer sessions, when the commute has gone.

sections.heading: A practice plan for twenty minutes, three times a week
paragraphs: This is the part of mathematics tutoring that decides the outcome and almost nobody plans. The weekly session is the visible purchase; the practice between sessions is where the marks come from. For a student who spends an hour a day travelling, the practice has to be short enough to happen on a weekday evening after school work, which in practice means twenty minutes rather than an hour.

Short practice works for mathematics specifically because the lost marks are habits. Showing working, controlling rounding, checking units, classifying a stationary point, attempting rather than abandoning the last question - each of these changes through repetition. Twenty minutes of mixed questions three times a week produces more change in a month than one two-hour session at the weekend, and it fits a week that is already full.

The structure that works is deliberately unvaried: five minutes of arithmetic or algebra warm-up, ten minutes on the current error type, five minutes on a question from a topic already covered so it does not decay. The last part matters more than it sounds, because IGCSE mathematics is cumulative and a topic learned in Year 10 and never revisited is a topic lost by May.

The table below sets out a week. It is modest on purpose: in this district the commonest failure is an ambitious plan abandoned by the second term, and a plan the household sustains for two terms beats a better one that lasts three weeks. The test is whether it still happens on a bad week rather than a good one.

sections.heading: What to confirm before anybody teaches anything
paragraphs: Five minutes of administration prevents a term of misdirected work, and in this district it is worth more than usual because students here change schools mid-course more often than in more settled neighbourhoods. A change of board in Year 10 leaves content covered under one specification and never under the other, which no report will show you.

The document to ask for is the examination entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option for every paper. The examinations officer produces it in minutes and the class teacher often does not know it. With it in hand, three decisions follow immediately - whether hand-arithmetic practice belongs in the plan, which topics the tier includes, and whether a tutor prepared for Specification A is any use at all.

The non-calculator question is the sharpest of the three. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its equally weighted papers. A student drilled in mental and written arithmetic for two calculator papers has spent weeks earning nothing, and a student who has never practised without one meets Cambridge Paper 1 unprepared despite understanding every topic on it.

sections.heading: Which topics to drill when there is not time for everything
paragraphs: In the final months, syllabus order is the wrong order. What matters is which topics appear most often across the papers and which ones repay practice fastest, and those two criteria agree more than they disagree. Algebraic manipulation is first on both counts, because it sits inside questions throughout rather than in a section of its own.

After that the priorities split by tier. At Core and Foundation, the reliable gains are number work, ratio and proportion, mensuration with its unit conversions, and basic trigonometry. At Extended and Higher, they are algebraic fractions, circle theorems with the theorem named, histograms with unequal intervals, vector questions involving ratio, and the sine and cosine rules.

The table below sets out a drilling order with a rough session count for each. Treat the numbers as planning figures rather than promises, and let the marked paper override them: a student who is already secure on trigonometry should not be drilled on it because a table said so. The order exists to prevent the commonest mistake, which is starting at the beginning of the syllabus and running out of weeks.

One more principle that matters when time is short. Partial attempts score in mathematics - setting up the right equation, drawing the right diagram, stating the right rule earns marks even when the answer never arrives - and students routinely do not believe this until a tutor shows them a mark scheme. Teaching that one fact converts blank space into marks on every paper.

sections.heading: Non-calculator discipline, and calculator discipline
paragraphs: Where the specification includes a non-calculator paper, it is a separate examination requiring separate preparation, and it is where a certain kind of capable student quietly loses marks. Fraction arithmetic, percentages, standard form, surd manipulation and estimation all have to be fluent by hand. A student who has used a calculator since Year 7 can understand everything on the paper and still run out of time.

The preparation is short and repetitive, which fits the practice structure on this page exactly: five minutes of hand calculation at the start of every practice slot, every time, for a term. It is the least interesting thing in a mathematics plan and it appears directly in a mark. It also cannot be crammed, which is another argument for starting it in Year 10.

On calculator papers the discipline runs the other way. The recurring errors are angle mode, premature rounding of a stored value, and reaching a numerical answer on a question that wanted algebraic reasoning and awarded marks for it. Storing intermediate values rather than retyping rounded ones is a two-minute habit that protects accuracy marks through an entire paper.

For Pearson 4MA1 candidates, where a calculator is permitted in both papers, the hours that would have gone into hand arithmetic belong elsewhere: the extended multi-step problems at the end of each paper, which carry substantial marks and are left blank far more often than they are attempted. Partial attempts score. Blank space does not, and that single fact is worth more across a paper than most topic revision.

sections.heading: From the mocks to June, on this timetable
paragraphs: Mock results in Dubai schools usually arrive in the second term, leaving a defined run to the June papers. Ask for the marked script and the question-level breakdown rather than the grade, because for mathematics the script is unusually informative: it shows not only which topics failed but how the marks were lost, which decides whether the remaining weeks go on content or on habits.

Read it for pattern. Marks lost with correct final answers mean method - working omitted or rounding applied early. Marks lost in clusters mean a topic. Marks lost heavily in the final third mean pacing, which responds fastest of the three to timed practice. A gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 is a question-style problem rather than a knowledge gap, and in mathematics it is often the calculator-versus-hand distinction showing up.

The plan from there, for a household in these clusters, is the same shape as the rest of the year with the weighting shifted: the weekday session becomes mark-scheme walkthrough on timed questions, the three practice slots become past-paper question sets by type, and the weekend morning becomes a complete paper every week without exception. No new content enters the plan in the final fortnight.

On dates: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones and says using the wrong version is the candidate's own risk.

sections.heading: The tier ceiling, checked before the teaching
paragraphs: Before buying a practice plan it is worth knowing whether the constraint is teaching at all. Cambridge Core caps the achievable grade at C or grade 5; Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5. Extended and Higher run the full range. A student entered for Core who needs grade 6 for A Level Mathematics or for the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches cannot reach it however good the practice, and no amount of technique work moves a ceiling.

Both lower tiers comfortably satisfy Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, which asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. So equivalency is almost never the reason to buy mathematics tutoring, and anyone suggesting otherwise is not describing the published rule.

The number that matters is the sixth-form requirement, and it belongs to the receiving school. Ask two sixth forms in Year 10 what grade they require for mathematics at A Level and for Analysis and Approaches, in writing. If the answer is incompatible with the tier your child is entered for, that is the problem to address first, and it is addressed with marked evidence at the higher tier gathered during Year 10.

Where a tier change is worth pursuing, the work is a named list rather than a general standard: function notation, circle theorems, vector geometry with ratio, histograms with unequal intervals and the harder trigonometry. A term of targeted sessions plus the practice structure on this page can produce the marked papers a school responds to. By the second term of Year 11 entries are made and the window has closed almost everywhere.

sections.heading: What it costs, and matching the band to the work
paragraphs: Every figure here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram rate. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For Key Stage 3 catch-up and Core-tier content that band contains genuinely usable help, and for a practice-marking session it is often enough.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, which is where most useful IGCSE mathematics tutoring in Dubai happens. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and advertised home-tutor rates at 200 to 500, with published monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, with published online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. For the wider household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year.

The useful principle is matching the band to the work rather than buying the highest one affordable. A session whose job is to mark practice, name errors and set the next questions does not require a premium specialist. A session whose job is to rebuild Extended-tier algebra or to argue a tier change with evidence does. Paying specialist rates for practice marking is as wasteful as paying budget rates for a tier push.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: There is one question worth asking before the first paid session, and it takes a sentence: do you hold a current MoHRE permit, and may I see it? The permit is the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor who teaches legitimately has no cost reason to be without one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere, which means any specific dirham amount quoted at you - by a tutor, an agency or a neighbour - was invented.

The reason that question is fair rather than awkward is that almost nobody teaching mathematics in International City is excluded from the permit. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students - which covers the engineering undergraduate two buildings over as squarely as it covers a full-time teacher. Nor is the process onerous. It runs through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, available via the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Two days, no fee, and a wide eligibility list leaves an unpermitted arrangement without much of an explanation.

One arrangement to decline rather than pursue: the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An offer of your child's own mathematics teacher, privately, is a problem for the teacher before it is a benefit to you.

What we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson; no promise about grades and no published predicted scores; no ratings we cannot evidence with countable dated reviews; and no board papers or mark schemes supplied as downloads, since we cite and link the official sources instead.

process.title: Tell us when the bus actually arrives
process.description: The time your child walks through the door on a bad day, not the end of the school day. That single fact sets the session slot, and a slot set against the worst case is a slot that still exists in February rather than one quietly abandoned.

process.title: Send the entry list and one marked paper
process.description: Subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option from the examinations officer, plus a recent marked paper. The first tells us whether hand-arithmetic practice belongs in the plan; the second tells us whether the losses are method, topic or pacing.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written note
process.description: A real lesson on real mathematics with the student working while the tutor watches. Afterwards a plain summary: the three or four recurring reasons for lost marks, and what the first six sessions and the practice slots will target.

process.title: Agree three practice slots, not a suggestion
process.description: Twenty minutes on three named evenings, with the structure fixed: warm-up, current error type, one revisit question. The session marks the practice and sets the next set. This is the part that changes the grade, and it only happens if it has a slot.

process.title: Protect the weekend morning
process.description: One complete paper to time, then walked through against the published mark scheme, every week through Year 11. It competes with no school homework and it is the only slot where a full paper is possible from this district.

whyPoints.title: Practice slots planned, not just a weekly hour
whyPoints.description: Mathematics marks are lost to habits, and habits change through repetition. Twenty minutes on three evenings beats one long weekend sitting, and for a student who travels an hour a day it is the only version that actually happens.

whyPoints.title: The specification confirmed before anything else
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants; Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. Drilling hand arithmetic for the wrong specification is weeks spent earning nothing, and it happens constantly.

whyPoints.title: A drilling order, not syllabus order
whyPoints.description: Algebraic manipulation first because it sits inside questions throughout, then working and rounding discipline, then mensuration, trigonometry, circle theorems and frequency density. Starting at the beginning of the syllabus is how families run out of weeks.

whyPoints.title: Mid-course board changes looked for deliberately
whyPoints.description: Students in these clusters move schools within Dubai more often than most, and a change of specification leaves content covered under one syllabus and never the other. It is invisible on a report and obvious in a marked paper.

whyPoints.title: The tier checked before the teaching
whyPoints.description: Core caps at C or grade 5 and Foundation at grade 5. A student needing grade 6 for sixth form cannot reach it from Core whatever the practice plan, so the entry list comes before the lesson plan rather than after it.

whyPoints.title: The band matched to the job
whyPoints.description: Marking practice and setting questions does not need a premium specialist; rebuilding Extended algebra or building a tier-change case does. Paying specialist rates for practice marking is as wasteful as paying budget rates for a tier push.

faqs.question: Can I get an IGCSE maths tutor in International City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your flat, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. For mathematics on this timetable the online version has a practical advantage: the session starts when the laptop opens rather than when a second person has also crossed the city at half past six, and the tutor can be matched to your child's exact syllabus code rather than chosen from the few who live within reach of Al Warsan.

faqs.question: How much practice should my child do between sessions?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes on three evenings a week, with a fixed structure: five minutes of arithmetic or algebra warm-up, ten minutes on the current error type, five minutes on a topic already covered so it does not decay. That beats one two-hour session at the weekend for mathematics specifically, because the lost marks are habits and habits change through repetition. It also fits a week that already contains an hour a day of travel.

faqs.question: Why does short practice work better than a long session for maths?
faqs.answer: Because the marks are not mostly lost to misunderstanding. They are lost to showing no working, rounding at an intermediate step, missing units, leaving the calculator in the wrong angle mode, and abandoning the final long question. Those are behaviours, and behaviours change by being repeated correctly many times rather than by being explained well once. Spacing the practice across the week also slows the decay of topics covered months earlier.

faqs.question: What should we confirm with the school before booking?
faqs.answer: The examination entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option for every paper, from the examinations officer rather than the class teacher. Four specifications are common in Dubai - Cambridge 0580 and 0980, Pearson 4MA1 and the separate 4MB1 - and they differ in grading scale, tiers and calculator rules. With that list, three decisions follow immediately about what belongs in the plan and what would be wasted effort.

faqs.question: Does my child need non-calculator practice?
faqs.answer: Only if the specification includes a non-calculator component, which common Cambridge 0580 variants do and Pearson 4MA1 does not. The right dose where it applies is five minutes of hand calculation at the start of every practice slot, every time, for a term - fraction arithmetic, percentages, standard form, surds and estimation. It cannot be crammed, which is another reason to start it in Year 10 rather than after the Year 11 mocks.

faqs.question: Which topics should we drill first if time is short?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation, because it sits inside questions across both papers rather than in a section of its own. Then the working, rounding and units discipline, which recovers marks on every question. Then mensuration with its unit conversions, trigonometry including the sine and cosine rules at Extended, circle theorems with the theorem actually named, and histograms with unequal intervals. Let the marked paper override that order wherever it disagrees.

faqs.question: Why does my son leave the last question on each paper blank?
faqs.answer: Usually because it looks unfamiliar and the time has gone, and both are fixable. Partial attempts score in mathematics: setting up the right equation, drawing the right diagram or stating the right rule earns marks even when the answer never arrives, and most students do not believe this until a tutor shows them a mark scheme. The timing fix is a minutes-per-mark habit practised on half papers, which usually recovers ten minutes that previously disappeared.

faqs.question: My daughter changed schools and boards in Year 10. What now?
faqs.answer: Look for the gap deliberately rather than waiting for it to appear. A mid-course specification change leaves content covered under one syllabus and never under the other, which no report will show. Ask both schools for the entry details and have one timed paper at the new specification marked question by question. In this district school moves are common enough that this is worth doing as a matter of routine after any transfer.

faqs.question: What time can a maths session start on a weekday from these clusters?
faqs.answer: Around six, and from the China Cluster or on a bus route it is closer to half past. The school day may end at half past two, but the afternoon return makes multiple stops and the Dragon Mart and Ras Al Khor junctions are slower then. Set the slot against a bad day rather than an average one: a session booked for five that starts at twenty past five every week loses a quarter of itself across two years.

faqs.question: Is Core tier a problem for A Level maths later?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Cambridge Core caps the achievable grade at C or grade 5 and Pearson Foundation at grade 5, while A Level Mathematics and the IB Diploma's Analysis and Approaches typically ask for grade 6 or above. So a Core candidate is often excluded before the paper is sat. Both tiers comfortably satisfy Ministry of Education equivalency, which asks for no less than E or grade 3 across five subjects, so equivalency is not the number to plan around.

faqs.question: Can we still move from Core to Extended tier?
faqs.answer: In Year 10, often, with marked evidence. The higher tier adds a named list - function notation, circle theorems, vector geometry with ratio, histograms with unequal intervals, the sine and cosine rules - rather than a generally higher standard, which makes it schedulable. A term of targeted sessions plus the practice structure on this page can produce papers at that tier for the school to look at. By the second term of Year 11 entries are made almost everywhere.

faqs.question: What should we ask for when the mocks come back?
faqs.answer: The marked script and the question-level breakdown, not the grade. For mathematics the script is unusually informative: marks lost with correct final answers mean method, marks lost in clusters mean a topic, and marks lost heavily in the final third mean pacing. A gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 often turns out to be the calculator-versus-hand distinction showing up, which is a fortnight of targeted work rather than a term of general revision.

faqs.question: When are the maths papers sat, and could the timetable be wrong?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November - its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. On the timetable itself: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate version for each, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE maths tutoring cost from this district?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026: budget and university-student online tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home one-to-one with travel at AED 180 to 500. Match the band to the job: marking practice does not need a premium specialist, while rebuilding Extended algebra does.

faqs.question: Must a tutor teaching maths privately here hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified. Ask to see it; somebody who holds one shows it without hesitation.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-international.closingHeading: Send the entry list, one marked paper, and the bus time
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-international.closingBody: If your child is sitting IGCSE mathematics and you live in International City, three things set the whole plan. The entry list tells us the board, code and tier, and therefore whether hand-arithmetic practice belongs in it. One marked paper tells us whether the losses are method, topic or pacing. And the time the bus actually arrives on a bad day tells us where the session and the three twenty-minute practice slots can sit. The trial lesson is free and comes with a written note; lessons are one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jbr.tutorsIntro: These tutors are listed by specification rather than by the word maths, because 0580 Extended and 4MA1 Higher are examined differently enough to need different teaching. Each names the code and the papers they have taught, and each holds a slot inside the window a JBR weekday leaves after the commute.

intro.heading: Does the tutor know 0580 from 4MA1? That is the whole question
paragraphs: Parents in JBR searching for an IGCSE maths tutor are usually trying to solve a proximity problem, and the proximity problem is not the real one. The real one is specification knowledge. Dubai schools enter students for at least three different mathematics qualifications that all get called IGCSE in conversation, and the differences between them are not cosmetic. Cambridge 0580 now sets a paper with no calculator permitted. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its papers and supplies a formula sheet. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 expects graphical-calculator work and a different investigation style. A tutor teaching the first as though it were the second will drill the wrong habits for a year.

The second thing a parent needs is the tier, and it carries a hard ceiling. Cambridge tiers 0580 as Core or Extended, and a Core entry cannot be awarded above a grade C. Pearson tiers 4MA1 as Foundation or Higher, and a Foundation entry cannot be awarded above a 5. The school makes that entry, usually on Year 10 evidence, and it can be changed up to the final entry deadline and not afterwards. Families who find out in the spring of Year 11 that the ceiling is in place have found out too late to move it.

Those two facts between them explain most disappointing IGCSE maths results in this part of Dubai, and neither of them is about ability. A capable student entered at Core will finish with a C. A student who has spent two years with a calculator permanently in hand will lose marks on Cambridge Paper 2 within the first ten minutes. Both outcomes are foreseeable in Year 10 and both are cheap to prevent, which is why the useful tutoring window in this subject is earlier than parents expect.

Geography matters less than families think but it is not irrelevant. There is no school inside the JBR towers, so every student here commutes: to Al Sufouh on a short run, to Al Barsha and Al Barsha South on a longer one, out to the villa belt around Emirates Hills and The Meadows on the longest. Mathematics is the subject least tolerant of a tired hour, because it needs a student willing to begin a line of working without knowing where it ends. The commute therefore sets the session time, and for the longest runs a weekend morning buys more than a weekday evening does at the same price.

This page is built to answer the specification question properly. It compares 0580, 0607 and 4MA1 on everything that changes teaching. It explains what the Cambridge non-calculator paper did to revision plans. It shows how to confirm what the formula sheet actually gives your child. It names where marks go missing topic by topic, sets out the tier decision and its deadline, covers Additional Mathematics and the step into A Level or the Diploma, and prices the market with every figure attributed. Lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India.
