dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: IGCSE mathematics sits in the middle of a longer sequence, and the decisions that matter are taken a stage before the one a family is worrying about. These are the four stages as a JBR household meets them.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint mathematics
programmes.description: The three years in which tiering is effectively decided, assessed internally and in many schools through Cambridge Checkpoint tests, which run in March, May and October. Checkpoint carries no certificate weight but schools use it to stream and to recommend Core or Extended. Number fluency, algebraic manipulation and the ability to work without a calculator are the three things that predict the later entry.
programmes.countryNote: Around JBR the Year 9 options process is where this becomes visible to parents, usually through an options booklet published in the spring term. A family reading that booklet carefully and asking which maths specification the school enters is doing the single most valuable piece of work available in this subject, and it costs nothing.

programmes.name: International GCSE mathematics
programmes.description: Two years ending in a tiered entry. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core, graded C to G, and Extended, graded A* to E, with a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper at each tier. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation, graded 5 to 1, and Higher, graded 9 to 4, with two two-hour papers and a calculator permitted in both. Cambridge 0607 is a separate syllabus built for cohorts heading into the IB.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 form the base, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Mathematics is almost always one of the five, and a capped tier that still delivers a comfortable pass does not disturb that arithmetic. What it does affect is the post-16 threshold.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is a separate single-tier qualification sat alongside or after 0580 Extended, graded A* to E, with two papers. It assumes the Extended content and then introduces calculus, series, further trigonometry and more demanding algebra. Schools offer it to the strongest mathematicians as preparation for A Level or Higher Level Diploma mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of schools around Al Barsha and the villa belt run 0606 as an extension set, and a JBR family offered it should treat the offer as information about their child rather than as extra homework. Students who take it arrive in Year 12 with the single biggest advantage available in maths, and those who decline it usually spend the first Diploma term catching up on calculus.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: The two destinations the IGCSE grade opens or closes. A Level mathematics departments publish a minimum IGCSE grade, usually at the upper end of the Extended or Higher range. IB schools set their own threshold for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, which is the most demanding of the four IB mathematics courses and the one most dependent on secure algebra.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in this part of Dubai run IGCSE to 16 and then offer both routes, so the choice arrives inside the existing school. The relevant signal differs: A Level selectors look at depth in mathematics alone, IB coordinators look at the whole transcript across six subject groups. Both read the mathematics grade first, which is why the Year 11 result matters past the certificate.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Below are the mathematics entries and the adjacent subjects JBR families ask about, listed with codes. If the code against your child's subject differs from the one here, that single detail is the most useful thing to tell a prospective tutor.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Extended
subjects.description: A non-calculator paper of two hours and a calculator paper of two and a half, which means written method cannot be avoided for two years. Algebraic manipulation, surds, indices and the harder trigonometry are where Extended candidates most often lose ground, and the non-calculator paper exposes any reliance on technology inside the first few questions.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Core
subjects.description: A one-hour non-calculator paper and a ninety-minute calculator paper covering the Core content only. The ceiling is a C, which is the fact a parent most needs to know before accepting the entry. Core candidates lose marks on multi-step word problems and on the number work the Extended paper takes for granted, rather than on advanced topics they never meet.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 Higher
subjects.description: Two two-hour papers, calculator permitted in both, formula sheet supplied. Because nothing is sat without a calculator, candidates are rarely exposed on arithmetic, but they are exposed on timing: the papers are long and the final questions are where the top grades are decided. Students who finish with ten minutes spare have usually not attempted enough.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 Foundation
subjects.description: The same two-paper structure at the lower tier, capped at grade 5. A student comfortably achieving a 5 in Foundation mocks is often the student who should have been entered at Higher, and that conversation has to happen before the final entry deadline. Afterwards the ceiling is fixed whatever the mock papers say.

subjects.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A distinct syllabus chosen by schools whose cohorts continue into the IB Diploma. A short non-calculator paper sits alongside a longer calculator paper, and graphical-calculator fluency is expected rather than optional. Students transferring between 0607 and 0580 mid-course find the question style unfamiliar even where the content overlaps.

subjects.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.levels: Single tier, graded A* to E
subjects.description: Two papers, no tiering, and content that assumes 0580 Extended is already secure: calculus, series, further trigonometry and harder algebra. It is the best available preparation for A Level or Higher Level Diploma mathematics, and it is also the qualification most likely to be underestimated, because it is sat in the same year as eight or nine other subjects.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics, where the maths is the real problem
subjects.description: A substantial share of physics enquiries from this neighbourhood are rearranging and proportion problems in disguise. Circuit reasoning, gradients from graphs and unit conversion account for more lost marks than any physics concept does. Testing whether the maths or the physics is weak takes one session and frequently changes which tutor is needed.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry calculation strands
subjects.description: Mole calculations, percentage yield, titration arithmetic and empirical formula work. Students secure in mathematics and shaky in chemistry behave differently from students shaky in both, and the second group gains more from maths support first. The multi-step calculation questions on the Extended papers are where this shows up.

subjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies and Economics quantitative work
subjects.description: Break-even analysis, ratio work, index numbers and percentage change. The mathematics is elementary and the context is not, so students who can calculate correctly still lose marks by failing to interpret the figure they produced. Data-response questions are the most under-practised part of both specifications.

subjects.name: MYP mathematics for pre-IGCSE years
subjects.description: Assessed against four criteria out of eight each, with investigating patterns the one that most reliably separates a strong mathematician from a fast one. For JBR families in MYP schools that will switch to IGCSE at 14, this criterion is also the best early warning of whether Extended or Higher will be comfortable.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jbr.regionsTitle: Which specifications the schools around JBR actually enter
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jbr.regionsIntro: The difference that matters between these neighbourhoods is not distance from the towers. It is which mathematics specification the local schools enter, how early they fix the tier, and what the return journey does to a weekday session. All three vary across a short stretch of New Dubai.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Established British-curriculum schools with settled departmental choices, which makes the code easy to confirm with one email. The short run from JBR also means these are the families who can realistically hold a 16:15 maths hour, which matters for non-calculator drilling.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The widest spread of specifications in this cluster, with several schools running IGCSE to 16 before splitting into A Level and the Diploma. Families here are the most likely to be unable to name their child's code without checking, because it differs by school and sometimes by set.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Across Al Mamsha Street, sharing the tram line and most school buses with JBR, so session windows are effectively identical. Marina and JBR students frequently sit in the same sets, which means a tutor matched for one is matched for the other.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: A highway crossing away, adding minutes at the worst point of the afternoon. JLT students attending the same Al Barsha schools start about fifteen minutes later than their JBR classmates, and for a non-calculator session those fifteen minutes are not trivial.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs
regions.note: The villa belt, with long-established schools and broader option structures that more often include Additional Mathematics as an extension set. The commute is the longest in this set, which pushes serious paper practice to the weekend.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Circle
regions.note: Newer schools absorbing New Dubai demand, with several running Pearson specifications. The return leg runs against the afternoon flow, so a 16:45 start holds up more reliably here than the distance from JBR suggests.

regions.name: Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Older British schools with long IGCSE histories and departments that have entered the same specification for years. Students joining mid-course from a different board are the group most likely to need a short question-style conversion rather than content teaching.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: JBR timings plus one bridge crossing, which is the variable that converts a dependable weekday slot into an uncertain one. Booking fifteen minutes later is a cheaper fix than hoping the bridge behaves on a Thursday.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: The main destination for JBR secondary students and the hardest cluster in which to guess the specification, because it varies by school and occasionally by set. Ask the department directly, or read the code off the statement of entry, before buying any hours in this subject.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the short-commute schools
schoolClusters.note: Settled departmental board choices and the shortest run from the towers. These are the families for whom a consistent weekly maths slot across both IGCSE years is genuinely achievable, which matters more in mathematics than in any other subject.

schoolClusters.city: The villa belt, Jumeirah Village and the older British schools
schoolClusters.note: Broader option structures, larger cohorts, and the places most likely to offer Additional Mathematics as an extension set. Mock timetables here are usually published early enough to plan a pre-series block around, which is the best use of a maths budget in Year 11.

sections.heading: Three specifications, one name: 0580, 0607 and 4MA1 compared
paragraphs: A tutor who knows IGCSE maths does not exist in the abstract. What exists is a tutor who knows the specification your child is entered for, and in Dubai that will be one of three in the overwhelming majority of cases. Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1. They differ on calculator policy, paper length, grading scale, tier structure and the formula support printed in the paper.

Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended. At each tier the candidate sits one paper on which no calculator is permitted and one on which it is. For Extended that is a two-hour non-calculator paper and a two-and-a-half-hour calculator paper; for Core, one hour and ninety minutes respectively. Grades run A* to G across the syllabus, with the Core tier capped at C. Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher, sits two papers of two hours each with a calculator permitted in both, supplies a formula sheet, and grades 9 to 1 with the Foundation tier capped at 5.

Cambridge 0607 is the one families most often cannot place. It is a separate syllabus, chosen by schools whose cohorts continue into the IB Diploma, with graphical-calculator work expected rather than permitted and an investigation style closer to the Diploma exploration than to a standard IGCSE paper. A student moving between 0607 and 0580 partway through two years meets unfamiliar question grammar even where the content overlaps almost completely.

Read the table against your child's statement of entry rather than against memory. The mark totals and component weightings are printed in the syllabus document for the year of entry, and because the Cambridge structure changed with the 2025 syllabus, an older document or an older revision guide will describe a different examination from the one your child is sitting.

sections.heading: What the Cambridge non-calculator paper changed, and who it caught
paragraphs: The 2025 Cambridge mathematics structure put a paper in front of every 0580 candidate on which no calculator may be used, and in Dubai it has caught a particular kind of student: the one who has been quietly competent for five years with a calculator in hand. Their school assessments were fine. Their homework was fine. Then a mock arrived with the calculator taken away and the marks fell by two grades, which looked like a sudden collapse and was in fact a long-standing gap becoming visible.

The content that bites is not advanced. It is fractions without decimals, indices and surds, proportion, percentage reversal, factorising and the arithmetic inside a multi-step word problem. Students can do all of it; what they cannot do is do it quickly, in writing, under time pressure, without checking each step on a screen. That is a motor skill as much as a mathematical one and it rebuilds in weeks rather than months, provided the sessions actually remove the calculator rather than talking about removing it.

For a family in JBR this changes when tutoring is worth buying. The non-calculator weakness is detectable in Year 10 from a single twenty-minute written test, long before it costs anything, and it is cheapest to fix then. Discovered in a Year 11 mock, the same gap now competes with eight other subjects for revision time. A tutor's first session on a Cambridge entry should include an unseen non-calculator question, every time, because that is the fastest available diagnosis of where the real problem is.

Pearson candidates are not exposed in the same way, since 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers. Their equivalent trap is timing: two two-hour papers with the hardest questions at the end, where a student who works carefully through the early questions and runs out of time loses exactly the marks that separate a 7 from a 9. Different specification, different failure mode, different hour.

sections.heading: The formula question: what the paper gives your child and what it does not
paragraphs: Every IGCSE maths candidate is given some formula support and almost no parent knows which. This matters because it determines what is worth memorising and what is a waste of revision time. Pearson 4MA1 supplies a formula sheet with the papers. Cambridge prints a list of formulas with the 0580 papers. What neither does is supply every result a student is expected to use fluently, and the gap between those two categories is where a term of misdirected revision goes.

Rather than asserting what is on your child's paper, the reliable method is to look. Download the specimen paper for the specific code and the year of entry from the awarding body's own site and read the front matter and the formula page. That takes ten minutes and it settles the question definitively for your child's examination rather than for a version of it from three years ago. Revision guides are frequently a syllabus behind, and this is one of the places where that lag does real damage.

The reason to do this early is that it changes the shape of practice. A student who knows a result will be printed should practise recognising when it applies, not reciting it. A student who knows a result will not be printed should practise it to automaticity, because hunting for a half-remembered formula under timing costs more than the mark itself. Those are two different kinds of session and a tutor can only plan them once the formula position is confirmed.

The table below is a checklist rather than a claim. Work down it with the specimen paper open, and the result is a one-page summary of what your child must know cold, which is the single most useful revision document a Year 11 mathematician can have.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: The losses are predictable and they are rarely conceptual. The largest category across both boards is incomplete method: a student who reaches a correct answer without writing enough working loses method marks they had earned, and a student whose working is unreadable loses them for the same reason. Mark schemes award specified method marks at specified points, and a student who has never read one does not know where those points are.

The second category is rounding and accuracy. Premature rounding partway through a multi-step calculation produces a final answer outside the accepted tolerance, and the mark goes even though every step was understood. Students also lose marks by giving money to three decimal places, angles to the nearest whole degree when more precision was wanted, and answers without units. None of this is mathematics; all of it is marks.

The third is the word problem, and specifically the step between reading and writing. Students who can solve a simultaneous equation cannot always see that the paragraph in front of them contains one. This is the difficulty that produces the biggest gap between a student's apparent ability in class and their performance on a paper, and it responds to practice on extraction rather than to more algebra.

The fourth is topic-specific and board-specific, and the table sets out the recurring offenders with the paper on which each one usually shows. Use it to turn a vague school report comment into a session objective. A comment about weakness in algebra is not actionable; a comment about losing marks on index laws in a non-calculator paper is.

sections.heading: Tier, ceiling and the Year 10 decision that fixes it
paragraphs: This is the most consequential decision in IGCSE mathematics and it is made largely out of sight. Cambridge enters a candidate at Core, capped at grade C, or Extended, graded A* to E. Pearson enters at Foundation, capped at 5, or Higher, graded 9 to 4. The department makes that entry on Year 10 evidence, it is usually provisional, and it can be revised up to the final entry deadline. In the UAE that deadline belongs to one of two series: Cambridge June, whose entries close in the spring months ahead of the papers, or the November series, which doubles as the resit route. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and the tier on them was fixed long before the timetable appeared. After the deadline the ceiling is fixed, and the only remaining question is how many marks can be won inside it.

Higher is not automatically better. A student who cannot access the Extended or Higher content securely can finish with a lower grade than the same student would have achieved at the capped tier, because the lower-tier paper rewards confident performance on foundation material. The question is not which tier is more ambitious, it is which tier this student can perform across in the months remaining, and that is a judgement that needs a marked mock script on the table rather than a general impression.

The intervention that genuinely changes the outcome sits in the window between a weak Year 10 result and the entry deadline. Eight to twelve focused hours on the content that separates the tiers, completed before entries close, is what keeps the higher ceiling available. The identical hours spent in March cannot recover a capped grade, which makes them the same money bought at the wrong time.

One UAE-specific note. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A capped tier that delivers a comfortable pass satisfies that. What a capped grade can do is fall below a post-16 department's own published threshold for A Level mathematics or Higher Level Diploma mathematics, so check those thresholds before accepting a tier recommendation rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: Past papers: how many, which ones, and the mark-scheme habit
paragraphs: The single most under-used revision tool in this subject is the mark scheme, and the single most over-used is the past paper sat without one. A student who works through twenty papers and never reads how they were marked has practised their existing habits twenty times. A student who sits six papers and marks each one against the official scheme, in detail, learns where credit actually sits and changes what they write.

There is a structure that works. Start with questions by topic while the content is still being taught, because a full paper in October of Year 11 only demonstrates that the syllabus is incomplete. Move to full papers under timing from the mock onwards, one a week at most, and spend as long marking each one as sitting it. Keep a single running list of recurring errors rather than a folder of completed papers; the list is the revision document and the papers are just where it came from.

Two cautions belong here. The first is that papers must match the specification and the year of entry. Because the Cambridge structure changed with the 2025 syllabus, older 0580 papers do not reflect the current component structure, and practising the wrong structure trains the wrong timing. The second is legal: past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the awarding bodies. We reference and link them; we do not reproduce or supply them, and a provider offering a downloadable archive of them is telling you something about how it operates.

The mark-scheme habit is also what makes tutoring hours cheaper over a year, which is the practical argument for teaching it early. A student who can mark their own work accurately needs a tutor for diagnosis and for the hard topics, not for every paper. That is a smaller number of hours bought at a better moment, which is a better use of a Year 11 budget than a weekly hour running until June out of habit.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition costs around JBR, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: The most interesting number in Dubai tutoring is not the rate, it is the gap between the online rate and the in-home rate, because that gap is the price of a journey. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 500, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packaging shows the same shape: roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

What the premium buys is physical presence, and it is worth something for a younger child who will not work without an adult in the room. What it does not buy is more teaching, and inside a JBR tower it buys slightly less. A tutor arriving at Murjan or Bahar at 17:00 negotiates visitor parking, a security desk and a lift, and unless the arrangement says otherwise that time sits inside the paid hour. The same premium spent online buys a tutor who has taught your child's exact code, which for a tiered subject with a non-calculator paper is a larger advantage than proximity.

The rest of the published market, read in October 2026, runs as follows. Tutopiya's comparison panel opens at AED 33 to AED 52, with a revision date around twenty-one months old. EdFlik publishes an entry tier at AED 45 to AED 65. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. BartyED quotes AED 650. Every one of those is on the provider's own page, which is the point: three of the six pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card here. The sequence is a free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, then a quote once the code, the tier and the component are known. For context on the wider education budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are fixed this year; tutoring is the line still moving.

process.title: Read the code off the statement of entry
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier are all on that document, and together they make the request answerable. 0580 Extended, 0607 Core and 4MA1 Higher need three different tutors. If entries have not been made yet, the head of department will tell you what the cohort is being entered for, and the options booklet usually says.

process.title: A diagnostic trial, non-calculator first
process.description: One free trial per student, no card details taken, in the weekday slot you intend to keep. For a Cambridge entry the tutor sets an unseen non-calculator question in the first ten minutes, because that is the fastest way to find out whether the problem is method, timing or content. You get the read in writing.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from the series
process.description: Before the second session the tutor sets out the sequence, built from the final entry deadline, the school's mock window and the examination period. In practice that means content consolidation first, question-style and non-calculator work second, and full timed papers in the last eight to ten weeks.

process.title: Written notes, and a change of tutor if it is wrong
process.description: A short record after each session names what was covered, what the student managed unaided and what remains open, and it can be shared with the school. Use it to decide whether to continue. If the match is wrong, change tutor after two sessions rather than persevering for a term.

whyPoints.title: Matched to 0580, 0607 or 4MA1, not to the word maths
whyPoints.description: These three specifications differ on calculator policy, paper length, grading scale and tier ceiling. A tutor fluent in one and improvising in another teaches correct mathematics with the wrong examination habits, which is the most common wasted hour in this subject anywhere in Dubai.

whyPoints.title: The non-calculator paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Cambridge candidates sit a paper with no calculator permitted, and that is where a quietly competent student is exposed. Sessions aimed at that component start with the calculator put away and stay that way, because talking about written method and practising it are not the same intervention.

whyPoints.title: The tier ceiling named before the deadline
whyPoints.description: Core caps at C and Foundation caps at 5, and no hours change that once entries close. We tell you where the ceiling sits and when it can still be moved, because the most valuable eight hours in a tiered subject are always the ones bought before the final entry date.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry names the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier, and it is the document to work from. Before entries are made, the head of mathematics will tell you, and the options booklet usually states it. Two quick checks also work: the endorsement printed on the school's textbook, and the front of any department-issued revision guide. The distinction matters because the two examinations differ on calculator policy, paper length and grading scale.

faqs.question: Why did my child's maths grade drop two bands in the mock?
faqs.answer: On a Cambridge entry the usual explanation is the non-calculator paper. A student who has been competent for years with a calculator in hand is exposed the moment it is taken away, and the content that bites is elementary: fractions, indices, surds, proportion and percentage reversal. Nothing has collapsed; a long-standing gap has become visible. It rebuilds in weeks of short written drills, provided the sessions genuinely remove the calculator rather than discussing it.

faqs.question: What is Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and why does my child's school use it?
faqs.answer: It is a separate Cambridge syllabus, usually chosen by schools whose students continue into the IB Diploma. Graphical-calculator work is expected rather than merely permitted, and the investigation style sits closer to the Diploma exploration than to a standard IGCSE paper. Students moving between 0607 and 0580 partway through the two years find the question grammar unfamiliar even where the content overlaps almost entirely, which is a short conversion problem rather than a content gap.

faqs.question: Does the formula sheet mean my child does not need to learn formulae?
faqs.answer: It changes what is worth learning rather than removing the need. Pearson supplies a formula sheet with 4MA1; Cambridge prints a list of formulas with the 0580 papers. Neither supplies every result a candidate is expected to use fluently. Download the specimen paper for your child's code and year of entry and read the formula page: ten minutes settles what must be known cold and what only needs to be recognised, and that distinction shapes a whole term of revision.

faqs.question: Is Extended always the better entry for a capable student?
faqs.answer: Not always. A student who cannot access the harder content securely can finish with a lower grade at Extended than they would have achieved at Core, because the Core paper rewards confident performance on foundation material. The decision needs a marked mock script rather than a predicted grade, and it needs to be made before the final entry deadline. The right question is which tier this student can perform across in the months actually remaining.

faqs.question: When is the last date my child's maths tier can be changed?
faqs.answer: The final entry deadline for the series, and nothing after it. A UAE candidate sits June or November, so the date depends on which: Cambridge June entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, while a November entry is settled well before its late-October start, as Pearson's November 2026 papers finishing on 19 November 2026 were. If the June tier turns out to be wrong, November is the route back, with results in the following January. Ask your school's examinations officer for the exact date for your child's series, in writing, at the start of Year 11, because families who ask once revision has begun have already missed it.

faqs.question: How many past papers should my child actually sit for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families assume, marked far more carefully. Six full papers marked properly against the official scheme beat twenty sat and filed, because the mark scheme is where a student learns that method marks sit at specified points. Work on topic-level questions while content is still being taught, move to full timed papers from the mock onwards at roughly one a week, and keep a single running error list rather than a folder of completed scripts.

faqs.question: Can you give us copies of past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider who does is worth a second look. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are the property of Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them, link the official source, and teach from the copies the student legitimately has through the school or the awarding body's own site. Reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement, and a provider relaxed about that rule is usually relaxed about others.

faqs.question: What is Additional Mathematics 0606 and should my child take it?
faqs.answer: It is a separate single-tier Cambridge qualification graded A* to E, sat alongside or after 0580 Extended, with two papers and content that assumes the Extended material is secure: calculus, series, further trigonometry and harder algebra. If a school offers it, that offer is information about your child's standing in the set. Students who take it arrive in Year 12 with the largest available head start in mathematics; those who decline usually spend the first term catching up on calculus.

faqs.question: My child is home at 16:40 from Al Barsha. Is a weekday maths session worth it?
faqs.answer: At 16:45 or later, yes for consolidation work, and generally not for non-calculator drilling. Mathematics needs a student willing to begin a line of working without knowing where it ends, which tiredness removes first. Families on the shorter Al Sufouh run can hold 16:15 and should treat that as the best hour in their week. For the villa-belt commute, one longer weekend session usually buys more than two tired weekday hours at the same total cost.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths grade do post-16 courses around JBR usually want?
faqs.answer: Each department publishes its own threshold, and they differ between A Level mathematics and Higher Level Diploma mathematics even inside one school. Ask for the published figure in writing during Year 10 rather than Year 11, because that number is what should drive the tier decision. A capped tier delivering a comfortable pass satisfies Ministry equivalency, which asks for five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, but it can still fall below a post-16 entry requirement.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE maths tutor need a permit to teach in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are eligible. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tutor from my child's own school help privately?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the option to avoid. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Beyond the rules, it puts the person marking your child's work into a paid relationship with your household. Verify the current position with the regulator before pursuing it.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE maths tutor come to our flat in JBR?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. UAE lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard for working through algebra line by line and saved worked solutions. The in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour is published on this page so you can see what the travel premium costs, not because the visit is on offer.

faqs.question: How much does the travel premium add to an hour of maths tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Roughly AED 30 to AED 200 an hour depending on tier, based on figures read in October 2026. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 500, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Inside a JBR tower the premium also buys parking, a security desk and lift time, which sit inside the paid hour unless the arrangement states otherwise.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free who knows my child's code in our slot?
faqs.answer: We say so before anything is paid. The main specifications at the common tiers are usually matched within the week. A narrow combination, such as 0607 Extended with a graphical-calculator focus in one fixed weekday slot, can take longer or occasionally cannot be staffed at all. In that case we offer the nearest workable time, suggest a weekend alternative, or tell you plainly that we cannot cover it rather than filling the hour with a mismatch.

intro.heading: Four ways to buy IGCSE maths help, and how they differ in practice
paragraphs: Before a Jebel Ali parent compares two tutors, they are already choosing between four quite different products. A tuition centre sells a group class at a venue. An agency sells a matched tutor and manages the relationship. A freelance tutor sells their own time directly. An online platform sells one-to-one lessons over video. These are not variations on a theme; they differ in price structure, in what happens when the match is wrong, and in how much the drive matters.

Nobody in this market sets that comparison out, because every competitor page compares itself favourably against an unnamed alternative. So this page compares the models rather than the brands, with the AED figures attributed to whoever published them in October 2026, and then applies the comparison to the specific geography of Jebel Ali and Dubai South.

The geography is the twist. Jebel Ali sits at the industrial western edge of the emirate, wrapped around the port and the free zone, with its residential communities spread out through Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community, Dubai South and Emaar South. Three of the four models get more expensive, slower or less available the further south the address sits. One does not change at all.

The second half of the comparison is academic rather than commercial, and it is the one families skip. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 are different qualifications. Cambridge splits candidates into a Core route sitting Papers 1 and 3 and an Extended route sitting Papers 2 and 4. Pearson runs two equally weighted papers across Foundation and Higher tiers. Hiring on the word "maths" risks a term aimed at the wrong paper.

One more comparison is worth making before any money changes hands, and it has nothing to do with price. Ask what happens when the match is wrong, because that is the most likely failure and it is rarely about competence. A tutor pitched for a confident Higher-tier candidate, working with a student whose algebra needs rebuilding from Year 9, will lose both of them within a month. An agency or platform has a replacement mechanism and that mechanism is what its margin pays for. A freelance arrangement has none, and a centre's answer is to move your child to a different class. For a family that has already spent three weeks finding someone, the replacement question turns out to matter more than the hourly rate.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

What follows: the model comparison table, the board comparison, the route and tier decision that sets your child's grade ceiling, the topics that cost marks in this catchment, the AED bands with their sources, and the calendar counted backwards from the series your child is entered for. Read it with the exam entry statement and one marked paper to hand.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics fails in a small number of predictable places. Below is what our tutors see repeatedly in marked papers from the schools serving Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Rarely examined on its own and present inside almost everything else. Students who practise algebra in isolation still lose marks when it appears buried inside a geometry or statistics question, because they do not recognise it there.

subjects.name: Rearranging formulae
subjects.description: Recognising a formula is not the same as transposing it under time pressure. This single skill determines whether the back half of a multi-part question is accessible, and it transfers directly into physics and chemistry marks.

subjects.name: Rounding and accuracy
subjects.description: Rounding applied at an intermediate step rather than at the end produces an answer just outside the acceptable range, and the mark is lost on an otherwise perfect method. One of the cheapest fixes available in the whole subject.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Non-right-angled triangles, the sine and cosine rules, and three-dimensional problems. Marks go on diagrams never drawn: students attempt the calculation from the text rather than sketching the situation first.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.description: Conditional probability and the without-replacement case. Candidates lose marks by writing the fractions correctly and then not multiplying along branches, or by failing to add the mutually exclusive paths.

subjects.name: Statistics and cumulative frequency
subjects.description: Reading estimates off a cumulative frequency curve, box plots and interpreting the spread. Interpretation sentences carry marks, and a correct median with no statement of what it indicates earns less than it could.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Transformations, inverse and composite functions, and sketching from an equation. The common failure is applying transformations in the wrong order, which is a rule to memorise rather than a concept to grasp.

subjects.name: Vectors and geometry proof
subjects.description: Column vectors, position vectors and short geometric arguments. Students who can calculate the vector often cannot write the one-line reason the examiner is paying for, which caps the question regardless.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606 topics
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, logarithms and trigonometric identities at a level above the main syllabus. The hardest code in this catchment to resource locally and the one where an online match matters most.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Arithmetic, fractions and index work done by hand, at speed, accurately. A calculator has usually been covering for a gap since Year 8, and the gap becomes visible at exactly the wrong moment.

sections.heading: The four tuition models, compared on what actually differs
paragraphs: A tuition centre sells a seat in a group class at a venue. The price per hour is the lowest of the four because the teacher's time is shared, and for a student who is broadly on track and needs structured practice it can be good value. The limitation is that a group class cannot diagnose one student's specific habits, and a Jebel Ali or Dubai South family also pays in travel twice a week.

An agency sells a matched tutor and manages the relationship, including replacing the tutor when the match is wrong. That management is what the margin pays for and it is genuinely worth something, because the commonest tutoring failure is a mismatch of pace rather than incompetence. Agencies offering in-home delivery price the drive into the rate, and that is where distance bites.

A freelance tutor sells their own time directly, usually at a lower rate than an agency for the same person, and with no replacement mechanism. The right question to a freelance tutor is not about qualifications but about the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years, and about which syllabus code they have actually taught.

Online one-to-one sells a matched specialist with no travel in the price. It is the only one of the four models whose cost, availability and earliest start time do not change between Jebel Ali Village and Emaar South. It is also the only one that cannot supervise a student who will not begin work without an adult in the room, which is a real limitation and worth naming.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Edexcel 4MA1, paper by paper
paragraphs: Both are International GCSEs in mathematics and both are accepted by UAE and overseas universities, and that is where the similarity ends for a tutor planning a term. The paper structures differ, the way candidates are divided differs, and the question styles that follow from those structures differ enough to matter over eight weeks of preparation.

Cambridge 0580 divides candidates by route. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. The Core route caps the maximum grade. Pearson 4MA1 divides candidates by tier - Foundation and Higher - and runs two papers of equal weight rather than a short-and-long pair. A student moving school between the two boards mid-course is doing more than changing textbooks.

There is an administrative difference that matters as much as the academic one. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then revises them. In both cases the live official PDF is the only safe reference.

Our first question to a family is therefore the code rather than the subject. If you do not have it, it is printed on the exam entry statement and on the front cover of any past paper your child has been set. One photograph settles it, and it prevents the single most expensive mistake in IGCSE tutoring.

sections.heading: The route and tier decision, which sets the ceiling before any teaching happens
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects a Jebel Ali student's final maths grade, and it is usually taken for pastoral reasons rather than evidential ones. A Year 10 has a bad term, the school proposes Core or Foundation to protect the grade, the family agrees because it sounds like safety, and the ceiling only becomes visible eighteen months later when a sixth form publishes its entry requirement.

The honest position is that Core and Foundation exist for students who cannot access the higher paper at all, and for those students they are plainly right: a very low grade on a harder paper serves nobody. They are not a revision strategy, not a confidence measure, and not a way to reduce workload. Used that way they trade one term of comfort for a permanent constraint.

Decide it with a marked paper rather than an impression. Sit a timed paper at each route, have both marked against the official scheme by someone who is not the student, and read what the marks say. A student losing Extended or Higher marks to unwritten method lines, early rounding and abandoned multi-part questions is not a Core candidate; they are a higher-tier candidate with three fixable habits. A student who cannot begin most questions is a genuinely different case, and the marking makes that obvious within an hour.

Then check the destination. Both A Level and IB Diploma routes are available within this catchment, and the maths entry grades are often the highest on a school's list. Some of them cannot be reached from a Core or Foundation entry at all. Read the requirement first; the entry deadline for a tier change is set by the school and it is earlier than most families assume.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go in this catchment
paragraphs: The pattern is remarkably stable across the marked papers we see from the Jebel Ali and Al Furjan schools, and almost none of it is topic ignorance. Four habits account for most of the recoverable marks, and all four respond to drilling inside eight weeks.

The first is the unwritten method line. A student works part of a question mentally, writes only the answer, and when a slip occurs loses every method mark that was available alongside it. The second is rounding applied at an intermediate step, which produces a final answer just outside the acceptable range on otherwise perfect work. The third is the abandoned multi-part question: part (a) does not resolve, the student moves on, and parts (b) and (c) which were reachable go unattempted.

The fourth is subtler and shows up most in Discovery Gardens requests: the question has not been read accurately. The mathematics is present and the student has solved a slightly different problem from the one on the page. For a student working in an additional language this is a reading problem wearing a maths costume, and treating it as a maths problem wastes the term.

What all four have in common is that they are invisible without external marking. Self-marking over-rewards, because the student reads their own shorthand generously and knows what they meant. An hour of someone else marking against the official scheme turns a vague sense of underperformance into a short, ranked list - and that list, not the textbook, is what the next six weeks should attack.

sections.heading: The AED numbers behind each model, and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: Everything in this section is a market figure published by somebody else, read in October 2026, and attributed. None of it is an IB Gram rate card; our fee depends on the course and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The point of publishing the bands is that a quote becomes checkable, which is more than three of the pages ranking for this search allow.

At the entry level, Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. In the qualified-tutor band, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 online. For in-home delivery, Dubai rate guidance puts one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors advertising to AED 500. Specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

Monthly figures are often more useful than hourly ones for a household budget. Dubai rate guidance estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Here is what a parent can actually verify, which is the part no competitor page addresses. You can ask for the tutor's MoHRE private tuition permit. You can ask which syllabus code they have taught and ask them to name the papers in it. You can ask whether marking is against the official scheme or by impression. You can ask what the replacement policy is if the match fails. Price is the easiest thing to compare and the least informative of the five.

sections.heading: The series calendar, counted backwards, for a maths candidate
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE mathematics in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a page quoting a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline to a Dubai family is handing them another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window.

Counting backwards from the paper is what makes a plan honest. The final entries close months before the exam, and the route or tier is confirmed at that point. Mocks land about a term ahead and exist to generate data rather than to be survived. A timed-paper cycle should begin eight to ten weeks out, which means the syllabus needs to have been covered once before that. Families who begin tutoring after the mocks have, by definition, missed the content window.

The Pearson dates that are checkable show how long the tail is: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November resit confirmed in late January is tight against spring sixth-form deadlines, and that is worth knowing before the resit is chosen rather than after.

Two rules follow. Work from the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page, this one included. And ask your centre which Cambridge administrative zone it belongs to, because the zone determines which timetable applies and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility if the wrong version is used.

sections.heading: Equivalency, permits and the claims to discount
paragraphs: Families in this catchment planning a UAE university application need Ministry of Education equivalency for the school-leaving certificate. The published British-track rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

That five-subject figure is worth stating precisely, because one page ranking in this market tells UAE parents the requirement is six subjects. Mathematics is almost always one of the five in practice, which is a reason to care about the tier decision beyond the sixth-form question. Equivalency is a Ministry process that IB Gram neither performs nor influences; we describe it and point you to the official channel, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

On permits: private tutoring in the UAE requires the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE. The UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years and lists eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with suspicion.

Finally, what to discount. IB Gram is not KHDA approved; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises and we hold none and operate no UAE office. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation or partnership, publish no self-asserted star rating, promise no grade or improvement figure, and quote no statistic without its source and date.

sections.heading: Starting, and the honest answer when a code cannot be covered
paragraphs: Send the syllabus code, the route or tier, the year group and a photograph of the most recent marked paper. If the code is unknown, the marked paper carries it on the front. That single photograph is worth more than a long conversation, because it shows where the marks went rather than where the student felt least confident, and those are frequently different places.

We match a specialist to that code and route. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 at either route usually match within a day. Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure 4PM1 can take two or three days, because the pool is narrow and substituting a general maths tutor for a calculus specialist helps nobody. We tell you which case applies at the enquiry stage.

The trial lesson is free, taught by the matched specialist rather than by a salesperson, and built on the paper you sent. The tutor works the lost marks with your child writing rather than watching, and finishes with a short written note of what the paper showed and what the first month should target. No card details are needed and there is nothing to commit to beforehand. The note is yours either way.

When no suitable specialist has a slot at the hour you want, we say so and offer real options: a different weekday with the right tutor, a short block until a regular slot frees up, or a recommendation to hire locally with the permit and code questions in hand. No competitor in this market publishes its unavailable case, which is exactly why it belongs here rather than in a reply to an email you have already waited a week for.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre or a one-to-one tutor better for IGCSE maths in Jebel Ali?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether your child needs diagnosis or structure. A centre class is the cheapest per hour because the teacher's time is shared, and for a student broadly on track who simply needs supervised practice it can be good value. What a group class cannot do is identify one student's specific habits - the unwritten method line, the early rounding - and drill them out. A Jebel Ali or Dubai South family also pays in travel twice a week. One-to-one costs more per hour and is the only format that diagnoses.

faqs.question: Why do freelance maths tutors in Jebel Ali quote less than agencies?
faqs.answer: Because the agency margin is paying for something specific: matching, management and replacement when the match is wrong. The commonest tutoring failure is a mismatch of pace rather than incompetence, and with a freelance arrangement there is no mechanism for it - you simply start the search again. That does not make freelance a bad choice. It means the two questions to ask a freelance tutor are whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit and which syllabus code they have actually taught, with the papers named.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 for a Year 11?
faqs.answer: They divide candidates differently and sit different papers. Cambridge 0580 uses a Core route sitting Papers 1 and 3 and an Extended route sitting Papers 2 and 4, with Core capping the attainable grade. Pearson 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiers and runs two papers of equal weight rather than a short-and-long pair. The question styles follow from the structures, so a term of preparation aimed at the wrong specification wastes weeks. The code is on the exam entry statement and the front of any past paper.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended maths partway through Year 10?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the deadline is set by the school rather than by the board, which is why it needs asking early. The evidence for the decision should be two timed papers, one at each route, marked externally against the official scheme. A student losing Extended marks to unwritten method lines, early rounding and abandoned multi-part questions is an Extended candidate with fixable habits. A student who cannot begin most Extended questions is a different case, and an hour of marking makes the difference obvious.

faqs.question: Which maths topics cost Jebel Ali students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Four habits rather than four topics. Method lines not written down, which forfeits every method mark when a slip occurs. Rounding applied at an intermediate step, producing an answer just outside the acceptable range. Multi-part questions abandoned after part (a) when later parts were reachable. And questions misread, where the mathematics is sound but the problem solved is slightly different from the one on the page. All four are invisible without external marking, and all four respond to drilling inside eight weeks.

faqs.question: Does distance from central Dubai really change what we pay for maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: For three of the four models, yes. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour with independent tutors advertising up to AED 500, and the journey sits inside that figure. From Dubai South or Emaar South the journey is long enough that tutors either surcharge, offer very few slots, or decline. A centre class costs you travel twice a week. Online one-to-one, published at AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor, is the one model whose price and availability are unaffected by your address.

faqs.question: How do we find an Additional Mathematics 0606 tutor near Green Community?
faqs.answer: Locally, with difficulty. Cambridge 0606 and Pearson's Further Pure 4PM1 have the thinnest specialist supply of any code in this catchment, because few students take them and fewer tutors cover the calculus and trigonometric identity content properly. A radius search from Green Community, Dubai South or Emaar South commonly returns nobody usable. Online, these codes are coverable, though matching takes two to three days rather than one. We tell you the expected wait at the enquiry rather than leaving you to discover it.

faqs.question: Is maths one of the five subjects UAE equivalency counts?
faqs.answer: In practice it almost always is, which is a further reason to take the tier decision seriously. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One page ranking in this market states the figure as six subjects, which is not what the published rule says. Verify through the Ministry before relying on it.

faqs.question: Should we book a maths tutor before or after the mocks?
faqs.answer: Before, if there is any choice. Mocks land roughly a term before the series and exist to generate data; by the time they are marked, the content window for new teaching has effectively closed, because a timed-paper cycle needs the final eight to ten weeks. A student who has not covered the syllabus once by then cannot both learn it and practise it, and something gets sacrificed. If you are already past the mocks, the honest plan is habit repair and timed papers rather than a late content push.

faqs.question: Do you mark my child's papers or do they mark their own?
faqs.answer: A tutor marks them, against the official scheme, and that is most of the value. Self-marking systematically over-rewards: the student reads their own shorthand generously and knows what they intended to write, so a missing unit or an absent method line passes unnoticed. External marking converts a vague sense of underperformance into a short, ranked list of habits, which is what the following weeks attack. We do not distribute mark schemes, which are copyright material; we work from them and link the official sources.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both our children's maths if they are in Years 9 and 11?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for maths specifically, because the content is continuous and one specialist can hold both ends of it. The practical caveats are that each child needs their own slot, since these are one-to-one lessons, and that a Core-route Year 10 and a Higher-tier Year 11 need genuinely different past-paper diets even within the same subject. Tell us both year groups, boards and routes at the enquiry and we will say honestly whether one tutor fits or whether two is the better arrangement.

faqs.question: How does an online maths lesson actually work from Emaar South?
faqs.answer: A video call at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot with a shared writing surface, so the tutor writes a line and the student writes the next and both see the same page. For marking a script together it is better than a single paper copy passed across a table, because both people can annotate. The scheduling gain is the bigger one here: a 4.30pm start catches a student who can still hold an algebraic manipulation, while a 6.15pm start after a tutor has crossed Dubai catches one who makes sign errors.

faqs.question: What if my child's problem is reading the question rather than the maths?
faqs.answer: It is a common and frequently misdiagnosed case, particularly where English is an additional language, and it shows up most in requests from the apartment communities in this catchment. The signature is correct mathematics applied to a slightly different problem from the one on the page. Treating it as a maths weakness wastes the term. The work instead is comprehension discipline: underline what is being asked before any calculation, restate the question in the student's own words, then solve. It is quick to fix once it is correctly named.

faqs.question: Can we pause maths sessions during Ramadan and the mock period?
faqs.answer: Yes, though for maths we usually suggest changing the shape rather than pausing. Fluency decays faster in mathematics than in content subjects, so two shorter sessions a week hold more than one long one when a student is fasting, and a complete pause often means relearning in the first week back. During Ramadan the hour typically moves to early afternoon or post-iftar. Because nobody is travelling to your address, shifting a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation, and it moves back just as easily afterwards.

intro.heading: IGCSE maths in JLT, costed by the month
paragraphs: Household budgets run monthly, so price this subject monthly. The two published package rates in this market are AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Both deliver eight contact hours. On a per-hour basis the first is about AED 100 and the second about AED 200 to 225, and the difference is a car crossing Sheikh Zayed Road rather than anything that happens in the lesson. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist exam-year support.

Those bands are a planning basis, not a price list, and they are published by the providers named rather than by us. What they do not tell you is how many months you should be buying. For most JLT families the answer is fewer than they assume, because IGCSE maths fails in a small number of repeatable places and three of them are habits rather than gaps. A student who forfeits method marks by not writing working down can be taught to write it down in about two sessions, and will then need practice, which is free.

Two decisions move the monthly figure far more than negotiating a rate. The first is the tier. Cambridge uses Core and Extended routes in Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher tiers in 4MA1, and the lower route in each carries a lower grade ceiling, with the exact range printed in the syllabus for the series your child sits. A student capped below the grade their post-16 course requires cannot reach it however many months are funded, which makes the tier a money question before it is an academic one.

The second is the board. The two codes are different examinations with different paper structures, different expected styles of working and different mark schemes. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0580 for years will teach a Pearson 4MA1 candidate good mathematics and the wrong exam habits, and the first evidence of it arrives in a mock. Ask the school's examinations officer for the board, the code and the tier, keep the answer, and use it as the brief. It costs one message and it is the highest-value thing a parent in this market can do.

IB Gram delivers to JLT as one-to-one online tuition over live video, with sessions set after the commute back from Al Barsha, Barsha South or Al Sufouh rather than during it. We do not run home visits in Dubai; those are an India-only service. For maths specifically the format matters because the whole lesson is a shared screen, a marked script and a worked past paper, none of which improves by having somebody in the room, while the in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour overlaps the specialist online band entirely.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: Maths money is spent at four points between Year 9 and the Diploma, and the cost of being late rises at every one. These are the stages and what each is genuinely for.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the tier is set
programmes.description: Nothing is examined and nothing is capped, which makes this the cheapest useful maths tutoring available anywhere in the route. The work is narrow: fractions, ratio, indices and the beginnings of algebraic manipulation. A student secure in those four at the end of Year 9 keeps the Extended or Higher tier open, and the school's tier decision in Year 10 rests largely on evidence gathered here.
programmes.countryNote: JLT families typically start looking in Year 11, which is the most expensive month in the sequence and the one with the least calendar left to influence. If your child is in Year 9 and wobbling, a block of six to eight sessions now costs less than the same work later and changes a decision rather than a grade.

programmes.name: Year 10, while the tier is still open
programmes.description: The tier decision is usually made during this year on internal evidence, and schools will normally say what evidence they would need to move a student up. That turns a vague worry into a fundable brief with a deadline. Support here is a mix of content and technique, and because there is a full year of assessed work ahead, the money has something to act on.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the school directly which tier your child is on track for and what would change it. In the JLT catchment, campuses in Al Barsha, Barsha South and the Marina handle this differently, and some will review a tier as late as the start of Year 11 while others close it earlier. The answer determines whether a Year 10 block is a tier purchase or a grade purchase.

programmes.name: Year 11, examination year
programmes.description: Tier and board are fixed, so the money goes on paper technique: showing working, reading command words, pacing, and the specific question types where marks are going. Six to ten sessions on a named paper is the usual shape. A full-year weekly booking at this stage is sometimes justified by a genuine content gap stretching back several years, and otherwise is more than the problem requires.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 availability tightens from February across the whole Marina corridor, so a family deciding in April is choosing from the smallest pool of the year and will pay at the top of whatever band applies. Booking a short block in the autumn term is both cheaper and more effective, because mocks still lie ahead.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: What comes next assumes fluency IGCSE does not drill to the same standard. A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches both assume fast, accurate algebraic manipulation without technology. A student who met the IGCSE grade threshold while still slow at rearrangement will meet the gap in the first weeks of Year 12, which is the most expensive term in which to be behind.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving JLT run both A Levels and the Diploma with different published entry thresholds for mathematics. Collect those thresholds before deciding how much Year 11 support to fund, since the number tells you how far your child has to travel. The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the cheapest window to close an algebra gap.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: This grid maps the IGCSE mathematics content by how much tutoring time it actually absorbs and where marks go, rather than in textbook order. Codes are the common ones in Dubai schools; confirm your child's own on the entry statement.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying. The largest single source of lost marks at the upper tiers and the skill the next course assumes most heavily. It is drillable, which makes it predictable in result and the first thing worth funding where any gap exists.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Reverse percentages, compound interest and ratio splitting carry more marks than their teaching time suggests. Students lose them to misread wording rather than to method, which means question-reading practice is cheaper and faster than re-teaching the content.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.levels: All tiers, with quadratics at the upper tiers
subjects.description: Simultaneous equations, quadratics by factorisation and formula, and inequality notation. The commonest loss is an answer given without the second solution or without the inequality direction preserved, both of which are habits rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients and intersections. Marks go on reading a question that asks for a sketch and receiving a plotted table instead, or on failing to state coordinates where coordinates were asked for.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: All tiers, with three-dimensional work at the upper tiers
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, Pythagoras, trigonometric ratios and the sine and cosine rules. Students who know the content lose marks for giving no reason with an angle answer, since the mark scheme frequently pays for the justification rather than the number.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, speed, density and pressure. Unit conversion is the recurring loss here, and it costs full marks on otherwise correct answers. Two sessions of deliberate unit discipline usually closes it permanently.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms and tree diagrams. The marks sit in reading the diagram correctly and in interpreting rather than calculating, which makes it one of the quicker areas to lift.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and describing transformations fully. The usual loss is an incomplete description: a rotation named without centre and direction scores below a rotation named with both, and that is a checklist rather than a concept.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.levels: The calculator paper at every tier
subjects.description: Efficient use of the machine, plus enough written working that a method is visible. A right answer with nothing written down forfeits method marks, and this is the single cheapest repair available in IGCSE mathematics for most students.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main course by students heading for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. Its real value is Year 12 readiness rather than the certificate, which is the honest basis on which to decide whether to fund support for it.

sections.heading: The monthly arithmetic, and how many months you actually need
paragraphs: Start with what a month costs and then decide how many months the problem deserves. The two published package rates in this market both deliver eight contact hours: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. That is roughly AED 100 against roughly AED 200 to 225 for the same teaching time, with the difference going on travel. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward across the three tiers.

The table below sets those monthly figures against the plan shapes that actually make sense for IGCSE mathematics. Read the final column first. A one-month diagnostic is a small, bounded spend that very often ends the matter. A two-month fluency burst addresses the commonest cause of a capped grade at the upper tiers. A twenty-month weekly booking is a different order of commitment and should be chosen deliberately, with a termly review, because nothing renews itself as quietly as a tutoring slot.

The number that surprises families is the total on the last row. Thirty-two teaching weeks a year across Year 10 and Year 11, at a mid-market AED 220 an hour, is roughly AED 14,000 for mathematics alone. That is a reasonable price for a genuine multi-year content gap and a poor price for a habit that two sessions would have fixed. Which of those you have is readable from a marked mock script in ten minutes, for nothing.
