sections.heading: Which topics carry the marks, and which carry the hours
paragraphs: Mathematics is unusual among IGCSE subjects in that the losses are highly predictable, which means a budget can be aimed rather than spread. At the Extended and Higher tiers, algebraic manipulation absorbs the most tutoring time and returns the most, because it appears inside questions on graphs, trigonometry, mensuration and statistics as well as in its own right. A student slow at rearrangement is slow everywhere, and that single weakness often explains an entire grade.

A second group of topics carries marks far out of proportion to teaching time. Reverse percentages, ratio splitting, compound measures and unit conversion are each small and each costs full marks on otherwise correct work. They are also quick: two or three sessions with deliberate practice usually closes the whole group, which makes them the best value in the subject.

A third group is about completeness rather than ability. Describing a transformation without its centre and direction, giving an angle without a reason, stating one solution to a quadratic, or answering an inequality without preserving the direction are all cases where the student knew the mathematics and did not finish the answer. These are checklist items, teachable in a session and then a matter of habit.

The table is a planning tool to take to your child's marked mock. Find the row the lost marks actually sit in and buy that. If marks are scattered across five rows rather than concentrated in one or two, the problem is more likely to be pace or confidence under time, and a timed-practice block with light teaching is a better purchase than a content review.

sections.heading: Two papers, two different skills: with and without the calculator
paragraphs: Under the current structure a candidate sits two written papers at their tier, one permitting a calculator and one not. Check the paper numbers and the precise arrangement in the syllabus for the series your child sits, since Cambridge has revised 0580 and Pearson's 4MA1 arrangements differ. The planning point is that these two papers test genuinely different skills, and a student can be comfortable on one while losing most of their marks on the other.

The non-calculator paper is a fluency test. Speed on arithmetic, fractions, indices and algebraic rearrangement decides how much of the paper gets finished, and it comes from repetition rather than from understanding. That is why a fluency burst of two shorter sessions a week beats one long weekly session for this particular weakness; the skill responds to frequency.

The calculator paper is a method-visibility test as much as a mathematics test. Marks are available for method, and a student who produces a correct figure with nothing written down forfeits them. Efficient machine use matters too, but the written trail matters more, and the repair takes about two sessions followed by practice. Families regularly fund months of content teaching while this leak stays wide open.

Ask the school for the mark breakdown by paper from the most recent mock rather than the overall grade. Most Dubai secondary schools hold it and will share it when the question is precise. With that one document a parent can brief a tutor in three sentences, aim a one-month block at the right paper, and avoid paying for a general review of a subject where only half the assessment was the problem.

sections.heading: Working, method marks and the cheapest fix in the subject
paragraphs: If this page persuades a parent of one thing, let it be this. In IGCSE mathematics a correct final answer with no working attracts the answer mark and forfeits the method marks, while a wrong final answer with correct working attracts most of the method marks. Over a full paper the difference between a student who writes down their reasoning and an identical student who does not is substantial, and it is not a mathematics problem at all.

It is a habit problem, which is why it is cheap. Two sessions spent rewriting a previously marked paper so that every step is visible, followed by a few weeks of practice with the habit enforced, usually transfers permanently. No new content is taught and nothing is revised. Parents often resist spending money on this because it feels like paying for handwriting, and it is routinely the highest-return two hours in the whole plan.

The habit has a second payoff on the calculator paper specifically. A student who writes down what they entered and what they were finding can check their own work, spot an implausible result, and recover rather than leaving a blank. Students who treat the machine as a black box lose both the method marks and the opportunity to notice that something went wrong, and the second loss is larger over a full paper.

There is a diagnostic any parent can run tonight for nothing. Take your child's last marked mock, cover the grade, and look only at the places marks were not awarded. If the working is largely right and marks are missing, you have a technique problem: a one-month block, not a year. If the working stops early or heads somewhere unrelated, you have a content problem, which is slower and costlier and is the one case where a standing weekly slot earns its place.

sections.heading: The tier decision, treated as a money decision
paragraphs: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 runs Core and Extended routes and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher tiers. The lower route in each carries a lower grade ceiling, and the exact grade range is printed in the syllabus for the series your child sits, which is where to read it rather than taking it from any tutoring page. Schools set the tier on internal evidence, usually during Year 10, and will normally say what evidence would change it.

Treat that as a budget question. If your child is on the lower route and the post-16 course they want requires a grade above its ceiling, no amount of monthly tutoring in Year 11 will reach it, because the ceiling is not a difficulty, it is a cap. Money spent in Year 11 in that situation buys a better grade inside a range that does not satisfy the requirement. Money spent in Year 10, aimed specifically at the assessment the school uses to decide, buys a different range entirely.

The arithmetic is unusually clear. A six to ten session block in Year 10 aimed at a tier review is a one or two month purchase. The alternative, discovered in Year 11, is either a year of support that cannot lift the cap or a change of post-16 plan. The table sets out the four situations a JLT family can be in and what each one costs to act on, which is the conversation worth having with the school in the autumn of Year 10.

One more thing to ask: whether the school will enter a student for a higher tier at the family's request against its own recommendation, and what it would want to see first. Policies differ between campuses in this catchment. Knowing the answer before February of Year 10 is what makes the decision fundable rather than theoretical.

sections.heading: What A Level and Diploma maths assume that IGCSE does not drill
paragraphs: A good IGCSE grade and readiness for post-16 mathematics are not the same thing, and the difference is the most common unpleasant surprise in Year 12. Both A Level Mathematics and IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches assume fast, accurate algebraic manipulation performed without technology, at a speed IGCSE rewards but does not require. A student can clear a grade threshold while still taking three lines and twenty seconds to rearrange something a Year 12 course expects in one line.

The second assumption is notation. Function notation, set and interval notation, and the conventions for stating a domain appear quickly in both courses and are only lightly touched at IGCSE. The third is stamina on multi-step unfamiliar problems, which IGCSE papers contain in small quantities and post-16 papers are largely made of.

The cheapest window to close all three is the summer between Year 11 and Year 12. There is no school timetable competing, the content is narrow and known, and six to ten sessions is normally enough. The same work in October of Year 12 competes with five other new subjects, and in a Diploma it competes with the Extended Essay as well, which is why families who skip the summer frequently spend more in the autumn for a worse result.

The table maps the common destinations. It is a planning aid rather than a prediction, and any tutor quoting an exact number of weeks for your child before seeing their work is guessing. Ask the receiving school for its published mathematics entry threshold, because that number tells you whether this is a readiness conversation or an admission one.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics, and whether to fund it
paragraphs: Cambridge 0606 and its equivalents sit alongside the main IGCSE mathematics course and are taken by students heading for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. The question families ask is whether it is worth the extra tutoring, and the honest answer depends on what they are buying it for. As a certificate it adds little that the main grade does not. As preparation for Year 12 it is the best predictor of a comfortable start that exists at this stage.

That makes it an unusual purchase: the value is in the course rather than the result. A student who works through Additional Mathematics meets calculus, more demanding algebra and function work a year earlier than their peers, and arrives in Year 12 recognising the shape of the material. Families whose child is heading for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or A Level Mathematics get more from funding this than from funding another month of main-course revision.

It is also the subject most often dropped under pressure in the spring of Year 11, usually because it is the eleventh thing on a timetable of ten. If the decision is between finishing Additional Mathematics and protecting the main mathematics grade, protect the main grade, since that is what the post-16 threshold is written against. Where both are viable, a small fortnightly block on Additional Mathematics through Year 11 is usually sufficient; it rarely needs a weekly slot of its own.

Ask the school two things before funding anything here: whether the course is examined or taught as enrichment, and whether the post-16 courses on your shortlist mention it in their entry requirements. Those answers settle the question faster than any general argument about rigour, and they cost nothing to obtain.

sections.heading: Papers, mark schemes and tutors who claim to have them
paragraphs: Mathematics attracts a specific bad offer in this market: a tutor who implies access to the papers themselves. Treat it as disqualifying. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are referenced and linked from the boards' own sites, not reproduced or supplied as folders of scans, and unreleased material is not something any legitimate tutor holds. A provider hinting otherwise is either misrepresenting or dealing in something a candidate must not touch.

The second bad offer is quieter and more common: doing the homework. A tutor who completes a set of exercises so that a student can submit them removes the only diagnostic the teacher has, which means the school's view of your child becomes inaccurate and the tier decision is taken on false evidence. The cost of that lands months later and is invisible at the time, which is exactly why it is worth naming now.

Where IGCSE mathematics involves no coursework, the honesty boundary mostly concerns practice material and homework, so it is simpler than at Diploma level. The screening question is still the same one. Ask what the tutor would do if your child sent a completed exercise set and asked them to check and fix it before submission. A teacher describes going through it together and the student rewriting. A service describes a turnaround time.

The habits formed here matter later. A student used to having work quietly improved will ask again in Year 12, when the component is an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay and the consequence is a malpractice process rather than an inaccurate homework grade. Setting the boundary in Year 10, in plain words, is one of the cheapest protections a parent can put in place.

sections.heading: Starting: the three numbers to send us
paragraphs: Three numbers and one document make this efficient. The board and syllabus code, the tier, and the mark breakdown by paper from the most recent mock, plus a photograph of the marked script if you have one. With those we propose a tutor who has taught that code at that tier and a slot set after the commute home to Jumeirah Lakes Towers, usually 17:00 or later on a school night.

You take a free trial lesson at no cost and with no card details required, and nothing is agreed until after it. For most enquiries we will propose the one-month diagnostic or a two-month fluency burst rather than a weekly standing slot, because those address the two commonest causes of a disappointing maths grade and both have an end date. The review point is the next real school assessment set against the breakdown you sent.

Coverage for mainstream IGCSE mathematics is good in UAE evening hours, with a match usually in two to four working days for both Cambridge and Pearson codes at either tier. Additional Mathematics is thinner and may take longer. Where we cannot staff your child's code and tier in the slot you need this term, we say so at the enquiry stage rather than placing someone who teaches the other board and letting a mock reveal it in March.

Three things we will decline: completing homework or practice material for submission, claiming a regulator or board relationship we do not hold, and promising a particular grade. What you will get instead is a session count, a named target, and a point at which you decide whether it worked, judged against a document you already own.

process.title: Get the board, code and tier

process.description: Four sessions aimed at a named paper, or eight across two months for fluency work. The review is the next real school assessment against the breakdown you started with. If nothing moved, the method or the tutor changes rather than the month count.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring cost per month for a JLT family?
faqs.answer: Published monthly packages in this market are AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, both delivering eight contact hours, which works out at roughly AED 100 and AED 200 to 225 an hour respectively. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist exam-year support. Those are the providers' own published figures. IB Gram scopes a plan after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a flat monthly rate.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics are worth paying to fix first?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation, if there is any weakness there, because it sits inside questions on graphs, trigonometry, mensuration and statistics as well as in its own right, so a slow student is slow everywhere. After that, the small high-yield group: reverse percentages, ratio splitting, compound measures and unit conversion, which cost full marks on otherwise correct work and usually close in two or three sessions. Then the completeness items: an angle without a reason, one solution to a quadratic, a transformation described without its centre and direction.

faqs.question: Is our problem the calculator paper or the non-calculator one?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the mock mark breakdown by paper rather than the overall grade; most Dubai secondary schools hold it and share it on request. The two papers test different skills. The non-calculator paper is a fluency test, where speed on arithmetic, fractions, indices and rearrangement decides how much gets finished, and it improves with short frequent drills. The calculator paper is largely a method-visibility test, where correct figures with nothing written down forfeit method marks. A student can be fine on one and losing heavily on the other.

faqs.question: Why does our child lose marks when the final answers are right?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded for working, and a correct answer with nothing written down collects the answer mark only. The reverse is also true: wrong answers with correct working collect most of the method marks. Over a full paper the gap between a student who writes their reasoning down and an identical student who does not is substantial, and it is not a mathematics problem. Two sessions spent rewriting a marked paper so every step is visible, then a few weeks of enforcement, usually transfers the habit permanently.

faqs.question: What does being entered on the lower maths tier actually cost us?
faqs.answer: Potentially the whole requirement. Cambridge 0580 runs Core and Extended routes and Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher tiers, with the lower route carrying a lower grade ceiling, printed in the syllabus for the series your child sits. If the post-16 course needs a grade above that ceiling, no monthly spend in Year 11 can reach it, because a cap is not a difficulty. Acting in Year 10, with six to ten sessions aimed at the assessment the school uses to decide the tier, is the only version of this that is a fundable problem.

faqs.question: Does a strong IGCSE maths grade mean our child is ready for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A Level Mathematics and IB Analysis and Approaches both assume fast, accurate algebra performed without technology, plus function, set and interval notation that IGCSE touches only lightly, plus stamina on multi-step unfamiliar problems. A student can clear a grade threshold while still taking three lines to rearrange something Year 12 expects in one. The cheapest window to close that gap is the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, where six to ten sessions on narrow, known content normally suffices.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth funding alongside the main course?
faqs.answer: It depends what you are buying. As a certificate it adds little to the main grade. As preparation for Year 12 it is the best predictor of a comfortable start available at this stage, because it introduces calculus and harder algebra a year early. Fund it for a student heading to A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, usually as a small fortnightly block rather than a weekly slot. If it ever competes with the main mathematics grade, protect the main grade, since that is what thresholds are written against.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a month are actually enough?
faqs.answer: Four, for most problems, aimed at one named paper or question type and reviewed at the next school assessment. Eight a month for one or two months is the right shape for fluency work specifically, because algebraic speed responds to frequency rather than to session length, so two shorter sessions a week beat one long one. More than eight a month for IGCSE mathematics is rarely about the mathematics and usually about anxiety, which is worth addressing directly rather than by buying more hours.

faqs.question: Should we pay for maths over the summer between Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is one of the two good windows, and usually cheaper per unit of progress than the spring term. With no school timetable competing, July and August suit fluency work: the non-calculator skills, notation, and the method-visibility habit. Six to eight sessions is normally enough. The other good window is the autumn of Year 10, while the tier decision is still open. The window to avoid relying on is April of Year 11, when availability across the Marina corridor is at its tightest and little remains in the calendar.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches A Level maths handle an IGCSE candidate?
faqs.answer: Mathematically, easily. Examination-wise, only if they know the board and tier. The risk is not that the content is beyond them but that they teach to a standard the mark scheme does not reward, skipping the written steps an IGCSE scheme pays for or using notation the paper does not expect. Ask which IGCSE codes they have taught and for how many series, and hand them a marked script. A tutor who reads it and names the question type where marks went has answered the question properly.

faqs.question: Is group maths tuition cheaper than one-to-one for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and that is not the comparison that matters. A group class moves at a common pace, which is efficient for content coverage and poor for the specific losses this subject produces, since one student's problem is unshown working and another's is unit conversion. Group classes also add a second school run for a JLT family, which is a real cost that never appears on the invoice. The sensible combination is a group class for coverage if the school recommends one, plus a short one-to-one block for the named loss.

faqs.question: What should a first maths session actually produce?
faqs.answer: A specific statement about where marks are going, and ideally one repair made. A session that produces 'we went over algebra and it went well' has produced nothing you can act on or measure. Send the marked script in advance and ask the tutor to name the paper, the question type and the fix in the first session. If the answer is a proposal to work through the syllabus from the start, the tutor has not read the evidence, and that is the most expensive plan on offer.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy a textbook or revision guide as well?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Schools issue the resources they expect to be used, and official past papers are published on the boards' own sites, which is where they should be read and linked from rather than copied. Buying a general revision guide for the wrong board is a common small waste, because the worked examples model the other scheme's expected working. Ask the subject teacher what they want practised before buying anything, then check that the material matches your child's code and tier.

faqs.question: What if a tutor claims to have this year's papers?
faqs.answer: End the conversation. Unreleased examination material is not something any legitimate tutor holds, and board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are referenced and linked from the boards' own sites rather than distributed as folders of scans. A provider hinting at access is either misrepresenting their position or dealing in something a candidate must not touch, and the consequence of involvement falls on the student. The same judgement applies to any offer to complete homework or practice sets for submission.

faqs.question: How do we know when to stop paying for maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: When the next real school assessment shows the named loss has closed. That is why a block should start from a document: the mock breakdown by paper, or a marked script. If the marks that were missing are now being awarded, the plan is finished and should be closed rather than renewed. If they are not, the method or the tutor changes rather than the month count. A plan that ends because it worked is the outcome worth paying for, and a tutoring arrangement with no stopping condition will not produce one.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work on IGCSE Mathematics with students across Dubai: Cambridge 0580 and 0980 Extended, Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher, and the stretch content in 0607. Every session is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a scanned past-paper question on screen rather than a slide deck.

intro.heading: Start from the date on the entry form, not from chapter one
paragraphs: Most families in Jumeirah 1 begin looking for maths help inside a narrow window. A mock comes back in late October or early February, the number sits two grades below what the sixth-form application needs, and the question turns arithmetical: how many weeks are left, and what can those weeks carry. Answering that honestly is more useful than listing topics, because the answer decides what a tutor should do in the first hour.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and those two are the ones a UAE candidate sits. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November too: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entry deadlines for every one of those series close months before the papers, and they are the fixed points a revision plan hangs from.

Eight weeks of one hour a week is eight hours of teaching and perhaps twenty-four hours of independent work. That is enough to rebuild two or three topic areas to a reliable standard and to change how a paper is attempted. It is not enough to cover a two-year syllabus. So the first session is diagnostic: a past paper marked question by question, then sorted into marks lost to content, marks lost to method and marks lost to the clock. The three piles need different treatment, and only the first of them needs teaching.

Jumeirah 1 sits between Al Satwa and Al Wasl, with Jumeirah Beach Road on one side and Al Mina Road on the other. Secondary pupils here travel out to school - Jumeirah College in Al Safa, Dubai College in Al Sufouh, Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah Baccalaureate School closer to home - and most get back between 15:30 and 16:30 once the bus has looped the coast road. A 16:00 slot is optimistic on a Sunday or a Monday. The 17:00 and 18:30 slots are the two that survive a whole term, and a term that holds is worth more than an ambitious one that collapses in week three.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Jumeirah 1 address, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. For maths that costs a family very little and buys something specific: the person on the call is chosen because they teach the exact syllabus your child is entered for, not because they happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Beach Road.

What follows is organised as a calendar. Which paper, which code, which deadline, which topics in which order, and what the Dubai market charges for the help. Where a figure appears, its source is named and dated, because a number without a source is worth nothing to a parent deciding how to commit AED 1,000 a month.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 1 families meet IGCSE as the middle of a longer route: Cambridge Lower Secondary or MYP below it, A Level or the IB Diploma above. The four stages below are the ones that decide a maths grade, and the Dubai note on each is the thing a tutor has to work around rather than a description of the stage.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course begins, usually assessed by school tests and sometimes by Checkpoint, which Cambridge runs in March, May and October. The content that matters later is narrow: directed number, fractions as operators, index laws, solving linear equations with brackets and fractions, and the first work on straight-line graphs. A pupil who leaves Year 9 unable to manipulate an algebraic fraction will meet that gap again in every Extended paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai British and American schools both compress Year 9, because the IGCSE course often starts in the January of Year 9 rather than in September of Year 10. Families in Jumeirah 1 frequently discover in Year 10 that two terms of foundation algebra were taught at speed during a term broken by National Day, winter break and a Checkpoint window. Repairing that is cheaper in Year 9 than in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Core
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the same topic headings as Extended with shallower treatment and no Extended-only material. Candidates sit Paper 1, one hour without a calculator, and Paper 3, two hours with one. The grade range available is C to G, so the tier itself sets a ceiling. Marks in Core are lost less to difficult content than to arithmetic slips, misread scales and unanswered multi-step questions at the end of Paper 3.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter a Core cohort more often than families expect, usually on Year 10 evidence. The tier decision is made by the school and locked at the final entry deadline for the series, which Cambridge publishes months ahead and the exam centre holds, so a Year 11 conversation in the spring term is often already too late for the June papers. If a UAE university route needs a stronger grade than C, the move has to be argued in Year 10 with marked evidence.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended
programmes.description: Extended adds functions, advanced algebra, histograms with unequal class widths, vectors in column form, matrix transformations and the sine and cosine rules in three dimensions. Candidates sit Paper 2, ninety minutes without a calculator, and Paper 4, two and a half hours with one. Grades run A* to E. The non-calculator paper is the newer pressure point: surds, standard form and exact trigonometric values are now worth real marks on their own.
programmes.countryNote: Extended is the default tier at Jumeirah College, Dubai College and most British schools serving the Jumeirah corridor, and it is the entry requirement most A Level Mathematics courses in Dubai state. A student aiming at Mathematics or Engineering at a UAE university is normally expected to show a grade 6 or B here before an A Level or Diploma Higher Level course will take them.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: The Pearson alternative, sat as Paper 1H and Paper 2H at Higher tier, two hours each, calculator permitted in both. Reporting is on the 9-1 scale. The content overlaps heavily with Cambridge Extended but the question style differs: Pearson tends towards longer structured questions with more marks for method, which rewards a student who writes down working and punishes one who jumps to an answer.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run Pearson for mathematics while using Cambridge for sciences, so one household can hold two boards at once. That matters for revision: a Pearson student practising Cambridge non-calculator papers is training for a paper they will not sit. The board is printed on the statement of entry, and checking it before December saves a wasted term of past papers.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: A graphics-calculator course designed as a bridge into the IB Diploma, taken as Core Papers 1 and 3 or Extended Papers 2 and 4. The syllabus expects fluent use of a graphing device for solving equations, finding intersections and reading distributions, and the mark schemes credit a correctly sketched calculator output. Students who try to answer 0607 by hand lose time rather than accuracy.
programmes.countryNote: 0607 is the usual code at Dubai IB continuum schools, including Jumeirah Baccalaureate School and Emirates International School, because it feeds Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at Diploma level. A Jumeirah 1 family moving a child from a British school into an IB school mid-Year 10 should expect the calculator work, not the content, to be the gap.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the subject this page is about, and the codes below are the ones Dubai schools actually enter. The rest of the grid is there because a Year 11 revision plan rarely stays single-subject: a maths timetable gets built around the three sciences, and the same household usually needs two or three of these.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580 Extended
subjects.description: Algebraic fractions, functions and composite functions, histograms with unequal widths, vectors, transformations by matrix, sine and cosine rules. Marks leak most in the non-calculator paper, where surds and exact values now carry their own method marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580 Core
subjects.description: The same headings without Extended-only content, graded C to G. Teaching concentrates on securing the first six marks of every question, reading scales correctly and finishing Paper 3, where unanswered final parts are the commonest single loss.

subjects.name: International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: The graphics-calculator route into the IB Diploma. Sessions cover solving graphically, reading intersections, sketching calculator output in a way the mark scheme credits, and the modelling questions that a Diploma Applications course builds on.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics. Introduces differentiation, integration, binomial expansion and radian trigonometry a year early, and is where the gap between a confident grade 7 and a true A* becomes visible.

subjects.name: Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Paper 1H and Paper 2H, calculator in both, reported 9-1. The method marks are generous but conditional on written working, so the teaching priority is layout and the habit of recording an intermediate value before rounding.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: A harder companion to 4MA1 covering series, calculus, logarithms and vectors. Dubai schools run it in small groups or not at all, which is exactly where a one-to-one online specialist is easier to find than a local one.

subjects.name: Physics 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: The subject most dependent on the maths grade. Rearranging formulae, standard form, gradients with units and significant figures are maths failures that show up as physics marks, and they are quicker to fix in a maths session.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, percentage yield and titration arithmetic account for a large share of calculation marks. Students who can handle ratio in maths rarely lose these, and students who cannot lose them twice.

subjects.name: Biology 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Lighter on calculation but heavy on graph reading, magnification and percentage change. The teaching focus is command terms: describe, explain and suggest earn different answers, and marks go to students who notice which was asked.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal, logic gates and pseudocode trace tables. Students who find 0580 algebra difficult usually find the trace tables difficult for the same reason, and the two respond to the same kind of step-by-step practice.

subjects.name: Economics 0455 and Business 0450
subjects.description: Data response questions reward a student who can read a percentage change, an index and a simple elasticity calculation. The quantitative marks are the ones most often dropped by otherwise strong essay writers.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of IGCSE maths can actually change
paragraphs: Eight weeks of weekly one-to-one maths tuition will reliably do three things: secure two or three topic areas that are currently costing marks, change how a paper is attempted under time pressure, and remove the arithmetic and notation errors that leak marks across every question. It will not teach a two-year syllabus, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling hours rather than a grade.

That distinction matters because the commonest wasted spend in Dubai is a Year 11 family buying twenty hours of general revision in February. General revision is what the school is already doing. A tutor earns the hour by being specific: this student loses four marks a paper to rounding too early, six to unattempted final parts, and eleven to histograms, vectors and algebraic fractions. Those are different problems with different fixes, and only the last needs teaching in the normal sense.

The diagnosis comes from a marked paper, not from a conversation. A past paper is sat under timed conditions, then marked against the official mark scheme question by question, and every lost mark is assigned to one of three causes. Content gaps are taught. Method losses are drilled with short sets at the same difficulty until the layout becomes automatic. Clock losses are solved by changing the order the paper is attempted in, which costs no teaching at all and often recovers the most marks.

By week four the plan is reviewed against a second marked paper. If the three priorities were right, the lost marks have moved. If they have not, the priorities were wrong and they change rather than the student being asked to work harder. The final fortnight is given to full timed papers, because a student who has never finished a paper in the allotted time will not finish the real one either.
bullets: Week 1: timed diagnostic paper, marked and sorted into three causes
Weeks 2-4: the single highest-cost topic, taught then tested
Week 4: second marked paper; priorities confirmed or replaced
Weeks 5-6: second and third priorities, plus non-calculator drill

sections.heading: Which IGCSE maths syllabus your child is sitting
paragraphs: There is no single IGCSE maths course. A Jumeirah 1 household can hold Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0980, Cambridge 0607, Pearson 4MA1 or Pearson 4PM1, and the codes differ in papers sat, calculator rules and the grade scale printed on the certificate. The code appears on the statement of entry the school issues before each series. Everything a revision plan does should follow from that line of text.

The calculator rule is the change that catches Dubai families out most. Cambridge 0580 and 0980 now set one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper at each tier, so a student who has done all their practice with a calculator in hand has been practising for half the assessment. Surds, standard form, exact trigonometric values and fraction arithmetic become worth real marks on their own rather than being incidental steps. Pearson 4MA1, by contrast, permits a calculator in both papers, which rewards a different habit entirely.

The grade scale matters for university and sixth-form applications. 0580 reports A* to G, 0980 and the Pearson International GCSEs report 9 to 1, and a UAE admissions office reading a transcript will see whichever applies. The two scales are not identical and should never be converted casually on an application form. Where a school runs 0580 for maths and 0980 for English, one transcript carries both, and that is normal rather than an error.

0607 is a different animal. It is built around a graphics calculator and designed as a bridge into the IB Diploma, which is why Dubai IB continuum schools use it. A student moving from a British school into an IB school mid-course meets 0607 as a technology gap rather than a content gap: the mathematics is familiar, but the expectation that a solution is found graphically and the output sketched for credit is not.

sections.heading: The entry clock, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Cambridge publishes key dates for each series months in advance, and the gap between the entry deadline and the paper is the fact families most consistently miss. UAE candidates sit the June series or the November series, and for either one the final entry closes well before the revision term begins. By that date the tier is fixed, the syllabus code is fixed and the candidate is registered. A conversation about moving from Core to Extended held in the spring term is therefore a conversation about the following series rather than the one coming.

The zone timetable is the second thing to settle early. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, with the explicit warning that it is essential to use the correct version and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam. A Dubai centre and a London centre do not share a timetable. The version that matters is the one the child's own exam centre gives out, printed and dated, not a PDF found by search.

Working backwards from the exam window produces a plan with dates rather than intentions. For a June series the last full timed paper belongs in the final fortnight of the spring term, the second marked diagnostic a month earlier, and the first one before the winter break. That places the decision to hire a tutor in the autumn term, which is also roughly when entries are being settled. In practice those two deadlines are one deadline.

Pearson runs a different rhythm. Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit is to read the live official timetable rather than to trust a date copied onto a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually leak
paragraphs: Across marked Extended papers the same half-dozen places account for most of the gap between a grade 5 and a grade 7, and almost none of them are the topics students name when asked what they find hard. Algebraic fractions are first: a student who cannot factorise a quadratic in order to cancel will lose marks in algebra, in functions and again in any rate question that resolves to a fraction. The topic is worth teaching early because it pays three times.

Rounding too early is second, and it is not a content problem at all. A student who writes 3.6 instead of 3.5833 and carries it forward loses the accuracy mark on a question they understood. The fix is procedural: record the full calculator value, round only in the final line, and state the degree of accuracy asked for. Two sessions of deliberate practice usually removes it, which is a better return than any topic.

Then come the named traps. Histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density rather than frequency is plotted. Bounds, where a student adds instead of subtracting at the lower limit. Vectors in column form, where the direction of travel reverses the sign. Transformations, where the matrix and the description are both wanted and only one is given. Probability without replacement, where the second denominator does not change. Each is a known mark-scheme behaviour, and each can be drilled to reliability inside one session.

The last leak is the clock. Paper 4 is two and a half hours and the final questions carry the most marks, so a student who works strictly front to back and runs out of time loses the highest-value marks on the paper. Attempting the paper in two passes - everything answerable at speed, then the rest - commonly recovers six to ten marks with no new mathematics at all. It has to be practised on full papers, because it is a habit rather than a tactic.
bullets: Algebraic fractions: factorise before cancelling, every time
Keep the full calculator value; round only in the final line
Histograms: plot frequency density when class widths differ
Bounds: subtract at the lower limit, add at the upper
Two-pass paper technique, practised on full timed papers

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the Year 10 decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: The tier decision is the single most consequential thing that happens to an IGCSE maths grade, and it is usually taken quietly, in Year 10, on the evidence of two internal assessments. Core caps the available grade at C. Extended runs to A*. A student entered for Core who later needs a grade 6 for an A Level Mathematics place has a problem that no amount of tuition inside Year 11 can solve, because the ceiling is set by the entry rather than by the performance.

Dubai schools enter more students for Core than parents tend to realise, and the reason is reasonable: a secure C is a better outcome than an insecure E, and an Extended paper attempted by an underprepared student produces a worse grade than the Core paper would have. The problem is not the judgement, it is the timing. The entry is locked at the final entry deadline, which the board publishes for each series and the exam centre holds, and after that date the tier cannot move for that series.

Arguing for a move upward requires evidence of the right kind. A marked Extended paper showing the student can access the Extended-only content - functions, histograms, vectors, the sine and cosine rules - is persuasive. A parent's view that the child is capable is not. The practical route is to sit a full Extended past paper in September or October of Year 11, mark it honestly, and take the script to the head of mathematics with a specific request rather than a general one.

There is an honest version of the opposite conversation too. If a marked Extended paper comes back at 18 per cent with the Extended-only questions untouched, the tier is not the problem and moving up would damage the grade. In that case the useful work is securing every available Core mark, which is a real and valuable outcome, and planning a November re-entry or an A Level alternative route rather than pretending the ceiling is not there.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition costs around Jumeirah 1, and the home-visit question
paragraphs: Read the Dubai market as a monthly bill rather than an hourly rate, because that is the number a household actually plans around. One weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor lands in the region of AED 600 to 1,200 a month on published market bands; a budget online tutor brings that down to roughly AED 240 to 600; an exam-year specialist with two sessions a week sits nearer AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures from published rate tables and competitor pages read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

The in-home premium is the part worth examining. The same hour taught at a Jumeirah 1 villa is quoted at AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 online, and the gap is travel. A tutor crossing Dubai at 17:00 cannot teach more than two or three sessions in an evening, and the rate has to carry the unpaid hour in the car. That premium buys physical presence. It does not buy a better mathematician, and in a thin subject such as Further Pure Mathematics it actively narrows the choice to whoever lives nearby.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; those are a service we offer only in India. Tuition for a Jumeirah 1 family is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a scanned past paper on screen. For maths that format is close to ideal: the working appears line by line where both people can see it, the question stays visible, and the session recording can be rewatched the night before a paper. What is lost is the drive, in both directions.

Two further costs belong in any honest budget. A private candidate entry, where a school will not enter a student for an additional code, is paid to the exam centre rather than to a tutor and is quoted per subject. And the VAT position on tuition fees in the UAE should be checked against the Federal Tax Authority rather than taken from a tutoring page; the only figure any provider can speak to is whether its own quoted price includes it.

sections.heading: Five accredited subjects: why the maths grade matters after results day
paragraphs: A UAE family planning on a local university needs to know what the Ministry of Education asks for, because the requirement is specific and it shapes which subjects are worth paying to improve. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. That single clause is where one ranking competitor page gets the rule wrong by asserting that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. Reading the requirement correctly changes a Year 10 option choice: a student with five strong academic subjects plus Arabic has five that count, not six, and mathematics is almost always one of the five a university will look at hardest.

The American track is separate and worth knowing if a sibling is in a US-curriculum school. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the same source, so any page quoting one for equivalency should be treated with caution until it is read on a Ministry of Education page.

Equivalency is a process a family completes with the authority, not something a tutor performs or guarantees, and tuition is not a requirement for it. What a tutor can do is make sure the five subjects that will be counted are the five the student is strongest in, and that mathematics is not the one carrying a grade 3. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry of Education channels before a decision is taken on it, because equivalency rules are revised.

sections.heading: Permits, and what a Jumeirah 1 parent can actually check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation runs the application through its smart app, website and e-services system, under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no published fee.

Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so any page quoting a figure is guessing. The honest position for a parent is simpler: the permit exists, it is free, and asking about it is reasonable rather than rude.

Two more rules are worth knowing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a restriction the MoHRE code of conduct echoes. Nobody should be marketing a child's own classroom teacher as their private tutor.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International, Pearson or the IB, it holds no KHDA training-institute permit, and it occupies no office in the UAE. Any page in this market claiming regulator approval for tutors should be asked for the permit number, because the permit is a real document with a real reference.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with school maths work
paragraphs: Mathematics at IGCSE has no externally assessed coursework in the common codes, which removes most of the academic-honesty risk that surrounds an IB Internal Assessment. It does not remove all of it. Schools set assessed investigations, modelling tasks and portfolio pieces that count towards internal reporting and towards the forecast grade a centre submits, and those pieces have to be the student's own work.

The line is about who does the thinking. A tutor may teach the mathematics a task needs, work through a parallel example with different numbers, explain what the marking criteria reward, read a draft and say which section does not justify its conclusion, and show a student how to check their own answer. A tutor may not supply the solution, correct the submitted work line by line until it is right, or produce any part of a piece that will be handed in as the student's.

That boundary is a selling point rather than a limitation in this market. The research behind these pages found a ranking site offering completed Internal Assessments for sale at AED 3,750, which is an academic-integrity breach and, for an IB candidate, a malpractice trigger with consequences far worse than a weak grade. A tutoring page that states the boundary plainly is telling a parent something useful about how the sessions will run.

The same rule applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the right behaviour is to reference them and link to the official source rather than to redistribute them. Sessions work from the official material where a student or school already has legitimate access to it, which in practice covers every past paper a revision plan needs.

process.title: Send the marked paper, not a summary
process.description: The most useful thing a Jumeirah 1 family can send first is a photograph of the last marked maths paper and the statement of entry showing the syllabus code. A school report says a grade; a marked script says where the marks went. One of those can be acted on in the first session and the other cannot.

process.title: A short call to fix the code and the date
process.description: Twenty minutes to confirm which syllabus and tier the student is entered for, which series they are sitting, and how many weeks that leaves. The outcome is a number of available sessions and a realistic statement of what those sessions can carry, agreed before any money is discussed.

process.title: A free trial lesson on one real question
process.description: One lesson, no card details and nothing payable, built around a question from the student's own marked paper. It tells a parent whether the tutor knows the code and tells the student whether the hour is bearable. If either answer is no, a different tutor is proposed rather than the same one argued for.

process.title: A written plan with three priorities and dates
process.description: After the diagnostic, the plan is written down: the three topic areas being worked on, the paper technique being changed, the dates of the two review papers, and the week the full timed papers happen. It is deliberately short, so that in week four it can be checked against results rather than reinterpreted.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marking in between
process.description: A fixed weekly hour on Gulf Standard Time, with work set at the end of each session and marked before the next. The marking is where the plan gets corrected. A session that only happens during the hour, with nothing between, produces about a third of the gain for the same fee.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code decides the teaching
whyPoints.description: 0580, 0980, 0607 and 4MA1 differ in calculator rules, paper lengths and grade scales, and a student practising the wrong board's non-calculator paper is working hard on an assessment they will never sit. The code is confirmed before the first session, from the statement of entry rather than from memory.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before content
whyPoints.description: The first hour is spent finding out where the marks actually went, using a marked paper and the official mark scheme. Marks lost to rounding, to unattempted final parts and to a missing topic are three different problems, and teaching all three as though they were content gaps wastes most of the term.

whyPoints.title: Timed papers, not worksheets
whyPoints.description: Paper technique on a two-and-a-half-hour Extended paper is a habit, and habits form under the real clock. Full papers are sat under exam conditions in the final fortnight, marked against the published scheme, and the lost marks are reported back by cause rather than as a total.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent platform with no regulator accreditation, no UAE office and no school partnerships, and it does not send tutors to UAE addresses. Saying so is more useful to a parent comparing providers than another paragraph of reassurance, and it is checkable.

whyPoints.title: A slot that survives the school run
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set at a time that works after a Jumeirah bus has crossed the coast road, usually 17:00 or 18:30, and held for the term. A fixed hour that actually happens every week beats a flexible arrangement that is rescheduled twice and then quietly dropped in November.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers, or none
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to a published market rate table or a competitor's own published price, with the month it was read. No invented statistics, no success percentages, no grade promises. A number that cannot be sourced is left out rather than rounded into something confident.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the paper is it still worth starting IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks of weekly sessions is enough to secure two or three topic areas and to change how a paper is attempted, which is where most of the recoverable marks sit. Four weeks is enough for paper technique and one topic. Two weeks is enough to fix rounding habits, question order and the non-calculator basics, which is not nothing. What no timescale allows is covering a two-year syllabus, so the shorter the runway, the narrower and more specific the plan has to be. The first session is a marked diagnostic paper in every case, because without it the hours get spent on whatever the student mentions rather than on what is actually costing marks.

faqs.question: Is my child sitting Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, and does it change the teaching?
faqs.answer: It changes it considerably, and the answer is printed on the statement of entry the school issues before each series. Cambridge 0580 and 0980 set one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper per tier, so surds, standard form and exact trigonometric values carry marks on their own. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers but awards more method marks in longer structured questions, which rewards written working. A student revising with the wrong board's past papers is practising for an assessment they will not sit. Checking the code before December is the cheapest thing a family can do, and it takes one message to the school office.

faqs.question: Why does one Cambridge maths paper now ban the calculator?
faqs.answer: Cambridge restructured its IGCSE Mathematics assessment so that each tier sits one paper without a calculator and one with. Core candidates take Paper 1 without and Paper 3 with; Extended candidates take Paper 2 without and Paper 4 with. The effect is that fluency with fractions, surds, indices, standard form and exact values is assessed directly rather than incidentally. For a Dubai student who has done two years of practice with a calculator in hand, this is usually the single largest unaddressed gap, and it responds quickly to short daily drills rather than to long sessions.

faqs.question: What does the final entry deadline actually commit us to?
faqs.answer: By the final entry deadline for a series, the school has registered your child against a specific syllabus code and a specific tier, Core or Extended. After that date neither can move for that series. The deadline sits months ahead of the papers, because the board has to issue statements of entry, allocate zone timetables and print scripts, and both Cambridge and Pearson publish the exact date for each series. That is why a tier conversation held in the spring term is really a conversation about the following series. If a change is wanted, the evidence needs to reach the head of mathematics in the autumn, as a marked Extended paper rather than an opinion.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but only before the final entry deadline for the series, and only with evidence the school can act on. The persuasive evidence is a full Extended past paper, sat under timed conditions and marked honestly, showing the student can access the Extended-only content: functions, histograms with unequal class widths, vectors in column form, the sine and cosine rules. If that script comes back with the Extended-only questions untouched, the move would lower the grade rather than raise it. In that case the better plan is to secure every available Core mark and to look at a November re-entry or an A Level route separately.

faqs.question: What does a forecast grade mean, and can it be changed?
faqs.answer: A forecast grade is the centre's estimate of the grade a candidate is likely to achieve, submitted to the board by a deadline published for each series and held by the exam centre. It is based on the school's own evidence: mocks, classwork and internal assessments. It is not a prediction to be negotiated, and it does not cap the result. The way to influence it is to give the school better evidence before the deadline, which means a strong marked mock rather than a conversation. Sixth forms and universities in the UAE may see it, so it is worth the effort it takes to improve it.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of IGCSE maths tuition is sensible in the final term?
faqs.answer: Two hours a week, split across two sessions, is the usual ceiling for useful work in an exam term. Beyond that the limit is not the teaching but the independent practice: an hour of tuition generates two or three hours of work, and a Year 11 student in a Dubai school already has coursework and mocks for seven or eight other subjects. Families who buy four or five hours a week in February tend to find the student stops doing the set work, at which point the sessions become revision lectures. One session plus marked work between is more productive than three without.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths tutor charge per hour in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands read in October 2026 run roughly as follows. A budget online tutor, often a university student, is advertised from about AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject teacher online sits around AED 150 to 300. In-home one-to-one, with travel built in, is quoted at AED 180 to 500. An IGCSE or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and above. Those are market rates from published rate tables and providers' own pages, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Does a Jumeirah 1 address change the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Not for online teaching, because there is no travel in the price. It does change in-home quotes: a tutor crossing Dubai to reach a villa off Jumeirah Beach Road at 17:00 is paying for an unpaid hour in traffic, and the rate carries it. That is the main reason the in-home band sits above the online band in every published rate table for this market. Where an address genuinely matters is availability rather than price - a coastal location narrows the pool of people who will travel, and in a thin subject that can mean the choice is one person rather than several.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our house in Jumeirah 1 instead?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not sell in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for a Jumeirah 1 family are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own marked paper on screen. For mathematics that is a strong format rather than a compromise: the working appears line by line where both people can see it, the question stays visible beside it, and the session can be rewatched the night before a paper. The in-home market exists in Dubai and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, which is a useful comparison to have.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday maths session start after the Jumeirah school run?
faqs.answer: Most Jumeirah 1 secondary pupils travel out to Al Safa, Al Sufouh or Umm Suqeim and reach home between 15:30 and 16:30, later when the coast road is slow. A 16:00 start is therefore optimistic on a Sunday or Monday. The two slots that hold for a whole term are 17:00 and 18:30, and the second of those survives a late bus and a sibling pick-up. Since sessions run online on Gulf Standard Time, there is no travel either way, which is what makes a fixed weekly slot practical rather than aspirational in a household with two school runs.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics calculator for Cambridge 0607?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics is built around one, and the syllabus expects fluent use of it for solving equations, locating intersections, sketching functions and reading distributions. Mark schemes credit a properly sketched calculator output, so a student answering 0607 by hand loses time rather than gaining rigour. Dubai IB continuum schools use 0607 because it feeds Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at Diploma level, where the same device is used again. A student moving into 0607 mid-course usually needs two or three sessions on the device itself before any new content.

faqs.question: How does the maths grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Mathematics is almost always one of the subjects an admissions office weighs most heavily, so a grade 3 in it is the weakest link to fix first. Equivalency is completed with the authority directly, and the current requirement should be verified on Ministry of Education channels.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to help with a school maths coursework task?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the mathematics the task needs, work a parallel example with different numbers, explain what the marking criteria reward, read a draft and say which part does not support its conclusion, and show the student how to check their own result. A tutor may not supply the solution, rewrite the submission, or produce any part of what is handed in. The common IGCSE maths codes have no externally assessed coursework, but schools do set internally assessed investigations that feed the forecast grade, and the same boundary applies to those. Offers to complete assessed work are an integrity breach, not a service.

faqs.question: Does a private maths tutor working with a Dubai family need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services, under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day turnaround. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amount has been published. Asking a prospective tutor about the permit is a reasonable question.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free for Pearson Further Pure Mathematics that week?
faqs.answer: It gets said rather than hidden. 4PM1 is a thin subject in Dubai, taught in small groups or not at all, and the pool of people who know its two papers properly is small. Where no UAE-based specialist is available at the time a family needs, the alternative offered is an IB and IGCSE specialist teaching the same syllabus from elsewhere, on Gulf Standard Time, and the family is told that is what is happening before anything is booked. The alternative some providers choose is to accept the booking and send a general maths tutor, which costs a term before anyone notices.

intro.heading: The IGCSE maths problem in Jumeirah 2 is a timetable problem first
paragraphs: Jumeirah 2 is a low-rise villa district running between Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road, with Jumeirah 1 to the north-east and Jumeirah 3 to the south-west. Almost no secondary school sits inside its boundaries. The Year 10 and Year 11 students who live here are driven out of the district every morning — inland to Al Safa, along the coast to Al Sufouh, or further to Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim. That single fact shapes everything about arranging maths tuition here, and it is the thing the search results never mention.

A child at Jumeirah College finishes at 3:05pm on a normal day and is home by 3:25pm if Al Wasl is clear. A child at Dubai College in Al Sufouh finishes at 3:20pm and, on a Sunday with Sheikh Zayed Road backed up at the Safa interchange, is not home before 4:10pm. A child at Kings' School Dubai in Umm Suqeim 3 who has a co-curricular commitment until 4:30pm is home at 5pm. Three families on the same street, three different windows. Any tuition arrangement that assumes one fixed 4pm slot will fail for at least one of them inside a month.

The second constraint is the syllabus code. Schools serving Jumeirah 2 do not all enter the same IGCSE Mathematics specification. Jumeirah College and Dubai College run Cambridge 0580 Extended for most of the cohort. Several IB-continuum schools in the area enter Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, which requires a graphics calculator and carries an investigation paper that 0580 does not have. A number of schools have moved to Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, which is tiered Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended and allows a calculator in both papers. A tutor who teaches 0580 habits to a 0607 candidate wastes the hour.

The third constraint is the one parents feel but rarely say out loud: the pool of maths specialists who live within a twenty-minute drive of Jumeirah 2 and happen to be free at 4:45pm on a Tuesday is small, and it shrinks further once you ask for someone who has taught Extended tier to the top band rather than Core tier for a pass. Geography is the binding constraint, and it is an artificial one. Live video removes it. Your child works with a specialist chosen for the syllabus code, not for a postcode.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. What that buys a Jumeirah 2 family is a session that starts the minute your child walks in, with no travel for anybody, and a tutor who can be an Extended-tier 0580 specialist rather than whoever was available in the neighbourhood.
