dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 2 families run across three different routes at 16, and the maths your child needs depends on which one their school has entered them for. These are the programmes the area's schools actually teach.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year qualification most British-curriculum schools near Jumeirah 2 enter at the end of Year 11. Mathematics is compulsory everywhere. Cambridge runs it as 0580 with a Core and an Extended tier; Pearson runs Mathematics A as 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers. The tier decision is normally taken in Year 10 and is harder to reverse late than parents expect, because the Extended and Higher papers assume content the lower tier never taught.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this sits under KHDA, which inspects every private school annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of private-school enrolment in the emirate, the largest single share, which is why the IGCSE maths cohort around Jumeirah 2 is large and why school maths sets can run to twenty-eight students. A one-to-one hour is doing something the set cannot.

programmes.name: Cambridge International Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate Cambridge specification, code 0607, used mainly by schools that continue into the IB Diploma. It assumes a graphics calculator throughout and adds a third component — an investigation paper at Core and Extended — that tests mathematical exploration rather than recall. Students arrive in DP Maths better prepared for the Internal Assessment, but a tutor who only knows 0580 will not recognise the investigation mark scheme at all.
programmes.countryNote: Several IB-continuum schools serving the Jumeirah and Al Safa catchment enter 0607 rather than 0580. If your child owns a Casio or TI graphics calculator for maths homework rather than a scientific one, that is the strongest single signal you are on 0607. Ask the head of maths for the code in writing before you book any tuition; it appears on the statement of entry.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The route a large minority of Jumeirah 2 students take after IGCSE, splitting into Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, each at Standard or Higher Level. The choice is made in Year 11, from an IGCSE maths grade, and it closes doors if it is made badly: engineering and most economics courses expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students make up 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places in total. The practical consequence for a Jumeirah 2 Year 11 is that the AA-or-AI decision is being taken in the same term as the IGCSE mocks, which is exactly when a maths tutor is most useful for something other than revision.

programmes.name: Pearson and Cambridge International A Level
programmes.description: The other post-16 route in this catchment, taken at Jumeirah College, Dubai College and most GEMS British schools. Mathematics at A Level assumes fluency with Extended-tier IGCSE algebra, not a bare pass: a student who scraped a grade 5 on 4MA1 Higher and then takes A Level Mathematics usually struggles in the first term on indices, surds and function notation rather than on anything new.
programmes.countryNote: For Jumeirah 2 families this makes the Year 11 summer the cheapest intervention point in the whole school career. Six to eight hours spent closing algebraic fluency gaps before Year 12 starts costs a fraction of remedial A Level support in the spring term, and it is the single most common reason a family here books maths tuition that is not exam-driven.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: Maths is the page, but the schools around Jumeirah 2 enter the same students for eight or nine IGCSE subjects at once. These are the ones that most often get booked alongside maths, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Two written papers per tier. From the 2025 series Core sits Paper 1 non-calculator and Paper 3 calculator; Extended sits Paper 2 non-calculator and Paper 4 calculator. The non-calculator requirement is the change that has caught most cohorts out, because arithmetic fluency had quietly stopped being taught.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of two hours each, 100 marks apiece, calculator permitted in both. Higher tier is graded 9 to 4, Foundation 5 to 1. The Higher paper leans harder on algebraic manipulation and proof than 0580 Extended does, and lighter on constructions and transformations.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: Graphics calculator assumed throughout, plus an investigation paper that asks students to generalise a pattern and justify the generalisation. Marks are lost almost entirely on the justification, not the pattern. This is the specification that feeds IB Maths most smoothly.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for A Level Mathematics, covering calculus, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities a full year early. It is the best predictor of a comfortable Year 12 and the hardest thing in the Year 11 timetable.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: The subject most often booked alongside maths here, because the overlap is real: rearranging formulae, handling standard form and reading gradients off a graph are maths skills examined in a physics paper. Paper 6 or the alternative-to-practical component is where graph marks are gained or lost.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, titration arithmetic and percentage yield are maths problems in chemical clothing. Students who are weak on ratio and proportion in maths lose the same marks twice, once in each subject, which is why a combined booking is often cheaper than two separate ones.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Less arithmetic than the other two sciences but far more dependent on command-term discipline: describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different answer shape, and a correct biological idea written in the wrong shape scores nothing.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries the marks. Axes labelled, curves shifted in the right direction, equilibrium relabelled after the shift. A student who can do simultaneous equations in maths can usually be taught the diagrams in four sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory plus Paper 2 algorithms and programming. Binary, hexadecimal and two's complement are directly transferable from number work in maths, and pseudocode trace tables reward the same ordered working a maths examiner wants.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Booked alongside maths more often than any other subject in this catchment, usually by families where English is a second or third language at home. Directed writing and the summary question are the two components where technique gains the fastest marks.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 2 parent is actually searching for
paragraphs: Someone typing "IGCSE maths tutor in Jumeirah 2" is usually not shopping for a subject. They are solving a logistics problem. The child has a maths test coming, the school report said "needs to show more working", and the parent has about forty-five usable minutes between the end of the school run and the start of dinner, homework and bedtime. The search is for someone who can occupy that window reliably, every week, without adding a second car journey to the day.

That is why the honest answer to this search is not a list of names. It is a timetable. The first thing worth establishing is the exact end-of-day time at your child's school, the realistic door-to-door time back to Jumeirah 2 on the two or three days you would consider, and what else already occupies those afternoons. Swimming at 5pm on Mondays, football at 4:30pm on Wednesdays and an Arabic class on Sundays are what actually determine when maths tuition happens. A tutor who has to drive to you narrows that list to almost nothing.

The second thing worth establishing is the syllabus code, because it changes who is qualified to help. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 cover broadly similar mathematics but assess it differently, and Cambridge 0607 is a different animal with a graphics calculator and an investigation paper. The code is printed on the statement of entry and the head of maths will confirm it by email in a sentence.

Everything after that is ordinary teaching. Find the gap, close it, prove it closed with a timed paper. The part this page can genuinely help with is the first two steps, because nobody else in these search results will tell you that the answer depends on what time your child's school finishes.

sections.heading: The Jumeirah 2 school day, and when a maths session actually fits
paragraphs: The table below sets out the schools a Jumeirah 2 student is most likely to attend, where each one sits, and the earliest hour at which a maths lesson can realistically begin once the child is home, changed and fed something. These are typical finishing times for a normal day without a co-curricular commitment; a fixture or a rehearsal pushes everything back by an hour and a half.

Two patterns matter. The first is that the inland Al Safa schools give you a usable 4:15pm to 4:30pm slot, while the Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim schools do not — there, 5pm is the first honest option, and a 4pm booking will be missed often enough to be worth avoiding from the start. The second is that Sunday and Thursday behave differently from the middle of the week. Sunday afternoon traffic on Al Wasl is the worst of the week in this district, and Thursday is the day most families would rather not schedule anything at all.

The practical recommendation that comes out of this is narrower than it sounds: pick a Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday, start at 4:45pm if your child is at a second-ring school and 4:15pm if they are at an Al Safa school, and keep the same slot for the whole term. Consistency is worth more than the exact hour. A session that moves every week stops happening by about week six, which is the most common way maths tuition quietly fails in this neighbourhood.

A session over live video also removes the half-hour buffer that an arriving tutor needs. The child closes the front door, opens a laptop and starts. In a district where the afternoon commute is the binding constraint, thirty minutes of nobody travelling is not a convenience argument — it is the difference between a 45-minute lesson and a 75-minute one.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE maths specification your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Three specifications dominate this catchment and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the most common, split into a Core tier graded C to G and an Extended tier graded A* to E. From the 2025 series the paper structure changed: Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. The arrival of a compulsory non-calculator paper is the single biggest shift in IGCSE maths teaching in a decade, and it exposed cohorts whose arithmetic had been quietly outsourced to a Casio since Year 7.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher, graded 5 to 1 and 9 to 4 respectively. Both papers are two hours and both allow a calculator. The Higher paper pushes harder on algebraic proof and manipulation and asks less about constructions and transformations than 0580 Extended does. A student moving between schools mid-course from one board to the other needs a gap audit, not a general revision plan, because the overlap is high but not complete.

Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is the specification used by schools continuing into the IB. It assumes a graphics calculator from the start and adds an investigation paper at both tiers. Students lose marks there almost entirely on justification: they spot the pattern, write the formula and never explain why it holds. That is a teachable skill and it is also the exact skill the IB Maths Internal Assessment rewards two years later, which is why 0607 students often find DP Maths less of a jump.
Ask for the code in writing. A tutor who prepares a 0607 candidate on 0580 past papers will produce a child who is fluent at the wrong thing, and you will not discover it until a mock.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: Marks are not lost evenly across the syllabus. In Extended-tier and Higher-tier scripts the same five areas account for most of the gap between a grade 6 and a grade 8, and none of them is an exotic topic. Algebraic fractions come first: students who can factorise a quadratic in isolation lose the marks when the quadratic is a denominator, because they cancel terms rather than factors. That single error is worth three or four marks on a Paper 4 and recurs every series.

Second is the trigonometry of non-right-angled triangles. The sine rule's ambiguous case, bearings expressed as three-figure angles, and three-dimensional problems where the required right-angled triangle has to be drawn before anything can be calculated. Students who skip the sketch almost always use the wrong side. Third is probability with conditional structure — tree diagrams drawn correctly, then read incorrectly, because the second branch was not renormalised after a without-replacement first pick.

Fourth is the reverse-percentage and compound-growth family. Finding an original price after a discount, a population after n years, or a depreciation after three years. Students multiply by 0.85 three times correctly and then, asked for the original, divide by 1.15 instead of 0.85. Fifth, and biggest on the new non-calculator papers, is plain arithmetic fluency: standard form without a calculator, surd simplification, fraction arithmetic with mixed numbers, and long multiplication done by a method the student half-remembers.

All five are diagnosable from one marked past paper and all five respond to drilling rather than to explanation. A good first session is a diagnostic paper and a written list; a bad first session is a tour of the syllabus. If a tutor cannot tell you after ninety minutes which of these five is costing your child the most marks, that is a signal worth acting on.

Bestimate's "Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026" rate table estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Jumeirah 2 family running one weekly maths session through Year 10 is therefore looking at the middle band, and one running two weekly sessions through the Year 11 exam term is in the upper one.

Converted to hours, the published market splits into reasonably clear tiers. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, both at the university-student end. A tutor sits at the dining table, the parent can hear what is happening, and a younger child is easier to keep on task with an adult in the room. It is worth saying plainly what it costs and what it involves rather than pretending the question does not arise. In Jumeirah 2 the practical reality is a tutor driving in from Al Barsha, Al Quoz or Bur Dubai between 4pm and 5pm, which is the worst hour on Al Wasl Road, and billing for an hour that includes the stress of having made it.

The published premium is AED 30 to 150 an hour over the online rate for an equivalent tutor, and it buys physical presence plus the travel. What it costs is selection. A tutor who must physically reach Jumeirah 2 by 4:45pm on a Tuesday is being chosen from everyone who lives within half an hour and is free in that window. An Extended-tier 0580 specialist who has marked the non-calculator paper is being chosen from a much larger pool once the drive is removed from the requirement. For a Core-tier student needing confidence, the local pool is usually sufficient. For a student chasing a grade 8 on 4MA1 Higher, it usually is not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. sections.heading: The IGCSE maths year counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. UAE candidates sit those two series. The February/March series is offered to India only, which matters because a parent who reads an Indian tutoring page and plans around a March exam will plan eleven weeks wrong.

Working backwards from the June series, the fixed points are these. Entry decisions, including the Core-or-Extended and Foundation-or-Higher tier choice, are made by the school in the autumn term, months before the exam, and once submitted they are awkward to change. Mocks fall in January or February. From there the useful question is not "how much revision" but "how many complete timed papers, marked against the official mark scheme, before the first real one". Eight is a reasonable target for an Extended candidate. Most students manage two or three.

The November series is the resit route and it is a genuine option rather than a consolation. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reach students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. One practical consequence for a Jumeirah 2 family: a November resit decision taken in late August gives roughly eight teaching weeks, which is enough for one or two subjects and not enough for four.

Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Always work from the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than from a date restated on a tutoring page, including this one. Timetables are revised.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor may and may not do with your child's work
paragraphs: IGCSE Mathematics carries no coursework component on the specifications used in this catchment, which removes the sharpest academic-honesty risk. It does not remove the issue entirely. Students at IB-continuum schools sitting 0607 produce an investigation; students across the area produce internally assessed work in other subjects; and homework submitted for a school grade is still the student's own work under every school's policy.

The boundary we hold is simple and we state it to the student in the first session. A tutor teaches the method, works through a parallel example, reviews what the student has written and gives feedback on it. A tutor does not produce the answer the student submits, does not write or rewrite an investigation, and does not complete a homework set so it can be handed in. One competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach and, for the student, an IB malpractice trigger with consequences that outlast any grade.

The practical version for a maths session is this: when a student brings in homework due tomorrow, the tutor teaches the first question and the student does the rest. When a student brings in an investigation, the tutor asks what the pattern suggests and why, and the student writes the justification. It is slower and the student learns something. A parent who is paying for the hour should expect to see the student's handwriting on the output, not the tutor's.

We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing them is a copyright problem. We link the official source and work from material the student legitimately has through their school.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects sitting alongside IGCSE maths
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for. KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines set out the requirement and state that it must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. This is the part of a Jumeirah 2 child's timetable that most expatriate parents understand least, and it eats hours that would otherwise be available for maths.

The organisation rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach those subjects — a credential a parent can reasonably ask about. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is a real constraint on how Arabic tutoring material may be described.

Two things follow for maths. First, the weekly timetable in a Dubai school is fuller than the equivalent UK one, so a Year 11 here has less free study time than a parent comparing with home might assume. Second, for the Ministry of Education equivalency route on the British track, Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five required subjects — so a student needs five other accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and maths is almost always one of them.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE maths tutor start with my child in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: Usually within two to four working days for Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 at either tier. The step that takes the time is not finding a tutor but fixing a slot that survives contact with your actual week, so the first thing we ask for is the school's end-of-day time and the afternoons already taken by sport or Arabic. Cambridge 0607, with its graphics calculator and investigation paper, is a smaller specialism and can take a few days longer. The trial lesson itself is free and carries no obligation, so there is no commitment attached to starting the process.

faqs.question: What time do IGCSE maths sessions usually start for families in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: For children at the Al Safa schools, around 4:15pm Gulf Standard Time works reliably: the day ends near 3pm and the drive back along Al Wasl is fifteen to twenty-five minutes. For Dubai College, Kings' School Dubai or the Al Sufouh schools, 4:45pm is the first honest option, because the afternoon run can take forty minutes. We would rather set a later slot that happens every week than an earlier one that gets missed twice a month. Sunday afternoons are the slowest in this district and Thursday is the day most families prefer to leave clear.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to our villa in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, on a shared screen, with your child's own past paper or exercise in front of both of them. In-home tutoring is a real option in Dubai and the published market rate is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, so the comparison is a fair one to make. What removing the drive buys you is selection: the tutor is chosen for knowing your child's syllabus code rather than for living nearby.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus code do schools near Jumeirah 2 use?
faqs.answer: Most British-curriculum schools in the Al Safa and Al Sufouh ring enter Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, usually at Extended tier for the main cohort. Schools continuing into the IB Diploma often enter Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 instead, which assumes a graphics calculator and adds an investigation paper. A growing number of schools use Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher. Ask the head of maths to confirm the code by email before booking any tuition; it is one line to answer and it changes which past papers are worth doing.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended tier in Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: Core tier is graded C to G and Extended tier A* to E, so a student who needs a grade A or B must be entered for Extended. The content differs as well as the ceiling: Extended covers functions, more demanding algebra, the sine and cosine rules and harder probability work that Core never teaches. From the 2025 series Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. Moving a student up a tier late in Year 11 means teaching a year of missing content in a term, which is why the decision deserves evidence.

faqs.question: Why has the non-calculator paper caused so much trouble in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Because arithmetic fluency had quietly stopped being practised. When every paper allowed a calculator, students could get through surds, standard form and mixed-number fractions by typing. The 2025 Cambridge 0580 structure requires one paper per tier with no calculator, and scripts now show correct methods ruined by arithmetic slips: a sign lost in a long subtraction, a fraction left unsimplified, a surd mishandled. It responds to short daily drilling rather than to explanation, so in exam term we practise the non-calculator paper as a separate activity from the calculator paper rather than mixing them.

faqs.question: What is the monthly cost of weekly IGCSE maths tuition for a Jumeirah 2 household?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Monthly packages advertised in this market include roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures as published in October 2026, not our prices. Ask any provider for the rate in AED in writing, and ask whether it is quoted per hour or per lesson.

faqs.question: Is the hourly rate for maths tuition in Dubai quoted with VAT included?
faqs.answer: That varies by provider and it is worth asking before you book rather than after the first invoice. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as settled fact here, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring page's assurance. What we will do is quote our own figure in AED in writing and say plainly whether that figure is the total you pay. The useful question to put to any provider is simply: is this the number that will appear on the invoice, yes or no.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working with a Jumeirah 2 family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own service page is the application route, and a tutor can simply be asked to confirm they hold one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and physics for the same Jumeirah 2 student?
faqs.answer: Often yes at IGCSE level, and it is frequently the better arrangement. Cambridge 0625 Physics is full of maths skills examined in a physics paper: rearranging formulae, standard form, gradients from graphs and unit handling. A student losing marks on ratio in maths loses them again on mole and density calculations elsewhere. One tutor across both subjects sees the same error twice and fixes it once. At IB Higher Level the subjects usually need separate specialists, because the depth required in each is harder for one person to hold.

faqs.question: My child has mocks in six weeks. Is it too late to book maths tuition?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is enough to change a grade boundary outcome if the time is spent on papers rather than on the syllabus. The plan we would run is a diagnostic paper in week one, a written list of the three areas costing the most marks, then four weeks of two sessions a week split between those areas and complete timed papers, with the non-calculator paper practised separately. Six weeks is not enough to move a Core-tier student onto the Extended paper, and we would say so rather than take the booking on a false expectation.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow my child's school scheme of work or a separate plan?
faqs.answer: The school's, through Year 10 and the first term of Year 11. Running a parallel syllabus means the student is learning two orderings of the same subject, which helps nobody and makes the unit tests harder rather than easier. We ask for the scheme of work, the unit test dates and the most recent marked assessment, and the tutor reinforces what was taught that week before anything else. From January of Year 11 the plan shifts to being driven by the past papers, because at that point the school is revising too.

faqs.question: Can maths sessions move to later evenings during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families here do move them. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the family's daily rhythm shifts around iftar, so an afternoon slot that worked in February often does not work at all. We reschedule to post-iftar evenings or to a shorter mid-afternoon session, whichever the household prefers, and we confirm the change in writing before the month starts rather than improvising week to week. Because lessons run over video, moving the time involves no renegotiation of anybody's travel.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's exact syllabus code?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than substituting quietly. Cambridge 0607 at Extended tier is the narrowest specialism in this subject and there are weeks when no tutor who has taught the investigation paper has a free slot at 4:45pm. In that case we say what is actually available, what the wait would be, and whether a 0580 specialist could usefully cover the shared content while you wait. Disclosing a coverage limit is a trust decision rather than a sales one, and no competitor page in this market discloses one at all.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor help with the IGCSE investigation or homework due tomorrow?
faqs.answer: The tutor will teach the method and work a parallel example, and your child will do the question that gets submitted. That boundary is not negotiable and we state it to the student in the first session. For a 0607 investigation the tutor will ask what the pattern suggests and why it holds, and the student writes the justification, because the justification is where the marks are. Work produced by somebody other than the student is a malpractice risk for the student and we will not take part in it.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE maths grades from Dubai accepted for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so maths is almost always one of them. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. Verify your own case with the Ministry directly, because we describe this process rather than perform it.

intro.heading: The code on the entry form decides what the tutoring has to be
paragraphs: Most wasted IGCSE mathematics tuition in Dubai is wasted on the right subject and the wrong syllabus. Three codes are in common use across the schools near Jumeirah 3. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the traditional algebraic course, tiered into Core and Extended. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is a different syllabus with a graphic display calculator expectation and a separate investigation paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 is a third course, tiered into Foundation and Higher, with its own paper structure.

Those three are not interchangeable. A student entered for 0607 who spends a term on 0580 past papers will cover a good deal of overlapping content with the wrong technique and no practice at the investigation paper they will actually sit. A 4MA1 candidate drilled on Cambridge mark schemes will meet a different style of question and a different balance of marks. The first question any competent tutor asks is which code is on the entry confirmation, and the answer comes from the school's exams officer rather than from the textbook on the shelf.

The second decision with consequences is the tier. Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G and Extended is graded A* to E, so a Core entry cannot reach the top grades however well the papers are answered. Pearson 4MA1 tiers the same way in effect, with Foundation capping the available grade and Higher opening the top of the scale. The tier is set at entry, which falls a term or more before the papers, so a family discovering it in the final weeks has very few options left.

Once the code and tier are settled, mathematics tuition becomes unusually tractable, because the marks are predictable. Dubai students lose them in the same places year after year: method not shown where the scheme awards it, premature rounding, units dropped, a correct answer to a question that was asking something else, and whole questions left blank because the time ran out. None of those is a knowledge problem, and all of them are teachable inside a term. The implication for a parent is encouraging: a marked script usually shows that three or four habits, not a specification-wide weakness, account for most of the missing grade, and habits are cheaper to change than knowledge.

Everything on this page is delivered one-to-one online over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around the Jumeirah 3 school run. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a subject this code-specific that matters practically rather than philosophically: the available pool stops being whoever teaches maths within a twenty-minute drive and becomes whoever teaches that exact syllabus at the hour you want.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics divides into topic areas that behave differently under examination conditions. These are the ones Dubai students most often lose marks in, with the specific trap in each.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, all three codes
subjects.description: Reverse percentages, compound interest and ratio-sharing with an unequal starting point. The trap is premature rounding: a figure rounded in step two produces a final answer outside the accepted range and loses the accuracy mark even though the method was right.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, algebraic fractions, simultaneous equations with one quadratic. Marks are lost for abandoning the working once the answer looks familiar. The scheme awards method, so an unsupported correct answer can score less than a supported wrong one.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching, reading values from a curve, gradients of tangents, and in 0607 using the graphic display calculator to find intersections. Students frequently give a coordinate when the question asked for a value, or omit the units that the mark scheme requires.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, perpendicular lines and equations of lines through given points. The trap is the sign error in a negative reciprocal, which propagates through an otherwise correct answer and loses the final mark. Checking by substitution takes ten seconds and is rarely taught.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Surface area and volume of composite solids, arcs, sectors and similar shapes. Marks go on unit conversion between centimetres and metres mid-question, and on using a diameter where the formula wants a radius. Both are habits rather than gaps.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled triangles, then the sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Bearings questions lose marks for measuring from the wrong reference direction; three-dimensional questions lose marks because no diagram was drawn before the calculation began.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Describing a transformation fully is a mark scheme requirement: name, centre, scale factor, direction, as applicable. Partial descriptions are the single most common loss here. Vector work rewards clear notation, which students treat as presentation rather than as marks.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and combined events. The usual error is multiplying along the wrong branch, or presenting a probability greater than one without noticing. A sanity check against zero and one catches most of it.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency, box plots, histograms with unequal class widths, and averages from grouped data. Histograms with unequal widths are the reliable discriminator: frequency density is required and students plot frequency instead.

subjects.name: Investigation, 0607 only
subjects.description: An extended exploration of a problem rather than a set of questions, which cannot be revised by topic. It has to be practised as a format: generating cases, spotting a pattern, generalising, justifying and communicating the result in writing. Students sitting it unseen lose marks they would never lose on a standard paper.

sections.heading: Three syllabuses, side by side
paragraphs: Parents are rarely shown the difference between the mathematics codes their children are entered for, and the schools do not always explain it, because inside a school everyone already knows which one they run. For a family hiring a tutor the difference is the whole decision. The table below compares the three codes in use around Jumeirah 3 on the points that change what a tutor should do.

The clearest divergence is technology. Cambridge 0580 restructured its papers from the 2025 series so that candidates sit both a non-calculator and a calculator component, which puts arithmetic and algebraic fluency back at the centre of preparation. Cambridge 0607 assumes a graphic display calculator and expects students to use it as a tool for exploration, including in an investigation paper. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator across its written papers and leans on longer multi-step problems.

The second divergence is the grade ceiling. Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E; Pearson 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher with the same practical effect. A student who is capable of a high grade but entered at the lower tier cannot reach it, and that is a conversation with the school about entries rather than something tutoring can resolve.

The third is the existence of an investigation. Only 0607 carries one, and it behaves like no other component in any of these courses. A 0607 candidate who has done four timed investigations will approach that paper calmly; one who has done none will meet an unfamiliar task under time pressure and lose marks for reasons unrelated to ability. Exact paper durations and mark totals are published on each board's own syllabus page and held by your exams officer, and should be read there rather than reproduced here, because they change between series.

sections.heading: The mark-scheme traps that cost marks a student had earned
paragraphs: A large share of lost IGCSE mathematics marks in Dubai are lost by students who knew the mathematics. That is an uncomfortable claim to make without specifics, so here are the specifics. Method marks are awarded for visible working, and an unsupported correct answer in a multi-step question can score less than a fully worked wrong one. Students who have been praised for doing things in their heads lose marks for exactly that habit, and they lose them in every paper.

Rounding is the second recurring loss. Mark schemes accept an answer within a stated tolerance, and a value rounded at an intermediate step frequently falls outside it. The rule to teach is mechanical: carry full accuracy through the calculation and round once, at the end, to the degree of accuracy the question asked for. Students who round early are usually doing it to make the numbers look tidy, which is a presentation instinct working against them.

Then there are the question-type traps, each with its own fix. Describing a transformation requires every element the scheme lists, and a partial description scores partially. Histograms with unequal class widths require frequency density, not frequency. Bearings must be measured from north and given as three figures. Units must match what the question asked for, not what the working produced. None of these is difficult; all of them are invisible to a student who has never read a mark scheme.

The fourth category is time. Papers are lost at the end rather than at the beginning, and a student who spends twelve minutes on a four-mark question has made a decision with consequences. Triage is teachable: read the mark allocation, attempt the questions that pay, leave the one that is not moving and come back. A student who has practised that in three timed papers does it automatically in the fourth.

sections.heading: Topic by topic: the trap and the fix
paragraphs: Generic advice about practising more does not help a student who is already practising. What helps is knowing which specific error each topic tends to produce, because the correction is usually a single habit rather than a re-teach. The table below pairs the topics Dubai students most often lose marks in with the error that produces the loss and the fix that removes it.

Read it as a diagnostic rather than a syllabus. The right way to use it is with a marked script in front of you: find the questions where marks were lost, match them against the rows, and you will usually find that three or four habits account for most of the gap. That is a much cheaper problem to solve than a specification-wide weakness, and it is the normal finding rather than the exceptional one.

The fixes are deliberately small because small fixes stick. Writing units in the answer line before calculating, sketching a diagram before starting a three-dimensional trigonometry question, or checking a probability against zero and one are each a few seconds of discipline. Across a two-hour paper they recover marks that no amount of additional content revision would have found.

One caution about the table: it describes tendencies, not your child. The reason a diagnostic session starts from a marked script rather than from a list is that the actual pattern is always more specific than the general one, and occasionally it is something nobody would have predicted.

sections.heading: Past papers, used properly
paragraphs: Almost every Dubai family already knows that past papers matter, and almost nobody uses them in a way that produces marks. The common pattern is to work through questions with help, get them right, and conclude that the topic is secure. That produces confidence and no evidence. A past paper only tells you something if it is sat alone, under the real timing, and then marked against the board's own scheme rather than against a feeling.

The routine worth teaching a student is four steps. Sit the paper cold, in one sitting, with a clock. Mark it yourself against the scheme, writing the mark gained next to each question rather than a tick. Categorise every lost mark as content, method, accuracy, misreading or time. Then rework only the questions in the two largest categories. A student who runs that cycle three times across a term improves faster than one who completes twice as many papers with help.

We do not supply past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement; for unreleased material it is considerably worse. The boards publish a great deal on their own sites and your school's exams officer has access to more, both of which are the correct and free route.

There is a timing point specific to Dubai. The winter break is the single best uninterrupted window for timed papers in the school year, and two or three sat properly across it are worth more than five squeezed into a busy term. Families on this coast who plan for that rather than improvising it usually arrive at the mock window with real data instead of a general impression.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the entry decision
paragraphs: The tier is the most consequential decision in an IGCSE mathematics course and the one families are least often consulted about. Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G; Extended is graded A* to E. Pearson 4MA1 separates Foundation from Higher with the same practical effect. A student at the lower tier cannot reach the top grades, whatever happens in the examination hall.

Schools make the decision for sound reasons: a student placed on a paper far beyond their current attainment can do badly on every question rather than well on the accessible ones, and the lower tier protects a usable grade. The problem arises when a student improves substantially in Year 11 and the entry is never revisited, or when a family assumes the ceiling does not exist because nobody mentioned it.

The practical steps are simple and cost nothing. Ask which tier your child is entered for. Ask what evidence that decision rests on and when it was taken. Ask the latest date at which it could be changed, which is set by the school's internal cut-off rather than by the board's published deadline. If the answers suggest the tier was set in Year 10 and never reviewed, that is worth a conversation now rather than after the papers.

Where a tier change is not available, the honest conversation is about what grade is actually in reach and what it is worth. A grade that secures a post-16 route is valuable; a grade that cannot change any subsequent decision is not worth three hours a week of a sixteen-year-old's life. That judgement belongs to the family, but it should be made with the ceiling visible rather than discovered afterwards.

sections.heading: What a code-specific maths tutor costs in Dubai
paragraphs: The cheapest tutor in this market is often the most expensive purchase, because a generalist at AED 50 an hour teaching the wrong syllabus for a term produces nothing a parent can measure. The figure worth comparing is not the hourly rate but the rate multiplied by the chance that the work matches the paper, and that calculation changes the answer for most families.

The published bands in Dubai are these. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget online end. Unitors publishes online IGCSE rates from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a qualified subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted to AED 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages of AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits circulate widely. All of those are each provider's own published figures rather than an IB Gram price list.

Within those bands, what you are buying at the AED 150 to 300 level for mathematics specifically is somebody who knows the code. A teacher who can say without checking that 0607 carries an investigation paper, that 0580 now includes a non-calculator component, or that 4MA1 question styles differ from Cambridge's, is worth the middle of the market. A teacher who treats all three as interchangeable is not worth the bottom of it.

The context figure for a household budget: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A flat fee year is the right moment to pay for a short, code-specific block with a specialist rather than a long, cheap one with a generalist.

sections.heading: Timing a session around a Jumeirah 3 school day
paragraphs: Schools along this coast finish between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm and the run home adds twenty to fifty minutes depending on direction and on how Jumeirah Beach Road is behaving. From Jumeirah 3 that makes around 5pm the first weekday start that survives a whole term, with 5pm to 6pm the most reliable window and 7pm to 8pm widely available for households where both parents commute.

For mathematics specifically, the length of the session matters as much as the hour. A full timed paper cannot be sat inside a one-hour slot, so the practical arrangement is that papers are sat independently and the session is used to mark, categorise and rework. That split is what makes a weekly hour sufficient; without it, a weekly hour becomes a slow walk through content.

Two shorter sessions a week work better than one long one in the final fortnight before papers, and online scheduling makes that trivial to arrange. A travelling tutor cannot double the number of visits without doubling the travel, which is the practical reason in-home arrangements tend to be weekly regardless of what the student needs that week.

Ramadan moves the usable window to the early afternoon after a shortened school day or to after Iftar, and both work normally over live video. Agreeing the month's slot in advance, with the same tutor and weekday, keeps a technique block intact rather than losing four sessions to improvisation. Families who wait until the first week of the month to raise it usually find the convenient hours have gone.

sections.heading: Starting with the right three facts
paragraphs: Three pieces of paper turn a vague search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Jumeirah 3 into a brief that any good subject teacher can act on immediately. The entry confirmation, showing board, syllabus code, tier and components. The most recent marked script, with the marks written on it. And a count of the teaching weeks genuinely left once school breaks are removed. Assembling those costs an evening and saves at least one paid session of diagnosis.

Use the free trial lesson to test a single thing: whether the tutor can take the marked script and name where the marks went in the language of that board's scheme. A tutor who says the student needs to build confidence has told you nothing. A tutor who says four marks went on premature rounding, three on incomplete transformation descriptions and five on time has given you a plan.

Expect candour about what is reachable. With two terms left, a tier conversation and full specification coverage are both on the table. With six weeks left, the realistic targets are technique, triage and the three topics that appear on every paper. We would rather say which situation a family is in than sell content revision to someone who needs mark-scheme discipline.

If no specialist in the exact code is free at your preferred hour, we will say so and offer alternatives rather than substituting a general mathematics tutor. For a subject where the code determines the mark scheme, that distinction is the whole value of the booking, and filling a slot with the nearest available teacher is precisely the failure this page exists to prevent.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE maths syllabus my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the entry confirmation in writing. It shows the board, the four-digit or alphanumeric syllabus code, the tier where the subject is tiered, and the components entered. The textbook is not reliable evidence, because schools sometimes teach from one publisher's book while entering a different code. Three codes are in common use around Jumeirah 3: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, and they need genuinely different preparation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and Cambridge 0607?
faqs.answer: They are separate syllabuses rather than variants. 0580 is the traditional course, restructured from the 2025 series so candidates sit both a non-calculator and a calculator component, with content centred on algebra, geometry, trigonometry and statistics. 0607 assumes a graphic display calculator, treats modelling and technology as part of the subject, and adds an investigation paper in which a candidate explores a problem rather than answering short questions. IB continuum schools more often enter 0607; British-curriculum schools more often enter 0580.

faqs.question: Does Core or Extended limit the grade my child can achieve?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the single most consequential decision in the course. Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G; Extended is graded A* to E. Pearson 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher with the same practical effect, Foundation capping the available grade. The tier is set at entry, usually a term or more before the papers, and the latest date for changing it is set by the school's internal cut-off rather than the board's published deadline. Ask which tier your child is on and when that decision was reviewed.

faqs.question: What are the commonest mark-scheme traps in IGCSE maths papers?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes award method as well as answers. In a multi-step question, visible working earns method marks, and an unsupported correct answer can score less than a fully worked incorrect one. The other recurring causes are rounding at an intermediate step so the final value falls outside the accepted tolerance, giving units that do not match what the question asked for, and describing a transformation without every element the scheme requires. All four are habits rather than knowledge gaps, and all four are fixable within a term.

faqs.question: How should my child actually use past papers for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Four steps, and the first is the one usually skipped. Sit the paper cold and alone, in one sitting, with a clock. Mark it against the board's own scheme, writing the mark gained beside each question rather than a tick. Categorise every lost mark as content, method, accuracy, misreading or time. Then rework only the two largest categories and re-sit those questions a week later, cold. A paper completed with help measures confidence, not readiness, which is why most past-paper practice produces no improvement.

faqs.question: Will a tutor send us a bundle of 0580 papers and marking guides?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables are the property of Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement; for unreleased material it carries a malpractice exposure as well. We reference them and link to each board's own pages instead. Your school's exams officer has access to more than is published publicly, and both routes are free. Any provider offering a bundle of these materials is telling you something about how they operate.

faqs.question: What does the 0607 investigation paper actually require?
faqs.answer: An extended exploration of a problem rather than a sequence of short questions. A candidate generates cases, identifies a pattern, generalises it, justifies the generalisation and communicates the result in writing, with the graphic display calculator used as a tool throughout. It cannot be revised topic by topic, which is why students meeting it for the first time in the examination hall lose marks unconnected to their mathematical ability. Several timed attempts, marked and discussed, is the only preparation that works.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor cost for a family in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands run from roughly AED 33 to 650 an hour. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget online end; Unitors publishes online IGCSE rates from AED 150; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350; BartyED publishes AED 650. For mathematics the AED 150 to 300 band is where a teacher who knows your child's syllabus code normally sits. These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor a false economy for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: It depends what you need. At the AED 45 to 65 end you are buying homework supervision, which has real value in Year 9 or Year 10 for a student who simply stops when stuck. What you are not reliably buying is somebody who knows that 0607 has an investigation paper, that 0580 now includes a non-calculator component, or how Pearson's question style differs from Cambridge's. In Year 11, where the whole value of a session comes from the mark scheme, that difference decides whether the money produced anything.

faqs.question: My child is strong at maths but scores badly in timed papers. What is the fix?
faqs.answer: Almost always triage and pacing rather than content. A student who spends twelve minutes on a four-mark question has made a decision that costs more marks than they gained. The teachable routine is to read the mark allocation, attempt the questions that pay, abandon anything that is not moving after a set time and return at the end. Practised across three timed papers it becomes automatic. A marked script in which no question is left blank is the test that it has worked.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Jumeirah 3 for maths lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition online over live video everywhere in the UAE and we do not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the Emirates; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do work in Dubai, quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate widely. The difference from the online band is logistics rather than teaching.

faqs.question: How many weeks of maths tutoring does a Year 11 student in Dubai need?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the diagnosis finds. If the losses are mostly method, accuracy and time, a six to eight week technique block with independent timed papers between sessions often does the work. If there are genuine content gaps across several topics, a full year at one hour a week from the start of Year 11 is the realistic answer, and starting in Year 10 is cheaper still. Build any plan assuming roughly six usable weeks in every eight, because Dubai school breaks and Ramadan remove the rest.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE maths papers and results fall for UAE candidates?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson's final November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge runs June and November series too and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Always plan against the live official timetable, because provisional versions can be revised.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat specific amounts quoted at you as unverified. This is a MoHRE permit, not a KHDA school licence.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the free trial maths lesson?
faqs.answer: The entry confirmation showing board, syllabus code, tier and components; the most recent marked script with the marks written on it; and a realistic count of the teaching weeks left once school breaks are removed. With those three a first session can produce a categorised list of where the marks went and a short habit checklist to apply in the next paper. The trial is free, needs no card details and carries no obligation, and a tutor who cannot name the losses specifically has answered your question anyway.

intro.heading: IGCSE maths is the cheapest subject to fix and the easiest to overbuy
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject Jumeirah Golf Estates families ask about most, and it is also the one where the gap between what tuition should cost and what it does cost is widest. The reason is that most lost marks in IGCSE mathematics are not knowledge gaps. They are four or five repeated technical habits that appear on every paper a student sits, and once named they go. Six to ten sessions is a realistic block for a grade move. Thirty weeks of general weekly support is what gets sold.

Here is the arithmetic that should frame the decision. A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, so nine targeted sessions at a mid-band rate is in the region of AED 1,800. A general weekly arrangement running thirty weeks at the same rate is around AED 6,000. The second one is not three times better. It is frequently no better at all, because nobody ever read a marked paper and named the habit.

Two decisions sit above all of that and both are made before a tutor is hired. The first is the board: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 are different qualifications with different paper structures, and a tutor working from the wrong scheme of work wastes a block. The second is the tier, which sets a hard ceiling. A Core or Foundation entry caps the available grade at 5. No amount of tuition lifts that, and buying hours against it is the most complete waste available in this market.

So the shape of this page is diagnostic rather than promotional. It sets out what each paper carries, maps the topics that decide the grade onto the papers they appear in, names the five habitual errors in order of cost, prices the work by tier with attribution, and explains what the November series is worth as a route. Then it says plainly which situations tuition cannot help.

One more thing worth knowing before you compare quotes. The November series is a genuine budget option that almost nobody mentions at the point of sale. Both boards run one, so a resit sits roughly five months after June rather than a year, and a focused block aimed at a single paper after results is a smaller spend than a general year before them. If the realistic view in February is that the grade will land a band short, that changes which plan is worth paying for.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf.subjectsIntro: Mathematics divides into topic clusters that behave very differently under examination pressure. These are the clusters tuition is actually bought for, with a note on where each one sits and what it costs in sessions.

subjects.name: Number and arithmetic fluency
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds and reverse percentages. On Cambridge this cluster decides the non-calculator paper, and it is where a student who has always had a device loses marks fastest. Two or three sessions of deliberate non-calculator work has an unusually high return.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations. The load-bearing cluster: weakness here shows up in trigonometry, in graphs and in problem-solving questions that are not about algebra at all. Usually four to six sessions and the highest-value block in the subject.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients, intersections and inverse functions. Students lose marks by producing a correct sketch and then not reading the required information off it, which is a question-reading problem rather than a graphing one.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, the sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems. The common failure is diagram labelling: an unlabelled sketch leads to the wrong rule, and the method marks go with it. Three sessions usually settles it.

subjects.name: Geometry and mensuration
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, similarity, surface area and volume. Circle theorems are a recall-plus-reasoning cluster where students name the theorem without stating the reason, and reasons carry marks. Efficient to tutor because the rules are finite.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths and averages from grouped data. Histograms with unequal widths are a reliable source of lost marks and take a single session to fix permanently.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations with full descriptions. Transformation questions want a complete description — type, centre, factor, direction — and partial descriptions earn partial marks at best.

subjects.name: Problem-solving and multi-step questions
subjects.description: The questions at the back of the paper that combine two or three clusters. These are where grade 7 becomes grade 8 or 9, and they need practice rather than teaching: the skill is deciding what to do first, which only comes from attempting many of them.

subjects.name: Calculus and logarithms
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, stationary points and logarithmic manipulation, a year ahead of A Level or the Diploma. Expect a higher session count here than for 0580, because it is genuinely new content rather than a technique correction.

subjects.name: Non-calculator technique
subjects.description: Not a topic but a skill, and the one most specific to Cambridge. Long multiplication, fraction arithmetic, surds, estimation and sensible mental checking. It decays quietly across Years 9 and 10 and needs rebuilding deliberately before the June series.

sections.heading: The five errors that cost the most marks
paragraphs: Parents describe a subject. Examiners see a small set of habits repeating across every paper, and in IGCSE mathematics there are five that account for most of the loss. Ranked by cost, the first is missing method. On a four, five or six-mark question most of the marks are for the steps, so a student who writes a single final answer loses nearly all of them when that answer is wrong. This is free to fix and it is worth several marks a page in a typical Jumeirah Golf Estates mock.

The second is rounding. An intermediate value rounded to three significant figures and carried into the next step produces a final answer that is close but not right, and the accuracy mark goes. The rule is to work to full precision and round once at the end; students break it constantly because it feels tidier not to.

The third is unlabelled diagrams. In trigonometry and geometry the choice of rule depends on which sides and angles are known, and a student who does not mark the diagram picks the wrong rule and then executes it perfectly. The fourth is question reading: the question asks for the perimeter and the student produces the area, or asks for a description of a transformation and the student names the type without the centre or the factor. Partial descriptions earn partial marks.

The fifth is specific to Cambridge: non-calculator decay. Every piece of homework a Year 10 student does has a device on the desk, so fraction arithmetic, long multiplication and surd manipulation quietly rot across two years and then appear on a paper where no device is allowed. All five of these are visible in a single marked paper, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything at all.

sections.heading: Which paper does what, and what that changes
paragraphs: Revision is usually spread evenly across a syllabus, and the paper structure says it should not be. The current Cambridge 0580 model assesses through two papers of equal weight, one taken without a calculator and one with, at both Core and Extended tiers. Pearson 4MA1 assesses through two papers of equal weight with a calculator permitted on both. Confirm the exact structure for your child's cohort with the school, because assessment models are periodically revised.

That single difference changes the whole revision plan. A Cambridge candidate needs a deliberate programme of non-calculator work, because half the available marks sit on a paper where arithmetic fluency is load-bearing. A Pearson candidate does not, and time spent drilling long division for them is time taken from problem-solving practice where their marks actually are.

The second thing the structure tells you is where the difficult questions sit. On both boards the multi-step problem-solving questions cluster towards the end of each paper, and they are what separates grade 7 from grade 8 or 9. Those questions cannot be taught in the usual sense; they need volume, because the skill is deciding what to do first.

The practical consequence for a Jumeirah Golf Estates family is that the question to ask a prospective tutor is not whether they teach IGCSE maths. It is which code your child sits, how many papers it has, whether one of them is non-calculator, and what they would drill differently as a result. A specialist answers that in a sentence.

sections.heading: The tier ceiling, and the money wasted against it
paragraphs: No conversation in IGCSE mathematics matters more than this one, and it is routinely had too late. A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5. A Pearson Foundation entry does the same. If the post-16 plan requires a grade 6 or 7 — and A Level Mathematics and IB Diploma Higher Level routinely do — a student on the lower tier cannot reach it however many sessions are bought.

Schools place students on the lower tier for defensible reasons. A borderline candidate entered for Extended can score below the lowest Extended grade and come away with nothing, where Core would have produced a safe 4 or 5. That is a genuine risk, not administrative timidity. But the placement is made in Year 10 on Year 10 evidence, and a student whose work changes materially in the first term of Year 11 can sometimes be moved. Nobody moves them unless a parent asks.

This is where a short diagnostic block has real value. Six sessions on Extended-tier material produces a straightforward answer: either the student handles the additional algebra and problem-solving or the gap is wider than one term can close. We have told Jumeirah Golf Estates families both, and the second answer saves more money than the first.

If the tier cannot be changed and the post-16 plan requires a higher grade, the honest options are to revise the post-16 plan or to enter the November series on the higher tier, potentially as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre. Both are legitimate. Buying thirty sessions against a ceiling is not.

For mathematics specifically, the useful observation is that the block sizes are small. A technique block is six to nine sessions. A single weak content cluster is four to six. sections.heading: Mapping topics onto the papers they appear in
paragraphs: One reason general revision underperforms is that it treats every topic as equally likely to appear and equally expensive to get wrong. That is not how a mathematics paper works. Some clusters are almost guaranteed, some are high-mark when they appear, and some are cheap to secure because the rule set is finite.

The clusters that reliably carry marks across both boards are algebraic manipulation, ratio and percentages, trigonometry, and averages from grouped data. The clusters that are cheap to secure are circle theorems, transformation descriptions, and histograms with unequal class widths, because each has a short, learnable set of rules and a predictable question shape. The clusters that are expensive and unavoidable are multi-step problem-solving questions, which carry the top marks and only improve with volume.

For a student targeting a grade 6 or 7, the efficient order is: fix the habits, secure the finite-rule clusters, then build algebraic fluency, then do problem-solving volume. For a student targeting an 8 or 9, the habits are usually already gone and almost all of the remaining work is problem-solving volume with careful marking.

A specialist answers from the marked paper. A generalist starts at the beginning of the syllabus, which is the most expensive place to start.

One caveat on using the table. Frequency is not the same as importance for your child specifically. If a marked paper shows every circle-theorem mark already secured, that row is irrelevant however reliably the topic appears, and the sessions belong somewhere else entirely.

sections.heading: The November series as a budget option
paragraphs: Almost nobody prices the resit route in, and for a family deciding how much to spend before June it changes the calculation. Cambridge runs a November series alongside June, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in November as well as May/June. A resit therefore sits roughly five months after the summer rather than a year, and private candidate entry through an approved Dubai centre is possible.

The arithmetic is worth doing. Thirty weeks of general weekly support before June, at a mid-band rate, is in the region of AED 6,000. A focused block of eight to ten sessions after results, aimed at one paper and one tier, is roughly AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 plus the centre's entry fee. If the realistic assessment in February is that the grade will land a band short, the second plan is both cheaper and more targeted.

Two practical cautions. The entry deadline for a November series falls well before the examination and often before a family has finished absorbing August results, so find the date in advance rather than after results day. And examination entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the centre, not to a tutor, which is a cost that belongs in the comparison.

The resit window is also the only realistic route past a tier ceiling. A student entered for Core in June can be entered for Extended in November, which converts an unmovable grade 5 into a genuine possibility. That is a conversation to have with the school in March, not in September.

sections.heading: When maths tuition is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: A page about cost should name the situations where the answer is to spend nothing. The first is the tier ceiling already described: a Core-tier student needing a grade 7 does not have a tuition problem, and the conversation with the school costs nothing.

The second is the student already on an upward line. A child who had a bad term and has since turned a corner will keep improving without a tutor, and nobody in this market will volunteer that. A short diagnostic block tells you which situation you are in for a fraction of the price of a year.

The third is the reading problem wearing a maths costume. A surprising proportion of students described as weak at mathematics are losing marks on comprehension of multi-step wordy questions, which is a reading and planning issue. It is still fixable, but by a different kind of work, and buying more algebra teaching will not touch it.

The fourth is the overloaded week. A student with three weekly tuition slots on top of a full Dubai timetable and clubs in Dubai Sports City has no time left for unaided practice, and the unaided attempt is where the learning happens. In that household, removing a tuition slot sometimes raises the grade. We would rather say that than bill for the third subject.

The fifth is a timing mismatch. A student eight weeks from the June series who is two full topics behind cannot be caught up and polished at once, and a provider promising both is selling optimism. In that situation the useful plan is to secure the marks that are reachable, accept the ceiling for this series, and treat the November entry as the second attempt rather than spending heavily on a schedule that was never going to fit.
