sections.heading: Fitting maths into a Jumeirah Golf Estates evening
paragraphs: Timing decides whether a block delivers. In this community the afternoon runs late: campus finish between 2.45pm and 3.30pm depending on the school, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue at Jumeirah Park or on the Sports City side, and twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving depending on whether the school sits in Al Barsha South or Arabian Ranches. Clubs then take a good proportion of children out again until after six.

So weekday maths sessions work between 6.30pm and 8.15pm, and they work best after a first attempt at the problem set. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which is exactly what a specialist resolves quickly. A session placed before homework becomes supervised homework, which is a poor use of the rate and builds dependence rather than technique.

Weekend mornings are underused here and they are the right slot for whole papers under timed conditions, because a paper needs an uninterrupted ninety minutes that a weekday evening in this community rarely offers. For Cambridge candidates, the non-calculator paper in particular should be sat at full length rather than in pieces.

Online delivery is what keeps all of this flexible. With no travel on the tutor's side a session can move within the week when a tournament or a school deadline collides, shift to post-Iftar during Ramadan, and pause through mock weeks. A stop date is agreed at the start, so the arrangement ends deliberately instead of running into a second year unreviewed.

process.title: Find the code and the tier
process.description: The syllabus code and the tier are on the last report or the entry confirmation: 0580 or 4MA1, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. Both answers change the quote. A tier ceiling in particular should be established before a single session is bought, because no number of hours lifts it.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: A marked mock shows a specialist in twenty minutes which of the five habitual errors is costing marks and whether there is a genuine content gap underneath. That is what determines the session count, and the session count is what the price actually is. Any quote made without it is a guess you will pay to correct.

process.title: Ask for a block, not a slot
process.description: Request a session count, a total, the specific errors being targeted, and a review date against the next school assessment. In IGCSE mathematics the honest answer is usually six to nine sessions. A proposal for thirty weeks of weekly support should prompt the question of what it is aimed at.

process.title: Take the free trial on a lost question
process.description: You and your child meet the proposed code-specific tutor over live video. Hand them a question from the mock that was lost. Afterwards you get their read on the problem, a session count and the fee, and you decide. No payment is required to reach that point and nothing is conditional on booking.

process.title: Review at the next assessment
process.description: Put the review in the calendar at the start. If the named errors have gone, stop or move to the next cluster. If they have not, we change the approach or the tutor. This step is what separates a block that works from a standing arrangement nobody has examined since September.

whyPoints.title: Blocks, not open-ended slots
whyPoints.description: Most IGCSE maths problems are six to nine sessions of habit correction, and we quote them that way with a review date attached. Selling a year of weekly support would be more profitable and would not be more honest, since the errors that cost the marks are visible in a single paper.

whyPoints.title: Staffed by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different qualifications with different paper structures, and one has a non-calculator paper while the other does not. That changes what should be drilled. We match on the code rather than on the subject name, because a generalist rarely volunteers which board they know.

whyPoints.title: We name the tier ceiling
whyPoints.description: A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade at 5, and we say so before taking a booking aimed at a 7. The useful response is a diagnostic block to test whether a tier change is realistic, or a November entry on the higher tier, not thirty sessions spent against a ceiling.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to stop
whyPoints.description: Sometimes three sessions on non-calculator fluency is the whole job. Sometimes a student is already improving and needs nobody. Sometimes removing one of three tuition slots raises the grade by freeing time for unaided practice. Saying so costs bookings and is why the ones we take tend to work.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor cost in Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Less than most families budget, if the work is specified properly. Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and most IGCSE mathematics problems are six to nine sessions of habit correction, so AED 1,200 to AED 1,800 at a mid-band rate. A single weak content cluster is four to six sessions. Additional Mathematics 0606 is the exception, at twelve to fifteen. Those are market rates researched in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices, which follow the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Which maths errors cost IGCSE students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Five, in order. Missing method lines on multi-mark questions, where the steps carry most of the marks and a wrong final answer loses nearly all of them. Rounding an intermediate value and carrying it forward, which forfeits the accuracy mark. Unlabelled diagrams, which lead to the wrong trigonometric rule executed perfectly. Answering a question adjacent to the one asked, including incomplete transformation descriptions. And, for Cambridge candidates, non-calculator fluency quietly decaying across Years 9 and 10. All five are visible in one marked paper.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge 0580 really have a non-calculator paper?
faqs.answer: The current Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics model assesses through two papers of equal weight, one taken without a calculator and one with, at both Core and Extended tiers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A permits a calculator on both of its papers. Confirm the exact structure for your child's cohort with the school, since assessment models are periodically revised. The difference matters because a Cambridge candidate needs deliberate non-calculator drilling for half the available marks, and a Pearson candidate's time is better spent on problem-solving volume.

faqs.question: My child is on Core tier but needs a grade 7. What now?
faqs.answer: Tuition cannot deliver that, and it is important to know before spending. A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum grade at 5, and a Pearson Foundation entry does the same. There are three honest routes. Ask the school whether a tier review is possible early in Year 11, which a six-session diagnostic block on Extended material can inform. Enter the November series on the higher tier, potentially as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre. Or revise the post-16 plan. Buying thirty sessions against the ceiling achieves nothing.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking in Year 11?
faqs.answer: If A Level Mathematics or IB Diploma Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is the plan, yes, and it is cheaper than any bridging tuition bought afterwards. It introduces calculus, logarithms, vectors and formal function notation a year early, which is exactly the content students arriving into the Diploma are missing. The caution is that it is genuinely harder, so a student not yet secure at Extended level should not be added to it as enrichment. Not every school near Jumeirah Golf Estates offers it, so ask before option forms are signed.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the best return for tutoring money?
faqs.answer: The finite-rule clusters, because they have a learnable set of rules and a predictable question shape. Circle theorems take one or two sessions and recur reliably for several marks. Transformation descriptions take one session, since the marks are lost only to incompleteness. Histograms with unequal class widths take a single session and are one of the best returns in the syllabus. Algebraic manipulation is more expensive at four to six sessions but comes first, because weakness there shows up in trigonometry, graphs and problem-solving questions that are not about algebra.

faqs.question: Would a November resit cost less than a year of weekly maths tuition?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is rarely priced in. Both Cambridge and Pearson run a November series, so a resit sits roughly five months after June. Thirty weeks of general support beforehand runs to around AED 6,000 at a mid-band rate; a focused eight to ten session block after results, aimed at one paper and one tier, is AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 plus the centre's entry fee. Two cautions: the November entry deadline falls before results have settled, and the entry fee is paid to the centre rather than to a tutor.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions does a grade move take at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Six to nine, where the losses are habitual, which they usually are. Four to six where a marked paper shows one weak content cluster such as algebraic fractions or circle theorems. Five for Core-tier consolidation aimed at securing a 4 or 5. Eight to ten for a June-series run-in built around whole timed papers. Twelve to fifteen for Additional Mathematics 0606, which is genuinely new content. Any provider quoting before reading a marked paper is pricing a guess, and the first sessions will be spent on diagnosis you have already paid for.

faqs.question: Can group maths tuition work for an IGCSE student here?
faqs.answer: For sweeping content before mocks, yes, where everyone in the group is on the same code and tier. For the thing most students actually need, no. The individual algebraic gap or the particular habit costing marks on every paper is only visible when somebody is reading that student's work, and in a group of four nobody is. Cost per student falls and attention per student falls with it. Scheduling also becomes the binding constraint for every family involved, which in a club-heavy community is not a small problem.

faqs.question: Is online maths tuition as good as somebody at the table?
faqs.answer: For mathematics it is arguably better, because the medium is a shared writing surface. A worked solution builds line by line where both people can see it, the mark scheme sits open on both sides, and the session can be revisited afterwards. What matters much more than the room is whether the tutor knows the code: a specialist in Cambridge 0580 Extended who understands the non-calculator paper will do more for a grade over video than a general maths tutor will at a kitchen table.

faqs.question: What time should maths sessions run for a Jumeirah Golf Estates student?
faqs.answer: Between 6.30pm and 8.15pm on weekdays, and after the first attempt at homework rather than before it. The afternoon here runs late: campus finish between 2.45pm and 3.30pm, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue, twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving, then clubs in Dubai Sports City for many children. A student who has already tried the problem set arrives with a specific sticking point, which is what forty minutes with a specialist fixes. Weekend mornings are the right slot for full timed papers.

faqs.question: Could my child's maths problem actually be a reading problem?
faqs.answer: It happens more often than families expect. A noticeable proportion of students described as weak at mathematics are losing marks on comprehension of multi-step wordy questions: the algebra is fine and the interpretation of what the question wants is not. It shows up as a pattern on a marked paper, where short technical questions score well and longer contextual ones do not. It is fixable, but by planning and question-dissection work rather than by more algebra teaching, and buying the latter will not touch it.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a UAE permit to teach my child maths online?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE sits under a private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask a tutor directly whether they hold it and under which category. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published.

faqs.question: What happens if the maths tutor turns out not to suit my child?
faqs.answer: We change them, and this is a question worth asking any provider before paying. A mismatch on pace or personality is our problem rather than yours, so a different code-specific tutor is proposed without argument and without a new joining cost. If no appropriate specialist is free in your windows, you are told the realistic wait instead, and where the available tutor is based outside the UAE you are told that before any payment is taken. Pearson 4MA1 supply is thinner in this market than Cambridge, which affects waits rather than rates.

intro.heading: Knowing maths is not the same as knowing your child's maths
paragraphs: Almost any competent tutor can do IGCSE mathematics. Rather fewer can tell you, without looking it up, which components your child's syllabus code has, whether a calculator is permitted in each, which tier they are on, and which topics that tier adds or removes. Those are the facts that decide what a session should contain, and they are the ones a parent cannot verify from a CV.

The two qualifications most Dubai schools use are Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, code 0580, tiered into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, tiered into Foundation and Higher. They cover similar mathematics and examine it differently, including the calculator position, which means their past papers are not interchangeable.

A tutor working from the wrong board's papers will look entirely competent. Your child will work hard, the sessions will feel productive, and the marks will not move, because the question styles and the assumptions about what can be computed differ. Parents usually discover this after a term, which is why one email to the exams officer is the highest-return action available before any money is spent on anything at all.

The tier is the second fact and it does more than cap a grade. In mathematics the higher tier includes topics the lower tier never teaches, and several of them are the ones post-16 courses assume. A tutor who has not confirmed the tier may spend weeks on content your child will not be examined on, or leave out content they will be examined on, and neither error is visible to a parent until a report arrives.

So the honest answer to whether anyone nearby knows your child's syllabus is: ask them. Five questions, answered without looking anything up, will tell you more than any amount of experience-reading. This page gives you the five, and then names the tier-separating topics so you can judge whether the answers were real rather than confident.

Two more facts belong in the first conversation rather than the fifth. The series: UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. And the timetable: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version, and the one that applies is the copy your school's exams officer holds rather than anything found online.

IB Gram matches your child to a tutor briefed on that exact entry and teaches live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and with no school or tuition centre inside the Jumeirah Islands gates, online removes a journey from the day rather than adding one.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-isla.subjectsIntro: The topics a tutor should be able to place immediately in your child's tier, with the characteristic failure in each. Use them to check whether a claimed specialism is real.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Both tiers, deeper at Extended or Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying algebraic fractions, rearranging formulae, indices and surds. Algebraic fractions and surds sit at the higher tier, and a tutor who cannot say that has not checked the specification. The characteristic loss is mid-question on multi-step work that was set up correctly.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic equations, simultaneous equations including one linear and one quadratic at the higher tier, and inequalities. Students find one root and stop, or reverse an inequality incorrectly when multiplying by a negative. Both are procedural fixes of about one session each.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.levels: Composite and inverse at the higher tier
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, reciprocal and exponential graphs, transformations, and composite and inverse functions at the higher tier only. Sketches are marked on features rather than neatness: intercepts, asymptotes and turning points, which students omit because nobody told them the marks were there.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Sine and cosine rules at the higher tier
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras at both tiers, with the sine and cosine rules, triangle area and three-dimensional problems at the higher tier. The failure is identifying the right triangle inside a three-dimensional diagram, which needs drawing practice rather than more formulae.

subjects.name: Mensuration and circle theorems
subjects.levels: Circle theorems at the higher tier
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, similarity, and circle theorems at the higher tier. Circle theorems reward stating the reason as well as the answer; students who give only the answer score partially, which is a cheap and very common loss.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: Histograms and conditional probability at the higher tier
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths, tree diagrams and conditional probability. Histograms with unequal intervals are among the most reliably dropped marks in the syllabus and take about one session to fix properly.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and bounds
subjects.levels: Upper and lower bounds at the higher tier
subjects.description: Standard form, percentage change, compound interest, direct and inverse proportion, and upper and lower bounds. Bounds questions are badly answered because students apply the wrong bound in a subtraction or a division, which is a rule rather than a concept.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.levels: Vector geometry at the higher tier
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations with full descriptions. Transformation answers must name type, centre, scale factor and direction as required, and partial descriptions score partially. Another cheap, recurring loss.

subjects.name: Calculus in Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Differentiation, stationary points, rates of change and basic integration, arriving far earlier than students expect. It assumes complete algebraic fluency, so any weakness in the main syllabus surfaces at once and is better closed before the course begins.

subjects.name: Working, rounding and timing
subjects.description: Showing working so method marks survive a wrong answer, avoiding rounding at intermediate steps, reading the accuracy instruction, and managing time across the paper. The cheapest marks in the subject and the ones most often left untaught because they feel too obvious.

sections.heading: Five questions that test a maths tutor on your child's entry
paragraphs: These have right answers, which is what makes them useful. Ask them in the trial session, before any discussion of price, and listen for whether the tutor answers from knowledge or from inference. A tutor who says they will confirm with the school and then does is acceptable; one who glosses over it will be guessing for a term.

First: what is my child's syllabus code and what components does it have? Second: does a non-calculator component apply at my child's tier? Third: which topics does the higher tier add that the lower tier does not teach? Fourth: which series will my child sit, and which series exist for a UAE candidate? Fifth: what will you ask me for before the first session?

The right answer to the fifth is a marked paper and the school's assessment calendar. A tutor who asks only for the textbook or the topic list intends to teach content, which is rarely the binding problem in IGCSE mathematics. The binding problems are reliability under time, method selection and specific procedural topics.

On the fourth, a tutor who mentions a February or March examination window has not prepared UAE candidates. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only; candidates here sit June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Checkpoint tests at lower secondary do run in March, which is the only legitimate March reference in this market.

sections.heading: The topics that separate the tiers, so you can check the answer
paragraphs: A parent cannot judge a tutor's claim to know the tier without knowing roughly what the tier contains, so here it is. The higher tier in IGCSE mathematics is not the lower tier with harder questions; it includes topics the lower tier never covers, and those topics are disproportionately the ones a post-16 maths course assumes.

The clearest examples: algebraic fractions and more demanding rearrangement; the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional trigonometry; composite and inverse functions; histograms with unequal class widths; conditional probability; upper and lower bounds; circle theorems; and vector geometry. A tutor who can produce most of that list from memory has read the specification.

This matters practically in two directions. A lower-tier candidate being taught higher-tier content is having their hour wasted and their confidence knocked. A higher-tier candidate whose tutor is working at the lower tier arrives at the paper under-prepared on exactly the topics that distinguish the grades.

It also matters for the tier decision itself. If your child is near the boundary and needs mathematics for A Level or the Diploma, the argument for the higher tier is made with marked evidence in Year 10, aimed specifically at the content in that list, followed by strong marks on the school's own assessments.

Specifications are revised and the school holds the version your child is actually sitting, so treat this list as a prompt to check rather than as the specification itself. The table sets out the separating topics with what each one means after Year 11.

sections.heading: What a specialist sees in a marked paper
paragraphs: Hand a tutor a marked paper at the start of the trial session and watch what they do. It is the most informative ten minutes available and it requires no subject knowledge from you. The signals are behavioural: what they look at first, what they ask the student, and how specific they are about the next six weeks.

A specialist reads the questions rather than the total. They look for where marks were lost, then ask the student what they were thinking on two or three of those questions, because the student almost always knows and nobody ever asks. Within ten minutes they can separate content gaps from method failures from exam conduct.

Those three need different responses over different timescales. A content gap, usually a topic never properly learned, takes one to three focused sessions and then stays fixed. A method problem needs marked past papers and a conversation about each decision. An exam-conduct problem, such as unshown working or early rounding, changes within two sessions if the tutor insists every time.

A general tutor does something recognisably different: reads the grade, lists the topics that appear in the paper, and proposes revising them. That produces an open-ended programme with no measurable end, which is the commonest shape of wasted tutoring spend in this city.

The second signal is whether your child writes. A session where the tutor explains for fifty minutes may be entirely accurate and will not move a mark, because the failures are in production rather than comprehension. The third is specificity: ask for two or three named targets with a rough session count each, and treat vagueness as the answer.

sections.heading: Calculator rules change what a session should contain
paragraphs: This is one of the five questions and it deserves its own section, because it changes the weekly work more than any other single fact. Cambridge's current 0580 assessment includes both non-calculator and calculator components at each tier. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A permits a calculator throughout. Confirm the current structure with your school, since specifications are revised.

For a candidate facing a non-calculator component, part of every session has to be spent on exact manual work: fractions, surds, standard form, algebraic manipulation, done quickly by hand and under time. It looks unglamorous next to teaching a new topic and it is where the marks are, because the paper tests that fluency underneath whichever topic it dresses it in.

For a calculator-active candidate the discipline is the opposite and equally specific: efficient use of the exact model the school permits, recording intermediate values to full accuracy, and rounding only at the end. A student who is slow with their own device loses marks on time rather than on mathematics, and that is trainable with the actual calculator in hand.

Both groups need the same thing in one respect: the accuracy instruction in the question read and obeyed. Three significant figures when three are asked for, exact form when exact form is asked for. Students lose marks here for reasons that have nothing to do with understanding, and a tutor who does not police it is leaving easy marks behind.

A tutor who has not established which position applies will default to their own habit, which is usually calculator-active because that is what most teaching looks like. That is how a 0580 candidate arrives at a non-calculator paper having practised with a calculator for a year.

sections.heading: The series, and what a resit actually costs in time
paragraphs: A tutor who knows the calendar is more useful than one who knows an extra topic, because the calendar decides what is possible. UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only and should never appear in a plan for your child.

November is therefore the resit route, and its cost is mostly in timing rather than money. The Pearson precedent shows the shape: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026.

So a November resit means a sixth-form application season carried out with a provisional grade in that subject. Schools are used to it and it is better discussed in August than in January. Where a June grade sits just below a boundary, the alternative is an enquiry about results, submitted by the school within a short window after results for a fee set by the board.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The version that applies is the one your school's exams officer holds.

The practical instruction is simple: plan from the live official timetable the school holds, and treat any date on a tutoring page, including this one, as context rather than as the date your child will sit.

sections.heading: Rates, and the bridging block nobody buys
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65. In-home visits run AED 180-350, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500.

For monthly planning, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All figures are the providers' or survey's own, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price. We publish no rate card because the right number depends on the tier and the weeks remaining.

The best-value purchase in IGCSE mathematics is the one almost nobody makes: a short block in the summer after Year 11, before A Level or the Diploma begins. A good IGCSE grade certifies accuracy with method marks and partial credit. The next stage assumes speed, exactness and much less scaffolding, which is a different thing entirely.

Six to eight sessions on surds, indices, algebraic fractions, rearrangement with the subject on both sides, and completing the square as a default rather than a special case, with nothing else in the diary, removes most of the first-term difficulty at the next level. It is cheaper than the weekly support that difficulty would otherwise require.

The second best-value purchase is the autumn of Year 10, for the same structural reason: acting before a problem compounds costs less than unpicking it afterwards, and it keeps the higher tier available while that decision is still open.

sections.heading: What we do not claim
paragraphs: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. Individual tutors in the UAE do need a permit, and asking about it is reasonable. We publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage, because a statistic without its sample size, date and method cannot be checked. Several providers in this market publish two conflicting ratings on a single page, which is a structured-data problem as well as a credibility one.

We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They are cited and linked, and your child's school holds licensed access to what it needs. Where a subject carries an assessed component, a tutor teaches the criteria and comments on work your child has written, and writes none of it.

And we do not promise grades. No honest provider can promise a score, a number of marks or a percentage improvement, and in a subject as measurable as mathematics the offer of one tells you more about the operator than about the teaching.

faqs.question: Our tutor seems good at maths. How do we know they know the right syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask five things and listen for whether the answers come from knowledge. The syllabus code and its components; whether a non-calculator component applies at your child's tier; which topics the higher tier adds; which series a UAE candidate sits; and what they want from you before the first session. A specialist answers all five without looking anything up and asks for a marked paper. A tutor who asks only for the textbook intends to teach content, which is rarely the binding problem.

faqs.question: What does the higher tier actually include that the lower one does not?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fractions and more demanding rearrangement, the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional trigonometry, composite and inverse functions, histograms with unequal class widths, conditional probability, upper and lower bounds, circle theorems and vector geometry. That list matters twice: it lets you check whether a tutor has read the specification, and it is disproportionately the content that A Level Mathematics and the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches assume a student has met.

faqs.question: Should any of the weekly hour be spent working by hand?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board, which is why the code question comes first. Cambridge's current 0580 assessment includes non-calculator components, so a 0580 candidate needs short, regular manual drills on fractions, surds, standard form and algebraic manipulation under time. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout, where the discipline is efficiency with the specific model and recording values to full accuracy before rounding at the end. Confirm the current structure with your school, because specifications are revised.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to the house here for maths lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. Mathematics tuition for Jumeirah Islands families is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared surface both people write on. Since there is no school or tuition centre inside the gates, online removes a journey rather than adding one. Published in-home rates run AED 180-500 an hour including travel.

faqs.question: What should we hand a tutor at the first meeting?
faqs.answer: One marked paper for your child's exact syllabus code, plus the code and tier from the exams officer and the school's assessment calendar. Then watch what the tutor does with the paper. A specialist reads the questions rather than the total and asks your child what they were thinking on two or three of them; the student almost always knows and nobody asks. That conversation separates a content gap from a method problem in about ten minutes.

faqs.question: Our child understands the work but keeps dropping marks. What is that?
faqs.answer: Usually method selection or exam conduct rather than understanding. A student who can perform every technique but chooses the wrong one, who sets up a question correctly and loses the middle, who rounds at an intermediate step, or who does not show working on a multi-step question where the answer comes out wrong, scores well below their comprehension. All of those are visible on one marked paper and all respond quickly, which is why papers matter more than chapters.

faqs.question: Which topics would you expect to fix first?
faqs.answer: The procedural ones, because they are quick and they are reliably worth marks: histograms with unequal class widths, upper and lower bounds in subtraction and division, circle theorems answered without the reason stated, and transformations described only partially. Each is a rule or a routine rather than a conceptual difficulty, and each takes one to two sessions plus targeted past-paper questions. Algebraic fluency under time is the slower job and runs alongside.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth adding for our child?
faqs.answer: For a student heading to A Level Mathematics, Further Mathematics or the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, usually yes, because it starts the calculus and the pace early. For a student already stretched by the higher tier it is a poor trade, since it assumes complete algebraic fluency and exposes any weakness immediately. Fewer tutors cover it and slots fill early in the year, so decide in Year 10 rather than in Year 11.

faqs.question: What time should the weekly session be?
faqs.answer: 17:00, or 17:30 if your child travels back from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. With no school inside Jumeirah Islands every pupil travels out, and the return leg usually serves two or three other communities first, so arrivals run from roughly 15:40 to 16:50. A 16:30 slot starts before a teenager has eaten and loses its first twenty minutes. Ask the transport office for your own route's timings, because households inside the same gates differ by twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Is a group class a reasonable substitute for one-to-one in maths?
faqs.answer: For a shared gap, yes, and cheaper per hour. A class on frequency density or on circle theorem reasoning works well because everyone needs the same thing. It stops working when your child's problem is their own pattern of errors, because the hour runs on someone else's weakness. The nearest density for group provision from these gates is around Jumeirah Lakes Towers; if you use a centre, note that premises-based training institutes in Dubai require a KHDA Educational Services Permit.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest moment to intervene?
faqs.answer: The autumn of Year 10, and then the summer after Year 11. The first prevents compounding and keeps the higher tier reachable while that decision is still open. The second is a short bridging block before A Level or the Diploma, on surds, indices, algebraic fractions, rearrangement and completing the square, which removes most of the first-term difficulty at the next level. The most expensive moment is February of Year 11, when both slots and weeks are scarce.

faqs.question: What if our child needs to resit in November?
faqs.answer: It is available and the cost is mostly in timing. UAE Cambridge candidates have June and November; Pearson runs May/June and November. The Pearson precedent shows the pattern: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January, and November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026. So a resit means applying to sixth form with a provisional grade. Where a grade sits just below a boundary, ask about an enquiry about results instead.

faqs.question: Do you cover MYP mathematics for a younger sibling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a different kind of work. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria including investigating patterns and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, so marks are lost on communication and on failing to generalise rather than on arithmetic. A tutor needs the school's own task sheet and criterion descriptors to be useful, because the standard is set by the school's boundaries rather than by a textbook. Screen sharing handles that well.

The constraint is the hour rather than the subject: weekday slots between 17:00 and 19:00 in the spring term are what every Year 11 household in Dubai wants and they fill from September. Saturday morning paper slots are popular and we quote a date. Where a tutor is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

A long package bought before the match has been tested, since unused sessions are the commonest complaint in this market. And one hour split between maths and another subject, which completes neither and marks no paper. If a marked paper shows the real issue is uncompleted school homework, we will say that instead of selling hours.

intro.heading: Two facts from the school before you hire anyone
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics is not one qualification. Your child is entered for a specific syllabus with a specific code, at a specific tier, and both of those change what a tutor should be doing on a Tuesday evening. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers. The past papers are not interchangeable and the paper structures differ.

Parents are rarely told this and almost never ask, which is why board-blind tutoring is the most expensive mistake in Dubai maths tuition. A tutor working from the wrong board's papers will teach competently, your child will work hard, and the grade will not move. One email to the school's exams officer asking for the code and tier for mathematics prevents the whole problem before any money is committed.

The tier is the second fact and the more consequential one. Core caps the grades available; Extended carries the top of the scale and covers more content. Dubai schools generally decide on Year 9 and early Year 10 evidence. If your child is near the boundary, and particularly if they need maths for A Level or the IB Diploma later, that is a conversation to have with the head of department in Year 10 rather than a decision to accept silently.

It is worth knowing how much of the local market this affects. Dubai held 387,441 private school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, with 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, so IGCSE mathematics is the single most tutored subject in the city. That means plenty of supply and very uneven quality, and it means the questions you ask before paying do more work than the price you pay.

Once both facts are established the work becomes precise. Mathematics is the most diagnosable subject on an IGCSE timetable: a single marked paper usually shows whether the problem is a content gap, a method-selection failure or exam conduct, and those three need different responses. A tutor who cannot tell you which of the three they are looking at in the first session is not reading the paper properly.

There is one more timing fact specific to the UAE. Cambridge candidates here sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a February exam window is wrong for your child's country. That is not a detail: it is a date a parent would act on, and it circulates in Gulf-facing tutoring content.

IB Gram delivers this as live online tuition to Jumeirah Park, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared working surface where both people can write. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For mathematics the online format is particularly workable, because the subject is written and shared rather than discussed.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: What an IGCSE maths tutor should actually be working on, topic by topic. A specialist can say immediately where each one costs marks at Extended or Higher tier.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying algebraic fractions, rearranging formulae and working with indices and surds. This is the foundation everything else sits on, and it is where Extended candidates most often lose marks in the middle of a long question that they had set up correctly.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic and simultaneous equations, including one linear and one quadratic at Extended. Students lose marks by finding one root and stopping, or by solving an inequality and reversing the sign incorrectly when multiplying by a negative. Both are trainable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, reciprocal and exponential graphs, transformations and, at Extended, composite and inverse functions. Sketching is marked on features rather than neatness: intercepts, turning points and asymptotes, which students omit because nobody told them the marks were there.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras at both tiers, with the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional problems at Extended. The common failure is not the formula but identifying which triangle to use in a three-dimensional diagram, which responds to drawing practice rather than more theory.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors, similarity and circle theorems at Extended. Circle theorems are a reliable source of marks for students who learn to state the reason as well as the answer, and a reliable loss for those who do not.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, tree diagrams and conditional probability at Extended. Histograms with unequal class widths are among the most commonly dropped marks in the whole syllabus and take about one session to fix properly.

subjects.name: Number and ratio
subjects.description: Standard form, upper and lower bounds, percentage change, compound interest, direct and inverse proportion. Bounds questions are disproportionately badly answered because students apply the wrong bound to a subtraction or division, which is a rule rather than an understanding problem.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations with their descriptions. Transformation questions demand a full description -- type, centre, scale factor, direction -- and partial answers score partially, which is a cheap and common loss.

subjects.name: Calculus in Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Differentiation, stationary points, rates of change and basic integration, arriving far earlier than students expect. The course assumes complete fluency in algebra, so weaknesses carried from the main syllabus surface immediately and are better closed before the course starts.

subjects.name: Exam conduct and paper technique
subjects.description: Showing working so method marks survive a wrong answer, managing time across the paper, avoiding early rounding, and reading the accuracy instruction. These are the cheapest marks in the subject and are routinely left untaught because they feel too obvious to teach.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor in Jumeirah Park actually does
paragraphs: The useful version of this service is narrow. A tutor reads a marked paper, identifies which topics are failing and why, teaches those topics properly, then runs past papers for that exact syllabus code under timed conditions and marks them with the student. That is most of it. Everything else is scheduling and honesty about what is possible in the weeks remaining.

IB Gram delivers it as live one-to-one online lessons to Jumeirah Park households, scheduled around when your child actually gets home. There are no home visits in the UAE; that service runs in India only. There is no centre or office here either, so nothing to drive to in either direction.

For mathematics specifically this format is strong rather than compromised. Both people write on a shared surface, the paper is on screen for both, and a graph can be redrawn five times in a minute. The student also keeps the written record of the session, which they do not when the working is on a loose sheet that goes missing by Thursday.

One thing a tutor should also do is tell you when the hour is not the constraint. If a student has not attempted the homework set by their own teacher for three weeks, no tutor fixes that, and buying a second weekly session makes it worse rather than better. The honest intervention there is a conversation with the school, and we would rather say so than sell the slot.

Where in-person wins is with students who will not stay on task without an adult present, and with households that have nowhere quiet at six in the evening. If that is your situation, hire locally and expect the travel premium: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200-500.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are examined differently
paragraphs: The two qualifications cover similar mathematics and assess it differently, which is why past papers are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is tiered into Core and Extended and its current assessment includes both non-calculator and calculator components at each tier. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered into Foundation and Higher and permits a calculator throughout.

That single difference changes the weekly work substantially. A 0580 Extended candidate needs trained exactness without a calculator: fractions, surds, standard form and algebraic manipulation done by hand, quickly. A 4MA1 Higher candidate needs calculator efficiency and discipline about rounding and recording intermediate values. A tutor who prepares one as though they were the other will produce the wrong habits.

Paper counts, mark totals and permitted components are set by the boards and are revised between syllabus cycles, so the authority is the current specification and the version your school holds. Ask the exams officer for the code and the paper structure, and confirm whether a non-calculator component applies at your child's tier before you build a revision plan around it.

There is also a practical consequence for how a session is run. A candidate facing a non-calculator component needs part of each hour spent on mental and written arithmetic under time, which looks unglamorous and is where the marks are. A candidate with a calculator throughout needs the opposite: drilling on efficient use of the specific model and on recording values to full accuracy before rounding at the end.

One further UAE-specific point. Cambridge runs its IGCSE and O Level examinations in June and November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only and is not available to UAE candidates, despite appearing in tutoring content aimed at this market. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

sections.heading: What the tier decides, in maths specifically
paragraphs: In mathematics the tier does more than cap a grade; it removes content. An Extended or Higher candidate studies topics a Core or Foundation candidate never meets, and several of those topics are the ones that matter for what comes next. A student capped at Core who later wants A Level Mathematics or the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches arrives without having seen material the next course assumes.

This is the part worth arguing about in Year 10 if your child is near the boundary. The argument is not made with enthusiasm; it is made with marked evidence. A term of weekly work aimed specifically at the content that separates the tiers, followed by strong marks on the school's own assessments, is what changes a head of department's view. A request without evidence does not.

The reverse case is just as real. A student placed on Extended who is consistently scoring poorly may finish with a better outcome on Core, depending on what they need the subject for. That should be decided with the school's marked work on the table, in the light of the sixth-form requirement, rather than on a feeling about ambition.

For tutoring the operational point is simple: confirm the tier before the first session and again if the school reviews entries in Year 11. Teaching Extended content to a Core candidate wastes the hour and damages confidence, and it happens more often than anyone admits because nobody checked.

sections.heading: The topics that decide an Extended grade
paragraphs: Examiner-report patterns and the marked papers we see point at the same short list every year, and it is shorter than parents expect. Most students losing marks at Extended or Higher are losing them in five or six identifiable places, not across the whole syllabus. That is good news, because a short list is a plan.

Histograms with unequal class widths, upper and lower bounds applied to subtraction or division, circle theorems stated without the reason, full descriptions of transformations, three-dimensional trigonometry, and algebraic fractions in a long multi-step question. Each of these is a rule or a routine rather than a conceptual mystery, and each responds to one or two focused sessions followed by targeted past-paper questions.

The second group is method and conduct rather than content. Not showing working where the final answer is wrong, which forfeits method marks that were available. Rounding at an intermediate step and carrying the error through. Running out of time on the last four questions. These are the cheapest marks in the subject to recover and the least often taught.

Parents often expect the list to be longer, and the length is the useful part. If a student is losing twelve marks a paper and nine of them sit in four identifiable places, then four sessions and some targeted questions are a plan with a measurable end. A general programme of revision has no end, costs more and usually produces less, which is why the marked paper matters more than the number of hours bought.

A tutor should be able to name which of these apply to your child in the first session, from a marked paper, and say roughly how many sessions each needs. If the answer is a general plan to revise the syllabus from the start, the paper has not been read properly.

sections.heading: Timing a maths session around the Jumeirah Park school run
paragraphs: This is the operational detail nobody publishes and it decides whether an arrangement survives a term. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30. A Jumeirah Park bus route that also serves Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village gets most children home between 15:20 and 16:40, depending on district and route. There is no metro station inside the community, so the nearest Route 2020 stations at Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens change nothing for tutoring.

For mathematics the rule is to take the earliest hour you can genuinely sustain, because arithmetic accuracy is the first thing tiredness removes. A student doing bounds and standard form at nine in the evening will make slips they would not make at half past four, and will draw the wrong conclusion about their own ability from them.

Students at the school inside Jumeirah Park can hold 16:00, which is the best maths hour available to anyone in this community. Bussed students should take 17:00 or 17:30 rather than squeezing in at 16:30 before they have eaten. Second-year sixth formers are different and often work better after dinner, but Year 10 and 11 students rarely do.

Keep full papers for the weekend. A Saturday morning slot is the only ninety-minute block in a Jumeirah Park week, and marking the paper on Sunday is where the learning happens. During Ramadan the pattern shifts: shortened school hours and a post-Iftar or late-morning weekend session work better than anything at five in the afternoon, and we reschedule rather than cancel because the series does not move.

sections.heading: From IGCSE maths to whatever comes next
paragraphs: The most valuable maths tutoring a Jumeirah Park family can buy is the term after Year 11 finishes, and almost nobody buys it. A good IGCSE grade certifies accuracy with method marks and partial credit. A Level Mathematics and the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches assume speed, exactness and comfort with abstraction, and they scaffold far less.

The specific gaps are predictable. Surds and indices handled instantly rather than carefully. Algebraic fractions manipulated without error under time. Rearrangement of a formula with the subject appearing twice. Solving a quadratic by completing the square as a default rather than a special case. Reading a graph's features rather than its points. Each of these is a few hours of work when there is no other pressure, and a persistent handicap when there is.

The route choice matters too. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes essentially all of Extended plus fluency; Applications and Interpretation assumes comfort with data and modelling. A Level Mathematics assumes Higher or Extended content. A student who took Core or Foundation needs a stated bridging plan rather than optimism, and the school is the right place to agree one.

There is an equivalency dimension worth noting while planning the next stage. On the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or better or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Mathematics is almost always one of the five, which gives the subject a second kind of weight.

sections.heading: What this costs, and what we will not sell
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65.

On a monthly basis Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages run from about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Every figure here is the provider's or survey's own, read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price.

What we will not sell: coursework of any kind written, part-written or supplied; grade guarantees or money-back improvement schemes; reproduced past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are cited and linked rather than distributed; or any claim of approval by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge or Pearson, none of which IB Gram holds.

We also publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage, because a statistic without its sample size, date and method is a liability rather than a credential. Several providers in this market publish two different ratings on the same page. We would rather show you the arithmetic of a year's support and let you decide.

faqs.question: Our school has not told us the maths syllabus code. Does it really matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than anything else you will decide. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 cover similar mathematics and examine it differently, including the calculator position, so their past papers are not interchangeable. A tutor working from the wrong set will teach well and move nothing, and you will usually find out after a term. Email the exams officer for the code and tier for mathematics specifically; departments within one school sometimes use different boards for different subjects, so ask per subject rather than assuming.

faqs.question: What exactly does being put on Core take away from my child?
faqs.answer: Content, not just grades. An Extended or Higher candidate studies algebraic fractions, the sine and cosine rules, three-dimensional trigonometry, composite and inverse functions, histograms with unequal intervals and conditional probability, among others. A Core candidate does not meet them. That matters at sixteen, because A Level Mathematics and the IB Diploma's Analysis and Approaches assume that content. The grade ceiling is the visible cost; the missing topics are the one that shows up a year later.

faqs.question: Which maths topics most reliably lose marks at Extended tier?
faqs.answer: A short and consistent list: histograms with unequal class widths, upper and lower bounds in subtraction or division, circle theorems answered without stating the reason, transformations described only partially, three-dimensional trigonometry where the wrong triangle is chosen, and algebraic fractions inside long multi-step questions. Most are rules or routines rather than conceptual difficulties, and most take one to three focused sessions plus targeted past-paper questions. That is why a marked paper is worth more than a general assessment.

faqs.question: Does my child need to practise maths without a calculator?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board, which is one more reason to confirm the code. Cambridge 0580's current assessment includes non-calculator components, so a 0580 candidate needs trained manual exactness with fractions, surds, standard form and algebraic manipulation. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout, so the discipline there is about rounding, recording intermediate values and efficiency. Confirm the current paper structure with your school, because specifications are revised and the school holds the version your child is actually sitting.

faqs.question: Can we book a maths tutor to come to the house here?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only. Mathematics tuition for Jumeirah Park families is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared surface both people write on and the paper on screen for both. For maths that format works well and the student keeps the written record. If someone in the room is essential, the Dubai market charges roughly AED 180-500 an hour for in-home visits including travel.

faqs.question: When in the week should maths sessions happen?
faqs.answer: As early in the evening as your household can genuinely sustain, and with full papers at the weekend. Arithmetic accuracy is the first thing tiredness takes, so a student working on bounds at nine at night makes slips that look like weakness. Students at the school inside Jumeirah Park can hold 16:00; bussed students should take 17:00 or 17:30 rather than squeezing in at 16:30 unfed. Saturday morning is the only ninety-minute block in the week and should be used for a timed paper.

faqs.question: My child says they understand it but keeps getting low marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Usually method selection or exam conduct rather than understanding. A student who can perform every technique but picks the wrong one, sets up the question correctly then loses the middle, rounds too early, or fails to show working on a multi-step question where the answer comes out wrong, will score well below their comprehension. These are visible on one marked paper and they respond quickly, which is why a tutor should be reading papers rather than re-teaching chapters.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking alongside the main course?
faqs.answer: For a student heading to A Level Mathematics, Further Mathematics or the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, usually yes, because it starts the calculus and the pace early. For a student who is already stretched by Extended, it is a poor trade: it assumes complete algebraic fluency and exposes any weakness immediately. Fewer tutors cover the course, so rates sit at the upper end of the qualified band and spring slots are scarce. Decide in Year 10, not in Year 11.

faqs.question: How long before we see a change in maths marks?
faqs.answer: On the topic-level work, quickly: histograms, bounds and transformation descriptions can show up as marks on the next assessment. On algebraic fluency, slower, because it is a trained speed rather than a fact. We judge at six sessions on timed work, looking for the named topics now scoring and the student choosing methods unprompted. If that has not happened, the match, frequency or diagnosis changes. Nobody can honestly promise a grade or a number of marks.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer after Year 11?
faqs.answer: A short bridging block, and it is the best-value maths tutoring a family in this community can buy. A good IGCSE grade certifies accuracy with partial credit; A Level Mathematics and the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches assume speed, exactness and much less scaffolding. Six to eight sessions on surds, indices, algebraic fractions, rearrangement and completing the square, with no other pressure in the diary, removes most of the first-term difficulty that otherwise needs weekly support to fix.

faqs.question: Are group maths classes at a centre a reasonable alternative?
faqs.answer: For a shared gap, yes, and per hour they are cheaper. A class on frequency density or on circle theorem reasoning can be excellent value because everyone needs the same thing. For a student whose problem is their own specific pattern of errors, the hour runs on someone else's weakness. If you use a centre in Dubai, note that premises-based training institutes require a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a reasonable thing to ask to see.

faqs.question: Which series will my child actually sit, and can they resit?
faqs.answer: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only and is not available here, despite appearing in content aimed at Gulf parents. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. November is therefore the resit route, and the Pearson precedent shows the timing cost: the November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January, and November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Do you cover MYP mathematics as well, for a younger sibling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a different kind of work. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria including investigating patterns and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, and marks are lost on communication and on failing to generalise rather than on arithmetic. A tutor needs the school's own task sheet and criterion descriptors to be useful, because the standard is set by the school's boundaries. Screen sharing suits that well, since the task sheet can be open in front of both of them.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether a maths tutor is any good in the trial?
faqs.answer: Three things. Did they read the marked paper and name specific topics, or did they offer to revise the syllabus from the start? Could they say which paper structure and calculator rules apply to your child's code? Did your child do most of the writing, or did they watch? A tutor who talks for fifty minutes may be entirely expert and still wrong for a student who needs to be made to work. And be wary of any grade promise.

faqs.question: We are travelling for three weeks. Do we lose the slot?
faqs.answer: No. Sessions follow the time zone you are in, provided we know the week before, and the weekly slot is held either way. Because no tutor has to travel anywhere, a reschedule is a slot swap rather than a renegotiation, which is one of the practical advantages of online delivery for a community where families move between the UAE and elsewhere frequently. Many Jumeirah Park households pause in July and August and restart with a bridging block in late summer.

intro.heading: Maths gaps appear on a schedule, and so should the help
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics is taught in a fairly predictable order across Years 10 and 11, which means the gaps appear on a predictable schedule too. Number and basic algebra come early. Trigonometry and geometry sit in the middle. The harder algebraic manipulation, the circle theorems, histograms with unequal class widths and the multi-step problem solving tend to land late in Year 10 or in Year 11. A student who looks fine in December of Year 10 and struggles in March of Year 11 has usually not deteriorated; they have simply reached the part of the syllabus their foundations could not carry.

That matters for when you buy help. A family in Jumeirah Village Circle ringing in the first term of Year 10 can close the algebraic manipulation gap before it starts costing marks everywhere else, which is the cheapest intervention in the subject by a wide margin. A family ringing in the second term of Year 11 is buying paper technique and recallable marks, which is genuinely worth having and is a narrower job that should be priced as one.

There is also a hard deadline in the middle of all this that nobody announces. The tier decision — Core or Extended with Cambridge, Foundation or Higher with Pearson — is made by the school during Year 10 on Year 10 evidence, and a Core or Foundation entry caps the available grade at 5. It is reviewable early in Year 11 if somebody asks before the final entry deadline, and it is unreviewable afterwards. That single date determines whether tuition can affect the ceiling or only the mark inside it.

And one calendar item specific to mathematics: non-calculator fluency. For Cambridge candidates, whose current mathematics model includes a paper taken without a calculator, exact arithmetic decays across two years of homework done with a device on the desk and then has to work for ninety minutes. Rebuilding it belongs in the final eight to ten weeks, because fluency rebuilt in Year 10 decays again before the papers.

The clearest illustration of all this is Additional Mathematics 0606, where the calendar advice inverts. Everything else in IGCSE mathematics can be repaired fairly late, because the content was taught earlier and is being revisited in revision. 0606 is new material delivered at pace across a single year with nothing earlier to fall back on, so an early slip becomes a teaching backlog rather than a revision gap, and backlogs in new content are expensive to clear. Starting in the first term costs a fraction of starting after the mocks.

We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Our fee follows a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on how many weeks are left and what a marked paper shows.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-vill.subjectsIntro: Mathematics divides into clusters that are taught at different points in the two years. These are the ones tuition is bought for, with a note on when each one usually becomes a visible problem.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Fractions, standard form, bounds, reverse percentages and compound change. Taught early, so a gap here is visible by the end of the first term of Year 10 and is the cheapest thing in the subject to fix at that point.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations. Taught across both years and the load-bearing cluster: weakness here surfaces later in trigonometry, in graphs and in problem solving that is not about algebra at all.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients, intersections and inverse functions. Usually mid-Year 10 onwards, and the point at which a student carrying weak algebra starts to lose marks on questions they could otherwise answer.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled work, sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Typically late Year 10. The classic failure is an unlabelled diagram leading to the wrong rule, executed perfectly — three sessions settles it whenever they are taken.

subjects.name: Geometry, circle theorems and mensuration
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, similarity, surface area and volume. Circle theorems usually arrive in Year 11 and are among the cheapest topics to secure, because the rule set is finite and the question shapes are predictable.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree and Venn diagrams, cumulative frequency, averages from grouped data and histograms with unequal class widths. The histogram work frequently lands late and costs reliable marks; one session usually fixes it permanently.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry and the four transformations with full descriptions. Often taught late in Year 11, which is why it is one of the topics most commonly still shaky going into the final eight weeks.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.description: The questions at the back of each paper combining two or three clusters. These are what separate grade 7 from grade 8 or 9, and they improve with volume rather than teaching, so they need calendar time rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Calculus and logarithms
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, stationary points and logarithmic manipulation. Entirely new in Year 11 and taught fast, so a student who falls behind in the first term rarely catches up without a deliberate block.

subjects.name: Non-calculator technique
subjects.description: Not a topic but a skill, and specific to Cambridge. Long multiplication, fraction arithmetic, surds, estimation and sensible checking. Decays quietly across both years and belongs in the final eight to ten weeks, not earlier.

sections.heading: When each maths gap becomes visible
paragraphs: Schools teach IGCSE mathematics in broadly the same order, which makes the timing of problems predictable. Number, ratio and percentages come first, so a weakness there is apparent by the end of the first term of Year 10 and is cheap to fix at that point. Algebraic manipulation runs across both years, so it is detectable early and keeps costing marks if it is not addressed.

Graphs and functions arrive next, and they are where weak algebra first becomes visible to a parent, because the student can describe what to do and cannot execute it. Trigonometry typically lands late in Year 10, with the unlabelled-diagram failure appearing immediately. Circle theorems, vectors, transformations and histograms with unequal class widths tend to arrive in Year 11, which is why those four are so often still shaky going into the final term.

The practical consequence is that a student who seemed fine in December of Year 10 and struggles in March of Year 11 has usually not got worse. They have reached the parts of the syllabus their foundation could not support, plus the multi-step problem-solving questions that combine clusters and reward volume of practice rather than explanation.

This is why the useful first question is not how is your child doing in maths but which topics has the school covered so far. Combined with a marked paper, it tells a specialist whether the problem is a foundation issue that will keep recurring or a single late-taught topic that needs four sessions. Those are very different purchases.

sections.heading: The tier window, and the date it closes
paragraphs: This is the deadline that matters most and the one families almost never know about. A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5, and a Pearson Foundation entry does the same. If the post-16 plan requires a 6 or a 7 — and A Level sciences and IB Diploma Higher Level routinely do — the ceiling is decisive and no amount of tuition lifts it.

The decision is made by the school during Year 10, on Year 10 evidence, for a defensible reason: a borderline candidate entered for the higher tier can score below its lowest available grade and come away with nothing, whereas the lower tier would have produced a secure 4 or 5. That is a genuine risk judgement. But it is reviewable early in Year 11 if the evidence has changed, and it is unreviewable after the final entry deadline.

So the calendar instruction is simple. Ask the school two questions in the first weeks of Year 11: which tier is my child entered for, and when is the final entry deadline. If the answer to the first is Core or Foundation and the plan needs more, a five or six session block on higher-tier material taken immediately produces a clear answer and written evidence a head of year can act on. Taken in February, the same block has nothing left to influence.

Where the tier cannot change, the honest options are to revise the post-16 plan or to enter the November series on the higher tier, potentially as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre. Both are legitimate routes. Buying thirty weekly sessions against a ceiling is not one, and we will say so before taking a booking.

sections.heading: The eight-week run-in, week by week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most Jumeirah Village Circle families actually buy, so here is what a sensible version contains rather than a vague promise of revision. The first fortnight is diagnosis and finite-rule topics: sit a full paper under timed conditions, mark it against the scheme, then secure circle theorems, transformation descriptions and histograms with unequal class widths — each a short, learnable rule set with predictable question shapes.

Weeks three and four are technique. Method lines on every multi-mark question, full-precision working with a single round at the end, and a mode check before every paper. Those three habits are worth several marks a page in a typical script and none of them requires new content. For Cambridge candidates this is also where daily non-calculator sets begin, with no device in the room.

Weeks five and six are papers at volume, particularly the multi-step problem-solving questions at the back, which only improve with practice because the skill is deciding what to do first. Each paper sat timed and marked, with the next session working on what was lost and nothing else.

Weeks seven and eight are consolidation and triage: a second attempt at a paper sat in week one to measure change, and an explicit decision about what not to revise. Telling a student which topics to abandon is one of the more valuable things a specialist does at that stage and almost never what a family expects to pay for. Sessions can shift post-Iftar during Ramadan, and there is a hard stop at study leave.
