sections.heading: Non-calculator fluency, and why it belongs at the end
paragraphs: This applies to Cambridge candidates, whose current mathematics model includes a paper taken without a calculator at both tiers. A substantial share of the available marks therefore depends on exact arithmetic: fraction work, long multiplication and division, surds, estimation and sensible checking.

Those skills decay quietly. Every piece of homework a Year 9 and Year 10 student does has a device on the desk, so the muscle is unused for two years and then required for a full paper. Students meet the consequence in a mock, can do the mathematics, cannot execute it without technology, and interpret the result as a content problem when it is a fluency problem.

The timing point is the one that gets missed. Rebuilding it in Year 10 is largely wasted, because it decays again before the papers. It belongs in the final eight to ten weeks, as short daily sets with no device present, supported by two or three sessions establishing which specific forms a student fumbles. That is a small, cheap, late block with an unusually high return.

Pearson candidates should skip it entirely. With a calculator permitted on both papers, their hours are better spent on question reading and problem-solving volume, which is where their marks actually sit. A tutor who prescribes non-calculator drilling without asking which board your child sits has told you something useful about how closely they are looking.

One practical note on the drilling itself: it has to happen with no device in the room, including the phone. A student who has a calculator within reach will use it on the question they find hardest, which is precisely the question the practice existed for.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics has the tightest calendar of all
paragraphs: If your child is taking Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 in Year 11, the calendar advice changes completely. Everything else in this subject can be repaired reasonably late, because the content was taught earlier and is being revisited. Additional Mathematics is genuinely new material — calculus, logarithms, vectors, formal function notation — delivered at pace across a single year, with no earlier version of it to fall back on.

So a student who slips in the first term does not have a revision problem; they have a teaching backlog, and backlogs in new content are expensive to clear. Twelve to fifteen sessions is a realistic figure for a student who has fallen behind, against six to nine for most main-course mathematics problems. Starting in the first term, when the slip is small, is dramatically cheaper than starting after the mocks.

The upside is that it is the best preparation available for A Level Mathematics or IB Diploma Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, because it introduces exactly the content those courses assume on day one. For a family in Jumeirah Village Circle whose child is heading that way, taking 0606 is more effective and cheaper than any bridging block bought in the following summer.

Whether a school offers it varies across the campuses this community uses, which makes it a Year 10 option-form question rather than something to discover in Year 11. Ask before the form is signed, and ask what support the school provides for it, because the pace assumes a strong Extended-tier student.

sections.heading: The November series, decided in the spring
paragraphs: Both boards run a November series, so a second attempt at IGCSE mathematics sits roughly five months after June rather than a year, and private candidate entry through an approved Dubai centre is possible. For mathematics specifically this is more useful than for most subjects, because a single paper-focused block can move a mathematics grade in a way it cannot always move an essay subject.

The arithmetic is worth doing in March. Thirty weeks of general weekly support before June, at a mid-band market rate, is in the region of AED 6,000. A focused block of eight to ten sessions after results, aimed at one tier and one paper, is roughly AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 plus the centre's entry fee. If the realistic spring view is that the grade will land a band short, the second plan is cheaper and better targeted.

Two timing cautions. The November entry deadline falls well before the examination and frequently before a family has absorbed August results, so the date needs finding in the spring term rather than in September. And entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the centre, not to a tutor, which belongs in the comparison.

The November window is also the only realistic route past a tier ceiling. A student entered for Core in June can be entered for Extended in November, which converts a fixed grade 5 into a genuine possibility. For a mathematics student whose post-16 plan needs a 6 or 7, that is the conversation to have with the school in the spring.

sections.heading: Mocks, and the fortnight after them
paragraphs: Mock examinations sit roughly a term before the June series and they are the best diagnostic the two years produce. A full marked mathematics paper shows, in twenty minutes of reading, whether the losses are method habits, rounding, calculator mode, specific topics, or multi-step question reading. Each of those has a different fix and a different session count.

The fortnight after mocks is therefore the highest-value booking window in the calendar, and it is also the busiest, because every family in Dubai has just received marked papers at the same time. Mock timetables across the schools this community uses differ by up to a fortnight, which helps a little: a Motor City family and a JVT family may not be competing for the same slot in the same week.

What to do with the paper: one session going through it with a specialist, before deciding anything else. That session should produce a named list — not a general impression — of the topics and habits at fault, and a proposed session count. Families who skip it buy a term of general support aimed at a problem nobody diagnosed.

Keep the paper, too. Re-sitting the same mock under timed conditions four to six weeks later gives a direct measure of whether the block worked, which is a far better review mechanism than a conversation about how the sessions are going. We build that re-sit into the eight-week plan for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and where a session fits
paragraphs: The UAE academic year runs in three terms from late August to early July, with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break later. For a Year 11 mathematics student those breaks are not neutral: the winter break sits between the mock period at many schools and the final run-in, and the spring break sits inside the eight to ten weeks before the June series. Four or five sessions across either one buys ground that term time cannot.

Ramadan adds a layer. School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and household energy patterns change for everybody including students who are not fasting. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, in the current period it falls close to the June run-in. Planning for it rather than being surprised by it is better practice: shorter sessions, post-Iftar timing, and whole timed papers moved to weekend mornings for that month.

On the ordinary week: most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South and are home by 3.45pm, but Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take students out between four and six. So mathematics sessions work around 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for those with one, later again for anybody commuting from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square.

Place the session after a first attempt at the problem set rather than before it. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which is what a specialist resolves quickly; scheduled earlier it becomes supervised homework at a specialist rate. Online delivery keeps the whole arrangement flexible, with no travel to renegotiate when a mock or a fixture moves.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor, and what to ask
paragraphs: Set the permit against the price of a single mathematics session and the comparison is instructive. One hour with an Extended-tier specialist costs a household more than the permit costs the tutor, because the permit costs the tutor nothing: MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and once issued stands free of charge for two years. Read that way there is no economic reason for a working maths tutor in Jumeirah Village Circle to be without one, which makes its absence a choice rather than an oversight.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category is relevant when comparing a very low rate to a specialist one: the low figure usually reflects tutor category rather than anything improper. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted.

One boundary becomes tempting in the fortnight after mocks, which is exactly when it should not be crossed. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as exact wording. Do not approach your child's own mathematics teacher privately.

Read the list of regulators the other way round, as a list of things not claimed. No approval, accreditation, licence or partnership exists between IB Gram and Cambridge, Pearson, the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. So a provider advertising an official stamp from the board for its mathematics tuition is making a claim no tutoring company in this market is in a position to support, and it is one to distrust wherever you meet it, including on a competitor's page about tier choice. There is likewise no KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is the document a Dubai tuition centre with premises would need and which is simply irrelevant to an operation holding no UAE office or centre. And no syllabus document, past paper or mark scheme is reproduced or distributed from here; tutors cite the official source and link to it.

faqs.question: When is the best time to start IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: The first two terms of Year 10, on algebraic manipulation specifically, if the aim is value. Algebra runs across both years and underpins graphs, trigonometry and problem solving, so closing that gap early prevents the same weakness costing marks for eighteen months. The second-best moment is the first weeks of Year 11, when a tier change is still possible. The most commonly bought moment is after the mocks, which is still useful but limited to technique and recallable marks rather than the ceiling.

faqs.question: My child was fine in Year 10 and is struggling now. What happened?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly nothing. Schools teach the harder algebraic manipulation, circle theorems, vectors, transformations and histograms with unequal class widths late in Year 10 or in Year 11, and the multi-step problem-solving questions that combine clusters are assessed at the end. A student who looked fine in December has usually just reached the parts of the syllabus their foundation could not carry. That is diagnosable from a marked paper and it changes the plan: foundation work rather than revision of the new topics.

faqs.question: When does the tier decision close, and can we still move it?
faqs.answer: It is made by the school during Year 10 on Year 10 evidence, reviewable early in Year 11 if somebody asks, and unreviewable after the final entry deadline. Since a Cambridge Core or Pearson Foundation entry caps the grade at 5, and A Level sciences and IB Diploma Higher Level routinely need more, this is the most consequential date in the qualification. Ask the school which tier your child is entered for and when the deadline falls, in the first weeks of Year 11 rather than later.

faqs.question: What should an eight-week maths run-in actually contain?
faqs.answer: Weeks one and two: a full timed paper, marked against the scheme, plus the finite-rule topics — circle theorems, transformation descriptions, histograms with unequal class widths. Weeks three and four: technique habits, meaning method lines on every multi-mark question, full-precision working rounded once, and a calculator mode check. Weeks five and six: volume on the multi-step problems at the back of each paper. Weeks seven and eight: a re-sit of the week-one paper to measure change, and a decision about what not to revise.

faqs.question: Why should non-calculator practice wait until the end?
faqs.answer: Because fluency rebuilt in Year 10 decays again before the papers. Every piece of homework a student does has a device on the desk, so exact arithmetic — fractions, surds, long division, estimation — is unused for two years. Rebuilding it belongs in the final eight to ten weeks as short daily sets with no device in the room, supported by two or three sessions identifying which specific forms the student fumbles. This applies to Cambridge candidates; Pearson permits a calculator on both papers.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 different on timing?
faqs.answer: Completely. Everything else in IGCSE mathematics can be repaired reasonably late because the content was taught earlier and is being revisited. 0606 is genuinely new material — calculus, logarithms, vectors, formal function notation — taught at pace in one year with nothing earlier to fall back on, so an early slip becomes a backlog rather than a revision gap. Twelve to fifteen sessions to clear a backlog, against six to nine for most main-course problems. Starting in term one is dramatically cheaper than starting after mocks.

faqs.question: When should we decide about a November resit?
faqs.answer: In the spring term, not in August. The November entry deadline falls well before the examination and often before a family has absorbed June results, so it needs finding early. The arithmetic also favours deciding early: thirty weeks of general support before June runs to around AED 6,000 at a mid-band rate, whereas a focused eight to ten session block after results, aimed at one paper and one tier, is AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 plus the centre's entry fee paid to the centre.

faqs.question: Can a November entry change the tier?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the only realistic route past a ceiling once the June entry is locked. A student entered for Core in June can be entered for Extended in November, which converts a fixed grade 5 into a genuine possibility across the full range. Private candidate entry through an approved Dubai centre makes this available even where the school does not offer it. For a mathematics student whose post-16 plan requires a 6 or 7, that conversation belongs with the school in the spring term.

faqs.question: How should we use the marked mock paper?
faqs.answer: One session going through it with a specialist, before deciding anything else, producing a named list rather than a general impression: which habits, which topics, and a proposed session count. Then keep the paper. Re-sitting the same mock under timed conditions four to six weeks into a block gives a direct measure of whether the work is landing, which is far more useful than discussing how the sessions have been going. We build that re-sit into the eight-week plan.

faqs.question: Does the winter break matter for a Year 11 maths student?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. In the UAE the academic year runs in three terms from late August to early July, and the winter break sits between the mock period at many schools and the final run-in — exactly where four or five sessions buy ground that term time cannot, because there is no homework competing for the hours. The spring break sits inside the eight to ten weeks before the June series and is more valuable still. Families rarely plan either, because holidays feel like time off.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the maths revision plan?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and household energy changes for everybody including students who are not fasting. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, in the current period it falls close to the June run-in. What works is shorter sessions, post-Iftar timing, and moving whole timed papers to weekend mornings for that month, since a paper needs ninety uninterrupted minutes. Online delivery makes the rearrangement trivial, with no travel to renegotiate on either side.

faqs.question: Which maths topics are cheapest to secure late?
faqs.answer: The finite-rule clusters, because they have short learnable rule sets and predictable question shapes. Circle theorems take one or two sessions and recur reliably for several marks. Transformation descriptions take one session, since marks are lost only to incompleteness — type, centre, factor and direction all required. Histograms with unequal class widths take a single session and are one of the best returns in the syllabus. What does not work late is algebraic manipulation, which needs time to embed.

faqs.question: What time can a maths session run for a student in the Circle?
faqs.answer: Around 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for those with one, with the later end for anybody commuting from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square. Most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel only five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South and are home by 3.45pm, but Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take students out between four and six. Weekend mornings are the right slot for whole timed papers.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting two weeks before the paper?
faqs.answer: Only for triage, and it should be sold as that. Two weeks allows timed paper practice with marking, so the student stops losing marks to process rather than knowledge, plus an explicit decision about what not to revise. Telling a student which topics to abandon is one of the more valuable things a specialist does at that point and almost never what a family expects to pay for. What two weeks cannot do is teach anything substantial, and a provider claiming otherwise is selling optimism.

intro.heading: The paper your child sits decides what revision is worth doing
paragraphs: IGCSE Mathematics is not one examination. On Cambridge 0580 a Core candidate sits Paper 1 and Paper 3; an Extended candidate sits Paper 2 and Paper 4. Those are different papers with different question styles, different durations and a different grade ceiling behind them. A family looking for an IGCSE maths tutor in Jumeirah Village Triangle who does not know which pair applies is paying somebody to revise material that may not appear and to practise a format the student will not meet.

That is a fixable problem and the fix takes one email. Ask the school's examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code and the tier of entry. For most Dubai schools the answer is Cambridge 0580 at Extended for the upper sets and Core for the rest, but Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is used widely too and some schools mix boards across subjects. With that written down, every subsequent decision becomes concrete.

The second thing worth knowing before booking anything is what the paper gives the student and what it expects them to carry. Cambridge provides a formula list for the Extended papers covering a defined set of results; everything outside that list has to be recalled. Students routinely waste revision time memorising what is printed and arrive without the formulae that are not. Pearson's provision differs again, which is one more reason the board matters. Both Extended papers also permit a calculator, and that is the quiet trap of this syllabus: the calculator becomes the method, the working disappears from the page, and the method marks that were available for the steps go with it.

Then the pattern of loss, which is remarkably consistent across Dubai cohorts. Early rounding in multi-step problems. Algebraic fractions. Graph transformations described loosely. Bearings. Answers given with no method, which forfeits marks that were available for the working alone. Percentage change in reverse. None of these are conceptual mysteries; they are habits, and habits can be changed in a defined number of sessions once named from a marked script. That is the most useful thing a parent can take from this page: ask for the habits, not the weak topics, because a habit has a known cost to change and a topic list does not.

This page covers the paper structure for both tiers, the topic-to-paper mapping, the differences between Cambridge and Pearson, where marks go and how to recover them, what tutoring costs in this market with sources attached, the examination calendar with the India-only series warning, and how to schedule around a Jumeirah Village Triangle school night. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

Papers are calculator-permitted on the Extended route, which misleads students into treating the calculator as the method rather than as a tool. There is no coursework; the grade is a weighted total across the two papers sat.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-vill.subjectsIntro: The topic areas within IGCSE Mathematics that generate the most requests from the Jumeirah Village Triangle area, with what the examination actually does with each. Ordered by where marks go rather than by syllabus sequence.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying algebraic fractions and rearranging formulae. The single largest source of lost marks on Extended papers, and almost always a fluency problem carried up from Key Stage 3 rather than a gap in teaching. Responds to short daily practice more than to long explanation.

subjects.name: Quadratics
subjects.description: Factorising, completing the square, the formula and the discriminant. Students who learned only one route struggle when the question requires another, and marks are lost by giving a decimal answer where an exact form was asked for or by discarding a valid negative root without reason.

subjects.name: Graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching, reading values from a curve, gradients of tangents and describing transformations. Descriptions must be precise: a translation needs a vector, a stretch needs a factor and a direction. Vague wording loses marks even when the picture drawn is correct.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, then on Extended the sine and cosine rules and area of a triangle. Bearings questions produce disproportionate loss because the diagram is drawn carelessly. Non-right-angled problems require the student to choose a rule, and the choice is the marked skill.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound shapes
subjects.description: Areas, volumes, surface areas, arcs and sectors, and problems combining several solids. Marks go on units, on rounding before the final step, and on forgetting that a composite volume may need a subtraction rather than an addition.

subjects.name: Percentages and reverse percentages
subjects.description: Increase, decrease, compound interest, depreciation and reverse percentage problems. Reverse percentages are the reliable trap: students divide by the wrong figure. Compound interest questions reward using a multiplier rather than repeated steps, which also avoids rounding error.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability on Extended, Venn diagrams and set notation. Marks are lost writing probabilities greater than one after adding branches, and in set questions where the notation itself is the content being tested.

subjects.name: Statistics and data representation
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal class widths and box plots. Histogram frequency density is a recurring weak point, and interpretation questions require a comparison in context rather than a bare number.

subjects.name: Vectors and matrices
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, vector geometry in a diagram, and matrix operations. Vector geometry questions, where a path has to be written as a combination of given vectors, are taught late in many schemes of work and consequently under-practised before mocks.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Calculus, trigonometric identities, logarithms and functions, taken by stronger sets. The best single preparation for A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches available at sixteen. Students who handle 0580 but struggle here are short on algebraic fluency rather than understanding.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 at paper level
paragraphs: On Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 the tier of entry decides which two papers a candidate sits. Core candidates take Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates take Paper 2 and Paper 4. In each pair the first is a shorter paper of structured short-answer questions and the second is a longer paper of multi-part structured questions, and the grade is a weighted total across the two.

The practical consequence is that past-paper practice has to match the pair. An Extended candidate working through Paper 1 past papers is practising questions pitched below the level they will sit and will arrive underprepared for the extended multi-part questions that carry most of the marks on Paper 4. A Core candidate working through Paper 4 is practising content that is not on their syllabus, which is demoralising as well as wasteful.

Formula provision is the second paper-level fact worth knowing. Cambridge supplies a formula list for the Extended papers covering a defined set of results, and everything outside it must be recalled. Students commonly spend revision time memorising what will be printed in front of them and arrive without the results that are not on the list — a mirror-image error that costs marks on both sides. Download the current list from the syllabus document and mark it up: what is given, and what therefore has to be learned. That exercise takes twenty minutes and it is one of the few revision tasks with an immediate, measurable payoff, because it converts a vague anxiety about formulae into a short finite list.

Both Extended papers permit a calculator, which creates the characteristic failure of this syllabus: the calculator becomes the method. A student who computes a chain of operations on the screen and writes only the final answer has forfeited the method marks available for the steps. Writing the intermediate values down costs fifteen seconds and recovers marks across the whole paper.

sections.heading: Which topics appear where, and what each paper wants from them
paragraphs: Topic lists are published by syllabus, but what is more useful to a student in the last two terms is a sense of how each topic typically appears. A short structured paper asks a topic cleanly: one skill, two or three marks, little context. A longer structured paper embeds the same topic in a multi-part question where part (a) sets up part (c), and a wrong answer early propagates. The revision for the two is not the same.

For algebra the short paper wants accurate manipulation at speed; the long paper wants the same manipulation inside a context, usually a problem that has to be translated into an equation first. For trigonometry the short paper wants a single application; the long paper wants the student to choose between the sine rule, the cosine rule and right-angled trigonometry, and the choice is the marked skill. For statistics the short paper wants a calculation; the long paper wants interpretation, which means a comparison expressed in the context of the data rather than a bare figure.

This is why a tutor who only sets topic worksheets produces students who improve on topic worksheets. Timed multi-part questions from the correct paper are the only practice that rehearses propagation, time allocation and the decision-making the long paper assesses. One full paper a fortnight under real conditions, marked honestly against the published scheme, is worth more than any number of exercise sheets.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: what actually differs for a maths student
paragraphs: Dubai schools use both boards and sometimes mix them across subjects, so this is a question to answer with the examinations officer rather than by assumption. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580; Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. The mathematics overlaps heavily — both are recognisable IGCSE mathematics courses covering number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics — but three things differ in ways that affect preparation.

The first is paper structure. The number of papers, their durations and how marks are distributed between them are not the same, and a student practising the wrong board is rehearsing a timing strategy that does not apply. The second is tiering. Cambridge 0580 is tiered into Core and Extended with a ceiling on Core; Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A is organised differently, with Foundation and Higher entries of its own, so the ceiling question has to be asked in the board's own terms. The third is formula provision, which differs between the two and determines what has to be memorised.

There is also a structural difference worth knowing on the Pearson side more generally: some Pearson International GCSE subjects can be entered modularly, with units sat across series rather than all at once, which Cambridge does not do in the same way. Whether that applies to your child's mathematics entry is a question for the exams officer, and it changes revision planning substantially if it does.

None of this makes one board better. It makes the identity of the board a prerequisite for sensible preparation, and it makes 'have you taught 4MA1?' a more useful question to a prospective tutor than 'are you good at maths?'

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys on a maths hour in the Triangle
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where paying for a home visit is hardest to justify, and it is worth being specific about why rather than simply asserting it. Published Dubai figures: Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. At the entry end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. All are provider-published and were read in October 2026.

So the premium is roughly AED 30-150 an hour for presence in the room. In mathematics what that presence adds is real for a younger student whose working needs correcting as it is written, and much less for a Year 11 candidate whose problem is rounding discipline, method presentation and time allocation on a multi-part question. A shared online whiteboard shows working just as well, and the recording lets the student watch their own error being corrected again a week later.

The premium also costs something besides money. A tutor travelling forty to sixty minutes each way on Al Khail Road in term traffic will usually want a two-hour minimum booking, which removes the 45-minute session from the menu. For a fluency programme that is exactly the wrong shape: fluency is built by short frequent practice, so three short sessions a fortnight beat one long one, and a travel-based model cannot offer them.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour come to roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support, with packages in this market around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. For reference, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so tutoring is the variable line in a family budget rather than the fees.

sections.heading: The habits that cost marks, and how long each takes to fix
paragraphs: Mathematics marks are lost in patterns, and the patterns are habits rather than gaps. That is good news, because a habit has a known cost to change. After reading a marked mock a tutor can usually name three habits and say roughly how many sessions each takes, which turns a vague worry into a plan with an endpoint.

The most expensive habit is answering without working. Method marks exist on both papers and are awarded for visible steps, so a student who computes a chain on a calculator and writes only the final figure forfeits marks even when the figure is right — and loses everything downstream when it is wrong. The fix is mechanical: write each intermediate value on its own line. It takes about two sessions to install and holds.

The second is rounding early. Rounding an intermediate value and then continuing produces a final answer outside the accepted tolerance, and the mark goes even though the method was sound. The rule is to carry full precision and round once, at the end, to the accuracy the question asks for. One session to teach, a fortnight of marked practice to make automatic.

After those come the topic-specific habits: dividing by the wrong base in reverse percentages, describing a transformation without a vector or a factor, drawing a bearings diagram carelessly, writing probabilities that add to more than one, and reading a histogram as frequency rather than frequency density. Each is two or three sessions. The table gives the realistic timescale for each, because a plan that does not say how long is not a plan.

sections.heading: The examination year for a Year 11 student in Dubai
paragraphs: Counting backwards is the only planning order that respects deadlines. Working forwards produces a revision timetable; working backwards from results day shows which decisions close and when. For mathematics the decisions that close are the tier of entry and the board, both set months before the papers are sat.

The published positions are these. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date anywhere, including here.

The one that catches UAE families out is the series that does not apply. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate sits June and November, and any revision plan built around a March window is built around a date that does not exist for them. Separately, Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and notes that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

Shaped around those fixed points, a sensible Year 10 to Year 11 mathematics plan runs: fluency work through Year 10, tier confirmed with evidence by the end of Year 10, full syllabus seen once by the autumn of Year 11, mocks in the winter, timed full papers from the mock onwards, and an error log maintained throughout so revision targets the student's own mistakes rather than the syllabus in general.

sections.heading: Booking a maths specialist, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier and a marked mock. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day naming the habits that are costing marks, with a realistic session count against each. You read it before anything is charged. Where the question is tier rather than grade, the diagnostic uses real Extended-standard questions so the evidence is markable.

Availability for IGCSE mathematics is the strongest in our subject list. Cambridge 0580 at both tiers and Pearson 4MA1 have deep cover for UAE evening slots, and a match normally takes one to three working days. Additional Mathematics 0606 is thinner but still routinely available. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the tutor comes from our India-based faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say which before the booking rather than after it.

Scheduling around the Triangle is straightforward. Children at Sunmarke School or Arcadia Global School inside the community can take 16:30, which suits a fluency programme well because short early sessions work better than long late ones. Families driving back from Motor City, Dubai Hills or the Dubailand schools usually want 17:30 or later. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00 and often 45 minutes. Mock weeks are generally paused, then resumed with a session reading the marked scripts.

What we will not claim, stated plainly because the market does claim it. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. We are not an examination centre and cannot enter a candidate; entries go through your school or an approved private-candidate centre. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises in Dubai and we do not hold one. We have no UAE office. Separately, the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws — no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Get the code and the tier
process.description: One email to the examinations officer returns board, syllabus code and tier of entry. For mathematics this is not administrative detail: it decides which two papers the student sits, which past papers are worth doing, what the formula list provides and what the grade ceiling is.

process.title: Send a marked mock
process.description: A marked paper is worth more than any description of the problem. It shows whether the loss is content, method presentation, rounding or time, and those need different work. If nothing recent is marked, the diagnostic session includes a short timed section at the correct tier instead.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent reading the student's errors rather than teaching a topic. The output is a list of habits, not a list of weak topics, because habits are what repeat across every paper and they are what can be changed on a known timescale.

process.title: Written diagnosis with session counts
process.description: Within a working day, a note naming each habit, what it costs and roughly how many sessions it takes to change. Answering without working takes about two sessions. Timing on the long paper takes four to six. A plan that does not say how long is not a plan.

process.title: Weekly session plus daily volume
process.description: Same tutor, same slot, 45 or 60 minutes, with short daily work set between sessions and marked at each one. For mathematics the work between sessions does most of the lifting, and the diagnosis says exactly what the daily volume should be rather than leaving it to goodwill.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the paper, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Core sits Papers 1 and 3; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4; Pearson 4MA1 has its own split again. Practice is set from the pair your child actually sits, so timing strategy and question style are rehearsed rather than approximated.

whyPoints.title: Habits named with a timescale
whyPoints.description: The diagnosis lists the habits costing marks and how many sessions each takes to change, from two for answering without working to four or six for timing on the long paper. That is a plan with an endpoint rather than an open-ended commitment.

whyPoints.title: Fluency scheduled the way fluency works
whyPoints.description: Manipulation is built by frequency, so the right shape is one specialist session plus short daily work, not several long paid hours. We will say that even though it bills less, because the alternative does not produce the result.

whyPoints.title: The formula list treated as information
whyPoints.description: Cambridge provides a defined set of results for the Extended papers and expects everything else to be recalled. We mark up the current list with the student so revision time goes on what is not printed, which is the opposite of what most students do unprompted.

whyPoints.title: Rates and dates with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is a named provider's published figure read in October 2026. Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the awarding bodies, including the fact that the February/March series is offered to India only and is not a route for a UAE candidate.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that is not held
whyPoints.description: No examination-centre status, no KHDA permit, no Cambridge or Pearson partnership, no UAE office. We explain what the regulators and boards do because parents need to know, and we name what we are not so the comparison with other providers is a fair one.

faqs.question: Which 0580 papers does my child sit, and does it change the revision?
faqs.answer: It changes it completely. On Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3 while Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4. In each pair the first is shorter structured questions and the second is longer multi-part work carrying most of the marks. An Extended candidate practising Paper 1 papers is rehearsing questions pitched below their examination; a Core candidate working on Paper 4 is revising content not on their syllabus. Ask the examinations officer for the tier and set practice from the matching pair only.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge formula list actually give an Extended candidate?
faqs.answer: A defined set of results, printed in the examination, and nothing beyond it. The mistake students make is symmetrical and expensive: they spend revision time memorising formulae that will be in front of them, and arrive without the ones that are not on the list. The useful exercise takes twenty minutes — download the current list from the syllabus document, mark up everything it provides, and treat the remainder as a learning task. Pearson's provision for 4MA1 differs, which is one more reason to confirm the board before building a revision plan.

faqs.question: The answers are correct but the 0580 mock score is low. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded for visible steps, and a calculator-permitted paper tempts students to compute a chain on screen and write only the result. If the answer is right they lose the method marks; if it is wrong they lose everything, because there is no working for an examiner to credit. The fix is mechanical: one intermediate value per line, every time. It takes about two sessions to install as a habit and it holds for the rest of the course. The second common version of this is rounding before the final step.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix early rounding in multi-step problems?
faqs.answer: One session to teach and about a fortnight of marked practice to make automatic. The rule is to carry full precision through every intermediate step and round once, at the end, to the accuracy the question specifies. Rounding partway produces a final value outside the accepted tolerance, so the mark goes even though the mathematics was sound — which is why it frustrates students who feel they knew the question. It shows up most on mensuration with composite solids and on compound interest, where a multiplier avoids the problem entirely.

faqs.question: Our JVT school has entered our daughter for Core maths. Can that still change?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot; evidence can. The school makes the entry decision on internal evidence, and entries close months before the series, so the window is finite and sits in Year 10 rather than Year 11. What helps is a short block of real Extended-standard questions, marked honestly, showing the student can handle the additional content and the pace. Two to four sessions normally settles it either way. Where the evidence does not support the move, Core is the protective choice and accepting it early beats discovering the ceiling in August.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 0580 and 4MA1 in practice?
faqs.answer: Three things that affect preparation. Paper structure differs, so the timing strategy a student rehearses is board-specific. Entry routes differ: Cambridge 0580 is Core and Extended with a ceiling on Core, while Pearson International GCSE Mathematics A uses Foundation and Higher, so the ceiling question has to be asked in the board's own terms. And formula provision differs, which decides what has to be memorised. The mathematics overlaps heavily, so a student is not disadvantaged by either board — only by practising for the wrong one.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth it for a student heading to IB maths?
faqs.answer: For a student likely to take Analysis and Approaches, usually yes. Cambridge 0606 introduces calculus, trigonometric identities and logarithms a year early, and the step into Diploma mathematics is noticeably flatter for students who have met them. The caution is load: it is an additional examination and a student already stretched by 0580 Extended is better served securing that grade. A reliable signal is fluency — students who handle 0580 comfortably but struggle with 0606 are nearly always short on algebraic manipulation rather than on concepts.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE maths tutor visit homes in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do, at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE. For mathematics specifically the online format has a structural advantage beyond the pool of tutors: fluency is built by short frequent practice, and a tutor absorbing a forty-to-sixty minute drive each way needs a two-hour minimum booking, which is exactly the wrong session shape for the work that moves an Extended grade.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 maths student from a JVT school need?
faqs.answer: For one diagnosed habit, two to three sessions. For a set of three habits, six to ten weekly sessions is the usual range, and that is what most Year 11 blocks look like. Timing on the long paper is the slowest to fix at four to six sessions, because it requires a full timed paper every fortnight rather than teaching. Moving a grade 4 to a grade 7 across a whole subject is a two-term project, not an eight-week one, and the written diagnosis says so when that is the honest answer.

faqs.question: Which topics do Dubai students most often arrive weak on?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation first, by a wide margin, and almost always as fluency carried up from Key Stage 3 rather than as a teaching gap. Then reverse percentages, where students divide by the wrong base; vector geometry, which is taught late in many schemes of work and consequently under-practised; histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density is read as frequency; and bearings, where the loss comes from a carelessly drawn diagram rather than from the trigonometry. Each of those is two or three sessions once named from a marked script.

faqs.question: Can we practise with real past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: In session, yes — we work real questions live and show exactly what the published scheme credits at each step. What we do not do is hand over copies. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright, and a tutor distributing scanned folders of marking material is creating a copyright problem rather than adding value. We link the official sources so you can download them through the legitimate route, and the student keeps the notes and working they produced themselves during the session.

faqs.question: Does my child sit IGCSE maths in March?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate does not sit it and any plan built around a March window is built on a date that does not apply to them. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. What does run in March, May and October are Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which are a different assessment entirely and are sometimes what has been half-remembered. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

faqs.question: How much should we budget monthly for one IGCSE maths subject?
faqs.answer: On Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for one weekly hour: roughly AED 240-600 at the entry level, AED 600-1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for specialist exam-year work. Published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' figures read in October 2026. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27, so tutoring is the variable line.

faqs.question: Can sessions be short and frequent rather than one long weekly hour?
faqs.answer: For a fluency programme that is usually the better shape, and the online format is what makes it possible. Three 45-minute sessions a fortnight with daily short work between them builds manipulation speed more effectively than one long weekly session, because fluency responds to frequency. A travel-based model cannot offer it: a tutor absorbing a drive across Dubai needs a two-hour minimum to make the journey worthwhile. Where the work is paper technique rather than fluency, a single longer session with a full timed paper is the right shape instead.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-vill.closingBody: IGCSE mathematics rewards precision about three things. Which papers your child sits, which decides what practice is worth doing and what the grade ceiling is. Which habits are costing marks, which a marked mock will reveal in an afternoon and which each have a known number of sessions attached. And whether the short daily work between sessions is actually happening, because manipulation is built by frequency and no amount of paid hours substitutes for it. Send the board, the code, the tier and a marked paper, and take the free diagnostic lesson before committing to a term.

Each starts from the series your child is entered for and works backwards, marking in raw marks against the published scheme so progress is measurable rather than felt.

intro.heading: Count the weeks first, then choose the tutoring
paragraphs: There is a version of IGCSE maths tutoring that starts at chapter one and works forwards, and in Karama it is sold a great deal. It makes sense in Year 10. It is close to useless with ten weeks to go, because the syllabus is not the unit of work at that point — the paper is. A student eight weeks from a June series needs a different plan from the same student eighteen months out, and the single most common mistake families here make is paying for the second plan while sitting in the first situation.

So the first thing to establish is the date. UAE candidates sit IGCSE mathematics in two series: June and November. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones — the zone decides which version of the timetable applies, and Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Your child's school will know its zone and its entries; ask for both in writing.

The second thing is the board and the tier, which parents in this belt frequently have wrong. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. Core and Foundation cap the attainable grade; Extended and Higher do not. The two boards also structure their papers differently, so revision material bought for the wrong one is wasted money. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE maths without asking which board is telling you something about how they plan.

The third thing is where the marks are currently going, which needs a paper rather than a conversation. A student at a grade 5 might be losing marks evenly across every question, or banking full marks on four questions and leaving three blank. The first student needs breadth; the second needs the three topics they avoid. Both are described as "around a 5" on a report, and the right eight-week plan for one is the wrong plan for the other.

The fourth thing is results, because what happens afterwards shapes the decision now. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. If a November resit is a live option, the gap between results and the next entry deadline is short, and knowing that in advance is worth more than any amount of revision advice. Always check the live official timetable from the board, because provisional timetables are revised.

Everything below is built around that calendar: the series counted backwards, the tier decision, the paper structures side by side, a week-by-week triage plan for a short run-in, and the published market rates. Lessons are delivered one to one, live online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-karama.programmesIntro: The Karama and Oud Metha school belt runs British, Indian and Pakistani curricula side by side, so IGCSE mathematics students here arrive from several different starting points. These are the stages that feed into it and lead out of it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Two tiers. Core covers number, algebra, coordinate geometry, mensuration, trigonometry in two dimensions, probability and statistics to a limited depth, with a capped grade ceiling. Extended adds functions, harder algebraic manipulation, three-dimensional trigonometry, vectors, transformations and more demanding probability. Both tiers are assessed by written papers with no coursework component, and the assessment pattern should be confirmed on the current syllabus document each year.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in this belt enter students for Core and move the stronger candidates to Extended during Year 10. A student sitting Core cannot reach the top grades, which matters for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency and for A Level or Diploma entry. If a tier decision is still open, it is the highest-stakes conversation to have with the school this term.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
programmes.description: Foundation and Higher tiers, each assessed by two written papers rather than three. Content overlaps heavily with Cambridge but the question style differs: Pearson papers tend towards longer multi-step problems with marks allocated across the method, and the formulae provided differ from Cambridge's. Students moving between the two boards mid-course find the mathematics familiar and the examinations unfamiliar.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so any date a tutor quotes you should be checked against the live official timetable rather than a PDF saved last year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results have historically reached students in January.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: The alternative route to sixteen in the IB continuum schools a short drive from Karama. Four criteria marked out of eight each, with extended and standard mathematics diverging in MYP 4. Students who transfer from MYP into an IGCSE cohort mid-course usually have strong investigation skills and weaker timed-paper technique, because MYP assessment is not built around a terminal examination.
programmes.countryNote: A mid-course transfer into Year 11 IGCSE from MYP 4 or 5 is survivable but needs a fast audit of the specific IGCSE topics the student has never met, particularly on the Extended or Higher tier. Transformations, vectors and the harder algebra are the usual gaps.

programmes.name: What IGCSE mathematics leads into
programmes.description: A Level mathematics or the IB Diploma. For the Diploma, Analysis and Approaches assumes strong algebraic fluency and comfort working without a calculator; Applications and Interpretation assumes data confidence and careful reporting. Schools in Dubai commonly publish their own entry guidance, often around a grade 7 at Extended or Higher for the more demanding post-16 routes.
programmes.countryNote: The decision matters for UAE university applications as well as overseas ones. Ask the receiving school or sixth form for its published entry requirement rather than relying on a general rule, because guidance varies noticeably between schools in Dubai even within the same curriculum.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-karama.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the page, but IGCSE students in this belt are usually sitting eight or nine subjects at once and the timetable is the constraint. These are the subjects our IGCSE specialists cover alongside maths.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Extended / Higher tier)
subjects.description: The full tier, including functions, harder algebraic manipulation, three-dimensional trigonometry, vectors and transformations. Marks are most often lost to method presentation in multi-step questions and to arithmetic under time pressure rather than to missing content.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Core / Foundation tier)
subjects.description: A capped-ceiling tier where the realistic objective is securing every accessible mark. The best use of tutoring here is relentless accuracy work on number, ratio, percentages and basic algebra, because that is where most of the paper's marks actually sit.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Offered by some schools as a bridge into A Level or Diploma mathematics. It introduces calculus, series and more advanced trigonometry early, and students taking it alongside 0580 need the two workloads sequenced rather than taught in parallel.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject that most rewards maths fluency. Rearranging equations, handling standard form and reading graphs are mathematics skills marked in a physics paper, which is why weak algebra costs a student marks twice over.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, titration arithmetic and percentage yield are maths questions wearing chemistry clothes. Students lose these marks to unit conversion and significant figures far more often than to misunderstanding the chemistry.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with marks concentrated in command-word precision: describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different shape of answer. Data-handling and graph questions carry the mathematical marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and data response decide the grade. A labelled diagram with a stated direction of change earns marks a long paragraph cannot, and the calculation questions reward the same arithmetic discipline a maths tutor drills.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Break-even, cash-flow forecasting and ratio work are the mathematical marks, and they are among the most reliably available on the paper. Case-study questions need application to the given business rather than a general answer.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal, logic gates and pseudocode tracing overlap directly with number work in mathematics. Students who can trace an algorithm on paper outperform those who only write code that happens to run.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response under time pressure. The transferable skill with mathematics is question triage: reading what is actually asked, allocating time by marks available, and not over-writing the cheap questions.

sections.heading: The IGCSE maths year counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Work backwards from the examination and the plan writes itself. UAE candidates sit IGCSE mathematics in June and in November. For Cambridge, the June series is the main sitting and November functions as the resit route; every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, examinations are available in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026.

Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, which is the fact that catches families out. A school makes entries in bulk, on the board's schedule, and a student who decides in April to switch tier or add a subject has usually missed the window. Results then arrive long after the papers: Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January gap is why a November resit has to be planned before the June result arrives, not after.

The practical sequence for a Karama family is short. Ask the school, in writing, which board and syllabus code the student is entered for, which tier, which series, and which Cambridge zone the centre sits in if the board is Cambridge. Ask when the school's internal entry amendment deadline falls, which is usually earlier than the board's. Then put the mock window and the school's internal deadlines on the same calendar as the series, because the mocks are the only full-length timed data anyone will have before the real thing.

Everything a tutor does should hang off that calendar. Breadth work belongs in the long stretch; technique and timed practice belong in the final two months; consolidation belongs in the last fortnight. The ordering is not a preference. A student taught a new topic eleven days before a paper has bought the least valuable hour available to them, and a student drilled on technique in Year 10 before the content is secure has bought the second least valuable.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision that caps the grade
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential decision in IGCSE mathematics and the one most often taken by default. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. The lower tier in each case covers less content and carries a ceiling on the grade attainable; the upper tier covers more and does not. A student who would comfortably reach the top of the lower tier and the middle of the upper tier is in a genuine dilemma. A student who is being entered for the lower tier because the class was split in Year 9 and nobody revisited it is not in a dilemma, they are in an administrative accident.

The reason to care beyond pride is what comes next. UAE Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A capped tier does not by itself block equivalency, but it can block entry to the post-16 mathematics course a student needs, and Dubai schools commonly publish their own minimum grades for A Level or Diploma mathematics.

The honest test is evidence rather than ambition. Give the student a full past paper from each tier under timed conditions and mark both against the published scheme. If the lower-tier paper produces near-full marks and the upper-tier paper produces a scatter of method marks with the hard questions blank, the student is close and the gap is nameable — usually the specific upper-tier topics they have never been taught. If the lower-tier paper itself produces gaps, the conversation is about accuracy, not about tier.

Where the tier is already fixed and capped, the right objective changes completely. Stretch work is wasted; accuracy work is everything. Most of a lower-tier paper's marks sit in number, ratio, percentages, basic algebra, mensuration and straightforward statistics, and a student who makes no arithmetic errors across those topics will reach the ceiling. That is a narrower job than teaching the full syllabus and it responds quickly to tutoring, which is why a short block often moves a capped-tier grade more than a year of general support.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1: the same mathematics, different papers
paragraphs: Families in this belt sometimes buy the wrong revision guide for a whole year, because the schools around Karama do not all use the same board. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is syllabus 0580. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics specification A is 4MA1. The mathematics overlaps heavily. The examinations do not feel the same, and the difference shows up precisely where marks are won.

The number of papers differs, the formulae supplied differ, and the question style differs. Pearson papers lean towards longer multi-step problems where marks are distributed across the method, which rewards a student who writes every step down even when they cannot finish. Cambridge papers include a larger number of shorter items, which rewards breadth of recall and speed. Neither is harder in the abstract; a student drilled for one and entered for the other loses marks to unfamiliarity rather than to mathematics.

The practical consequence for tutoring is that past papers must come from the right board and the right tier, and the mark scheme must come with them. A tutor who marks a Pearson script using Cambridge expectations will tell your child the wrong things about where the marks went. This sounds obvious and is a routine error in the lower end of this market, where the tutor is working from one generic set of worksheets for every student.

Students can also sit different subjects with different boards, which happens when a school changes provider mid-cohort or a student transfers in. If your child is sitting Cambridge mathematics and Pearson physics, that is normal and manageable, but every revision resource has to be checked against the syllabus code. Check the code on the entry confirmation, not on the textbook cover, because textbooks are reprinted and syllabuses are revised.

sections.heading: Eight weeks out: what each week has to achieve
paragraphs: A short run-in is a sequencing problem. There is enough time to recover a surprising number of accessible marks and not enough to rebuild two years of fluency, so every week has to have one job. The plan below is the shape our tutors use when a Karama family arrives with a June or November series eight weeks away and a mock result that disappointed everyone.

Week one is diagnosis and nothing else. A full past paper from the correct board and tier, sat under timed conditions, marked in raw marks against the published scheme, question by question. The output is not a grade. It is a list: marks lost to content not known, marks lost to method not shown, marks lost to arithmetic, marks lost to running out of time. Those four categories have four different remedies and the proportions decide the next seven weeks.

Weeks two to five are the content and technique weeks, ordered by marks available. A topic worth twelve marks across the papers that the student cannot do outranks a topic worth three that they nearly can. Each session pairs one teaching block with one timed set from a previous paper, and the timed set is marked before the next session so the student sees the movement in marks rather than hearing an opinion about it. Alongside this runs a short daily arithmetic and algebra routine, because fluency only responds to frequency.

Weeks six to eight change character. Full papers under timed conditions, one a week minimum, with the review session spent on the marks lost rather than on the paper as a whole. No new content after week six. The final fortnight is consolidation, sleep and the dull mechanical checks that reliably earn marks: reading the question twice, showing the method, carrying full precision and rounding once, and attempting every question even when the answer is not visible.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition costs around Karama, counted by the month
paragraphs: Most families here budget monthly rather than hourly, so the monthly figures are the ones worth starting from. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Monthly packages circulating in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published numbers.

Translated to the hour, the market divides into bands rather than by neighbourhood. Budget online tutoring, generally delivered by university students or high-volume platform tutors, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150: EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IGCSE, IB and A-Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home work is priced separately because the travel is inside the rate. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. A Karama family should notice what that premium is actually buying: for a short journey from Bur Dubai or Al Mankhool, it buys a drive, not better teaching. The premium is sometimes worth paying for a younger child who will not focus over video. For a Year 11 working against a fixed series date, it rarely is.

The figures that should move a decision are the ones you can check yourself. Ask what a tutor charges for an hour of marking as well as an hour of teaching, because a run-in plan needs both and some rates quietly exclude the second. Ask whether the rate changes closer to the examinations, which in this market it sometimes does. Ask which board and tier they have taught and how recently. For IB Gram's own arrangements, start with the free trial lesson and the consultation rather than a published rate card.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor in a Karama flat against one-to-one online, with a deadline running
paragraphs: Karama removes the usual objection to in-home tutoring. The schools are minutes away, the grid is walkable, and a tutor in Bur Dubai can be at a flat in Karama quickly. So the comparison here is not about traffic. With a fixed series date it comes down to three things: whether you can get the right specialist at the right hour, whether the flat has a usable hour, and what happens when a session is missed in the last fortnight.

Specialist availability is the first. Core-tier accuracy work can be taught by a large number of people. Higher-tier functions and transformations on 4MA1, taught at speed, with scripts marked against the Pearson scheme, narrows the field considerably, and the probability that one of those people lives nearby and is free at 4pm on a Wednesday in May is low. Online changes the constraint from postcode to diary, which matters most precisely when the calendar is tight.

The flat is the second. Karama apartments are busy in the evening and often shared across several people, so an in-home session needs a table and a quiet room at exactly the hour everyone else is home. An online session needs a corner, a laptop and headphones, and can run at 3:45pm when the flat is empty because the nearby schools finish early. In a run-in, when sessions may be twice a week, that difference compounds.

The third is resilience. In the final fortnight a missed session is expensive. Online sessions survive a sandstorm, a sick tutor's replacement, a family trip and a traffic failure on Sheikh Zayed Road; an in-home arrangement survives none of those cleanly. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that service exists only in India — and we would rather state it plainly here than at the point of booking. Where a child genuinely needs a person in the room, we will say so.

sections.heading: Permits, private candidates, and the things we will not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified.

A permit is a legal status, not a teaching credential, and nobody should present it as an endorsement. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring service in this market holds a board accreditation that makes its tutors official. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises in Dubai; we do not operate premises in the UAE and do not claim one. What we will tell you is which board, tier and syllabus code a tutor has taught, and when.

Some families in this belt sit IGCSE mathematics as private candidates, usually after a school change or a home-education period. That is arranged with an examination centre, not with a tutor, and entry deadlines for private candidates are often earlier and the fees separate. A tutor can prepare a student thoroughly for the papers; the entry, the centre, the zone and the identification requirements are between the family and the centre. Ask the centre in writing what the deadline is, because missing it costs a whole series.

On materials and claims the limits are firm. We will not supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because those belong to the boards; a tutor references them, teaches from them in the session and points you at the official source. We will not predict a grade. A specialist can tell you where the marks are currently going and what looks reachable from here, and that is a different statement from a promise. We will not write or complete coursework of any kind for a student.

process.title: Confirm the board, tier, series and zone
process.description: Ask the school in writing for the syllabus code, the tier, the series your child is entered for and, for Cambridge, the centre's timetable zone. Everything else in the plan depends on these four facts, and families regularly arrive with at least one of them wrong.

process.title: Sit one diagnostic paper
process.description: A full past paper from the correct board and tier, under timed conditions, marked in raw marks against the published scheme. The output is a breakdown of marks lost to content, method, arithmetic and time, which is what the plan is built from.

process.title: Free trial lesson, no card required
process.description: One full session with the matched specialist at a time that fits the school day, at no charge and with no payment details taken first. You receive a written note naming what the diagnostic showed and what each of the remaining weeks would target.

process.title: Lock the weekly shape
process.description: Session count, slot in Gulf Standard Time, what gets set between sessions and when it is marked. In a run-in we also fix the dates of the full timed papers in advance, so they happen rather than slipping.

process.title: Measure in marks, change if it is not moving
process.description: Progress is reported as raw marks on comparable papers, not as impressions. If the marks are not moving by the midpoint of the block, we change the plan or the tutor, and if a specialism is unavailable at your hour we say so rather than substituting.

whyPoints.title: Plans anchored to the real series
whyPoints.description: June or November, with entry deadlines and results dates confirmed from the board's live timetable before the plan is written. The India-only February series does not apply to UAE candidates and never appears in our planning.

whyPoints.description: Every piece of work comes back with a mark and a breakdown of where the marks went. Six weeks in, you can compare a number to a number instead of taking anyone's word for the direction of travel.
