faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths series will my child in Karama actually sit?
faqs.answer: June or November. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for international candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The February series some providers mention is offered to India only and does not apply to UAE candidates. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, and the zone determines which version of the timetable applies, so ask the school which zone its centre sits in. Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable.

faqs.question: When do November IGCSE results arrive, and is a resit realistic afterwards?
faqs.answer: Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. The gap between a result and the next entry deadline is short, which is why a resit has to be planned before the result lands rather than after. Confirm every date against the board's own live timetable, because provisional timetables are published early and then revised.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough time to move an IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: Often yes, for accessible marks, and the plan has to be built backwards from the paper. Week one is a full timed diagnostic marked in raw marks. Weeks two to five tackle content gaps in order of marks available, paired with timed sets. Weeks six to eight are full papers under timed conditions with review focused only on marks lost, and no new content after week six. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild arithmetic and algebraic fluency from scratch, so the objective is recovering marks the student can already nearly reach.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended on Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: Decide it on marked evidence, not on confidence. Give the student a full timed past paper from each tier and mark both against the published scheme. If the Core paper returns near-full marks and the Extended paper returns scattered method marks with the hard questions blank, the gap is usually a nameable set of Extended-only topics. If the Core paper itself shows gaps, the conversation is about accuracy rather than tier. Core caps the attainable grade, which can block entry to a school's post-16 mathematics course, so ask the receiving school for its published minimum.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether we revise from Cambridge or Pearson past papers?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics specification A is 4MA1. The mathematics overlaps but the number of papers, the formulae supplied and the question style differ, with Pearson leaning towards longer multi-step problems and Cambridge towards more shorter items. A script marked against the wrong board's scheme will tell your child the wrong thing about where the marks went. Check the syllabus code on the entry confirmation rather than on a textbook cover, since textbooks are reprinted and syllabuses revised.

faqs.question: Can my child sit maths with one board and science with another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens regularly in this belt when a school changes provider mid-cohort or a student transfers in. The practical consequence is administrative rather than mathematical: every revision resource, past paper and mark scheme has to be matched to the right syllabus code, and the two boards may sit their papers on different days within the same series. Ask the school for the full entry list with codes, confirm the series for each subject, and build the revision calendar from that list rather than from a single generic timetable.

faqs.question: What should the eight weeks before a June series not include?
faqs.answer: New content after about week six, for a start. A topic learned eleven days before a paper rarely survives it, and the hour spent teaching it would have earned more marks spent on method presentation or timed practice. Also avoid full-syllabus re-reading, which feels productive and produces nothing measurable, and avoid adding a second subject to the tutoring plan in the last fortnight. The final two weeks belong to consolidation, full timed papers, the mechanical checks that reliably earn marks, and enough sleep to sit a two-hour paper properly.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether the tutoring is working before the exam arrives?
faqs.answer: Compare raw marks on comparable papers, not impressions of confidence. The week-one diagnostic gives a baseline total and a breakdown of marks lost to content, method, arithmetic and timing. By week six the same student sits a full paper of equivalent difficulty, and the two totals sit side by side. Movement in the breakdown matters as much as the total: method marks appearing on questions previously left unshown is real progress even when the headline mark has barely moved. If nothing moves by the midpoint, change the plan.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published figures. Ask specifically whether marking between sessions is included in a monthly rate, because a run-in plan needs it and some rates exclude it.

faqs.question: Is paying the in-home premium sensible when the tutor lives ten minutes away?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for a Year 11 working to a fixed series date. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor, and in Karama that difference buys a short drive rather than better teaching. It also narrows the choice of tutor to those living nearby and free at your hour, which bites hardest on the specialisms you most need. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

faqs.question: My child is sitting IGCSE maths as a private candidate. Can tutoring still work?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one division of labour made explicit. A tutor prepares the student for the papers; the entry itself is arranged with an examination centre, and private-candidate deadlines are often earlier than school deadlines with fees charged separately. Ask the centre in writing for the entry deadline, the series, the papers it offers and the identification requirements, and get that confirmed before planning any revision schedule. Missing a private-candidate deadline costs a whole series, and no amount of preparation recovers it. The centre, not the tutor, owns those dates.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities accept IGCSE maths, and how many subjects are needed?
faqs.answer: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel before acting, and treat equivalency as a process the family completes, not something a tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: Does our tutor need a MoHRE permit, and can we ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. You can and should ask any tutor directly whether they hold it. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Can sessions run during Ramadan and the school holidays in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing usually has to change rather than the frequency. Shortened school days during Ramadan free up earlier afternoon slots, and some families prefer a post-Iftar session instead; both work online, since nobody is driving anywhere. Holiday periods are often the most productive weeks of a run-in because the school workload pauses while the series date does not move. What we would avoid is suspending a plan for a long holiday eight weeks before a paper, then restarting cold with five weeks left.

faqs.question: What will you not do for an IGCSE maths student, even if we ask?

We will not supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because they belong to the boards; a tutor references them, teaches from them and points you at the official source. intro.heading: The tier decision is the one that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics is tiered. On Cambridge 0580 a candidate is entered for Core or Extended; on Pearson 4MA1 for Foundation or Higher. The entry caps the grade: a Core or Foundation candidate cannot reach the top grades however well they perform on the day. Most families in this catchment do not find that out until Year 11, by which point the entry is either already made or about to be, and the window to change it is a conversation with the school's exams officer rather than a form.

That is why a search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Knowledge Park should start with a question rather than a booking. Ask the school which tier the student is entered for and on which syllabus code. If the answer is Core or Foundation and the student is aiming at A Level maths, Diploma mathematics, engineering, medicine or economics, the tier is the problem and tutoring content is downstream of it. If the answer is Extended or Higher and the grades are low, the content is the problem and the tier is fine.

The second thing to establish is the board. Schools around Al Sufouh and Al Barsha use both Cambridge and Pearson, and some use different boards in different subjects, so a student can be on Cambridge for maths and Pearson for physics at the same school. Revision guides, past papers and mark schemes are not interchangeable between them. A term spent on 4MA1 papers by a 0580 candidate is a term of real work that produces almost no marks.

Where marks are lost in this subject is consistent enough to plan around. Algebraic manipulation is the single largest drain, because it sits underneath everything else: a student who cannot handle fractions with letters in them will lose marks in trigonometry, in simultaneous equations, in rearrangement and in the long questions at the back of the paper. After that come transformations of graphs, probability trees with conditional branches, and the multi-step questions where method marks are available and never claimed because nothing was written down.

Knowledge Park itself is an education free zone off Al Sufouh Road, with university campuses and training institutes rather than homes, so the families running this search live in Al Sufouh, Media City, Barsha Heights, The Greens or the Marina towers. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor attending a UAE address is a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, which for a tiered subject with two boards and four relevant syllabus codes means the match can be made on the code rather than on the postcode.

Everything below follows from those two facts - the tier and the code. The first section works through what Core and Extended actually cap and when the decision can still be moved. The second compares the two boards by code, because the material a student practises on has to match the paper they will sit. The third is a diagnostic table of where Extended marks drain away, meant to be read against a marked script rather than in the abstract. The rest covers calculator discipline, what the in-home travel premium does and does not buy, and the step up into post-16 maths, which is the point at which a tier decision taken at fifteen finally shows what it cost or saved.

sections.heading: What Core and Extended actually cap, and when the decision can still change
paragraphs: The tier is the most consequential thing about IGCSE maths and the least discussed. On Cambridge 0580 a Core candidate sits a different pair of papers from an Extended candidate and cannot access the top grades at all. On Pearson 4MA1, Higher tier covers grades 9 to 4 and Foundation covers 5 to 1, so a Foundation candidate's best possible outcome is a 5. These are not difficulty settings; they are ceilings, applied at entry, months before the examination.

The consequence lands at 16 rather than at 15. A Level maths departments in this catchment typically want a 7 or better from the upper tier, and often prefer candidates who also took Additional Mathematics or Further Pure. Diploma Analysis and Approaches expects the same background. A student entered for Core or Foundation is usually ineligible for both, which means a decision taken in Year 9 on the strength of patchy Year 8 number work has quietly closed two post-16 doors.

The decision can still move, and the window is Year 10 into early Year 11. It moves on evidence, not on argument: a timed upper-tier paper, sat cold and marked strictly, with a topic-level breakdown of what is missing and a realistic estimate of how long that would take to close. Schools respond to that far better than they respond to a parent's confidence. If the evidence says the lower tier is right, that is worth knowing too - a secure grade at the capped tier beats a poor one at the uncapped tier on any transcript.

What should not happen is the tier being discovered in March of Year 11. By then the entry is made, the past papers the student has been practising may be the wrong ones, and the only remaining question is how high a grade is reachable inside the cap. Ask the school in Year 10 which tier is intended and on what evidence. It is a short email and it is the highest-value question in this whole subject.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1, by code
paragraphs: Parents in this catchment frequently do not know which board their child's maths department uses, and both are common around Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. The practical consequence is not difficulty but material: question style, paper structure, formula provision and tiering all differ, so a revision guide or a past-paper pack bought for the wrong board produces work without marks. It takes one email to the school office to establish the code, and that email is the first thing any tutoring plan should wait for.

The two extension qualifications are worth separating out as well. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics and Pearson 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics are standalone syllabuses taken alongside the main one, usually by students heading for A Level or Diploma maths. They bring calculus, series and trigonometric identities forward by a year, and they are frequently timetabled into an option block with fewer contact hours than the content needs. That under-teaching is the single most common reason a strong mathematician ends up with an unexpectedly weak extension grade.

Paper structure matters for practice design. Pearson 4MA1 is two papers of two hours each, 100 marks apiece, with a calculator available throughout. Cambridge 0580 has been through a syllabus revision that changed the calculator arrangements, so check which syllabus version your child's cohort is entered against before building a non-calculator practice routine - the school's exams officer or the department head will know, and the board publishes the current syllabus document openly.

One more practical point about Cambridge administration: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in rather than downloading whichever timetable a search returns first.

sections.heading: Where Extended tier marks actually drain away
paragraphs: Mark loss in IGCSE maths is patterned, and the pattern is stable enough to build a term's work around. The largest single drain is algebraic manipulation, and it is a drain rather than a topic because it sits underneath everything else. A student who cannot confidently handle fractions containing letters loses marks in rearrangement, in simultaneous equations, in trigonometry, in the quadratic questions and in every multi-step problem at the back of the paper. Repairing it lifts the whole script rather than one question.

After that the pattern is more specific. Transformations of graphs is taught in a week and tested for years, and students reliably confuse the direction of a horizontal translation. Probability with conditional branches is lost because the tree is drawn without labelling what changes on the second draw. Cumulative frequency and box plots are lost to reading the scale rather than to the statistics. Vectors and geometric proof are lost because the student does not write the argument down, only the answer.

The last category is not mathematical at all. Method marks are awarded for a correct approach even when the arithmetic fails, and students who do the middle steps mentally forfeit them. On a paper of a hundred marks, that habit alone is commonly worth five to eight marks, which at the grade boundaries is a full grade. It is the cheapest thing to fix in the entire subject and the thing most rarely taught explicitly, because it looks like advice rather than content.

The table below is the diagnostic version of all this. It is meant to be read against a marked paper rather than in the abstract: find the topics where marks were actually lost, look at why, and allocate the weeks accordingly. A plan built this way usually targets three topics rather than the whole syllabus, which is what makes it finishable.

sections.heading: Calculator discipline and the fluency that survives without one
paragraphs: Two opposite problems show up in this subject and both cost marks. The first is over-reliance: a student who has learned the course through the calculator produces a plausible wrong answer from a mode error or a mistyped bracket and writes it down, because no estimate was made first. The second is under-use: a student who grinds through arithmetic by hand on a calculator paper and runs out of time before the final questions, where several accessible marks were waiting.

The fix for the first is a routine rather than knowledge. Estimate the answer mentally to one significant figure, compute it, then compare. Any mismatch gets investigated before the answer is written. That habit takes about two weeks to install and protects every calculator question for the rest of the course. It also quietly builds the mental fluency that non-calculator work requires, so it pays twice.

The fix for the second is knowing what the device is for. Repeated percentage change, standard-form arithmetic, trigonometric evaluation and statistical functions should all go through the calculator, and a student who does them by hand is spending their time budget badly. Teaching the specific key sequences on the model the school uses - rather than on whichever model the tutor owns - is a small thing that recovers real minutes in the examination.

Underneath both is number sense, and this is where a Year 10 intervention pays off most. A student who knows the common squares, cubes, surds and fraction-to-decimal conversions by sight moves faster through every question and spots wrong answers immediately. It is unglamorous work and it is the single most reliable thing a Year 10 tutoring hour can be spent on in this catchment, where many students arrive strong on procedure and weak on quantity.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: Published rates in this market separate cleanly into online and visiting, and the gap between them is almost entirely travel. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price; Bestimate's in-home band runs AED 180 to 350 and home tutors are advertised at AED 200 to 500. Online, a qualified subject tutor is published from around AED 150 to 300 - Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 - while the budget end starts at roughly AED 33 to 52 with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik.

The clearest illustration is the monthly packaging. Advertised in-home packages in this market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions. Advertised online packages run around AED 799 a month for eight sessions. That is twice the money for half the number of contacts, and the difference is the time a tutor spends in a car. For a Year 10 student building algebra over a year, the number of contacts matters more than the length of each one, which makes the comparison unflattering.

What the premium genuinely buys is presence. A thirteen-year-old who will not engage on a screen, a student with attention difficulties, or a household where supervision during the lesson is the real need - those are cases where a person in the room is worth paying for, and saying otherwise would be dishonest. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor attending a UAE address is a service we run only in India, so the honest position is that the in-home option exists in this market and we are not it.

What the premium does not buy is expertise. The tutor who can reach Barsha Heights by 5pm is selected by geography, and geography correlates with nothing useful about teaching Extended tier transformations or Further Pure calculus. IB Gram publishes no rate card here, because a figure quoted without knowing the tier, the board and the frequency is a number rather than information. The trial lesson and consultation are free. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

sections.heading: From IGCSE maths into A Level or the Diploma without a cliff
paragraphs: The transition at 16 is where the tier decision finally shows its consequences, and it is also where a well-used summer makes a real difference. A student moving from Extended tier into A Level maths or Diploma Analysis and Approaches meets calculus as a core tool rather than a topic, meets proof as a requirement rather than an exercise, and meets algebraic manipulation at a density the IGCSE papers never demanded. Students who took Additional Mathematics or Further Pure have met most of that once already.

The students who struggle most are not the weak ones. They are the ones who got a 7 or an 8 on the main syllabus alone by being quick and accurate, and who have never had to hold a long argument together. The first term of a post-16 maths course asks for exactly that, and the drop in reported grade can be two or three bands while nothing has actually gone wrong except the kind of thinking required. Knowing that in advance makes it survivable rather than alarming.

A targeted summer block between Years 11 and 12 is the cheapest intervention available in this whole sequence. Six to eight sessions on differentiation from first principles, on algebraic fraction work at post-16 density, and on writing a proof properly, removes most of the first-term cliff. It is a far better use of money than an equivalent block in the middle of Year 12, when the course is already moving at full speed.

For Applications and Interpretation, the preparation is different and usually overlooked. That course leans on statistics, and the statistics in IGCSE maths is thin by comparison. A summer spent on data handling, correlation, and the interpretation of statistical output serves an Applications and Interpretation student far better than more algebra would. The point is to prepare for the course the student is actually taking, which requires knowing which one that is before the summer rather than in September.

sections.heading: Honest limits: what a tutor will not do, and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: IGCSE maths has no coursework, which removes the commonest academic-honesty trap in this market - there is no piece of assessed written work for anyone to produce on a student's behalf. The honesty questions here are different. The first concerns materials: we reference Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes, cite where to find them, and link to the boards. We do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads, because they are the boards' copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

The second concerns outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is selling something they cannot deliver. What can be described honestly is the shape of the work: the topics that will be targeted, how progress will be measured, and what the evidence says is realistic from the current starting point. Where a tier cap already limits the possible outcome, that gets stated at the start rather than discovered in the results envelope.

The third concerns who teaches. Abu Dhabi's ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring the same arrangement. Those are press-reported positions, so verify them against the current policy document. The underlying principle travels: paying your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to put that teacher in breach.

The fourth is about coverage. Some combinations are genuinely thin - Further Pure 4PM1 at short notice, or a specific Cambridge syllabus version - and when no specialist is free we say so rather than substituting a generalist. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is itself a reason to ask every provider the question directly before paying for anything.

sections.heading: KHDA, the timetable squeeze and why maths gets fewer hours than it needs
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The sector ran 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum schools the largest group by enrolment at 37 per cent. For a maths family the useful output of that oversight is the published inspection report, which names subject-level strengths rather than only an overall band.

The timetable itself is shaped by a federal and emirate requirement that affects maths indirectly. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time against a forty-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory subject lesson.

Those periods occupy real space. In a Year 10 timetable that also has to fit eight or nine IGCSE subjects, the squeeze usually falls on the option blocks, which is where Additional Mathematics and Further Pure sit. That is the mechanism behind a complaint parents in this catchment make often without knowing the cause: the extension maths qualification is being taught in materially fewer hours than the content requires, and the student is expected to make up the difference at home.

KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are prohibited. Schools must ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval, and for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. That last rule constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer in those subjects.

process.title: Ask the school three questions first
process.description: Which board, which syllabus code, and which tier. Those three answers determine the past papers, the revision material and the realistic ceiling, and they take one email to obtain. Any tutoring plan built before they are known is a guess dressed up as a plan.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a report grade
process.description: A marked script shows whether marks went to unknown content, unwritten method, misread questions or the clock. A report grade shows none of that. The script is what lets the first session start on the actual problem rather than on diagnosis.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a live topic
process.description: The tutor teaches whatever is currently stuck, at the correct tier and on the correct board's question style. That tells you more about whether explanations land than any credential list, and there is nothing to cancel if the pairing is wrong.

process.title: Settle the tier question before the content plan
process.description: If the tier is wrong, fixing content inside it has a low ceiling. We run the upper-tier paper, mark it strictly, and give you a written view you can take to the exams officer. If the lower tier is the right call, we say that too.

process.title: Fix a slot that fits the school day
process.description: Schools in this catchment finish between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, so 4.30pm works for students who go straight home and 7.30pm works where a parent in Media City finishes late. The slot that survives the term is worth more than the slot that looks ideal in September.

process.title: Measure by paper, every few weeks
process.description: A timed paper of the correct board and tier, marked strictly, with lost marks categorised and compared against the previous one. That is the measure that tells you whether to continue, change tutor, or stop - and it is harder than asking whether the student feels better.

whyPoints.title: The tier question comes first
whyPoints.description: Before any content plan, we establish which tier the student is entered for and whether the evidence supports it. A cap nobody checked is the most expensive thing in this subject, and it is invisible until results day.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0606, Pearson 4MA1 and Pearson 4PM1 are four different jobs with four different question styles. A tutor is matched to the code the student is entered for, not to the word maths.

whyPoints.title: Method marks taught as a habit
whyPoints.description: Writing every step is worth five to eight marks a paper for most students, which at the grade boundaries is a whole grade. It is the cheapest improvement in the subject and the one most rarely taught explicitly.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: A marked paper, lost marks categorised by cause, and three target topics rather than a whole-syllabus sweep. A plan with three topics gets finished; a plan with twenty does not.

whyPoints.title: Frequency over session length
whyPoints.description: For building algebraic fluency, more contacts beat longer ones. That is why the online packaging in this market - roughly eight sessions a month against four longer visits - matters more than the hourly comparison.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated at the start
whyPoints.description: We say when a tier cap limits the outcome, when a target is not reachable in the weeks remaining, and when no specialist is free for an extension syllabus. A disclosed limit is worth more than an optimistic plan.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is entered for Core or Extended maths?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office or the head of maths directly; it is one email. You want the syllabus code and the tier: Cambridge 0580 Core or Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Foundation or Higher. The answer matters because the tier caps the grade at entry rather than reflecting difficulty, and because past papers are tier-specific. Do this in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because Year 10 is when the decision can still be changed on evidence and Year 11 is when it is being locked in.

faqs.question: My son is on Foundation tier at a school near Al Barsha and wants to do A Level maths. Is that possible?
faqs.answer: Not usually from Foundation, because Pearson's Foundation tier covers grades 5 to 1 and A Level maths departments in this catchment typically want a 7 or better from the Higher tier, often alongside Further Pure or Additional Mathematics. The realistic options are to make the case for a tier change while there is still time, which means producing evidence rather than an argument, or to plan a post-16 route that accepts the Foundation outcome. Both are workable; discovering the problem in Year 13 is not.

faqs.question: Does it matter for revision whether the Al Sufouh school uses 0580 or 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Mostly question style, paper structure and tier naming rather than mathematics. Pearson 4MA1 is two papers of two hours and 100 marks each with a calculator permitted, tiered Foundation and Higher, with Higher covering grades 9 to 4. Cambridge 0580 runs Core and Extended tiers and has been through a syllabus revision that changed calculator arrangements, so check the version your child's cohort sits. The practical point is that past papers and revision guides are not interchangeable, so confirm the code before buying anything.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking if my daughter already finds 0580 hard?
faqs.answer: Probably not in that situation. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics brings calculus, series, logarithms and trigonometric identities forward by a year and is designed for students who are comfortable with the main syllabus rather than struggling with it. It is also frequently timetabled into an option block with fewer hours than the content needs, so the student is expected to absorb the shortfall at home. A secure strong grade on 0580 Extended alone serves a post-16 application better than two mediocre results.

faqs.question: Which single topic is most worth paying for if we can only afford a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fractions and rearrangement, almost always. It is not the topic that feels most urgent, but it sits underneath simultaneous equations, trigonometry, quadratics, rearranging formulae and every multi-step question at the back of the paper. A student who becomes fluent there picks up marks across the whole script rather than in one question. Four to six weeks of focused work on structure rather than on answers usually shows up in the next timed paper, which is why it is the best value in the subject.

faqs.question: His answers are right but the marks are not there - what is the examiner not seeing?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the working is not there. Mark schemes award method marks for a correct approach even when the arithmetic goes wrong, and on a hundred-mark paper that typically accounts for five to eight marks - a full grade at the boundaries. Students who do two or three operations mentally forfeit those marks silently. The rule worth imposing is that nothing above two operations gets done in the head. It feels slow for a fortnight and then stops feeling like anything, and the marks arrive immediately.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE maths tutor come to our villa in The Springs or The Meadows?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tutors attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring does exist in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price. The honest comparison is that the travel premium buys presence, which matters for some students, and buys nothing at all in terms of subject expertise.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths tutor cost per month around Dubai Knowledge Park?
faqs.answer: Think monthly rather than hourly. Published market figures for Dubai put weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and higher for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours. Our trial lesson and consultation are free.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 maths student actually need?
faqs.answer: One a week is enough through most of Year 11 if the student does the work between sessions; two a week is the sensible shape for the final spring term if a grade has to move. More than two rarely helps, because the binding constraint becomes independent practice rather than teaching time, and a student doing six hours of tuition a week across three subjects stops doing any homework at all. Frequency matters more than length for building fluency, so two shorter sessions beat one long one.

faqs.question: Should my child retake IGCSE maths in November if the June grade is disappointing?
faqs.answer: Decide before results arrive, by agreeing in advance what grade would be worth retaking for. November entries close well before the late-October start, and the window between results and the deadline is short. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November retake means a January result. Ask for the paper-level breakdown: a near-miss caused by one paper is a far better retake case than a uniform shortfall across both.

faqs.question: Is the February series an option for a Dubai maths candidate?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers its February/March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. If a revision schedule you have been handed counts down to a February examination, it was built for a different country. Confirm the series with your school's exams officer, and also ask which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, because the timetable differs by zone and using the wrong one is the candidate's risk.

faqs.question: My daughter got an 8 in IGCSE maths and is now struggling in Year 12. What happened?
faqs.answer: This is the most common version of the post-16 drop and nothing has gone wrong. IGCSE rewards speed and accuracy on recognisable question types; A Level and Diploma maths ask a student to hold a long argument together, use calculus as a tool rather than a topic, and manipulate algebra at a density the IGCSE papers never required. Students who were quick rather than deep feel it hardest. Six to eight targeted sessions on differentiation from first principles and on writing proofs properly usually resolves it within a term.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if the problem is timing rather than maths?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the faster things to fix. Running out of time usually comes from two habits: working question one to the end in order, so the hardest question takes the most time and the accessible marks at the back are never reached, and doing arithmetic by hand on a calculator paper. The repair is to read the whole paper first, take the accessible parts of every question, and route repeated percentage, standard-form and trigonometric work through the calculator. It needs practising under timed conditions to survive the real paper.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic requirement affect how much maths teaching my child gets?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA calculates their instructional time against a forty-minute lesson unit with a weekly total that must be met. Those periods occupy real timetable space, and in a Year 10 timetable fitting eight or nine IGCSE subjects the squeeze usually lands on the option blocks. That is why extension qualifications like Additional Mathematics often run on fewer contact hours than their content needs.

faqs.question: What if nobody is available who teaches our exact syllabus and tier?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist. Some combinations are genuinely thin: Pearson Further Pure 4PM1 at short notice, or a particular Cambridge syllabus version mid-revision. When that happens you get three straight answers - how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist could cover part of the need, and whether the school's own department is the better route for now. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, so it is worth asking every provider directly.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-knowledge-par.closingHeading: Settle the tier, then settle the tutor
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-knowledge-par.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai Knowledge Park, the most useful thing you can do this week costs nothing. Email the school and ask for the board, the syllabus code and the tier. With those three facts the plan becomes obvious: either the tier is right and the work is content and method, or the tier is the problem and the evidence has to be built while there is still time to change it. Send a marked paper with that information and a trial lesson becomes a test of the match rather than an introduction.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE Mathematics at Core and Extended tier on Cambridge 0580 and at Foundation and Higher tier on Pearson Edexcel 4MA1. Each works one-to-one over live video with LA Mer families, in evening slots set in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor in LA Mer actually costs, and what the price is paying for
paragraphs: Start with the number, because most pages in this search will not give you one. Published rates for IGCSE maths support in Dubai sit in five bands. University-student and budget online tutors advertise from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE rates from AED 150. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to AED 500. Named IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium examiner-branded tutors reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are market figures from the providers named, not an IB Gram price list.

Now the part that matters for a family living in LA Mer. The jump from AED 150 to AED 350 is often sold as a quality difference, and sometimes it is. Frequently it is a travel difference. A tutor who drives from Al Barsha to the Jumeirah coast in the 5pm hour spends an unpaid hour on Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road and prices that hour into your lesson. You are paying for Dubai traffic at the same rate you are paying for mathematics. On a weekly booking across a two-year IGCSE course, the travel component alone can exceed AED 7,000.

The second cost that families underestimate is the subject-mismatch cost. IGCSE Mathematics is two different qualifications depending on the school. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core, graded C to G, and Extended, graded A* to E, and from the 2025 syllabus the Extended tier sits two papers: Paper 2 without a calculator over two hours and Paper 4 with a calculator over two hours, each carrying 100 marks and half the grade. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, sits two papers of two hours each at Foundation or Higher tier, and a calculator is permitted in both. A tutor who has taught only one of those two structures will spend your first four paid hours learning the other one.

The third is sequencing. Families in this part of Dubai often book in January of the exam year, which leaves perhaps fourteen teaching weeks before the June series. That is enough to fix technique and topic gaps, and not enough to rebuild an algebra foundation laid in Year 8. Booking a single hour a week from the start of Year 10 costs less in total than booking three hours a week in a panic in Year 11, and produces a different result. The arithmetic of that is set out further down the page.

What IB Gram does with all of this is narrow. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. What that buys an LA Mer family is a specialist chosen for the syllabus code their child sits rather than for a postcode, and an hour of teaching rather than fifty minutes of teaching and ten minutes of a tutor finding parking off Jumeirah Beach Road.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.programmesIntro: LA Mer sits inside the Jumeirah and coast cluster, where British-curriculum schools dominate and most students meet IGCSE Mathematics in Years 10 and 11 before choosing A Level or the IB Diploma. These are the programmes the maths teaching on this page connects to.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year qualification most British-curriculum students in Dubai sit at 16. Mathematics is almost always compulsory. Cambridge 0580 tiers into Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher. Tier choice fixes the grade ceiling, so it is a decision with a price attached, and it is usually made in Year 10 on the strength of a mock paper.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. Mathematics is one of the five in practice for almost every LA Mer family, which is why a borderline maths grade is a costlier problem here than a borderline arts grade.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Several schools within a short drive of LA Mer run MYP rather than IGCSE to 16. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria rather than terminal papers, and students who transfer into an IGCSE cohort mid-course arrive strong on investigation and weak on timed non-calculator technique. That gap is specific and it is cheap to close early.
programmes.countryNote: A transfer from MYP 5 into an IGCSE Year 11 class in Dubai usually means picking up two years of Cambridge 0580 Extended past-paper convention in a single term. The cost of that catch-up is roughly ten focused hours, which at market online rates is AED 1,500 to AED 3,000, and it is far lower if the transfer is planned a term ahead.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where many IGCSE students in the Jumeirah cluster go next. The Diploma splits mathematics into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Standard and Higher Level. A strong Extended tier result at 0580 is the normal entry signal for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and a Core result closes that route off.
programmes.countryNote: Families along the LA Mer and Jumeirah 1 strip often decide between A Level and the IB Diploma in the spring of Year 11. The maths grade is the hinge: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is the harder of the two routes and several Dubai schools set an Extended grade 7 or above as the condition for entry. Spending on maths in Year 10 is partly spending on that choice staying open.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: IGCSE Mathematics is one qualification with several distinct cost centres inside it. These are the topic blocks that generate the most paid hours among families in the Jumeirah and coast cluster, with what each actually demands.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and rearrangement
subjects.description: The topic that quietly determines the whole grade. Expanding, factorising, changing the subject of a formula and simplifying algebraic fractions appear inside almost every other question. A student weak here loses marks in geometry, mechanics-style problems and statistics without the mark scheme ever mentioning algebra.

subjects.name: Quadratics: factorising, formula and completing the square
subjects.description: Extended tier expects all three methods and expects the student to choose. Completing the square is the one most often skipped in class and most often needed, because turning-point questions and sketching questions depend on it. Two taught hours here usually recovers more marks than two hours of revision cards.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.levels: Extended, with graph sketching at Core
subjects.description: Reading a graph is a Core skill; transforming one is Extended. Students lose marks by describing a transformation in words when the paper asks for notation, and by sketching without labelling intercepts or asymptotes. Both are corrigible in a single session with past-paper mark schemes open.

subjects.name: Trigonometry, including non-right-angled triangles
subjects.description: Sine rule, cosine rule and the area formula, plus bearings and three-dimensional problems. The common loss is not the rule but the diagram: students do not draw, so they pick the wrong rule. Teaching the diagram habit is faster than teaching the trigonometry again.

subjects.name: Number: ratio, proportion, percentage change and reverse percentages
subjects.description: High-frequency, low-glamour, and a reliable source of dropped marks on the non-calculator paper. Reverse percentage and compound interest questions are the two that separate a grade 6 from a grade 7, and they are pure technique rather than insight.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Surface area and volume of cylinders, cones, spheres and composite solids, plus area and volume scale factors for similar shapes. The scale-factor squared and cubed rule is the single most commonly misremembered fact on the Extended papers, and it recurs every series.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and conditional probability without replacement. Students lose marks by not writing the second-branch probability as a changed fraction, and by shading a Venn region that does not match the notation given. Both errors are visible in two minutes of marked work.

subjects.name: Statistics: cumulative frequency, histograms and averages from tables
subjects.description: Histograms with unequal class widths require frequency density, and that is the reliable trap. Cumulative frequency questions reward careful reading of the axis rather than calculation. This block is where a well-prepared Core candidate can protect a grade rather than chase one.

subjects.name: Vectors and vector geometry
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and proving collinearity or ratio along a line. Students who can compute a vector often cannot write the reasoning sentence the mark scheme wants, which is where the method marks sit. A tutor's job here is the written argument, not the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic and estimation
subjects.description: A Cambridge-specific cost. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers; Cambridge 0580 does not permit one in Paper 2. A student moving between the two syllabuses, or one who has leaned on a calculator since Year 7, needs deliberate rebuilding of standard form, surds and fraction work.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for IGCSE maths, by provider model
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai costs between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and the spread is explained by provider model rather than by subject. The table below sets out each model with the published figures and the provider that published them, read in October 2026. Nothing here is an IB Gram price list.

Read the table from the cheapest row upwards rather than from the premium row down, because that is the order in which a family's money is actually at risk. The AED 45 to AED 65 band buys a tutor who can answer a textbook question. It does not reliably buy someone who has marked a Cambridge 0580 Paper 2 against the published mark scheme and can tell you which two marks your child dropped on a reverse-percentage question. For topic-gap work in Years 7 to 9 that distinction may not matter. In the twelve weeks before the June series it is the only thing that matters.

The in-home row is the one worth looking at hardest, because it is the only row whose price contains something other than teaching. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350; independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions are commonly quoted at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799, against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. That comparison is not subtle. sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1: why the code on the paper changes the bill
paragraphs: Before paying anyone, find out which syllabus code your child's school enters them for. The answer is on the exam entry statement and the school's maths department will confirm it in a sentence. It changes which past papers are useful, which tier decision is coming, and whether non-calculator technique is a cost centre at all.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended. From the 2025 syllabus, Core candidates sit Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 3 with one, each one hour thirty minutes. Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, each two hours and 100 marks, carrying half the grade apiece. Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, so the tier decision sets a ceiling before a single paper is marked.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, works differently. There are two papers of two hours each, both with a calculator permitted, and the tiers are Foundation and Higher. A student who has spent a year drilling Cambridge non-calculator technique has spent part of that year on something 4MA1 does not test in the same way. The reverse is sharper: a 4MA1 student moved to 0580 Extended meets a two-hour non-calculator paper for the first time, which is a real and quantifiable catch-up cost.

This is the first place families in LA Mer waste money. A tutor hired on proximity and general reputation, with no question asked about the code, spends the opening sessions calibrating. At AED 250 an hour, three calibration sessions is AED 750 spent on something a single question at booking would have prevented.

sections.heading: Online against in-home in LA Mer: the same hour at two prices
paragraphs: Home tutoring is what most LA Mer parents search for, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In-home one-to-one maths tuition in Dubai is widely available, it is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, and for some families the simple fact of a person sitting at the kitchen table is worth the premium. That is a legitimate preference and this page is not going to pretend otherwise.

What the premium does not buy is a wider choice of tutor. It narrows it. A tutor who must physically reach LA Mer on a Tuesday at 5pm is drawn from the set of people who live close enough and are free at that hour, which in practice is a small set, and it is smaller again once you require someone who has taught Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 2 specifically. The usual outcome is a competent general maths tutor rather than a specialist, at the specialist price.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for LA Mer families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing for past-paper work. The practical consequence is that the pool a family chooses from is the whole pool rather than the twenty-minute radius, and that the hour billed is an hour taught.

sections.heading: The three places LA Mer families lose money on maths tuition
paragraphs: The first is the two-hour in-home block. It exists because a tutor who has driven for forty minutes needs the trip to be worth making, not because a fourteen-year-old concentrates on quadratics for 120 minutes. Attention on technical maths work degrades sharply after about fifty minutes. Two one-hour sessions on different days teach more than one two-hour session, and the market monthly packages are priced the other way round because of travel economics rather than pedagogy.

The second is paying specialist rates for homework supervision. A great deal of what is billed at AED 250 to AED 350 an hour in this cluster is a competent adult sitting beside a student while the student does the homework the school set. That has value, and it is not worth AED 300. If the requirement is supervision and momentum, the budget online band exists and is honest about what it is. Pay the specialist rate when the task is mark-scheme work: diagnosing why a method mark was lost, rebuilding non-calculator arithmetic, or converting a grade 6 into a grade 7 on the Extended papers.

The third, and the most expensive, is starting late. Fourteen weeks before the June series, a tutor can fix technique, teach exam convention and drill a list of named topics. A foundation problem in algebraic manipulation laid down in Year 8 needs a different and longer intervention, and compressing it into a term means paying for three hours a week where one would have done. A single weekly hour from the start of Year 10 is roughly seventy hours across the course; the panic route is often forty hours in one term at the same rate, with less to show.

There is a fourth that is less about money. Buying tuition in more subjects than a student can absorb produces a week with no unsupervised study in it, and unsupervised practice is where maths is actually learned. Two subjects supported properly beats five supported thinly, and it costs less.

sections.heading: Cost in context: tuition against the rest of a Dubai school bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line in a larger budget, and in Dubai that budget has been unusually stable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning two years of IGCSE support, that is a rare piece of certainty to plan against.

The scale of the market around that decision is worth knowing. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

What that means for a maths tuition budget is supply. A deep British-curriculum market means a deep pool of people who have taught Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, and it also means a deep pool of people who have taught maths generally and will quote the same rate. The scarcity is not teachers; it is teachers who have marked these specific papers against these specific mark schemes. Pricing in this market does not reliably signal that distinction, which is why asking about the syllabus code does more for your budget than comparing hourly rates.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Spending decisions make more sense when they are placed on the calendar, and this is a part of the picture no competitor page in this search sets out. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so an LA Mer family should disregard any February or March dates they see quoted. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

Dates that are publicly checkable are worth stating with their provenance. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and they give a reliable shape to the year even as specific future dates shift. Always check the live official timetable before acting on any of them, because provisional timetables are revised.

One Cambridge administrative detail deserves attention from any family in the Gulf. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone it sits in rather than downloading the first timetable a search returns.

Counting backwards, the spending shape falls out on its own. Entries are made months before the papers. Mocks sit in the winter term and are the only honest diagnostic a family gets. The last genuinely useful intervention window closes several weeks before the first paper, because the final fortnight belongs to the student's own timed practice rather than to new teaching.

sections.heading: How to verify that a tutor you pay in Dubai is permitted to teach
paragraphs: This is a question about money as much as about legality, because an unverifiable tutor is an unverifiable invoice. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broader than many families expect. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Two further points apply specifically to this cluster. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Separately, in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

The practical test for a parent is short. Ask whether the person holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Ask whether your child is enrolled at the school where that person teaches. Both answers should come back without hesitation, and neither costs you anything to obtain.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor may and may not do with your child's assessed work
paragraphs: IGCSE Mathematics is examined by terminal papers, which means the academic-honesty question looks simpler here than it does in a coursework subject. It is not absent. Students in the Jumeirah cluster frequently sit IGCSE maths alongside subjects that do carry assessed coursework, and several go on to the IB Diploma where the mathematical exploration is 20 per cent of the grade.

The boundary is the same in every case and it is worth stating plainly, because at least one operator in this search sells completed Internal Assessments. A tutor teaches, explains, sets practice, marks work and gives feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor does not write, complete or redraft an assessed piece, and no tutor on this platform will do so. A student who submits work that is not their own risks a malpractice finding, and that risk sits with the student rather than with the person who sold them the shortcut.

For maths specifically the useful version of this is narrow and concrete. A tutor can teach the technique a question needs, work through a parallel problem, mark the student's attempt against the published mark scheme and explain why a method mark was awarded or withheld. A tutor can teach a student how to structure a written vector-geometry argument. A tutor cannot sit beside a student during a timed school assessment, and should not be asked to supply solutions to a paper the school is still using.

Nor should anyone offer you downloaded syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as a package. Those materials belong to Cambridge International and to Pearson, and the correct route is the official site or the school's own licensed access. A tutor who arrives with a folder of copied mark schemes is telling you something about their standards before the first lesson begins.

One hour weekly across Years 10 and 11 is the lowest-total-cost route. Intensive blocks are available but should be bought against a diagnosed list, not as a replacement for teaching.

In the final four weeks the hours taper deliberately so the student has unsupervised timed practice, which is where the technique actually sets.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor in LA Mer cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates run from about AED 33 to AED 650 an hour. Tutopiya lists from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE rates from AED 150 for a qualified online subject tutor. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist work, and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500. Those are market figures from the named providers, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Ask for the current rate and the free trial before committing.

faqs.question: Is online maths tuition cheaper than a home tutor coming to LA Mer?
faqs.answer: Usually, and for a structural reason. The in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour includes an unpaid driving hour that the tutor prices in. Market monthly packages make the gap visible: roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. For the same outlay you are choosing between four long visits and around sixteen shorter online lessons. The second difference matters more than the money: online removes the driving radius, so the pool you choose from contains specialists rather than only whoever lives nearby and is free at five o'clock.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to our villa or apartment in LA Mer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for LA Mer families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing for past-paper work. The page is deliberately plain about this because the search term is a home-tutor term and you should know before you spend an evening on a call. What the online format buys is a tutor chosen for the syllabus code your child sits rather than for how close they live.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths syllabus does my child's school in the Jumeirah cluster use?
faqs.answer: It will be either Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, and the two are not interchangeable. The code appears on the exam entry statement, and the maths department will confirm it in one email. It matters because Cambridge 0580 includes a two-hour paper with no calculator while 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, and because the tier names differ: Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher. Establish the code before hiring anyone, or the first paid sessions go on calibration rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended in cost terms?
faqs.answer: Core is graded C to G; Extended is graded A* to E. That difference sets a ceiling, so the tier decision is the most financially significant choice in the course. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3 at one hour thirty minutes each; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4 at two hours and 100 marks each. Extended tutoring tends to cost more in total because the content is deeper and the non-calculator paper is longer, not because the hourly rate differs. A single diagnostic hour on a mock paper is the cheapest way to make the tier decision well.

faqs.question: Can one weekly hour really be enough for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: For most students who are broadly coping, yes, provided it starts early and the week leaves time for unsupervised practice. One hour weekly across Years 10 and 11 is roughly seventy hours of teaching. The alternative families often end up buying is around forty hours compressed into the final term at the same hourly rate, which costs less in total and achieves less, because a foundation gap in algebraic manipulation needs months rather than weeks. If a mock paper shows failures across several unrelated topics, two hours a week for a fixed block is the better purchase.

faqs.question: Why do tutors quote more for sessions in the Jumeirah and coast area?
faqs.answer: Because of the drive rather than the mathematics. A tutor coming from Al Barsha or Business Bay to the Jumeirah 1 shoreline in the 5pm hour crosses Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road at their worst, and that unpaid hour is priced into the lesson. Across a weekly booking over two years the travel component alone can exceed AED 7,000. Nothing in that figure buys better teaching. Online delivery removes it, which is why the published online band for a qualified subject tutor sits well below the in-home band for comparable experience.

faqs.question: My child has fourteen weeks before the June series. What should we spend on?
faqs.answer: Buy one diagnostic hour first, on a marked mock paper, and turn it into a topic list with approximate mark values attached. Then spend ten to twelve weeks teaching that list rather than the syllabus. In the final four weeks reduce the paid hours deliberately and protect timed, unsupervised practice, which is where exam technique actually sets. Fourteen weeks is enough to fix technique, exam convention and a short list of named topics. It is not enough to rebuild arithmetic laid down in Year 8, and spending as though it were is the most common way money disappears here.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit IGCSE maths exams, and what about the February series?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so disregard any February or March dates quoted at you by a tutor or a website. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. As checkable reference points: the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026. Confirm current dates against the official timetable, since provisional timetables are revised before each series.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge zone timetable should a LA Mer family be planning revision against?
faqs.answer: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. For a family in Dubai the practical step is to ask the school which zone it sits in, rather than downloading the first timetable a search returns. A tutor planning a revision schedule should be working from the school's zone timetable, not a generic one.

faqs.question: Is a cheap AED 50 an hour maths tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if you are honest about the task. The AED 33 to AED 65 band published by Tutopiya and EdFlik buys someone who can explain a textbook question and keep a student working. For homework momentum in Years 7 to 9 that is adequate and the cheaper rate is the sensible one. It does not reliably buy someone who has marked a Cambridge 0580 Paper 2 against the published mark scheme and can identify the two method marks your child lost. In the twelve weeks before a series, that specific skill is the only thing worth paying for.

faqs.question: Does my maths tuition budget need to allow for a resit?
faqs.answer: Holding a small reserve is sensible rather than pessimistic. The November series exists as a resit route for UAE candidates, and a decision taken in August about a June result needs money available in September. As a checkable shape for the year: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit means a result arriving in the following January rather than in the summer. Factor that timing into any university or sixth-form application that depends on the grade, and confirm current deadlines with the school's exams officer.

faqs.question: How do I check that a maths tutor in Dubai is legally permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for anyone to lack one. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Also ask whether your child is enrolled at the school where that person teaches, because the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. No fine amounts are published, so treat any quoted figure sceptically.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the mathematical exploration if my child moves to the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. The exploration is worth 20 per cent of the Diploma mathematics grade and it must be the student's own work. A tutor can teach the mathematics the student has chosen to use, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write, complete or redraft it, and will not do so. One operator in this search sells completed Internal Assessments; submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk that falls on the student, not on the seller.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we buy tutoring in at once?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. A week filled with paid sessions leaves no unsupervised study time, and unsupervised practice is where maths is learned rather than explained. Two subjects supported properly produces more than five supported thinly, and it costs less. If the mock results show problems in four subjects, the honest sequence is to fix the one carrying the most marks first, hold the others at school level for a term, and revisit. A tutor who encourages you to book everything at once is selling hours rather than diagnosing a problem.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.closingBody: The single most useful thing an LA Mer family can do before spending anything is find out whether the school enters their child for Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, and at which tier. That answer narrows the search faster than any price comparison. After that, take the free trial lesson, which is a taught session rather than a pitch, and ask the tutor for a topic list with mark values attached. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the rate carries no travel component and the hour you book is the hour that gets taught. No grade is promised, because no honest tutor can promise one.
