dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-living-legend.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach International GCSE mathematics to families in Living Legends and the neighbouring communities. Each profile names the board and the tier, because the content in scope differs and generic preparation wastes part of every paid hour.

intro.heading: Does the tutor know which maths specification your child is sitting?
paragraphs: There is no shortage of people in Dubai who can teach secondary mathematics. There is a shortage of people who will ask, before anything else, which board and which tier your child is entered for. That question is not pedantry. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics is 4MA1; they have different paper structures, different grading scales and different formula provision. Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended with the grade ceiling fixed at entry; Pearson tiers into Foundation and Higher. The content in scope genuinely differs.

The consequence is concrete rather than abstract. A Core-tier student working through Extended-tier material is spending hours on topics they will never be examined on, which at mid-band rates is real money for no marks. An Extended-tier student drilled on Core material arrives under-prepared for the questions that separate the top grades. And a Cambridge candidate practising Pearson-style questions meets an unfamiliar paper layout in the first ten minutes of the examination, which costs time and composure even where the mathematics is secure.

Living Legends makes the supply side of this harder. It is a single gated community of villas and apartment towers off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, between Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Remraam, with no secondary school inside the gates. Local tutor supply is small by definition, so the realistic choice is frequently between whoever is nearby and whoever actually knows the specification. When those are different people, distance is an expensive way to decide.

What makes mathematics unusual is that the specification knowledge is testable in a minute. Ask a tutor which topics sit in Extended and not in Core, or what the formula sheet provides and what it does not, or where the mark is lost when a student writes a correct answer with no working. Somebody who has taught the specification answers immediately and precisely. Somebody who has not will talk about practice and confidence, which is true of every subject and useful for none.

IB Gram matches on board, code and tier, teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and does not send anybody to a Living Legends address because home visits are a service we run only in India. The first session is a free full-length trial with no card, and it is used as a diagnostic rather than an introduction: a parent should finish it knowing which part of the paper is losing marks and roughly how many sessions closing that would take. What follows is the specification detail a parent can use to run the test themselves: paper structures, the Core and Extended content boundary, formula provision, where the marks actually go, and what the market charges.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-living-legend.programmesIntro: Four stages matter, and the mathematics in each is genuinely different work rather than the same work at increasing difficulty.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9 mathematics
programmes.description: No certificating examinations. What is being built here is the fluency that decides the tier: negative and fractional indices, fraction arithmetic, expanding and factorising, and proportional reasoning. Cambridge Checkpoint tests in March, May and October give an indication of trajectory. Weaknesses visible at this stage are the ones that cap the tier two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Students from this community attend nearby schools in Motor City, Sports City and Remraam for these years, so journeys are short and afternoon sessions are realistic. It is the stage where work is cheapest and most effective, and the stage families most often skip.

programmes.name: Year 10 on Core or Foundation tier
programmes.description: A reduced content list with a capped grade ceiling: Cambridge Core leads to grades C to G and Pearson Foundation sits below the top grades. Preparation should respect that boundary strictly, because every hour spent on Extended-only content is an hour not spent securing the marks that are actually available.
programmes.countryNote: The tier is set at entry by the school on internal evidence. If a family needs a grade above the Core ceiling for a post-16 route, the conversation has to happen before entries close, supported by evidence rather than by conviction.

programmes.name: Year 10 on Extended or Higher tier
programmes.description: The fuller content list, reaching A* on Cambridge and grade 9 on Pearson. Algebraic manipulation, functions, advanced trigonometry and the harder mensuration work all appear here and nowhere else. The step in abstraction is what separates the tiers, more than the number of topics.
programmes.countryNote: This is the tier most families in this community are aiming at, and the one where a specialist genuinely outperforms a generalist, because the questions that decide the top grades are structurally different rather than simply longer.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the series
programmes.description: Work shifts from content to paper mechanics: question triage, method-mark discipline, timing on the longer multi-step items and the phrasing habits of the board being sat. Cambridge runs June and November series in the UAE; Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November.
programmes.countryNote: Students here commute out of the community for school, so Year 11 sessions have to be placed after the real arrival time. A fixed 6pm slot that holds through the year is worth more than an earlier one that is rescheduled every fortnight.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-living-legend.subjectsIntro: Mathematics divides into topics with distinct failure modes, and which topics are in scope depends on the tier. These notes name the content boundary as well as the loss.

subjects.name: Indices, surds and standard form
subjects.levels: All tiers, surds at Extended and Higher only
subjects.description: Negative and fractional indices underpin graphs, growth problems and algebraic manipulation. Surds appear only at the higher tiers, which is one of the clearest content boundaries and a frequent source of wasted Core-tier revision.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and fractions
subjects.description: Simplifying algebraic fractions, rearranging formulae and factorising non-monic quadratics sit largely above the Core boundary. This is where Extended papers separate candidates and where losses are procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous systems
subjects.description: Linear work appears at every tier; quadratics by formula and completing the square, and simultaneous systems with a quadratic, belong to the higher tiers. Students abandon a method halfway more often than they choose the wrong one.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Function notation, inverse and composite functions, transformations and gradients of curves. A sketch without intercepts and asymptotes loses marks regardless of whether the shape is right, which makes this a checklist fix as much as a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right angles
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Core and Foundation candidates meet right-angled work only, so Extended-tier trigonometry is one of the sharpest content boundaries in the specification.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.levels: All tiers, scale factors at higher tiers
subjects.description: Arcs, sectors, surface areas and volumes. Area and volume scale factors for similar figures are reliably among the worst answered questions on the paper and among the quickest to close, often in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Probability and tree diagrams
subjects.levels: All tiers, conditional work at higher tiers
subjects.description: Students who understand the ideas still lose marks by not drawing the diagram, because the diagram carries the method marks. Conditional probability sits above the Core boundary on most specifications.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.levels: All tiers, histograms at higher tiers
subjects.description: Averages from grouped tables, cumulative frequency and box plots. Histograms with unequal class widths are a standard higher-tier trap, and frequency density is the specific thing students get wrong.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude and geometric proof with vectors. A compact topic that appears reliably and is frequently left out of revision because it feels peripheral, which makes it good value as a late block.

subjects.name: Paper technique and timing
subjects.description: Question triage, method-mark discipline and knowing when to leave a question and return. Not a topic and not revisable, only drillable on timed papers of the correct board, and the block that most often moves a grade in the final weeks.

sections.heading: Paper structure: what 0580 and 4MA1 actually ask for
paragraphs: Both boards examine International GCSE mathematics through written papers at a chosen tier, and both expect working to be shown. Beyond that the experience of sitting them differs in ways that matter on the day. Question phrasing differs. The presentation of multi-part questions differs. The amount of formula support provided differs. And the grading scales are not the same: Cambridge reports A* to G and Pearson reports 9 to 1 in most subjects.

The formula question is worth examining because it changes what a student has to memorise. Each board provides some formulae and expects others to be known, and the lists are not identical. A tutor who assumes one board's provision while preparing a candidate for the other will under-drill something the student needs in the room. The authoritative answer is the current specification document on the board's own website, which is where a specialist will send you rather than reciting a list from memory.

Tiering then determines what is in scope at all. Cambridge Core papers lead to grades C to G and Extended papers to A* to E; Pearson mathematics splits into Foundation and Higher. The tier is set at entry by the school. That makes the tier the single most important fact in a tutoring brief, because it defines both the ceiling and the content list, and no amount of later effort changes either once entries close.

Exactly one syllabus code appears across the entire competing area-page cluster researched for this project. That is how little attention this receives in the market, and it is the cheapest advantage available to a family here. The table below sets out what to establish with the school before paying for anything.

sections.heading: The Core and Extended content boundary, topic by topic
paragraphs: This is the single most useful thing a parent can understand about International GCSE mathematics, and almost nobody explains it. The tiers are not the same syllabus taught to different depths. They are different content lists with substantial overlap, and a meaningful group of topics appears at the higher tier only.

Working from the student's actual specification, the pattern is consistent. Surds, algebraic fractions, non-monic quadratic factorising, completing the square, function notation with composite and inverse functions, the sine and cosine rules, three-dimensional trigonometry, area and volume scale factors for similar figures, histograms with unequal class widths, conditional probability and vector geometry all sit substantially or entirely at the higher tier. Linear equations, basic percentages, right-angled trigonometry, averages and simple probability appear at every tier.

Two practical consequences follow. For a Core or Foundation candidate, revising higher-tier topics is pure waste, and a surprising amount of generally available revision material makes no distinction. A family paying mid-band rates for a term of such work has bought very little. For an Extended or Higher candidate, those higher-tier topics are precisely where the top grades are decided, and they are frequently under-practised because they appear later in the course and feel peripheral.

The third consequence is about the tier decision itself. If a student is on Core and needs a grade above C, the question is not whether they can work harder but whether they can master the higher-tier content list in the time available. That is an assessable question. Three to five diagnostic sessions against the boundary produces an honest answer and a written case for the school, and occasionally the honest answer is that a strong Core grade serves the student better than a weak Extended one.

sections.heading: Where the marks go, paper section by paper section
paragraphs: Mathematics losses can be mapped to parts of the paper rather than only to topics, and doing so changes how a plan is built. The early questions, the middle questions and the final long questions fail for different reasons, and a student can be losing marks in all three places for entirely unrelated causes.

Early questions are short, single-step and worth one or two marks each. Losses here are arithmetic slips, misread instructions and rounding errors, and they are almost always caused by moving too fast on material the student finds easy. The fix is not more mathematics; it is a checking habit applied to the first fifteen minutes of the paper. It is also the cheapest grade improvement available in the subject, because the marks are already within reach.

Middle questions are multi-step and worth three to five marks. This is where method communication decides the outcome: a correct answer with no visible working collects a fraction of the available credit, while a shown method ending in a slip collects most of it. Students resist this because showing work feels slow, and the only thing that changes their mind is seeing their own marked paper line by line against what the markscheme actually awarded.

The final questions are long, combine topics and carry the highest marks, and they are where timing failures bite. A student who spent too long in the middle of the paper arrives with eight minutes for twelve marks. The remedy is question triage, practised on whole papers rather than single questions: identify the accessible marks, bank them, and return to the hard parts. That requires a long session, which in this commuting community means a weekend morning.

sections.heading: Why this community has no Extended-tier maths specialist of its own
paragraphs: Mathematics is the best-supplied tutoring subject in Dubai, so the scarcity argument sounds weaker here than it does for physics or computer science. It still holds, and the reason is the tier rather than the subject.

Plenty of people can teach Core and Foundation content well. Far fewer are fluent in the Extended and Higher content list and in how the markscheme behaves on the longer questions, and fewer again are fluent in both boards. Now apply the local-demand arithmetic: a single gated community holds a limited number of households, only some have examination-year students, only some of those are on the higher tier, and only some are on a given board. The local demand for an Extended 0580 specialist in Living Legends in any one year is perhaps a household or two.

So specialists do not locate by community. They travel and price the journey, or they stay local and widen their range until the diary fills with whatever is nearby. A tutor advertising mathematics across Years 7 to 11 on both boards and both tiers is not necessarily weak; they are responding sensibly to a dispersed market. But a family needing Extended-tier technique eight weeks out from the June series is not well served by that breadth.

Removing distance changes the question into one with an answer: who has taught 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher recently, and can they take six o'clock on a Tuesday? That is the same answer inside this community as anywhere else in Dubai. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; the service exists only in India, and specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced Cambridge and Pearson teachers outside the Emirates, which a parent should know before paying rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: Calculator papers still need non-calculator skill
paragraphs: International GCSE mathematics papers generally permit a calculator, which leads students to assume that arithmetic fluency no longer matters. It matters a great deal, for three reasons that a specialist will raise without being asked.

The first is exact form. Markschemes frequently want an answer left as a fraction, a surd or in terms of pi, and a student who converts everything to decimals because the calculator offers them loses marks on correct mathematics. Recognising when exact form is wanted is a reading skill as much as a mathematical one, and it is drilled rather than explained.

The second is estimation and sanity checking. A student who mistypes a value gets a wrong answer with full confidence, because the calculator has no opinion about plausibility. A student with arithmetic instinct notices that a length of 4,000 metres in a triangle problem is wrong. That instinct is built through mental arithmetic practice, which feels old-fashioned and reliably recovers marks.

The third is speed. A student who reaches for the calculator for every step, including ones they could do mentally, loses minutes across a paper and arrives short of time at the long questions where the marks are heaviest. Reducing calculator dependence on the easy steps is a timing intervention disguised as an arithmetic one, and it fits a short weekday slot well because it needs frequency rather than length.

None of this argues for taking the calculator away. It argues for knowing when the machine helps and when it quietly costs marks, which is a judgement a student builds by being made to attempt each step mentally first and reach for the calculator only when the step genuinely needs it.

sections.heading: What a specification-matched tutor costs here
paragraphs: Mathematics sits in the competitive middle of this market, which is good for families and makes the bands worth knowing precisely. Each figure below names the provider or source that published it, which matters in a market where three of the six most visible pages publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For Years 7 to 9 fluency work that band is honest value and we say so. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150; that is the working band for Year 10 consolidation. Specialist International GCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, which is the band Extended-tier examination-year technique genuinely needs. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching 500. That is a delivery tier rather than a quality tier, and in a gated community it also loses teaching minutes at the gate on every visit. Monthly, four two-hour in-home sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions.

For budgeting, Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. One figure should be zero: the MoHRE private tutor work permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a licensing line item in any quote is charging for something that costs nothing. None of these figures is an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Materials, honesty and what we will not provide
paragraphs: Mathematics tutoring generates a constant demand for past papers, and it is worth being clear about what a provider may legitimately supply. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure in addition to the copyright question. We do not reproduce or distribute them.

What a tutor does instead is better practice anyway. Cite and link the official source so the family can access what is legitimately available. Work from material the school has issued to the student. And write equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty, which in mathematics is entirely achievable and has the advantage of being targeted at the specific gap rather than drawn from whatever a past paper happened to test. A provider advertising a download library of papers is offering an unresolved problem rather than a benefit.

The same discipline applies to grade boundaries. Boundaries move between series, and a figure restated on a tutoring page risks being wrong without anybody touching it. Ask the school what boundaries it is using for internal predictions, and treat any page quoting specific boundaries as a source to verify rather than to rely on.

Where any assessed coursework exists, the boundary is the same as in every subject. A tutor may teach, explain criteria, test an approach, read what the student wrote and show where marks are being lost, and teach referencing. A tutor must never produce the submission. One page ranking in this market sells completed assessed work, and the penalty for that falls on the student rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and honest availability
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any figure circulating is unverified. There is also a conduct rule worth knowing: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise. That reporting is press-sourced, so verify against the current ADEK document before relying on exact wording.

School regulation sits with the emirate. Dubai is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

On availability, mathematics matches faster than any other subject in this market. The limiting factor is the contested half past five to seven weekday window rather than the subject, and shifting twenty minutes or taking a weekend morning normally resolves it. The narrowest request is Extended-tier technique on a specific board at short notice before a series, and where no suitable specialist is free we give a date rather than substituting a Core-tier generalist. No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere.

faqs.question: How do I know a maths tutor really knows my child's specification?
faqs.answer: Ask two questions that cannot be bluffed. Which topics sit at Extended or Higher and not at Core or Foundation? And what does the formula sheet provide for this board? A specialist names surds, algebraic fractions, non-monic factorising, the sine and cosine rules, function notation and area and volume scale factors immediately, and will direct you to the current specification document for the formula list rather than reciting it. A generalist answers in terms of practice and confidence, which is true of every subject and useful for none.

faqs.question: What is actually different between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Question phrasing, paper layout, formula provision, the grading scale and the tier structure. Cambridge reports A* to G and tiers into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended reaching A*. Pearson reports 9 to 1 and tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher. The mathematics overlaps heavily, but a student drilled on the wrong board's past questions meets an unfamiliar paper in the first ten minutes, which costs time and composure. Ask the school's examinations officer for the code and the tier.

faqs.question: Which maths topics are out of scope on the Core tier?
faqs.answer: Working from the student's own specification, a consistent group sits at the higher tier only: surds, algebraic fractions, non-monic quadratic factorising, completing the square, function notation with composite and inverse functions, the sine and cosine rules, three-dimensional trigonometry, area and volume scale factors for similar figures, histograms with unequal class widths, conditional probability and vector geometry. A Core or Foundation candidate revising those is spending hours on marks that do not exist for them, and a surprising amount of general revision material makes no distinction.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on the easy questions?
faqs.answer: Because the opening questions are short, worth one or two marks, and feel beneath attention, so students move too fast. Arithmetic slips, misread instructions and rounding errors account for most of it. The fix is not more mathematics but a checking habit applied specifically to the first fifteen minutes of the paper, and it usually takes two or three sessions. It is the cheapest grade improvement available in the subject, because those marks are already within the student's reach and are simply being dropped.

faqs.question: Does showing working really matter if the answer is right?
faqs.answer: Substantially, on the middle and later questions. Markschemes award credit for a stated method, a correct substitution and a correct manipulation independently of the final answer, so a student who writes a bare answer collects a fraction of what the question offers, while one whose method is visible and whose arithmetic slips collects most of it. Students resist this because it feels slow. The only thing that reliably changes their mind is seeing their own marked paper reviewed line by line against what the markscheme actually credited.

faqs.question: Is arithmetic fluency still needed in a calculator paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, for three reasons a specialist will raise unprompted. Markschemes often want an answer left as a fraction, a surd or in terms of pi, and converting everything to decimals loses marks on correct work. A student with no estimation instinct accepts an implausible answer after a mistyped entry, because the calculator has no opinion about plausibility. And reaching for the calculator on steps that could be done mentally costs minutes across a paper, leaving too little time for the long questions where the marks are heaviest.

faqs.question: Can the tier still be changed for my child?
faqs.answer: Only before entries close, and the question is assessable rather than a matter of persuasion. A Cambridge Core entry leads to grades C to G; Extended reaches A* to E. If a higher grade is needed, what matters is whether the higher-tier content list can be mastered in the time available. Three to five diagnostic sessions against the boundary produces an honest answer and a written case for the school. Sometimes the answer is that a strong Core grade serves the student better than a weak Extended one.

faqs.question: Which maths topics give the quickest improvement?
faqs.answer: Three stand out at the higher tiers. Area and volume scale factors for similar figures, reliably among the worst answered questions and often closed in two or three sessions. Histograms with unequal class widths, a standard trap with a standard remedy. And vector geometry, a compact topic that appears dependably and is frequently left out of revision because it feels peripheral. Across all tiers, the fastest change of all is method presentation, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap and shifts within three or four sessions.

faqs.question: How soon should a Living Legends family expect the grade to shift?
faqs.answer: Method usually changes before grades do, which is the honest sequencing. Habit-level failures such as unshown working or careless opening questions shift within three or four sessions and are visible immediately in marked work. Self-contained higher-tier topic blocks take six to eight. A foundational gap in indices or algebraic fractions carried from Year 8 is a term or more, because it touches every later topic. Anyone quoting a timeline before seeing a marked paper is guessing rather than estimating.

faqs.question: Is there an Extended-tier maths specialist based near Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Possibly in Motor City, which has the closest genuine tutor market, but the local arithmetic is against it. A single gated community holds a limited number of households, only some have examination-year students, only some are on the higher tier, and only some are on a given board. That cannot sustain a specialist locally. Visiting specialists price the journey and lose minutes at the gate; local generalists widen their range. Matching on board and tier without a distance filter is what actually widens the choice.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring cost from this community?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is honest value for Years 7 to 9. Qualified online subject tutors are AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Specialist provision is AED 200 to 450 and upward, TutorChase at AED 270, which is the band Extended-tier examination-year technique needs. In-home visits are AED 180 to 500 including travel.

faqs.question: Will you send us Cambridge or Pearson past papers?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables are Cambridge and Pearson copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites and links the official source, works from material the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and difficulty, which has the advantage of targeting the specific gap rather than whatever a past paper happened to test. A download library is an unresolved copyright problem a family using it would be sharing.

faqs.question: Which series will my child sit, and does it change the plan?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series in the UAE, and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE page quoting a spring window is giving you a date you cannot use. Checkable anchors: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge centres also sit in one of six timetable zones.

faqs.question: Does my child's maths tutor need a UAE permit to teach online?
faqs.answer: The permit requirement attaches to private tuition rather than to a format. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no amounts are published, so any quoted figure is unverified.

Book a free full-length trial lesson with somebody who teaches that exact specification, send a marked paper first, and buy a defined block rather than an open-ended arrangement.

intro.heading: Start at the cheapest rung and work up only when you have a reason
paragraphs: The usual order in this market is backwards. A tutoring site opens with its most expensive offering, explains why quality matters, and leaves the parent to work out whether their child needs any of it. For an IGCSE maths problem, which is often narrow and fixable, that order wastes money. So this page runs the other way: cheapest first, each rung described honestly, and a stopping rule for each one.

The bottom of the Dubai market is cheaper than most parents expect. Advertised rates start around AED 33 to 52 an hour on one platform and AED 45 to 65 on another, which puts an hour of tutoring below the price of a family takeaway. At that level you are buying a university student or a recent graduate who will explain a question the child is stuck on, correctly. For a Year 10 student who has missed a fortnight of lessons to illness and needs to catch up on quadratics, that is often sufficient and nothing more is required.

The rung above sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, which is where most serious IGCSE maths work happens in this city. Above that, IGCSE and IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and in-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because the figure includes travel. Those are market figures from other providers, read in October 2026, each attributed in the ladder table below. They are not IB Gram's price list; our pricing follows a free trial lesson and depends on how many sessions the student actually needs.

What determines the right rung is not the family's budget but the shape of the problem. A content gap is cheap to fix. A tier misplacement is expensive and urgent. A student losing marks through method and presentation rather than through understanding needs someone who can read a mark scheme, which the bottom rung generally cannot. The sections below give you the ladder, the tier decision, the Cambridge and Edexcel comparison, and five checks you can run on any tutor in a single trial lesson.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-meydan.programmesIntro: IGCSE maths in Meydan is taught under more than one specification and in more than one school structure. These are the three contexts that change what the first lesson should contain and, because this page is about cost, what the sensible spend looks like in each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Two years, two tiers and two papers. Core and Extended are separate entries with different grade ranges, and under the syllabus in use from 2025 each tier has one paper where a calculator is not permitted and one where it is. Each paper carries half the grade, so there is no coursework component to absorb a weak performance. Tiering is decided by the school, usually in Year 10, on the basis of class performance.
programmes.countryNote: Across the central corridor, Cambridge is the commonest IGCSE route and many Meydan students sit it at a school a short drive away rather than in the community itself. Because the tier decision is made in school, a Meydan parent's first useful question to a tutor is not about topics but about whether the tier looks right, which can be assessed from one marked paper.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The other main route in Dubai, and structurally different in a way that matters. Specification A has Foundation and Higher tiers, two papers of two hours each at 50% apiece, and a calculator is permitted in both. A student who has drilled non-calculator arithmetic for a Cambridge paper is preparing for something their specification does not test, and the reverse is worse: a Cambridge student who has never practised without a calculator is in trouble.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year, so a Meydan student has a genuine resit route within the same academic year. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why every date on this page points to the official timetable rather than restating something that can be revised.

programmes.name: What follows IGCSE maths
programmes.description: The IGCSE maths grade is a gate, not an end. A student heading for IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or for A Level Mathematics, needs more than a pass; they need algebraic fluency that an Extended or Higher tier grade of 6 does not guarantee. Spending a short block in Year 11 on algebra specifically, rather than on examination technique generally, is the cheapest preparation for post-16 maths available.
programmes.countryNote: In Meydan and Nad Al Sheba several schools offer both the IB Diploma and A Levels after IGCSE, which makes the Year 11 maths grade a decision point rather than a formality. Families who plan for the post-16 course while still in Year 11 tend to buy less tutoring in Year 12 than those who treat the IGCSE as a finish line.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-meydan.igcseSubjectsIntro: The Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel subjects most often booked alongside maths by Meydan families, with the specification detail that changes how a session is spent.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The page subject. Marks go missing in algebraic manipulation, in multi-step problem questions where the first line is never written down, and in the geometry and trigonometry questions where students stop before the final required statement.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Extended students in some corridor schools as a bridge to A Level or IB Higher Level maths. It is a genuine step up in abstraction, and students who find it hard usually have an Extended-level gap rather than an Additional Mathematics one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Where weak maths is most visible. Equation rearrangement, standard form and unit conversion cost marks in Physics that have nothing to do with physics understanding, so one maths block often lifts two grades.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and percentage yield are arithmetic problems in chemical clothing. A student who is slow with ratio and proportion will be slow in every chemistry calculation, and slowness costs marks even when the method is right.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Lighter on calculation but heavy on data interpretation, graphs and magnification sums. Students who dislike maths often choose Biology to avoid it and then meet it in the practical and data questions anyway.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Break-even, ratios and cash-flow forecasts are the quantitative core. A student weak in percentages loses these marks reliably, and the fix sits in the maths session rather than the business one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Requires confident work with percentage change, index numbers and graph reading. The analysis marks are verbal, which means a numerically weak student can still do well if the arithmetic is secured first.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal and logic are the maths-adjacent parts, and they are learnable in a handful of sessions. Algorithmic reasoning overlaps with the problem-solving habits that Extended maths rewards.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Included because written explanation affects maths marks in problem questions, where a method has to be communicated. A student who writes clearly loses fewer method marks than one who writes nothing.

subjects.name: ICT
subjects.description: Spreadsheet modelling is formally assessed and overlaps with the arithmetic and formula work in maths. Students comfortable in one are usually quick in the other, which makes it an efficient subject to pair.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
igcseSubjects.description: Under the syllabus in use from 2025 each tier pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper, both at 50%. Core and Extended have different grade ranges, so the tier a school enters a student for sets a ceiling as well as a floor.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers of two hours, 50% each, with a calculator permitted throughout. Higher tier reaches the top grades; Foundation tier does not. Confirm which specification and tier the school has entered your child for before buying any tutoring.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 and 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge and Pearson differ in paper structure and in how practical skills are assessed. A tutor who does not ask which board is being sat is preparing the student for the wrong paper.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 and 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Calculation-heavy at the top tier and heavily dependent on the maths this page is about. Organic chemistry and moles are where Extended and Higher tier students most often need targeted sessions.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 and 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Terminology precision matters more than calculation, but the data and graph questions carry real marks. Command-term practice transfers directly from maths problem-solving work.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455 and 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Diagram accuracy and percentage work are the two mark-losing areas. A student secure in maths usually needs fewer economics sessions than their grade suggests.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the tier decision and what it costs
paragraphs: The tier your child is entered for sets the grade ceiling, and it is the most consequential cost decision on this page because getting it wrong is expensive in both directions. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics runs Core and Extended as separate entries with different grade ranges. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A runs Foundation and Higher on the same principle. In both cases the lower tier cannot reach the top grades and the higher tier can produce a low grade or none at all if the student is out of their depth.

Schools make this decision, usually in Year 10, from class performance. They get it right most of the time and the cases where they do not are predictable. A student placed in the lower tier because of a weak Year 9, who has since improved, may be capped unnecessarily. A student pushed into the higher tier on the strength of good effort rather than good algebra may spend two years failing to access half the paper. Both situations are visible in one marked paper to anyone who knows what to look for.

This is why a tier review is the single best use of a first tutoring session for a Year 10 student in Meydan. It costs one lesson, which at the trial stage costs nothing, and it either confirms the school's judgement or gives you a specific, evidenced conversation to have with the maths department. The table sets out what each tier actually implies so you can read your child's own paper against it. Entry decisions and deadlines belong to the school, so any change has to go through them and the earlier it is raised the more possible it is.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1: why the board changes the lessons
paragraphs: A tutor who does not ask which board your child sits is not ready to teach them, and a Meydan parent can use that as a filter in the first two minutes of a conversation. The two main IGCSE maths specifications in Dubai differ in ways that change what a session should contain, and the biggest of those differences is the calculator.

Under the Cambridge syllabus in use from 2025, each tier of 0580 pairs a paper where a calculator is not permitted with one where it is. That makes mental and written arithmetic examinable in its own right, and it means a student who has done all their practice with a calculator in hand will meet a paper they have never rehearsed. Pearson Edexcel's Specification A, 4MA1, permits a calculator in both papers, so the same preparation that is essential for one specification is close to irrelevant for the other.

There are smaller differences too. The examination series differ slightly: Cambridge runs June and November for IGCSE, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Paper durations differ. Formula provision differs. None of these is complicated and all of them matter in the final eight weeks, which is exactly when a mismatched tutor is least affordable. Ask the school which specification code they enter, write it down, and give it to the tutor before the first session.

One caution on both boards: specifications are revised. Treat the detail on this page as a reason to check rather than as a substitute for checking, and confirm the current structure with the school or on the board's own site before planning a revision programme around it.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE IGCSE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series that circulates in some online revision guides is offered to India only, and planning a Dubai student's year around it is a straightforward error that costs real money in misplaced intensity. If you see those months in a revision plan sold to you, that is a reason to doubt the rest of it.

Working backwards from a series is more useful than working forwards from today, because the deadlines that bite are set months ahead. Entry deadlines sit well before the examination window. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results follow in January: the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the summer series, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are past dates, cited so you can check the pattern rather than so you can act on them.

For a future series, the right move is to open the board's live timetable rather than trust any restatement of it, including this one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That zone point alone is worth more than most revision advice, and almost nobody tells parents about it.

sections.heading: Five checks to run on any maths tutor before you pay
paragraphs: Since this page is about not wasting money, here is the part that saves the most of it. These five checks take a single trial lesson and a short conversation afterwards, and they separate a tutor who will move a grade from one who will keep a student company while they do homework. None of them requires you to understand IGCSE maths yourself.

First, ask which specification and tier your child is entered for, before you tell them. A tutor who does not ask is not ready. Second, after the trial lesson, ask what is costing your child marks and listen for specificity. 'They need to practise more' is a budget answer; 'they lose method marks because they stop writing once they can see the answer' is a specialist one. Third, ask what they will set between sessions and how it will be marked, because unmarked practice is the commonest reason a weekly arrangement produces nothing.

Fourth, ask how many sessions they think this will take and what the end point looks like. A tutor who cannot describe an end point is describing a subscription. Fifth, ask what they will not do: a tutor who will happily complete coursework or supply answers is telling you something about their standards that will show up elsewhere. Run those five checks and you will reject most of the market in twenty minutes, which is the cheapest filtering you will ever do. None of them is rude, and a good tutor will be pleased to be asked, because the questions are the ones they would ask on your behalf.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Students describe maths difficulty in general terms. Mark schemes are specific, and in IGCSE maths the losses concentrate in a small number of places that are almost all procedural. Knowing them lets you judge whether a tutor's diagnosis is real, and it is why the ladder in this page's first table pays off: the higher rungs are worth it precisely because they can name these.

Algebraic manipulation is first and largest. A student who hesitates expanding brackets or solving a linear equation will be slow everywhere, and in a paper with a fixed time limit slowness is indistinguishable from not knowing. Second is the multi-step problem question where no working appears. Method marks are awarded for the working, so a student who does the thinking in their head and writes only an answer loses most of the available marks even when the answer is right.

Third is the family of topics students quietly skip: bearings, similar shapes, cumulative frequency, compound measures. These appear reliably on papers and are often absent from revision because nobody likes them. Fourth is the final statement. Geometry and trigonometry questions frequently require a reason or a conclusion, and a student who stops at the number loses the last mark on question after question. Fifth, on boards that test it, arithmetic without a calculator, which is now examinable in its own right under Cambridge's current structure and is the single most common gap in a Dubai student's preparation.

sections.heading: KHDA, the corridor schools, and what an IGCSE grade has to do for MoE equivalency
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. It inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the outcome school by school. For a Meydan family comparing schools, the secondary mathematics commentary inside those reports is worth more than the headline band, because a strong maths department can sit inside a school rated Good.

Scale and cost context: Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen curricula, and KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the fee line flat, tutoring spend is more visible in the household budget than usual, which is a good reason to judge it on results.

Then there is the use the IGCSE grade is eventually put to. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor ranking for these queries publishes a requirement of six subjects, which is wrong. Verify your own case with the ministry's attestation channel rather than with any tutoring site, including this one; equivalency is a process the ministry performs and that no tutoring service can perform or guarantee.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or licensed by any UAE education authority and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any service advertising KHDA-approved tutors is describing something else or saying something untrue, and for a parent comparing quotes that is a useful early filter.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, past papers and what we will not supply at any price
paragraphs: Some things in this market are available for money and should not be. Completed coursework is the clearest case: at least one operator ranking for UAE curriculum queries sells finished assessed work outright. IGCSE maths has no coursework component, which removes the temptation at this level, but the same operators sell it for other subjects and the same students are their customers. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the website that took the payment.

The second thing we will not supply is examination material. We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and we do not host them for download. We reference them and link to the board's own page, which is both the lawful position and the more useful one, because the official version is the current version and a stale PDF circulating in a parents' group is how a student ends up revising a withdrawn topic.

What a tutor does supply is teaching, practice selected from legitimately accessible material, marking against the published criteria, and an honest account of where the student stands. That last one is worth paying for and is the thing most often missing at the cheaper rungs of the ladder, not because budget tutors are dishonest but because reading a student's work against a mark scheme is a skill that takes years to acquire. If a tutor at any price tells you only that things are going well, you are not getting it.

sections.heading: Starting from Meydan, cheaply, and what we do when nobody is free
paragraphs: Begin by naming the problem rather than booking a block. Tell us the specification code and tier from the school, the mock grade, and the topics your child says they cannot do. If you can name a topic, say so, because that usually means a short block and the cheapest rung that works. If you cannot, the trial lesson will produce the diagnosis and you can decide afterwards with something concrete in front of you.

The trial lesson is free and it is a diagnosis, not a sales call. Run the five checks from earlier in this page on whoever takes it. The tutor should finish able to tell you which of the loss patterns applies to your child, and you should finish knowing whether your child will work with this person without resistance. If not, say so and we propose someone else. A match a teenager tolerates rather than respects does not survive a term.

Finally, the part this market usually leaves out. Availability is not unlimited. IGCSE maths is better covered than Diploma Chemistry or Higher Level Paper 3 work, but specific slots fill, particularly the early-evening Gulf Standard Time ones that Meydan families want after the school run. When the tutor we recommend is not free at your time, we say so and offer a different slot, a short wait, or a different tutor with the same specification experience. We will not put someone who has never taught your child's board in front of them to fill a diary, and we will not charge a specialist rate for a session that is really homework supervision.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to get IGCSE maths help in Meydan that actually works?
faqs.answer: A group class at a tuition centre is cheapest per head, and it works when several students share the same named gap. After that, a short block of three to five online sessions with a budget tutor, advertised in this market from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, is genuinely sufficient for a single topic a student has missed. The cheap options fail when the problem is general, when the tier looks wrong, or when marks are being lost on method rather than understanding. Name the gap first; the answer follows from that rather than from the budget.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay an IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai per hour?
faqs.answer: The published market, read in October 2026, runs as follows. Budget online tutors advertise from about AED 33 to 65 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to 300. IGCSE and IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 500 because the figure includes travel. Premium or examiner-linked tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and beyond, which is rarely necessary at IGCSE. Those are other providers' figures, attributed in the ladder table on this page, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE maths tier change what tutoring they need?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Cambridge Core and Pearson Edexcel Foundation cap the available grades and their typical failure mode is careless arithmetic, which responds to short topic blocks. Cambridge Extended and Edexcel Higher reach the top grades and their typical failure mode is being unable to access the harder half of the paper at all, which needs sustained algebra work across a term before any examination technique is worth teaching. A student in the wrong tier is not a tutoring problem at all; that is a conversation with the maths department, and it needs to happen early.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths board does my child's school use, and why does it matter for cost?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the specification code in writing: Cambridge 0580, or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 or 4MB1. It matters because the preparation differs. Under the Cambridge syllabus in use from 2025, each tier pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator paper, so mental and written arithmetic is examinable. Pearson Edexcel Specification A permits a calculator in both papers. A tutor preparing a student for the wrong structure wastes every hour you pay for, and in the final eight weeks that is the most expensive mistake available.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE maths exams run for students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The February and March series that appears in some online revision guides is offered to India only, so it should not appear in a Dubai student's plan. For actual dates, open the board's live timetable rather than any restatement of it: Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them, and Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the centre's own risk.

faqs.question: Is a group class a false economy for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Not always, and treating it as one costs families money. A group class works when the gap is a single topic shared by the group and the pace suits your child, which is plausible for something like trigonometry or probability. It works badly when the loss is personal, such as a habit of not writing working, because that will not be noticed in a room of six. The test is whether you can name the gap. If you can, a group class on that topic is often the most efficient purchase on this page's ladder.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 10 maths gap usually take to close?
faqs.answer: Three to five for a single named topic, in most cases, which is why we sell short blocks rather than upgrading every enquiry to a weekly arrangement. A general drift from a 6 to a 5 is different and usually needs a term of weekly work, because the underlying issue is algebraic fluency and fluency is built by frequency rather than by intensity. A Year 11 student eight weeks from a series needs a different plan again, with some topics deliberately abandoned. Ask any tutor what finished looks like before you buy.

faqs.question: What should I ask a maths tutor before paying for a block?
faqs.answer: Five things. Which specification code and tier is my child entered for, asked before you tell them. After the trial lesson, what specifically is costing marks, and judge how precise the answer is. What practice will be set, and how will it be marked. How many sessions will this take and what does finished look like. And what will you refuse to do with assessed work. A tutor who cannot describe an end point is describing a subscription, and a tutor who will complete coursework is telling you about their standards.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their answers are right?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the working is not written down. Method marks are awarded for the steps, so a student who does the arithmetic mentally and writes a single number forfeits most of the marks on a multi-step question even when the number is correct. The second common cause is a missing final statement: geometry and trigonometry questions often require a reason or conclusion, and stopping at the number costs the last mark repeatedly. Both are habits rather than knowledge gaps, which means they are cheap and fast to fix with marked practice.

faqs.question: Is an in-home maths tutor in Meydan worth the extra cost?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic is worth seeing before you decide. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure includes travel, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. At the same price you are often choosing between a specialist from the whole market and whoever is willing to drive to Meydan at four in the afternoon. The premium buys logistics and a person in the room, which matters for some younger students and rarely for examination technique. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all.

faqs.question: Does the IGCSE maths grade itself count towards UAE equivalency, and how many subjects are needed?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that, equivalency requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is incorrect. Verify your own case through the ministry's attestation channel, because equivalency is a process the ministry performs and no tutoring service can perform or guarantee it.

faqs.question: Do I need to check whether a Dubai maths tutor is licensed?
faqs.answer: It is a fair question to ask and a permitted tutor will not mind it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications run through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during Ramadan or school holidays to save money?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families it is sensible rather than disruptive. Because lessons are online there is no journey to renegotiate, so a session can shift to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan or pause entirely for a holiday and resume with the same tutor. The one caution is timing relative to a series: pausing in the eight weeks before a June examination costs more than the saving. Agree the pause in advance so the slot is held, and agree which time zone the session is pinned to if the family is travelling.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with six weeks to go. What is the honest minimum spend?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is enough to move a grade if the sessions are used correctly, and the honest minimum is higher per week than a normal arrangement because the work is compressed. Expect two or three sessions a week for the period, with the first spent marking the mock question by question and the plan that follows dropping some topics deliberately. That drop is uncomfortable and it is the correct use of a short window. Nobody can promise a grade, and a tutor who does at this stage is selling something other than teaching.

faqs.question: Can we save money by getting the tutor to send us the mark schemes and papers?
faqs.answer: We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and we do not host them for download. We reference them and link to the board's own page. That is the lawful position and also the more useful one, because the official version is the current version, and a stale document circulating in a parents' group is a common way a student ends up revising content that has been withdrawn. Tutors set practice from material they can legitimately access and mark it against the published criteria.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor you recommend is not free when we need them?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than quietly substituting. Early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots are the ones Meydan families want after the school run and they are the first to fill. The options are a different slot, a short wait, or a different tutor with experience of the same specification and tier. What we will not do is put someone who has never taught your child's board in front of them to fill a diary, or charge a specialist rate for a session that is really homework supervision. The trial lesson is free and comes first, so you risk nothing by asking.

intro.heading: Why the family two streets away gives you the wrong advice
paragraphs: Mirdif is one of the most curriculum-mixed parts of Dubai, and that has a specific consequence for anybody hiring a maths tutor. The eastern suburbs - Mirdif, Al Mizhar, Al Warqa, Al Khawaneej, Al Rashidiya, Nad Al Hamar - are served by schools running British, Indian, American and IB programmes within a short drive of each other. Dubai had 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum taking 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. In this part of the city those shares feel much more evenly distributed than the citywide numbers suggest.

So the neighbour whose child is doing brilliantly in maths may be on CBSE, where the syllabus sequence, the question style and the calculator rules are all different. The recommendation they pass on in good faith - a tutor, a workbook, a revision routine - may be excellent for their child and close to useless for yours. This is the single most common reason a Mirdif family hires a maths tutor who turns out not to fit: the referral came from a household on a different qualification.

It cuts the other way too. A student arriving into IGCSE from CBSE often has stronger algebraic manipulation than their new classmates and weaker performance on the structured, multi-part, context-heavy questions the IGCSE papers favour. A student arriving from an American middle-school programme may have met statistics and modelling earlier and surd and index work later. Neither is behind. Both have a mapping problem, and mapping problems are solved in weeks when they are named and in terms when they are not.

The first practical step is therefore not to find a tutor but to establish exactly what your child is sitting. Ask the school, in writing, for the board, the syllabus code and the tier. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, tiered Core and Extended, with 0606 Additional Mathematics alongside it. Pearson Edexcel runs 4MA1 Mathematics A tiered Foundation and Higher, 4MB1 Mathematics B as a single harder tier, and 4PM1 Further Pure. Those are different qualifications, and the tier within them caps what is arithmetically reachable before any teaching happens.

Then the market, with every figure attributed. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Named specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at 200-450+, and BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently - and from the eastern suburbs, with most of the city's tutoring supply concentrated further west, that premium sits near the top of the band.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Mizhar family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes the cross-city drive from the price entirely.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: An eastern-suburb maths enquiry can arrive from any of several starting points. These are the routes a Mirdif student is actually on, or arriving from.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Syllabus 0580, tiered Core and Extended, with two written papers per tier and calculator permissions varying by component. Extended reaches into functions, vectors, transformations and harder algebra. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics is taken alongside by stronger candidates heading for advanced post-16 mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: The most widely sat IGCSE maths route in Dubai and common across the eastern suburbs' British-curriculum schools. Core is capped, so the tier is the first thing to establish in writing - it governs the ceiling before any teaching affects the floor.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Mathematics A 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher, with two equally weighted papers and a calculator permitted throughout. Mathematics B 4MB1 is a single harder tier. Further Pure 4PM1 serves as advanced preparation. Pearson exams are available in May/June and November each year.
programmes.countryNote: The calculator-throughout design changes the skill balance noticeably against some Cambridge components: a candidate who leans on the calculator is less exposed on arithmetic and more exposed on method, interpretation and showing working that earns method marks.

programmes.name: Arriving into IGCSE from another curriculum
programmes.description: Mid-course transfers into IGCSE mathematics from CBSE, an American programme, the IB MYP or a national system. The content overlap is substantial and the sequencing differs, so a transferring student usually arrives with some topics ahead and some not yet met, plus an unfamiliar question style and paper structure.
programmes.countryNote: Extremely common in the eastern suburbs, where families move between schools on different curricula inside the same few neighbourhoods. The fix is a written gap list built by comparing the two syllabuses, done in the first fortnight rather than discovered in a mock.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma mathematics ahead
programmes.description: Where IGCSE maths leads. A Level Mathematics assumes algebraic fluency the IGCSE only begins; the IB splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level with an internally assessed exploration in all four.
programmes.countryNote: The financial reason to fix IGCSE maths properly rather than to grade-hunt. Post-16 specialist tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 200-450 and above, so fluency built now at IGCSE rates is fluency that does not have to be bought again in Year 12.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: IGCSE maths is best approached by topic, and transferring students need a different order from students who have been on the course since Year 9.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Rearrangement, expanding, factorising, indices and surds. Usually the strongest area for students arriving from CBSE and the weakest for those arriving from some American programmes. It underpins everything else, which makes it the first thing to assess rather than assume.

subjects.name: Structured multi-part questions
subjects.description: Not a topic, and the thing transferring students most often find unfamiliar. IGCSE papers build a question across parts where earlier answers feed later ones, which rewards showing working and punishes abandoning a part. A genuinely learnable habit and a fast one.

subjects.name: Equations and inequalities
subjects.description: Linear, simultaneous and quadratic work, with inequalities and number lines at the higher tiers. Marks go on solutions never checked and on quadratics taken to the formula when factorising was faster and safer under time pressure.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Transformations, domains, composite and inverse functions, and sketching. Students lose marks sketching without labelling key points and giving a domain they have not checked. Conceptually demanding but bounded, so it responds to a defined number of hours.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled work at the lower tiers, then sine and cosine rules and non-right-angled triangles. The classic loss is a calculator left in the wrong angle mode, which costs whole questions and takes one session to eliminate permanently.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle reasoning where marks are awarded for naming the theorem rather than for the number. A right answer with no reasoning shown forfeits most of the marks, which makes this a cheap fix with a visible effect on a paper total.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similarity
subjects.description: Areas, volumes, arcs, sectors, and similar shapes with length, area and volume scale factors. Applying a length factor to an area is the classic single misconception rather than a body of content, and it is corrected in one session.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude and geometric arguments using vector paths. Usually taught late and rushed, which is why it is overrepresented in dropped marks, and frequently absent from a transferring student's prior course entirely.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms. Often an area where students arriving from American programmes are ahead and British-curriculum peers are behind, which is worth knowing before buying hours.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and bounds
subjects.description: Percentages and reverse percentages, compound interest, ratio, standard form and upper and lower bounds. Heavily weighted at the lower tiers and routinely under-practised by students who consider it beneath them - which is exactly where Core and Foundation grades are won.

subjects.name: Calculator technique and formula recall
subjects.description: Which formulae are provided and which must be known differs by board and route, and students assume wrongly. Pearson Mathematics A permits a calculator throughout, so memory use, mode discipline and sensible rounding recover marks across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Advanced preparation for A Level or IB Higher Level maths, with a steep jump in algebraic demand. Worth paying for where the post-16 destination requires it, and worth declining where it would take hours from subjects that will decide the outcome.

sections.heading: What transfers from another curriculum, and what does not
paragraphs: This is the section that does not exist anywhere else in this market, and in the eastern suburbs it is the most useful thing a parent can read. Students move between curricula constantly here, and the resulting gaps are predictable rather than mysterious. A mapping exercise in the first fortnight turns a term of confusion into a list of three or four things to cover.

From CBSE into IGCSE, the usual pattern is strong algebraic manipulation and arithmetic fluency meeting an unfamiliar question style. IGCSE papers build questions across multiple parts in a context, where earlier answers feed later ones and marks are awarded for method shown rather than for the final value alone. A student used to a different convention may produce correct answers and lose method marks, which reads as a maths problem and is a presentation problem.

From an American middle-school or high-school programme, statistics and data handling have often been met earlier and more thoroughly, while surds, bounds, and some of the geometry and circle-theorem work may not have been covered at all. The student is not behind; the sequence was different. Identify the missing blocks and they are a handful of sessions, not a year.

From the IB MYP, the student usually arrives comfortable with investigation and generalisation and less practised at speed under timed conditions, because MYP mathematics is criterion-assessed rather than examined for most students. The fix is timed-paper work, which is cheap and fast. The table below sets out the mapping so a parent can hand it to a tutor rather than hoping one produces it.
