faqs.question: Where are the marks really being lost on my child's maths mock?
faqs.answer: Split them by question size and find out. Total the lost marks in two columns — questions worth one or two marks, and questions worth three or more. For most students in the fours and fives the first column is larger than anyone expects, sometimes larger than the second. Those early short questions are the cheapest marks on the paper and the quickest to concede through miscopying, rounding at the wrong point, or answering a slightly different question from the one asked. That single count usually reframes the whole revision plan.

faqs.question: How do we work out how fast my child should be going?
faqs.answer: Divide the total marks by the total minutes printed on the paper's front page. That gives a marks-per-minute rate, and the rate gives checkpoints: at a quarter of the way through and again at halfway, compare marks completed against time used. It takes ten seconds at the start of the paper and it is self-correcting during the paper rather than afterwards. A student who reaches halfway with a third of the marks done knows at that moment to change behaviour, rather than discovering the problem on the last page.

faqs.question: Should my child answer the paper in order?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and for a student with an uneven topic profile the order is a lever worth using. A thirty-second scan at the start, marking the questions that look immediately doable, then starting there. Marks banked in the first fifteen minutes are the most reliable on the paper, and the confidence they produce measurably improves performance on the harder questions afterwards. Two cautions: answers must still go in the correct place for each question, and the order should be set once rather than renegotiated whenever something looks hard.

faqs.question: When should a student give up on a question and move on?
faqs.answer: A workable rule is double the mark value in minutes. If a four-mark question has consumed about eight minutes and is not resolving, it gets a mark in the margin and a return visit later. Students resist this because leaving something unfinished feels like failure, which is precisely why it has to be practised on timed papers rather than simply explained. Reserve the final few minutes for revisiting flagged questions and for making sure nothing is completely blank — a partial method often scores, and a blank never does.

faqs.question: Can strategy work move a grade without learning new topics?
faqs.answer: For many students, yes, and that is the argument for buying it first. Banking every available one and two-mark question, following a time budget, choosing an answer order and installing the four procedural habits — method written as produced, rounding once at the end, checking part (a), reading the question twice — addresses the bulk of recoverable loss for a student in the fours and fives. It is four to six sessions of work with a measurable before and after, against a term or more for comparable gains from content teaching.

faqs.question: Why does rounding partway through cost a mark?
faqs.answer: Because the final answer ends up outside the accepted tolerance even though the method was sound, so the accuracy mark goes. The rule is to carry full precision through every intermediate step and round once, at the end, to the accuracy the question specifies. It shows up most on compound shapes and on compound interest, where a multiplier method avoids it entirely. Students find this the most unfair loss on the paper, which is useful — it makes the habit easy to motivate, and it takes one session plus a fortnight of marked work to fix.

faqs.question: How do the 9-1 and A*-G IGCSE scales relate for maths?
faqs.answer: Not as neatly as parents expect. The 9-1 scale runs with 9 highest and was designed to spread the top end more finely than A*-G did, so assuming 9 equals A* and 7 equals B will mislead you. Some Cambridge syllabuses and regions still report letters. What matters in practice is the threshold the receiving school names and the scale it names it in: a sixth form asking for grade 6 is asking in numbers, and one asking for a B is asking in letters. Get the requirement in the scale your child's certificate will use.

faqs.question: Will strategy work help if my child is entered for Core?
faqs.answer: It will secure the grade but it cannot raise the ceiling. A Cambridge Core entry is commonly capped at grade 5 on the 9-1 scale or C on the letter scale, and no performance exceeds the cap. So for a Core student aiming to be certain of their 4 or 5, the mark economy work is valuable. For a Core student whose sixth-form target needs grade 6, the useful conversation is the tier itself, and that belongs in Year 10 with marked Extended-standard evidence the school can act on, because entries close months before the papers.

faqs.question: What grade do we need for A Level Mathematics in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Commonly grade 6 or 7 in the subject, with some selective sixth forms asking higher and some accepting a strong 6 with conditions. An IB school offering Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches expects comparable algebraic fluency whether or not it names a number. A grade 4 or 5 is a pass that satisfies the Ministry of Education equivalency floor — five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education — without opening a post-16 mathematics route. Get the requirement in writing from the school your child will attend.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for a full timed paper to be marked?
faqs.answer: It is the only way to practise pacing, selection and propagation control, none of which can be rehearsed on topic sheets. The value is in the marking rather than the sitting: awarding only what the published scheme credits, line by line, and then classifying every lost mark as content, method, strategy or time. One full paper a fortnight with a session to mark each covers a term in about six sessions, and the error log that comes out of it is what the final weeks should be revising from.

faqs.answer: Before the final six weeks, and ideally straight after the mocks. Strategy needs two or three timed papers to embed, because a student meeting the abandon rule for the first time a fortnight before the series will not trust it under pressure. The mock also produces the marked script the whole diagnosis depends on. Buying it in the autumn is fine too and has a secondary benefit: the habits transfer to every other subject the student sits that summer, not just mathematics.

intro.heading: Two boards, two tiers, four different ceilings
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths grade is produced by three decisions and one performance. The decisions are which board the school enters students for, which tier they are placed in, and when revision switches from topics to papers. The performance happens on the day. Families focus almost entirely on the performance, and the decisions are where the grade is actually constrained.

Mudon makes the comparison concrete. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand with no secondary school inside its own boundary, so students travel to Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, South View School towards Remraam, GEMS FirstPoint in The Villa or further along Al Khail Road. Those schools do not all use the same board, and a few use different boards for different subjects, which means two Mudon neighbours in the same year group can be sitting entirely different maths papers.

The board comparison matters because the papers differ in structure rather than in difficulty. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended. Pearson 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher. The number of papers, the phrasing of questions, the amount of working the mark scheme expects to see, and the way a multi-step problem is scaffolded all differ. A student who revises from the other board's past papers learns to expect questions that will not appear.

The tier comparison matters more, and almost nobody raises it until it is too late. Core and Foundation cap the available grade. A student entered for the lower tier cannot earn a top grade however well they perform, and the entry is usually lodged months before the papers on the basis of work done late in Year 10. If a science A Level or a Higher Level Diploma maths route is in view, the higher tier is not optional.

The third decision, when revision switches from topics to papers, is the one a family controls directly. Most students in this belt keep revising topics until the week before the papers, because topic revision feels productive and a timed paper feels like a test. The switch should happen around three months out, and it should be complete by six weeks out. A student who has sat six full timed papers under conditions behaves differently in the exam hall from one who has read six chapters, even where the two know the same mathematics.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the code and tier the student is actually entered for. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to arrive at a Mudon address. What follows is the comparison in tables: board against board, tier against tier, grade against what it opens, and the market rates attached to each kind of help.

subjects.description: Algebra, number, geometry, trigonometry, statistics and probability. The reliable losses are early rounding, unshown method on multi-step questions, and abandoning the last page because question order was never planned.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main course at some schools as preparation for A Level. Coverage for it is thinner in any tutoring market, and that is disclosed when a request arrives rather than discovered later.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject where weak maths most often looks like weak physics. Rearrangement, standard form and graph gradients carry marks across the paper, and fixing the maths usually moves the physics grade with it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, concentration and yield all depend on confident proportional reasoning. Students who fail these questions often understand the chemistry and cannot execute the arithmetic under time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Less calculation than the other sciences but more data interpretation, where reading axes, scale and units correctly before applying any biology is what separates grades.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Break-even, cash flow and ratio work reuse the same proportional reasoning as the maths paper, so the two subjects reinforce each other more than timetables suggest.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and precise terminology, with some numerical work. One of the most improvable subjects by drilling, because many of the losses are mechanical rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal and data representation sit directly on number work, and pseudocode rewards the same slow mechanical discipline that trace tables and long division do.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Included because it is the second subject Mudon families most often add. Register and task type matter as much as vocabulary, and timing failures here mirror those in maths.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1
paragraphs: The two boards examine overlapping mathematics and are not interchangeable in practice. The differences that matter to a student are structural: how many papers are sat, how a multi-step question is scaffolded, how much working the mark scheme expects to see written down, and how the command phrasing is worded. None of those change what mathematics is true; all of them change what a well-prepared answer looks like.

Working shown is the clearest example. Both boards award method marks, but the amount of intermediate working a student habitually writes is trained by the papers they practise on. A student used to one board's style who sits the other's paper will sometimes produce a correct answer with insufficient method and lose marks they had earned. That is a training artefact, not a knowledge gap, and it is entirely avoidable.

Tier naming differs too, which causes real confusion in parent conversations. Cambridge uses Core and Extended in 0580; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher in 4MA1. People use the words interchangeably in community groups, and a family can leave a conversation believing their child is on the higher tier when the school has entered them otherwise. The fix is to ask the school for the entry in writing: subject, board, code, tier.

For tutoring the implication is simple. The code on the past paper must match the code on the entry, every time, from the first session. Where a school uses different boards for different subjects, which happens in this belt, the list is per subject rather than per student.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the grade it rules out
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential decision in IGCSE maths and the least discussed with parents. The lower tier covers a narrower syllabus and caps the available grade. The higher tier covers the fuller syllabus and reaches the top. A student entered for the lower tier who performs flawlessly still receives a capped grade, because the paper they sat does not contain the questions that earn more.

Schools place conservatively and there is a reason for it. A student who sits the higher tier and cannot access the harder questions can end up with a worse outcome than one who sits the lower tier and performs strongly. That is a genuine risk and a careful department weighs it. The problem is that the judgement is made on attainment at a particular moment, usually late in Year 10, and students change after that.

Which means the decision is contestable, with evidence and with timing. If a student's work improves after placement, the case has to be made in writing and before the entry deadline, which sits months ahead of the papers. Three questions to the school settle it: which tier is my child entered for, what evidence would change that, and what is the last date an amendment can be made.

The consequence reaches beyond the grade. A capped maths grade can close a science A Level or a Higher Level Diploma maths route, because sixth forms set thresholds that the lower tier cannot reach. For a Mudon family planning a sixth form at a different school from the current one, that is worth checking a full year before applications.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths grade opens next
paragraphs: The grade is not the end of the decision; it is the entry condition for the next one. A Mudon student finishing Year 11 chooses between A Level mathematics, one of the two IB Diploma maths routes, or a timetable without mathematics beyond the compulsory minimum. Each has a different expectation, and schools set thresholds rather than boards.

The hardest step on a Dubai timetable is IGCSE maths into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The content jump is real, but the larger jump is in expected independence and in the proportion of work done without technology. Students who coasted to a strong grade with a calculator permanently in hand find Paper 1 brutal, and the discovery usually happens in the first mock rather than in September.

A Level mathematics is a different kind of step: narrower in breadth, deeper in algebra, and unforgiving about fluency. Applications and Interpretation is more accessible from a mid-range IGCSE grade and is not a soft option at Higher Level, where its statistical content and modelling investigation defeat students who chose it to avoid calculus.

The practical move for a family in this belt is to ask the intended sixth form for its published thresholds before Year 11 results, not after. Thresholds differ between schools in the same emirate, and the summer bridging block that makes the step survivable has to be booked before results arrive if it is going to happen at all.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks are lost, and how fast each is fixed
paragraphs: Marks in IGCSE maths go missing in four ways, and the four have wildly different repair times. The first is early rounding: a student rounds an intermediate value, carries it forward, and the final answer falls outside the accepted range. That is a habit and it is fixed in about a fortnight by requiring full precision until the last line.

The second is unshown method. A multi-step question awards marks along the way, and a student who writes only the answer loses them even when the answer is right, and loses everything when it is wrong. This is trained by marking their own scripts against the scheme until they see where the marks sat, which takes three or four sessions to become automatic.

The third is timing collapse, visible as a strong first half and an abandoned final page. It responds quickly to a question-order rule and full papers under conditions, and it is the single most common reason a capable student underperforms. The fourth is misreading, where a correct method answers a question the paper did not ask, and that responds to reading the question aloud before writing for a couple of weeks.

Content absence is the fifth and the slow one. Whole questions untouched, rather than scattered small losses, is the signature, and it needs months rather than weeks. The honest conversation at that point is about which topics carry enough marks to be worth the time, and which are being written off deliberately.
bullets: Early rounding: about a fortnight, by requiring full precision until the last line
Unshown method: three or four sessions of self-marking against the scheme
Timing collapse: a question-order rule plus full papers under conditions
Misreading: two weeks of reading the question aloud before writing
Content absence: months, and a deliberate decision about which topics to drop

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs in this market, cheapest first
paragraphs: Starting at the bottom is honest, because that is where most searches begin. Budget online tutors and university students advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour in Dubai, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. For working through exercise sets with a student who is already organised, that tier is defensible, and dismissing it would be dishonest.

The qualified online band sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. This is where a tutor who can classify losses from a marked script and set work against them normally sits. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table giving AED 200 to 450 or more, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home visits have their own band because travel is inside the quote: roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Across a month, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. All of these are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Group maths classes against one-to-one, from Mudon
paragraphs: Group revision classes are cheaper per student and genuinely effective in one configuration: everyone in the room sitting the same code at the same tier with roughly the same gap. That configuration occurs most often in spring-term maths, which is why maths group classes are the most defensible group product in this market.

The problem in Dubailand is assembling that room. Children from one community attend several different schools on different curricula, and the schools do not share a board, so a maths group formed from Mudon, Remraam and Arabian Ranches 3 families will usually mix 0580 and 4MA1 students at two tiers. The teacher then has to teach content, because paper technique cannot be taught to both boards at once, and paper technique is what the spring term needs.

The travel arithmetic is the second factor. From Mudon, a ninety-minute class in Motor City costs most of an evening once the round trip at peak time is counted, and a Year 11 who left school at four is home at eight. A one-to-one session over video starts at 4.30pm and the evening still holds homework and dinner.

The honest recommendation is sequencing rather than loyalty. If a group class exists at a workable time and matches the code and tier, use it for broad revision. Use one-to-one for the two specific losses a marked script identifies, because those cannot be addressed in a room of eight.

One further consideration specific to this belt: group timings. A class that starts at six in Motor City suits a family living in Motor City. For a Mudon or Town Square student it means leaving before homework starts and returning after it should have finished, which quietly transfers the cost from the fee to the schoolwork. That trade is worth making consciously rather than by default.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and the questions worth asking
paragraphs: The legal position is clear enough to check in a single message. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students.

MoHRE's own service listing is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted as the penalty is unverified.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different matter: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram has no premises in the UAE, holds no such permit, and does not describe itself or its tutors using any regulator's name.

One arrangement to refuse: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. A maths teacher offering to tutor your own child privately is the first case to ask about directly.
bullets: Individual tutors: MoHRE private tuition permit, free, two years, two working days
Centres with premises: KHDA Educational Services Permit, renewed annually
No published fine schedule exists for tutoring without a permit

sections.heading: The five subjects that count, and why maths is usually one of them
paragraphs: Beyond the grade, an IGCSE timetable has a second function for families who may stay in the UAE: satisfying Ministry of Education equivalency for a later university application. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is the detail that leaves families short when they assumed otherwise. Mathematics is nearly always one of the five in practice, both because it is compulsory at most schools and because degree programmes that specify a subject usually specify it.

On the American track the requirements differ, with English proficiency shown by an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, no points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page without being read on the Ministry's own site.

IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation, does not guarantee any outcome from it, and does not suggest that tutoring is required for it. The process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate authority, and their official channels are the place to verify every detail of it.

faqs.question: Which maths board do schools near Mudon actually use?
faqs.answer: It varies, and that is the point of asking rather than assuming. The schools most Mudon students attend run British curriculum through Year 11, and some use Cambridge 0580 while others use Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, with a few using different boards for different subjects. Ask the school for the entry in writing: subject, board, code and tier. It takes one message and it determines which past papers are useful. Practising the wrong board's papers is the most common avoidable error in self-directed revision in this city.

faqs.question: Can a Core entry still produce a top IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation cap the available grade in the middle of the scale, because the paper does not contain the questions that earn more. A student entered for the lower tier who performs flawlessly still receives a capped grade. That is why the tier decision matters more than almost any amount of revision, and why it should be discussed with the school in the autumn term of Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11, when the entry is already lodged.

faqs.question: How do we argue for a tier change with the school?
faqs.answer: With evidence and early. Schools place conservatively for a defensible reason: a student who sits the higher tier and cannot access the harder questions can end up worse off. The judgement is made on attainment at a moment in time, usually late in Year 10, and students change afterwards. Bring improved work on the harder topics, in writing, before the entry deadline. Three questions settle the process: which tier is my child entered for, what evidence would change that, and what is the last date for an amendment.

faqs.question: My daughter rounds early and keeps losing final-answer marks. Fixable?
faqs.answer: Quickly, yes. Early rounding is a habit rather than a knowledge gap: an intermediate value is rounded, carried forward, and the final answer falls outside the accepted range. The repair is mechanical. Require full calculator precision until the final line, write the unrounded value down at each stage, and round only once at the end to the accuracy the question asks for. Two weeks of short timed sets with that one rule enforced usually settles it, and the marks recovered are marks she had already earned.

faqs.question: Why does she get the right answer and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because multi-step questions award method marks along the way and an answer alone collects none of them. Written working is also what rescues a question when the arithmetic goes wrong, since consequential marks can follow a correct method to a wrong value. The repair is for her to mark her own scripts against the published scheme until she sees exactly where the marks sat. Three or four sessions of that usually makes the habit automatic, and it is the single most transferable thing a maths tutor can teach.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class in Motor City worth the drive from Mudon?
faqs.answer: Only if it matches the code and the tier. A group works well when everyone in the room sits the same paper with roughly the same gap, which happens most often in spring-term maths revision. Dubailand groups usually mix Cambridge and Pearson students at two tiers, which forces the teacher to teach content rather than paper technique. Then count the evening: a ninety-minute class at peak time costs a Year 11 most of the night from Mudon, against a video session that starts at half past four.

faqs.question: What is the honest jump from IGCSE maths to Diploma Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Large, and larger in independence than in content. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level expects non-calculator fluency, comfort with proof and a willingness to work without being set exercises. Students who reached a strong IGCSE grade with a calculator always to hand find Paper 1 brutal, and they usually discover it in the first mock rather than in September. Six to eight sessions across the summer on manipulation, exact values and notation makes the first term survivable, and that block has to be booked before results arrive.

faqs.question: Which is the better next step, A Level maths or IB Applications?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student and on where they intend to apply. A Level mathematics is narrower and deeper, unforgiving about algebraic fluency. Applications and Interpretation is broader, assumes technology throughout and rewards written interpretation, and at Higher Level it is not the soft option it is assumed to be. Ask the intended sixth form for its published entry thresholds before results, since schools set these rather than boards, and read any university requirement from the institution's own published entry profile.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Year 11 maths need from January?
faqs.answer: One to begin with, moving to two if the marked papers justify it. The limiting factor during term is practice time between sessions rather than input, and a second hour that leaves no time to work on the first is wasted. From about March, two sessions a week built on timed papers is a reasonable ceiling. Where a student needs more than that, the issue is usually content absence rather than technique, and the honest conversation is about which topics carry enough marks to be worth the remaining weeks.

faqs.question: Do you teach Additional Mathematics alongside the main course?
faqs.answer: Where the school offers it and a tutor covers it, yes, and coverage for it is thinner than for the main syllabus in any market. That is disclosed when a request arrives rather than discovered after a booking. Additional Mathematics is usually taken as preparation for A Level and it makes the summer bridging block considerably easier, so students doing it are generally in a stronger position for Year 12 than their main-course grade alone suggests. Tell us the school and the course title when you enquire.

faqs.question: Does maths count towards the UAE equivalency subject total?
faqs.answer: In practice almost always, and it is usually compulsory at the school anyway. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking page states six subjects are needed; the published rule is five. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, and the Ministry's channels are where to verify it.

faqs.question: What does a marked script tell a tutor that a report card does not?
faqs.answer: Where the marks went, which is the only information a plan can be built on. A report gives a grade and a comment about effort. A script separates early rounding from unshown method, timing collapse from misreading, and scattered small losses from whole questions untouched. Those five patterns have repair times running from a fortnight to several months, and they look identical to a student. Sending one marked paper before the trial lesson means the first hour is spent working rather than discovering what is wrong.

faqs.question: Can lessons fit around a long school run from Dubailand?
faqs.answer: That is most of the reason this format suits the belt. Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time and start when the student sits down, so a 4.30pm slot works for someone home early and after 8pm works where both parents commute. Because nobody is driving to Al Salam or Arabella, a late bus does not cost the lesson and the slot can move within the evening. During Ramadan, slots after Iftar can be arranged week by week at no additional cost.

faqs.question: Will a tutor use the school's own textbook and worksheets?
faqs.answer: Where it helps, yes, alongside past papers from the entered code. The school's materials show the order topics are being taught in and the notation the class uses, which keeps sessions from contradicting the classroom. What a tutor will not do is circulate board material: Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to their publishers, and sessions reference the official pages and link to them rather than distributing copies. Nobody has access to unreleased papers whatever is claimed elsewhere.

intro.heading: "Does anyone near me actually know this paper?"
paragraphs: That is the real question behind an IGCSE maths search in this part of Dubai, and it deserves a direct answer rather than reassurance. Plenty of people in and around Muhaisnah can teach mathematics. Far fewer can tell you, without looking it up, how many papers Cambridge 0580 Extended consists of, which of them permits a calculator under the current syllabus, how the grade range differs from the Core tier, or why a Pearson 4MA1 Higher candidate meets a different question style in the final twenty marks.

The distinction is not pedantry. By the spring of Year 11 the content is largely taught and the remaining marks live in paper structure: how long each paper is, what the question types look like, where the long-answer marks sit, what the formula provision is, how the examiner expects working to be presented. A tutor who teaches mathematics rather than the qualification will do a competent job on content and be of limited use in exactly the weeks that decide the grade.

Muhaisnah makes this harder than it needs to be. The schools this neighbourhood feeds sit in Al Qusais, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Garhoud and Dubai Festival City, and they use different boards, sometimes splitting by subject within one school. The local tutoring supply reflects the neighbourhood's dominant demand, which is Indian-curriculum mathematics, so an advertised IGCSE maths tutor here is frequently a CBSE specialist with IGCSE as a secondary line. That is not dishonest, but it is not what a Year 11 Extended candidate needs in March.

So this page is a verification tool first and a service page second. It lists the syllabus codes used in this catchment so you can match them against what your school has told you. It explains what the tier decision does to the grade your child can be awarded, which is the single most consequential fact nobody explains clearly. It names the topics where Extended marks actually go. And it gives you a thirty-minute test you can run on any tutor, including ours, that will tell you whether they know the paper or are improvising.

On delivery, so it is not buried: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India, and the published Dubai market rate for in-home visits is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included if that is what you want. What we offer a Muhaisnah family is one-to-one tuition over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, from a tutor matched to the exact syllabus code, with a free trial lesson before anything is charged.

One thing no page can offer you, including this one, is a promise about the grade. The papers are marked externally, the tier was set by the school, and the performance on the day belongs to the student. What a syllabus specialist genuinely changes is the number of marks lost for reasons that have nothing to do with mathematical understanding, and in this qualification that number is reliably large enough to matter.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 mathematics
programmes.description: The years in which the tier decision is effectively being made, although nobody says so. Index laws, negative numbers, fractions, algebraic manipulation and proportional reasoning are the five foundations that determine whether a student can cope with Extended content later. None of them is externally examined, which is why gaps survive here.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Muhaisnah families buy mathematics support at this stage and it is the cheapest, most effective point to do it. A Year 8 can genuinely manage a half past five session, which a Year 11 in this catchment usually cannot, and the slots are uncontested.

programmes.name: Year 10 IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: The first examined year, covering most of the syllabus content and confirming tier placement. The work available here is foundational: closing the algebra gap, building fluency, and establishing presentation habits before any of it is under time pressure. There is still room to influence the tier the student is entered for.
programmes.countryNote: This is where we advise Muhaisnah families to spend if they are going to spend. A weekly hour through the autumn and spring of Year 10 costs less than a Year 11 intensive, has more to work with, and can still change the tier, which is the only thing that lifts the grade ceiling.

programmes.name: Year 11 IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: The examination year. The tier is fixed, the content is largely delivered, and the remaining marks are in technique: paper structure, timing, presentation of working, accuracy and the discipline of answering what was asked. Mock papers in the autumn are the best available diagnostic and are routinely under-used.
programmes.countryNote: Most families here start in Year 11 and many start after the spring mocks, which is late. By then weekday slots have been taken by school revision clinics, so bookings from this catchment commonly end up at half past seven or on Saturday mornings.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates

programmes.description: UAE candidates sit the June and November series, so a June result can be improved in November. A resit involves re-entry through a centre, which for a private candidate means finding and booking a centre independently, with fees and deadlines set by the centre rather than by any tutor.
programmes.countryNote: The decision window is the fortnight after results in August, not October. Eight focused weeks from early September are worth considerably more than twelve unfocused ones, and the entry deadline for the November series sits months before the exams, so the arrangement has to be made quickly.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: These are the areas of IGCSE mathematics Muhaisnah enquiries name, with what goes wrong in each at the Extended or Higher tier.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying. The foundation everything else rests on, and the commonest undiagnosed gap in students who look competent on topic tests but collapse on a mixed paper. Index laws and surds are where it usually breaks.

subjects.name: Quadratics and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Factorising, completing the square, the formula, and non-linear simultaneous systems. Students reach a correct solution and lose marks for not stating both roots or for abandoning exact form when the question required it.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, gradients and areas under graphs. Marks go missing on sketches without intercepts or asymptotes labelled, and on reading values from a graph to the accuracy the question demands.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled work, then the sine and cosine rules and three-dimensional problems at the higher tier. Bearings are a reliable source of lost marks because students measure from the wrong reference direction.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, similarity, congruence and circle theorems. The marks are for the reason, not the answer: a correct angle with no theorem named scores less than a wrong angle with correct reasoning shown.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area, arcs and sectors. Straightforward content under-practised because it looks easy, then costing marks on units, on rounding, and on compound shapes where one dimension has to be deduced.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms. Histograms with unequal class widths are the single most reliable Extended loss, because frequency density is skipped in revision.

subjects.name: Ratio, proportion and rates
subjects.description: Direct and inverse proportion, compound measures, percentage change and reverse percentages. Reverse percentage questions are where many students at this tier lose two marks they fully understood how to earn.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and describing transformations fully. A transformation described without its centre, scale factor or mirror line loses marks even when the drawing is perfect, which is purely a communication issue.

subjects.name: Sequences and algebraic fractions
subjects.description: Nth terms including quadratic sequences, and simplifying or solving algebraic fractions. Both reward systematic working, and both punish the student who tries to do several steps mentally to save time.

subjects.name: Problem solving across topics
subjects.description: The final questions on a higher-tier paper combine topics without signalling which. Recognising which tool a question wants is a trainable skill distinct from knowing the tools, and it is what separates the top two grades from the next one down.

subjects.name: Calculator fluency
subjects.description: Statistical functions, exact-form entry, memory use and degree mode. Students lose both time and accuracy doing by hand what the permitted device does instantly, and this is fixable in a single session.

sections.heading: Which mathematics qualification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Get this from the school's exams officer or the mathematics teacher, in writing, before you book anybody. Do not get it from the student: most cannot say, and the confident ones are sometimes wrong. Dubai schools use Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, some use OxfordAQA, and a single school may use different boards for different subjects. Cambridge sciences with Pearson mathematics is a common pairing in this catchment and is exactly the configuration that produces a mismatched tutor.

The table below lists the codes you are most likely to be told, with the tiers each offers and what to confirm. Take the code to any tutor you are considering and ask them to describe its papers. A specialist answers immediately: number of papers, duration, calculator position, where the long-answer marks sit. A generalist says the boards are broadly similar, which is true of the content and false of the paper, and the paper is what March and April are about.

Two of these deserve a specific warning. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics is a different syllabus from 0580 with a different assessment design, and a tutor who assumes 0580 will mislead a 0607 candidate about what the paper asks for. And Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics is a genuinely harder qualification taken alongside the main one by stronger candidates; if your child has been entered for it late, the useful question is whether the entry is appropriate rather than how to revise for it.

Paper numbers, durations and calculator rules are revised when a syllabus is reissued, so confirm the current detail against the board's published syllabus for your child's cohort rather than against anything on a tutoring page, including this one. What does not change is the principle: the code is the unit of matching, and a tutor who cannot describe your code's papers should not be teaching your child in Year 11.

sections.heading: The tier decision and the grade ceiling nobody explains
paragraphs: This is the fact that changes what a family should buy and it is rarely stated plainly. Tiered mathematics qualifications do not award the full grade range on both tiers. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade that can be awarded, regardless of how well the student performs. A student who scores extremely highly on a Core paper receives the top grade available on that tier, not the top grade available in the qualification.

That has two consequences. First, no amount of tutoring lifts a grade above the ceiling of the tier the student is entered for, so if the target grade sits above that ceiling the conversation is about the entry and not about tuition. Second, a confident Core grade is a genuinely good outcome for a student who would have struggled on Extended, and families who force an Extended entry on a borderline student frequently end up with a worse result than the Core entry would have produced.

The decision belongs to the school, is based on evidence from the student's work, and is usually taken well before Year 11. The honest sequence for a Muhaisnah family who wants to change it is to ask the mathematics teacher two questions: what evidence would change the entry, and by what date does the decision have to be made? Then work on exactly that evidence. A tutor who promises to move a child up a tier without having seen a marked script is guessing.

The table sets out the comparison across what actually differs, and the last column is what matters for planning. Note the tutoring implication is not simply more hours for the higher tier: the higher tier needs different work, aimed at multi-topic problem solving and at the extended questions that only appear on that paper.

sections.heading: Where higher-tier marks actually go in this catchment
paragraphs: Mock scripts from students in this catchment show the same losses year after year, and almost none of them are about not knowing the mathematics. The largest single category is reasoning not shown. Circle theorem questions award marks for naming the theorem; a correct angle with no reason attached loses them. Transformation questions award marks for a complete description; a perfect drawing with no centre or scale factor stated loses them. Both are communication failures dressed up as mathematics failures.

The second category is specific topics that are systematically under-revised because they look like minor content. Histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density is the whole question. Reverse percentages, where students apply a forward calculation. Bearings, measured from the wrong reference direction. Compound and inverse proportion. Algebraic fractions, where a student who can simplify will not combine. Each is a small number of marks and together they are a grade.

The third category is accuracy and rounding. Carrying an approximated intermediate value forward converts correct method into a wrong answer. Giving a final answer to three significant figures when the question asked for two decimal places loses a mark the mathematics had earned. Leaving an answer in decimal form when exact form was required does the same.

The fourth is timing, and it is the one most visible on a mock script: a student who has answered everything up to a point and then produced fragments. That is a pacing problem and it has a specific remedy, which is timed sections rather than untimed practice. Topic revision does not fix it, and families who respond to an incomplete mock by buying more content coverage are solving the wrong problem at considerable expense.
bullets: Name the circle theorem; the reason carries the mark, not the angle
Describe transformations fully: type, centre, scale factor, mirror line
Histograms with unequal widths need frequency density every time
Reverse percentages: never apply a forward calculation
Keep intermediate values unrounded; check the accuracy the question demands

sections.heading: Thirty minutes that prove whether a tutor knows the paper
paragraphs: Run this on any tutor, local or online, and on us. It needs no mathematical knowledge from you and it is far more informative than a credential list. Five requests, in order, and note that each one has a right answer the tutor either produces instantly or does not.

One: describe the papers for my child's syllabus code, with tiers, durations and calculator positions. Two: name three topics that appear on the higher tier and not on the lower one. Three: show me, on my child's mock script, three marks lost for a reason that is not about understanding the mathematics. Four: what will you set between sessions, and will you mark it before the next one? Five: what should my child be able to do after six sessions that they cannot do today?

The third request is the strongest filter in the list, because it cannot be prepared for. A tutor who knows the qualification will find those three marks in two minutes and explain each one in a sentence. A tutor who teaches mathematics in general will talk about the topics the student got wrong, which is a different and much less useful answer. The distinction will be obvious to you even if you cannot do the mathematics yourself.

The fifth request tests whether the tutor plans or improvises. A specialist narrows it: not "improve in maths" but "describe transformations completely without being prompted, and handle a histogram with unequal class widths". That narrowness is what makes a review at session six possible, and a tutor who will not narrow it has given you no way to evaluate what you are about to pay for.

sections.heading: Year 10 or Year 11: when the hour is actually worth buying
paragraphs: Almost all the demand in this catchment arrives in Year 11, and almost all the value sits in Year 10. The reason is structural rather than motivational. In Year 10 the tier is still movable, the content is still being taught for the first time, the student is less tired, and the evening slots are uncontested. In Year 11 the tier is fixed, the content is largely delivered, and the available work is technique within a ceiling somebody else set.

That does not make Year 11 support pointless. Technique work is real and it moves grades, particularly for a student whose mock script shows the losses described earlier. But it is a narrower product and it should be bought as a bounded block with a stated target, not as an open-ended weekly slot renewed out of anxiety. A family spending across a whole Year 11 without a review point is usually paying for reassurance.

The highest-value purchase in this catchment, if a family is going to buy anything, is a weekly hour through the autumn and spring of Year 10 aimed at algebraic fluency and at presentation habits. Both transfer to every subsequent paper. Both are cheap to fix at that stage and expensive to fix later. And in a student who is borderline between tiers, both are exactly the evidence the school needs to see before an entry decision.

For Key Stage 3 the same logic goes further back and almost nobody acts on it. Index laws, negative numbers, fractions and proportional reasoning are the four things that decide whether Extended content is accessible, and they can be rebuilt in a term at a lower rate with no examination pressure. A family who fixes those in Year 8 generally never buys mathematics tutoring again.

sections.heading: Resits, the November series and private candidates
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June and November series, which means a June result can be improved in the same calendar year rather than waiting twelve months. That is a genuine option and families in this catchment under-use it, usually because the decision window is misunderstood. The useful fortnight is immediately after results in August, not October, because entries close months before the exams and because eight focused weeks from early September are worth more than twelve drifting ones.

Do not use any February or March dates you find quoted. The Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only; UAE candidates sit June and November. A page quoting a February exam window or a November entry deadline for a March series to a Dubai parent is giving them a date that is wrong for their country, and it is the kind of error a family acts on.

On verifiable dates: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

If the student has left the school that entered them, they become a private candidate, which changes the logistics rather than the qualification. A centre has to be found and booked independently, and the centre sets its own fees and deadlines. Those figures should come from the centre, not from a tutoring page: we will not quote an entry fee we cannot source. The school's exams officer is the best first call even after a student has left, because they will know which local centres accept private candidates.

sections.heading: What syllabus-specific maths support costs here
paragraphs: Mathematics is the most heavily tutored subject in Dubai, which means supply is good and rates sit mid-band rather than at scarcity levels. The published figures: qualified subject tutors working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one Dubai agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists across IB, IGCSE and A Level at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. Budget online provision from roughly AED 33 to 65 depending on the provider. In-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel included.

What the extra buys at the specialist end, in this subject specifically, is paper knowledge rather than mathematical knowledge. Anybody in the qualified band can teach circle theorems. Fewer can look at a mock script and identify in two minutes that the student is losing reasoning marks rather than getting angles wrong, and fewer still know the question-type patterns of one particular code well enough to predict where the student will next lose two marks. In Year 10 that premium is optional. In the spring of Year 11 it is most of the value.

The cheapest effective purchase in this catchment is the three-session mock diagnostic, because it frequently concludes that a short block is sufficient. The most expensive is an open-ended Year 11 weekly slot with no stated target, renewed monthly; published monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for a weekly hour, so a year of that unevaluated is a substantial sum.

Our own figure is agreed at the consultation, once the code, tier and cadence are known, and we sit in the qualified-specialist part of those bands rather than the budget part. The trial lesson is free and nothing is charged before it. If the mock diagnostic says a bounded block will do, we will quote the block rather than the year, which is the smaller sale and the right advice.

sections.heading: Starting, with the code in hand
paragraphs: Send three things and the match is right first time. The syllabus code and tier from the school in writing. The most recent mock or marked paper, because that is where a specialist finds the real problem. And the school's weekly timetable, including which afternoons finish late, so the slot is chosen rather than assumed.

We propose a tutor who teaches that code habitually and a free trial lesson in a slot the school run can survive. In this catchment that usually means six o'clock or half past seven on a weekday, or half past nine on a Saturday. Use the trial to run the five requests from the thirty-minute test, especially the third one about marks lost on the student's own script.

Then agree one narrow target for session six, visible in a marked paper. Describing transformations completely without prompting. Handling a histogram with unequal class widths. Completing a paper section in the time allowed without fragments at the end. At session six you look at a script and decide: continue, change the tutor, change the diagnosis, or stop.

Finally, the advice we would give a Muhaisnah family regardless of whether they use us. If your child is in Year 10, buy the autumn. If they are in Year 11 and the mocks are done, buy the diagnostic before you buy any hours. If the target grade sits above the tier ceiling, go and talk to the mathematics teacher before you spend anything at all, because that conversation is free and no tutor can substitute for it.

whyPoints.description: If the target grade sits above the ceiling of the tier your child is entered for, no amount of tuition reaches it and the conversation belongs with the school. We say that before taking a booking rather than after six months of it.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from a script, not a conversation
whyPoints.description: The three-session mock diagnostic exists because content gaps, method losses, accuracy losses and pacing failures look identical when described in words and completely different on a marked paper. Buying hours before that distinction is made is how money is wasted here.

whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November. The February/March series is offered to India only, and quoting its deadlines to a Dubai parent hands them a date that is wrong for their country. We link the board's live timetable rather than restating dates.

whyPoints.title: We will point you at the free option
whyPoints.description: If the school runs its own revision clinic in mathematics, it is free and aligned to the school's own entries, and competing with it wastes your money. If the tier is the problem, the mathematics teacher is the person to see. Both conversations cost us a booking.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE maths tutor in Muhaisnah who knows our exact syllabus?
faqs.answer: There are maths tutors who will travel here, but the local supply reflects the neighbourhood's dominant demand, which is Indian-curriculum mathematics, so an advertised IGCSE tutor is often a CBSE specialist with IGCSE as a second line. That is adequate for content and thin for paper technique, which is what the spring of Year 11 is about. IB Gram matches on the syllabus code rather than on proximity and teaches one-to-one over live video; we do not send tutors to UAE addresses at all. Ask any tutor to describe your code's papers before booking.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and 0607?
faqs.answer: They are different syllabuses with different assessment designs, both offering Core and Extended tiers. A tutor who assumes 0580 will mislead a 0607 candidate about what the papers ask for and how the questions are structured, even though much of the content overlaps. The practical step is to confirm which code your child is entered for with the exams officer, in writing, and then to ask any prospective tutor to describe that code's papers specifically. Confirm current paper numbers and durations against the board's published syllabus for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: Can tutoring get my child a grade above their tier?
faqs.answer: No. Tiered mathematics qualifications cap the grade awarded on the lower tier, so a student entered for Core or Foundation receives at most the top grade available on that tier however well they perform. If your target grade sits above that cap, the conversation is about the entry rather than about tuition, and it belongs with the mathematics teacher. Ask them two questions: what evidence would change the entry, and by what date must the decision be made. Then work on exactly that evidence rather than on general improvement.

faqs.question: Is a confident Core grade worse than a shaky Extended grade?
faqs.answer: Often it is better, and families underweight this. A student who would be pressured throughout an Extended paper and finish in fragments frequently ends up below where a secure Core entry would have placed them. The tier is a judgement about what the student can sustain under timed conditions, not a verdict on their ability. Look at marked mock scripts rather than at aspiration: if the student is losing marks to pace across the whole paper, the higher tier will amplify that rather than reward the extra content.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics do students here lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Four recur every year in mock scripts from this catchment. Histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density is the whole question and is routinely skipped in revision. Reverse percentages, where a forward calculation gets applied. Circle theorems, where the mark is for naming the theorem and a correct angle with no reason scores less. And transformations described without a centre, scale factor or mirror line. Each is a small number of marks, all four are fixable within weeks, and together they are commonly a grade.

faqs.question: My child's mock paper stopped halfway. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It is a pacing problem, not a content problem, and the two need opposite responses. A script with everything attempted and scattered errors says content and method; a script answered correctly up to a point and then fragmentary says the student cannot sustain the required rate. Buying more topic coverage for the second case is solving the wrong problem at considerable expense. The remedy is timed sections every session, marked to the published scheme, until the student can complete a full paper section inside the allowance.

faqs.question: How can I test a maths tutor if I do not know the maths myself?
faqs.answer: Make three requests that need no mathematics from you. Ask them to describe the papers for your child's syllabus code with tiers, durations and calculator positions. Ask them to name three topics that appear on the higher tier and not the lower one. Then hand them your child's mock script and ask them to find three marks lost for a reason that is not about understanding the mathematics. The third cannot be prepared for, and a specialist does it in two minutes while a generalist talks about the topics the student got wrong.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to buy maths support?
faqs.answer: Year 10, decisively, and almost all the demand arrives in Year 11. In Year 10 the tier is still movable, the content is being taught for the first time, the student is less tired and the evening slots are uncontested. In Year 11 the tier is fixed and the available work is technique inside a ceiling somebody else set. Year 11 support is still real, but it should be bought as a bounded block with a stated target rather than as an open-ended weekly slot renewed out of anxiety.

faqs.question: Should my child retake IGCSE maths in the November series?
faqs.answer: It is a genuine option because UAE candidates sit both June and November, and families here under-use it. The decision window is the fortnight after results in August rather than October, because entries close months before the exams and eight focused weeks from early September beat twelve drifting ones. Do not use any February or March dates you find quoted: that series is offered to India only. Entry logistics and fees come from the centre and the exams officer, not from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: What happens if my child has left the school that entered them?
faqs.answer: They become a private candidate, which changes the logistics rather than the qualification. A centre has to be found and booked independently, and the centre sets its own fees and deadlines. The school's exams officer is still the best first call, even after a student has left, because they will know which local centres accept private candidates. We will not quote an entry fee, because that figure belongs to the centre and varies, and a number we cannot source is worse than no number.

faqs.question: Does Additional Mathematics 0606 need a different tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the first question is whether the entry is appropriate at all. Cambridge 0606 is a genuinely harder qualification taken alongside the main mathematics course by stronger candidates, and a student entered for it late with a shaky Extended foundation is being asked to run before walking. Fewer tutors cover it properly. If your child has been entered recently and is struggling, consolidating the main syllabus usually produces a better overall outcome than splitting attention across both.

faqs.question: How much should syllabus-specific maths support cost in eastern Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and specialists across IGCSE and A Level at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Mathematics is well supplied here, so rates sit mid-band rather than at scarcity levels. What the specialist premium buys in this subject is paper knowledge rather than mathematical knowledge, which matters most in the final two terms.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: A tutor should be pointing you to the board's published material or working from what the school supplies, not selling a pack. Cambridge and Pearson publish syllabus documents and past papers, and the school has access to more. We will not reproduce or distribute board material as downloads, because reproducing it is a copyright matter and, for unreleased content, worse. If a provider is charging for a past-paper bundle, ask where it came from and whether they are permitted to distribute it before paying for it.

faqs.question: Can we do maths sessions in the school holidays instead of term time?
faqs.answer: Holidays are often the best time for foundational work, and we would encourage it for a Year 9 or Year 10 student with an algebra gap. There is no competing homework, no fatigue from the school run, and the student can rebuild index laws and manipulation without also keeping up with the current unit. For Year 11 technique work the opposite is true: timed practice is most useful when it sits alongside the school's own mock and revision schedule, so term time is the better fit.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-muhaisnah.closingBody: One email to your child's school settles the thing that matters most: the syllabus code and the tier. Nothing is charged before the trial, and if the mock says a three-session diagnostic is all you need, that is what we will quote.

intro.heading: Three shortlists, one missing question
paragraphs: A parent in Nad Al Hamar, a parent in Mirdif and a parent in Al Warqa run the same search and get three different shortlists. The Mirdif list is longest, because Mirdif has the most schools and the most tuition centres within a short drive. The Al Warqa list leans toward tutors who serve the large British and Indian curriculum schools there. The Nad Al Hamar list is the shortest of the three, because the district has no secondary school inside it and few resident subject specialists. None of the three lists is sorted by the question that decides whether a maths tutor can help, which is which specification your child is entered for.

That question has three answers in Dubai, not two. Cambridge International Mathematics is syllabus 0580, with a Core and an Extended tier. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, with Foundation and Higher tiers, and it is the route most British-curriculum schools use. Specification B, 4MB1, is a different and more demanding assessment that some schools enter stronger cohorts for, and a tutor who has only taught Specification A will be working from the wrong paper structure for a Specification B candidate.

The second missing question is what format the help should take. A one-to-one hour, a tuition centre group class, a subscription app and the school's own free provision are four different products at four very different prices, and each solves a different problem. Families tend to compare providers within one format rather than comparing formats, which is where the money goes wrong. A student whose problem is practice volume does not need the most expensive format; a student stuck on graph transformations does.

The third is what the marks are actually distributed across. Revision time gets spread evenly across the syllabus when it should be weighted toward the topics that carry the most marks and the ones a student is leaving blank. Number, algebra and geometry carry the bulk of any IGCSE maths paper, and the higher-tier-only topics such as circle theorems, vector proofs and graph transformations are routinely abandoned rather than attempted, which makes them the cheapest marks available.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a fixed weekly hour set around the eastern-suburb school run. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The Dubai in-home market is real and priced in this page with the source of every figure, so the alternative can be weighed with numbers. What the online format buys a Nad Al Hamar family is the ability to pick on specification rather than on distance.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.programmesIntro: The three stages at which eastern-suburb families ask for maths help, and what each stage can still change.

programmes.name: The year before the entry
programmes.description: Algebraic fluency is built here, and it is what determines whether the higher tier is a realistic entry. Rearrangement, indices, negative numbers and fraction work done securely in Year 9 keep every option open; done loosely, they produce a Year 10 student who will be recommended for the capped tier on perfectly reasonable evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Nad Al Hamar families have a specific advantage here, which is that the work needed is narrow. Two short sessions a month aimed only at manipulation is cheap and changes what is possible two years later, and it is the one intervention in this market that is reliably better value than its price.

programmes.name: Tier evidence year
programmes.description: Content is introduced and the school gathers the evidence on which it will enter your child for a tier. The higher-tier-only topics appear in this year: functions and graph transformations, circle theorems, vector geometry and the sine and cosine rules. These take months to build, which is why a tier conversation in Year 11 is usually too late to act on.
programmes.countryNote: Schools across Mirdif, Al Warqa and the Festival City cluster run Year 10 assessments at different points, so a family comparing their child's progress against a cousin's at another eastern-suburb school is often comparing two different assessment calendars rather than two levels of attainment.

programmes.name: Entry and examination year
programmes.description: Entries are submitted with the tier attached, mocks are sat, and the papers arrive in the June or November series. The content has been covered once by spring, so the marginal value of teaching falls and the marginal value of timed practice rises. Revision should be weighted by topic marks and by what the student is leaving blank.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE equivalency the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count. That is a much lower bar than any sixth form applies for A Level Mathematics, and the two are frequently confused.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics splits into topic blocks that carry very different shares of the paper. These are the ones worth naming when you talk to a tutor.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, reverse percentages, standard form, bounds, ratio and compound interest. The highest-volume block on a lower-tier paper and the place where accuracy rather than understanding decides the grade. Reverse percentages in particular are reliably answered the wrong way round.

subjects.name: Algebra and manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, indices, surds, simultaneous and quadratic equations. The block that determines performance in every other block, because multi-step questions pass through an algebraic step whatever they appear to be about.

subjects.name: Functions and graph transformations
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, and the translation, reflection and stretch of graphs. Absent from the lower tier entirely, which is why a candidate moved up late has a specific and sizeable gap here rather than a general one.

subjects.name: Geometry and circle theorems
subjects.levels: Circle theorems on the higher tier
subjects.description: Angle properties, similarity, congruence, and the circle theorems. A bounded learnable set that appears reliably and is left blank by borderline candidates, which makes a fortnight of focused work worth a grade boundary on its own.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Sine and cosine rules on the higher tier
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry on both tiers, then the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems above. The failure point is consistently the move away from right-angled triangles rather than the trigonometry itself.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude and vector geometry proofs. The proof questions carry full marks and are abandoned by most candidates, making them, with circle theorems, the cheapest recoverable marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Statistics and data
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, box plots and histograms with unequal class widths. Frequency density is a concept rather than a formula and is the reliable mark-shedder in this block across both boards.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and set notation. Marks are usually lost to reading rather than to probability: the words without replacement are missed and a different question is answered correctly.

subjects.name: Calculator operation
subjects.description: Fraction entry, stored answers, statistical modes, degree settings and table functions. A skill rather than a topic, and the difference between finishing a paper and leaving a page blank. Worth ten minutes of every session until it stops limiting the student.

sections.heading: Nad Al Hamar, Mirdif and Al Warqa compared for maths specifically
paragraphs: The three areas sit within fifteen minutes of each other and differ in ways that matter to a maths decision. Mirdif has the highest density of schools and tuition centres, which means real group-class options and the longest local shortlist. Al Warqa has the heaviest higher-tier maths demand because of its large British and Indian curriculum schools, so a tutor working that area is more likely to have taught the higher tier in the current cycle. Nad Al Hamar has neither: no school inside the district, few resident specialists, and a shortlist made mostly of generalists and centres elsewhere.

What that means in practice is that the three areas offer different versions of the wrong product. A long Mirdif list of centres offers scheme-paced group teaching. A Nad Al Hamar list offers travelling generalists. Neither is sorted by specification, and for a student stuck on graph transformations in Specification B the specification is the only attribute that matters. The local advantage Al Warqa has is real but accidental, and it is not an advantage a Nad Al Hamar family can acquire by looking harder.

The logistics do differ and they should shape the slot rather than the choice of tutor. From Nad Al Hamar, Festival City is twelve to fifteen minutes off-peak and twenty to twenty-five at pickup, and Mirdif is eighteen to twenty against thirty to thirty-five. Door times across the three areas land between about 3.40pm and 4.35pm, pushed past 5pm on activity days. In all three the slot that survives a full Year 11 term sits between 6pm and 7.30pm.

So the comparison resolves the same way for all three: choose on specification and tier, set the hour after the real door time, and buy a bounded block rather than an open-ended arrangement. In Mirdif that is a preference exercised among several options. In Nad Al Hamar it is the only route to a specialist at all.
