sections.heading: Specification A against Specification B, and Cambridge alongside both
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel runs two International GCSE mathematics specifications and Dubai schools use both. Specification A, code 4MA1, is the mainstream route with Foundation and Higher tiers. Specification B, code 4MB1, is a different assessment used for stronger cohorts, with a more demanding question style and content that reaches further toward early A Level material. They are not tiers of one another and the past papers are not interchangeable.

This matters because a tutor who has taught Specification A for years will know the content a Specification B candidate needs but not the shape of the questions they will face, and in the final eight weeks the shape is what is being practised. A Specification B student working through Specification A papers will find them easy, conclude they are ready, and then meet a paper that asks for more sustained reasoning. That is a real and avoidable failure, and it starts with nobody establishing the code.

Cambridge International Mathematics, syllabus 0580, sits alongside both with Core and Extended tiers. Its Extended papers tend toward longer multi-part structured questions where later parts depend on earlier ones, so an early slip is expensive. Edexcel Higher papers tend toward a greater number of shorter items, which rewards pace and punishes dwelling. Those are different examination habits to train, and a tutor who has taught both will say which one your child is losing marks to.

The administrative facts to hold alongside this: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series and the November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with different timetables, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's version.

sections.heading: Where the marks sit, and where revision time usually goes instead
paragraphs: Students revise what they are comfortable with, which means time flows toward number and basic algebra and away from the topics that are both heavily marked and poorly attempted. Across both boards, number and algebra together carry the largest share of any paper, geometry and trigonometry carry a substantial block, and statistics and probability carry a smaller but reliable one. On the higher tier, functions, transformations, circle theorems and vectors appear every series and are precisely the material a borderline candidate has abandoned.

The right weighting is therefore not even. It is proportional to marks available multiplied by marks currently missed. A student scoring well on number and leaving every circle theorem question blank should spend almost no revision time on number. This sounds obvious and is almost never how revision is organised, because the student chooses what to do and chooses the comfortable thing.

The practical method is to take the marked mock, go through it question by question, and record for each lost mark both the topic and the reason. Then total the marks lost by topic. The top two topics by marks lost are the revision plan for the next month, and if one of them consists mainly of blank answers it comes first, because an abandoned topic is full marks currently scoring nothing rather than partial marks being squeezed.

One caution. A topic a student has never been taught, because they were entered for the lower tier and have been moved up, is a different case and needs teaching rather than revision. Mixing the two produces a plan that treats a content gap as a practice gap, and three weeks of past papers on a topic that was never covered is three weeks lost.

sections.heading: One-to-one, group class or an app: what each format solves
paragraphs: Families compare providers inside a format and rarely compare formats, which is where the money is actually decided. There are four products on the table in eastern Dubai. The school's own provision, usually included in fees. A subscription practice app, cheap and unlimited. A tuition centre group class, cheapest per head of the taught options. And one-to-one hours, the most expensive per hour and the only one that can stop on a single topic.

The school's provision should be tried first and frequently is not. Subject clinics and teacher support are free, aligned exactly with the assessment your child will sit, and staffed by people who know the internal calendar. A parent who has not asked what is available may be buying something already included. An app is excellent for practice volume and useless for explanation: it will tell a student they got a question wrong and will not work out why they keep getting that kind of question wrong.

A group class supplies structure, pace, a fixed weekly commitment and peer pressure, which is precisely the remedy for a student who is not doing enough work. It cannot spend forty minutes on circle theorems for one student while nine others wait. One-to-one hours are the reverse: expensive, and the only format that can take a single named topic and stay on it until it holds. The honest rule is to buy the cheapest format that can solve the problem you have actually identified.

Which brings the matter back to identification. A parent who can name the topic should buy one-to-one time on it, in a bounded block. A parent who can only name the grade should buy a diagnostic first, then decide. Buying three subjects of one-to-one hours on the strength of a disappointing mock report is the single commonest expensive mistake in this market, and it happens in Mirdif and Nad Al Hamar equally.

sections.heading: Both papers are calculator papers, and that changes the preparation
paragraphs: Unlike IB Analysis and Approaches, IGCSE mathematics on these routes permits a calculator throughout. That sounds like a simplification and is actually a trap, because it moves the failure point from algebraic fluency to machine fluency and nobody teaches the second. A student who knows the method and spends ninety seconds per question finding the right menu will not finish the paper, and an unfinished paper costs more marks than any topic gap.

The specific skills are short and teachable. Fraction entry, so that a student is not converting to decimals and rounding early. Storing an answer and recalling it, which is the single commonest source of accumulated rounding error and costs accuracy marks across a whole paper. Statistical modes for one and two-variable data. Degree mode, which silently ruins trigonometric answers if left in radians. Table functions for graph sketching. Standard-form entry and display.

Teaching this on video works better than teaching it beside a student, which is the opposite of what parents expect. The tutor shares an emulator or the matching software on screen, so the menu path is projected at a readable size and can be repeated, while the student follows on the handheld model they will take into the examination hall. In a kitchen-table session the student watches a small screen at an angle and copies approximately.

The discipline we apply is ten minutes of every session on calculator work until it stops limiting the student, and then it stops. Alongside that sits the rounding rule: work to full precision throughout and round only at the end, to three significant figures unless the question specifies otherwise. Those two habits together recover more marks for a middling candidate than another month of content.

sections.heading: What a parent can actually verify before paying
paragraphs: Most of what a tutoring provider says about itself cannot be checked, so it is worth knowing which claims can be. The specification a tutor has taught is checkable by asking them to describe the paper structure of it, which takes thirty seconds and cannot be bluffed. The tier is checkable the same way, by asking which higher-tier-only topics they have taught most recently. A permit is checkable because it is a document. A rate is checkable because it is a number.

What is not checkable, and should therefore be discounted entirely, is any statistic offered without a sample size, a date and a method. Competitor pages in this market publish star ratings of 4.92 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page, and one shows five out of five from twenty reviews next to a claim about student numbers the review count cannot support. Self-asserted review markup is a structured-data violation and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. We publish no rating at all.

On permits specifically: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's service page titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two working-day completion time. Operating without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson, because it holds none. It operates no office or centre in the UAE. It does not present any named school as a partner or client. Those four absences are the most checkable statements on this page, and in this market they are also the rarest.

sections.heading: Additional Mathematics, and the step after the main entry
paragraphs: Some schools in eastern Dubai enter stronger candidates for an additional or further mathematics qualification alongside the main entry. It is worth being clear about what that is for. It is an extension rather than an insurance policy: it covers material that overlaps with early A Level or Diploma mathematics, and its value is in the transition rather than in the certificate. A student who takes it and does well arrives in Year 12 having already met calculus and more demanding algebra.

The sequencing rule is firm. Additional mathematics should only be tutored once the main entry is secure, because the main grade is the one that sixth forms and the Ministry of Education count. A student spending tutoring hours on the extension while sitting on a borderline main grade has inverted their priorities, and a tutor who encourages that is not reading the situation.

Where it earns its place is for a student heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Those courses demand sustained algebraic fluency and a willingness to justify rather than execute, and the additional qualification is the only point before sixth form where that is formally assessed. For such a student, six to eight weeks of bridging work in the summer after Year 11 is the natural continuation and the highest-value block available.

For everyone else, the honest answer is that the extension is optional and the main grade is not. A parent choosing between tutoring hours on the extension and hours on circle theorems for the main paper should choose circle theorems every time, because those are marks on the certificate that counts.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Edexcel Specification A and Specification B in maths?
faqs.answer: Specification A, code 4MA1, is the mainstream International GCSE route with Foundation and Higher tiers. Specification B, code 4MB1, is a separate and more demanding assessment that some Dubai schools enter stronger cohorts for, with a question style that asks for more sustained reasoning and content reaching further toward early A Level material. They are not tiers of one another and their past papers are not interchangeable. A Specification B candidate practising Specification A papers will find them easy and conclude wrongly that they are ready.

faqs.question: Is it harder to find a maths tutor in Nad Al Hamar than in Mirdif?
faqs.answer: Harder to find a long local list, yes. Mirdif has the densest concentration of schools and tuition centres in eastern Dubai, while Nad Al Hamar has no secondary school inside the district and few resident specialists. But neither list is sorted by specification, and for a student stuck on graph transformations in Specification B the specification is the only attribute that matters. The Mirdif advantage is a longer list of scheme-paced options rather than a better chance of the right specialist.

faqs.question: Which maths topics should we revise first with eight weeks to go?
faqs.answer: The ones carrying the most marks that your child is currently leaving blank, which for a borderline higher-tier candidate is usually circle theorems, vector proofs and graph transformations. An abandoned topic is full marks scoring nothing, so recovering it is cheaper than squeezing partial marks out of a topic already being attempted. Take the marked mock, total the marks lost per topic, separate blanks from errors, and let that table rather than the student's comfort set the order.

faqs.question: Would a maths app be enough instead of paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: For practice volume, often yes, and it is the cheapest option available. An app will set unlimited questions and mark them instantly, which is exactly what a student who is not doing enough work needs. What it cannot do is work out why the same kind of question keeps going wrong, which is the thing a tutor is for. The useful combination is an app for volume plus a small number of one-to-one hours on the two topics the app shows are consistently failing.

faqs.question: Why does calculator technique matter if both papers allow one?
faqs.answer: Because permission shifts the failure point from algebra to machine fluency, and nobody teaches the second. A student who knows the method and spends ninety seconds per question hunting a menu will not finish, and an unfinished paper costs more than any single topic gap. The specific skills are short: fraction entry, storing and recalling answers rather than retyping rounded values, statistical modes, degree mode, standard form and table functions. Ten minutes a session fixes it, then it stops.

faqs.question: Our child was moved up a tier mid-course. What exactly is the gap?
faqs.answer: Structural rather than general, which matters because it needs teaching rather than revision. The higher tier examines topics the lower tier does not: functions and graph transformations, circle theorems, vector geometry proofs, and the sine and cosine rules in harder settings. Your child has not underperformed on those; they have never been taught them. Three weeks of past papers on untaught content is three weeks wasted, so audit the gap against the new specification first and teach the missing blocks before practising.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a maths tutor really knows our specification?
faqs.answer: Ask them to describe the paper structure of the exact code: how many papers, their length, whether a calculator is permitted, and which topics appear only on the higher tier. That takes thirty seconds and cannot be bluffed. Then ask which higher-tier-only topics they have taught most recently and to which cohort. A specialist answers both immediately and often volunteers what they would not claim; a generalist redirects the conversation to experience in general.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth tutoring alongside the main entry?
faqs.answer: Only once the main grade is secure, because the main grade is the one sixth forms and the Ministry of Education count. The additional qualification is an extension covering material that overlaps with early A Level or Diploma mathematics, and its value lies in the transition rather than in the certificate. For a student heading to A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level it is genuinely useful. For a borderline candidate on the main paper it is a misallocation of hours.

faqs.question: How many contact hours does AED 1,000 actually buy in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on format. At budget online rates of AED 33 to 65 an hour, roughly fifteen to thirty hours. At a qualified online tutor's AED 150 to 300, roughly three to seven. At specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 and above, two to five. An in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 buys the same two to five while part of the money pays for travel. Those are market figures published by the providers named and read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Do Dubai schools near us use Cambridge or Edexcel for maths?
faqs.answer: Both, and the choice is the school's rather than the family's. Schools across the Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej belt and the Al Warqa and Festival City cluster between them use Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel entries, and a school may use different boards for different subjects. Check the statement of entry for the code per subject rather than assuming a school-wide answer. Schools are named on this page as local context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: Should we trust a tutoring site that advertises a 4.9 star rating?
faqs.answer: Ask for the sample size, the date and the method, and discount the figure entirely without all three. Pages in this market publish ratings of 4.92 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page, and one shows five out of five from twenty reviews beside a student-number claim the review count cannot support. Self-asserted review markup breaches Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, carries consumer-protection exposure. We publish no rating at all.

faqs.question: Can our daughter sit a maths resit in February if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. So the resit route from a June result is the November series, with results reaching students in January. Confirm the entry route with the school early, because some schools will not enter retake candidates and a private examination centre is then needed.

faqs.question: What is the smallest useful amount of maths tutoring we could buy?
faqs.answer: A single diagnostic session plus a four-week bounded block on one topic, which for a borderline higher-tier candidate is usually circle theorems or vector proofs. That is roughly five hours in total and it targets marks that are currently scoring zero rather than marks being partly earned. Beyond that, a second block on accuracy habits at forty-five minutes twice a week for a month. Both are measurable by error count and blank count, which a parent can track without any specialist knowledge.

faqs.question: Does our school's free maths support count for anything?
faqs.answer: More than most families assume, and it should be tried first. Subject clinics and teacher support are usually included in fees, are aligned exactly with the specification your child will sit, and are run by staff who know the internal calendar and the mock dates. A parent paying for tutoring without having asked what the school provides may be buying something already included. Use paid hours for what the school cannot supply, which is sustained one-to-one attention on a single named topic.

intro.heading: Four neighbourhoods, two boards, one answer
paragraphs: Families searching for an IGCSE maths tutor in Nad Al Sheba are almost never thinking about Nad Al Sheba alone. The district sits inside a four-community block — itself, Meydan, Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City — whose schools get toured together, compared together and chosen between on a single afternoon. Children from all four end up in the same handful of schools, and parents from all four ask the same question in slightly different words.

The comparison is worth making properly because the differences are real. Nad Al Sheba holds Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba and GEMS Modern Academy inside its own boundaries, so the school run is short and a 15:30 session is genuinely available. Sobha Hartland holds Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai, with the same advantage. Mohammed Bin Rashid City has long internal roads and few exits onto Al Khail, which costs twenty minutes at pick-up before a car reaches a main road. Meydan sits between them, newer, with more families in their first UAE year and more mid-course arrivals.

Where the four communities genuinely differ is the board their children sit. Dubai licenses seventeen curricula and UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of the emirate's 387,441 private-school students, but UK curriculum does not mean one board. Some schools in this block enter students for Cambridge International IGCSE, others for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a few split by subject. For maths that distinction decides the papers, the tier labels, the grade scale and whether a calculator is allowed at all.

That is the comparison that matters, and it is not geographic. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 sets a non-calculator paper at both tiers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, allows a calculator on both of its papers. A student who has spent two years on 4MA1 and is then shown a Cambridge non-calculator past paper looks much weaker than they are, and a tutor who does not know which board the child sits will spend the first month solving the wrong problem.

So the answer to the geographic question is that it does not matter much, and the answer to the board question is that it matters enormously. IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The effect for all four communities is the same: the tutor is chosen for knowing 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher rather than for living on the right side of Dubai-Al Ain Road.

A note on what to bring to the first conversation. A report card tells you the size of a problem; a marked script tells you its shape. Parents across these four communities who send the most recent piece of marked maths work get a straight answer in one session about whether the issue is algebraic fluency, a missing mechanical topic like circle theorems, or simply never writing down enough method for a marker to award partial credit. Those three need completely different purchases.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.programmesIntro: Four stages decide an IGCSE maths outcome, and two of them happen before Year 10 begins. For a family comparing schools across Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and Sobha Hartland, the stage that matters most is the options decision, because it is taken inside whichever school they chose.

programmes.name: The Year 9 options decision
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE maths route is effectively set. Schools decide, or advise, on tier placement and on whether a student takes Additional Mathematics alongside. A student placed provisionally in a lower tier in Year 9 and never reviewed is the most common avoidable outcome in this subject, because placement made on Year 8 data gets treated as permanent.
programmes.countryNote: Across the Nad Al Sheba block this decision happens in schools with different boards, so two neighbours in Year 9 can be choosing between genuinely different qualifications. Ask the school which board it enters for and whether tier placement is reviewed, and when. A review date is a reasonable thing to request and it costs the school nothing to give.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Two tiers. Core sits Papers 1 and 3; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4, each tier with one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper, split evenly. The non-calculator paper is the part most students under-prepare, because homework is almost always done with a calculator to hand. Grade ceilings differ by tier, so the entry decision sets the maximum before any revision begins.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone. The dates governing a Nad Al Sheba student are the ones their own school's exams officer issues, not a generic timetable found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two papers of two hours each, weighted 50% apiece, with a calculator permitted on both. Foundation tier reports grades 5 to 1; Higher tier reports 9 to 4 with a safety net at 3. Because both papers allow a calculator, the demands sit in algebraic fluency and in problem-solving over several steps rather than in mental arithmetic.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Link the live official timetable rather than relying on restated dates.

programmes.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
programmes.description: Taken alongside the main qualification by students heading for A Level Mathematics or a Higher Level IB maths course. It front-loads calculus and advanced trigonometry, which means a student arriving in Year 12 has already met the first term's content. It is the single most useful optional subject for either exit from Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools across the Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland block offer both A Level and the IB Diploma after Year 11, which turns Additional Mathematics from a nice-to-have into a route decision. A student who knows by the January of Year 11 which exit they want can choose accordingly; one who waits until results day cannot.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.subjectsIntro: IGCSE maths is one subject with two boards, two tiers and a short list of topics that decide most grades. Below are the strands and adjacent courses Nad Al Sheba students bring, described by where the marks actually go rather than by what the topic covers.

subjects.name: Algebra and manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. The highest-value strand on every paper and the one where a sign error early in a long manipulation costs every mark downstream rather than one. On Cambridge non-calculator papers this is where fluency separates grades; on Pearson it is where multi-step problems begin.

subjects.name: Number and accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, bounds, percentages, ratio and rounding. Marks go missing on accuracy instructions ignored — an answer given to two decimal places when three significant figures were asked for is a wrong answer. Upper and lower bound questions are reliably available and reliably skipped.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, transformations and reading information off a curve. Students lose marks by solving algebraically when the question said use the graph, or sketching without marking intercepts and turning points. Gradient-from-a-tangent questions are the common Extended and Higher tier gap.

subjects.name: Geometry and mensuration
subjects.description: Angle rules, circle theorems, area, volume and similar shapes. Circle theorems are learnable in a fortnight and worth several marks on most papers, which makes them the best return available for a short block of work. Reasons must be stated, not implied; an unnamed theorem loses the reasoning mark.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled triangles at every tier, with sine and cosine rules and 3D work at the higher tiers. Calculator mode is the quiet killer: a correct method in the wrong angle mode gives a confident wrong answer. Bearings questions reward a drawn diagram before any calculation begins.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms and tree diagrams. Histograms with unequal class widths are the single most skipped topic in this strand, and they are mechanical once practised. Probability losses come from not reading whether replacement occurs.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry and the four transformations with full descriptions. Transformation questions award marks for naming the transformation and giving every required parameter, so a correct drawing with a missing centre of rotation still loses. Vector proof questions reward writing the route rather than guessing.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Core
subjects.description: Two papers, one without a calculator and one with, weighted evenly, with a grade ceiling below the top grades. The right entry for a student who will otherwise meet questions they cannot start, and a secure Core grade is frequently worth more than a scraped Extended one for post-16 routes that do not need maths.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Extended
subjects.description: Two longer papers, again split between non-calculator and calculator, covering the core syllabus plus the extended content — roughly a term of additional material. Required for A Level Mathematics and for Higher Level IB maths, so the entry decision should follow the post-16 plan rather than lead it.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MA1 Foundation
subjects.description: Two two-hour papers, calculator permitted on both, reporting grades 5 to 1. Because the calculator is always available, the preparation concentrates on reading multi-step questions accurately and on showing method so partial credit lands, rather than on mental fluency.

subjects.name: Pearson 4MA1 Higher
subjects.description: Two two-hour papers, calculator permitted on both, reporting grades 9 to 4 with a safety net at 3. The step up from Foundation is algebraic: functions, iterative methods, more demanding geometry and proof. Time management across two full-length papers is the recurring issue rather than content.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.levels: Extended or Higher tier students only
subjects.description: Calculus, advanced trigonometry, logarithms and further algebra taken alongside the main qualification. The best preparation available for A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, and the subject where a tutor's level specificity matters most because it is taught by fewer teachers and timetabled thinly.

sections.heading: Nad Al Sheba against the three communities next door
paragraphs: Parents comparing these four communities are usually comparing schools, commutes and villa sizes. For tutoring the comparison reduces to two things: what time a session can start on a weekday, and which exam board the child's school enters them with. Everything else about the four is the same from a tutoring point of view, which is a more useful finding than a longer list of differences would be.

On timing, the split is clean. Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland have schools inside their own boundaries, so a child can be home and ready by 15:30 and a maths session can land in the window where concentration is still available. Mohammed Bin Rashid City loses time inside its own road network before a car reaches Al Khail, and Meydan sits between the two depending on which school. Al Quoz families travel furthest and consistently start latest.

On boards, there is no geographic pattern at all, which is exactly why the comparison people make is the wrong one. Schools within walking distance of each other enter students for different boards, and a few split by subject. The practical rule for any family in this block is to ask the school for the syllabus code before hiring anybody, because 0580 and 4MA1 need different preparation even though both are called IGCSE maths.

The reason the answer comes out the same across all four is that online delivery removes the only variable geography controls. A tutor who has to drive is constrained by the roads; a tutor on video is not. So a Mohammed Bin Rashid City family gets the same 16:00 slot as a Sobha Hartland family, and both get a tutor matched to the board and tier rather than to the drive.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1
paragraphs: This is the comparison that actually changes what a tutor does, and almost nobody in this market publishes it. Both qualifications are called IGCSE maths, both are taken in Years 10 and 11, and both are accepted everywhere a UK-curriculum qualification is accepted. Underneath that they are different exams with different paper structures, different tier names and different grade scales.

Cambridge Mathematics 0580 runs two tiers, Core and Extended, and each tier sits two papers split evenly between a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper. Core sits Papers 1 and 3; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4, which are longer. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, runs Foundation and Higher tiers over two two-hour papers weighted 50% each, with a calculator permitted on both.

The non-calculator difference is the one that shows up in a first session. A 4MA1 student has never been examined without a calculator and does not need to be. A 0580 student has half their marks riding on a paper where one is not allowed, and almost all of their homework has been done with one to hand. Give the same student both papers and they will look like two different candidates, which is why a tutor who starts by asking for the code is doing the one thing that matters most.

The grade scales differ as well, and parents comparing results across the block should know it. Cambridge 0580 reports letter grades with different ranges by tier. Pearson 4MA1 reports numbers, with Foundation covering 5 to 1 and Higher covering 9 to 4 plus a safety net at 3. A grade 7 on 4MA1 and an A on 0580 are not the same label, and comparing children across two schools using the wrong scale produces a conversation nobody needed to have.

sections.heading: The topics that pay for themselves in four sessions
paragraphs: Not all IGCSE maths topics are worth the same per hour of tutoring, and the difference is large enough to plan around. Some strands are conceptually demanding and take a term to secure. Others are mechanical: learnable in a fortnight, worth several marks on almost every paper, and skipped by a large share of candidates because they look harder than they are.

The mechanical ones are where a short block of tutoring produces visible movement. Circle theorems are the clearest example — a fixed set of rules, a requirement to name the reason, and marks available on most papers at the higher tiers. Histograms with unequal class widths are another: one idea, applied the same way every time, routinely left blank. Upper and lower bounds, transformations with complete descriptions, and standard-form arithmetic all behave the same way.

The strategy that follows is unglamorous and works. Take the student's most recent marked script, identify which of these mechanical strands cost marks, and buy three or four sessions on each in turn rather than a general weekly hour. The alternative — a weekly session that moves through the textbook in order — spends most of its time on topics the student already has, because the textbook does not know what they got wrong.

The table below is a starting map rather than a prescription. The right list for any individual student comes from their own script, which is also why the first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. Where a strand is strong already, leaving it alone is the correct decision and saying so is part of the job.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: Set the hourly rates side by side and the most interesting number in the Dubai market is not the top or the bottom. It is the gap between an online qualified tutor and an in-home one: roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour. That gap is the price of a car journey, and it is worth asking what it actually delivers before paying it across a two-year IGCSE course.

It buys three things honestly. A parent can see the session happening. A child cannot quietly open another browser tab. And a tutor in the room notices drift faster than one on a screen. Those are real and they matter more for a thirteen-year-old than for a sixteen-year-old. What the premium does not buy is subject depth: it is paid for proximity, and proximity is not correlated with having marked a 0580 Extended Paper 4 before.

The published figures, read in October 2026, put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table giving 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500. Online qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150, EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and the premium end reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

Across the four communities on this page the premium behaves differently in one respect only. Mohammed Bin Rashid City and Al Quoz are harder to reach at pick-up, so a travelling tutor there either charges more or starts later. Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland are easy to reach, so the premium there is paid for convenience rather than difficulty. Either way the arithmetic across two years of weekly sessions runs to several thousand dirhams, which is a term of specialist support in itself.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, the freeze and a year of maths
paragraphs: A tutoring budget makes more sense beside the other education costs a Nad Al Sheba family already carries than it does on its own. The useful anchor is public: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion out of AED 2.5 billion in total.

That freeze matters for a tutoring decision in a specific way. A family that had budgeted for a fee increase and did not get one has headroom that did not exist a year earlier, and the most common use of it in this corridor is one subject of weekly support in an examined year. It is worth being deliberate about that rather than letting it drift, because a weekly hour bought without a diagnosis is the easiest money to waste in this market.

Set against that, the market's monthly figures are modest for one subject and substantial for three. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen elsewhere include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The context also includes capacity, which affects fees over time. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More UK-curriculum places across the emirate means more IGCSE candidates, which is worth knowing when a school tells a parent that a tier decision is set by class sizes.

sections.heading: One-to-one, a group class or a tuition centre
paragraphs: Comparing formats honestly means comparing models rather than brands, and the models behave differently for maths than for essay subjects. A group class moves at one pace through one sequence, which suits a student whose gaps match the group's and penalises one whose gaps do not. In maths, where a single missing idea blocks everything built on it, that mismatch is expensive.

A tuition centre adds structure, a fixed timetable and often a room full of peers, which some students genuinely need. It also adds a commute at the end of a school day, and in this corridor that commute lands in the same traffic that makes a travelling tutor arrive late. For a Mohammed Bin Rashid City family, a centre in Al Quoz is a forty-minute round trip attached to every session.

One-to-one, whatever the delivery, buys the thing maths specifically needs: a tutor watching the student's own working and intervening at the exact line where it goes wrong. That is not available in a group of eight, however good the teacher. What one-to-one does not buy is peer pressure, which for some students is the only thing that produces practice between sessions.

The comparison table below compares models rather than companies, and quotes a competitor figure only where that competitor published it. One thing worth saying plainly about every option: nobody in this market should be promising a grade, and the researched set contains providers who publish self-asserted ratings and contradictory price claims on the same page. A provider whose figures contradict each other across two sections of its own site is telling you something about its record-keeping.

sections.heading: Method marks, and why showing working is worth a grade
paragraphs: The single cheapest grade improvement available in IGCSE maths has nothing to do with knowing more maths. It is the discipline of writing down enough working that a marker can award partial credit when the final answer is wrong. Students who work in their heads and write one line are throwing away marks they have already earned.

Mark schemes award method marks explicitly. A question worth four marks typically carries two or three for method and one or two for accuracy, which means a student who sets the problem up correctly and then slips on the arithmetic can still take most of the marks — but only if the setup is visible on the page. In an eight-mark multi-step question, invisible working converts a near-miss into a zero.

Teaching this is a matter of habit rather than understanding, and habits need enforcing in practice rather than explaining once. The drill is to mark the student's own work against the official scheme with them watching, awarding marks strictly, and letting them see a correct method score nothing because it was never written. That lesson lands once and holds. On a shared screen it is more effective than on paper, because the scheme and the working sit side by side.

Board materials for this come from the school's licensed access or the board's own platform. We do not host, reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides; they are copyright, some of it unreleased. Reference the official sources at cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com and work from the copies the school or the board provides.

sections.heading: After Year 11: how the maths tier decides the exit
paragraphs: In this block of communities the Year 11 exit is a genuine fork, because several schools offer both A Level and the IB Diploma. The maths tier taken at IGCSE constrains that fork more than parents expect, and the constraint is usually discovered after the entry deadline has closed rather than before.

A Level Mathematics assumes the content of the higher tier, and so does Higher Level IB maths on either course. A student entered for Cambridge Core or Pearson Foundation has not met the algebra that the first term of either post-16 route takes for granted. That does not close every door — plenty of excellent degrees need no maths beyond the basics — but it closes the engineering and mathematics doors, and it is better to close them deliberately than by default.

The reverse error is also common: a student pushed into Extended or Higher tier who will struggle to score at all, when a secure Core or Foundation grade would have cleared the floor they actually need. That floor is worth naming. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five.

The honest way to decide is evidence rather than ambition. Sit the student a past paper from the higher tier under timed conditions in Year 10 and mark it against the official scheme. If they reach the lower boundaries of that tier, enter them for it, because the ceiling is worth more than the comfort. If they are far below, the question becomes whether eight months of focused work closes that distance — a judgement a specialist can make from a script and a parent cannot make from a report card.

sections.heading: What a parent can check in twenty minutes
paragraphs: Everything above comes down to a short list of things any parent in these four communities can verify before paying anybody, and most of them take minutes. The reason to run the list is that the researched competitor set in this market contains pages with contradictory prices, self-asserted ratings, unparseable structured data and, in one case, a school listed that appears not to exist.

First, ask for the syllabus code and tier and see whether the tutor asks for it back. A tutor who accepts 'IGCSE maths' as a brief has told you they will work it out later, at your expense. Second, ask them to talk through where marks are lost on the specific paper your child sits. A specialist answers in method marks and command wording; a generalist answers in topics.

Third, check the permit position. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone who tells you the permit is costly or optional is misinformed. MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Fourth, be sceptical of credentials borrowed from institutions. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises and has a number that can be shown. Fifth, use the free trial lesson. Twenty minutes of watching somebody mark a paper tells you more than any page, this one included.

process.description: The useful opening message names the board and syllabus code, the tier, the school and the year group, and attaches or describes the most recent marked piece of work. A script shows the shape of the problem; a grade only shows its size. That difference decides whether the next term should be algebra, technique or a short topic block.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson

For a Cambridge student that section is usually from the non-calculator paper, because that is where the hidden gap sits. You get a written note naming the dominant pattern. No payment is involved in this lesson.

process.title: Pick the format to match the gap
process.description: A diagnosed mechanical gap gets a short topic block of three or four sessions and then stops. A broad weakness in algebra gets a weekly session across a term. The wrong purchase is a general weekly hour bought to cover an undiagnosed problem, which spends most of its time on topics the student already has.

process.title: Weekly sessions on the student's own tier
process.description: Practice is always on the tier the student is entered for, with notes naming the topic, what was set, and which paper section comes next. Extended practice given to a Core candidate demoralises them, and Core practice leaves an Extended candidate unready for the back half of the longer paper.

process.title: Rebuild on the mock scripts
process.description: When mocks return, the plan is rewritten rather than continued. Every lost mark is sorted into content, method not shown, arithmetic slip or ran out of time, and the dominant category becomes the work for a fixed fortnight. A list of topics being abandoned is written and shown to the student.

faqs.question: Does it matter that we are in Nad Al Sheba rather than Meydan or Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: For tutoring, barely. The four communities differ in commute and in which schools sit inside their boundaries, which changes what time a weekday session can start — 15:30 in Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland, closer to 17:00 in Mohammed Bin Rashid City. They do not differ in what the children need. Because lessons run one-to-one over live video rather than by home visit, the road network stops being a factor at all, and the tutor is chosen for knowing the board and tier your child sits.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer or the head of maths for the syllabus code, not just the board name. You are looking for something like 0580 for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics or 4MA1 for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, plus the tier. Some schools in this block enter students for different boards in different subjects, so the answer for maths may not be the answer for science. It takes one email and it changes what a term of tutoring should contain.

faqs.question: Why does my child find past papers much harder than schoolwork?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge 0580 the usual reason is the non-calculator paper: half the marks at each tier sit on a paper where no calculator is allowed, and almost all homework is done with one to hand. The student can set up a problem and cannot finish it by hand. On Pearson 4MA1, where both papers allow a calculator, the more common reason is multi-step problem wording. Identifying which of the two applies is the first session's job, and it needs the actual paper rather than a report.

faqs.question: What grades can each tier actually reach?
faqs.answer: Cambridge 0580 reports letter grades with different ranges by tier: Core cannot reach the top grades and Extended covers the full range. Pearson 4MA1 reports numbers, Foundation covering 5 to 1 and Higher covering 9 to 4 with a safety net at 3. Comparing a grade 7 on one board with an A on the other is comparing different scales. Whichever board applies, the tier sets the ceiling before any revision starts, which is why the entry decision deserves evidence.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics give the quickest improvement?
faqs.answer: The mechanical ones, which are routinely skipped because they look harder than they are. Circle theorems take three or four sessions and appear on most higher-tier papers. Histograms with unequal class widths are one idea applied identically every time and are frequently left blank. Upper and lower bounds, complete transformation descriptions and standard-form arithmetic behave the same way. Algebraic fractions do not — those need a term rather than a block, and promising otherwise would be dishonest.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the group's gaps match your child's. A group moves at one pace through one sequence, which works when the student's weaknesses are the common ones and fails when a single missing idea is blocking everything built on it. Centres also add a commute at the end of a school day, which in this corridor lands in the same traffic that delays a travelling tutor. For a diagnosed specific gap, one-to-one is the format that can intervene at the exact line where the working breaks.

faqs.question: How much is the travel premium for an in-home maths tutor here?
faqs.answer: Roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour above the equivalent online rate, based on figures read in October 2026. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate's Dubai table giving 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500, while a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300. Across two years of weekly sessions that gap adds up to several thousand dirhams. It buys presence and a fixed slot; it does not buy board-specific marking experience.

faqs.question: Does my child need Extended or Higher tier for A Level Maths?
faqs.answer: Yes in practice. A Level Mathematics assumes the content of the higher tier, and so does Higher Level IB maths on either course. A student entered for Cambridge Core or Pearson Foundation has not met the algebra that the first term of either route takes for granted. That closes the engineering and mathematics doors rather than all doors, and the right time to decide is before the entry deadline, using a timed higher-tier paper marked against the official scheme as the evidence.

faqs.question: How do we know whether a maths tutor is any good before paying?
faqs.answer: Give them the syllabus code and tier and see whether they ask for it back, then ask them to describe where marks are lost on that specific paper. A specialist answers in method marks and command wording; a generalist answers in topic names. Then use the free trial lesson and watch them mark a past-paper section against the official scheme. Twenty minutes of that tells you more than any website, including this one. No tutor should be promising a grade.

faqs.question: Can my child retake IGCSE maths if the summer grade is disappointing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both Cambridge and Pearson run a November series available to UAE candidates, and that is the standard resit route. The February-March Cambridge route is offered to India only and does not apply here. Before committing, request the script rather than just the grade: if the losses were timing and method presentation, a short block before November is a realistic target. If whole topics were missing, the following June is usually the honest answer and a tutor should say so.

faqs.question: Why does showing working matter so much in the mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Because most multi-mark questions award more for method than for the final answer. A four-mark question typically carries two or three method marks and one or two accuracy marks, so a correct setup followed by an arithmetic slip still scores — if the setup is visible. Students who work in their heads and write one line convert near-misses into zeros. The fix is habit rather than understanding: mark their own script strictly against the official scheme while they watch.

faqs.question: Do you provide the Cambridge or Pearson papers to work from?
faqs.answer: No. Board materials are copyright, some of it unreleased, so we do not host, reproduce or distribute papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Your school holds licensed access, and both boards publish material through their own platforms at cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. Sessions work from the copies your school or the board provides, and the time goes on marking against the official scheme rather than on hunting for documents.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking alongside the main qualification?
faqs.answer: For a student heading towards A Level Mathematics or Higher Level IB maths, it is the most useful optional subject available. It front-loads calculus, logarithms and advanced trigonometry, so the first term of either post-16 route is partly covered before it starts. For a student who will not take maths beyond Year 11 it adds load for no return. The deciding question is the post-16 exit, which in this block of schools is often a genuine choice between A Level and the Diploma.

faqs.question: What happens to our school fees and does that change the tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For families who had budgeted for an increase, that creates headroom, and the most common use of it in this corridor is one subject of weekly support in an examined year. Worth spending deliberately on a diagnosed gap rather than letting it drift into a general weekly hour.

faqs.question: Are private tutors in the UAE required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around the school run from Mohammed Bin Rashid City?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the clearest practical difference between the formats. District One's internal roads and single exit onto Al Khail can absorb twenty minutes before a car reaches a main road, so a travelling tutor cannot realistically hold a 16:00 slot there. A video session can, because nothing has to arrive. Families in Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland have schools inside their boundaries and can take 15:30; Al Quoz families usually start after 17:00 whatever the format.

intro.heading: Two years, two different weeks, one mathematics course
paragraphs: The mistake most families in this district make with IGCSE mathematics is treating it as one two-year block to be supported at a constant rate. It is not. Year 10 and Year 11 are different weeks with different pressures, and the hour that works in the first is often the wrong hour in the second. A plan built for Year 10 and left running into Year 11 drifts into exactly the pattern that produces a disappointing grade after two years of paid sessions.

Year 10 in the Oud Metha school belt is comparatively roomy. The teaching day ends mid-afternoon, the commute home to Karama, Al Mankhool or Bur Dubai is short, and the evening has space in it. Content is still arriving, nothing is being revised yet, and the student has no marked past paper to learn from. The useful work in that year is building algebraic fluency and establishing the habit of writing method, because method marks are the single largest recoverable loss in IGCSE mathematics and the habit takes a year to form.

Year 11 is a different animal. Mocks land, usually twice. Coursework and controlled assessment in other subjects consume evenings. The school adds revision clinics, which eat precisely the weekday slots a family had been using. And the student starts sitting full papers under time, which exposes a problem that was invisible in Year 10: they know the mathematics and cannot finish the paper. That is a timing failure, not a content gap, and it needs a different kind of session.

There is a constraint in Dubai specifically that a generic plan ignores. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated by KHDA on a forty-minute lesson unit. Those periods are inside the school day, pressing against mathematics teaching time rather than sitting outside it. The week a parent imagines, with long open afternoons, is not the week the school timetable actually produces.

One more thing shapes the plan in this particular belt. A large share of students here move campus at sixteen, because the schools on the Oud Metha Road run to IGCSE while much of the local Diploma and A Level provision sits further out in Al Jaddaf, Al Garhoud or Nad Al Sheba. That means the mathematics grade a student leaves Year 11 with is also an admissions document, and the subjects the next school expects are set by somebody the family has not met yet. It is worth asking the receiving school what it wants to see before deciding whether Additional Mathematics 0606 is a luxury or a requirement.

So the structure here follows the two years rather than the subject. What a Year 10 week has room for and what a Year 11 week does not. How to audit a weekday honestly before booking an hour. Which board your child is sitting, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different calculator rules. How the non-calculator paper fails students who revise comfortably. What the three weeks around a mock are for. And when a November resit is a sensible plan rather than a panic.

Year 11 work: full timed papers, error-pattern analysis and paper-by-paper timing

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: Four qualification routes run through the schools in and around Oud Metha, and mathematics sits differently in each. The code on the entry statement matters more than the subject name, because the papers and the calculator rules are not the same.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The most widely sat mathematics course in this belt, tiered into Core and Extended. Extended carries the algebra, functions, trigonometry and probability that post-sixteen courses assume. The Core tier caps the available grade, which is the single most consequential fact in a family's planning and the one least often discussed at a parents' evening.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For an Oud Metha family that means dates come from the school's entry statement, not from a search result.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: The other board sat widely in Dubai, tiered Foundation and Higher with two papers at each tier. The question style differs from Cambridge enough that past-paper technique does not transfer cleanly, and a tutor working from the wrong board's papers will look convincing for about six weeks before a mock exposes it.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - a gap worth knowing if a December university or school deadline is in play. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: The variant some IB continuum schools prefer, tiered Core and Extended, with a stronger emphasis on graphical calculator use and on investigation. It is not interchangeable with 0580 and the past papers are separate. Families sometimes discover the difference only when a tutor arrives with the wrong paper set.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school near Oud Metha runs the IB Middle Years Programme into a sixteen-plus qualification, 0607 is the one that most often appears. It also prepares the calculator habits that Diploma Applications and Interpretation assumes, so for a student heading that way it is a reasonable fit rather than an inconvenience.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: An additional course taken alongside 0580 Extended by students aiming at Higher Level Mathematics, A Level Mathematics or engineering. It introduces calculus, logarithms and matrices before Year 12. It is demanding and it is optional, and it is the best predictor of a comfortable start in a post-sixteen mathematics course.
programmes.countryNote: In this belt, where many students move to a different campus for the Diploma or A Level, 0606 is the cheapest insurance available against a difficult October in Year 12. Funding it at sixteen usually removes the need for a remedial block a year later, and the hours cost the same either way.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: The mathematics a tutor needs to know is not "IGCSE maths". It is a specific code, a specific tier and a specific paper set. These are the ones students in the Oud Metha belt actually sit, with what each one asks for.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Extended
subjects.description: The full content set and the full grade range. Algebra, functions, trigonometry, vectors and probability carry the paper. Most losses are method marks surrendered by unshown working, and the fix is a habit rather than a topic.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Core
subjects.description: A reduced content set with the grade range capped below the top. Worth confirming early, because hours spent chasing a grade the tier cannot award produce nothing, and a tier conversation with the school is free to have in Year 10.

subjects.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: Graphical calculator work and investigation feature far more heavily than in 0580, and the past papers are a separate set. A student on 0607 practising 0580 papers is practising the wrong question style for part of the course.

subjects.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, logarithms, matrices and more demanding trigonometry, taken alongside 0580 Extended. It is a genuine step up in pace, and a student who is not already secure in algebraic manipulation will struggle with it rather than be stretched by it.

subjects.name: Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1, Higher
subjects.description: Two papers, the full grade range, and a question style that builds differently from Cambridge. Students moving between schools sometimes change board mid-course, which needs explicit retraining on the new paper set rather than more content.

subjects.name: Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1, Foundation
subjects.description: The capped tier. The useful work here is accuracy and completeness: Foundation papers reward getting the available marks reliably rather than reaching for harder questions, and students lose more to carelessness than to difficulty.

subjects.name: Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: The Pearson equivalent of taking mathematics further at sixteen, with calculus and series. Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics, and the same reasoning applies as for 0606: it buys an easier Year 12.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Physics structured questions assume rearrangement, unit handling and graph interpretation that some students have not secured in mathematics yet. A handful of targeted sessions on the mathematics often lifts the physics grade more than physics teaching would.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, final years
subjects.description: Where a school runs MYP to sixteen instead of IGCSE, assessment is against four criteria on a 1-8 scale rather than by terminal papers. The support looks nothing like past-paper drilling and should not be planned as though it were.

subjects.name: Year 9 bridging into IGCSE
subjects.description: A short block before the two-year course begins, aimed at algebraic fluency. Students who arrive in Year 10 unable to manipulate expressions reliably spend the whole course paying interest on that gap, and it is far cheaper to close before the course starts.

regions.name: Bur Dubai

sections.heading: Audit the weekday before you book the hour
paragraphs: A mathematics hour fails for scheduling reasons more often than for teaching reasons, and the failure is predictable. The family picks a day that suits the parent, the school then adds a revision clinic or a fixture on that day, the session is moved twice, and by half term it has become the appointment that gets cancelled. Nobody decided to stop. The slot simply never had a weekday that was genuinely free.

The audit takes ten minutes and it needs the school's term calendar, which schools publish at the start of term. Write out the five weekdays and mark, for each, when the teaching day ends, what the school has already claimed on that day, and what the household routine does to the evening. In this belt the answer is usually that one or two weekdays are genuinely clear and the rest are contested. Book into the clear ones.

Then match the subject to the hour rather than the hour to the diary. Mathematics is sequential: a missed step blocks the rest of the question instead of merely weakening it, so it belongs in the freshest hour available. If a family is running two tutors, mathematics takes the earlier slot regardless of which subject currently looks worse on the report. And if the only available hour is late, shorten it: forty focused minutes at seven o'clock beats a drifting ninety.

sections.heading: Year 10 and Year 11 need different things bought
paragraphs: Treat the two years as one plan and you will buy the wrong thing in at least one of them. In Year 10 the content is still arriving. There is no complete syllabus to revise, no marked paper to learn from, and the student's weaknesses have not yet shown themselves under time. The work that pays in Year 10 is fluency and habit: algebraic manipulation drilled to automatic, and the discipline of writing out method on every answer rather than only on the hard ones.

That habit is worth more than any topic. In IGCSE mathematics the examiner awards method marks for a correct approach even where the final answer is wrong, and the most common loss across every tier is a student who knew what to do, did it in their head, got the arithmetic wrong, and scored zero on a question they understood. A year of writing method out properly converts that into partial credit on every paper for the rest of their life.

Year 11 is diagnostic rather than developmental. The syllabus is largely taught, mocks produce real marked scripts, and the useful hour is spent finding and repairing specific losses rather than covering ground. This is where families go wrong by continuing to buy topic teaching: the student sits through an explanation of a topic they already understand, feels reassured, and goes into the exam still unable to finish the paper. The problem was never the topic.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson, and the calculator question
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE mathematics in Dubai and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended. Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics is a separate course with its own papers and a heavier graphical-calculator emphasis. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher with its own question style. A tutor who has taught one of these well will still misdirect a student sitting another, because the shape of the questions differs and past-paper practice is most of the final-year work.

The calculator position is where this bites hardest and where parents are least often told anything. Each board specifies which papers permit a calculator and which do not, and the non-calculator paper is a different skill rather than the same skill without a tool. A student who has done all their practice with a calculator to hand has not practised the paper they will sit. They will know the mathematics, run out of time, and lose accuracy marks on arithmetic they can do perfectly well when unhurried.

The fix is simple and almost never done: practise the non-calculator paper separately, under time, from early in Year 11. Twenty minutes of mental and written arithmetic a week, with a clock, changes the outcome more than another hour of topic teaching. It is also the kind of work a student will not do unsupervised, because it is uncomfortable and produces no feeling of progress until it suddenly does.

sections.heading: The three weeks around a mock are the most valuable in the course
paragraphs: Mocks are the only point before the real series where a student in this belt produces a marked script under genuine time pressure, and most families waste them. The script comes home, the grade is discussed, the paper goes in a drawer, and the next session covers whatever topic was next in the syllabus. The single most valuable document in the whole two years has just been filed.

The week before a mock should not contain new content. It should contain one full paper under time, marked honestly, so that the mock is not the first time the student has met the clock. The week of the mock should contain nothing at all beyond light review, because a tired student mocks badly and the mock's value lies in it being a fair reading.

The two weeks after are the ones that matter. Take the marked script and sort every lost mark into four categories: content not known, method not shown, question misread, and time mismanaged. Count them. In most scripts from this belt the first category is the smallest, and families have been buying sessions aimed at it exclusively. The other three are faster to fix and the repair is specific: this type of question, this command word, this point in the paper where the minutes disappeared.

Then rebuild the plan from that count rather than from the syllabus order. It is the difference between a Year 11 that improves and a Year 11 that repeats Year 10 with more anxiety. Ask the school for the mock dates at the start of term so the block can be built around them rather than discovered a week out.
