sections.heading: Where the marks actually go in an IGCSE mathematics paper
paragraphs: Lost marks in IGCSE mathematics cluster in places that have very little to do with how hard the mathematics is. The largest single group is unshown method. A question worth four marks typically awards two or three for a correct approach, and a student who works in their head and writes only an answer forfeits all of them on a slip. Across a full paper this routinely accounts for more marks than any topic weakness.

The second group is the command verb. Work out, calculate, show that, prove, explain and give a reason each demand a different response, and a student who answers the wrong one competently still scores badly. Show that in particular catches students out: it requires working toward a stated result, and an answer that simply asserts the result earns nothing.

The third is accuracy and rounding. Papers specify how answers should be given, and marks are lost for premature rounding in the middle of a multi-step calculation. This is pure discipline and entirely teachable, and it is almost never taught because it is not a topic.

The fourth is the clock. Students in this belt frequently reach the end of a paper with questions unattempted that they could have answered, because they over-invested in one hard question early. A full timed paper plus an honest audit of where the minutes went fixes this faster than any amount of content work. Taken together, these four account for most of the gap between what a student knows and what their grade says.

sections.heading: The June series, the November series, and when a resit makes sense
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Those two series are the UAE candidate's calendar, and the practical consequence is that one subject going wrong in the summer is recoverable in the autumn rather than catastrophic.

A warning worth repeating, because a great deal of UAE tutoring content gets it wrong: the Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. Any plan that has a student in Oud Metha revising toward a February or March examination window is working from the wrong country's calendar. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of exams in every series, which is why a resit has to be decided early rather than when the results arrive.

The second thing to know about a November resit is the results gap. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit is not a quick fix if a school or university deadline falls in December. The June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are backward-looking figures and are useful precisely because they show the shape of the gap.

Cambridge's own administrative point belongs in any planning conversation. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Take the dates from the school's entry statement and the board's live timetable, and link rather than restate them.

sections.heading: What an hour costs in this market, and what the clock in it is worth
paragraphs: Published rates across Dubai span an order of magnitude. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026, puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one including travel at AED 180 to 350, specialist IB and IGCSE provision at AED 200 to 450 or more, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. None of these is an IB Gram price; each belongs to the provider named.

What those figures do not tell you is what an hour is worth at different times of day, and in this district that is the live variable. An hour of non-calculator practice at half past three with a rested student produces measurable improvement. The same hour at eight o'clock, after three hours of homework, produces a session that happened. Both cost the same. The most expensive mathematics tuition in Oud Metha is a cheap hour in the wrong slot, repeated for a term.

Monthly figures are easier to compare than hourly ones. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages in the same market are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, roughly AED 200 to 225 for the same eight hours. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 for budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions for Oud Metha students run one-to-one over live video, which removes the travel premium and, more usefully here, removes the fixed arrival window that makes an in-home slot impossible to move in the fortnight around a mock.

sections.heading: The mandatory block, the regulator and what you can check yourself
paragraphs: Any plan for a Dubai IGCSE week has to account for a block of periods that is not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

KHDA is specific on organisation too. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That last point constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer in those subjects.

On the regulator: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and its inspection reports are published on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Read your own school's. If it names mathematics attainment as a strength, the school may already be providing what you were about to buy, and the money is better spent on timing and technique. Elsewhere in the country, ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

One check a parent can make before paying anyone: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it is free, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee. Operating without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no regulator approval and has no UAE office; we explain what these bodies do and link their own pages.

process.title: Send the entry statement and the term calendar
process.description: Two documents the school already has. The entry statement gives the board, code and tier, so the match is exact. The term calendar shows which weekdays are already claimed by clinics, fixtures and mocks, so the hour is booked into a day that will still be free in November.

process.title: Free trial lesson at the time you mean to keep
process.description: Take it in the slot you intend to book permanently rather than whenever is convenient this week. A mid-afternoon session and an eight o'clock session are different products, and the trial is the cheap way to find out which one this student can actually work in.

process.title: One marked script, read properly
process.description: Bring the most recent marked mathematics work, however poor. A tutor learns more from a marked script in five minutes than from a report comment in an hour, because the script shows whether the losses are content, method, misreading or timing.

process.title: The plan is sized by the diagnosis
process.description: After the trial you get the four-way split of where marks are going and a plan whose length follows from it. In Year 10 that is usually a term of fluency work. In Year 11 it is usually shorter and narrower than parents expect, because technique moves faster than content.

process.title: Review against school marks, and change course if needed
process.description: Progress is judged against the school's own assessments and mocks, not against how sessions feel. If the marks have not moved across a block, the plan changes or the tutor does. We would rather say that than sell another term on the strength of a comfortable hour.

whyPoints.title: Planned around the real weekday
whyPoints.description: The session is booked into a weekday the school has not already claimed, at the earliest hour your child is genuinely home and alert. In this district that hour exists and almost nobody uses it, which is why so much local tuition underperforms for scheduling reasons.

whyPoints.title: The exact code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: 0580 Extended, 0607, 0606, 4MA1 Higher and 4PM1 are different courses with different papers and different calculator rules. We match on what the entry statement says, because a tutor on the wrong board looks convincing until the first mock.

whyPoints.title: Non-calculator practice treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: Most students practise everything with a calculator to hand and then sit a paper without one. A short weekly block of timed written arithmetic changes more marks than another hour of topic teaching, and no student does it unsupervised.

whyPoints.title: Mocks used, not filed
whyPoints.description: The marked mock script is the most valuable document in the two years. We sort every lost mark into content, method, misreading and timing, count them, and build the next sessions from the count rather than from the syllabus order.

whyPoints.title: A slot that can move when the term tightens
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a session can shift inside the same week when a school adds a mock or a clinic. A fixed in-home arrival window is the hardest thing in a Year 11 week to move, and it needs moving most in the fortnight that matters.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, claims limited to what we can show
whyPoints.description: Every dirham band here belongs to the provider that published it, with the month it was read. No regulator approval, no UAE office, no grade guarantees, and no statistic without a source. Ask any provider claiming more to evidence it.

faqs.question: When in the week should an IGCSE maths session actually sit for a student in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: In the earliest hour your child is genuinely home and alert, on a weekday the school has not already claimed. Students at the Oud Metha Road campuses can be working mid-afternoon, which is the strongest window for anything sequential. Before booking, get the school's term calendar and mark which weekdays carry revision clinics, fixtures or supervision meetings - those are the days a session will be cancelled on. One or two weekdays in this belt are usually genuinely clear, and the hour belongs in those.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 too early to start maths tutoring, or Year 11 too late?
faqs.answer: Neither, but they need different things bought. Year 10 work is algebraic fluency and the habit of writing out method, built while there is still time for a habit to form; past-paper drilling in Year 10 tests content the student has not been taught. Year 11 work is timed papers, honest marking and repair of the specific losses a marked script reveals. Buying Year 11's product in Year 10 demoralises; buying Year 10's product in Year 11 reassures without moving the grade. Match the purchase to the year.

faqs.question: My child understands the maths but runs out of time in the paper. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: A full paper under genuine time conditions, followed by an audit of where the minutes went rather than only where the marks went. Students in this belt commonly over-invest in one hard question early and leave easier marks unattempted at the end. The repair is a paper strategy: a rule for how long a question gets before moving on, and practice abandoning and returning. It is quick to teach and almost never taught, because it is not a topic and therefore does not feel like teaching.

faqs.question: How much difference does writing out method actually make to an IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: More than any single topic. A four-mark question typically awards two or three marks for a correct approach, so a student who works in their head, writes only an answer and makes one arithmetic slip scores zero on a question they understood. Across a full paper this routinely accounts for more lost marks than any content weakness. It is a habit rather than knowledge, which is why it has to be built across Year 10 rather than installed in the spring of Year 11.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child sits Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Enough that it should be the first thing you establish. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics is a separate course with heavier graphical-calculator work, and Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher with a distinct question-building style. Past-paper practice is most of the final-year work, so a tutor using the wrong board's papers is training the wrong question shape. Get the board, code and tier from the school's entry statement before paying for a single hour.

faqs.question: How should we prepare for the non-calculator paper specifically?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a separate skill and timetable it separately. Most students do all their practice with a calculator to hand and then sit a paper without one, so they know the mathematics, lose accuracy under time and run short. Twenty minutes a week of timed written and mental arithmetic, from early in Year 11, changes the result more than another hour of topic teaching. No student does this unsupervised, because it is uncomfortable and shows no progress until it suddenly does. Build it into the weekly hour.

faqs.question: What should we do with my child's marked mock paper?
faqs.answer: Not file it. Sort every lost mark into four categories - content not known, method not shown, question misread, time mismanaged - and count them. In most scripts the content category is the smallest, which is awkward, because it is the one families have been paying to address. Then build the next six sessions from the count rather than from the syllabus order. The week before a mock should hold one timed paper and no new content, and the week of the mock should hold almost nothing, so the result is a fair reading.

faqs.question: Can the Core tier limit the grade even if we buy plenty of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that makes the tier the most load-bearing fact in the plan. Cambridge 0580 is tiered Core and Extended, Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher, and the lower tier caps the available grade regardless of how many hours are bought. The conversation with the school is free to have and should happen in Year 10, when a change is still practical. One or two diagnostic sessions on past papers from each tier will tell you which one the student is genuinely working at, which is better evidence than a report comment.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking on top of 0580 Extended?
faqs.answer: For a student heading toward A Level Mathematics, Higher Level Mathematics or engineering, usually yes - and it is the cheapest insurance available against a difficult first term in Year 12. It introduces calculus, logarithms and matrices before the post-sixteen course assumes them. The caveat is pace: a student not already secure in algebraic manipulation will find 0606 a struggle rather than a stretch. Secure the 0580 Extended algebra first, then add it, rather than running both from an unsteady base.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit, and can a poor result be retaken?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. So a subject that goes wrong in the summer is recoverable in the autumn, with a second entry fee and a concentrated block of work. Decide early, because entry deadlines sit months ahead of exams. Note the results gap too: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so an autumn resit is not a quick fix if a December deadline is in play.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge mention administrative zones on the timetable?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable differs between them. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a family in Oud Metha the authoritative dates therefore come from the school's entry statement and the board's live timetable rather than from a PDF found through a search engine. Any revision plan built on the wrong zone has an avoidable failure in it.

faqs.question: Is a February or March exam window relevant to a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and this is worth checking against anything you read. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. A fair amount of tutoring content aimed at Gulf parents quotes a February or March window and an autumn entry deadline that belongs to a different country, and a parent who plans around it loses months. Confirm the series from your school's entry statement, and treat any provider that has this wrong as unreliable on the rest of the detail too.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring cost around Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end - EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 - through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270, up to AED 650 at the premium end from BartyED. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 including travel. All read October 2026, all the providers' own figures rather than ours. Monthly, one provider publishes AED 799 for eight online sessions.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education block affect maths teaching time?
faqs.answer: It presses on it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods sit inside the school day, so the mathematics teaching time your child receives is tighter than a subject list suggests - which is part of why a well-placed weekly hour outside school does real work.

faqs.question: Will a weekly hour over video hold a fifteen-year-old's attention?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether they are working or watching. A session spent listening to an explanation loses any teenager in any setting. A session where the student is solving problems with their written work shared on screen and marked line by line holds attention, because the feedback is immediate and they are the one doing the work. For mathematics, shared digital working is often clearer than a notebook at the edge of a kitchen table. Take the free trial in the slot you intend to keep and judge this student rather than the format.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free on our exact code and tier?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. For the common combinations - 0580 Extended, 4MA1 Higher - a match is usually quick. For 0607, 0606 or 4PM1 the pool is narrower and the wait can be longer, and the honest options are to wait, to start with a related specialist on a clearly stated interim basis, or not to book. Because sessions are delivered online rather than by someone driving to Oud Metha, the pool is every specialist on that code, which keeps those gaps shorter than they would otherwise be.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingHeading: Two documents, then a trial in the right slot
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingBody: Ask the school for two things before you spend anything: the entry statement, which names the board, code and tier you are actually buying support for, and the term calendar, which shows which weekdays will still be free in November. Those two documents prevent most of the ways IGCSE mathematics tuition goes wrong in this district. Then book a free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, bring the most recent marked piece of mathematics however poor it looks, and let the four-way split of where marks are going set the length of the plan. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Why the maths problem on Palm Jumeirah is usually a clock problem
paragraphs: Palm Jumeirah has nurseries and early-years provision, and it has no secondary school. Every Year 10 and Year 11 student living on a frond, on the Crescent, in Shoreline, Marina Residences, Tiara, Oceana, Golden Mile or Balqis leaves the island each morning and comes back to it each afternoon. The school day ends somewhere between 14:45 and 15:30 at most Dubai secondaries, the bus or the car then crosses the Trunk, and the front door opens between 15:45 and 16:45 depending on which frond you live on and how Al Sufouh Road is behaving. That single piece of geography shapes everything about IGCSE maths support here, and almost no tutoring page written for this island mentions it.

What it means in practice is that the window for useful maths work on a weekday is narrow and it is late. A student who walks in at 16:30 is not the same student who sat the first lesson of the day at 08:00. Algebraic manipulation, bounds, vectors and the non-calculator arithmetic that Cambridge now examines all need working memory, and working memory is the first thing a two-hour round trip spends. Booking a 16:00 session because that is when a tutor happens to be free is the most common scheduling error families on the Palm make, and it is expensive because the hour is paid for whether or not it lands.

An IGCSE maths tutor in Palm Jumeirah who arrives in person has to solve the same geography, from the other direction. The Palm is reached by one trunk road off Al Sufouh Road, the Crescent by tunnel, and each frond is a dead-end spine with a single entrance. A tutor driving from Al Barsha or Dubai Marina into a mid-frond address at 17:00 is committing an hour of unpaid travel to deliver sixty minutes of teaching, and that hour is priced into the rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. The published UAE market bands make that visible: in-home one-to-one sits roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, while qualified online subject tutors sit roughly AED 150 to 300.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Palm Jumeirah families are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own past papers on screen and the written work marked between sessions. The practical gain is not comfort, it is choice: the pool stops being whoever can reach your frond before dark and becomes whoever teaches Extended tier 0580 or Higher tier 4MA1 properly, at a time your child can still think.

The rest of this page is built around the school run. It names the schools students on the Palm actually travel to and what time each day ends, maps the three maths syllabuses those schools enter students for, shows where the marks go missing topic by topic, and sets out a weekly timetable that survives one road off the island. The AED bands are market figures with sources, not our price list, and the Cambridge and Pearson entry dates are counted backwards from the series so you can see how early the real deadlines sit.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Palm Jumeirah families sit across the two secondary routes Dubai's British-curriculum schools run, and a growing number sit in IB continuum schools that use Cambridge papers at 16. These are the programmes an IGCSE maths tutor in Palm Jumeirah is asked about most, with what each one does to the maths workload.

programmes.name: International GCSE (Years 10-11)
programmes.description: The two-year course that ends in the exam series your child's school enters them for. Maths is compulsory at every Dubai British-curriculum school, and it is tiered: a Core or Foundation entry caps the grade, an Extended or Higher entry opens the top grades and examines more content. The tier decision is usually taken in Year 10 on the strength of internal assessment, and it is reversible for longer than most parents are told.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the entry is made by the school as a Cambridge or Pearson centre, and each centre is allocated to one of six Cambridge administrative zones with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's risk and that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam. Ask the exams officer which zone your child's centre sits in before you plan revision around any published date.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme (Years 7-11)
programmes.description: The IB's middle-school programme, which several schools in the Palm commute belt run before the Diploma. MYP Mathematics splits into Standard and Extended in the final years, and it is marked against four criteria out of eight rather than against a paper total. Students moving from MYP into a Cambridge 0607 or 0580 entry meet timed written papers and mark-scheme method marks for the first time, which is where most of the early marks go.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB continuum schools sit mainly in Al Barsha, Al Safa and Umm Al Sheif, so a Palm Jumeirah family in this route has a 25 to 35 minute drive each way. That matters more here than in a British-curriculum family's week, because MYP assessment is spread across units all year instead of concentrated in one series, and the pressure points move rather than cluster.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme (Years 12-13)
programmes.description: Where many Palm Jumeirah students go after IGCSE maths. The Diploma splits mathematics into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher or Standard Level, and the route taken at 16 constrains the choice. A student finishing 0580 Extended with strong algebra has both doors open; a student finishing Core has neither Higher Level door open and should know that in Year 10, not in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: The IB does not publish a UAE Ministry of Education equivalency points figure that we can cite, so this page states none. The Ministry's published British-track rule is specific and verifiable: five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Confirm any IB figure on moe.gov.ae before planning around it.

programmes.name: A Level and Further Maths (Years 12-13)
programmes.description: The other post-16 route in this belt, and the one Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 exists to feed. A Year 11 student who adds 0606 alongside 0580 Extended arrives at AS Pure with calculus, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities already met once. Students who skip it spend the first term of Year 12 learning the same material under exam pressure instead of revisiting it.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series, the International GCSE November window included. Dubai schools entering students in November usually do so for retakes or for early entry, and a November entry compresses an eight-week revision block into the first half of the autumn term.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: IGCSE maths is one subject with several different papers behind it, and the paper decides the teaching. These are the maths and maths-adjacent courses a tutor working with Palm Jumeirah students is asked for, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The most widely entered maths syllabus in Dubai British-curriculum schools. Core reports grades C to G, Extended reports A* to E. Both tiers now sit a calculator paper and a non-calculator paper of equal weight, which pushed arithmetic fluency, surds, exact values and index laws back into the centre of revision after a decade on the margins.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: The graphics-calculator route, chosen by many IB continuum schools because it feeds Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation cleanly. It adds an investigation component that 0580 does not have, and rewards students who can explain a method rather than only execute one. A tutor who teaches 0580 well is not automatically fluent in 0607.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers, equally weighted, calculator permitted throughout, reported on the 9 to 1 scale. Higher tier reaches grade 9 and allows a grade 3; Foundation caps at grade 5. The question style is more structured than Cambridge Extended, with more marks available for a correct method even when the final value is wrong, which changes how working should be set out.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for Higher Level maths or A Level. It introduces differentiation, integration, the binomial theorem, logarithms and trigonometric identities at IGCSE level. Students who sit it arrive in Year 12 having already met the hardest ideas of the first term, which is the clearest tutoring return available at this stage.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: The Pearson equivalent of an additional maths entry, sat alongside 4MA1 Higher. It covers calculus, series, coordinate geometry and proof, and it is the fastest way to find out whether a student genuinely wants Higher Level or Further Maths later. Fewer Dubai centres enter it, so a specialist tutor is often the only route to proper paper practice.

subjects.name: IGCSE statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Histograms with unequal class widths, cumulative frequency, box plots, averages from grouped data and probability trees with and without replacement. Marks here are lost to frequency density, to reading a scale wrongly and to multiplying along the wrong branch, not to conceptual confusion. It is the most recoverable block on the paper in a short run-up.

subjects.name: IGCSE algebra and sequences
subjects.description: Expanding and factorising, algebraic fractions, simultaneous equations including one quadratic, rearranging formulae, inequalities, nth-term rules for linear, quadratic and geometric sequences. This is where the Extended tier separates from Core, and where a student who is fluent on paper but slow becomes a student who runs out of time on Paper 4.

subjects.name: IGCSE geometry, trigonometry and vectors
subjects.description: Circle theorems, similarity and congruence, the sine and cosine rules, bearings, three-dimensional trigonometry, vector geometry and transformations. Bearings and vectors are the two topics Dubai teachers most often report as under-taught, usually because they sit late in a scheme of work that the year has already eaten.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, Standard and Extended
subjects.description: The route into IGCSE for students at IB continuum schools in the commute belt. Assessment is against four criteria, each marked out of eight, including investigating patterns and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student strong on criterion A can still be weak on the timed written technique a Cambridge paper demands, and that gap is worth closing before Year 10.

subjects.name: Maths for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency
subjects.description: Maths is one of the five accredited subjects a British-track student needs at grade E or grade 3 or better for equivalency, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry, not by any tutoring provider, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own pages.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsTitle: Palm Jumeirah, frond by frond, and the belt your child commutes into
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsIntro: Session timing on the Palm depends on where on the Palm you live and which direction the car goes in the afternoon. These are the parts of the island and the school belt beyond it, with what each one does to a weekday maths slot.

regions.name: The Trunk and Golden Mile
regions.note: Closest to Al Sufouh Road, so the shortest afternoon return in the whole community. Families here can realistically hold a 16:30 or 17:00 maths slot on a weekday without the student arriving flattened.

regions.name: The Fronds (A to N)
regions.note: Single-entrance spine roads with villa addresses set well back. Add ten to fifteen minutes to any journey estimate for the frond itself, and treat 17:00 as the earliest honest weekday start for a mid-frond address.

regions.name: The Crescent, east and west
regions.note: Reached by tunnel from the Trunk, which adds distance in both directions and bunches badly around hotel traffic in the early evening. A 17:30 or 18:00 slot works far better here than a 16:30 one.

regions.name: Shoreline Apartments and Marina Residences
regions.note: Apartment living on the Trunk, with the shortest door-to-car time on the island. Useful for students who need two shorter maths sessions a week rather than one long one, because the overhead per session is low.

regions.name: Oceana, Tiara and Balqis Residences
regions.note: Crescent-side and mid-Trunk apartment clusters where lift and parking time is real. Families here often prefer a fixed weekend morning slot for the heavy algebra work and a short weekday slot for marking review.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif
regions.note: The nearest secondary belt to the Palm, and where many island students go to school. A 15:00 finish here puts a student home on the Trunk around 15:45 and on a frond around 16:10 on an ordinary day.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The IB continuum and large British-curriculum campuses, 25 to 35 minutes from the Palm in the afternoon. An island family on this run should assume a 16:45 arrival at best and plan the maths slot after it.

regions.name: Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah 1-3
regions.note: The coastal school belt east of the island, reached along Jumeirah Beach Road rather than Sheikh Zayed Road. Beach Road at 15:00 is slower than the motorway, so finishes here land later than the distance suggests.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif belt
schoolClusters.note: The closest secondary schools to Palm Jumeirah and the most common destination for island students, which is why afternoon maths slots here can start earlier than anywhere else in the community. Curricula and programmes change; confirm the current offer with the school.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha and Al Barsha South campuses
schoolClusters.note: The larger campuses, including IB continuum provision, on a 25 to 35 minute afternoon run from the Palm. Students on this commute need the later weekday slots and benefit most from a fixed weekend session for the heavy algebra work.

schoolClusters.city: The coastal belt: Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: Reached from the Palm along Jumeirah Beach Road. Shorter in kilometres than the Al Barsha run and often longer in minutes, which is the single most common planning mistake in island families' weekday timetables.

sections.heading: What a Palm Jumeirah family is actually searching for
paragraphs: Searching for an IGCSE maths tutor in Palm Jumeirah almost never means a parent wants a tutor who lives on Palm Jumeirah. It means a Year 10 or Year 11 student has a maths problem, the family lives on the island, and the search box is the shortest way to ask whether anybody can help inside the hours the week leaves free. The honest answer is that proximity has nothing to teach your child and the clock has everything, because there is no secondary school on the island and the afternoon is already spent before any lesson starts.

That makes the question concrete rather than vague. Which school does your child travel to, and what time does the day end there? How long is the return across the Trunk and down the frond? What is the first hour after that in which real algebra is possible? Which syllabus code is on the exam entry, and which tier? Those five answers determine the shape of useful support, and none of them is improved by a tutor who happens to live in Marina Residences rather than Al Barsha.

The pages that rank for this search mostly answer a different question. They list subjects, promise a match in twenty-four hours and show a photograph of a tutor at a kitchen table. What they do not do is name the schools island families actually attend, or say what time a lesson can start from the Crescent, or tell you which of the three maths syllabuses in this belt your child is on. This page does those things first, because they are the parts of the decision that are specific to living here.

One more piece of plain speaking before the detail. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We run no in-home visits in the UAE and no office in Dubai; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. The argument for online delivery on this island is not that it is modern, it is that a frond is a cul-de-sac on an artificial peninsula and a Chemistry or Extended-tier maths specialist should not have to be within driving distance of it to teach your child.

sections.heading: The school run from the Palm, hour by hour
paragraphs: A weekday maths slot on Palm Jumeirah is set by three numbers: the time the school day ends, the time the journey takes in the afternoon rather than at 06:30, and the time it takes to get from the Trunk to your own front door. The third number is the one families forget. A mid-frond villa adds ten to fifteen minutes to every journey estimate, and the Crescent adds the tunnel in both directions. Add them up honestly and a 16:00 lesson is impossible for most of the island, while a 17:00 lesson is comfortable for nearly all of it.

The table below works through the main school destinations for students living on the Palm. The finish times are the published shape of a Dubai secondary day rather than a promise about any one school, so check your child's timetable: schools stagger finishes by year group, and a Year 11 day often ends later than a Year 7 one. The last column is arithmetic, not advice, and the arithmetic is deliberately conservative because a lesson that starts ten minutes late every week loses more teaching than one scheduled thirty minutes later.

What follows from the table is a different way of buying tuition. If your realistic weekday start is 17:15, a single sixty-minute session is better placed at 17:30 than squeezed in at 16:30 where it competes with the journey. If it is 16:45 and your child is on the long Al Barsha run, two shorter sessions spread across the week will land better than one long one, because the useful attention in a late-afternoon hour runs out well before the hour does.

Weekends change the arithmetic completely. A Saturday morning session from any frond costs no travel, no traffic and no accumulated school day, which is why the heavy topics belong there. Families who hold one weekend slot for new teaching and one short weekday slot for marking review get more from two hours than families who buy a single ninety-minute weekday session they then spend fifteen minutes arriving at.

sections.heading: Which maths syllabus your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: There are three maths syllabuses in common use across the schools Palm Jumeirah students attend, and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the default at most British-curriculum schools. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is the graphics-calculator route favoured by IB continuum schools because it feeds the Diploma's two maths courses. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 is the Edexcel entry, reported on the 9 to 1 scale. A tutor who teaches one fluently is not automatically fluent in the others.

The single biggest change in this space is Cambridge's move to examine a non-calculator paper at both tiers of 0580. For a decade a student could reach a respectable grade with weak arithmetic and a good calculator technique. That route is closed. Index laws, surds, exact values, fraction arithmetic and estimation now carry marks directly, and students who learned maths on a calculator find the first non-calculator past paper genuinely alarming. If your child's school entered them for 0580 and nobody has mentioned this, it is the first thing to check.

Tier is the other decision hiding in the exam entry. Cambridge Core reports grades C to G and Extended reports A* to E; Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 while Higher reaches grade 9 and allows a grade 3. Schools provisionally tier in Year 10 from internal assessment, and that provisional decision is reversible for longer than families assume, because the binding moment is the centre's final entry deadline rather than any internal conversation. Knowing the deadline turns a vague worry into a dated decision.

Ask the exams officer for three things in one email: the syllabus code, the tier on the current entry, and the Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones with its own timetable version and states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Those three facts take one reply to obtain and they change what a tutor should spend your money on.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Most students who sit at a grade 5 or a C are not confused about mathematics. They lose marks in a small number of repeatable, diagnosable places, and a tutor who finds those places in the first two sessions is worth considerably more than one who starts at chapter one. The list below is what Dubai teachers report most often, and it is the list a first session should work through with your child's own marked papers rather than with a textbook.

Method marks are the most expensive habit. Pearson 4MA1 in particular hands out marks for a correct method even when the final answer is wrong, and a student who works mentally and writes only the answer throws those away silently. The fix is mechanical, not conceptual: write the substitution, write the rearrangement, write the units. It typically moves a Higher-tier student by several marks a paper within three weeks, which is faster than any topic teaching.

Rounding is the second. Rounding mid-calculation and then rounding again at the end produces answers just outside the accepted range, and the paper gives no credit for being nearly right. Exact-form answers in surds or in terms of pi are the related trap, because a decimal where an exact value was asked for scores nothing. Both are habit faults, both are fixed by marking the student's own work rather than by explaining the rule again.

Then the topics. Bearings and vector geometry sit late in most schemes of work and are routinely taught in a rush. Histograms with unequal class widths require frequency density and almost everybody forgets it. Probability trees without replacement break the second denominator. Algebraic fractions collapse when a sign is dropped. Three-dimensional trigonometry fails because no diagram was drawn. None of these is hard; all of them are reliably worth marks to a student who practises them deliberately in the eight weeks before a series.

sections.heading: The forty-five-minute problem after a Palm school run
paragraphs: There is a fact about tutoring that nobody selling tutoring likes to put in writing: a tired student does not learn mathematics at the rate a rested one does. A Palm Jumeirah student who left the frond at 06:50, sat six lessons and spent forty minutes in a car has roughly forty-five genuinely productive minutes left, and then a steep decline. Buying ninety minutes into that window means paying full price for a second half that mostly consists of a tutor talking while a fifteen-year-old nods.

The practical answer is to match the session length to the slot rather than to a package. On a short commute from Al Sufouh, a sixty-minute session starting at 16:45 is comfortable. On the Al Barsha South run, two forty-five minute sessions placed on different evenings will outperform one ninety-minute session, and cost the same. On the Crescent, where the tunnel adds time twice a day, the honest weekday start is 17:30 and the honest weekday length is an hour.

Session content should follow the same logic. New teaching, the kind that needs a student to hold three ideas at once, belongs in a weekend morning. Late-afternoon weekday slots are better spent on marked work: here is where you lost four marks, here is the same question type again, do it now while I watch. That is lower-load work with a higher return, and it is exactly the work a tired student can still do well.

This is also where in-home tutoring quietly loses on its own terms. A tutor who has driven from Al Barsha into a mid-frond address at 17:00 has an incentive to run the full ninety minutes they travelled for, whatever the student has left. An online session can be sixty minutes on Tuesday and forty-five on Thursday with no travel penalty for either, which is the kind of flexibility that only exists when nobody has to get into a car.

sections.heading: A weekly timetable that survives one road off the island
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the Palm's geography fails in the third week, not the first. The first week everybody is enthusiastic. By the third week the 16:00 Tuesday slot has been missed twice because of traffic on Al Sufouh Road, the student has started the session irritated, and the family has concluded that tutoring does not work. The problem was the slot, and it was predictable on day one.

The table below sets out the slots that work from a Palm address and what each one is good for. It is built from the arrival times in the school-run table above rather than from a template, and it assumes a student who is at a Dubai secondary school and lives on the island rather than one who can walk home in ten minutes. Read it against your own frond and your own school rather than averaging it.

Two patterns do most of the work. The first is one weekend morning plus one short weekday slot, which suits students who need new teaching as well as correction, and which is the default for a Year 10 student with a full year ahead. The second is two short weekday slots plus a Friday evening paper, which suits a Year 11 student in the eight weeks before a series who already knows the content and needs timed practice and marking cycles.

Ramadan shifts all of it. Weekday afternoons compress, school days shorten, and the productive study window moves to the evening after Iftar. Families on the Palm usually move the maths slot later by two to three hours for the month and keep the frequency the same, which preserves the marking cycle through a period when most tutoring simply stops. Plan that move before the month starts rather than during it.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition costs around Palm Jumeirah
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the number a family actually lives with. One maths hour a week is four or five hours a month, and the published UAE market bands turn that into something concrete: a budget online tutor at AED 45 to 150 an hour comes out around AED 240 to 600 a month, a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour comes out around AED 600 to 1,200, and a specialist in an exam year at AED 200 to 450 and above comes out at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Those monthly bands are Bestimate's own estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in its Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026.

The hourly figures behind them come from providers' own published rate cards, also read in October 2026. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour. One Dubai agency's rate card listed IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. A UK-based agency operating in the Gulf published AED 270. At the top, a named-tutor service published AED 650. In-home one-to-one across Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is in the price, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799, against around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

None of those numbers is an IB Gram price, and this page does not publish one. What it does say is what the spread means: the gap between the budget band and the specialist band is not a quality mystery, it is mostly whether the person teaching your child has taught the exact syllabus code and tier before, and whether the hour includes marking your child's written work between sessions. That second question is the one most families forget to ask, and it is worth more than fifty dirhams an hour either way.

Set the plan against the school fee rather than against nothing. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A family already paying Dubai secondary fees can see where one maths hour a week sits in that picture, and can decide honestly whether three subjects at once is a budget or a panic. For our own fees, take the free trial lesson and ask on the consultation.

sections.heading: Online lessons versus a tutor who drives onto the fronds
paragraphs: This page targets a phrase parents type, so it should answer the question inside it. In-home maths tutoring on Palm Jumeirah is a real market with real providers, and it has genuine advantages: a younger child stays in a familiar room, a parent can see the session happening, and there is no technology to fail. It also has a structural cost that is specific to this island, and the cost is the road.

A tutor serving the Palm in person is serving a peninsula with one trunk connection, tunnel access to the Crescent and fourteen dead-end fronds. That geography limits how many students one tutor can see in an afternoon, which limits who is willing to do it, which limits what your child can be taught. If the best available Extended-tier 0580 teacher in that radius is a general science graduate, your child gets a general science graduate. The travel premium in the market bands above, roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour over the comparable online rate, buys the drive rather than better teaching.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and no sentence on this site will promise a tutor at a UAE address. Our lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own past papers on screen and annotated working saved afterwards. The trade is deliberate: you give up a person in the room and you gain a tutor selected for the syllabus code and tier your child is sitting rather than for their postcode.

The table sets the two formats side by side on the things that actually differ for an island family. Read the last row carefully, because it is the one that decides most cases: a frond address with a 17:00 arrival and a Higher-tier 4MA1 entry has a much larger online tutor pool than in-home pool, and the gap widens the more specific the requirement gets.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson dates, counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Exam calendars are the single biggest gap in this part of the search results, and the reason is that the useful dates are not the exam dates. They are the deadlines that sit months earlier and quietly fix what your child can do. A family that learns in January that the tier was locked in November has lost a decision it did not know it held. Counting backwards is the only way to see them in time.

Start with which series your child is actually sitting, because getting that wrong invalidates every other date. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and those are the two available to UAE centres. Cambridge also operates a February/March series, but it is offered to India only, so a key-dates document or timetable found through a general search can belong to a series your child will never sit. Cambridge then allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong one was used.

Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables for future series, including the International GCSE November series still to run, and those can be revised, so plan against the live official timetable rather than against a date restated on somebody else's website.

Two practical consequences for a Palm Jumeirah family. First, ask the exams officer for the series, the centre's Cambridge zone and the entry deadline in the same email as the syllabus code, because all four shape the revision plan and none is guessable. Second, work in eight-week blocks counted back from the first paper: weeks one to three for the diagnostic and the weakest two topics, weeks four to six for timed questions by topic, weeks seven and eight for whole papers under exam conditions with marking in between. That block fits inside a Dubai term, and it fits around a school run across the Trunk.

sections.heading: Permits, academic honesty and what a maths tutor may not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rule is specific enough to check. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is the MoHRE service page for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears on this page, and you should treat any website quoting a specific figure with care. The other side of the rule matters for Abu Dhabi families and for anyone considering a teacher from their child's own school: professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. No tutor is KHDA approved as an individual, because KHDA's Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises, not to people.

Academic honesty has a clear line in maths and it is worth stating because some pages in this market cross it. A tutor may teach a technique, set practice questions, mark a student's working, explain a mark scheme's logic and coach the process of writing up an investigation. A tutor may not write or complete an Internal Assessment, an exploration, an Extended Essay or any coursework, and nobody at IB Gram will. Work that must be the student's own stays the student's own; the consequences of the alternative fall on the student, not on the tutor.

Two smaller points in the same spirit. Official syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson, so this page links to their own pages rather than hosting their documents. And no tutor on this site is described as a current examiner unless that status can be evidenced, because examiner status is widely claimed in this market and rarely checkable. If anybody claims it to you, ask which board, which component, and which series.

faqs.question: Is there a secondary school on Palm Jumeirah for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: No. The island has nurseries and early-years provision, and no secondary school, so every Year 10 and Year 11 student living on a frond, on the Crescent or in the Trunk apartments commutes off the Palm each day. The nearest secondary belt is Al Sufouh and Umm Al Sheif, roughly twenty to thirty minutes away in the afternoon, with the larger Al Barsha campuses thirty to forty-five minutes out. That is why the useful question for maths support here is what time your child is actually home, not which tutor lives closest.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE maths lesson start if the school run gets us back to the Palm at 16:15?
faqs.answer: A 16:15 arrival on the Trunk means 16:30 is workable and 16:45 is comfortable. On a mid-frond address, add ten to fifteen minutes for the spine road and start at 16:45 or 17:00. On the Crescent, where the tunnel adds time in both directions, 17:15 or 17:30 is the honest answer. The reason to be strict about this is that a session which starts ten minutes late every week loses more teaching over a term than one scheduled half an hour later, and a student who walks straight in from a car has nothing left for algebra.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus code should I look for on my child's exam timetable?
faqs.answer: Look for one of four. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics is 0607, Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics is 0606, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. The code appears on the exam entry and the statement of entry, and your school's exams officer can confirm it in a single reply. Ask for the tier at the same time, and for the Cambridge administrative zone your centre sits in, because all three change what revision should look like and none of them is guessable from the textbook on the kitchen table.

faqs.question: Does the non-calculator paper in Cambridge 0580 change how we revise?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Both tiers of 0580 now sit a non-calculator paper alongside a calculator paper, so index laws, surds, exact values, fraction arithmetic and estimation carry marks directly rather than being bypassed by good calculator technique. Students who learned maths with a calculator in hand usually find their first non-calculator past paper a shock. The practical fix is short, frequent arithmetic drilling rather than long sessions, which is one reason two forty-five minute weekday slots often beat one ninety-minute slot for a student commuting back to the Palm.

faqs.question: Should my child sit the Core or the Extended tier in maths?
faqs.answer: It depends on the grade they need and the evidence they have. Cambridge Core reports C to G, so it closes the top grades; Extended reports A* to E and examines more content. Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 while Higher reaches 9 and allows a 3. The decision is usually provisional in Year 10 and becomes binding at the centre's final entry deadline, which Cambridge sets with the centre months before the papers. Ask the exams officer what is currently on the entry, then decide against a marked paper rather than against a feeling.

faqs.question: My child is on Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier and stuck around grade 5. What moves it?
faqs.answer: Usually working, not knowledge. Pearson awards method marks generously, and a student who calculates mentally and writes only the final answer loses them invisibly on every question. Writing the substitution, the rearrangement and the units typically recovers several marks a paper within three weeks. After that, the highest-yield topics are algebraic fractions, simultaneous equations involving a quadratic, histograms with unequal class widths and probability without replacement. A first session on a recent marked paper will show which of those is costing your child the most.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Year 11 student on the Palm need?
faqs.answer: One a week is enough for maintenance and for a student who is broadly fine but slipping. Two a week is the normal answer inside the eight weeks before a series, and the reason is marking cycles rather than teaching time: two sessions means two rounds of written work marked and corrected. Past two a week, the limiting factor is usually the student's own practice time rather than tuition, and more hours start to crowd out the independent past-paper work that the hours are supposed to be improving.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IGCSE maths support cost for a family on Palm Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands, read in October 2026, run from AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or IB specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in. As a monthly figure for one hour a week, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. None of those is our price list; ask on the consultation.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor drive out to the Crescent for a 17:00 session?
faqs.answer: Some in the Dubai market will, and the market rate reflects it: in-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and no page here will promise a tutor at a UAE address; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Our lessons are one-to-one over live video, which on the Crescent has a practical advantage beyond price: the tunnel does not have to be crossed twice for an hour of teaching to happen.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge entries close for the next IGCSE maths series?
faqs.answer: Earlier than families expect, and the exams officer is the only person who can give you the exact date. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and those two are what UAE centres sit; the February/March series is offered to India only, so dates found through a general search may belong to a series your child will never take. Final entry deadlines are agreed between Cambridge and your child's centre and sit months before the first paper, and the tier is part of that entry. Ask for the series, the deadline and the centre's administrative zone in one email.

faqs.question: Does the exam timetable zone matter for a Dubai exam centre?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone. Cambridge also says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, and plan revision against that version rather than against a timetable found through a general search.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children if they are in different maths tiers?
faqs.answer: It is possible and it is usually the wrong buy. A Core or Foundation student and an Extended or Higher student need different content, different question styles and different pacing, and a single tutor covering both tends to teach to the middle, which serves neither. Online delivery removes the reason families compromise: there is no travel cost to a second tutor, so each child can have a specialist in their own tier at a time that suits them. Siblings sharing one visiting tutor is a logistics saving, not a teaching one.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors working with Dubai families need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without the permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, treat any site quoting a specific amount with suspicion.

faqs.question: How do weekend maths sessions compare with weekday evenings for a Palm address?
faqs.answer: A weekend morning is the best hour of the week for a student living on the Palm, because there is no commute, no school day behind it and full working memory available. That is where new teaching and full timed papers belong. Weekday evening slots are better used for correction work: here is where the four marks went, here is the same question type, do it now. Many island families settle on one weekend morning plus one short weekday slot, which gives both new teaching and a marking cycle inside the same week.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start maths tuition if the series is four months away?
faqs.answer: Four months is a comfortable run, not a crisis. It fits two eight-week blocks with a gap, which is more than enough to fix working habits, drill non-calculator arithmetic and cover the recoverable topics properly. Even eight weeks is workable: weeks one to three on diagnostics and the weakest two topics, weeks four to six on timed questions by topic, weeks seven and eight on whole papers with marking in between. What nobody can do is promise a particular grade, and a provider who offers one is telling you something about themselves.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE maths grades count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Maths counts as one of the subjects in the British-track rule. The Ministry's published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring provider, tutoring is not required for it, and the current rule should be confirmed on the Ministry's own pages.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.closingHeading: Start with the timetable, then the syllabus code
dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the arithmetic: find out what time your child is genuinely home on your frond, then choose a slot after it rather than before it. Then get the syllabus code and the tier from the exams officer, and ask any prospective tutor to talk for five minutes about that specific paper. A tutor who can describe where marks go missing on Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher is worth more than one who can reach your door. Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one and online, with a free trial lesson in one subject before any paid block is booked, and marking of your child's written work between sessions rather than as an extra.

intro.heading: Two slots, two years, and two different jobs
paragraphs: The useful question for a Pearl Jumeira family is not whether their child needs a maths tutor but when the session is going to happen and what it is for. Those two answers change more about the outcome than the choice of tutor does, and almost nothing in a search result addresses either.

Start with when. Senior school days in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster end between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm. Pearl Jumeira is reclaimed land reached by a single causeway from the Jumeirah 1 shoreline, so the drive home means crossing Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road and then joining one queue onto the island, which takes thirty to forty-five minutes at that hour. Activity programmes in these schools run roughly 4pm to 6pm. That leaves exactly two windows that hold up across a full academic year: an early one from about 4:45pm on activity-free days, and a dependable one from 6:45pm after food. Maths after 8:30pm on a school night is money spent on a tired student, because tiredness in this subject produces arithmetic slips rather than visible confusion, and a tutor then chases a problem that is not there.

Now what the session is for, which is where most families lose value. Year 10 and Year 11 need different sessions, and treating them as one continuous arrangement is the commonest planning error in this cluster. Year 10 is about coverage and foundation: the content is being met for the first time, algebraic manipulation is still being built, and the right session reinforces the week's teaching and repairs gaps before they compound. Year 11 is about papers: the content is largely taught, the marks are being lost in specific identifiable places, and the right session works from marked scripts against the published mark scheme.

The practical consequence is that the same tutor doing the same thing for two years is doing the wrong thing for one of them. A Year 10 session spent on past papers is premature, because the student has not met half the content. A Year 11 session spent working through the textbook is a waste, because the content is not the problem. Saying which mode a session is in, at the start, converts an hour of maths into an hour of teaching.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working annotated on a shared screen and kept afterwards. For this island the timing benefit is concrete: a 4:45pm start is a 4:45pm start, with nobody sitting in the causeway queue, and the early slot is the better slot for quantitative work.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Mathematics

For families on this island who expect to choose the Diploma, that is a reason to take the non-calculator work in Year 10 seriously rather than as an inconvenience.

The practical implication for a Year 10 family is the same as for the Diploma: the tier decision and the quality of the algebraic foundation in Year 10 determine which post-16 courses remain available, which makes early spending more useful than late spending.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE maths topics that generate the most sessions among Pearl Jumeira families, grouped by whether they belong in a Year 10 coverage session or a Year 11 paper session.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and rearrangement
subjects.description: A Year 10 priority, because it sits underneath almost every other topic. A student weak here loses marks in geometry, trigonometry and statistics without any mark scheme mentioning algebra. Repairing it in Year 10 is cheap; repairing it in Year 11 is not.

subjects.name: Quadratic equations and the three solution methods
subjects.description: Factorising, the formula and completing the square, with the expectation that the student chooses. Completing the square is the method most often skipped in class and most often required, because turning-point and sketching questions depend on it.

subjects.name: Simultaneous equations, linear and non-linear
subjects.description: Procedural once the method is secure, and a reliable source of full marks. The Extended non-linear case, where a line meets a curve, is the version students have least practice with and it recurs regularly.

subjects.name: Indices, standard form and surds
subjects.description: Belongs squarely in non-calculator preparation for Cambridge candidates. Pearson students permitted a calculator throughout meet these as rules rather than as working skills, which is a real difference in what the session should cover.

subjects.name: Trigonometry including sine and cosine rules
subjects.description: The failure is almost never the rule; it is the absent diagram, which leads to the wrong rule being chosen. Teaching the habit of drawing before calculating recovers more marks than reteaching the trigonometry.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar shapes
subjects.description: Volumes and surface areas of composite solids, plus area and volume scale factors for similar figures. The squared and cubed scale factor rule is among the most commonly misremembered facts on the Extended papers.

subjects.name: Probability with tree and Venn diagrams
subjects.description: Conditional probability without replacement is the specific loss: students do not change the second-branch fraction. Venn questions are lost by shading a region that does not match the set notation given. Both are visible in minutes of marked work.

subjects.name: Statistics: histograms and cumulative frequency
subjects.description: Histograms with unequal class widths need frequency density, which is the reliable trap. Cumulative frequency rewards careful axis reading rather than calculation, which makes it a good place to protect marks rather than chase them.

subjects.name: Vectors and vector reasoning
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and proving collinearity or a ratio along a line. Students who can compute the vector frequently cannot write the reasoning sentence the mark scheme wants, and that sentence is where the method marks are.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Transformation notation rather than verbal description is what the paper asks for, and sketches lose marks when intercepts and asymptotes are unlabelled. A Year 11 paper-session topic rather than a Year 10 coverage one.

sections.heading: The two slots that survive a Pearl Jumeira school year
paragraphs: Session timing is treated as an afterthought in most tutoring arrangements and it is the variable most likely to end them. The table maps the afternoon from the school bell to the point where quantitative work stops being productive, as it actually runs for a household on this island.

The 4:45pm slot is the better of the two and the harder to keep. A student home by 4:15pm who has no activity that day is at their most able, and an hour of algebra at that point goes further than the same hour three hours later. Its weakness is that it is the slot activity programmes, school fixtures and revision clinics take first, so families who want it have to decide in September rather than negotiate in January.

The 6:45pm slot is the one to build the year on. It sits after the activity run and after food, it leaves a short window afterwards in which the student can attempt something unaided, and it survives from September to the examinations without collapsing. For most IGCSE students a single hour in this slot is the entire requirement across two years.

The reason to rule out later slots is specific to mathematics. A tired student reading a set text still absorbs something. A tired student doing a multi-stage calculation produces errors that resemble conceptual gaps, and a tutor working from that evidence will spend the following week teaching a topic the student already understood. The session then costs twice: once in the hour, once in the misdirection. That is the argument for moving a slot rather than adding one.

sections.heading: Which topics sit on which paper, and why that changes the session
paragraphs: Most revision is organised by topic, and most papers are not. Knowing which paper a topic is likely to be examined on, and in what style, is what lets an hour be aimed rather than spread. The table maps the main Cambridge 0580 Extended topic blocks against the paper where the marks tend to sit and the way the question is usually framed.

The non-calculator paper is the one that reorganises everything. On Cambridge 0580 Extended, Paper 2 permits no calculator across two hours and 100 marks, which means exact fractions, surds, standard form, indices and mental estimation are assessed skills rather than background competence. A student who has used a calculator reflexively since Year 7 is not weak at these topics; they have never been required to perform them. That distinction matters because it is fixable in a defined block rather than being a general weakness.

Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 works the other way. A calculator is permitted in both two-hour papers, so the premium shifts to setting a problem up correctly, working efficiently, and managing time across long multi-step questions. Hours spent drilling mental arithmetic for a 4MA1 candidate are hours spent on something the paper does not reward, and this is the single most common mismatch produced by hiring a tutor without confirming the code.

The practical rule that follows is to name the paper at the start of each Year 11 session. An hour aimed at the non-calculator paper looks nothing like an hour aimed at the calculator paper: the first is exact methods and estimation, the second is setup, efficiency and checking. A session described only as maths revision will drift to whichever topic feels most pressing, which is how twelve paid hours produce no measurable change.
