sections.heading: Why Year 10 and Year 11 need opposite kinds of session
paragraphs: This is the planning point that saves the most money on this island, and it is the one almost no tutoring arrangement makes explicit. The job in Year 10 is the opposite of the job in Year 11, and a tutor doing one of them for two years is wasting a year.

In Year 10 the content is arriving for the first time, roughly half the syllabus has not been met, and algebraic fluency is still being built. The right session reinforces the week's class teaching, closes the gap the student noticed on Tuesday, and spends deliberate time on manipulation, because every later topic depends on it. Past papers in this year are mostly a morale problem: a student who cannot yet answer two thirds of a paper learns that they cannot answer two thirds of a paper.

In Year 11 the content is largely taught and the problem has become specific. The marks are being lost somewhere identifiable, usually in a small number of places, and the right session begins with a marked script and works against the published mark scheme. The questions are set in advance and attempted alone, because the session's value is in the marking and the correction rather than in the explanation.

There is a third mode worth naming, which is the transition. Somewhere in the first term of Year 11 a family should convert the arrangement: fewer explanations, more marked papers, a written topic list with mark values attached. Families who never make that switch often report the same frustration, which is that the sessions continue pleasantly and the grades do not move. The sessions have not failed; they have continued doing the Year 10 job into the year that needed the other one.

sections.heading: Mock season: turning a marked script into a plan
paragraphs: The winter mock window is the only honest diagnostic a family gets, and most of its value is thrown away because the script is read as a grade rather than as data. The grade tells a parent roughly where the student is. The script tells a tutor exactly what to teach, and the difference between those two readings is worth several marks.

A script read properly produces four separate pieces of information. Which topics lost marks, which is the obvious one. Which kinds of error, which is more useful: arithmetic slips, misread questions, correct method with a wrong final step, or genuinely absent knowledge. Where marks were left unattempted, which usually indicates a timing or confidence issue rather than a content one. And how many marks each problem is actually worth, which is what makes prioritisation possible rather than arbitrary.

That reading takes about an hour and turns into a topic list with mark values attached. A list like that answers the only question that matters in the weeks after the mocks: what should the next eight hours be spent on? Without it, the sessions drift to whatever came up in class that week, which is how a family funds twelve hours of pleasant teaching and sees no change in the next assessment.

One further point about the mock itself. A mock sat on a paper the school will reuse should not be worked through with a tutor in detail afterwards, and a tutor should not be supplying solutions to a live school paper. The legitimate work is on the student's own script and on past papers obtained properly. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables belong to Cambridge International and to Pearson; they are referenced and linked rather than redistributed, and a tutor arriving with a folder of copied material has answered a question nobody needed to ask.

sections.heading: The Core or Extended decision, and the honest way to make it
paragraphs: Somewhere in Year 10 the school will decide, or ask you to help decide, which tier your child sits. It sets a ceiling before any teaching happens: Cambridge Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, so a Core candidate cannot achieve an A however well they perform. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers work on the same principle.

The decision is often made on classroom impressions, which are an unreliable instrument in both directions. A student who is quiet in class and accurate on paper looks weaker than they are. A student who is articulate in discussion and careless under time pressure looks stronger. Neither impression predicts a tiered paper result well.

The honest instrument is a marked Extended or Higher past paper taken under timed conditions, read for pattern rather than for total. If the lost marks are technique, that is, method lines not written, questions misread, time mismanaged, then the student is an Extended candidate who needs a term of work. If the lost marks are content across several unrelated topics with the series approaching, protecting a strong Core grade is usually the better decision than chasing a weak Extended one, because a secure grade is worth more than an ambitious failure.

For MoE equivalency on the British track, the published rule is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One provider ranking for these searches publishes a different subject count. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than through any tutoring website, this one included.
bullets: Cambridge Core is graded C to G; Extended A* to E

sections.heading: The examination year, and the dates worth knowing
paragraphs: Session planning in Year 11 is calendar-driven, and this is ground no competitor page in this search covers. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any February or March dates quoted to a family on this island should be disregarded. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

Checkable reference points are worth stating with their provenance. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations, which is what makes them verifiable. The live official timetable is what should be checked before acting, because provisional timetables are revised before each series.

One Cambridge administrative detail has a practical cost attached. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the timetable differs by zone, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A revision schedule built from the wrong timetable is effort spent against the wrong dates. Ask the school which zone it sits in rather than downloading the first timetable a search returns.

The shape of the final term follows from all this. Ten to twelve weeks out, the sessions should be on the diagnosed list from the mock script, which are the highest-value hours of the whole course. In the last four weeks the paid hours should reduce rather than increase, because at that stage accuracy and speed set through the student's own timed practice, and a session is more useful for marking that practice than for adding new teaching.

sections.heading: What this costs, and what a parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are easy to find and hard to interpret, so the useful frame is what a parent can check rather than what a provider claims. Three things are verifiable: the figure, its source, and the date it was read. Everything else in a tutoring advertisement generally is not.

On that basis: in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE rates from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Budget online options start at AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Premium examiner-branded providers reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Each of those belongs to the provider named and was read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price list.

What cannot be verified is a satisfaction percentage without a sample size and a method, a star rating a provider has awarded itself, or a claim about examiner status that cannot be evidenced. The competitor audit for this market found pages publishing different review totals in different places on the same page, and one quoting a self-asserted rating in its page code that did not match the figure on the page. Those are the things to weigh alongside the rate, and examining them is free.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the figure does not vary with the causeway and the hour booked is the hour taught. No grade or improvement is guaranteed here, because nobody can honestly stand behind such a promise, and any provider offering one has told you something useful about the rest of their claims.

Not verifiable: satisfaction percentages without n, date and method
Not verifiable: self-awarded star ratings or unevidenced examiner status

process.title: Confirm the code and the tier
process.description: Find out whether the school enters for Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, and at which tier. It is on the exam entry statement. It determines whether non-calculator work is a priority at all, and it prevents the first paid sessions going on calibration.

process.title: Claim the slot in September
process.description: We ask for school finish time and activity days before discussing mathematics. The 4:45pm window is the better one and it is taken by January. A slot chosen around the week lasts two years; one chosen around tutor availability lapses by the second term.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge, taught rather than pitched, with the student. The tutor looks at recent marked work and starts teaching. One trial lesson per student, before any booking; if the match is wrong, say so and nothing is owed.

process.title: Run the Year 10 session on coverage
process.description: Through Year 10 the hour follows the school's teaching order, closes the gaps the student noticed that week, and spends deliberate time on algebraic manipulation. Past papers are used sparingly, because half the syllabus has not been met yet.

process.title: Switch to paper mode in Year 11
process.description: In the first term of Year 11 the arrangement changes on purpose: marked scripts, the published mark scheme, a topic list with mark values attached, and timed practice as the series approaches. In the final four weeks the hours taper rather than rise.

whyPoints.title: The slot is decided before the tutor
whyPoints.description: In a cluster where school ends by 3:30pm, a causeway adds half an hour and activities run to six, the session time determines whether the hour works at all. It is the first thing discussed, which is why the arrangement is still standing in March.

whyPoints.title: Year 10 and Year 11 treated as different jobs
whyPoints.description: Coverage and foundation in the first year; marked papers and diagnosed lists in the second. A tutor doing the same thing for two years is doing the wrong thing for one of them, and that is the most common reason sessions continue while grades do not move.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended has a two-hour paper with no calculator; Pearson 4MA1 permits one in both papers. Drilling mental arithmetic for a Pearson candidate is work the paper does not reward, and matching on the code prevents it.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the hour
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video, so a 4:45pm start is a 4:45pm start and the rate is identical whether a family lives on the island or in Jumeirah 1. The early slot, which is the better one for quantitative work, becomes genuinely available.

whyPoints.title: Figures with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every AED number here carries the provider that published it and the month it was read. What cannot be verified, including satisfaction percentages without a sample size and self-awarded ratings, is named as unverifiable rather than repeated.

whyPoints.title: Hours that taper on purpose
whyPoints.description: In the last four weeks before a series the paid sessions reduce, because accuracy and speed set through the student's own timed practice. No grade or improvement is guaranteed, and advice to buy fewer hours is given when that is the honest answer.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE maths session start for a Pearl Jumeira student?
faqs.answer: Two windows work. An hour from about 4:45pm on days without an activity, which is the stronger slot because the student is not yet tired. And an hour from 6:45pm after food, which is the one to build the year on because it survives from September to the examinations. School here ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm and the Al Wasl Road crossing plus the causeway queue takes thirty to forty-five minutes. Nothing useful happens after about 8:30pm.

faqs.question: Why is late-evening maths tutoring worse than late-evening revision in other subjects?
faqs.answer: Because of how tiredness presents. A tired student reading a set text still absorbs something. A tired student working a multi-stage calculation makes arithmetic slips that look exactly like conceptual gaps, so the tutor takes the wrong diagnosis away and spends the following week teaching a topic the student already understood. The session then costs twice: once in the hour and once in the misdirection. Where no earlier slot exists, moving the slot beats adding another one.

faqs.question: Should Year 10 maths sessions be working through past papers?
faqs.answer: Mostly not. In Year 10 roughly half the syllabus has not been taught, so a past paper tells the student what they cannot yet do and little else. The productive Year 10 session follows the school's teaching order, closes the gap the student noticed that week, and spends deliberate time on algebraic manipulation, because almost every later topic rests on it. Paper work belongs in Year 11, started from a marked script rather than from a clean paper.

faqs.question: When should a family change how the maths sessions are run?
faqs.answer: In the first term of Year 11, deliberately. The job changes: content is largely taught, the marks are being lost in a small number of identifiable places, and the useful session begins with a marked script worked against the published mark scheme. Families who never make that switch usually report the same thing, which is that sessions continue pleasantly while the grades stay where they were. The sessions have not failed; they are still doing the Year 10 job.

faqs.question: Which 0580 topics are examined on the non-calculator paper?
faqs.answer: Exact fractions, surds, indices, standard form and estimation concentrate there, along with algebraic manipulation, which appears on both papers. On Cambridge 0580 Extended, Paper 2 permits no calculator across two hours and 100 marks, which makes those skills assessed in their own right rather than assumed background. Trigonometry, mensuration and statistics tend to carry more weight on the calculator paper, where the questions are longer and more contextual.

faqs.question: My child has always used a calculator. Is that a real problem for Cambridge?
faqs.answer: It is a specific and fixable one rather than a general weakness. A student who has reached for a calculator since Year 7 has not practised exact fractions, surds and standard form as working skills, and Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 2 requires them across two hours. That is a defined block of six to eight sessions rather than a long-term deficit. It also happens to be the best preparation available for the Diploma's non-calculator paper if the student goes that route.

faqs.question: Does a Pearson 4MA1 student need non-calculator practice at all?
faqs.answer: Not in the same way, and this is the most common mismatch produced by hiring without confirming the code. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both of its two-hour papers, so the premium shifts to setting a problem up correctly, working efficiently and managing time across long multi-step questions. Hours spent drilling mental arithmetic for a 4MA1 candidate are hours spent on something the paper does not reward. Check the entry statement before anybody is booked.

faqs.question: How should we read a marked mock script rather than the grade?
faqs.answer: For four things. Which topics lost marks, which is obvious. What kind of error occurred, which is more useful: slips, misread questions, correct method with a wrong final step, or absent knowledge. Where marks were left unattempted, which usually means a timing or confidence problem rather than a content one. And how many marks each issue is worth, which makes prioritisation possible. An hour spent on that produces a topic list with mark values, which is what the following weeks should follow.

faqs.question: Can a tutor go through the school's own mock paper with my child?
faqs.answer: The student's own marked script, yes. The paper itself, where the school intends to reuse it, no, and a tutor should not be supplying solutions to a live school paper. The legitimate material is the student's script plus past papers obtained properly. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables belong to Cambridge International and Pearson and are referenced and linked rather than redistributed. A tutor arriving with a folder of copied material has told you about their standards.

faqs.question: How should the Core or Extended tier decision be made?
faqs.answer: From a marked Extended or Higher past paper taken under timed conditions, read for pattern rather than total. If the lost marks are technique, meaning method lines not written, questions misread or time mismanaged, the student is an Extended candidate who needs a term of work. If they are content across several unrelated topics with the series approaching, protecting a strong Core grade usually beats chasing a weak Extended one. Cambridge Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, so the choice sets a ceiling.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE maths exams run for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so disregard any February or March dates quoted to you. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. As checkable reference points, Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026. Confirm current dates on the official timetable, since provisional versions get revised.

faqs.question: Could our revision plan be built against the wrong Cambridge timetable?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth checking. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and the exam timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone it sits in and make sure any tutor planning a revision schedule is working from that version rather than one found through a search.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor across the causeway to Pearl Jumeira?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working annotated on a shared screen and kept afterwards. For this island the timing consequence is the useful one: the better 4:45pm slot becomes genuinely available, because nobody is sitting in the causeway queue trying to reach it.

faqs.question: What can a parent actually verify in a tutoring advertisement?
faqs.answer: Three things: the figure quoted, the source it came from, and the date it was read. On that basis, in-home tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, with Bestimate's 2026 table at AED 180 to AED 350; online qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors from AED 150 and TutorChase at AED 270. What cannot be verified is a satisfaction percentage without a sample size and method, or a self-awarded star rating, and both are common in this market.

dubai/igcse-maths-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.closingBody: Three moves carry IGCSE maths for a family on this island, and only one of them involves choosing a tutor. Find the awarding body and tier on the exam entry statement, because it decides whether non-calculator work matters at all. Claim the 4:45pm or 6:45pm slot in September, before the activity calendar takes it. Then change the session deliberately in the first term of Year 11, from coverage to marked papers with a topic list and mark values attached. Take the free trial lesson first. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no travel inside the hour.
